Significant problems may occur if sufficient effort is not committed to communications. The program manager should constantly monitor and foster an environment where stakeholder communication needs are met. Reference is standard for program management page#112&66.

text: Your are a program manager for one of a critical programs in your organization. The program contains 8 projects, one of these projects has been closed, what will you update immediately?

choices.text: Update the program charter.
Update the program business case.
Update the program roadmap.
Update the program issue log.

explanation: Correct answer is C: The initiation and closure of these components are significant milestones in the program roadmap and schedule, so when the project closed, you should update its milestone in the program roadmap. Reference is the standard for program management page#52.

text: You are a program manager of a system development program. Now you and your team are working on the delivery phase assessing the program’s progress toward achieving its expected benefits. Which of the following tools can help you?

choices.text: SWOT.
Comparative analysis.
Ishikawa.
Program roadmap.

explanation: Correct answer is D: The program roadmap can be a valuable tool for managing the organization of a program and for assessing a program’s progress toward achieving its expected benefits. Reference is standard for program management page#37.

text: You are assigned as a program manager of the ASD program for your organization. You are in the planning sub-phase developing the financial framework. choices.text: Program scope statement.
Program business case.
Financial management plan.
Program charter.

explanation: Correct answer is B: As the program financial framework is developed and analyzed, changes may be identified that impact the original business case justifying the program. Based on these changes, the business case is revised with full involvement of the decision makers. Reference is standard for program management page#114.

text: You are a program manager of a very important program for your organization. The project manager of project A escalates to you a risk that may impact other projects in the program. What should you do first?

choices.text: Document the risk in the program risk register.
Develop response strategy for the risk.
Perform qualitative risk analysis.
Escalate to the program governance board.

explanation: Correct answer is A: The first step is capturing the risk in the risk register, the second is qualitative and quantitative risk analysis the last step is developing the risk response plan.

text: DICKO TEC is an organization for information technology. They have been awarded one of the most important programs with the Ministry of finance. You are the program manager of this program and the customer is very happy by the program performance. Now you are in the closure phase and all the program benefits have been delivered. Within the above context, what will you do to transition the program?

choices.text: Close all components and their contracts.
Transfer the program immediately to the customer, since they are happy by the program performance.
Present the final performance report to governance board.
Complete the transition of all program components.

explanation: Correct answer is C: Option A is wrong because all components and their contracts already closed and the benefits have been delivered. Option B is wrong because we can’t transition the program without approval from the program steering committee. Option D is wrong because all components already transitioned during delivery phase. Option C is Correct: For transition or closing the program we have to get approval from the steering committee.The program closure phase includes program activities necessary to transition program benefits to the sustaining organization and formally close the program in a controlled manner. During program transition, the program steering committee is consulted to determine whether: (a) the program has met all of the desired benefits and that all transition work has been performed within the component transition, or (b) there is another program or sustaining activity that will oversee the ongoing benefits for which this program was chartered. Reference is Standard for program management Page# 97. Obtain authorization(s) and approval(s) through stage gate reviews by presenting the program status to governance authorities in order to proceed to the next phase of the program. Examination Content Outline Domain 5/Task 3. Obtain stakeholder approval for program closure in order to initiate close-out/transition activities. Examination Content Outline Domain2 / Task 31, 32 and 33.

text: You organization had been awarded a construction of a new airport in your city. You are the program manager of that program. choices.text: Escalate to the Program governance board.
Write a recommendation to close that project.
Do the impact analysis to know the effect of closing that project on other components of program.

explanation: Correct answer is C: A- is wrong because the program manager will not escalate any things without recommendations. And maybe the matter under the authority of the program manager, that doesn't need escalation. B- is wrong, the program manager didn't decide yet that the program will be recommended for closing. C- is correct: There is no any decision for closing the project yet. The program manager has to analyze the impact of misalignment issue and the closing project risk on the program.Maybe the program manager can realign the project or maybe escalates a recommendation to the program governance board for closing the project.

text: Which of the following options contain the direction of the program?

choices.text: Program management plan and roadmap.
Program business case.
Program Roadmap.
Program management plan.

explanation: Correct answer is A: Programs often have a significant level of uncertainty. While the program management plan and program roadmap may document the intended direction and benefits of the program. SPM Page#95

text: Your organization had been awarded a construction of a new industrial city. You are the program manager of this program. choices.text: Program formulation activities.
Program Benefits identification activities.

explanation: Correct answer is D: Developing business cases and the potential initiation of new projects or programs to respond to operational issues with the deployed product, service, or capability is being supported or public acceptance/reaction to the improvement or to legislative changes; political, economic, and socioeconomic changes; cultural shifts; or logistics issues with a deployed product, service, capability, or results is being supported. SPM Page# 56. A- is wrong because the business case in the question not for the main program, its only for responding to operational issue with the delivery product. B- is wrong no any development for business case in the identification activities. SPM page# 46. C- is wrong no any development of business cases in the transition activities. SPM Page# 54.

text: You are assigned as a program manager for a new hospital program. Now you are in the delivery phase, one of the components is completed and you want to explain to the steering committee that this component is completed. How can you do that?

choices.text: Explain to them that the closure conditions of the component are met.
Explain to them that the deliverables of the component are delivered successfully.
Explain to them that the benefits of the component are delivered.
Explain to them that the component produced the intended results in accordance with the program management plan.

explanation:
Correct answer is A: After the program components have produced deliverables and coordinated the successful delivery of their products, services, or results, these components are typically scheduled for closure or transition to operations or ongoing work. The criteria for performing these activities and the organizational expectations are documented in the governance plan. SPM Page# 97. The review of any recommendation for the transition or closure of a program component generally includes:
1- Confirming that the business case for the component has been sufficiently satisfied or that further pursuit of the component’s goals should be discontinued.
2- Ensuring appropriate program-level communications of the component’s closure to key stakeholders.
3- Ensuring component compliance with program-level quality control plans (when required).
4- Assessing organizational- or program-level lessons learned as a consequence of performance of the component in transition.
5- Confirming that all other accepted practices for project or program transition or closure have been satisfied. SPM PAGE# 77.
B, C and D are wrong because after the deliverables, result or benefits of the component are delivered successfully, will typically scheduled for closure or transition to operations or ongoing work.

text: You are a program manager of HYC program. You completed the delivery phase and now in the Closure phase that includes program activities necessary to transition program benefits to the sustaining organization and formally close the program in a controlled manner. Within the above context, which of the following is not included in program transition?

choices.text: Program resources disposition.
Program steering committee approval.
Components transition.
Transition from as-is to to-be.

explanation: Correct answer is C: Because the transition of the components done during the delivery phase. Prior to the end of the program delivery phase, all component areas are reviewed to verify that the benefits were delivered and to transition any remaining projects and sustaining activities. SPM PAGE#97. A, B and D are wrong; all are performed during program transition. During program transition, the program steering committee is consulted to determine whether: (a) the program has met all of the desired benefits and that all transition work has been performed within the component transition, or (b) there is another program or sustaining activity that will oversee the ongoing benefits for which this program was chartered. In the second instance, there may be work required to transition the resources, responsibilities, knowledge, and lessons learned to another sustaining entity. Once the transitioning activities are completed, the program manager receives approval from the sponsoring organization to formally close the program. SPM PAGE#97.

text: DSDS is a large organization in the production of steel. They want to increase the productivity by the construction of a new factory. The management assigned you as a program manager for the construction of the new factory. Now you are in a meeting with your team identifying the impacts to the program components from overruns or underruns. In which phase are you?

choices.text: Program Closing Phase.
Program Delivery Phase.
Program Planning Sub-Phase.
Program Definition Phase.

explanation:
Correct answer is B:
Typical financial management activities during the delivery phase include:
- Identifying factors that create changes to the budget baseline,
- Monitoring the environmental factors for potential impacts,
- Managing changes when they occur,
- Monitoring costs reallocation impact and results among components,
- Monitoring contract expenditures to ensure funds are disbursed in accordance with the contracts,
-Implementing earned value management (schedule performance index, cost performance index),
- Identifying impacts to the program components from overruns or underruns,
- Communicating changes to the budget baseline to the governance groups and to the auditors (at both the program and component levels), and
- Managing the expenditure on the program infrastructure to ensure costs are within expected parameters. Standard for program management SPM page# 128.

text: MANZI is a large construction company in the Middle East. You are the program manager for the construction of a new airport program. The program is complex and has 20 components. Program governance board.
OPM.
Program Business Case.

OPM provides a framework in which portfolio, program, and project management practices are integrated to achieve strategic objectives. OPM supports the coordinated practice of portfolio, program, and project management by linking portfolio, program, and project management principles and practices. OPM is employed to produce improved performance, better results and sustainable strategic benefits for organizations. SPM Page#10.
A: is wrong because.
It’s not mentioned PMO for portfolio, program or project. So how will provide framework by which the Portfolio, program and project management will be integrated.
B: is wrong because,
Program governance board can provide framework for the overall program, but not the portfolio.

text: Your organization just awarded the construction of a new seaport. During the portfolio meeting, some of the members prefer to pursuit it as a project, while other members suggest to pursuit it as program to enhance the delivery of benefits. How can the program enhance the delivery of benefits?

choices.text: By ensuring that the strategies and work plans of the program are responsively adapted to changes in the direction or strategies of the sponsoring organization.
By ensuring that the strategies and work plans of program components are responsively adapted to component outcomes, or to changes in the direction of the sponsoring organization.
By ensuring that the strategies and work plans of the program are responsively adapted to component outcomes, or to changes in the direction or strategies of the sponsoring organization.

By ensuring that the strategies and work plans of program and its components are responsively adapted to component outcomes, or to changes in the direction or strategies of the sponsoring organization.

explanation:
Correct answer is D:
The program manager has to ensure that the strategies and the plans of both program and its components are responsively adapted to the components outcomes, or to changes in the direction or strategies of the sponsoring organization.
The outcomes or outputs generated by the components of programs may be unpredictable and uncontrollable. As a consequence, programs should be managed in a way that recognizes the potential need to adapt strategies and plans during the course of a program to optimize the delivery of benefits. A primary role of the program manager is to monitor the outputs and outcomes of a program’s component activities and ensure that the program adapts appropriately to them. Program managers ensure that program components are adapted as required to meet the organization’s strategic objectives. SPM Page# 16.

text: Mark is a program manager for the construction of a new road. He is discussing with the team about the program benefits and outcomes. Program Charter.
Program Benefits register.
Program Roadmap.

Here the keyword is Visual. Depending on the nature of the program, the program roadmap is a graphical representation of the incremental benefits and provides a visual of when the return on investment may help fund the future program benefits and outcomes. SPM Page#45
We know that the program business case is a documented economic feasibility study used to establish validity of the benefits to be delivered by a program. But will not provide visual information.

text: Your company just awarded 15 projects, each project scope is “construction of a new factory”, in the same industrial city. All factories are different and all will be funded and supported by the government. All projects material will be provided from Hitachi Japan, as a preferred vendor. Now, you are a program manager of an existing program and your manager requests your proposal on; how you will manage these projects. What is the best proposal?

Will be managed as a sub program.

explanation:
Correct answer is C:
Component projects or programs that do not advance common or complementary goals; or that do not jointly contribute to the delivery of common benefits; or that are related only by common sources of support, technology, or stakeholders are often better managed as portfolios rather than as programs. SPM Page#3.
The components of your existing program are not related to the new projects. So cannot be managed as a subsidiary program under your program.
The new 15 projects are not related, so you can't manage them as a program or subsidiary program.

text: You program is designed to produce a new generation of electrical cars. While you are in the formulation sub-phase, the sponsor informs you that MeCa Company is planning to produce the same type of cars. Immediately you started the environmental analysis.Which of the following will you use?

SWOT Analysis for optimizing the program charter and program management plan.

Assumptions analysis.

text: DEGA is a large organization in the production of steel. They what to increase the productivity by the construction of a new steel factory. text: You are a program manager of the construction of a new hospital. During the execution of the program, you have identified a delay in getting resources allocated to the program components. Within the above context, what is your action?

Escalate the matter to the PMO.

Escalate the matter to the functional manager.

explanation:
Correct answer is A:
A program sponsor is an individual or a group that provides resources and support for the program and is accountable for enabling success. SPM Page#20.

text: X and Y are two programs in the same portfolio. You are the program manager of Program Y, which is not critical to the portfolio. You have a risk strategy in your program that needs a scarce resource. But this scarce resource was assigned to program X .Within the above context, what will you do?

choices.text: Call the Program manager-X and request him to inform you when the scarce resource is not scheduled in his program and change your program schedule accordingly.
Meet the program manager X for optimization of resources and need then inform the sponsor when the resource can be available to your program and plan accordingly.
Discuss with the sponsor about program X and get the guide line to do your own work and don’t think about the scarce resource.
Perform resource prioritization process.

explanation:

You have to meet the program manager of program X for optimizing the usage of the scarce resource, and inform your proposal to the sponsor to take the decision because you and program manager X are program managers under the sponsoring portfolio.

text: You are the program manager of the construction of the new airport extension in your city. Now you are in the delivery phase and one of your team informed you that many of the products and deliverables have been tested many time by the same test which lead to increase the cost. choices.text: Review the program schedule management plan.
Review the risk management plan.

It is beneficial to analyze program quality in order to evaluate it across the program with the goal of combining quality tests and inspections in order to reduce costs, where feasible. If the tests are not coordinated, products and deliverables could be tested several times throughout a program and a cost incurred for no valid reason. The quality management plan provides the quality assurance measures and quality controls that are incorporated in the program and the methods of inspection based on the program scope. SPM Page#118.
A: is wrong because the program schedule management plan establishes the criteria and the activities for developing, monitoring, and controlling the schedule. The program schedule management plan should include guidance on how changes to schedule baselines are to be coordinated and controlled across program components. SPM Page#122.
B: is wrong because risk management plan will be reviewed later to address such risks in future.

text: You are a program manager of the construction of a new tower in your city. The program contains 4 projects (project 1 up to project 4). text: You are discussing the program with an individual or a group that is required to drive changes through the organization so the operations can accommodate capabilities delivered by the program, and to secure the available positive benefits and steward the handling of negative benefits. Program Governance board.

the program sponsor is required to drive changes through the organization so that operations can accommodate capabilities delivered by the program, and to secure the available positive benefits and steward the handling of negative benefits. text: Program management office (PMO) and Program management information system (PMIS) are very important elements in the program management. choices.text: Program Governance framework.
Program management plan.
Program infrastructure.
Program information management plan.

text: You are a program manager for the construction of the infrastructure of a new Village. The organization’s vision and mission are used as input to the strategic planning cycle and are reflected throughout the strategic plan."Reference is Standard for program management page#35.

text: You are a program manager for a construction of a new power plant program. The program charter is approved, and now you officially commence the program planning sub-phase. text: You are a member in the selection committee to select the programs and projects that your organizations will pursuit next season. One of the selected programs is for socioeconomic changes. text: You are a manager of a large program. The program contains 7 projects and 3 subsidiary programs. While you are discussing the benefit register with the key stakeholders, for clear understanding of stakeholders, you should map the benefits to program components as in ----------

The benefits management plan
The program business case.

text: Which of the following is logically linking components, milestones, and high-level activities necessary to deliver program benefits?

Program Roadmap.
Program Architecture.
Program Master Schedule.

The Master schedule includes.

- activities related to stakeholder engagement

B: is wrong, because no any activities in the roadmaps .The roadmap include major milestones and decision points. The program roadmap is a chronological representation of a program’s intended direction, graphically depicting dependencies between major milestones and decision points, which reflect the linkage between the business strategy and the program work. SPM page# 36. The roadmap reflects the pace at which benefits are realized and serves as a basis for transition and integration of new capabilities. Roadmap describes evolving aspects of the program including incremental benefits delivery. SPM PAGE# 50.
C: is wrong because Program Architecture maps how the components will deliver the capabilities and outcomes. And no activities in the architecture. SPM PAGE# 50.

text: Your company had been awarded a new program. You are the program manager of that program. The stakeholders don't know why the program will be pursued and they don't have any visibility about the program. Within the above context, what is the best document will be used?

Program high level scope statement.
Program benefits register.
Program business case.

text: You are a program manager of a new hospital which is aim to improve the treatment procedures. The components have initiated to achieve the program objectives and benefits. During the evaluation of this component benefits, the stakeholders are not agreeing about the value that will be delivered from this component. choices.text: The expected levels of value that will be delivered from the tangible and intangible benefits are not clearly documented in the business case.

text: Kelly is a manager of an infrastructure program for her organization SDF Inc. During the planning meeting with the team, she is discussing a document that contains the boundaries of the program scope. Which of the following documents is she discussing?

text: One of the stakeholders submitted you a request to change some points in the program, you discussed that request with the stakeholder and you started the impact analysis of that request. You found that the request will impact the program scope, schedule, cost and benefits. You submitted the change request with the analysis to the program governance board for approval. After three days the governance board replied with approval, immediately you documented the approval in the change log. Within the above context, what will you do next?

choices.text: Update the change log.
Communicate the approval to the stakeholders.
Update the program management plan.
Update risk, schedule, cost, scope, and benefits management plans.

explanation:
Let's analyze each option based on the provided scenario:
Option A: Update the change log
Why Incorrect: The scenario explicitly states that you have already documented the approval in the change log immediately after receiving the governance board's decision. Therefore, this step has already been completed, and repeating it is unnecessary.
Option B: Communicate the approval to the stakeholders
Why Correct: After updating the change log, the next immediate action is to communicate the approval to the appropriate stakeholders. This communication ensures that all relevant parties are informed and can prepare for the next steps, which may include updating various plans and initiating the approved changes.
Option C: Update the program management plan
Why Incorrect: While updating the program management plan is necessary, it is not the immediate next step after documenting the approval in the change log. Communicating the approval to stakeholders precedes any updates to the program management plan. This sequence ensures that stakeholders are aware of the changes before the plans are formally updated.
Option D: Update risk, schedule, cost, scope, and benefits management plans
Why Incorrect: Similar to updating the program management plan, updating the specific management plans for risk, schedule, cost, scope, and benefits is also necessary. However, this action should follow after the stakeholders have been informed of the approval. Communicating the approval is a critical step to ensure all parties are aligned and aware of the changes before the detailed management plans are updated.
Conclusion:
The best answer is B. Communicate the approval to the stakeholders. This step is essential to ensure that all relevant parties are informed and can prepare for the subsequent updates to the program management plan and specific management plans, following the approved changes. This aligns with the logical sequence of actions needed to implement the approved change request effectively.

c- No! Are you really sure that this will stop the delay?
d- No! Maybe some dependencies from non ­ delayed projects will cause delays to other components. ALL projects should be reviewed NOW!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 25

text: You are managing a program which has four component projects: A, B, C and D. During the definition phase of the program, with the help of the PMO, you have defined several rules for your project managers, such as: all issues must be logged in a project issues register, with a predefined code, in order to be able to track them easily. You request that the status of those issues be reported and discussed during your weekly status meetings with the project managers. During today's meeting, project manager C reports a high severity issue which has a major impact on the delivery of a project outcome which is urgently expected at program level. During the meeting, project manager A says that he encountered a similar problem, and it took him a long time to develop a correction which works. The correction is documented. Project manager A proposes to provide the fix to project manager C. What IMMEDIATE action should be taken?

choices.text: The program manager immediately brings the meeting to a close and asks project manager C to apply the fix right away
Project Manager C reads the documentation related to the correction, and then decides whether or not to apply the fix
Project manager C applies the correction to project C with the assistance of a person from project A
The program manager spends the necessary time to understand what the similarities between projects A and C are

explanation:
a- No! This is a program review; you have many other items for today; please go on with the meeting
b- Correct! Project manager C should first carefully read the existing documentation before deciding to apply it or not
c- No! Project manager C should first read the documentation before applying it
d- No! This may take too much time, and is not very productive.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 27

text: Embracing the PM/ Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct is a requirement for PMP® and PgMP® certifications. The code specifies the behavior that project and program managers should have for themselves and the behavior they can expect from other project and program management practitioners. From the following lists, what are the essential obligations of the Code?

choices.text: Responsibility, respect, fairness, accountability
Responsibility, respect, fairness, honesty
Responsibility, leadership, fairness, honesty
Responsibility, leadership, power, honesty

explanation:
No! Accountability only means responsibility for a specific activity. It is often used in matrix­ based charts of human resource management, especially the Responsibility Assignment Matrix or RACI table, to assign responsibility for a specific activity to one person
b- Correct!
c- No! Leadership is not part of the code but responsibility is.
d- No! Power is much too focused on the practitioner and is somewhat pejorative in this context.
The standard, section 1.1 and PM/ Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

text: Company XYZ has decided to launch a program which has a strategic position in the company portfolio. A high number of change requests are expected to impact the program, and your company has decided to have a dedicated change manager for the program. You are the change manager for the program. In your position, you review all change requests, and recommend accepting or rejecting them. Your main focus is on reviewing changes on scope, but also on time, quality, costs, risks, contracts and rewards. Which DOCUMENT will you base your decisions upon?

choices.text: The program scope statement
The program scope management plan
The change management plan
The program management plan

explanation:
a- No! The correct answer is the 'change management plan'
b- No! The correct answer is the 'change management plan'
c- Correct! In order to correctly manage changes, you base your decisions upon the change management plan which should detail rules for accepting or rejecting changes. The change management plan Is an output from the Program change management planning activity
d- No! The correct answer is the 'change management plan'.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 28 and standard, section 8.1.2.1

text: Which artifact contains component TRANSITION CRITERIA related to organizational expectations?

choices.text: Benefits management plan
Component management plan
Governance plan
Delivery management plan

explanation: The standard, section 7.1.3.3

text: Once the transitioning activities are completed, WHO provides the authorization to formally close the program?

choices.text: The Customer
The program manager
The portfolio manager
The sponsoring organization

explanation: The standard, section 7.1.4

text: The request to CLOSE a program component and then to ACCEPT the request is done by:

choices.text: The project manager and the program manager
The program manager and the steering committee
The project manager and the steering committee
The customer and the program manager

explanation: The standard, section 7.2.2.2

text: What is a condition to PREMATURELY CLOSE the program?

choices.text: The charter is fulfilled
Expected benefits will be realized
Customer is unhappy
Expected benefits cannot be achieved

explanation: The standard, section 7.2.2.5

text: Successful completion of the program is judged against:

choices.text: The approved business case, actual program outcomes, and the current goals and strategic objectives of the organization
The approved business case, the customer dissatisfaction, and sponsor expectations
The customer dissatisfaction, the money spent and the sponsor recommendation
The program roadmap, the current goals of the organization, and the sustainment activities

explanation: The standard, section 7.2.2.5

text: A program may be closed under various conditions. Among the following choices, which one is NOT a condition to close the program?

choices.text: The program has been cancelled
The sponsoring organization has approved the program closure
All program objectives have not been achieved yet
The program has become unnecessary

explanation:
a- Wrong! The program has been cancelled, so now it may be closed
b- Wrong! The sponsoring organization has approved program closure, so now it should be closed
c- Correct! All program objectives have not been achieved yet, so keep the program open!
d- Wrong answer! The program has become unnecessary. so it may be closed.
The standard, sections 7.2.2.5 and 8.3

text: You are the program manager of a new line of breakfast cereals to be sold worldwide. The program is organized in several projects, one per line of products which ore each adapted to their targeted market. This year, you have successfully completed the commercial launch of a number of new products. Your governance board asks you to initiate close-out activities related to these projects so that operations can start working. Among the following reasons, which one is NOT a typical reason to invoke the "Program closure "activities?

choices.text: Only one out of several projects released its products onto the market
Several projects released their products onto the market
The new product lines have been released according to the benefit plans, and the governance board needs a formal sign-off from the operations
You have not fully convinced the board that benefits will be realized, but lessons learned have been thoroughly collected and documented

explanation:
a- No! The "Program closure" activities are invoked each time (non-) project activities are closed. For instance, component resource disposition and lessons learned need to be evaluated by the program manager
b- No! The "Program closure" activities are invoked each time (non-) project activities are closed. For instance, component resource disposition and lessons learned need to be evaluated by the program manager
c- No! This is an essential reason to invoke the "Program closure" activities. For instance, component resource disposition and lessons learned need to be evaluated by the program manager
d- Correct! You have to first convince your governance board that benefits will be achieved, before asking for program close out. Gathering lessons learned is neither a valid nor typical reason to invoke "Program closure" activities.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Closing the program - Task 32 and standard, section 7.2.2.5

text: You are the program manager of a new line of breakfast cereals to be sold worldwide. The program is organized in several projects, one per line of products which ore each adapted to their targeted market. This year, you have successfully completed the commercial launch of a number of new products. Your governance board asks you to initiate close-out activities related to these projects so that the operations can start working. Program performance has been analyzed and proven to be high, and according to the survey of the stakeholders' opinion, they seem to be very satisfied. Among the following choices, which one is NOT a probable end of this program?

choices.text: The program has performed satisfactorily and is fully closed
The program is transitioned to the operations
The program is cancelled
The program has partially realized benefits and you will have to propose new benefits to the governance board

explanation:
a- No! This is probable because benefits have been delivered satisfactorily
b- No! This is probable because benefits have been delivered satisfactorily
c- Correct! Benefits are delivered and stakeholders are satisfied (see text) so why cancel the program?
d- No! Stakeholders may ask you to close some activities. After this. they may come back with more requests that you will have to take into account for potential new benefits.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Closing the program - Task 31 and standard, section 7.2.2.5

text: Program X hos three component projects: A, B and C. All three component projects have been closed with the agreement of the steering committee. One month later, the program is still not closed. Generally, the final decision to close a program is under the sponsor's responsibility. What is the MOST probable cause for NOT closing program X?

choices.text: Not all of the expected benefits have been realized
The program closure recommendation was not formulated by the steering committee
The steering committee has been disbanded
The program sponsor has left the organization

explanation:
a- No! All expected benefits may not occur before the program ends
b- Correct answer! This Is the most probable cause for not closing the program
c- Wrong answer! It may be true, but it is not the most probable cause for not closing the program
d- No! That may be the case, but it is not a valid reason not to close the program!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Closing the program - Task 32 and standard, section 6.2.2

text: A program is made up of a number of projects or discrete components. These components mainly consist of activities organized to produce specific deliverables. Aggregation of these deliverables at the program level serves the strategic benefits of the performing organization. Program management targets the global optimization of its resources. This needs a specific management effort. Among the following choices, which one BEST describes this management effort?

choices.text: The management effort of a program is only made by the program manager
The management effort is ultimately the responsibility of the PMO
The management effort often resides outside the scope of the discrete components
The management effort always requires a specific infrastructure

explanation:
No! It is mainly a joint effort between project managers and the program manager
b- No! The PMO assists the program manager in the program's day-to-day activity. The program manager is ultimately in charge of management
c- Correct! This refers to 'other program, related activities' d- Not always! A periodic program review and informal day-to­ day synchronization of contacts may be sufficient in certain cases to implement the management effort.
The standard, section 1.2

text: Program X hos three component projects: A, B a n d C. As of today, projects A and B are closed, but project C is due to close in one month. Three months later, the program remains open. The steering committee requests that the program be closed as soon as possible. What is the MOST probable cause for the steering committee to ask for the closure of program X?

choices.text: Program governance does not recommend the program closure
All contracts are not formally closed
The program has been cancelled
All component projects are not formally closed

explanation:
a- No! Program governance has requested that the program be closed!
b- No! All contracts must be closed before formal program closure, but this is not the most probable cause
c- Correct answer! Among all options, this must be the most probable cause
d- No! The text says that two projects are closed and project C is due to close in one month. Three months later, there is a high probability that the program will be cancelled!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Closing the program - Task 32 and standard, section 7.2.2.5

text: What is NOT true concerning program benefits?

choices.text: Benefits are the gains and assets realized by the organization and other stakeholders as the result of outcomes delivered by the program
Program benefits management do not consider negative impact but rather concentrates on maximizing positive benefits
A benefit may be realized after program closure
Program benefits management continually aligns benefits with the organization's goals and objectives

explanation: minimizing negative impacts is as important as realizing the benefits: and should be managed, measured and properly communicated to affected stakeholders The standard, section 4

text: What are the 5 phases of program benefits management?

choices.text: Identification, analysis and planning, delivery, transition, sustainment
Assessment, analysis and planning, delivery, transition, sustainment
Identification, analysis and planning, execution, transition, sustainment
Identification, analysis and planning, delivery, transition, closure

explanation: The standard, section 4

text: What is NOT included in a typical benefit register?

choices.text: KPls and thresholds for achieving the benefit
Risk assessment for achieving the benefit
Target dates and milestones for benefits achievement
Change Log for non-benefits achievement

explanation: The standard, section 4.1.1

text: What is TRUE concerning the costs to realize benefits after program closeout?

choices.text: There are no additional costs because the program is closed
Operational costs may be needed to sustain benefits
There are no additional costs because benefits are always higher than costs after program closure
There are no additional costs for intangible benefits as they cannot be measured

explanation: The standard, section 4.2

text: What is the MAIN purpose of an effective governance when dealing with benefits delivery?

choices.text: To control and sign off the benefits
To authorize, oversight and close components
To adapt program resources to program pace
To align the program with the organization's strategy

explanation: The standard, section 4.3.2

text: You have managed a program and all planned benefits have been realized when the program ends. At the start of the program, you developed the benefits management plan which was the baseline for the management of benefits. The board wants to ensure that the program delivered the full benefits for which it was created. At the end of the program, benefits should Al WAYS be compared against those promised in:

choices.text: The benefits management plan
The program charter
The program business case
The portfolio objectives

explanation:
a- No! The benefits management plan describes when and how planned benefits will be realized
b- No! The program charter itself is based upon the business case. The business case is an input to the Program formulation sub phase, and the charter is an output from this sub phase
c- Correct! Expected benefits are derived from the program business case and must remain in line with that business case until the end of the program
d- No! Portfolio objectives do not describe planned program benefits.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Benefits Management - Task 1 and standard, section 7.2.2.5

text: The main purpose of a program is to realize benefits that are aligned with a company's strategic objectives. Identified benefits may or may not be easily measurable, but benefits should be defined with a clear notion of improvement that can be tracked and analyzed. As an example, a program benefit for a commercial company could be identified as 'bigger profits'. From the list of options, which one is LEAST clearly stated as a benefit?

choices.text: Increased market share
Lower manufacturing costs
Faster product delivery
Better administrative support

explanation:
a- Wrong answer! 'Increased market share' is a benefit which can be measured and tracked
b- Wrong answer! 'Lower manufacturing costs' is a benefit which can be measured and tracked
c- Wrong answer! 'Faster product delivery' is a benefit which can be measured and tracked
d- Correct! 'Better administrative support' does not mean that much. It will actually be difficult to track and analyze. You need to be more specific. Other answers can be tracked and analyzed.
The standard, section 4 introduction

text: You manage program X which is composed of four projects: A, B, C and D. From the beginning of your program, you have been extremely sensitive to the fact that program outcomes must generate benefits which are in line with the strategic objectives of your company. The program is well underway, but you realize that several opportunities have emerged that your program could take advantage of. You believe that with a few more resources added into the component projects, more benefits could be generated. You think about what you should do in order to seize the opportunities for your program. What will be the LEAST useful action to take?

choices.text: You start interviewing new people with the objective of increasing the size of your project teams
You talk to your sponsor about these opportunities in order to have his position
You update the benefits management plan and distribute it to all key stakeholders for advice
You ask that the business case of your program be updated and re-evaluated with the new opportunities

explanation:
a- Correct answer! This Is the worst option. Much too early!
b- No! This is a valid action. It is always good to inform, and get advice from your sponsor
c- No! This is a valid action. It is always good to inform, and get advice from key stakeholders
d- No! This is a valid action. In fact, the business case of your program will need to be updated and validated with the new opportunities, before deciding to proceed or not.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Benefits Management - Task 2

text: You manage program X which is composed of four projects: A B, C and D. From the beginning of your program, you have been extremely sensitive to the fact that program outcomes must generate benefits which are in line' with the strategic objectives of your company. The program is well underway, but you realize that several opportunities have emerged that your program could take advantage of. You believe that with a few more resources added into the component projects, more benefits could be generated. You think about what you should do in order to seize the opportunities for your program. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: You start interviewing new people with the objective of increasing the size of your project teams
You tell your sponsor that your program will be updated to seize these opportunities
You inform key stakeholders that your program will include these opportunities
You ask that the business case of your program be updated and re-evaluated with the new opportunities

explanation:
a- No! You are going too fast! You don't yet have the agreement to get new people
b- No! You are going too fast! You should discuss it with your sponsor, but don't tell them yet that your program will be updated; it's too soon!
c- No! This is too early. You may inform key stakeholders about the possibility of including these opportunities, but it is only a possibility
d- Correct answer! This Is the best action to take. The business case of your program will need to be updated and validated with the new opportunities, before deciding to proceed or not.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Benefits Management - Task 2

text: A program is made up of a number of projects or discrete components. These components mainly consist of activities organized to produce specific deliverables. Aggregation of these deliverables at the program level serves the strategic benefits of the performing organization. Program management targets the definition and production of strategic benefits. According to the following choices, which one BEST describes how the discrete outcomes produced by the projects will be organized at the program level?

choices.text: The unitary deliverables produced by all discrete components should have a one-to-one relationship with the benefits of the program. Then, it is easy to justify the budget for each of them
Each project outcome is targeted in order to be directly transitioned to the operations
The interdependent components are integrated, controlled and monitored in order to deliver program's strategic benefits
All the unitary deliverables produced by the discrete components will be justified in front of the SAME business objective as their hosting portfolio

explanation:
No! High level benefits often aggregate discrete components deliverables, and benefits are far less numerous than deliverables
b- No! Not necessarily. For example, a validation process could be an essential requirement to qualify products before transition. However, this process is not transitioned to operations that only care about the results of the final qualification report
c- Correct!
d- Not necessarily! Deliverables may target several different business objectives from the same portfolio.
The standard, section 1.3

text: You work for construction company ABC for which you have been managing a program over the last four years. The main product generated by the program is a hospital which will bring lots of benefits to the community. According to the plan, most benefits will occur only after the program is completed. You are currently in the closure phase of the program. In order to request formal closure acceptance from the program steering committee, you prepare the program transition plan. The steering committee wants to understand what type of guarantee will be included in the transition plan in order to make sure that benefits will be sustained when the hospital is operational. What type of guarantee is NOT related to benefits sustainment?

choices.text: The Customer has an appropriate support organization for the hospital
Company ABC support organization is well trained to understand hospital support requirements
Company ABC support organization understands when and how updates should be made to the hospital
Company ABC program resources are properly redeployed when the program is over

explanation:
a- No! There should be an appropriate customer support organization at transition time
b- No! Support staff must be well trained at transition time
c- No! Support staff must be able to understand what the planned changes to the product are in order to make sure that the Customer will be able to support the updated product
d- Correct answer! Redeployment of program resources is not related to benefits sustainment.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Benefits Management - Task 8 and standard, section 4.5

text: Why is it preferable to focus on the notion of stakeholder engagement rather than stakeholder management?

choices.text: Because engagement means "to have a direct managerial relationship", which is often the case between the program manager and a stakeholder
They are basically the same notions, but as there is no stakeholder management plan, the word "engagement" is better
People have a tendency to resist direct management, and most of the program stakeholders do not have a hierarchical affiliation with the program manager
Because most of the time it is enough to just engage with the stakeholders in order to gain their support. and nothing more

explanation: The standard, section 5

text: What is the primary goal of stakeholder engagement?

choices.text: To gain and maintain stakeholder buy-in for the program's objectives, benefits, and outcomes
To keep them aware of the program progress
To obtain from the stakeholders a formal approval of the program's benefits
To have them elaborate and approve the stakeholder engagement plan

explanation: The standard, section 5

text: What is a typical composition of a program steering committee?

choices.text: Sponsor, business owner, portfolio manager, key senior managers, program manager
Sponsor, PMO director, key senior managers, program manager
Sponsor. business owner, project managers, key senior managers, program manager
Sponsor. business owner, portfolio manager, key senior managers, financial VP

explanation:
The program manager is NOT a member of the steering committee.
The standard, section 5

text: What is NOT the purpose of the stakeholder register?

choices.text: To systematically identify all key stakeholders
To collect emerging stakeholders
To easily report, distribute program deliverables, and provide formal and informal communications
To contain and distribute confidential information

explanation: The standard, section 5.1

text: What is the primary role of the program sponsor?

choices.text: The program sponsor is accountable for the program success
The program sponsor is accountable for enabling the program success
The program sponsor is responsible to achieve program objectives
The program sponsor provides only financial resources to the program

explanation: The standard, section 5.1

text: You are managing a program which is composed of three projects: A B and C. The three projects all work with different subcontractors, but they also have the same subcontractor X in common. Project managers A and B have no problem with subcontractor X, but you are aware that project manager C and subcontractor X have difficulties in their relations, and that the work climate tends to be deteriorated as a result. Project manager C h a s already spent a lot of time with you explaining the situation. One day you receive a phone call from subcontractor X who complains about project manager C's attitude towards him. Subcontractor X plays a key role in the program and you do not want him to leave! What is the BEST action you should take to handle the situation?

choices.text: Call a meeting between subcontractor X and yourself
Discuss the problem with project manager C in order to understand the situation better, and then decide whether or not to talk to subcontractor X
Call a meeting between project manager C, subcontractor X and yourself
Call a meeting between project managers A B and C, subcontractor X and yourself

explanation:
a- No! You need to involve project manager C as well, in order to make sure that all aspects of the problem will be discussed
b- No! Project manager C has already spent a lot of time explaining things to you!
c- Correct! The best attitude is to have a three-party meeting with project manager C, subcontractor X and you in order to take corrective actions. Project manager C has already spent a lot of time with you regarding this problem, so you are well aware of the situation
d- No! You do not want project managers A and B to be involved in the discussion which only concerns project C.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 5

text: You manage the PMO of a large program in your company. You understand that the main purpose of the PMO is to support and help the program manager to make the program a success. There ore various types of PMO, depending on the need of the organization. Some PMOs provide mainly administrative support; some may have more responsibilities such as providing expertise in certain critical areas of the program. There are some characteristics which ore common to any type of PMO, as far as program support is concerned. What is a COMMON characteristic of all program PMOs?

choices.text: The PMO is accountable for the success of the program
The PMO is a member of the steering committee
The PMO is responsible for assigning component project managers of your program
The PMO is a program stakeholder

explanation:
a- No! The PMO is not accountable for program success, but the program sponsor is
b- No! In most cases, the PMO is not a member of the steering committee although they could be on some programs
c- No! The PMO is not responsible for assigning project managers
d- Correct! As an entity, the PMO Is a stakeholder of the program.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 1 and standard, section 5.1

text: You are managing a program in a construction company. You know that many stakeholders will be impacted by the results of the program. You have performed an in-depth analysis of the stakeholders and you have developed the stakeholder engagement plan. Key stakeholders have been identified and recorded in the stakeholder register. A detailed communication plan specifying key meeting dates has been distributed to all stakeholders. Your program is progressing well, but your project managers report the fact that more and more key stakeholders do not show up at key meetings. Your project managers do not know if this non-attendance is really impacting their projects or not. You realize that, in the stakeholder engagement plan, certain information is missing with regard to stakeholder engagement in program activities. What did you forget?

choices.text: You did not develop stakeholder metrics in order to help track stakeholder attendance at key meetings, and identify potential risks caused by their non-participation
You developed stakeholder metrics but you did not identify who the key stakeholders are, and what their expectations are
You did not develop a stakeholder register with the list of key stakeholders and their expectations
You did not communicate to key stakeholders the fact that they should attend those meetings

explanation:
a- Correct! The fact that your project managers do not know If the non-attendance of key stakeholders is impacting their projects means that you forgot to develop adequate stakeholder metrics
b- No! The text says that you have performed an in-depth stakeholder analysis
c- No! The text says that you have performed an in-depth stakeholder analysis
d- No! A detailed communication plan has been established and distributed.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 5

text: You are leading the definition phase of a new program for your company. A list of key stakeholders has been established, and you now want to understand what their attitude is with regard to the program and you also want to build a preliminary strategy to manage them. Many stakeholders come from the same business unit of your organization. You have started to interview some of them, but you find out that this is very time consuming. You think about other possible methods you could use to speed up gathering information from this specific group of stakeholders. Among the following tools or methods, which one should be MOST efficient to collect information regarding stakeholders' attitude towards the program?

choices.text: Questionnaires and surveys
Stakeholder checklists
Interviews
Focus groups

explanation:
a- Wrong answer! This method may take a lot of time and may not be the most efficient
b- Wrong answer! This method may take a lot of time and may not be the most efficient. Also, existing checklists may not be appropriate for your needs
c- Wrong answer! You have already started to interview some of them and you are looking for a more efficient too1. Individual interviews usually take a lot of time!
d- Correct answer! Focus groups with open-ended questions sessions allow participants to Interact with each other. Where groups are concerned, focus groups are known to be more efficient than other methods. The text specifies that 'Many stakeholders come from the same business unit'.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 2 and standard, section 5.2

text: Even though a program may be composed of a number of different projects; program and project domains are really different. Among the possible choices below, which one is WRONG when describing their relationships?

choices.text: The interactions between a program and its projects tend to be iterative and cyclical
At the beginning of the program, the program identifies candidate projects, defines objectives and dates
When the program is in the execution phase, the project reports to the program for monitoring and controlling purposes
When the program is in the closing phase, all projects are scheduled to terminate at the same time

explanation:
a- No! This is correct; at the beginning, the program directs the projects and afterwards, projects update performance and status, and based on this information, the program redirects them
b- No! This is true; the program is in charge of giving clear goals to projects.
c­ -No! This is especially true in big programs
d- Correct answer! In fact, the program may delver Incremental benefits. In this case, projects providing early benefits may be terminated while some others are still being executed.
The standard, section 1.4.3

text: The PM/ Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct describes what is expected from program and project management practitioners. PMI has identified four sections in that code: Responsibility, Respect. Fairness and Honesty. You are a program manager and you want to develop and foster good relationships with your stakeholders, internal and external to your organization. As a practitioner in the global project management community, what is NOT an appropriate attitude to show towards your stakeholders?

choices.text: You conduct yourself in a professional manner, even when it is not reciprocated
You take ownership for the errors you make
You make decisions and take actions only in the best interest of your program
You only file ethics complaints when they are substantiated by facts

explanation:
a- No! This is valid behavior (Respect section 3.2.4)
b- No! This is valid behavior (Responsibility section 2.2.4)
c- Correct answer! You should not ALWAYS make decisions only based on the interest of your program. The code says that 'you should make decisions and take actions based on society, public safety and the environment' (Responsibility section 2.2.1)
d- No! This is a valid behavior {Responsibility section 2.3.4).
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 7 and PM/ Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

text: Program Governance is the performance domain that:

choices.text: Enables and performs program decision making, establishes status reports of the program, but takes no program related decisions
Enables and performs program decision making, establishes practices to support the program, and develops project oversight
Enables and performs project decision making, establishes practices to support the program, and maintains program oversight
Enables and performs program decision making, establishes practices to support the program, and maintains program oversight

explanation: Program decision making and NOT project decision making! The standard. section 6

text: What systems and methods are usually NOT part of a program governance plan?

choices.text: Definitions of roles and responsibilities
Project governance plans
Planned governance meetings such as health checks, phase gate reviews, and audits
Benefits, performance metrics, and measurement

explanation: The standard. section 6.1.1

text: What is NOT the purpose of the Program charter?

choices.text: To authorize the project management team to use organizational resources in order to pursue projects related to the program
To authorize the program management team to use organizational resources in order to pursue the program
To link the program to the organization's strategy
To link the program to its business case

explanation: The standard. section 6.1.3

text: When dealing with governance, the escalation processes for managing risks or issues typically operate at:

choices.text: Individual, deliverable, benefit, and strategic levels
Inside the program, between component teams

Both b- and c-

Core quality management processes may be identified at component level

text: In order to assess program performance against expected outcomes and planned benefits, the program manager will prepare phase-gate reviews to be approved by the steering committee.
