choices.text: Impose a date for the audit
Document deviations from the approved processes
Document decisions that show how the program is managed
Follow the organization's approved processes for program management

explanation:
a- Correct answer! Imposing an audit date Is rarely the best option!
b- Wrong answer! Before the audit. the program manager should document any deviation from the approved processes
c- Wrong answer! For the audit, the program manager should document decisions that show how the program is managed
d- Wrong answer! The program manager must follow the organization's approved processes for program management (including processes for audit management!).
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 2 and standard. section 6.1.1.2 (planned governance meetings)

text: You are the program manager of a new line of breakfast cereals to be sold worldwide. The program is organized as several projects, one per line of products which are adapted to their targeted markets. This year, you have successfully completed the commercial launch of a number of new products. You are asked by the governance board to initiate close-out activities related to these projects so that operations can start. When performing program closure, an important activity is documenting the lessons learned. According to the following statements, what BEST describes this activity from the governance board point of view?

choices.text: This is used by governance board members to refine their opinion of the program's performance
This is used by governance board members to compare your program with other programs in progress which are similar to yours
This is used by governance board members to compare your program with other programs in progress which are different from yours
This helps to support organizational best practices

explanation:
a- No! The performance report that has been provided BEFORE program closure initiation is a better document for that. and should already contain all the performance information. Lessons learned are then extracted from the final performance report
b- No! The performance report that has been provided BEFORE program closure initiation is a better document for that
c- No! The performance report that has been provided BEFORE program closure initiation is a better document for that
d- Correct! This is the goal of this activity.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 8, and standard, section 7.2.2.5 and section 8.2.4.1

text: A uniform set of program and project standards needs to be developed at program level in order to enforce efficiency and consistency throughout the program. According to the following options, which one MOST accurately describes these standards?

choices.text: These standards shall be based on organizational standards only
These standards shall be based on industry standards only
These standards shall be based on both industry and organizational standards only
These standards shall be based on PMI® standards only

explanation:
a- No! Industry based standards can also be considered
b- No! Organizational standards can also be considered. These standards are defined internally to the organization and are a result of organizational assets that may be applicable to this program
c- Correct! Industry and organizational standards already include PMI® standards
d- No! Even if PMI® standards are good practices. they may not fully reflect the organizational and industry standards that may be applicable to this program. Therefore. they cannot be the only source of applicable standards.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 1

text: There are several factors that may influence benefit realization: quality, stakeholders' engagement, financial sourcing, market conditions, the political climate, etc. Another important factor is related to risks. As a program manager, you have to regularly provide updated information related to program risks to your governance board. Among the following choices, what BEST describes this updated information?

choices.text: It provides all details on project risks and on component risks. It allows the governance board to make decisions based upon the severity of the risks that are affecting the program and the components
It gives the minimum but sufficient information related to existing and new risks so that the governance board can understand whether or not strategic benefits are jeopardized within this program
It mainly consists of program and project risk register updates
It mainly consists in updating the risk register and the stakeholder register

explanation:
a- No! As program manager, you have to provide PROGRAM LEVEL information to the governance board. You cannot only provide details but must also provide a proven analysis showing how risks may impact the strategic objectives of your program
b- Correct! This Is the only purpose of this document at governance board level
c- No, as program manager, you cannot provide details only but must also supply a proven analysis showing how risks may impact the strategic objectives of your program. Even if the risk register provides an exhaustive description, it does not explain how risks impact altogether the strategic benefits of your program
d- No! As program manager, you cannot only provide details but also must supply a proven analysis showing how risks may impact the strategic objectives of your program. Even if the risk register provides exhaustive descriptions, it does not explain how risks impact altogether the strategic benefits of your program.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 6

text: You are a program manager of a program to deliver exceptional benefits to the organization. The implementation of program transition and sustainment plans are started. You discover that the program may be closed early due to a shortage of funding. Within the above context, what should you do next to ensure continued funding?

choices.text: Continue in the implementation of the sustainment plan and update the benefits management plan.
Review the program’s strategic alignment, business case, and long-term benefits with the program steering committee.
Submit the IRR and NPV to the program sponsors.
Submit the CBR to the program sponsors for a common understanding of the continuous benefits realization after closing the program.

explanation:
You have to ensure that the program is still aligned with the strategic objectives and goals and ensure that the benefits will be as specified in the business case.
Program governance facilitates program funding to the degree necessary to support the approved business case. Reference is standard for program management page#72.
When the program continues, it may or may not provide additional funds to the organization accepting the benefit to cover the deferred costs of new benefits; in some cases, the organization may have to self-fund the costs. In addition, quantifiable benefits have not yet exceeded program costs in this example; program benefits are expected to exceed program costs over time, as specified in the business case. Reference is standard for program management page#48.

text: Which one of the following options can guide the program manager during the development of the program WBS?

choices.text: The contingency reserve and the program resource.
WBS should be stopped at the third level.
Decomposition stops at a level sufficient to achieve control.
Decomposing the program up to the level requested by the component managers.

explanation: Decomposition stops at the level of control required by the program manager (typically to the first one or two levels of a component). The program WBS serves as the framework for developing the program master schedule and defines the program manager’s management control points. Reference is standard for program management Page#123

text: You are a program manager of the construction of a new airport. The closing phase is started and now you are transitioning the program to the operation. You and the sponsor are concerned about the benefits realization. What should you do for a successful transition?

choices.text: Request the project managers to archive all the program documents in the organization.
Confirm that all the documents of the program including lessons learned are archived in the organization repository.
Call the components manager to get their personal information then demobilize them to their departments.
Request the component teams to collect the program documents.

explanation: For legal reasons or to support ensuing operations or other programs, there may be a need to collect program records and organize them for archiving or for use by other elements of the organization. The scope of this activity may include the collection and archiving of records and documentation from components as well. Reference is standard for program management Page#139

text: You are a program manager of new software called KKH. This program will be released to the AGK program team and software developer for the upgrade. During the closure, the sponsor and the program manager are concerned about the support after the closing of KKH. What should you do?

choices.text: Continue in the KKH program and do not close it until close AGK.
Update the exit criteria of KKH to confirm its support is included in the AGK program.
Release the resources of your program to AGK.
Develop and execute the transition plan to transfer the support to operations.

explanation: Develop the transition/integration/closure plan by defining exit criteria in order to ensure all administrative, commercial, and contractual obligations are met upon program completion. Exam content outline/Domain2/task13

text: You are a program manager of a new management system. You have concerned due to the delay in the delivery of the procurement team. The software team has many dependencies with the procurement team. The procurement team doesn’t report to you and contains 3 qualified persons only to complete their program work. What should you do next to handle this problem?

choices.text: Meet with the procurement team to transfer them to the software team and update the benefits management plan.

Review the roles and responsibilities of the procurement team in the program, define the impact on benefits delivery, ask the software project manager to meet with the procurement team to ensure dependencies are understood and that the required resources will be available.
Escalate the issue to the program steering committee and update the risk management plan.
Determine an appropriate contingency and management reserves to handle the delay and update the risk register.

explanation: You have to review and clarify the roles and responsibilities of the procurement team in the program for the required commitment, define the impact on benefits delivery, ask the software project manager to meet with the procurement team to ensure dependencies are understood and that the required resources will be available.

text: A new program contains 20 projects. The program is for the development of a management planning system for a multinational company. One of the projects is a pilot project that will be followed by many projects. During the execution of the program, new rules and regulations are issued that will change the tax. Within the above context, what should you update as a program manager?

choices.text: Program governance plan.
Program communication plan.
Benefits management plan.
Program stakeholders register.

explanation:
Due to the change in the tax, the cost and the benefits will be changed, so you have to update the benefits register and benefits management plan.
The purpose of the benefits delivery phase is to ensure that the program delivers the expected benefits, as defined in the benefits management plan. As the program is implemented, risks affecting benefits may be realized, may need to be updated, or may become obsolete; additionally, new risks and updated ones should be included in the benefits register with the associated benefits. Reference is standard for program management Page#51.

text: What should the program manager do after the initial approval from the initiatives selection committee to proceed with the program?

choices.text: Define the benefits management plan.
Define the high-level road map.
Submit the charter for approval.
Study the lessons learned from the previous program.

explanation: Establish a high-level road map with milestones and preliminary estimates in order to obtain initial validation and approval from the executive sponsor then define the high-level road map/framework in order to set a baseline for program definition, planning, and execution. Exam content outline/ Doman1/ Task1&2.

text: You are a program manager of a new system. You must reconcile data including the consultant’s hour estimates and the estimates of other resource hours. And you must arrange the cash flow analysis. Which of the following will be considered to develop the budget baseline?

choices.text: Component payment schedules.
Future interest rate increases or decreases.
Component cost estimates.
Program payment schedules

explanation: Since programs are, by definition, composed of multiple components, program budgets should include the costs for each component as well as costs for the resources to manage the program itself. The baselined program budget is the primary financial target that the program is measured against. Reference is standard for program management Page#129.

text: You are a program manager. One of the key stakeholders has requirements against the organization’s objectives. You meet with the stakeholder many times, but you can’t solve the problem. What should you do first?

choices.text: Meet with the key stakeholder again.
Meet with the program management office.
Meet with the customer to address the issue.
Meet with the program sponsor to handle the issue

explanation: The program manager manages program risks and issues and escalates critical risks and issues beyond the program manager’s control to the steering committee or Sponsor if the steering committee option is not available. Reference is standard for program management Page#83

text: You are a program manager of a new product for your organization. the program is near completion and will start the transition to operation soon. The operation manager informed you that the operation department failed to be informed in advance to receive the new production line. The operational department is disagreed to receive the production line now since the department is not ready and the staff is untrained to support the new production. What should you have done first to prevent that problem?

choices.text: Identified the Operation Manager in the program stakeholder register.
Review the transition steps in the communication management plan.
Meet the PMO and governance board to develop appropriate training for the operation area.
Develop the transition plan during the planning phase for the impacted operational area.

explanation:
Develop a transition plan to operations in order to guarantee the sustainment of products and benefits delivered by the program. Exam content outline/Domain3/Task8.
Developing a transition plan to facilitate the ongoing realization of benefits when turned over to the impacted operational areas. Reference is standard for program management Page#53.
The Benefits transition activities may include but are not limited to:- Evaluation of program and program component performance against applicable acceptance criteria, including key performance indicators; Review and evaluation of acceptance criteria applicable to delivered components or outputs; Review of operational and program process documentation; Review of training and maintenance materials (if they apply); Review of applicable contractual agreements; Assessment to determine if resulting changes have been successfully integrated; Activities related to improving acceptance of resulting changes (workshops, meetings, training, etc.); Transfer of risk(s) affecting the benefits transitioned to the receiving organization; Readiness assessment and approval by the receiving person, group, or organization; and u Disposition of all related resources. Reference is standard for program management Page#54

text: You are a program manager of a software program. A key program stakeholder is concerned about the received information of component A. Within the above context, who is responsible for reviewing and assuring that the communications management plan is providing adequate information to the stakeholder?

choices.text: Stakeholder manager
Component manager
Program manager
Program sponsor

explanation:
Reviewing and approving the plans are the responsibility of the program governance board. The program sponsor is a member or Chairperson of the board.
Before sending the program communication plan for approval, you have to review and assure that the communications management plan is providing adequate information to the stakeholder.
The program communications management plan is the component of the program management plan that describes how, when, and by whom the information will be administered and disseminated. Communication requirements should be clearly defined to facilitate the transfer of information between the program and its components and from the program to the appropriate stakeholders with the appropriate content and delivery methods. Reference is standard for program management Page#112.

text: During the strategic planning of the organization, the senior executive manager is discussing the mission and vision of the organization to create a strategic plan to achieve the vision. What should the program manager do to establish a program by using the organization’s vision?

choices.text: Fulfill the strategic objectives by defining the program and program’s components.
Fulfill the strategic objectives by identifying the program benefits.
By selection session to select and prioritize the program’s components.
Define the program’s roadmap with highlight the benefits of each program component.

explanation:
You have to develop a high-level roadmap to obtain initial validation and approval for the program.
Establish a high-level road map with milestones and preliminary estimates in order to obtain initial validation and approval from the executive sponsor. Exam content outline domain1/task2.
The program roadmap is a chronological representation of a program’s intended direction, graphically depicting dependencies between major milestones and decision points, which reflects the linkage between the business strategy and the program work.

text: Your program budget is $1500M and is expected to last one year. Now the program is 30% complete and has spent $490M. The program is planned to be 40% now. What is the CPI for the program?

Program risk register.
Project risk register.
Program risk management plan.

text: Your program has an unexpected risk. The stakeholders want to assign a risk response team for mitigation plan preparation. The stakeholders consider this risk as a critical risk but ultimately you found that the risk is a very low risk and can be ignored. Within the above context, what should you recommend to stakeholders to handle that type of situation in the future?

choices.text: Develop a central on demand team.
Accept the risk.
Ask for an expert opinion.
Check the risk severity matrix.

explanation:
A is wrong because of no central on-demand team for risk management.
B is wrong because you must assess the risk then prioritize by probability and impact matrix before assigning a response.
C is wrong because risk prioritization needs risk probability and impact matrix (risk severity matrix).
D is correct because risk prioritization by using risk probability and impact matrix (risk severity matrix).

text: A global management system for a petroleum company is being delivered by the program team to provide an easy way to access the system across the world. A new regulation has been applied in some countries that will affect the privacy of the system. The senior executive manager of the company requests an independent auditor to validate the compliance with the new regulation. This is additional work and is not included in the roadmap and the plan. Within the above context, what should the program manager do now?

choices.text: Agree to accept the risk of the audit and continue the program without any modification.
Analyze and assess the impact of that audit and the potential remediation on the program.
Discuss the matter with the senior executive manager to stop the audit.
Decrease the scope of some projects of the program.

explanation:
A is wrong. Because you have to assess the impact of any change before doing any action.
B is correct. In the first action, you have to access and analyze the impact on the program then do the next step.
C is wrong. Because you can not go to the executive manager without any analysis and recommendations to cancel the audit.
D is wrong. Because it is not easy to take a decision of decreasing the scope to avoid the impact of the additional work.

text: A financial program is completed, and the benefits are realized. What should the program manager do before the execution of the transition and/or closing the program?

Develop and update the program final report.

Before executing the transition and closing activities of the program, we have to obtain stakeholder approval for program closure in order to initiate close-out activities. Exam content outline /domain2/ task32 and 33.
Other options are parts of the closure activities.

text: You are a program manager of a construction program. You are concerned that the program cannot achieve the expected benefits. Within the above context, what should you do to handle that concern?

Review the charter and business case with the stakeholders.

Accelerate the pending requests.
Submit a request to start program closure.

If the cost of the output is lower than originally planned, the program manager may present an opportunity to the program sponsor for additional products that would be acquired later in the program. Reference is Standard for program management page#129.
is wrong: As the program nears completion, the program budget is closed, and the final financial reports are communicated in accordance with the program communications management plan. Any unspent monies are returned to the funding organization not receiving organization.
is wrong: Has no meaning.

choices.text: Escalate this issue to the program steering committee.
Request additional funds from the accountant manager.
Meet the key stakeholders to advise the sponsor to close the program.

Now you have an issue out of your control, you have to escalate to the governance board to review and give recommendations to the sponsor.
The program manager manages program risks and issues and escalates critical risks and issues beyond his control to the steering committee. Reference is Standard for program management page#83.

text: What is the difference between the portfolio and the program?

choices.text: The portfolio outcomes are interdependent.

In portfolios, the organization’s strategic plan and business cycle dictate the start or end of specific investments, and these investments may serve widely divergent objectives. And temporary endeavors associated with projects. So, the portfolio is independent. Reference is the standard for program management Page # 27.

text: You have been assigned as a program manager for an ongoing multi-year program. The stakeholders do not understand how the program will assist the organization in the achievement of the strategic objectives. Within the above context, what will you present to the stakeholders to handle their concerns?

choices.text: Present business roadmap.
Present Program charter.
Present risk management plan.
Present Program scope assessment results

explanation:
The high-level scope statement is a result of the program scope assessment.
The program manager cannot give the charter to any stakeholder since it contains costs, issues, risks and stakeholder considerations, etc. The scope statement is the description of the program scope, major deliverables, assumptions, and constraints. The program scope statement documents the entire scope. It describes, in detail, the work required to create the program deliverables. It also provides a common understanding of the program scope among all stakeholders.

text: You are a program manager of a new hospital program. One of the components has many issues. During the meeting with that component manager, you suggested many resolutions. choices.text: Create and implement an immediate ive action plan with the component manager and train him on decision-making.
Help the component manager during the issues resolution meeting to finish the issues rapidly.
Escalate the issues to the program steering committee to assign an experienced component manager.
Request the component manager to resolve the issue as soon as possible.

explanation:
Develop an immediate corrective action plan with the component manager then coach him on the decision-making skill to avoid these types of issues in the future.
Identify and manage unresolved project-level issues by establishing a monitoring and escalation mechanism and selecting a course of action consistent with program constraints and objectives in order to achieve program benefits. Reference is exam content outline/domain2/task12.

text: You are a program manager of a new construction program. The program sponsor asks for the weekly and monthly performance report. Which of the following are tools/techniques for monitoring and controlling program performance?

choices.text: Brainstorming, SWOT, Major run chart, Lummi chart, and matrix-based charts.
The program performance index, portfolio criteria reweighting scatter, Ishikawa, and statistical sampling test.
Nominal group, Delphi technique, impact analysis, scatter diagram, and organization charts.
EVM, PMIS, performance measurement techniques, and financial reporting systems.

explanation:
Program performance reports include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met, and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. These reports generally provide current status information about what work has been accomplished (especially milestones and phase gates); what work remains to be completed; earned value; and risks, issues, and changes under consideration. Reference is the standard for program management Page #101.
Options A, B, and C contains wrong tools and techniques or are not available.

text: You are a program manager of a new construction program. The program has 13 projects, you have to assign a project manager to each project. What should you do before assigning the project managers?

choices.text: Assess the skills of project managers and match them to the needs of the projects.
Evaluate the project managers’ salaries and the program budget.
Compare the relationships of the project managers.
Ask the HR department about the qualifications and certificates of the project managers.

explanation: The selection of the project manager should be by their skills experience and the requirements of the projects. A project that is complex because of technical design issues may require a project manager with an engineering or technical background; a project that is complex because it involves many hundreds, or thousands of interconnected activities may require a project manager with extensive background and experience in project management. Reference is the standard for program management page#19

text: The high management informed you that the program must deliver a 20% reduction in customer complaints by the end of the next month. In which of the following will this expectation be documented?

choices.text: Complaints management plan
Benefits management plan.
Program quality standards.
Benefits transition plan.

explanation: Benefits are gains and assets realized by the organization and other stakeholders as the result of outcomes delivered by the program.

You and the sponsor review the final program outcome.
Present and review the business plan and benefits register with the steering.
Review the final program quality, schedule, status, and costs reports.

explanation:
The program at the end and the new members do not know their roles and responsibilities. So, options A, C, D are wrong because they cannot review the program outcomes or reports.
The sponsor is a member of the program steering committee and may be the chairperson of the committee. Here in the question isn’t mentioned that the sponsor is a member, therefore he is the chairperson of the committee. You and the sponsor have sufficient experience to review the program. The program sponsors ensure program goals and objectives are aligned with the strategic vision; Enable the delivery of benefits, and Remove barriers and obstacles to program success. Reference is standard for program management page#80.

text: You are a program manager for a financial system program. Now you are working with the sponsor, stakeholders, and governance board to develop the program’s benefits transition and sustainment plans. What should you do to develop these plans?

choices.text: Update the program benefits management plan.
Define the key metrics and measures to compare expected benefits in the benefits management plan with actual performance when benefits sustainment and transition start.
Update the benefits management plan to measure the transition and sustainment period.
Assign the responsibility of the creation of the sustainment and transition plans to an organizational executive manager.

explanation:
You have to identify the metrics and measures that will be used once the execution of transition plan and sustainment plan.
The benefits sustainment plan should be developed prior to program closure to identify the risks, processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary to ensure the continued realization of the benefits delivered. Reference is standard for program management page#55.
Verifying that the integration, transition, and closure of the program and its components meet or exceed the benefit realization criteria established to achieve the program’s strategic objectives. Reference is standard for program management page#53.
Develop a sustainment plan that identifies the processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary for the management of benefits beyond the completion of the program in order to ensure the continued realization of intended benefits. Exam content outline/domain3/task3.

text: You are the program manager of a new program. What should you do first to define the program and assess the target market and customer needs?

choices.text: Assess the target market needs with the program sponsor.
Ask the competitors to give you information about the target market.
Meet the program team to assess the target market needs.
Ask the project managers to assess the target market.

explanation:
Now you are defining a program that means the program just started the formulation sub-phase. Now there are no team, no project managers to ask or meet, so C and D are wrong. B is illogical.
A is correct: To demonstrate how the program will deliver the desired organizational benefits, the sponsor, sponsoring organization, and the program manager works closely together to: 1- Initiate studies and estimates of scope, resources, and cost; 2- Develop an initial risk assessment; and 2- Develop a program charter and roadmap. Studies of scope, resources, and cost are also performed to assess the organization’s ability to deliver the program. At this time, the candidate program is compared with other organizational initiatives to determine the priority of the program under consideration. This information serves as critical input into the creation of the business case. Reference is standard for program management page#92.

text: During an important meeting, the program manager observed that one of the component managers wants to withdraw to avoid the conflict. What should the program manager do to get more information and input from this component manager?

choices.text: Develop a motivational and reward system to encourage the team.
Request each component manager to say his ideas individually and give each one a chance to express their opinion.
Ask the component managers to exchange their offices to improve their communication skills.
Develop a solicitation management center to get ideas from them.

explanation:
You have to ask each one individually to get input from them and give them a chance to express their opinion without any interruption or conflict.
the program manager may utilize strong communication, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills to help defuse stakeholder opposition to the program and its stated benefits. Large programs with diverse stakeholders may also require facilitated negotiation sessions among stakeholders or stakeholder groups when their expectations conflict. Reference is standard for program management page#65.
options A and D will not help the program manager to get the ideas from this component manager. C is wrong because exchanging offices will not improve the communication skills and will not help the program manager to get input from this component manager.

text: The organization is implementing a new business strategy to improve the revenue. The chairman of the company wants to initiate a new program to support this strategy. Before initiating the program, the strategy should be aligned with the strategic goals of the organization. What should you do first as a program manager?

choices.text: Program risk responses.
Program schedule management plan.
Program risk threshold.
Program risk management plan.

explanation: Such a risk management strategy includes defining program risk thresholds, performing the initial program risk assessment, and developing a high-level program risk response strategy, as well as determining how risks will be communicated to strategic levels of the organization. Strategy alignment requires program risk thresholds to take into account the organization’s strategy including its risk appetite, which is an assessment of the organization’s willingness to accept and deal with risks. Reference is standard for program management page#41.

text: An organization initiated a critical program to deliver a key benefit to achieve the strategic objectives. The program manager requests a newly graduated project manager to manage a complex program component that has dependencies with other components in the program. What should the project manager do?

choices.text: Agree and request training.
Agree to gain new experience and skills and request help from other project managers.
Reject the offer, it is not ethical to accept work for which the project manager is not qualified.

explanation: He has to reject the assignment. The successful component manager uses knowledge, experience, and leadership effectively to manage the component and archive the component objectives and outputs required by the program to deliver a key benefit to the organization. It is not ethical to manage a component as an area for training or gaining skills, the component is complex and has dependencies with other projects, if the component is failed to deliver the intended outcome, the program may be subject to cancelation.

text: The program manager of program A asks the program manager of program B about the time of the benefits delivery of program B because program A benefits sustainment depends on the outcomes of program B. after one month the program manager of B informed that the program is closed. What should the program(A) manager do first?

text: A multinational company initiates a program for central advertisements and virtual training. Optimize the program management plan by identifying, reviewing, and leveling resource requirements (for example, human resources, materials, equipment, facilities, finance) in order to gain efficiencies and maximize productivity/synergies among constituent projects. text: You are a program manager of a complex program. The program is facing many issues during the execution. The stakeholders are worried about that and you need many actions to handle all issues. Stakeholder management plan.
Cause and effect diagram.
Key performance indicators

Key performance indicators and other measures that will be used to monitor program performance.
Evaluating key performance indicators related to program financials, compliance, quality, safety, and stakeholder satisfaction in order to monitor the delivery of benefits. Reference is standard for program management page#51

text: The program manager performs an initial program assessment by defining the program objectives, requirements, and risks in order to ensure program alignment with the organization’s strategic plan. Program steering committee.

text: An organization is releasing new technology. The program manager has received the program objectives and developed the program roadmap, which contains 4 projects. Approval from the program steering committee has been obtained. What will the program manager do next?

Create the program business case.
Assign the portfolio managers and program sponsor.

text: You are a program manager. You assigned a qualified project manager for one of the components. The customer rejects the project manager because of a shortage of the qualification requirements for the component. Within the above context, what should you do next to handle this issue?

If done for the entire team and against a specific standard, it reveals the skills gaps that need to be filled if a company wants to reach its strategic goals. C and D are wrong because these points have already been done before the assignment of the project manager for the first time. B will be the last action, not the next action.

text: The organization has a program by a contractor. All the components are coming to the end. Which of the following should be completed first to close the contracts?

Evaluate all contracts to ensure all conditions are met.
Perform contracts audit to review the procurement process.
Update procurement management plan.

The first point is that the terms and conditions should be met.
Program procurement closure activities are those that formally close out each agreement of the program after ensuring that all deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, that all payments have been made, and that there are no outstanding contractual issues. Reference is standard for program management page#140.

text: You are a program manager of a construction program. An unexpected disaster has happened, and the banks and all the operations are closed for five days. The program has an important payment after 3 days. What should you do first?

choices.text: Assess the impact, reassess the program risks, and select appropriate options to be presented to the steering committee.
Use the risk response plan and the planned actions.
Use the contingency reserve to accelerate the program schedule.
Meet the sponsor to select the responses.

The disaster is an unknown risk. The occurrence of unknown risk is a reason for risk reassessment to identify new risks and assess the probability and impact of the existing risks then determine appropriate responses and actions that will be presented to the governance board.
Regularly evaluate new and existing risks that impact strategic objectives in order to present an updated risk management plan to the governance board for approval. Exam content outline/domain5/Task#6

text: You are a program manager. One of the program components has been impacted by the changes in the organizational strategy. Conduct impact assessments for program changes and recommend decisions in order to obtain approval in accordance with the governance model. Exam content outline/domain2/Task 29.

text: You are a program manager of the construction of a skyscraper tower. The program contains 10 components. The program has two sponsors. The sponsors do not agree on some points regarding the tower’s marketing and advertisements. What should you do as a program manager?

choices.text: Develop the program engagement plan and the stakeholders register to get the best decision.
Develop the charter, business case and meet the CEO for approval.
Establish market analysis with your team for approval.
Meet with the two sponsors and the program governance board to discuss the market analysis and resolve the conflict.

explanation:
To resolve any conflict, you have to meet with the parties to the conflict.
When necessary, the program manager may utilize strong communication, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills to help defuse stakeholder opposition to the program and its stated benefits. Large programs with diverse stakeholders may also require facilitated negotiation sessions among stakeholders or stakeholder groups when their expectations conflict. Reference is standard for program management Page#65.

text: You are a program manager of an important program. The executive manager approves the charter. The high management is not sure of how you can deliver the program benefits successfully. Develop a high-level milestone plan using the goals and objectives of the program, applicable historical information, and other available resources (for example, work breakdown structure (WBS), scope statements, benefits realization plan) in order to align the program with the expectations of stakeholders, including sponsors. Exam content outline/domain2/task3.

text: One of the projects delivers all the expected deliverables. The project manager gets approval from the stakeholders and transitions the benefits to the receiving organization. Which of the following should the program manager do next?

Reference is standard for program management page#97.

text: You are the program manager of a risky program due to the changes in the environment of the organization. Your organization’s program management maturity level is high and has very high experience in program management. Given the history of the successful programs and projects in the organization. What should you do during planning?

choices.text: Review the benefits register, risk management plan, and strategic objectives.

Report lessons learned and best practices observed and archive to the knowledge repository in order to support future programs and organizational improvement. Exam content outline/domain2 /task 35.

text: You are a program manager. You want to improve the program’s team commitment to the objectives and goals of the program. What should you do?

choices.text: Identify the organization’s best practice with the sponsor.
Identify the organization’s best practices with the program management office.
Identify the organization’s best practice with the program stakeholders, and the program management office.
Identify the organization’s best practice with the sponsor, the program stakeholders, and the program management office.

explanation:
The best practice is one of the responsibilities of the program management office. But to improve the team commitment, you should involve them in the program activities. Therefore, develop the organization’s best practice with the program stakeholders including the sponsor, and the program management office (PMO provides professional expertise using staff highly trained in applying program governance practices to provide oversight, support, and decision-making capability to the program. The PMO role may extend to monitoring compliance to program management practices.)
Stakeholders including the sponsor can be engaged by involving them in goal setting, quality analysis reviews, or other program activities. The primary objective is to gain and maintain stakeholder buy-in for the program’s objectives, benefits, and outcomes. Reference is standard for program management page#57.
The program management office (PMO) facilitates the governance practices. It is a management structure that standardizes the program-related governance processes and facilitates the sharing of resources, methodologies, tools, and techniques. It provides professional expertise using staff highly trained in applying program governance practices to provide oversight, support, and decision-making capability to the program. The PMO role may extend to monitoring compliance to program management practices. Reference is standard for program management page#82.

B is wrong because the option doesn’t include the stakeholders.
C is wrong because the sponsor is not mentioned in the option to confirm his participation.

text: You are a program manager. Now you are in a meeting with a component project manager and the master program scheduler. Which of the following options should be included in the program master schedule?

choices.text: All project activities and all program benefits.
The activities of the program, component activities, and all other work.
Program-level activities and component projects.
Project resources and the accountability matrix.

explanation:
The program master schedule is the top-level program planning document that defines the individual component schedules and dependencies among program components (individual components and program-level activities) required to achieve the program goals. It should include those component milestones that represent output to the program or share interdependency with other components. The program master schedule should also include activities that are unique to the program including, but not limited to, activities related to stakeholder engagement, program-level risk mitigation, and program-level reviews. The program master schedule determines the timing of individual components, enables the program manager to determine when benefits will be delivered by the program, and identify external dependencies of the program. Reference is standard for program management page#121.
A and C and D are wrong because the program components are not only projects.

text: You are a program manager of a program that contains 20 projects. The program will be completed after one year. During the delivery phase, you identified many essential changes in the projects that would impact the program schedule. Within the above context, what should you do next?

Write and submit a change request for extending the program schedule.

Conduct impact assessments for program changes and recommend decisions in order to obtain approval in accordance with the governance model. Exam content outline/ domain2/Task29.
The program master schedule should also be reviewed to assess the impact of component-level changes on other components and on the program itself. There may be a need to accelerate or decelerate components within the schedule to achieve program goals.
Due to the complexity and potential long duration of programs, the program master schedule may need to be updated to include new components or remove components as a result of approved change requests to meet evolving program goals. The program roadmap should be assessed for potential revision when there is a significant change in the program master schedule. Reference is standard for program management page#136.

text: During the monitoring and controlling stage, the manager of the testing and commissioning component has informed you that budgeted hours will be increased by130%. What should you do as a program manager?

Reference is standard for program management page#133.

Communication requirements should be clearly defined to facilitate the transfer of information between the program and its components and from the program to the appropriate stakeholders with the appropriate content and delivery methods. Collect all templates and record them in the knowledge repositories.

Update the program budget and implement the project by managing it closely. Next, update the project for approval from the steering committee.

A, C, and D because:-
We do not have implementation plans.

3-Management of the components is not the program manager's responsibility.

text: Your company X has acquired company Y. the systems, standards, and processes in the two companies are different. Send the relevant program standard to the project manager.

text: A program manager of a new program. He is preparing the program charter for review to get the funding from the sponsor. Which of the following options should be included in the program charter?

choices.text: Assumptions that will be added to the benefits management plan.
The delivery notes of the product.
Budget, Milestone dates, and staff details.
Key decision-makers, their expectations, and interests.

explanation:
The contents of the program charter generally consist of the following questions and their answers: Justification. Why is the program important and what does it achieve?
Vision. What is the end state and how will it benefit the organization?
Strategic alignment. What are the key strategic drivers and the program’s relationship to the organizational strategic objectives and any other ongoing strategic initiatives?
Benefits. What are the key outcomes required to achieve the program vision and benefits?
Scope. What is included within the program and what is considered to be out of scope at a high level?
Benefit strategy. What is the approach to ensure the realization of the planned benefits?
Assumptions and constraints. What are the assumptions, constraints, dependencies, and external factors considered and how have they shaped or limited the program’s objectives?
Components. How are the projects and other program components configured to deliver the program and the intended benefits?
Risks and issues. What are the initial risks and issues identified during the preparation of the program roadmap?
Timeline. What is the total length of the program, including all key milestone dates?
Resources needed. What are the estimated program costs and resource needs (i.e., staff, training, travel, etc.)?
Stakeholder considerations. Who are the key stakeholders, who are the most important stakeholders, and what is the initial strategy to engage them?
This information contributes to the development of the communications management plan. (See Section 5 for more information on Program Stakeholder Engagement.)
Program governance. What is the recommended governance structure to manage, control, and support the program? What are the recommended governance structures to guide and oversee the program components, including reporting requirements? What authority does the program manager possess? This information is updated in the program governance plan. (See Section 6 for more information on Program Governance.). Reference is standard for program management Page#93.

text: You are a program manager of a new platform. The new area manager requests you to use social media to improve communications. The new area manager has used social media before, so he prefers to use it in this program. What should you do?

text: You are a program manager. Now you are articulating the boundaries of the program scope. Which of the following will capture the program scope boundaries?

Program organization plan.
Program WBS.
Program scope statement.

text: You are a program manager of construction of a new city. You have received the approved charter and the stakeholder register has been developed. Which of the following aspects should you consider during the stakeholder engagement planning?

Relevant phase(s) applicable to stakeholders’ specific engagement.
Expectation of program benefits delivery.
Degree of support or opposition to the program benefits.
