text: An organization has issued a program to improve production and sale branches. The organization has 15 branches over the world. Within the above context, what is the first step?

choices.text: Develop a program scope.
Create an organizational change request.
Identify and quantify the program’s business benefits.
Develop the organizational chart.

explanation: The purpose of the benefits identification phase is to analyze the available information about organizational and business strategies, internal and external influences, and program drivers to identify and qualify the benefits that program stakeholders expect to realize. Activities that makeup benefits identification include defining the objectives and critical success factors for the program and identifying and quantifying business benefits. Reference is standard for program management Page# 46

text: A program manager of a new strategic initiative. Many of the project managers in the organization want to join the new program. The management has recommended a list of project managers to join. Within the above context, what should the program manager do?

choices.text: Request the CVs of the project managers and meet them individually.
Develop a comprehensive skill set inventory and select the most suitable resources.
Accept the recommendation of the management.
Call the HR department for the available project managers.

explanation: The creation of a skill set inventory will help the program manager to select the qualified project managers with the right criteria.

text: While the high management meets the key clients, they found that there are conflicts between them. The high management has requested the program management office to initiate a program to improve the service which is provided to the clients based on their interest and effect on the organization’s goals. What should you do as a program manager to develop and manage the program’s direction?

choices.text: Develop a program roadmap to get the program funding.
Improve the communication with the stakeholders.
Select the appropriate projects and subsidiary programs.
Perform interviews with the stakeholders to address their concerns and expectations.

explanation: Define the program mission statement by evaluating the stakeholders’ concerns and expectations in order to establish program direction. Exam content outline/Domain1/Task4.

text: Your company Beta requests you to improve the transition procedure to meet the closeout requirements. You have reviewed the procedure to remove any item that doesn’t relate to the closeout phase? What item should you remove?

choices.text: Review the benefits with the stakeholders including the program sponsor.
Perform any required transition to operation.
Managing the transition from the current position to the future position.
Start lessons learned documentation in the organizational database.

explanation: Managing the transition from the current position to the future position is not a part of the closing domain. Exam content outline/ tasks31 to 35.

text: After one year of the strategic cycle, the program manager has been informed that last year the company needed to comply with new laws and regulations that impacted the organizational strategy. Within the above context, what should the program manager do?

choices.text: Send email to the stakeholders and update the program roadmap to ensure strategic alignment.
Meet the stakeholders to cancel the programs and modify the program roadmap.
Review the program priorities, interdependencies, resource capacity, and capability and create a change request to update the program roadmap to ensure strategic alignment.
Modify the program management plan, benefits management plan, priorities, and interdependencies.

explanation: The program manager can’t update the plans without approval and can’t cancel the program without approval as well, so the best answer is C.

text: Your company has a program to strengthen its profits. One of the key projects has performance is not meet the expected program objectives. The project manager writes a change request to handle the matter. What should you do next as a program manager?

choices.text: Escalate to the governance board.
Evaluate and analyze the benefits and impact on the program.
Change the program schedule, cost, and scope baselines.
Update the register.

explanation:
You have to start the impact analysis on the program baselines and to know the risks that may impact the program then update the risk register. And you can not escalate without impact analysis.
The program change requests should be analyzed to determine their urgency and impact on program baseline elements and other program components. When there are multiple ways to implement the change, the costs, risks, and other aspects of each option should be assessed to enable the selection of the approach most likely to deliver the program’s intended benefits. Reference is standard for program management page#125.

text: You are a program manager. While you are in the execution stage the sponsor requests you to close the program due to the changes in the business environment. Within the above context. What should you add to complete the final report?

choices.text: Financial and performance assessments, Change requests, and successes and failures.
Financial and performance assessments, lessons learned, and reasons for program closure.
Financial and performance assessments, sustainment plan, change request, successes and failures, and reason for program closure.
Financial and performance assessments, Lessons learned, successes and failures.

explanation:
A and C are wrong because no change request in the final reports.
B and D are correct but already we have the reasons to close the program (changes in the business environment), so we want other items to complete the final reports.
The final program report may be required to document critical information that can be applied to improve the success of future programs and component projects. This final report may consist of: financial and performance assessments, lessons learned, successes and failures, identified areas for improvement, risk management outcomes (risk register, risk management plan,…), unforeseen risks, customer sign-off, reason(s) for program closeout, history of all baselines, and archive plan for program documentation. Reference is standard for program management page#102

text: You are a program manager of a multinational finance system development. The program is impacted due to new financial laws and regulations in one of the countries. You have to change the financial statements of the branches in that country by the end of the next month. If you fail to change the statement on time that may lead to closing these branches or fines. The manager of the branches has met you to arrange a subject matter expert in the financial to change the statement. The experts in this field are scarce and in high demand. This issue will be a cause for high risk if the change will not be finished on time. What should you do to handle this risk?

choices.text: Make a contract with the government of that country.
Define all scenarios and assign contingency reserve and management reserve.
Assess and evaluate the risk, incorporate the risk in the program risk management plan, and escalate to the program governance board.
Create a contract with a subject matter expert with rewards to finish on time.

explanation:
Evaluate risks identified by stakeholders, including sponsors, and incorporate them in the program risk management plan, as necessary. Exam content outlines/Domain4/Task6.
Regularly evaluate new and existing risks that impact strategic objectives in order to present an updated risk management plan to the governance board for approval. Exam content outlines/Domain5/Task6.

text: One of the components is completed and ready for the transition. What should you do as a program manager to proceed with the component transition?

choices.text: Update the program business case.
Update the program roadmap.
Update the stakeholder register.
Submit a change request to close the component.

explanation: As the program components reach the end of their respective life cycles or as planned program-level milestones are achieved, the program manager collaborates with the customer or sponsor to present a request to close or transition the component. This formal request is sent to the program steering committee for review and approval. The process of component transition includes making updates to the program roadmap. Reference is standard for program management Page#101.

text: You are a program manager of a construction program. You want to confirm that the program can contribute to the value of the stakeholders. What should you verify the alignment with?

choices.text: Business case and charter.
Organization’s strategic objectives.
Organizational policies and procedures.
Governance.

explanation: The Program Governance Performance Domain integrates with the Benefits Management Performance Domain to help ensure that the program is continuously aligned with the organizational strategy and that the intended value can still be achieved by the delivery of program benefits. Reference is standard for program management page# 52

text: You are a program manager of a new advertisement program. The stakeholders always request information in a routine manner. This behavior led to gaps in communications, reporting, and program performance as well. Within the above context, what should you review and change to handle that issue?

choices.text: Performance management plan.
Program Benefits Management plan.
Change management plan.
Program communications management plan.

explanation: The program communication management plan includes who needs what information, when they need it, how it will be given to them, and by whom. Reference is the standard for program management page#112.

text: You are a program manager of a large program. The program contains 10 projects. The program steering committee has informed you that all projects should be undergo to user acceptance test before transition. Within the above context, in which of the following will you document this?

choices.text: Program communication management plan.
Program governance plan.
Program stakeholders’ management plan.
Program quality management plan.

explanation:
The request is a part of the program success criteria in the program governance plan.
Governance (which could be at the organizational, portfolio, or program level) establishes the minimum acceptable criteria for a successful program and the methods by which those criteria will be measured, communicated, and endorsed. The criteria describe the definition of success consistent with the expectations and needs of key program stakeholders and reinforce the program alignment to deliver the maximum attainable benefits. Reference is the standard for program management page#72.
The review of any recommendation for the transition or closure of a program component generally includes: -
Confirming that the business case for the component has been sufficiently satisfied or that further pursuit of the component’s goals should be discontinued.
Ensuring appropriate program-level communications of the component’s closure to key stakeholders.
Ensuring component compliance with program-level quality control plans (when required).
Assessing organizational- or program-level lessons learned as a consequence of the performance of the component in transition.
Confirming that all other accepted practices for project or program transition or closure have been satisfied. Reference is the standard for program management page#77.

text: You are a program manager of a new program. Now you want to start preliminary stakeholder analysis to evaluate their support to the program. What should you do?

choices.text: Create the stakeholder charter and communication plan.
Develop the stakeholder register, map, and stakeholder engagement plan.
Develop RACI matrix.
Perform visibility study and SWOT analysis.

explanation:
A is wrong because nothing in program management is called a stakeholder charter.
C is wrong because of RACI for assigning the responsibilities, not for stakeholder analysis.
D is wrong because SWOT is not a tool in the stakeholder areas.
B is correct creating because the stakeholders register, stakeholder map, and stakeholder engagement plan are the main outcomes of the stakeholder domain.
Program Stakeholder Engagement is the performance domain that identifies and analyzes stakeholder needs and manages expectations and communications to foster stakeholder support. Reference is the standard for program management page#57.

text: You are a program manager of the development of a new product. Your program contains 12 projects and a subsidiary program. The executive officer requests you to crash the project-1 one month for market needs purposes. The project-1 is depending on the outputs of project_2 and 3. Within the above context, what should you do first?

choices.text: Ask the project managers to crash the 3 projects immediately.
Send change request to the governance committee.
Review the resource management plan with the 3 project managers focusing on the critical paths and shared critical resources for accelerating the schedule.
Request support from the executive managers and sponsors.

explanation: The program manager manages resources at the program level and works with the component managers who manage resources at the component level to balance the needs of the program with the availability of resources. Reference is the standard for program management page# 133

text: You are a program manager of a critical program. The sponsor worries about the program cost variance and the risks. What should you refer to?

choices.text: Program performance plan
Program stakeholder engagement plan.
Scheduling tools.
Program performance report.

explanation: Program performance reports include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. These reports generally provide current status information about what work has been accomplished (especially milestones and phase gates); what work remains to be completed; earned value; and risks, issues, and changes under consideration. Reference is the standard for program management page#101.

text: You are a program manager of the software program at three locations. The client focuses on maintaining quality and decreasing the timeline. Which of the following should be added to the benefits register to achieve the above?

choices.text: Plans for defining KPIs and metrics, and procedures to measure benefits.
Plans for program quality assurance and control.
Tracking and communicating program risks.
Program schedule control to monitor the timeline.

explanation: The benefits register may take many forms, but typically includes (at a minimum): List of planned benefits; Mapping of the planned benefits to the program components, as reflected in the program roadmap; Description of how each benefit will be measured and Key performance indicators and thresholds for evaluating their achievement. Reference is the standard for program management page# 47

text: You are a program manager. One of the components has been delivered. And another component did not meet the expectations due to a change request. What should you do next?

choices.text: Resource prioritization.
Perform program delivery management.
Perform benefits sustainment and program transition.
Perform program performance monitoring and controlling.

explanation: We are in the program delivery management. The program performance monitoring and controlling is performed during program delivery management, so the next step is benefits sustainment and program transition. Reference is standard for program management page#99,101.

text: You are a program manager of a multinational program to implement a protection system for the company copyrights. The company is intolerant of processes to the point of being considered process-adverse but is tolerant of long-term program activities of the protection of its intellectual property. The expectation for progress is slow. Within the above context, what should you do next?

choices.text: You have to insist on maintaining a tightly controlled stakeholder register and engagement plan to meet the expectations.
Develop engagement and communications activities to meet the company's expectations.
Document the information of the most important sponsors and stakeholders.
Develop an appropriate level of communications required to meet the component needs.

explanation: Since the company is intolerant of processes to the point of being considered process-adverse but is tolerant of long-term program activities of the protection of its intellectual property, you have to insist on maintaining a tightly controlled stakeholder register and engagement plan to meet the expectations.

text: A program with 15 components, the program for monitoring and controlling the roads in many countries around the world. After the planning phase, the program manager conducts a review meeting and he identifies many issues that to be resolved to accelerate the progress. One of those issues is the lack of configuration management tools and financial management software. Which of the following will be reviewed?

choices.text: Benefits sustainment and program transition.
Program management information system (PMIS).
Program closeout.
Program Business case.

explanation: A PMIS consists of tools used to collect, integrate, and communicate information critical to the effective management of one or more organizational programs. An effective PMIS incorporates the following: Software tools; Documents, data, and knowledge repositories; Configuration management tools; Change management system; Risk database and analysis tools; Financial management systems; Earned value management activities and tools; requirements management activities and tools; and Other tools and activities as required. Reference is standard for program management Page#100.

text: Program near to complete. The benefits of the program will be continued realization and generation of revenue for 10 years after closing the program. The program manager and the operation manager are in conflict regarding who is accountable for managing the benefits after program closure. The program manager replies that the benefits management after the program closure is out of the program scope. But the operation manager worries about the availability of the knowledge and information necessary to manage the benefits after the program closure. What is action should the program sponsor take?

choices.text: Request the program manager to develop the plans required for transition and sustain the benefits after the program closure.
Request the operations manager to develop the plans required for transition and sustain the benefits after the program closure.
Ask the program manager to assign a program team member to ensure that the benefits and knowledge have been transitioned to the process area.
Ask the operations manager to assign an operation team member to ensure that the benefits and knowledge have been transitioned to the process area.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
Develop a sustainment plan that identifies the processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary for the management of benefits beyond the completion of the program in order to ensure the continued realization of intended benefits. Exam content outline/Domain3/Task3.
Develop a transition plan to operations in order to guarantee the sustainment of products and benefits delivered by the program. Exam content outline/Domain3/Task8.

text: You have created the program performance report for review by the program steering committee. You noticed that the scope and the schedule have been met, but the quality is low moreover the cost and resources are very high more than the planned and out of the acceptable level. The program cannot achieve the intended benefits and no benefits have been realized yet. The ROI of the program cannot be accepted. What should you do after reviewing the analysis of the performance metrics?

choices.text: Request additional funds.
Request extension for the schedule.
Transition the existing results to the operation area.
Ask for program cancellation based on performance indicators and metrics.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The intended benefits cannot be achieved so the program should be terminated. You have to submit the recommendations to the steering committee for review and decision.
A program is closed either because the program charter is fulfilled or internal/external conditions arise that bring the program to an early end. These conditions may include changes in the business case that no longer make the program necessary or a determination that the expected benefits cannot be achieved. Reference is the standard for program management page#102

text: You are a program manager of a program near completion. All the components are completed and all identified benefits are delivered. The executive manager is concerned about the long-term benefits realization. Which of the following can ensure the long-term realization of the benefits?

choices.text: Risk management plan.
Benefits indication
Benefits sustainment plan
Benefits transition plan

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
The purpose of the benefits sustainment phase is the ongoing maintenance activities performed beyond the end of the program by receiving organizations to ensure continued generation of the improvements and outcomes delivered by the program. As the program is closed, responsibility for sustaining the benefits provided by the program may pass to another organization or another program. Benefits may be sustained through operations, maintenance, new components, or other efforts. A benefits sustainment plan should be developed prior to program closure to identify the risks, processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary to ensure the continued realization of the benefits delivered. Reference is the standard for program management page#55.

text: You are a program manager. While you are in the execution phase, you receive an email from the sponsor that some of the stakeholders may not understand the benefits of the program. Within the above context, which of the following will provide the greatest value to clarify stakeholder perceptions?

choices.text: Send them the program charter.
Stakeholder analysis.
Update the stakeholder communications requirements.
Send them the benefits management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The benefits with all details are available in the benefits management plan.
The benefits management plan should:
1- Define each benefit and associated assumptions and determine how each benefit will be achieved.
2- Link components outputs to the planned program outcomes.
3- Define the metrics (including key performance indicators) and procedures to measure benefits.
4- Define roles and responsibilities required to manage the benefits.
5- Define how the resulting benefits and capabilities will be transitioned into an operational state to achieve benefits.
6- Define how the resulting capabilities will be transitioned to the individuals, groups, or organizations responsible for sustaining the benefits.
7- Provide a process for managing the overall benefits management effort.

text: You are a program manager. While you are in the execution phase, a stakeholder complains to you that he did not receive a very important and critical communication about project X. What should you do to handle the above situation?

choices.text: You should review and revise the stakeholder engagement plan.
You should review and update the detailed stakeholder list.
You should conduct the component communications management plan.
You should add the risk to the program risk register.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
The stakeholder engagement plan contains a detailed strategy for effective stakeholder engagement, based on the current situation. The plan includes stakeholder engagement guidelines and provides insight on how the stakeholders are engaged in various components of the program. The plan defines the metrics used to measure the performance of stakeholder engagement activities. This could include measures of participation in meetings and other communication channels. Reference is the standard for program management page# 64.

text: You are a program manager for the development of new technology by using the existing technologies. The sponsor and the steering committee want to create a strong and exhaustive risk management plan. In which phase is the program risk management plan created?

choices.text: Program risk management planning activity.
Program definition.
Transition phase.
Program delivery phase.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
A is an activity, not a phase.
The program risk management planning activity should be conducted early in the program definition phase. The outputs from this activity include the Program risk management plan and Program risk register. Reference is the standard for program management page#120.

text: You are a program manager of a designing and manufacturing program. During the organization strategy alignment meeting, you notice that another program is developing a new technology to improve the operations performance and cost. What should you do to add the new technology to your program?

choices.text: Add the new technology to the sustainment plan.
Meet the component managers to update the program risk register by using the NPV of the new technology.
Update the benefits management plan with the benefits of the new technology.
Analyze the benefits management plan to identify any new risks that may arise due to this new technology.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Analyze then update the benefits management plan.
Analyze and update the benefits realization and sustainment plans for uncertainty, risk identification, risk mitigation, and risk opportunity in order to determine if corrective actions are necessary and communicate to stakeholders. Exam content outline domain3/ task7.

text: You are a program manager for the construction of a new airport. The sponsor came back from a high management meeting after identifying a critical schedule risk that may impact the program benefits realization. What should you do next?

choices.text: Implement the risk response plan for the identified risk.
Document the risk in the register and create a mitigation response plan.
You should update the program risk and benefits management plan.
Cancel the program to avoid the risk.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The risk has been identified during the meeting, you have to document it in the program risk register, analyze and assign appropriate response.
Nothing will be updated in the benefits management plan before analysis.
And we can’t implement a mitigation plan without documentation of the risk in the register.

text: You are a program manager of production and shipping of 50 million items over 3 years. You notice that one of the suppliers has a history of overestimating its planned values, which may impact production. Within the above context, what should you do to monitor and control the supplier?

choices.text: You should Use expert judgment, and update the procurement plan.
You should review performance reports, inspections, and audits.
You should ask the CEO and the stakeholder for approval.
You should review the evaluation criteria, analyze risks and risk response strategies.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Procurement monitor and control tools & techniques are. 1 Expert judgment. 2 Claims administration 3- Data analysis (Performance reviews • Earned value analysis • Trend analysis). 4 Inspection. 5 Audits. Pmbok6 page#492.

text: You are a program manager; your program is in the definition phase. You and your team determine that the best way to deliver the program benefits is through the use of external suppliers to supplement the corporate resources. Within the above context, which of the following should you use to determine and document the results of the procurement planning activity?

choices.text: RFB, RFPs, RFQ, alternatives analyses, approach to competition.
RFP, proposal evaluation criteria, contract management,
Make-or-buy decisions, contract management, and RFQ.
Alternatives analyses, Make-or-buy decisions, the best mix of contract types, and approach to competition.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
RFB, FRQ, RFP, and proposal evaluation criteria are outputs from program procurement management activity during the delivery phase. Reference is the standard for program management page#131.
We are in the definition phase
A program manager should understand the resources required for the delivery of benefits expected of the program. Techniques such as make-or-buy decisions and program work-breakdown-structure charts aid in this activity.
The best mix of the types of procurement contracts planned across the program; at the component level, a particular type of contract (e.g., firm-fixed-price) may appear to be the best procurement solution, but a different contract type (e.g., incentive fee) may be optimal for that same procurement when viewed at the program level
The best program-wide approach to competition (for example, the risks of sole-source contracts in one area of the program could be balanced with the different risks associated with full and open competition in other areas of the program);
Often, an analysis of alternatives is performed in the planning stage. This may include requests for information (RFIs), feasibility studies, trade studies, and market analysis to determine the best fit of solutions and services to meet the specific needs of the program. Reference is the standard for program management page#117.

text: You are a program manager for the development of new technology. Now you are evaluating the conflicting stakeholder demands associated with the program objectives, you notice that the team members have a high interest in schedule and cost, but they have a low interest in quality and benefits. The client organization has a high interest in benefits. Within the above context, what should you do?

choices.text: You should follow the team members as internal stakeholders to finish the program on time and within budget.
You should follow the client organization to achieve the intended benefits.
Meet with the stakeholders to allow everyone to state their priorities.
You should balance stakeholder needs by using trade-offs among the stakeholder groups.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
In many cases, external stakeholders have more influence than the program manager, the program team, and even the program sponsor. Balancing stakeholder interests is important, considering their potential impact on program benefits realization or the inherent conflicting nature of those interests. Reference is the standard for program management page#57.
A and B are wrong because all costs, schedule, quality, and benefits are important.
C is wrong because already you know the priorities of them.

text: You are a program manager in your country. You are assigned to another program during the definition phase. You create the program team by defining resources of the component management requirements. Within the above context, which of the following is an initial step that is needed to evaluate the alignment of the available resources with the needs of the program?

choices.text: Identifying the program resource requirements.
Assessment of skills and competencies.
Contact the functional department manager to get information about the available resources.
Develop the program resource management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
An estimate of the required resources includes people, office space, laboratories, data centers or other facilities, equipment of all types, software, vehicles, and office supplies. And particularly the estimation of staff and facilities, which may have longer lead times or affect ongoing activities, is required to prepare the program business case and should be reflected in the program charter. Reference is the standard for program management Page #109.
A: Is wrong because the program resource requirement is an output of program resource management planning. Reference is the standard for program management Page #119.

text: The project managers have completed the project management plans for all projects in your program. You are the program manager and you notice that some project managers prefer one progress report template but others prefer another template. What should you do to select one template for all projects?

choices.text: Review the issue with the project managers for reaching to an agreement on which template to use.
Discuss the matter with the program PMO to determine which template is appropriate to use.
Escalate the issue program steering committee to select the template.
Ask the project managers to use any report templates they like.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The program management office (PMO) facilitates the sharing of resources, methodologies, tools, and techniques. It defines standard program management processes and procedures that will be followed; provides training to ensure that standards and practices are well understood, and supports program communications. Reference is standard for program managementpage#20&85.

text: A financial system had been delivered to the beneficiaries after 3 years program. After 3 months utilization of the system, the beneficiaries have noticed that the quality and the level of accuracy of the financial data is not sufficient to determine the key performance indicators KPIs. Moreover, the main financial department forgot to add the analytical tools to know the cause of discrepancies. To address these shortcomings, the beneficiaries request the program manager to develop a follow-up process. Which of the following is defining that process?

choices.text: Benefits register.
Benefits sustainment plan.
Benefits transition plan.
Benefits report.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
A benefits sustainment plan should be developed prior to program closure to identify the risks, processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary to ensure the continued realization of the benefits delivered.
Monitoring the performance of the product, service, capability, or results from a reliability and availability-for-use perspective and comparing actual performance to planned performance, including key performance indicators; u Monitoring the continued suitability of the deployed product, service, capability, or results to provide the benefits expected by the customers owning and operating it. This may include the continued viability of interfaces with other products, services, capabilities, or results and the continued completeness of the functionality. Reference is standard for program managementpage#55.

text: A multinational company wants to centralize its system by transitioning 20 branches around the world. The scope of this program includes 3 important points: 1- Technology.; 2- HR system.; 3- Policies and procedures. You already selected your main team and now preparing the business case. Which of the following should be included in the business case?

choices.text: The inventory and the employee details.
Interdependencies between the projects.
A cost/benefit analysis of the different scenarios and their respective contributions.
The compensation packages that offered for all countries.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
The business case may include details about the program outcomes, approved concept, issues, high-level risk, and opportunity assessment, key assumptions, business, and operational impact, cost-benefit analysis, alternative solutions, financial analysis, intrinsic and extrinsic benefits, market demands or barriers, potential profits, social needs, environmental influences, legal implications, time to market, constraints, and the extent to which the program aligns with the organization’s strategic plan. Reference is the standard for program management page# 35.

text: The program manager and the program team of the XYZ program have created and updated the benefits register in the early stage of the program. Within the above context, which of the following should be included in the benefits register?

choices.text: Planned benefits list, EV, and responsible stakeholder.
Planned benefits list, benefits realization date, and benefits creator.
Planned benefits list, components mapping, and measurement method.
Planned benefits list, stakeholders, and program management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
the program benefits register is updated. The benefits register may take many forms, but typically includes (at a minimum): List of planned benefits; Mapping of the planned benefits to the program components, as reflected in the program roadmap; Description of how each benefit will be measured. Reference is the standard for program management page# 47

text: You are a program manager in a matrix organization. The program contains projects for high technology development. You have assigned the project managers for all projects. Each project needs specific experience and skills. You use the existing time reporting process to avoid budget overruns. Which of the following is a critical component of the Program Schedule Management Process?

choices.text: Activity/ component start and finish dates and intermediate milestones.
A list of all the projects.
The training time for all team members, and the project managers.
The project team members and the projects manager skill levels.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
The first draft of a program master schedule often only identifies the order and start/end dates of components and their key interdependencies with other components. Later, it may be enriched with more intermediate component results as the component schedules are developed. Reference is the standard for program management page# 121.

text: You are a program manager of Company X. Your company has signed a contract with company Y to develop a new software system. Company Y is excited about this contract. The quality assurance (QA) team in your company identified a potential issue with the main front-end servers due to the new enhancements which are required by company Y. In the meeting with company Y, you determine that you need additional funding and resources. What is the most important step should you do next?

choices.text: Arrange the fund and the resources from the canceled projects.
Inform and advise company Y about the non-availability of the funding and resources.
You should follow the integrated change control process.
You should use the program management reserve.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
You and company Y representatives are in the meeting, and they know that you need additional funds, resources, and time. You have to submit a change request through the integrated change control process to get the decision.

text: During the last 6 months, you notice that the phase gate reviews have excellent feedback and exceeded the stakeholder expectations. Therefore, the customer wants to stop the phase gate reviews. What should you do next as a program manager?

choices.text: Ask recommendations from the stakeholders.
Don’t stop the periodic phase gate reviews to maintain program effectiveness for benefits realization.
Follow the customer and submit change control.
Use a periodic communications report instead of the periodic phase gate reviews.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Program governance endorses reviews of programs at key decision points in the program life cycle. These reviews often are conducted at times that coincide with the initiation or completion of significant segments of a program to enable governance to approve or disapprove the passage of a program from one significant segment to another. They also facilitate the review and approval of any required changes to the program at key decision points. Reference is the standard for program management page#75.

text: A Program is near completion and the program manager going to close the program. Although the training has been provided to the operational staff, they are concerned about the benefits realization that will not be fully realized. What should you do to avoid such concerns in the future?

choices.text: Send the capabilities' benefits to the operational staff.
Update the risk register and assign appropriate responses.
Development program benefits transition plan the operational area's readiness.
Collaboration with the operational staff to develop the program benefits sustainment plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Develop a sustainment plan that identifies the processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary for the management of benefits beyond the completion of the program in order to ensure the continued realization of intended benefits. Exam content outline domain3/task3.

text: You are a program manager of the Customer relationship system (CRS). You join the team to fix a problem in the data. After analysis of the data, you found that the data of the customer is duplicated. You use the lessons learned from the repository for a program similar in nature. Corrective action has been taken and the change has been implemented. What should you do with the knowledge gained from this situation?

choices.text: Add the lessons learned to the monthly report.
Update the lessons learned database.
Add the lessons learned to the communications management plan.
Submit the corrective action to the program steering committee.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Lessons learned are a compilation of knowledge gained. This knowledge may be acquired from executing similar and relevant programs in the past, or it may reside in public domain databases. Reference is the standard for program management page#130.

text: You are a program manager for the construction of a new airport. External resources are required for the program. You receive the bids from vendors and select the top bidder and present them to the program steering committee. One of the governance members asks you to select a vendor who was rejected because he was not available on the approved vendor's list. You learn that the vendor is relative to the governance member. What should you do?

choices.text: Select the vendor immediately.
Start a new vendor selection bid process.
Add the vendor to the approved list.
Write an ethics violation.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct requires that practitioners demonstrate a commitment to ethical and professional conduct, and carry with it the obligation to comply with laws, regulations, and organizational and professional policies. Reference is the standard for program management page# 2.

text: You are a program manager of program X. you take over the responsibilities of program Y. Which of the following should you review to assess the cost and benefits justifications of the program?

choices.text: Program risk management plan.
Program charter.
Program benefits management plan.
Program business case.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The business case also serves as a formal declaration of the value that the program is expected to deliver and a justification for the resources that will be expended to deliver it. The business case is required as one of the document deliverables before the program can be formally chartered and may be considered as the primary justification document for an investment decision. Reference is the standard for program management page#35.

text: An organization looking forward to improving the business strategy to meet future challenges and put the business in an optimum way. The main point in the new strategy is IT infrastructure improvement through the transition to the cloud computing platform that will increase the performance, reliability and decrease the cost. To appropriately plan the program's success, what should the program manager do to engage the stakeholders?

choices.text: By identifying stakeholder expectations and clearly outlining key indicators and expected benefits, and creates a framework to address ongoing program activities and evolving stakeholder needs.
Outlines how all program stakeholders will be engaged throughout the duration of the program using the stakeholder register and stakeholder.
Document, prioritize, and track issues help the entire program team understand the feedback received from the stakeholders.
Understand the organizational culture and politics, the overall program impact, and program-related stakeholder concerns.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
According to the question, the program before stakeholders planning.
D is the first step in the analysis.
A is step two during analysis.
B is a planning step.
C is the program stakeholder engagement step.
So, the correct step is D.
Perform stakeholder analysis through historical analysis, personal experience, interviews, knowledge base, review of formal agreements (for example, request for proposal (RFP), request for information (RFI), contracts), and input from other sources in order to create the stakeholder management plan. Exam content outline domain4/task2.
Key information should be obtained from stakeholders in order to better understand the organizational culture, politics, and concerns related to the program, as well as the overall impact of the program. This information may be obtained through historical information, individual interviews, focus groups, or questionnaires and surveys. Reference is the standard for program management page# 62.

text: A 5 years program, during the delivery phase, many of the projects have been transitioned to the operations area. One of the project managers identified risk and escalated it to the program team. What should be done with this risk?

choices.text: Mitigate the risk before it is incorporated into the risk management plan.
Document the risk in the program transition plan and identify it as a potential issue.
Incorporate it into the risk register and perform a thorough analysis.
Document it in the issue log and immediately notify the steering committee.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
The first step for the escalated risk is adding to the risk register then analyzing and assigning an appropriate response. The risk is not an issue to add it to the issue log.

text: You are a program manager for the construction of a new multimedia system. You initiate the program, but significant resources and funding are required now for the early activities until the completion of the estimated budget and cost. What should you do to understand the financial environment?

choices.text: Develop the program's financial framework.
Compare the costs to the expected benefits realization.
Develop a budget based on historical information.
Take the funding from the sponsor.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
The type of program and the funding structure dictate the financial environment for the duration of the program.
A program financial framework is a high-level initial plan for coordinating available funding, determining constraints, and determining how funding is allocated. The financial framework defines and describes the program funding flows so that the money is spent as efficiently as possible. Reference is the standard for program management page# 114.

text: You are a program manager of a new 7 projects program; the charter is approved and now you want to communicate the program's intended direction and the linkage between organizational strategies and planned work. Which of the following will you use?

choices.text: Program business case.
Program roadmap
Program charter.
Program risk register.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The program roadmap is a chronological representation of a program’s intended direction, graphically depicting dependencies between major milestones and decision points, which reflects the linkage between the business strategy and the program work. Reference is the standard for program management page#36.

text: During the review meeting with the CEO, the CEO informs you about the potential budget cuts that would impact the program resources and will push you to accelerate the schedule to deliver the benefits quickly to continue the program. Within the above context, what should you do first?

choices.text: Update the benefits register and benefits management plan.
Perform a risk assessment related to the acceleration of the schedule, update the risk register, and request approval from the steering committee.
Record the impact on the program then meet the steering committee to present the finding to determine the next step.
Update the program schedule and submit it to the steering committee for approval.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Conduct impact assessments for program changes and recommend decisions in order to obtain approval in accordance with the governance model. Exam content outline/Domain2/task29.

text: How do you ensure that benefits are realized according to the program governance during the program execution?

choices.text: Update the program benefits register.
Ask the steering committee.
Review the benefits management plan
Review the program business case.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
During the execution, you have to review the benefits management plan, but at the end of the program review the business case.
For a benefit to have value, it needs to be realized to a sufficient degree and in a timely manner. The actual benefits delivered by the program components or program itself should be regularly evaluated against the expected benefits, as defined in the benefits management plan. Reference is the standard for program management page#52
At the end of the program, the resulting benefits should be compared against those intended in the business case to ensure that the program will actually deliver the intended benefits. Reference is the standard for program management page#53.

text: You have been assigned as a program manager of a low-performance program. You have reviewed the program documents and performed interviews with the stakeholder and sponsors. You have realized that the program is not aligned with the organizational goals and objectives. You have to realign the program components to meet the program needs. Within the above context, what should you do to realign the program?

choices.text: Create a change request to get approval from the steering committee, cancel some projects, accelerate some projects and reassign some resources.
Meet with the program sponsor and follow his decision.
Perform program schedule assessment to know how to maintain all components within the program.
Meet with the program stakeholders and follow their decision.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
B and D are wrong, you cannot follow the decision of the stakeholders or sponsor without change request approval from the steering committee.
C is wrong. Maintaining all the components cannot guarantee alignment.
the program’s ability to deal with uncertainty because programs can change the direction of projects, cancel projects, or start new projects to adapt to changing circumstances. Reference is the standard for program management page#28
Due to the complexity and potential long duration of programs, the program master schedule may need to be updated to include new components or remove components as a result of approved change requests to meet evolving program goals. Reference is the standard for program management page#136.

text: A software company wants to improve its delivery methodology. The company develops a benefits management plan to identify formal program governance. What is the benefit of structuring the work into a program?

choices.text: The coordinated practice of portfolio, program, and project management by linking portfolio, program, and project management principles and practices.
Delivery the initiatives and objectives by using portfolios alignment.
Commitment to the constraints to achieve specific activities.
Bundling of components or work to gain efficiencies unachievable if managed individually.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
D is related to program definition:
program is defined as related projects, subsidiary programs, and program activities managed in a coordinated manner to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually. Reference is the standard for program management page#3
A is related to OPM:
OPM supports the coordinated practice of portfolio, program, and project management by linking portfolio, program, and project management principles and practices. Reference is the standard for program management page#10
C is related to the project:
Projects are used to generate the outputs or outcomes required by programs, within defined constraints, such as budget, time, specifications, scope, and quality. Reference is the standard for program management page#4
B is related to the organization strategy plan:
The organization strategy plan is subdivided into a set of organizational initiatives.
Portfolios of programs and projects are the vehicles for delivering these initiatives. Reference is the standard for program management page#14

text: You are a program manager of a new program. After the RFP you found that the lowest price and the best schedule from a bidder out of the prequalified vendor list. During the final review, you are informed that the vendor is relative to one of the project managers. But the bid meets all the organization's policies and procedures. You are concerned about the conflict of interest. What should you do?

choices.text: Insert the new bidder in the prequalified vendor list and replace the project manager.
Choose the best bid from the prequalified vendor list.
Choose the bid of the new bidder and document the decision.
Advise the sponsor of a potential conflict of interest before awarding the bid.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Since there is a conflict of interest, you have to discuss the matter with the sponsor to take the decision before awarding the bid to the selected vendor.

text: You are a program manager of the program of 10 projects. You determine that the first 5 projects face many change orders and fail to be completed on time. You meet with the project managers to understand the problem. During this meeting, the project managers informed you that the reasons for the problems are the key risks and the lack of resources. What should you do to keep the second 5 projects On Track?

choices.text: Develop a change management strategy.
Update the program management plan.
Update the baseline of the second 5 projects.
Meet with the project managers weekly.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
Manage changes in accordance with change management strategy in order to control scope, quality, schedule, cost, contracts, risks, and rewards. Exam content outline/Domain2/task28

text: A three years complex program to develop an autopilot system for a new electric car. Several of the key stakeholders are concerned because they don’t know enough information about the program and they have not been involved regularly within the program. Also, they don’t understand the benefits of the program. What should the program manager do to handle the stakeholder’s concerns?

choices.text: Send them a progress report after next week's status meeting.
Identify the stakeholder expectations, and update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Revise the communications management plan after discussion with the program governance board.
Meet with the key stakeholders and update the program stakeholder map.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
For complex programs, the program manager may develop a stakeholder map to visually represent the interaction of all stakeholders’ current and desired support and influence. The map serves as a tool to assess the impact of a change on the program community. It allows the program team to make informed decisions about how and when to engage stakeholders, taking into account their interests, influence, involvement, interdependencies, and support levels. Reference is the standard for program management page#62.
The stakeholder map can function as a tool to help identify the need for interactions with stakeholders. It brings to light the potential partnerships among stakeholders and the collaboration opportunities that contribute to the success of the program. As the need arises, the program manager can use the stakeholder map to remind teams of which stakeholders need to be engaged at various times in the program life cycle. Reference is the standard for program management page#63.

text: Which of the following options is providing program and components status information, cost information, risk analysis, and other information?

choices.text: Communications log.
Program performance report.
Program communications management plan.
Information gathering techniques.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Program performance reports include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met, and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. These reports generally provide current status information about what work has been accomplished (especially milestones and phase gates); what work remains to be completed; earned value; and risks, issues, and changes under consideration. Reference is the standard for program management Page #101.

text: The objectives of your program impact a large number of the population. The public organizations are commenting negatively on your program objectives. What should you do first?

choices.text: Update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Perform risk of negative media coverage.
Review the program stakeholder register to determine the ability of these stakeholders to affect the program outcomes.
Meet with the governance board to discuss the problem and determine the next steps.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
Program and project managers need to be aware of the stakeholders’ impact and level of influence to understand and address the changing environments of programs and projects. Reference is the standard for program management Page #57
A is wrong, maybe the next step.
B is wrong because the stakeholder register is input to the risk identification and analysis, so reviewing the stakeholder register is first.
D is wrong, you cannot go to the governance board without analysis.

text: You are a program manager of the transformation of the customer service and sales of your organization to the Customer Relation Management System. The key stakeholders are happy with the progress of the program. An employee in the Sales department asks you to integrate an application with the new system. You have informed him that the new request is out of the program scope and need analysis, additional fund and should be developed as a new project on its own. You request additional funding through the change management plan and you get approval on the new scope. What should you do next?

choices.text: Approval from key stakeholders
Assign a new project manager to the new project.
Close an existing project to reassign all resources to the project.
Prioritize the existing program components to ensure optimal resource allocation and management of interdependencies.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Since the new scope is approved means the project business case, project charter, and program scope are completed and approved. The next step is “prioritize the existing program components to ensure optimal resource allocation and management of interdependencies”. The project manager is already assigned through the project charter.

text: The program is started and preparation is completed. In which phase the component projects are planned?

choices.text: Program delivery phase.
Program definition phase.
Program transition phase.
Program planning phase.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
In the delivery phase, each program component will progress through the following program delivery subphases: Component authorization and planning, Component oversight and integration, and Component transition and closure. The standard for program management page#95.

text: You are assigned as a program manager. The leaders in the organization have listed the benefits required from the program. They requested you to determine when the incremental benefits will be realized. What should you do first?

choices.text: Develop the program transition plan.
Develop the program schedule.
Develop the program management plan.
Develop the program roadmap.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The program is in the formulation subphase, so you have to develop the program roadmap first.
Establish a high-level road map with milestones and preliminary estimates in order to obtain initial validation and approval from the executive sponsor. Exam content outline/Domain1/task2.

text: You are a program manager. A project in your program is scheduled to close after 4 days. What should you verify prior to allowing the project closure?

choices.text: Verify that the project has met or exceeded the benefits realization criteria to meet program objectives.
Verify that the project has released resources to achieve program objectives
Verify that the project has met the financial requirements to meet goals.
Verify that the project has met the procurement to meet program objectives.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
Verify that the close, transition, and integration of constituent projects and the program meet or exceed the benefit realization criteria in order to achieve the program’s strategic objectives. Exam content outline/Domain3/task5

text: A project in your program is facing a number of emerging risks but you fall behind in reviewing and approving the plans. that is why the project manager cannot address the risks effectively. Within the above context, what should you do about the risk management plan in this situation?

choices.text: Assign the resolution responsibility of project-level risks to the project manager.
Ask the project manager to cancel the project.
Create risk escalation policies and procedures in the risk response plan.
Ignore the risks.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
project risk management activities focus on risks to project execution and success, while program risk management incorporates escalated project risks and program risks and also monitors interdependencies that affect multiple component projects. The standard for program management page#98
B is wrong, no reason to cancel the project.
C is wrong because the risk policies and procedures in the governance plan and risk management plan are not in the risk response plan.
a key element of program risk strategy is the establishment and monitoring of program risk thresholds. Examples of program risk thresholds include:
The maximum level of risk exposure that can be managed within the program (beyond which an escalation is triggered). The standard for program management page#41
program governance may establish program risk thresholds for adherence within the program. The standard for program management page#73
D is wrong, we cannot ignore the risks, we have to address the risks proactively.

text: A water and wastewater infrastructure program for 5 years. The program to replace and improvement of the old infrastructure. The program is 30B$. The responsible of the city is concerned due to the increases in the annual rate. After receiving the proposal for the key program which is almost 50% of the overall program, the program team is hired and the business case is approved. What should the program manager do next?

choices.text: Develop the transition plan.
Develop a program charter.
Develop the program management plan.
Develop the final report.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The business case is then further used as an input to the program charter and subsequently the program roadmap. The standard for program management page#34

text: You are a program manager of a large program. you assign project managers to 7 projects and continue to develop the program team. What is your strategy?

choices.text: Assign the project managers the responsibility of risks between the projects.
Motivate project managers to share expertise.
Motivate the project managers for more responsibilities.
Train and Coach the project managers to manage project resources.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
During the development of the program team, you can train and coach the project managers on how to manage the project resources.

text: You are a program manager. You completed the program benefits analysis and planning activities. What will that provide to the program?

choices.text: Information to establish key benefits KPIs.
Sustainment plan.
Benefits management plan to guide the work through the remainder of the program.
Transition plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
The purpose of the benefits analysis and planning phase is to establish the program benefits management plan and develop the benefits metrics and framework for monitoring and controlling both the components and the measurement of benefits within the program. Reference is the standard for program management page# 48.
program benefits management plan provides a process for managing the overall benefits management effort. Reference is the standard for program management page# 50.

text: The CEO requests the executive manager to issue a program to change the paper-based process to an automated process for airline tickets and boarding. The executive manager is assigned as a sponsor of the program and he has assigned a program manager for the program. Which of the following should be elements of the program charter?

choices.text: Scope, justification, outcomes, and scope management plan.
Scope, justification, outcomes, and stakeholder considerations.
Scope, justification, outcomes, and procurement management plan.
Scope, justification, outcomes, and benefits management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The charter does not contain any plans so A, C, and D are wrong. Reference is the standard for program management page# 93.

text: A project in your program is facing several change requests. You are concerned, that may delay the program milestones. There are insufficient skilled resources within the project to complete the milestones and change requests. What should you do to handle that risk?

choices.text: Prioritize which resources are critical to the project based on impact analysis of the critical change requests and updating the program roadmap.
Stop the change requests until overdue milestones have been completed and update the risk register.
Add the risk from lack of skilled resources to the issue log.

You should Prioritize the change requests to determine which are critical to the project according to impact analysis, then resource only critical change requests until the delayed milestones are achieved, and update the risk register.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
A: is wrong because, resource prioritization allows the program manager to prioritize the use of resources that are not available in abundance and to optimize their use across all components within the program. This often involves human resource planning to identify, document, and assign program roles and responsibilities to individuals or groups. Reference is the standard for program management page#133.

text: You are a program manager of a program with 7 projects. While you are in the planning phase, you request the project managers to develop detailed schedules of their projects, these schedules will be merged into the program master schedule. What should you do to ensure that the overall program life cycle will meet stakeholder expectations and deliver intended benefits?

choices.text: Develop a review of the project schedules.
Decompose the project schedules to minimize risk and better understand the dependencies and resource needs.
Develop a program WBS to align program execution with stakeholder expectations and the benefits management plan.
Decompose the component schedules to accelerate the execution to deliver value earlier than planned.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
A, B and D are the project managers' responsibility, not the program manager.
Program scope encompasses all benefits to be delivered by the program, which are reflected in the form of a program WBS.
The program WBS provides an overview of the program and shows how each component contributes to the objectives of the program.
The program WBS serves as the framework for developing the program master schedule and defines the program manager’s management control points. It is an essential tool for building realistic schedules, developing cost estimates, and organizing work. It also provides the framework for reporting, tracking, and controlling. The standard for program management page#123.

text: A program manager of a program is near the end. The program manager is terminated due to low performance. A new program manager has been assigned to manage this program. The last project of this program will be completed after 5 days. What should the new program manager do prior to the program closure?

choices.text: Review and update the benefits management plan to ensure that the first project meets stakeholder expectations and needs.
Determine with the sponsor who is responsible for benefits sustainment, and identify measures from the benefits management plan to measure success.
Request an immediate closing from the program steering committee.
Document the lessons learned from all stakeholders, and prepare mitigation strategies.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Develop a sustainment plan that identifies the processes, measures, metrics, and tools necessary for the management of benefits beyond the completion of the program in order to ensure the continued realization of intended benefits. exam content outline/ domain3/task3.

text: You are a program manager of the implementation of the CMC System. The company mandates the program after the failure of the sales department in the audits. After you start the program, you discovered that the sales department already has selected the technology that will be used in the CMC system. What should you do to ensure the program's success?

choices.text: Conduct a kick-off meeting, request the requirements from the sales department, conduct a design session, meet the steering committee with a solution that meets the requirements.
Meet with the CEO to discuss the risks related to the selected solution before the requirements have been analyzed.
Ask a program team to act as the program sponsor, meet the steering committee and get approval on the chosen solution.
Issue RFQ to select the solution and gain approval from the sales department.

You have to Conduct a kick-off meeting, request the requirements from the sales department, conduct a design session, meet the steering committee with a solution that meets the requirements.

text: At the last meeting, you presented the realized benefits to the program governance board. you are conducting the closing procedure for the program. What should you do next?

choices.text: Develop the integration management plan.
Start transitioning program resources and program management plans to update the program's status.
Get the sponsoring organization approval to begin closeout procedures to transition benefits sustainment to the supporting organization.
Update the contract management plan, stakeholders and archive them in the program information repository.

Once the transitioning activities are completed, the program manager receives approval from the sponsoring organization to formally close the program. 97.

Program-2

text: Your program contains 6 projects. The program sponsor requests you to deploy uniform management plans, procedures, technology, and processes across the program. Ignore the request and respond to the program sponsor if he asks again.

Meet with the sponsor and present the risks and benefits of the changes.

Since the sponsor is new, you have to discuss the issues and costs and other impacted areas with the stakeholders to get an appropriate option for all stakeholders and the sponsor.

text: You are a program manager of the integration of a billing system of company A. Company A acquires company B. Company B is aligned with the strategy of company A. Company B uses a different billing system than company A. The executive financial officer of Company-A consults you to study the two systems and inform him which solution would be the better option moving forward. What should you do?

choices.text: Search for the same system in other companies and ask the projects managers to document why the proposed system is better.
Determine the resources you needed to implement the proposed solution and clarify why this solution will save the company money.

Meet all stakeholders to perform stakeholder analysis and develop a program management plan.

The correct answer is C:
Conduct impact assessments for program changes and recommend decisions in order to obtain approval in accordance with the governance model. Exam content outline/Domain2/task29

text: The benefits delivery of a program is incrementally and the program is far from closure. The organization acquired another company and defined the new strategic objectives. What should the program manager do next?

choices.text: Add the new acquisition into the program to align with the new strategic objectives.

A is illogical.
