D is correct because the actual benefits delivered by the program components or program itself should be regularly evaluated against the expected benefits, as defined in the benefits management plan.
The Program Governance Performance Domain integrates with the Benefits Management Performance Domain to help ensure that the program is continuously aligned with the organizational strategy and that the intended value can still be achieved by the delivery of program benefits. The standard for program management page#52

text: In your program, the benefits were realized and you have asked the governance board to transition the program to the receiving area. Within the above context, what can you obtain from the post-review meeting?

choices.text: Risk register updates.
Performance plan report.
Feedback and lessons learned.
Benefits register updates.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
Conduct the post-review meeting by presenting the program performance report in order to obtain feedback and capture lessons learned. Exam content outline/ Domain2/Task34

text: You are an experienced program manager in your company. While you reviewing the formulation procedures in the company, you notice that there is no procedure to manage the suppliers. What should you do first to obtain the program approval?

choices.text: Create the stakeholder engagement plan.
Meet the program team to identify and analyze the stakeholders.
Project stakeholder analysis.
Analyze the business environment to identify key stakeholders, and then perform a stakeholder analysis.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
You just start preparing the charter to get approval, so no team and no projects at this time. Only D is correct.
Develop program charter using input from all stakeholders, including sponsors, in order to initiate and design program and benefits. Exam content outline/Domain2/Task1.

text: You are a program manager. The kickoff meeting had been done, but one of the key stakeholders was not present at the meeting. What should you do to ensure that he is familiar with the program's benefits and supports the program?

choices.text: Add the stakeholder expectations in the program charter and the benefits sustainment plan.

Meet with the key stakeholder to ensure stakeholder communication needs are documented in the communications management plan and that his expectations of benefits are documented in the benefits management plan.
Write a note about the stakeholder communication needs in the communications management plan and document their expectations in the benefits management plan.
Meet with the stakeholder and ensure that his expectations of benefits are documented in the benefits sustainment plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
A, C and D are wrong because, he is a key stakeholder, so you have to meet him first to ensure stakeholder communication needs are documented in the communications management plan and that his expectations of benefits are documented in the benefits management plan.
The benefits management plan defines each benefit and associated assumptions and determines how each benefit will be achieved. The standard for program management page# 50.

text: The program sponsor is concerned that the knowledge acquired throughout the program needs to be reused for future programs. What should you do as a program manager to ensure that knowledge is captured efficiently?

choices.text: Document the lessons learned in the program management plan.
Use review sessions after each program stage to document successes, issues, and lessons learned.
Document the lessons learned in the program training documents.
Document the lessons learned in the create event logs.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Lessons learned are critical assets to be reviewed when updating the program stakeholder register, program risk register, and program communications management plan or when considering major changes to the program management plan, including the introduction of new program components. The lessons learned database is updated when necessary, including at the completion of components and at the end of the program. The standard for program management page#130.

text: An organizFation assigned a program manager to manage a healthcare system. After 3 months he identifies an opportunity that will add value to stakeholders. The program sponsor approved the changes in the scope. The program manager should ensure that the results obtained by this opportunity are working in tandem with ………….

choices.text: Critical success function (CSF)
KPIs
Stakeholders register.
Program benefits management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The benefits (the results of the opportunity) should be added to the benefits management plan.
The benefits management plan is also used during the benefits delivery phase to verify that benefits are being realized as planned while providing feedback to program stakeholders and the program steering committee to facilitate successful benefit delivery. The standard for program management page#49
The benefits management plan is the documented explanation defining the processes for creating, maximizing, and sustaining the benefits provided by a project or program. The benefits management plan formally documents the activities necessary for achieving the program’s planned benefits. It identifies how and when benefits are expected to be delivered to the organization and specify mechanisms that should be in place to ensure that the benefits are fully realized over time. The standard for program management page#50

text: A chief executive officer issues a mandate to replace the paper-based system to an automated system. You and the sponsor work together and obtain the formal approval of the program charter. What should you do next as a program manager?

choices.text: Estimates for time, scope, resources, and cost.
Place a team to develop the program management plan.
Define the program delivery, and develop the resource management plan.
Update the benefits management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
After the approval of the program charter, you have to start the planning sub-phase to develop the program management plan and its subsidiary plans.
Program planning commences upon formal approval of the program charter by the program steering committee. In this phase, a governance structure is established, the initial program organization is defined, and a team is assembled to develop the program management plan. The standard for program management page#94.

text: You are a program manager of the upgrade of IT systems of your company. you are leading a program team from cross-cultural backgrounds and areas. You observe the varying levels of delivery excellence due to cultural differences. What should you do to achieve commitment to program goals and improve the engagement level of the team?

choices.text: Ask the project managers to address the issue.
Invite them to a party to support the communications and motivate team members.
Send email to all team members to deliver program objectives.
By a formal mentoring, coaching, and support program to handle cultural differences that will enable the team to work collaboratively.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Lead human resource functions by training, coaching, mentoring, and recognizing the team in order to improve team engagement and achieve commitment to the program’s goals. Exam content outline/Domain2/Task19.

text: You are assigned as a program manager during the preparation of the program. What should you do to obtain formal sponsor approval to begin the benefits delivery phase?

choices.text: Develop the program charter.
Establish a high-level program roadmap of milestones.
Create the program management plan based on the organization's strategic plan.
Define the program benefits in the benefits management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
We are in the preparation sub-phase (planning sub-phase). So A and B are wrong because already have been developed during the formulation sub-phase.
The program delivery phase begins after the program management plan is reviewed and formally approved. Programs are typically authorized by a program steering committee. The standard for program management page#95.

text: You are a program manager of the development of a new drug for your company pharma-Y. You write the program scope boundaries. Which of the following captures the program scope boundaries?

choices.text: Program benefits management plan.
Program scope statement.
Program schedule management plan.
Program WBS.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
An assessment of program scope, which includes boundaries, links to other programs/projects, and ongoing activities, is required as part of the program charter and to support initial cost, change, resource, risk, and schedule assessments. This initial program scope assessment develops the program scope statement from the program goals and objectives. The standard for program management page#110.

text: You are a program manager in the delivery phase. When should you approve the closure of a project in your program?

choices.text: When the benefits have been delivered.
When meeting or exceeding the acceptance criteria of the project.
When deliverables of the program are complete.
When deliverables of the project are complete.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
After the program components have produced deliverables and coordinated the successful delivery of their products, services, or results, these components are typically scheduled for closure or transition to operations or ongoing work. The standard for program management page#97.
Benefits transition activities ensure that individual program component results or outputs meet acceptance criteria, are satisfactorily closed or integrated into other program elements, and contribute to the overall achievement of the collective set of program benefits. The standard for program management page#53.

text: You are a program manager of the Enterprise management system (EMS). You are conducting an analysis to confirm the feasibility of the program. What should you do next to complete?

choices.text: Create the program mission.
Review of strategic goals and objectives.
Link the benefits to the EMS system.
Identify and document the initial risks for the EMS system.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Program formulation involves the development of the program business case which states the overall expected benefits to be addressed by the program in support of the strategic initiatives.
To demonstrate how the program will deliver the desired organizational benefits, the sponsor, sponsoring organization, and the program manager work closely together to:
1-Initiate studies and estimates of scope, resources, and cost; 2- Develop an initial risk assessment, 3- Develop a program charter and roadmap.
When the business case was developed prior to program formulation, it is revised and updated accordingly. Additionally, an initial risk assessment is conducted to analyze threats and opportunities. The standard for program management page#92.

text: The program steering committee has decided that the phase gate review meeting should be started by tomorrow to review the projects and the current phase to proceed to the next phase. One important part of the review is reporting and tracking the benefits realization. Which of the following is a point in the review?

choices.text: Ensure that the other requirements of the stage-gate have been met.
Monitoring and tracking on benefits plan.
Identify risks and benefits.
Meet with the stakeholders and collect their expectations.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
Phase-gate reviews are reviews at the end of a phase in which a decision is made to continue to the next phase, to continue with modification, or to end a program or program component. These enable governance to approve or disapprove the passage of a program from one significant phase to another.
Fulfillment of criteria for exiting the preceding phase and entering the succeeding phase. Reference is the standard for program management page#75

text: The risk manager of a program in company x. He informed you that in order to address all risks effectively, additional actions are required. What should you do next?

choices.text: Use the known risks.
Mitigate all project threats.
Establish a contingency reserve.
Use the schedule management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
The fund of the contingency plan and fallback plans of the identified risks from the contingency reserve. And addressing the failed responses, secondary risk and residual risks will be funded from the contingency reserve. The standard for project risk management.

text: You are a program manager of a large infrastructure program. the program contains 4 projects, 2 for water pipelines projects and 2 for electrical power cables. During the weekly meeting, a project manager of the pipelines project informed you that a project risk related to interdependency with the cable projects exceeds the thresholds. What should you do next?

choices.text: Update the program roadmap to mitigate the risk.
Ask the component manager to escalate to the program sponsor.
Incorporate the project risk into the program risk response strategy.
Ask the project manager to manage the risk at the project level.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
Since the risk is related to interdependencies between more than two projects, the project manager should monitor the risk if the risk increases than the threshold, he should escalate to the program level to assign an appropriate response plan.
project risk management activities focus on risks to project execution and success, while program risk management incorporates escalated project risks and program risks and also monitors interdependencies that affect multiple component projects.
Risk control is performed continuously at both the component level and the program level itself; project-level risks may be escalated to the program level or may have a cumulative effect that requires the risks to be addressed at the program level. The standard for program management page#98.

text: ou are a program manager of the construction of a ship. You and the client representative review the program management plan. The reprehensive of the client notice that 50% was planned, but only 40% has been completed. What should you do to ensure benefits realization?

choices.text: Escalate the issue to the program management office (PMO).
Conduct performance analysis and update the program business case.
Escalate to the program sponsor and the steering committee.
Perform impact analysis of the delay, review risks identify any corrective actions, and update the benefits management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
You cannot escalate without impact analysis.
The benefits management plan formally documents the activities necessary for achieving the program’s planned benefits. It identifies how and when benefits are expected to be delivered to the organization and specify mechanisms that should be in place to ensure that the benefits are fully realized over time. The standard for program management page#50

text: You are a program manager of a multinational software program. While you are in the planning phase, the contracts manager informed you that the primary subcontractor's agreement includes incentives that would potentially conflict with program objectives. What should you do first?

choices.text: Create a change request for approval from the governance board.
Ask program management office.
Review the program charter, then update program objectives accordingly.
Review the agreement, then create a program budget contingency.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
You have to review the program objectives that are included in the program charter, then update them according to the official channels.

text: While you are in the program delivery phase, a key stakeholder asks if the program is meeting its defined objectives. How do you demonstrate the program's progress?

choices.text: Submit additional program performance reports to the key stakeholder.
Maintain the program benefits register and provide it to the key stakeholder.
Submit the program charter to the key stakeholder for review.
Identify/Define key performance indicators (KPIs) to the key stakeholder.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Maintain benefits register and record program progress in order to
report the benefit to stakeholders via the communications plan. Exam content outline/domain3/task6.
The benefits register collects and lists the planned benefits for the program and is used to measure and communicate the delivery of benefits throughout the duration of the program. The benefits register contains: -
Key performance indicators and thresholds for evaluating their achievement;
Risk assessment and probability for achieving the benefit;
Status or progress indicator for each benefit;
Target dates and milestones for benefits achievement. The standard for program management page#47.
Option A is wrong because written additional performance reports. The performance reports contain huge information about the components and the program. Program performance reports include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. These reports generally provide current status information about what work has been accomplished (especially milestones and phase gates); what work remains to be completed; earned value; and risks, issues, and changes under consideration. The standard for program management page#101.
Option D is wrong because KPIs already have been defined in the program benefits management plan.

text: You are a program manager of the Upgrading IT infrastructure program. your organization drafts a new strategy to face the new challenge. One of these initiatives is upgrading the IT infrastructure and the strategic business direction to transfer the systems to a cloud base. How should you use the program mission to engage program stakeholders?

choices.text: Send the program mission statement to the stakeholders to ensure their support.
Update the program mission statement to address strategic goals, and the stakeholders’ concerns, interests, and expectations.
Document the current state, and how the program will support its mission.
Add the key stakeholders and their influence, power, and authority into the program's mission statement.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
Define the program mission statement by evaluating the stakeholders’ concerns and expectations in order to establish program direction. Exam content outline/Domain1/task4.
The mission should be based on evaluating the stakeholders’ concerns and expectations. Then the next step sends to the stakeholders.
Adding the stakeholders into the mission is wrong because the stakeholders and their influence, power, and authority should be added to the stakeholder register.

text: You are a program manager. You plan to address the negative variance and add a red mark in the status reports. What should you do?

choices.text: Collect all the details, perform impacts analysis, recommend corrective actions, and present the results to the steering committee for the decision.
Meet the project sponsors to get the impact analysis of the possible corrective actions regarding the negative variance.
Request additional funding from the sponsor.
Request the program team to collect all the details, perform impacts analysis, recommend corrective actions, and present the results to the steering committee for the decision.

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
You have to collect all the details, perform impacts analysis, recommend corrective actions, and present the results to the steering committee for the decision.
D is wrong: the team cannot preset the results to the steering committee, this is the responsibility of the program manager.

text: An important and influential stakeholder requests you to add a new technology immediately to the program to increase the benefits and accelerate the schedule. What should you do next as a program manager?

choices.text: Submit a change request to implement the new technology.
Tell the stakeholder that the program will not be changed.
Assess the new technology and discuss the results with the program governance board to determine the next steps.
Study the new technology and start the implementation in the next phase.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
B is wrong: you cannot refuse the request without analysis and decision from the steering committee.
A is wrong: you cannot submit the change request without analysis.
D is wrong: you cannot implement the new technology approval.

text: You have been informed that a successful resource being used in project X may also be used in project Y. What should you do first to optimize the utilization of this resource?

choices.text: Transfer project X resource to project Y.
Use the resource in project Y after the completion of project X.
Use another resource in project X.
Resource prioritization of the use of the resource to optimize the use across both projects X and Y.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
Resource prioritization allows the program manager to prioritize the use of resources that are not available in abundance and to optimize their use across all components within the program. This often involves human resource planning to identify, document, and assign program roles and responsibilities to individuals or groups. The standard for program management page# 133.

text: You are a program manager of an important program for your company. The program is performing good and all projects are on track and delivering their objectives. But the stakeholders are concerned about the new processes because the current environment may not reflect the actual performance of the program. the stakeholders fear that the program will fail. What should you do to assure that the performance is good in the current environment?

choices.text: Inform the stakeholders that the new processes are better than the current processes.
Meet with stakeholders to ensure they understand that the expectations for the new processes are superior to the current processes.
Meet with stakeholders, discuss and mitigate their concerns by changing the processes that will be delivered.
Advise the program governance board to motivate the stakeholders.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
You have to meet the stakeholders to ensure they understand that the expectations for the new processes are superior to the current processes.
C is wrong: you cannot change the processes without approval from the governance board.
Negotiate the support of stakeholders, including sponsors, for the program while setting clear expectations and acceptance criteria (for example, KPIs) for the program benefits in order to achieve and maintain their alignment to the program objectives. Exam content outline/ Domain4/Task3.

text: An important and critical program for the organization fails to achieve the intended benefits. The board of directors decided to terminate the sponsor and the CEO because they are responsible for the failure. Within the above context, what should the program manager do before closing the program?

choices.text: Update the benefits management plan.
Establish the PMIS.
Hand over all program knowledge and documentations to the deputy program manager.
Share the lessons learned with program teams.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The program failed, so it should be terminated, so no need to update any plan. The program manager is still available and is not terminated so he will not hand over any document to a deputy program manager. Just he will share the lessons learned to avoid that failure in the future.
Lessons learned should be readily accessible to any existing or future program to facilitate continuous learning and avoid similar pitfalls encountered in other programs. Reference is the standard for program management page#102.

text: You are a program manager of a program that contains 6 projects. The project manager of project X creates a communications management plan. But the project manager of project Y doesn’t know how to develop an appropriate communication management plan. What should you do to ensure communications on all projects are consistent?

choices.text: Change the project manager of project Y.
Request all project managers to use project X's communications management plan as a template.
You have to develop communications management plans for all components.
Develop a program communications management plan across all component projects.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
You have to develop a program communications management plan, and all the component managers should create communications management plans align with the program communication management plan.

text: Two project managers of X and Y projects in the XYZ program schedule the same scared resource at the same time to perform tasks in their projects. This causes an over-allocation; the program manager reviews the resource management plan and decides that project X can wait until project Y finishes the tasks. Which of the following are we talking about?

choices.text: Resource interdependency management.
Program schedule management planning.
Program risk management planning.
Project procurement planning

explanation:
The correct answer is A:
Resource interdependency management:
Resources are often shared among different components within a program, and the program manager should work to ensure that the interdependencies do not cause delays in benefits delivery. This is achieved by carefully controlling the schedule for scarce resources. The standard for program management page#133.

text: The sponsor of your program requests you to accelerate the implementation of a new manufacturing process to create a market advantage. You are concerned that several of the program goals and objectives could be affected negatively. What should you do?

choices.text: Inform the program sponsor that we have to follow the program management plan unless the change control board has approved changes to the plan.
Implement fast-tracking and update the resource management plan.
Document the concerns that program goals and objectives may be affected and present at the next program governance board review meeting for guidance and actions to be taken.
Create key performance indicators (KPIs) to monitor the benefits.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
You have to document the concerns that program goals and objectives may be affected and present at the next program governance board review meeting for guidance and actions to be taken.
B is wrong: you cannot implement any change without governance board approval.
A is wrong: you have to submit the issue to the governance board first.

text: You are a program manager of a new program. you want to establish direction and identify important aspects of a program to ensure that the context and framework of the program are correctly defined, assessed. Which of the following will support the above activity?

choices.text: Program procurement management plan.
Program scope statement.
Program benefits management plan.
Program schedule.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The program scope statement describes the boundaries of the program, and what is included, and what is out of the program.
Program scope defines the work required to deliver a benefit (major product, service, or result with specified features and functions) at the program level. The standard for program management page#110.

text: You are a program manager of a program in its last month of execution. You will get a bonus if the high management and the program governance board decide that the program is a success. How can you justify receiving the bonus upon program closure?

choices.text: Use customer satisfaction survey.
Update the business case analysis document indicating how each objective was attained.
Create a financial framework to align with metrics.
Present a report using the benefits management plan to clarify overall benefits realization.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The benefits management plan is also used during the benefits delivery phase to verify that benefits are being realized as planned while providing feedback to program stakeholders and the program steering committee to facilitate successful benefit delivery.

text: You take over the management of a large program from another program manager. While you are visiting the site, you notice the stakeholders upset due to a lack of communications and updates about the program. What should you do first?

choices.text: Review the program management plan.
Review the program stakeholder engagement plan.
Escalate to the program sponsor.
Review the program communications management plan and stakeholder register.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
The program communication management plan includes who needs what information, when they need it, how it will be given to them, and by whom. Reference is the standard for program management page#112.

text: You are a program manager of a program that contains several projects. The project manager of project X escalates a risk to you. After the risk assessment, you determine that the risk may impact other projects within the program. The risk has a low impact and probability. What should you do first?

choices.text: Ask for additional reserve from the sponsor.
Document the risk details and analysis in the program risk register.
Ask the project managers to manage the risk at the project level.
Meet with the project manager to develop a risk response strategy.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The risk will impact more than one component, so it should be escalated to the program level. Since the risk is a program-level risk, it should be added to the program risk register with qualitative and quantitative analysis and the appropriate risk response strategy.

text: You are a program manager of a program that contains 100 stakeholders. You develop the communications management plan that defines how the communication should happen, what should be communicated. Which one of the following is input to the information distribution process?

choices.text: CCB.
EV.
Stakeholder analysis plan.
Performance reports.

explanation:
The correct answer is D:
a critical element of program communications, as it supports both program governance and stakeholder engagement. Program reporting is the activity of consolidating performance and reporting related data to provide stakeholders with information about how resources are being used to deliver program benefits. Reference is the standard for program management page#127.
Program performance reports include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. These reports generally provide current status information about what work has been accomplished (especially milestones and phase gates); what work remains to be completed; earned value; and risks, issues, and changes under consideration. Reference is the standard for program management page#101

text: Which of the following will define how the benefits of the program will be transferred to the operations?

choices.text: Program transfer plan.
Program benefits transition plan.
Benefits transfer management plan.
Program change management plan.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The purpose of the benefits transition phase is to ensure that program benefits are transitioned to operational areas and can be sustained once they are transferred. Reference is the standard for program management page# 53.

text: You are a program manager for the construction of an international program that will impact the local community. you need to determine the best approach for communications. A garden will be built for the local community’s use as a condition of the program. What should you do to ensure community support?

choices.text: Meet with the program sponsor and community representatives to review the program scope.
Arrange an advocacy group and facilitate community engagement.
You should negotiate the program scope with community representatives.
The community representatives should be a part of the program governance board.

explanation:
The correct answer is C:
You have to negotiate the scope with the community representative. In a negotiation, each party tries to persuade the other to agree with his or her point of view. By negotiating, all involved parties try to avoid arguing but agree to reach some form of compromise.
Develop and foster relationships with stakeholders, including sponsors, in order to improve communication and enhance their support for the program. domain4/task7.
stakeholder engagement concerns negotiation of objectives, agreement on desired benefits, commitment to resources, and ongoing support throughout the program. Reference is standard for program management Page#58
Successful program managers utilize strong leadership skills to set clear stakeholder engagement goals for the program team to address the change the program will bring. These goals include engaging stakeholders to assess their readiness for change, planning for the change, providing program resources and support for the change, facilitating or negotiating the approach to implement change, and obtaining and evaluating the stakeholders’ feedback on the program’s progress. Reference is standard for program management Page#60

text: You have completed the program and you want to start program closure. Which of the following can prevent you to start program closure?

choices.text: Failure to update the scope management plan.
Failure to get approval from the program governance board.
Failure to update the procurement management plan.
Failure to update the risk register.

explanation:
The correct answer is B:
The program steering committee reviews and makes decisions on recommendations for the closure of programs. It assesses whether conditions warranting the program are satisfied and that recommendations for the closure of a program are consistent with the current organizational vision, mission, and strategy. Reference is the standard for program management page#78

text: You have been assigned as a program manager for your new program. Your component project team consists of eight members to date. Recently, you've started observing slippage on your component project schedule due to resource constraints and you think there is a possibility of not meeting the project timeline. Which of the following would help you take the necessary steps to address this scenario?

choices.text: Procurement management plan
Risk management plan
Schedule management plan
Communications management plan

explanation:
Answer B is correct. Obviously, the possibility of not meeting the project deadline is a component project risk, as the program manager sees it. The risk management plan is a program management plan component that describes how risk management activities will be structured and conducted.
Answer D is incorrect. The communications management plan defines the information and communication needs of the program stakeholders depending on who needs what information, when they need it, how it will be given to them, and by whom.
Answer A is incorrect. The program procurement management plan is a program management plan component that describes how goods and services will be acquired by the program from outside of the performing organization.
Answer C is incorrect. The program schedule management plan is a program management plan component that establishes the criteria and the activities for developing, monitoring, and controlling the schedule.
Lesson: Program Activities
Objective: Program Definition Phase Activities
Exam Objectives:
2.0 Domain II: Program Life Cycle
2.30 Task 30: Manage risk in accordance with the risk management plan in order to ensure benefits realization.

text: During the meeting, a program plan report shows that the stakeholders are not efficiently engaged in the Tech development program. Who among the following is responsible for making sure that all stakeholders are adequately and appropriately engaged throughout the duration of the Tech development program?

choices.text: Program manager
Stakeholders themselves
Corporate PMO
Program sponsor

explanation:
Answer A is correct. Stakeholder engagement is a continuous program activity due to the fact that the stakeholders' list and their attitudes and opinions change as the program progresses and delivers benefits. Throughout the program's duration, the primary role of the program manager is to make sure that all stakeholders are adequately and appropriately engaged.
Lesson: Program Stakeholder Engagement
Objective: Program Stakeholder Engagement
Exam Objectives:
4.0 Domain IV: Stakeholder Management
4.1 Task 1: Identify stakeholders, including sponsors, and create the stakeholder matrix in order to document their position relative to the program.

text: Which of the following statements are true about a program? Each correct answer represents a complete solution. Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A program is a group of activities managed individually for obtaining benefits.
A program is managed as a stand-alone project, within a project, or within a portfolio.
A program is conducted for generating the outputs and outcomes required to support an organization's strategic objectives.
A program is a group of related projects that are managed together using coordinated processes and techniques.

explanation:
Answers D and C are correct.
A program is a group of related projects that are managed together using coordinated processes and techniques. It is conducted for generating the outputs and outcomes required to support an organization's strategic objectives.
Answer A is incorrect because a program is a group of related projects, subsidiary programs, and program activities managed in a coordinated manner for obtaining benefits that are not available from managing them individually.
Answer B is incorrect because a project is managed as a stand-alone project, within a program, or a portfolio.
Lesson: Introduction
Objective: What is Program?

text: Which of the following uses change management for monitoring and controlling the impact of variability on its baselines?

choices.text: Project
Program
Portfolio
Subsidiary program

explanation:
Answer A is correct. Projects use change management for monitoring and controlling the impact of variability on their baselines and managing the impact of variance caused by known risks and unknown risks that were triggered on its path to a project's completion.
Answer B is incorrect. In programs, change management is used for understanding and controlling the variability of each component's schedule, cost, and output.
Answer D is incorrect. Subsidiary programs are programs that are sponsored and conducted for pursuing a subset of goals important to the primary program, and it also uses change management for understanding and controlling the variability of each component's schedule, cost, and output.
Answer C is incorrect. In portfolios, change management is about managing the cumulative and collective impact of change to achieve the desired outcome, ROI, or benefit realization.
Lesson: Program Management Performance Domains
Objective: Program and Project Distinctions

text: Your organization currently requires funding for preparing a critical program. Which of the following cannot be considered as a source for funding?

choices.text: Supported with internal and external sources of funding
Funded and managed entirely by the program team
Managed within a single organization but funded separately
Funded entirely within a single organization

explanation:
Answer B is correct. The type of program and the funding structure dictate the financial environment for the program's duration. Funding models vary, from those that are funded entirely within a single organization, managed within a single organization but funded separately, funded and managed entirely from outside the parent organization, and supported with internal and external sources of funding.

2.0 Domain II: Program Life Cycle
2.27 Task 27: Manage program level issues (for example, human resource management, financial, technology, scheduling) by identifying and selecting a course of action consistent with program scope, constraints, and objectives in order to achieve program benefits.

text: Your program team is working with stakeholders in the ABC program. How should they deal with the stakeholders' issues and concerns?

choices.text: They should select the important issues and concerns only to record.
They should accept and log stakeholder issues and concerns and should manage them to closure.
They should review the stakeholders' issues and concerns with the program manager before logging them.

explanation:
Answer B is correct. As the program team works together with the stakeholders, they should gather/accept and log stakeholder issues and concerns and manages them to closure. They should not filter the issues and concerns of the stakeholders. Using an issue log for documenting, prioritizing, and tracking issues helps the entire program team to understand the feedback received from the stakeholders.

text: Who is responsible for performing management activities ensuring that the program is run within the governance framework while managing the day-to-day program activities?

choices.text: Program sponsor
Program governance board
Program manager
Project manager

explanation:
Answer C is correct. A program manager is responsible for performing management activities ensuring that the program is run within the governance framework while managing the day-to-day program activities. The program manager also makes sure that the program team understands and acts in accordance with the governance procedures and the underlying governance principles.

text: A program manager has been assigned a new program in her organization. She is required to perform the stakeholder analysis activity for her new assigned program. Which of the following will help her better to obtain feedback from a greater number of stakeholders?

choices.text: Focus groups
Questionnaires and surveys
Historical information
Individual interviews

explanation:
Answer B is correct. After listing all the major stakeholders in the stakeholder register, the program manager is required to categorize them to start analyzing them. The categorization will show the differences in their requirements, expectations, or influence. Some important information needs to be obtained from stakeholders for better understanding the organizational culture, politics, and concerns related to the program, along with the overall impact of the program. This information may be acquired through historical information, individual interviews, focus groups, or questionnaires and surveys. Questionnaires and surveys allow the program team to obtain feedback from multiple stakeholders than is possible with interviews, historical information, or focus groups.

text: Which of the following is a core part of the program infrastructure and helps in establishing consistent policy, standards, and training for programs in the organization?

choices.text: PMIS
OPM
WBS
PMO

choices.text: Program Benefits Management
Program Governance
Program Life Cycle Management

Program sponsor
Program team
Program responder

The stakeholder register

text: Bob, as a program manager, has reached to the closure phase of his long-running program. Before closing his program, Bob wants to be sure that he is not leaving behind any important task. text: A software company is working on introducing a new technology that will reduce the labor cost, which will be done through a program. Which of the following will be the first step in the sequence of program activities?

Business case

choices.text: Program governance plan
Stakeholder engagement plan
Sustainment plan
Program charter

Holly, the project sponsor, has asked him to perform an analysis for the program that specifies the program objectives and identifies the internal and external factors that are favorable and unfavorable for achieving those objectives.
