explanation: The P-WBS is based on "deliverables", and does not really contain any milestones or phase gates. It does not contain all the work packages in all the projects - it only goes up to a level of granularity that the program manager wants to manage at. The P-WBS does not really contain a detailed description of the program packages. It merely breaks up the program deliverables into smaller, more manageable units.

text: A program in a company with a diversified portfolio is meant to come up with a cross-cutting reporting framework. The program is cross-functional and crosses company boundaries as well. What would be the biggest challenge for the program manager in this situation?

choices.text: Integrations and interfaces across projects
Getting the necessary resources assigned to the projects
Getting a clear scope definition for the projects, working within the respective functions
Getting executive sponsorship for the program

explanation: Typically the biggest challenge in a matrix (cross-functional) organization is one of communication. This will likely lead to issues while managing the integrations and interfaces where communication is most essential.

text: As part of developing new hybrid engines for smaller vehicles, a project discovered an engine component that might also save cost of building conventional engines. It needs additional tests and prototyping before it can be commercialized. The project manager brought it up at a program review meeting and requested for additional funding to carry out these tests. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Accept the request as there is a possibility to deliver additional benefits for the organization
Spin off a different program for cost reduction of conventional engines
Contact the program steering committee for advice about the possibility of a new dimension to the program
Refuse the request as the activity is not aligned with the program objective of hybrid engine development

explanation: The new component might help the program deliver additional benefits and hence it has merit. It does need to be taken to the steeting committee to ensure that it is an appropriate change to make in the context of the overall organization.

text: Which of the following quality policies are most suitable at the program level?

choices.text: All projects will perform prescribed acceptance tests and benchmarks for the raw materials being used
The program will follow applicable safety and security standards
The detailed test plans from all projects will have to be reviewed and signed off by the PMO
A mandatory training for introducing "culture of quality" will be rolled out for all team members on all projects

explanation: The program should lay down policies and standards that can be applicable to multiple components. The adherence to safety and security standards is an example. The program should not intrude on project level quality issues and use of a peanut butter approach would likely backfire

text: One of the projects within a program was being executed in a different division that comprises of staff derived mainly from the acquisition of a startup company. Several quality issues were detected within this component as a result of the lack of focus on quality. The culture was more oriented towards innovation than about ensuring quality. What should the program manager do to address this situation?

choices.text: Relax the quality specifications for some time to allow for the culture change within the division
Ask the project manager to deal with quality issues with an iron hand and give her clear quality objectives
Replace the project manager with another one having more focus on quality
Meet with the team members along with the project manager to convey the importance of quality

explanation: Option A implies passing the buck to the project manager which may or may not work. Option B is a delaying tactic and will do nothing to improve the situation. Getting rid of the project manager may not solve the root cause - and may actually backfire. The best answer is to take the team into confidence.

text: A program manager was invited to review the staffing management plan for one of the component projects. Which of these should the program manager be most concerned about?

choices.text: Matching the skill sets during the recruitment process
Optimal utilization of the shared resources
Management of attrition rates
Diversity and inclusiveness

explanation: One of the ways in which program managers provide additional benefits and control is by ensuring that the resources are shared and their utilization across projects is optimized. Especially for the critical resources, this is what the program manager will focus on.

text: What would be the best set of criteria to evaluate whether people should be on the program steering committee?

choices.text: Communication skills, Technical expertise, Political savvy
Decision making authority, Insight and ability to represent stakeholder groups
Functional and technical expertise, Amount of interest in the program
Motivational and leadership skills, Technical expertise

explanation: The steering committee for a program needs to represent the stakeholders, make decisions to steer the program in the right direction and have the insight to provide direction. Among the options provided, B covers these aspects the most

text: A project manager in consultation with the program manager decided to outsource a complex piece of work on her project, as the project did not have in-house technical expertise. The contract is about to be finalized. The project manager requests the program manager for suggestions regarding the appropriate contract type to be used. What should be the program manager's response?

choices.text: The program should have an overall standard contract template and the same should be used for all projects within the program
Cost reimbursable with penalty clauses
Cost reimbursable with incentive clauses
Fixed price with penalty clauses

explanation: Use of standard contract type would be fine if this was a routine transaction being followed by multiple projects within a program. From the question, there is no evidence to suggest that it is. The work is known to be technically complex and the scope of work is unstable. Therefore fixed price contract cannot be used. Among options B and C which both recommend cost reimbursable contracts, option B is best because it would provide an incentive to the vendor.

text: Work under a large government program is offered under tender to a number of private firms. Some of the private firms are also competitors in specific businesses but have to collaborate for the purpose of this program. How should the steering committee be structured for this program?

choices.text: The government should invite individuals from the public who are perceived to be neutral to serve on the board
Government representatives, supplier representatives and selected stakeholders
There could be a federated structure where the main board overseas overall program and sub-programs have their own boards
The board should comprise of representatives from the government and all the suppliers

explanation: Under a complex program with multiple suppliers, there may need to be a different governing structure (see Section 6.1 in the Standard for Program Management, 4th edition). A single board may not be able to effectively oversee the entire program

text: A traffic management program relies on sensors and devices located in multiple locations and developed by different projects. The data from these devices is brought into a central server and analyzed. What should be the most important aspect of the program quality plan?

choices.text: Integration tests for the equipment with the server
Calibration of the devices to the necessary precision
Checking boundary value conditions
Stress tests for the data repository

explanation: A, B and D are tests that should be part of the project level quality plans. C addresses integrations and is more likely to be part of the program level quality plan.

text: A pharmaceutical company is working on a program with presence in 5 countries and 14 cities. Work at each site is to carry out specific trials and is treated as a separate project. The findings are collated and coordinated at the program level and more such components are set up as needed. The following risks have been identified. Which one should require the most attention from the program manager?

choices.text: Though the client is pretty demanding about dates and timely completion
One of the cities is in a remote hilly region, causing high transportation costs
The program earns revenues in dollars and spends in 5 different currencies, hence exchange rate fluctuations is a risk
One of the cities has introduced a new tax that might impact the finances for one of the components

explanation: This question is essentially about prioritizing risks from a program perspective. A and C are valid risks, but probably will be managed by the respective project managers. B and D are both program level risks. D says the client is particular about dates and is quite generic - all clients are particular about dates; whereas B is more specific and therefore seems to be higher priority.

text: A program utilizes the services of 8 vendors, many of them in similar or overlapping areas. A new program manager has recently taken over the program. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Set up a new component to consolidate the vendors to a smaller number within a 6 month time period
Meet the project managers and the procurement manager to identify opportunities to optimize
Set up a policy granting autonomy to the project managers for deciding the vendors to be used on their projects
Review the performance and rank the vendors, gradually eliminating the bottom performers

explanation: The program manager should definitely look for consolidation opportunities, but it should be done in consultation. Option A and B are too specific without providing any justification about why the plan is being recommended. Option C loses out on the potential benefits of consolidation.

text: Project X is part of a program. An activity on the critical path for the Project, is also critical for the overall program. The program has incentive and penalty clauses in terms of schedule. The team working on the task has estimated the time required to be 20 days. The manager of project X feels it can be done in 15 days, whereas the program manager thinks it should take no more than 10 days and is keen to reduce the time. What can be done to resolve the issue?

choices.text: Outsource the work to a third party with strict time deadlines
Use the team's estimates and look for other options to reduce the time
Ask the team to crash the schedule down to 10 days to meet the program's expectations
Use the project manager's estimate and negotiate the program level expectations

explanation: Ultimately, it is the team's estimate which is most likely to be closest to reality. While reconciling top-down and bottom-up expectations, different options like crashing can be used, but no plan will be realistic until the team has bought into it. Outsourcing is an extreme step (especially for a difference of 10 days in the time estimates) - and it need not be the first option to explore in this case

text: A shared test lab is used by many projects within a program. While Project A was performing tests, one of the electric equipment malfunctioned and it needs a down time of 2 days. Project A's work is not likely to be affected by the delay as it has adequate buffer, but the cascading effect on other components is not predictable at present. How should this event be documented?

choices.text: It should be logged into project A's risk register and the program issue register
It should be logged in the risk register for the project A as well as the program
It should be logged in project A's issue register and the program risk register
It should be logged in the issue register for both project A and the program

explanation: The event of malfunction and delay has already occurred, so it is an Issue (not a risk) for Project A. For the program this gives rise to possibility of cascading delays on other projects, so it needs to be logged in the program risk register.

text: The quarterly financial results of an organization were disappointing. As a result, the funding for many of the strategic programs may be cut - some to the extent of 50-70%. How should a program manager react to this information?

choices.text: Approach the program sponsor with a solid business case and negotiate for protecting the program's budget
Inform all project managers that they would need to replan for a 50% budget reduction
Pad next financial period's budget request by 50% to allow for a cut during negotiations
Review the overall program budget and re-align funding to the most critical components

explanation: Since the cut is drastic, the program manager needs to review and shrink the budget needs to the lowest common denominator. One of the techniques to do this is to review where each item of budget, and ensure it is absolutely necessary to be funded

text: A program is time critical and in the spotlight. One of the projects within the program is delayed by 1 month due to the late arrival of a deliverable from a vendor. The project is not on the critical path and the delay is not significant from the overall program perspective. How should the program manager present this information in the next review by the program steering committee?

choices.text: Escalate this delay and ask for the vendor to be blacklisted
Show the program status as "on schedule" but increase the risk level
Report the overall program as "on schedule" due to the non-critical nature of the project
Remove the late project from the reports to prevent unnecessary alarm

explanation: The program manager should be transparent and not try to hide the facts. The fact is that the overall program may still be on schedule but the delay (and the possibility of a reduced buffer) indicates higher risk. It is not clear whether the delay from the vendor's end is cause to blacklist at this point. The program manager needs to manage what can be managed at the program level and maintain clarity at the same time.

text: A program manager is contemplating calling a meeting to discuss the impact of an issue. The problem has to do with some changes to technical specifications that have been suggested and might result in rework on some projects and ultimately have an impact on the program costing. Who should be the invitees to this meeting?

choices.text: The program manager, concerned project managers and technical experts
The program steering committee, program sponsor and the program manager
The program manager, the concerned project managers and the program management office
The project managers, project teams and program management office

explanation: Technical experts are needed as the change is technical in nature, and technical advice may be relevant to the discussion. Also, the program manager first needs to understand the full impact of the change after discussing with the project managers before it can go to the program steering committee.

text: A program manager working at a bank is suggesting roll out of a new system for managing cash counters across the bank which will speed up transactions and reduce customer waiting time. What is the least effective articulation of the benefits of this program to the bank's executives?

choices.text: It will improve customer satisfaction by reducing wait times
It will increase traffic for the bank's vendors thereby increasing their revenues
It will enable bankers to have more meaningful conversations with the customers and offer them higher value services
Branches will be able to serve more customers which will lead to increase revenues

explanation: All the benefits are probably valid, but benefit B is probably more relevant for the bank's vendors more than the bank itself. While presenting to the bank's executives, the narrative should focus on the benefits most relevant to the audience.

text: Who is responsible for authorizing a component within a program?

choices.text: Sponsor
Program management office
Executives in the performing organization
Portfolio manager

explanation: The sponsor funds a component within the program. The Executives authorize the sponsor and the program steering committee. The portfolio manager is responsible for managing a portfolio. The program management office plays a supporting role to a program and does get into decision making or authorization.

text: A travel company wants to focus on customer delight as a theme. They are primarily focused on word-to-mouth publicity and publicity through social media. With this in mind, they have started a program to increase customer satisfaction and keeping them happy with every interaction. Which is the best way to figure out if the customer satisfaction is going up?

choices.text: Measure the cancellation or changes in the itineraries to track potential dissatisfaction contribution
Conduct customer satisfaction survey on a rating scale and monitor the trend
Measure the net promoter score - how many customers are recommending them to others
Measure the average spend by a customer per year and plot a trend line

explanation: Since the company relies heavily on word-to-mouth publicity, the net promoter score would be the best indicator of customer satisfaction

text: A program manager is designing a balanced scorecard for a research oriented program. The program is experimenting with different extraction methods to remove harmful chemicals from effluents and come up with commercially usable techniques. Which one of the following would be least useful as success measures for the program?

choices.text: Safety record
Compliance with environmental regulations
Commercial value of the methods invented
Budget variance

explanation: This program involves uncertainty about the outcome and complexity. Budget variance reports are less relevant than the others. Even if the budget was exceeded, it might be worthwhile if the returns were good. On the other hand, ending up under budget may not necessarily indicate success either, unless the program delivered the benefits in the form of developing usable technology.

text: Project A is part of a program. During risk identification and response planning, the project manager had identified a risk, for which the response plan was identified as "Accept". The risk event has actually occurred, causing a cost increase of $300,000. How should this be handled within the program?

choices.text: The contingency reserves of Project A should be used
The management reserves of project A should be used
The project manager and program manager should approach the sponsor for additional funding
The contingency reserves of the overall program should be used

explanation: The risk was already identified, hence it is a known unknown. Contingency reserves are used for known unknowns. The program level reserve is not a replacement for the project level reserves, hence this comes from the project contingency reserve.

text: A scientific program is experimenting with technologies meant to harness nuclear energy in more efficient ways. The project manager has identified a risk that there is a possibility of radiation losses which can be hazardous to human life. The project does not have sufficient reserves to cover liabilities, hence the project manager has proposed to move the experiment to a different country where the liability clauses are lenient. This requires additional funding, so a change request has been generated. What should the program manager recommend?

choices.text: Decision should be left to the Program Sponsor after a discussion with the program steering committee
The project should be encouraged to find ways to avoid the risk
Opinion should be sought from the Legal department as they are in a better position to take a call about liabilities
Decision should be based on a comparison of the additional cost of movement and the expected value of the liabilities arising from radiation

explanation: The scenario seems to indicate that the there are potential safety issues including potential risk to human life. This being the case, the shifting of experiments to another country simply to escape liabilities is an unethical practice. The project manager should be asked to try to reduce the risk.

text: Which communication approach is most appropriate for a relief and rehabilitation program?

choices.text: Press releases and community outreach, stakeholder group meetings, social media
Program dashboard, regular formal and compliance reporting, TV advertising
Program dashboard, stakeholder group meetings, public website
Public website, 1X1 meetings, email campaign

explanation: The program is public and visible, therefore there needs to be a public outreach and attempts to reach a larger population through different media.

text: Cement is required by many projects on a construction project and there is a high likelihood that the cost of cement may increase in the near future due to a demand spike in the economy. What is the best way for the program to mitigate this risk?

choices.text: The project managers should ensure they have adequate contingency reserves built in to take care of the additional spend
The program manager should re-plan the whole program and file a revised budget proposal
Get a forecast from economists about the future movement of prices
The program manager should explore possibilities of locking in prices by entering into forward contracts

explanation: Option-C represents a pro-active strategy and is probably the only one that "mitigates". A is "Accept", B is "Avoid" and D is just a preparatory step

text: A program was initiated by a software company to launch a product suite. After the release, it was discovered that there were significant problems with the integration of the products within the suite. Who is accountable for these issues?

choices.text: Program manager
Program sponsor
Concerned project managers
Manager of the quality assurance team

explanation: Deming's quality philosophy was Total Quality Management (TQM) which involves being proactive, utilizing accountability and leadership. Especially since the issues were found in the integration of the suite, it is squarely in the program domain.

text: In a program with a large number of projects, who is responsible for stakeholder management and why?

choices.text: The program sponsor will deal with the program level stakeholders and the program manager being the sponsor of the projects, will deal with the project level stakeholders
The program manager will need to be in touch with stakeholders throughout the program; the project managers will have less frequent contact
Program manager will focus on program level stakeholders whereas the project managers will focus on project level stakeholders and there will be some areas of overlap
When a project is part of a program, the project managers may not be involved in stakeholder management as it will be performed at program level

explanation: Stakeholder management is the responsibility of the program team. The program manager and project managers will all have to chip in at their level. All other statements have some shortcomings.

text: A project manager was recently promoted to become the program manager for the overall program that his project was originally part of. She approached the program management office for guidance about applying the concept of critical path for the overall program. What is the most correct response?

choices.text: The program manager needs to talk to the sponsor and determine the critical path based on the critical business requirements
The critical path of the projects can be summed together to make the critical path for the program
Critical path applies to individual projects bt is a project level concept and does not apply to programs
The program manager needs to work with the project managers to identify the critical path for the program

explanation: The critical path of the projects cannot be summed together to make the critical path for the program. The projects within the program will have dependencies among them and the program manager needs to discuss with the project managers to figure out the critical path for the program.

text: Program Governance is an important area of focus for the program manager. Which of the following is the best set of focus areas for program governance?

choices.text: Approve and authorize the program and the components of the program, Communicate the risks and uncertainties, Maintain historical records and templates
Conducting periodic review of the program and components, Ensuring the program's components contribute to overall program benefit, Keeping the program on track with regard to the plan
Establishing interface with the sponsoring organization, Determining the degree of autonomy and oversight, Ensuring alignment of the program with the organizational strategy
Ensure the program adheres to organizational standards, Facilitating engagement of stakeholders, Participating in the program planning

explanation: The best answer is A. Maintaining historical records and templates is a PMO function and not necessarily a part of program governance. Also, the issuance and management of components is largely within the program purview, as is program level planning.

text: The output of Project B is a critical input for project A. Project A and B are both part of the same program. From the program perspective, this is an example of:

choices.text: External dependency
Mandatory dependency
Finish-to-Start dependency
Internal dependency

explanation: From the perspective of project B, the dependency is on another project, hence it is an external dependency. However from a program perspective, it is an internal dependency since both are components of the same program. There is not enough information to say if it is mandatory or finish-to-start.

text: Why does it make sense for the development and maintenance activities to sometimes reside within the same program?

choices.text: It simplifies the management of the operations and projects
Customers benefit from the technical expertise of the development teams
Maintenance is revenue positive and this helps the program to invest more in the development
Sharing of knowledge across development and maintenace may be mutually beneficial

explanation: A is a very generic statement. There is no guarantee that option B will actually occur or that the customers are lacking in technical knowledge. D may be valid, but the funds would accrue to the organization any way. C makes most sense because it provides a clear indication about how maintenance operation and development projects can benefit by co-existing within a program

text: A project manager was recently promoted to become the program manager for the overall program that his project was originally part of. How should her approach to change management evolve?

choices.text: Project level change management is all about understanding and meeting changing requirements, whereas program level change management is about delivering benefits in changing environment
Project level change management focuses on the triple constraints, program level change management focuses on risk, procurement, communication and stakeholders as well
Project level change management looks to avoid change, program level change management looks to initiate change
Program level change management is triggered by project level changes

explanation: The program manager looks at changes from the point of view of impact to the ability of the program to deliver benefits, whereas the projects look at it from delivering on the requirements (encoded by the triple constraints)

text: A large program involving a substantial financial outlay is about to close the program definition phase. Which of the following may NOT be available yet?

choices.text: Business case, Governance structure and approval to proceed
Program and Project charters, Appointment of the program and project managers, initiated components
Business case and high level Roadmap along with Program Charter
Program charter, program roadmap, Program manager and key program team assignments

explanation: The components of a program are usually initiated during the benefits delivery phase - project charter and initiated components may not be ready at this stage.

text: How does the program manager contribute to the benefits management function in a program?

choices.text: Identify benefits, plan for benefits delivery, ensure benefits are realized and transitioned
Identify, Develop, transition and sustain the benefits
Develop the benefits, measure the benefits and sustain the benefits
Create the benefits register, benefits realization plan and the benefits transition plan

explanation: The program manager identifies benefits, plans for them and ensures that the program takes steps to realize, monitor and transition the benefits. The program manager may not be responsible for sustenance of the benefits after they are transitioned. B represents the best set of activities for the program manager to focus on.

text: One of the projects in a program made use of a review template and a review workflow process that helped it to reduce defects at source and improve operational efficiencies. The program manager was impressed with the technique and findings at a routine project review. What is the best action for the program manager after this?

choices.text: Present the findings to the program steering committee and ask for additional funding to roll out the techniques across the rest of the program
Evaluate if similar techniques will be able to help other components within the program as well
As the cost of quality will reduce, make adjustments to the program budget and determine how to deploy the savings
Reward the project manager for this achievement and showcase this at the organization's quality circle meeting

explanation: The program manager should definitely consider if the techniques can be useful elsewhere in the program. Although the other actions are also valid and important, this is perhaps the most important step for the program manager to follow through on

text: What is the difference between benefits and deliverables in the context of the program?

choices.text: Deliverables are planned both at the program and project level, but benefits can result only at the program level
Benefits may be tangible or intangible, deliverables are usually tangible
Benefits are specific and measurable outcomes, deliverables represent the tangible or intangible value to the organization
Benefits are usually realized only at the end, deliverables are produced throughout the program

explanation: The benefits from a program could be tangible (e.g. specific product, or process or result) or intangible (e.g. improved morale, better capabilities, etc.). Deliverables are usually tangible, and more easily recognized and validated. Among the given statements, this one comes closest to correctly explaining the differences between benefits and deliverables

text: A program at a pharmaceutical company is to quickly develop and launch generic versions of medicines going off patent protection. One of the steering committee members suggested that the test and pre-launch marketing should also be managed under the program. These activities are currently handled by a different organization and under a different budget. What should the program manager recommend?

choices.text: Leave the decision with the program steering committee
Merge only if the funding and management of the activities can be centralized under one organization
Merge the activities as it seems aligned with the benefits being delivered by the program
Do not merge the activities with the program as it will dilute focus on core activities

explanation: The program may include "other work" if it is relevant to the cause. It does not matter if the funding and management control of the other work resides outside the program's organizational boundaries.

text: A highly visible program is also very time critical, with severe penalties attached to delayed completion. The program includes several projects, which eventually roll into operations. One of the project managers has been consistently under-performing in terms of meeting deadlines. The Program Board is concerned and asks the Program Manager to take visible action. How should the program manager proceed?

choices.text: Replace the project manager with somebody with greater expertise in project scheduling
Personally take over the management of the project till it comes back on track
Focus on keeping the rest of the projects in the program on track
Investigate the causes of the delays with the project manager and concerned stakeholders

explanation: The causes of the delay need to be investigated before appropriate action can be determined

text: A program is about to shut down and transition to operations. One of the projects within the program received a change request. How should the project manager deal with this?

choices.text: Fast track work on the change so that it does not delay the project or program closure
Push back on the change in view of the fact that the program is about to enter into closure
See if the change is aligned with the overall program objectives before moving forward
Raise the change request to the program level along with the impact analysis and present some alternatives to accommodate the change

explanation: The project manager should not unilaterally push back or accept it. The evaluation of alignment with program objectives is really a program manager responsibility. Raising the change request and presenting the evaluation is the logical thing for the project manager to use.

text: Which of the following is a good practice regarding resource management for a program and its components?

choices.text: Resource management is based on the expense thresholds; up to the threshold, the resources are managed by projects and more expensive ones at the program level
Human resources should ideally be managed by the projects, whereas other resources like budgets and finances should be managed by the program
The program should own all the resources and merely allocated to the projects for specific periods
Shared resources should belong to a central resource pool and are better managed at the program level whereas dedicated resources can be managed by projects

explanation: Program manager can add value by ensuring optimal utilization, assignment and prioritization of shared resources. This is probably the most logical distribution of responsibilities for resource management in the program

text: Program management has similarities and differences with project management. Which of the following captures the essence of the differences?

choices.text: Programs are run within a governance structure, projects have a lose governance framework
Projects are run within a governance structure, programs have a lose governance framework
Programs and projects create deliverables, projects create incremental benefits
Programs and projects create deliverables, programs create benefits

explanation: Program and projects can both create deliverables, with the main focus of the program being to create incremental benefits via the project deliverables. Projects themselves do not create incremental benefits, those come via the program. Both programs and projects should be run within a governance structure.

text: The program manager in a complex program is a believer in autonomy. One of the project managers is a believer in close supervision and micro-management. What should be done to reconcile the different management styles?

choices.text: It may be beneficial the way it is, because the program manager needs to manage at a high level and the projects need to have close management
The project managers should adapt to the program manager's style of management to ensure consistency of culture
The management style depends on the specific situation prevalent in the projects and program at any given point in time
The program manager should adopt the philosophy of "trust but verify"

explanation: The management style should be driven by whatever is appropriate at the given moment in time. There is no right or wrong style.

text: A program manager is preparing to present the program charter to the board. What should be the key focus of the presentation?

choices.text: Showcase how the program will give the organization a competitive edge over the competition
Explain the important milestones and the details of funding needed
Explain the key deliverables of the program and introduce the program team
Define the overall program and explain how it delivers organizational benefits

explanation: At the program authorization (chartering) stage, it is most important to define what the program is about and how it benefits the organization. It is not as if the other topics are not important, but they need to be stated in the context of this.

text: A program is different from a portfolio in that:

choices.text: Programs can have operations, whereas a portfolio cannot
Programs need not have related components, whereas components of a portfolio must be related
Programs have a definite time frame, portfolios are not initiated with a time frame in mind
A portfolio is strategic and a program is tactical

explanation: Portfolios is a strategic collection of components that meets some business objectives. They are not constituted with a time line in mind. A program can be long and the duration may not even be known upfront, but they are by nature temporary. A, B and C are not correct statements.

text: A program for a diversified engineering company deals with developing and manufacturing printers. As part of an annual strategy exercise, the company decided to stop investing in the growth of the printer business and simply support the existing customers and product lines. As the program manager tries to adjust to the shift in strategy, which would be the least appropriate thing to do?

choices.text: Review and selectively cancel components related to development of new models
Discuss with the program steering committee on goals for the program and see if the charter needs to be revised
Look at ways to reduce the program's footprint and cost structure
Raise a request to close the program and convert into an operation

explanation: The program may have revised objectives but it is not necessarily shutting down or transitioning immediately. In order to achieve the business outcomes, there may be several things that the program can still contribute. Therefore requesting closure and transition may be premature as compared to the others

text: A program functioning on a remote site in a foreign country has a stated policy of renting machinery to avoid creating too many fixed assets. A project manager within the program is requesting to buy a machine as the renting arrangement is proving inconvenient. What should be done in this situation?

choices.text: Discuss the requirements of the project manager with the suppliers of the machines and try to work out a solution
Explain the benefits of renting to the project manager
If the request is prima facie justified, it can be approved by making an exception
Reconsider the whole buy vs. rent philosophy for the entire program

explanation: The reasons for the project manager's dissatisfaction has to be understood and discussed with the suppliers before making the call. There may be reasons behind the policy being what it is and it should not be changed light-heartedly. Nor should the request be denied out of hand without establishing the need and trying to address it.

text: The SPI for the overall program is 1.1 and a project within the same program is reporting an SPI of 0.9. Which of the following best explains this situation?

choices.text: The program manager may have been too aggressive in estimating durations whereas the project manager may have been conservative
The project may have contributed resources to other areas in the program resulting in delay to the project's activities
The project may have used resources from other parts of the program and therefore be ahead of schedule
The project might have fast tracked some activities even at the cost of adding risk to other projects and the overall program

explanation: A, C and D contain scenarios that would lead to the project being ahead of schedule and the program being behind, whereas the situation stated is the opposite.

text: How should a project that is part of a larger program be planned?

choices.text: Working with the project/program sponsor to align with their expectations
Referring to applicable and available historical records and trying to align with the planning approach with other components
Respecting the uniqueness of the project and inventing the best methodology applicable to the project
After discussing with the other components in the program and following the same templates so that it is easier to standardize

explanation: Where they are available, historical records is the best place to begin planning and such information and guidance can be provided by the PMO. The other answers also have some merit, but remember PMI places a lot of emphasis on creation and usage of historical records

text: A program manager needs to help the program realize the benefits by:

choices.text: Setting up measurement systems for quantifying current and desired state
Planning specific activities for benefits realization, monitoring and tracking benefits delivery
Distributing responsibility among the project managers
Creating a benefits realization plan

explanation: Creating a benefits realization plan does not (on its own) help in realizing the benefits, nor does assignment of responsibility or assigning performance objectives. The program manager needs to plan specific activities for benefits realization.

text: A mass transportation improvement program once included a proposal for a tram system on some of the arterial roads. About $5 million were spent on this project creating some basic infrastructure like tracks and overhead cabling before it was stopped due to opposition from some local groups. After 3 years, the proposal has been revived as the tram lines can serve as feeder to the underground metro rail system. While preparing the business case for this project to be included in the program, what factors should the program manager consider?

choices.text: Make-or-buy analysis for the service being offered, capital expenditure incurred till date, benefits from the service
The capital expenditure incurred till date, additional expenditure required to complete, likely benefits from the service
Cost needed to complete works and start the service, cost of alternative options such as bus feeders, benefit from the service
Economic forecast and traffic projections, the capital expenditure incurred till date, opportunity cost of the additional spend

explanation: The principle sunk costs suggests that the costs that are already incurred should not be taken into consideration while taking forward looking decisions. This rules out considering capital expenditure incurred in the past (A, C and D).

text: A program manager wants to establish temporary workers or contracting as an alternate resourcing mechanism. She senses that the project managers are not convinced and they believe all the work must be done in-house to give them the necessary control. How should the program manager proceed?

choices.text: Get the program steering committee to create a procurement policy that will be applicable for the program
Talk to the project managers and strive to achieve consensus
Call for a bidder's conference so that the vendors can showcase their capabilities to the project managers
Start a pilot project with the new resourcing mechanism and build on the success of the pilot

explanation: Ideally, the program manager should not try to bulldoze the idea nor should they spend too much time courting or trying to convince everybody. The best way to promote a new idea is to build a showcase and highlight the achievements

text: A program for data analytics techniques announced a competition to crowd-source some algorithms for use in its products. One of the participants came up with some very original ideas which were raw and untested, but potentially high value. What risk management strategy might be most useful in this case?

choices.text: Ask the participant to develop the ideas fully and come back if they are found successful
Invite the participant to develop the ideas by offering a risk sharing contract
Appoint an expert to further enhance some of the ideas
Buy the rights to the ideas from the participant and initiate a project

explanation: The opportunity exists both for the author and the company, so the best approach would be to establish a venture to share the opportunity. This may potentially involve a risk sharing contract with the participant.

text: A program manager noticed that one of the projects on the program did not have a baselined scope though it was at the execution stage. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Ask the project manager to immediately baseline the scope, while continuing work on the project
Discuss the finding and provide assistance if necessary
Let the project manager deal with the issue unless there are any deviations in the plan
Stop work on the project till clarity on the scope can be arrived at

explanation: The scope not being baselinedmay or may not be a problem. In many iterative methodologies, projects will want to try out different options before deciding how and what it wants to accomplish. However, the program manager should inquire if there is anything that can be done to bring clarity for the project.

text: The work involved in a ____ is usually inter-dependent in a way that the intended outcome requires all the elements to deliver; whereas the work involved in a _____ is grouped together due to some common factor but may or may not be inter-related. Find the appropriate words to fill in the blanks.

choices.text: Programs, Projects
Portfolios, Programs
Projects, Programs
Programs, Portfolios

explanation: Grouping of work under a portfolio requires some common factor (like geography, same customer, shared resource pool, etc.) though the components may not be related. A program requires (by definition) that the components are inter-related.

text: During a particular year, the organization's strategy has changed as a result of getting acquired by a bigger company. A program is in progress, and is on target to deliver the benefits and has only about 6 months left. However, the program is not in alignment with the new strategy of the organization. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Evaluate the options to continue, stop or scale down the program and approach the program steering committee to ask them to make a decision
Prepared a revised business case and justification to continue the program
Stop work on the program as it is no longer aligned with the strategy
Continue with the program until the management of the new organization conveys otherwise

explanation: Alignment with strategy is an important part of the program manager's responsibility. Even though the project makes business sense, this needs to be validated with the program steering committee, which represents the interest of the organization.

text: A project within a program is likely to be late by 2 months. This delay is likely to have a snowballing effect on other components. The program manager and the project manager are discussing the issue and exploring suggestions to address this. Which of the following is the most useful suggestion?

choices.text: Find the best way to reset stakeholder expectations about the project and the overall program
Check if some of the work can be outsourced under stringent time lines
Find ways to assign resources from other components to the troubled project to speed it up
Check if there are ways to quickly unblock the work of other components while looking to speed up the troubled project

explanation: The program manager should be primarily concerned with resolving the inter-dependencies and getting the other projects unblocked. The project manager is responsible for specific ideas about speeding up the project.

text: Stakeholder engagement is a joint responsibility of the program steering committee, program manager and the project managers. Which is the best set of focus areas for stakeholder engagement by the program manager?

choices.text: Identification, assessing and establishing their interest in the program, agreement about sought benefits and resources, determining the engagement strategy
Identify the only a few key stakeholders and prioritize the engagement approach, engage them using multiple channels
(Along with the project managers) identify the stakeholders, determine who is a supporter and who is resisting, start with the supporters and then address the resistors
Identify stakeholders, establish a relationship with the stakeholders, determine how to make each stakeholder happy with the outcomes of the program

explanation: Option A provides a systematic approach for stakeholder engagement. All other answers have some issues. Option B gives less importance to the resisting stakeholders which may not always work. Option C assumes that each stakeholder needs to be "happy" which may not always be possible. Option-D asks to focus on just a few stakeholders which may not be a good idea

text: One of the projects in the program is frequently getting affected by lack of support from IT function. The project manager has escalated this to the program manager. Who is primarily responsible for solving this problem?

choices.text: Program manager
Program sponsor
Manager of IT function
Concerned project manager

explanation: The program manager or sponsor can help escalate the matter and get the right level of attention to it, but at the end of the day, it is an IT issue and has to be resolved by the IT function.

text: A program has started initiating the components and they have started delivering the work and benefits have started to accrue to the program. At this time, what should the program manager focus on?

choices.text: Ensuring that the benefits realization is as per expectations and taking steps to address any deviations
Exercising tight control over and managing the changes at the program level
Issuing charters to the components and signing off on the closure reports
Spending quality time with the team, ensuring they are actively engaged and enabled

explanation: The program manager is primarily accountable for benefits delivery and during this phase of the life-cycle, they sould be monitoring and tracking the delivery of benefits. Other items are also valid, but the primary focus should be on the benefits.

text: A program is in the Definition phase and the program management plan is being prepared. The program manager performed an assessment of the risks early on during the planning process. She then involved a broad spectrum of stakeholders in the risk identification, risk analysis and response planning. The initial set of project level risk registers have been prepared and reviewed. The frequency and mechanisms for risk monitoring and control at project and program level have also been defined. What seems to be the biggest missing element in this process so far?

choices.text: There needs to be an explicit plan for unknown unknowns and appropriate workarounds need to be identified
The program manager needs to map the risk profile of the program with the risk tolerance of the organization
The program sponsor needs to be involved in the risk identification as well
The program manager ought to have conducted a third party independent assessment of the risks on the program

explanation: One of the important goals of the risk management planning at program level is to ensure that the risk level of the program is in line with the risk thresholds of the organization. It is not clear whether a third party review is necessary or whether it has been done or not. From the description, it seems the program manager has ensured broad involvement from stakeholders. Workarounds can only be identified once unknown and unforeseen events occur. They are inherently "unplanned" responses.

text: What can be inferred from the program management plan once it has been baselined?

choices.text: A blueprint to prevent and manage changes to the scope of the program and its projects
The bare minimum expectations that can be kept about the program and its components. Ideally, the program should try to deliver more than the baseline.
The correlation between the work of the components and the desired benefits
The agreement between the program and its stakeholders about the outcomes and benefits that the program will deliver

explanation: C is the most correct statement. Option A talks about expectation management. which is right, but it states that the program should strive to deliver more - that would amount to gold plating. Option B is incorrect - correlation of the components and the benefits is part of the benefits management plan. The baseline does assist in performing change management but that is not the sole purpose of the baseline.

text: In a program led by NGO's working for common social benefit under funding received from donors, what is the most likely role of the local government authorities?

choices.text: Performing organization
Provide governance structure for the program
Sponsor
Providing constraints and local expertise

explanation: The government is not providing resources, hence they are not sponsors. The teams also do not come from the government, so they are not the performing organizations. The NGO is managing the program so the governance structure is also unlikely to involve the government. Hence the best option seems to be that they will establish the constraints (legal boundaries) and local expertise.

text: Project A and Project B are part of a program with a number of inter-dependent activities. One of the deliverables from Project A is delayed and the project manager of project A has asked for help. How can the program manager help expedite project A?

choices.text: From the contingency reserves, announce an incentive for people willing to work extra hours to complete the work
Analyze the casues of the delay and work with the manager of project A to identify options to speed up the delivery
Identify idle resources from the program's resource pool and temporarily assign them to project A
Ask the manager of project A to identify activities that can be performed in parallel so that they can be fast tracked

explanation: The program manager needs to first understand the reasons for the delay and what might be helpful in this case. This insight can only come from the project manager. Addition of resources (A) or fast tracking (B) may or may not be the appropriate option here. Overtime and rewards may also be helpful, but the best way to decide determine what might work would be to involve the manager of the project in the analysis

text: How does the project level WBS add value for a project that is being done as part of a program, which already has a program WBS created?

choices.text: To facilitate make-or-buy analysis
To better organize the work of the projects into smaller, more manageable units that the project manager can keep track of
To meet the requirements of relevant standards
To illustrate the dependencies among the projects and sequence them

explanation: The reason to develop a WBS is to basically break the work down into smaller deliverables that can be better managed by the project managers. All other answers have some inaccuracies. For example, WBS does not involve make-or-buy analysis or determine sequencing. The WBS should not merely be used to satisfy some compliance requirements.

text: A company is working on a new technology that will produce operational efficiencies. The discovery and planned rollout is being considered as a program. What should be the first step to kik off this activity?

choices.text: Ensure the program aligns with organizational strategy
Assign a program manager
Determine significant milestones and prepare a business case
Check the level of risk involved and if it is in line with the organization's risk threshold

explanation: The assignment of the program manager seems to be the logical first step. The other activities would likely be spearheaded by the program manager itself.

text: M-series is a music company. It was extremely popular at one time, but is losing ground to competitors quickly. The key issue according to the portfolio managers is that M-series has failed to expand its appeal to the Gen Y audience. There is a program to try and improve its ratings and make it a competitive brand again. The program team wants to dig deep and figure out the best way to appeal to this audience. What is the best way to figure out activities that will help achieve this goal?

choices.text: Getting expert musicians together to generate more content which appeals to the target audience
Conduct interviews with randomly selected representatives of Gen Y
Open house brainstorming sessions with stakeholders from different age groups
A structured questionaire which is administered through the social media

explanation: This is a program that will require a lot of lateral thinking to figure out which set of features will enable the company to compete successfully. This is best accomplished in a face-to-face setting that facilitates ideation. Option A (brainstorming) is the only technique that involves face-to-face discussions and seems most appropriate in this case.

text: A program is up against a rigid budget constraint. The program manager and the project managers agreed that creating a tool for monitoring and optimizing program finances (especially the shared resources) will be helpful for the program. How should the chartering process work for this project?

choices.text: A separate charter is not needed as it is an internal tools project
Provide a vision statement for the tool and start the work
The charter should be issued only after the program steering committee approves it
The project will create a tool for optimizing program finances

explanation: The request for a charter is valid. The charter formally establishes the need for a project and commits organizational resources to it. Therefore, the program manager must work with the project manager to produce and get approval for the charter.

text: A program management plan will contain a number of subsidiary plans. Which of the following is not likely to be a part of the program management plan?

choices.text: Communications management plan
Management plans for each of the component
Governance plan
Benefits realization plan

explanation: The program management plan is a high level plan that outlines how the overall program will be management. It provides guidance and direction to individual project management plans but does not necessarily contain all the project management plans.

text: A company is working on advanced telemetry for an early warning system for severe weather conditions. The program will cover a geographically diverse and large target area. Which of the following components should probably not be included in the program?

choices.text: An disaster recovery unit to manage relief operations after adverse weather events
An operational unit to process the data collected by the systems and issue severe weather warnings when required
Installation and commissioning of the radar systems integrated with computing resources to process the readings
A project to create an algorithm that will correlate the data points and the output parameters

explanation: The program's main purpose as stated in the question is in providing early warning systems. A, B and D are aligned to the purpose. C is not directly able to contribute to the main purpose of the program.

text: The output of Project B is a critical input for project A. Project A and B are both part of the same program. The output of Project A is delayed, which causes resources from Project B to remain idle. Who is primarily responsible for solving this problem?

choices.text: Program Manager
Manager of Project A
Manager of Project B
The functional managers

explanation: The management of inter-dependencies within a program is a responsibility of the program manager. The program manager has the visibility and the authority to make the msot informed decision on this.

text: Should the non-project work ("other work") be included in the Program WBS (P-WBS)?

choices.text: It should be included. The P-WBS should cover all the work of the program at a high level
It should not be included. The P-WBS only focuses on project level deliverables.
It should be decided by the program manager and the managers of the projects and the other work
It depends upon whether the other work contributes to the "value creation" or "value realization"

explanation: The P-WBS is created at a relatively high level so that the program manager can manage at a fairly high level of granularity. However, for it to be useful, it must include all the work in the program, not just the work performed on the projects

text: Due to a resource crunch, a program needs to re-prioritize the work on various components. Who is primarily responsible for determine the priorities?

choices.text: Program Sponsor
Program Manager
Program Team
Program steering committee

explanation: The primary responsibility of keeping the program on track and determining how it will be best equipped to deliver the intended benefits would lie with the program manager, who will consult all the other stakeholders based on the criticality and need

text: The CFO of a large company decided to embark on a program to deploy the temporary and static surpluses through a more proactive investment strategy to generate higher returns. Which of the following benefit measures is best to assess the success of the program?

choices.text: Planned vs. actual returns on investment
Number of investments that made money vs. those that lost money
Current and forecast return generated on the invested surplus
Risk adjusted return on investment compared with benchmarks

explanation: The return on investment needs to be compared against benchmarks and balanced against risks. For example, in a year where the markets have been booming, even a high rate of return may not be viewed as success, whereas in a recessionary condition even a modest return would be viewed as success

text: A project is part of a program. The project manager has used many different techniques to identify and analyze risks and plan responses. She has further provided for contingency reserves. However, the project manager feels (based on sixth sense) that there are probably more risks that could arise during the project execution. What would be the program manager's view about this while finalizing the plan?

choices.text: To create workarounds to be deployed in case some unidentified risk occurs
Tell the project manager not to worry too much; if an unknown risk occurs it is always possible to raise a change request to cover for the impact
Use the program level contingency reserves can be utilized for these
Set aside some management reserves to be used in case an unknown risk event occurs

explanation: The program manager must advocate a proactive approach towards risk management. C is the best choice because it recognizes the existence of some risks which may not have been identified up-front and provides for it. Workaround by definition is an unplanned response, so it cannot be decided in advance. The program level contingency reserves should be used for program level risks, not to cover unknown unknowns at project level.

text: A program charter was drafted by a new program manager and sent for review to the PMO. It clearly articulated the justification for the program along with the vision for the program. It contained a high level scope statement along with desired outcomes and benefits. It also outlined a high level plan in terms of cost, time and an initial assessment of stakeholders and risks. Which is the most important piece of information that may be missing from this?

choices.text: The details about the components that will be initiated and how they will be inter-connected
Technical approach
Strategic fit of the program
Information about how the program should be governed

explanation: It is very important at the chartering stage to clearly outline how the program is aligned with the overall strategy of the organization. The other choices also represent important inclusions, but they can be elaborated during the planing processes

text: A program has recently concluded and is in the transition phase of the program life-cycle. What is the best description of what should be transitioned during this phase from the Program team to the receiving organization?

choices.text: Program Deliverables, Program Benefits, Program Knowledge
Program Resources, Lessons learned, Financial surplus
Programs assets, Program Budget, Program Deliverables
Lessons learned, Program Budget, Program Deliverables

explanation: The transition phase includes (potentially) transfer of resources, responsibilities, lessons learned, benefits, etc. The key element in answer C is benefits. The benefits need to be transitioned back to the organization and is the key deliverable from the program.

text: Program management is trying to meet program requirements and to obtain benefits and control not available by managing the projects individually. In trying to achieve greater benefits and control, which of the following is the least beneficial to the program manager?

choices.text: Resolving resource constraints and/or conflicts affecting multiple projects in a program
Responding proactively to risks affecting multiple components of the program
Ensuring the compliance with the local and governmental regulations
Aligning overall program activities with the strategy of the organization

explanation: Compliance with regulations is mandatory and not really an opportunity to achieve greater benefits and control.

text: What role does the program manager play in the quality assurance activities on each project?

choices.text: The program manager should establish guidelines and processes. They should look to optimize and rationalize processes and resources across projects.
The program manager is responsible for consolidating and reporting on the metrics and control charts at program level
The project managers are responsible for QA processes in their own projects. The program manager should only ensure adequate involvement from the program management office in this process
The program manager is responsible for overall quality, so they need to act as the final reviewer and arbiter of all project level quality assurance activities.

explanation: All the statements have some merit, but A is closest to the mark. B misses the point by asking the program manager to be the final reviewer - the program manager may not have the time or know-how to arbitrate on QA processes on all projects. C is suspect because the PMO's role is not to get involved in the program/project level activities. D is talking about control charts, which is a Quality control process, not Assurance. As the program manager should try to standardize and rationalize, A seems the most reasonable choice.

text: The most beneficial role for the program manager in change management activities at component level is:

choices.text: To audit that the defined process is followed
To escalate the change requests to the Program steering committee
To initiate changes that enhance the ability to achieve the overall program objectives
To prevent changes as far as possible to avoid disruption to the plan

explanation: Slightly different from project level, program level change management thrives on positive change. A program manager needs to focus on the needs and goals of the overall program and may often need to initiate changes required to achieve the larger goals.

text: A program contains several projects with inter-dependencies. One of the issues in arriving at a program schedule is that some projects are "research oriented" and the project managers are unable to provide definitive estimates. How should the program manager proceed?

choices.text: Ask the project managers of research projects to use bottom-up estimation to improve the confidence level in the estimates
Ask the project manager to submit a coarse estimate and use rolling wave planning
Plan for an estimation workshop with all the project managers and try to get to more reliable estimates
Proceed with the planning for the rest of the program considering only those projects whose estimates are available

explanation: In an environment where there is a great degree of uncertainty, it's good to use a rolling wave planning approach. This approach allows team members to start working and refine the plan as more details become available. Option-A is not workable, as there are dependencies and therefore the program schedule cannot be prepared by ignoring some projects. Bottom-up estimates will not be possible for research projects.

text: A program has a number of stakeholders and they refer the program's progress reports frequently. What is the least appropriate mechanism for information distribution about the program?

choices.text: An email attachment containing the details of progress on all the tasks on the components and the overall program
By using social media tools
As a formal communication from the Program office to the relevant stakeholders
An online program dashboard summary page that refreshes automatically as data is added

explanation: Communication should use multiple channels and should be customized to the needs of the stakeholders. So all means are good. Statement C is least appropriate because it seems like too much information which may not be appropriate for all the stakeholders

text: A project manager in consultation with the program manager decided to outsource a complex piece of work on her project, as the project did not have in-house technical expertise. As a result of this change, the program had to shell out additional funds. Another risk was added to the program risk register pertaining to the financial stability and reliability of the vendor. This is an example of:

choices.text: Secondary risk for the program
Residual risk for the project
Unknown unknown or black swans
Peripheral risk for both project and program

explanation: Secondary risks arise from the response plans employed to address an existing risk.

text: A large manufacturing company is working on a program for roll-out of an ERP system across the board. This has widespread impact on all functions. The program is sponsored by a senior executive and the program manager has been appointed. The program manager fears that there would be a lot of reservations among the different departments, especially at mid-management and lower levels. The extent of change they will experience is quite large. What of the following ways may be most effective in reducing the resistance to change?

choices.text: Ask the CEO to announce the change and lend his personal brand to the initiative
Start with a small scale pilot roll out and showcase the success of the pilot
Establish small task forces across functions to drive the change
Start a visible communication campaign about the expected benefits to the organization

explanation: Change initiatives that cut across organizational boundaries are likely to create resistance. Of the stated approaches, D seems most likely to succeed, because it will use past data in the same organization to propagate in a wider setting.

text: A company working in the metals and minerals industry has been acquired by another company. The ongoing programs in the acquired company are being reviewed for alignment with the overall group strategy. Which of the following documents will be least useful in this process?

choices.text: Business case
Benefits realization plan
Governance plan
Program Charter

explanation: The governance plan is about how the program will be administered and governed, and does not really address the strategic alignment. The program charter gives an idea about the high level goals of the program. Business case provides the opportunity being addressed and outlines the target benefits. All of this is more relevant than the governance plan.

text: A program relies heavily on vendors for completing different components. The components need to integrate together for the product suite to come together. The vendor establishments are in 5 different locations. The program is approaching a deadline and the deliverables from components are not integrating properly. None of the teams is taking ownership of resolving the issues. Which of the following is most likely to be useful in this situation?

choices.text: Adding penalty clauses to the contracts of all the vendors in case the product is not successful
Co-locating the teams for a short period till issues are resolved
Increase the contingency reserves with regard to cost and time in anticipation of over-runs
Call for an emergency meeting of all the project managers and issue a deadline

explanation: Bringing everybody together in the same location (Co-location) is likely to bring focus on resolving the problems in a timely manner.

text: A program is being executed largely with the help of vendors at offshore locations. Couple of vendors have complained that the business representatives have not been responsive about queries related to specifications. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Use the program sponsor's political clout with the business functions to coax the business to be more responsive
Ask the vendors for more details about their queries and to quantify the impact of delay in responses
Organize a meeting of the business representatives with the vendors to gain more clarity
Ask the concerned project managers to help the vendors

explanation: Option A does not solve the problem. Option D pushes it back to the project level. Option C is superior to option B because B is about escalating without any value addition, whereas C is about the program manager taking steps to get to a resolution

text: A program is designed to release a suite of products related to processing of complex data consists of multiple projects, with complex integrations and interfaces between them. A couple of the projects are completed and ready for deployment. The project managers are keen to release their products and get market feedback, but the program manager feels it is better to release together. The decision is referred to the program steering committee. How should the decision be taken?

choices.text: It is advisable as per Agile principles to unlock value to the market as fast as possible, hence releasing early is advisable
It is inappropriate to release the products piecemeal as it might confuse the market - hence it is better to wait
The early products can be released as unsuported or "beta" offerings to garner feedback
Consider the relative benefit of early release of value against the cost of incurring the testing and release overhead

explanation: Clearly, early release has some benefits, but each time a release cycle is started, it also involves overheads. So the best answer is to make an informed decision based on the relative cost and benefits.

text: Two projects were part of a program. They both produce some intermediate artifacts that come together to deliver the output for the program. The integration tests failed leading to a blame game. Both projects are adamant it is not their fault. What is the best course of action for the program manager, who is keen to solve the problem and move forward?

choices.text: The project managers along with a program team member should draw up an Ishikawa diagram to try and identify a root cause
The QA managers of the two projects need to look at the Pareto diagrams for their projects to prioritize the best course of action
The program manager needs to review the process flowchart to discover where the process is lacking
The project managers should be draw up a Control or run chart to identify the extent of the quality issues

explanation: The Ishikawa diagram is useful for isolating the area or areas that could be causing the problem. Identifying the root cause is the first and important step in finding a remedy. The Pareto diagram is useful for determining the priorities between possible underlying causes. The flowchart is a diagram that displays the connectivity between pieces of a system. The control or run chart is useful for determining the measured output over the manufacturing process for acceptable and failed products.

text: A quality control engineer has risen through the ranks of a company to become a project manager and has recently been selected to lead a program. Which of the following issues should be her topmost priority?

choices.text: One of the projects needs help on prioritizing the quality related issues
Most projects are meeting the quality goals but one project has been a consistent outlier
Recruiting good test engineers for the project teams has been a challenge
The specifications for one of the products have changed requiring a recalibration of the test equipment

explanation: Option A seems most appropriate because it seems to be a generic problem across projects. The program manager's time is best spent on activities that cut across different components. The other activities probably are more appropriate for the project domain

text: A program manager has just received approval for the program charter and is about to start the planning process. Which of the following steps should be done first?

choices.text: Prepare the project level plans first, then aggregate them to form the program management plan
Proceed to define the scope of the program and how it should be managed
Quantify the potential benefits from the program compared with the likely cost and see if the program is justified
Prepare a plan that achieves the best balance between scope, cost and time objectives

explanation: Scope planning is usually the starting point in all the planning processes on a program or project. The project plans cannot be the starting point for the program plan. Identification of benefits and costs should already have been done prior to the issuance of the charter. C is too much of a generic statement. Therefore, D is the best answer.

text: A program for a petroleum company is targeting reduction in effluents discharged from the factories to meet stricter compliance requirements. The program generated a set of deliverables and is about to close. Which of the following would be LEAST important artifact from the closure processes?

choices.text: Acceptance report from the relevant compliance authority
Cost-benefit analysis of the program
Lessons Learned
