Training plan for the factory employees

explanation: A, C and D are obviously expected outputs. B is least important, because this is a compliance oriented program.

text: A program has been initiated by a gas distribution company to build a complex grid based distribution system for natural gas to commercial and domestic customers. There are multiple components in this program with complex dependencies. The program manager finished writing a Program Scope Management Plan based on a template provided by the Program Management Office. How should this plan be used by the project managers?

choices.text: To validate the scope of the program once it is ready to be closed and transitioned
Based on this plan, they can determine the scope statement for their project
To determine how the program scope and that of its components will be managed
To build the Program WBS together with the Program team

explanation: The program scope management plan does not contain the actual scope of the program, rather it explains how the scope of the overall program will be managed. Hence C is the most appropriate answer.

text: A program is about to close and transition to the function which will oversee the operations. As part of the transition, it is needed to conduct training for the staff members and develop a system for managing the inventory and supply chain. Which is the most logical source for the budget needed for these activities?

choices.text: As part of a separate entity that is explicitly meant to track the transition
The budget of the function that is taking over
The overall portfolio budget
The program budget

explanation: Providing for the transition and sustenance of the benefits is part of the Program Closure phase and therefors it is most logical that the program budget would have provisions for these activities. If it has not been provided fo any reason, any of the other 3 options may be considered

text: Project A and Project B are part of a program with a number of inter-dependent activities. One of the deliverables from Project A is delayed. What should the program manaer do first?

choices.text: The program manager should work with the manager of project B to try and crash the schedule to absorb the delay
The program manager should analyze the impact on the overall program schedule and flag a risk to the program steering committee
The program manager should analyze the impact of the delay on the program's benefits
The program manager should work with the manager of project A to expedite the completion of project A

explanation: The program manager should focus on the benefits that are expected from the program - rather than on individual projects or specific aspects of the Scope, Cost, Time equation for the program

text: A product manager for a project within a program suggested a modification that would reduce the development cost. However, it will increase the operations and maintenance cost slightly. An older version of the product is in service at present. How should this request be handled?

choices.text: Refuse the change as increase in operational cost will more than offset the saving in development cost
Submit a change request and discuss the change with operations to come up with mitigating actions
Approve the request as it reduces the program cost
Ask the project manager for the concerned product to give a recommendation

explanation: This change should definitely be considered because there is a potential benefit on the development cost. This requires to be offset against increased operational cost, which is why involvement from operations is necessary.

text: Which is the most complete and correct set of activities that should be performed during a program's closure?

choices.text: Approve component transitions, document lessons learned, archive project and program records, close contracts and take acceptance from the customer
Close the program, approve component transitions, deliver required reports along with financial and benefit realization reports and document lessons learned
Close projects and document lessons learned, produce financial and benefit realization reports, close contracts and release the resources of the program
Approve closure and transition of components, close contracts, perform financial closure, plan for benefits transition and sustainment and create lessons learned

explanation: A is the most complete set of activities. B and D are missing the transition and sustainment of benefits, whereas C is missing closure of contracts

text: A multi-year program ran into budget constraints during a particular financial period due to the limitations of the funding organization. The program manager would like to prioritize funds allocation based on the value delivered against the plan. Which of these would be the best metrics to use as the basis for allocation?

choices.text: Earned value
S-curves
Milestones completed
Trends and Forecast reports

explanation: The earned value method measures the utilization of budget against the actual work done and provides a holistic view to the program manager. These reports will be most helpful for the program manager to keep tabs on the budget utilization and progress.

text: A new drug program for a pharmaceutical company is in its second year. The program level CPI was reported to be 0.78 and SPI is 1.22. Which of the following is most likely to have caused this?

choices.text: Some of the dependencies between the projects may not have been met
The projects may have used crashing techniques to save time
The projects may have used less expensive resources to save on cost
The cost of man-power or materials may have gone up

explanation: CPI of 0.78 and SPI of 1.22 means that the project is ahead of schedule and over budget. Option A explains both, whereas option D explains only CPI. Options B and C explains neither.

text: A project within a program is likely to get delayed, causing a cascading effect on other components. The project manager in consultation with the program team has come up with a mitigating plan that needs to be presented to the Program steering committee. Who should be the primary communicator for this?

choices.text: Chairperson of the Program steering committee
Manager of the concerned project
Program Sponsor
Program Manager

explanation: The program manager is the primary communicator for the program.

text: A large aerospace component design program is in vendor selection proces. A number of projects require similar parts made of the sub-assemblies, which are relatively standardized and have large number of suppliers in the market. Which of the following vendors should the program manager consider?

choices.text: Vendor D, which has the best reputation for after sales service
Vendor C who has manufacturing facilities near all locations that the projects have and can offer volume discounts
Vendor A, who seems to have the confidence of most of the project managers
Vendor B, who has the lowest price point

explanation: The question here is about a program wide procurement strategy that should seek to optimize the procurement effort to meet the needs of all the components and overall program. C seems to address the need the best.

text: Which of the following is the most important activity for a program manager?

choices.text: Creates a framework to plan for and track the delivery of benefits to the organization
Communicates aggressively using appropriate escalation paths about the risks involved in the components and the overall program
Balances the RoI from different business areas and determines which areas the organization should invest in
Create detailed plans across the different components and makes sure that the appropriate level of oversight is given to the components

explanation: The primary role of the program manager is to manage the inter-related components to ensure that the benefits are passed on to the organization

text: All the components of the program have been closed, the lessons learned were documented and formal sign-offs on the deliverables were received. The contracts and financials were audited and closed as well and the team members released. Which of the following is the most important additional step that needs to be performed for the program to be formally closed?

choices.text: Provision has to be made for the transition and sustenance of the benefits
The payments for the vendors need to be released
Formal acceptance is required not just on the deliverables, but also the benefits delivered
The skill sets of the team members need to be updated in the resource database

explanation: Programs must take the responsibility for the long term sustenance of the benefits. A and C are also valid but probably less important than the sustenance of benefits. D seems redundant because it is stated that all the contracts were closed (implying that payment and settlement has already occurred)

text: A program is under severe cost constraints and the program manager would like to ensure targeted allocation of the funds to the projects within the program. Which of the following techniques is most helpful for the program manager exercise close control over program costs?

choices.text: Hedging and forward contracts
Work authorization system
Quality management frameworks
Program change control system

explanation: A work authorization system helps to ensure that only the planned and essential work is being performed at any given point in time. It can be used during tough financial periods to exercise control over costs and prevent unnecessary expenditure.

text: A technology startup company is famous for innovation and is known for coming up with and working with path-breaking programs. A progam manager is working on a new idea and is seeking a charter. What is the most important step for the program manager at this stage?

choices.text: Identify potential sponsors for the idea
Identify what resources and skillsets would be needed
Prepare a draft proposal and solicit some feedback
Creating a water-tight business case that outlines the resourcing requirements and likely benefits

explanation: Since this is a startup organization and the program is path-breaking, the first step would be to identify a sponsor. Once the sponsor is convinced, we can work on the detailed proposal, business case and resource requirements. Without the firm backing of a sponsor, the best ideas and business cases also may not really take off

text: Many of the projects in a construction program rely on the procurement of steel of various grades. This is an important part of the materials budget for most of the components. The parts are standardized and are procured using open bidding through a web portal. It is seen that the cost of steel is rising and is likely to rise further and vendors are requesting for an increase in the price upper limit specified in the system. What should be done in this case?

choices.text: Discuss with the vendors and inform the project managers and the procurement team about the situation
Check the cost buffers on the projects to ensure they can accommodate an increase in material cost
Request the Centralized procurement team for their opinion
Refuse the request so long as suppliers are ready to bid

explanation: If the material cost goes on rising, the seller's margins go down and the likelihood of receiving less bids or compromise on quality rises. So the buyer needs to be considerate in case of events that go beyond the control of the supplier. The stakeholders must come together and arrive at a satisfactory solution

text: A fast food restaurant chain is expanding into a new geography. There are a number of projects to set up the restaurants, supply chain and manage the operations. All of these components share a common area budget though they are not necessarily related to each other in a significant way. This is best described as?

choices.text: Portfolio
Project
Program
Operation

explanation: If the components are characterized by synergistic benefits delivery, they would more likely be treated as a portfolio (ref: Standard for Program Management, 4th edition, Section 1.4

text: A program has several projects and a couple of operations. It has been in progress for a while and the processes across the different components have evolved and matured over a period of time. A new manager was recently appointed as the manager of the portfolio and has taken over program sponsor responsibilities. She has directed the program manager to "increase the focus on quality". Which of the following techniques might be most helpful for the program manager in this scenario?

choices.text: Follow an Agile life-cycle which allows more frequent checks
Introduce a culture of quality by applying Kaizen principles
Increase the investment in testing
Try to reduce the cost of quality across the projects

explanation: The program level responsibility on culture of quality. Kaizen involves proactively improving the organization and continuously trying to improve as an organization. Since this is a mature program, there are unlikely to be spectacular gains coming out of implementing novel philosophies. Kaizen is least intrusive and at the same time provides for the possibility of continuous, incremental improvements

text: Feasibility studies for a project being initiated as a part of the program whose RoI and marketability have already been established should consider which of the following?

choices.text: Checking if there is a valid business case behind the project
Ensuring that the necessary resources and capabilities are present within the organization
Ensuring that there is a qualified project manager available
Checking if the benefits projected will eventually translate into reality

explanation: Feasibility from an organization's standpoint needs to be evaluated. In asserting that financial and market feasibility is established, the business case is already taken care. The project manager being certified will be beneficial but not sufficient factor for accepting it. Whether or not the project actually delivers the results cannot be known for certain in the beginning.

text: A pharmaceutical company is planning to consolidate all the projects related to drug discovery into a single organizational entity with an executive in-charge. This will be most likely to be managed as a:

choices.text: Operation
Program
Portfolio
Product line

explanation: If the relationship among the projects is only a shared client, seller, technology or resource the effort should be classified and managed like a portfolio - rather than programs.

text: What should be the role of a program manager in risk management processes within a program?

choices.text: Program manager focuses only on the risks escalated from the project to program level. Otherwise, the project managers basically manage risks on the program.
Risks are identified by the project managers and responses are developed at the program level
Program manager focuses more on risks impacting overall program - this may overlap with some project level risks
The program level risk register is essentially a master copy of all the project level risk registers including time allocation, cost, and resources needed to established responses

explanation: B is the best statement. Risk management is required both at project as well as program levels. The program manager needs to look out for anything that impacts the ability of the program to deliver the intended benefits

text: A research program identified a large number of opportunities that could be developed as potential offshoots in the future. What is the best course of action for harnessing the opportunities given that the budget for the program itself may be limited?

choices.text: Use the opportunities to offset some of the threats that the program faces
Work with the program team and project managers to build strong business cases for the opportunities identified
Request the program steering committee to spawn off separate projects or programs in light of these opportunities
Draw upon contingency funds to help realize additional benefits by realizing some of the opportunities

explanation: It is common in programs that the team will specifically earmark some reserves for developing the opportunities (similar to the contingency reserves for threats).

text: What should be part of a program level resource plan?

choices.text: Policies around compliance, diversity, equal opportunity, etc.
Job descriptions and skill sets for the projects
Optimal utilization of shared resources across the program management plan
Identifying clear reporting lines for all the project's human resources

explanation: The program manager needs to ensure that the resources are being optimally utilized. A and C really should be project level considerations and B is usually dictated by organizational policies

text: While deciding whether or not to approve the charter for a component within a program, which should be the most important criterion?

choices.text: Contributes to delivering additional benefits to the program
Reduce the cost of the overall program
Having dependencies with other components within the program
Having shared resources with other components within the program

explanation: The key criterion for inclusion in a program should be the ability to contribute to the additional benefits/control as laid down in the definition of the program. Alignment with corporate strategy is perhaps more relevant at the program (rather than component) level whereas B and C specify just some of the ways in which a component may be related to others within a program.

text: A public facing web portal containing many components is about a week from launch. During operational readiness assessment, a defect was discovered which will make it vulnerable to security breaches under certain circumstances. How should this situation be dealt with?

choices.text: The marketing department in consultation with the program team as it is a public facing launch
The program steering committee should decide in consultation with the influential external stakeholders
The program manager should decide how to proceed in consultation with the program steering committee and technical expert
The technical expert should determine the way forward in consultation with the program manager and program steering committee

explanation: The program is very close to launch and there may be many parameters which will need to be carefully considered. The board will also need to be involved given the sensitivity of the issutaking the board into confidence

text: A large program involves laying down, interlinking and commisioning undersea pipes. The program scope statement has just been approved. The Program WBS has been prepared and the program team along with the component managers have agreed upon the allocation of work among various components. What is the next logical step for the program manager and the component managers?

choices.text: Determine the schedule, cost and resource requirements and the implications on risk and quality
Determine the RoI for the agreed scope based upon an estimation of the time required and cost
Baseline the scope and start the planning processes relate to scheduling, budgeting and risk planning
Get stakeholder approval on the schedule, cost and scope, then move on to planning the resources and procurements related to the projects and the program

explanation: A and C are incorrect because the scope cannot not be baselined without considering trade-offs with (among other things) schedule and budget. D is a more complete answer than B as it recognizes that schedule, cost and resource needs will have to be balanced and this will impact risk and quality.

text: A program in a company with a diversified portfolio is meant to come up with a cross-cutting reporting framework. The program is cross-functional and crosses company boundaries as well. What qualities and capabilities would be most helpful for the program manager?

choices.text: Expertise in general management, ability to command respect
Pleasant personality, hard to say no to
Negotiation skills, ability to create win-win situations
Influencing without authority, encouraging others to contribute

explanation: All of these are useful qualities, the most helpful attribute for this program manager is going to be the ability to be able to influence the project managers and the team members without having direct authority over them because the program is in a matrix structure and is cross-functional

text: A program is in the "Program Delivery" phase of the program life-cycle. At this time, how should any new components be initiated?

choices.text: In the same sequence, and as per the schedule laid out in the program management plan right in the beginning
By taking prior approval of the program steering committee
After validating that component level business cases are validated
Checking that the components will end up contributing to the benefits of the program

explanation: Components that are initiated should contribute to the benefits. This should be the primary concern of the program manager, since we are in the program delivery phase. Other considerations are also valid, but option-D is the most important.

text: A company manufacturing automotive components issued the charter and appointed a program manager for an ambitious program to double the topline in 2 years. The program manager is now trying to figure out the details and the components needed to achieve the results. Which technique will help the program manager in this case?

choices.text: Establish a task force to examine the feasibility of the target
Start a geographic expansion inititive to get into newer markets
Perform a SWOT analysis to understand the strengths and the opportunities
Go for deeper price cuts to expand market share that will ultimately result in higher volumes

explanation: Feasibility studies (option A) should be carried out before the charter is issued. All the other options may have to be explored. However, a good point to start would be a SWOT analysis to understand what opportunties can be identified and how the organization can take advantage of them.

text: A program has many projects which are inter-dependent. The program manager has determined a critical path for the overall program and found that 4 projects viz. W, X, Y and Z are critical for the program schedule and occur in sequence. The projects use probabilistic estimation techniques and have expected duration as 10, 12, 14 and 16 weeks respectively. The standard deviations are 4, 6, 8 and 10 weeks respectively. From a scheduling perspective, which project should the program manager be most concerned about?

choices.text: Project W
Project Y
Project X
Project Z

explanation: All the projects are on the critical path so they are all important. However, the variability of project Z as compared to the expected duration (10/16 = 0.62) is highest for project Z. Other things being equal, the program manager needs to worry most about Project Z.

text: A program has just received a charter. The program manager appointed a few project managers and wants to initiate a few of the components. One of the project managers asked for a project charter. Which of the following is the most appropriate statement about this situation

choices.text: A project charter may be necessary only if the business case for the project has not been approved yet
Instead of separate charters for the projects, the program charter itself can be modified to include all the components
A project charter is needed to formally authorize each project and provide buy-in to apply organizational resources to it
A separate project charter is not required for every component as long as the overall program has been chartered

explanation: The main reason for a charter is that through a charter, the senior management of the organization formally brings a component into existence and agrees to commit organizational resources to it. In case of components of the program, the program manager is responsible for issuing the charters at the appropriate time

text: A program manager is anxious that the initial risk identification for the program is as thorough as possible. Which of these techniques would be most helpful in this regard?

choices.text: Use techniques like Ishikawa diagrams to identify risks
Ask the project managers and team members to prepare mind maps
Conduct an anonymous risk identification exercise with a wide variety of stakeholders using the Delphi technique and consolidate the findings
Ask the project managers to prioritize the risks and focus on the top 20% as per the Pareto principle

explanation: The requirement is to identify a wide range of risks, which requires lateral thinking. Pareto analysis is used to prioritize and not really useful in the initial identification. Ishikawa diagrams are used to uncover root causes and may hint at some risks. Mind maps is a technique used to organize the thoughts in a systematic manner. The technique that will probably result in the biggest bang for the buck in terms of number of risks uncovered would be the Delphi technique

text: A project manager who was a stickler for details has recently been promoted to a program manager position. She is now managing a program comprising of 12 projects spread across 3 locations and a combined staff of over 90. What is the level of detail that should be included in the program management plan?

choices.text: The plans should be very high level. Details should be linked to the project management plans
The plan should be as detailed as possible. It should guide all the activities across the projects
The level of detail in the plan should be such that the program team can effectively handle
The PMO should provide guidance about the level of detail in the plan

explanation: The program manager (not the PMO) should determine how detailed or high level the plan should be. This should be based on the assessment of how much detail the program office can handle and require.

text: A product created by one of the projects within a program is ready for deployment. During the transition process, the manager of the operations team responsible for taking over the product sales and service suggests that some extra expenditure on creating a spares supply chain would greatly increase the service experience and drive future sales. What should the program manager do with this request?

choices.text: Pass on the suggestion to the operations team which is taking over the product and let them decide
Close the project that created a product, but raise a request for a new project to set up the supply chain
Grant the request only if the project or program level contingency reserve can cover the additional spend
Create a change request and work with the project and operations manager to quickly put together a business case

explanation: The request is in line with the strategic benefit that the program is trying to deliver and therefore needs to be studied. It is better to do this as part of the program while the resources and skills are still available to the program. It is part of the transition and benefits sustainment processes of a program.

text: A program has recently been chartered and is in early stages of planning. There is a high degree of variability and multiple parameters that could impact the program. A program manager and the project managers on the team have been asked by the program sponsor to compute the overall contingency reserve requirements for the program. How should they go about this task?

choices.text: Use techniques like Monte Carlo simulation to evaluate the likely spread of outcomes and provide guidance
Add up the contingency requirements of all the individual projects and then add a program level buffer
Categorize the overall risks using a probability-impact matrix and use it to prioritize which risks should be included in the computation
Perform an expected monetary value calculation for all the projects to determine the likely impact of all the risks

explanation: Monte carlo simulation allows you to forecast the variation in target values. This can give guidance about the extent of contingency reserves needed

text: Zero defects is a quality philosophy that requires clearly identifying what the customer wants and providing it the first time, without having to repeat or rework. In which of the following programs would this be the MOST important goal?

choices.text: A program to roll out an enterprisewide resource planning (ERP) system across the company
A program to build embedded software for medical devices used in life saving surgeries
A program for utilizing data analytics services to program traffic signals
A program to integrate the billing systems in use by a large telecom operator

explanation: In this program, even a single defect can cause loss of life. Hence the philosophy should be geared towards zero defects.

text: What is the difference between projects, programs and portfolios?

choices.text: A project provides benefits to a program, which coordinates them to create a strategic value, whereas portfolios effectively maintain and sustain the benefits for the organization
A portfolio create a program for effectively delivery management of projects, which then deliver the strategic benefits
A project provides a set of deliverables to a program which integrates them to create benefits which flow into the portfolio which is of strategic importance to the organization
A projects goal is to create something of temporary and unique value, whereas a program takes over what a project creates and a portfolio elevates it to a strategic level

explanation: This is the best statement keeping in mind the definitions of projects, programs and portfolios (Section 1.2.1)

text: A manufacturer of high end watches based in Switzerland is planning to enter a new market. What should be the first step for the company on this venture?

choices.text: Establish a joint venture with a local company
Prepare a business case
Undertake a detailed market study
Issue a program charter and appoint a program manager

explanation: The first step should be to prepare a business case and come up with a business justitiction. The market study may be a part of the business case preparation activity, but a detailed one may not be necessary if data is already available about the target market. Establishment of a joint venture may or may not be desirable and seems a bit presumptive, when the program is still in the evaluation stage. For similar reason, issuance of a program charter is a little premature. The business justification needs to be created first.

text: A company is looking to reduce its operational expenses by half in view of a tough financial year and mounting debt. Which of the following programs will help achieve this?

choices.text: Undertake a review of the portfolio and the competitive positioning of the company
Find the worst performing businesses in the past year and exit those businesses
Carry out a cost audit across the company to find out where the money is being spent
Start separate programs in each portfolio to look at opportunities to cut costs

explanation: Option C seems the only realistic option because the cuts (50%) are very deep. It cannot be achieved by cost audits or cost reduction programs in each business. Though it is a tough choice, the company needs to decide which business it intends to continue to invest. It cannot be based on past performance alone

text: In what way does the program architecture help in benefits management?

choices.text: It documents the initial understanding of the businesss requirements and expectations from a program
It helps establish a mechanism for monitoring and controlling the program
It helps correlate the components and how they contribute to the benefits
It is helpful in understanding the technology and design principles for the program

explanation: The program architecture defines the structure of the components by identifying the relationships among the components and the rules that govern their inclusion. (Section 4.2.2 of the standard for program management, 4th edition). B maps closest to this idea of the architecture.

text: Who should attend the closure meeting for a program?

choices.text: Select team members, project managers, program manager, program sponsor
Select team members, project managers, a neutral facilitator, program steering committee
All team members, project managers, program manager, program sponsor
A Program manager, project managers, PMO representative, select stakeholders

explanation: D represents a good choice because it covers a balanced set of representatives. Select stakeholders (including team members) can provide insights into what went well and what could be better, The PMO representative can function as a neutral facilitator as well as provide guidance with regard to what kind of information may be useful to capture. The other options are missing one or more of these elements. For example, A is missing a neutral facilitator, B misses the point by asking ALL team members to be present, C is missing stakeholders who may not be team members

text: A program consists of 5 projects and 2 operations. Who should be responsible for the identification of risks on the program?

choices.text: The program managers and the project managers
All the stakeholders of the program
The program manager, the project managers and the operations managers
The program team

text: Which of the following is the most appropriate sequence for closure activities on a program?

choices.text: Closure of projects, Program Closure, Transition and benefits sustainment, Financial closure, Closing Program Procurements
Closure of projects, Closing Program Procurements, Transition and benefits sustainment, Financial Closure, Program closure
Transition and benefits sustainment, Closure of projects, Financial closure, Closing Program Procurements, Program Closure
Program Closure, Closure of projects and operations, Transition and benefits sustainment, Closing Program Procurements, Financial Closure

explanation: The projects within the program must be closed first. The program procurements must be closed, which may have an impact on the transitions and finances. The program will close only when all of these processes are completed.

text: A newly initiated program has most of its work components being executed in foreign countries. Which of the following would be the biggest concern for the program manager?

choices.text: Finding the best set of partners for the work components in foreign countries
Ensuring that the right resources are available
Ensuring that the scope of the work components being executed remotely are broken down using the WBS
Optimize the program's ROI by shutting down the components with lower RoI and initiating those with higher RoI

explanation: A and B are generic concerns which are common to every program. The primary concern would be to ensure availability of resources to work - especially when they are in a foreign country. Outsourcing or partnering (option-C) would be just one of the options that can be used for this

text: The program manager was sitting on the change control board for a project within the program. They were evaluating a change request that was within the reserves of the project and the project manager was in favor of moving forward. What else should be the program manager be worried about?

choices.text: Adherence to organization wide processes in change and configuration management
Evaluating the impact on any other program component
The change should contribute to the benefits that the program is trying to deliver
Making sure the change is aligned with the strategy of the organization

explanation: The project manager seems to have already done the due diligence with regard to the impact assessment, so there is not much "process" related concern here. All of the project level changes may not necessarily have a correlation with program level benefits (D). Maintaining the strategic alignment may be important, but it is unlikely to be disturbed by a small change that can be accommodated by a project's reserves. The most logical choice is C, because the program manager definitely needs to worry about the impact of the change on other components.

text: A program manager looks after a program comprising 15 projects at different sites spread out geographically over different continents. The program manager regularly holds a “staff meeting” where she calls all the project managers to share information about the program and topics of general interest. Which of the following is the LEAST suitable agenda item for such a staff meeting?

choices.text: Demonstration of a tool built by Project C to carry out non-destructive testing of micro-electronic parts, which may be useful to other projects
Discuss measures to address the people retention issues in the program
Discuss final performance data about Project D, a project that was recently concluded successfully
Best practice sharing by Project A – initiative to trigger innovation

explanation: The performance data for a specific project may not necessarily be relevant to other projects; hence this is the least relevant topic. All other topics may be relevant for the meeting.

text: A program manager took over the management of a program which has been running for about 3 years. She found that many of the projects use the services of fabrication and manufacturing units operated by different vendors in a remote location. She sensed that there may be an opportunity to rationalize and optimize. How should the program manager go about this?

choices.text: Centralize procurement for the program for a period of 6 months, during which time she can evaluate the current vendors and move all the work to the best among them
Ask the project managers how open they would be to switch vendors if there were opportunities to save money in the bargain
Initiate a component and assign resources to a team that will evaluate the work currently being outsourced and recommend opportunities to rationalize and optimize
Use the services of the PMO to identify the preferred suppliers among supplier units and start negotiations

explanation: The program manager must first evaluate the possibility and get into the detailed feasibility analysis. Many aspects including cost, time, quality, risk etc. need to be considered before a decision can be made.

text: An organization has a practice of a six monthly audit of all programs conducted by the Program Management Office. After a recent audit, a number of recommendations were made. Which of the following is the LEAST appropriate recommendation to be included in the final report?

choices.text: The program seems to be making good use of the organization’s tools and templates with regard to quality assurance procedures and should continue to leverage them
The program should review the effectiveness of the communication plan as the customers did not find many of the reports being sent to them to be useful
The program should review the adequacy of the contingency reserves of the components and the overall program on a regular basis
The program seems has done a thorough job of stakeholder identification but it is focused on the engagement of only some stakeholders – it should ensure equal engagement with all stakeholders

explanation: This is an incorrect statement. The engagement plan for stakeholders is to be customized based on the program’s view in terms of their interest and influence. It is not correct to say all the stakeholders need to be actively engaged. The other statements make sense if they are borne out by the findings of the audit.

text: Projects A and B are part of a larger program. Project A was delayed due to an identified project level risk, and there is a cascading effect of the delay on Project B and the overall program. The delay will cause a monetary loss of $50,000 to Project A. The impact of the delay in project B is $40,000. How should this be funded?

choices.text: It should be funded through the program level contingency reserves
It should be funded through the management reserves of project B and if those are insufficient, through the program reserves
It should be funded by the program level management reserves
It should be funded through the contingency reserves of project A, since the delays were caused by project A

explanation: Options A and C are ruled out because they mention management reserves, which are not appropriate in this case (see explanation for Q. 169). Project A’s contingency reserves cannot provide for the cascading impact of its own risks. It is squarely the program management responsibility to manage dependencies and provide solutions for the issues arising out of unmet dependencies. So in this case, the program’s contingency reserves should be used.

text: A large software company just announced a goal of getting 20% operating margins within the next year. A program manager is trying to cascade the organization level objectives down to the individual components and their managers. The program has negative operating margins and is hoping to achieve break even in the following year. Which of the following is the best way to achieve alignment with the organizational objectives?

choices.text: Discuss with the component managers how the program can achieve the goal of 20% or higher margin in a year
Discuss with the portfolio manager and program sponsor to clarify and set expectations
Set goals for each component to contribute to increasing revenue by 20%
Set goals for each component to reduce operational expenses by 20%

explanation: The contribution of each item in the portfolio is different. For instance, some portfolios may be targeting revenue growth, whereas others might be targeting operational savings. When an organization sets a strategic goal, it is not necessary that all the portfolios and programs within the organization have uniform goals. It is important to understand properly the context for a program rather than blindly try to mimic the goals.

text: A program consists of several projects. One of them has been hit with several risk events recently and the project manager escalated a concern to the program manager that she has run out of her allocated contingency reserves, with 6 months left to completion. How should the program manager respond?

choices.text: There is no point in asking for additional reserves as only 6 months are left - the project manager can always dip into management reserves if an eventuality arises
Ask for an estimation of the required reserves based on a revised outlook towards risks in the remaining period
Ask for an estimation of the required reserves based on a revised outlook towards risks in the remaining period
It is not a matter of concern, as long as the program reserves are adequate and can cover the uncertainties related to the project

explanation: It is important to note that the program level contingency reserves are not a substitute for the project level reserves (section 8.7.4). Each project must maintain a comfortable level of reserves based on the outlook towards risks in the remaining period.

text: A program for a multinational company comprises of 10 different projects. The purpose of the program is to standardize on procurement practices, global supplier agreements. In doing so, it is envisaged that there is potential to cut operating costs by about 20% because more than 40% of the operational expense is routed as payments to contractors. The program office is designing a dashboard for tracking progress. Which of the following would be of most interest to the program manager?

choices.text: Percent of milestones delivered on time
Number of escalations received from Suppliers
Actual v/s planned progress on the projects
Number of suppliers, with whom contract consolidation was achieved

explanation: The program manager’s primary focus is to ensure that the benefits desired are being delivered. C is most in line with the intended benefits (operational cost savings).

text: A UN mandated re-construction program is being conducted in a remote country in Africa. Health centers are being run in each major location to help the personnel who are working on the program. It works out very well because medical facilities are otherwise far away and people working on the program often need assistance. These health centers can be referred to:

choices.text: Work that is related to but not part of the program
Other work that is part of the program
A part of the Program Office – supporting the program
A project that is part of the program

explanation: A program can incorporate other work that is not part of any component project but adds to or contributes to additional benefits of control in terms of program management. Provision of health care facilities to workers is an institutionalized benefit run by the program to help the staff working on different components.

text: Emilio was recently appointed as a program manager for a program that aims to achieve a 30% cost reduction across 10 different functional areas of an organization. The program charter is about to be issued. The organization has traditionally been functionally focused and the functional leaders enjoy tremendous clout. Emilio is worried how he would be able to influence the functions and deliver the results that the organization expects. What is the best thing for Emilio to do?

choices.text: Call for a meeting of all the functional leaders and explain to them the benefit of the program to the overall organization
Emilio should focus on doing the best he can and leave the rest to the program steering committee
Attend a class about influencing without authority, as he would need to do that a lot during the program
Negotiate up-front to get the required authority and commitment from the functional leaders

explanation: For a functionally oriented organization to go in for a significant (30%) cut in costs would be a big change. It will not be easy for Emilio to drive this change unless there is clear commitment from all the functional leaders and he has been sufficiently authorized. The best time to ask for this authority is up-front, during the chartering process and Emilio should try to that first – before resorting to other means (A, C or D).

text: A well-diversified automobile company just launched a new commercial vehicle in the market. It has not done very well despite getting the highest ratings from independent rating agencies. The reason is that the company is viewed as a low cost supplier and does not enjoy customer confidence. As the revenues have not met the targets, the program is not being funded to develop the model further. What is the best thing for the program manager to do?

choices.text: Think of easy to add new features that will create a greater excitement for the vehicle
Stop the current model and launch a new one with a greater style quotient
Invest in a targeted marketing campaign that stresses on the quality and utility of the vehicle
Lower the cost of the vehicle to boost sales

explanation: If the product is good (as the ratings suggest), then it should be possible to correct perceptions about cost and quality – especially since the company is targeting the commercial segment. This is probably among the first things to try to boost sales which are the core problem.

text: During a recently portfolio review, a set of medical products owned by a healthcare company were deemed “non-strategic”. Although they make decent revenues and have a fairly large customer base, they do not align with the future strategic plan for the company. Which of the following would be the best course of action for program managers who are currently managing these products?

choices.text: Initiate a research project to study these products became non-strategic and recommend ways to make them strategic again
Try and internally search other positions in the company so that they get to work on strategically important products
Look for partners who would be interested in licensing and re-selling these products, so that the costs can be minimized, while protecting the interests of existing customers
Put up a strong business case in favor of continuing to retain these products on the strategic roadmap given the number of customers and revenues they bring in

explanation: Once the strategic decision is made, there is no point in arguing against – or trying to reverse the decision (Options B and D). A is trying to jump ship. In a way, C is also trying to get the organization out of the product lines, but it is a much more professional way of doing so. By finding a partner who may be interested in the license and re-sell model, the products may get a new lease of life, while the existing customer base will continue be served.

text: A program has been constituted for a healthcare company to ensure regulatory compliance. Due to a recent change in the norms, a few projects now need additional resources and funding for meeting the new reporting purposes. The change was not anticipated earlier and cannot be met out of the project or program reserves. Who is responsible for providing the additional resources and funds needed?

choices.text: The concerned project managers
Program Manager
The regulatory authorities
program steering committee

explanation: The program steering committee is responsible to take decisions about funding requirements. (Sec 6.2.3 - Standard for program management). This requirement has come about as a result of the change in regulatory norms and affects multiple projects, so the program manager will most likely raise a change request which will go to the program steering committee for approval.

text: A company makes cleaning appliances and finds that the market for its products in the United States and Europe is saturated. It has therefore initiated a program to launch a foray into the growing economies in the APAC region. Which of the following would be candidate projects to be included as part of this program? (A) – Conduct market research in target geographies to identify the size of the opportunity (B) – Make the user manuals and support web sites available in local languages (C) – Identify partners to source and sell spares locally (D) – Set up sales quotas and compensation structure for the sales people in the region

choices.text: A, B and C
A, B, C and D
B , C and D
A, C and D

explanation: The components A, B and C clearly are projects that would add value to and contribute towards the benefits that the program is trying to achieve. D is also aligned with the program but falls in the category of “Other work” and not really a project.

text: A company engaged in business process outsourcing for banks and financial institutions recently had a data integrity issue reported in an audit. This is a very serious issue as the company handles all the customer data for its clients. The company took the breach seriously and has launched a program to look at all aspects of security and implement water-tight measures. One of the recommendations was to set up a governance structure for periodically reviewing the security measures. Which of the following are relevant factors to consider while designing the governance structure for security? (I) Industry standards like ISO, BS 7799, etc. (II) Organization’s current practices (III) Expert recommendations (IV) Compliance requirements from specific customers

choices.text: I, II and IV
I, II, III and IV
I, III and IV
IV only

explanation: The industry standards are important because they set a benchmark in terms of security practices in place. Expert recommendations are welcome because they bring in a lot of experience in terms of possible weaknesses and loopholes. Similarly, specific customers may have specific requirements which need to be adhered to. The existing structure in the organization is not relevant because it has obviously proven to be inadequate. Paying attention to the existing structure may limit the thinking in terms of measures that need to be put in place.

text: A program manager working in a venture funded startup company in the highly competitive online advertising metering space is reviewing its roadmap. There are three main areas in which project ideas were presented. (A) Adding a new search engine to the algorithm which competitors already support and might result in customers switching over (B) Improving the scalability of the existing engine to support expected transaction volumes (C) Improving the accuracy of the hit counts so that space can be auctioned with more precise information. Which of the following should be of greatest concern to the program manager?

choices.text: There are no new or exciting features in the this list
It is important to correctly predict the future volumes so that idea B can be based on a realistic goal
Absence of feature A seems to add serious risk and it must be completed as soon as possible to remain competitive
It is important that data quality issues are sorted out which will help development of all the new ideas

explanation: For a small company in a highly competitive space, it is very important to have a competitive differentiator, so the program manager must constantly look for exciting ideas and prioritize them higher.

text: There are about 1500 staff members working on a large international program with multiple projects and operations included in it. The program manager holds a quarterly all-hands meeting where all team members around the globe join in via telephone and video conferencing. During the Q&A session of one of the meetings, a team member brought up a risk that the program manager was not previously apprised about. In the project she was working on that many tasks were being performed manually, because the machinery that was ordered had not yet arrived and this could delay or compromise the quality of the deliverables. What should the program manager do about this?

choices.text: Ask the team member to take the matter offline with her project manager and let them investigate the issue internally
Ask the procurement manager to investigate the reasons for the delay in delivery of the machines and expedite it
Thank the team member for bringing the issue up and make a commitment to investigate and come back with a response
Put the project manager on the spot by asking him to explain why this risk was not flagged earlier and what was the action plan

explanation: This is a large program. Prima facie, this appears to be a local issue that the project manager should solve. The important thing though is that as a program manager, you would want all the team members to feel that they can flag risks and issues to you early and that you would take necessary action on it. Option D seems closest to providing the right feedback to the team member and encouraging this behavior.

text: The telecom regulatory authority (let us call it R) in a country has mandated the introduction of mobile number portability, i.e. allowing subscribers to switch providers (let us call them P) without having to change the number. An external vendor (let us call it O) has been appointed to operate the program and the providers have been given a period of 3 months to make necessary changes in their systems. The regulator is contemplating how to constitute the program steering committee, in particular whom to appoint as the Program Sponsor and Program manager. What would the best recommendation for this program?

choices.text: The Sponsor should be from R, program manager from R or O and the Board should comprise representatives from R, P and O
The Sponsor should be from P or R, program manager from R and the Board should comprise representatives from R, P and O
The Sponsor should be from O, program manager from R or P and the Board should comprise representatives from R and O
The Sponsor should be from R, program manager from P or O and the Board should comprise representatives from R, P and O

explanation: In this case the program is mandated by the regulator and therefore the sponsor should be from R. This is true even if the regulator may not necessarily provide funds or resources for the program, because ultimately the regulator will evangelize and drive the program forward. The program manager could be from R or O, because the operator will need to be able to transition the program and the regulator will also need to ensure the transition is smooth. The representatives from R, P and O will need to be on the Board because they are all key contributors and stakeholders in the program.

text: A program is going through an annual budgeting cycle. There is a possibility of a 50% budget cut across the board in the organization. The program manager is collecting component level budget estimates so that they can be rolled up. What guidance should the program manager give the component managers for their budgeting exercise?

choices.text: Look for projects that can be canceled or deferred for the time being
Look at the activities that can be pushed to the following year to reduce the current year’s budgetary needs
Look at means to reduce the budget requirements by 50% over the previous year
Take a fresh look at the component’s activities for the forthcoming year and be prepared to prioritize

explanation: The cut in budget is quite drastic (50%) and cannot be achieved by using incremental budgeting approaches. Of all the options provided, the most inclusive is to look at all activities and prioritize what is essential. This technique is sometimes called zero base budgeting

text: A start-up company has an app development program that scouts for opportunities to develop applications for mobile devices primarily focused on maps and related services. In the latest release, Google maps started offering similar features for free. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Discuss with the project and product managers about the features to be added to the next release of the app
Recommend closure of the component team for this app and consider how the accrued benefits can be transitioned and sustained
Recommend investment in a marketing campaign to promote the features of the app over Google’s
Consider acquiring Google’s map functionality so that it can be integrated with the application

explanation: The program manager has to display a sense of pragmatism while determining strategy. When a competitor is offering the same features for free, there seems to be no point in continuing to invest in that area. It is better to exit the space and try to identify other spaces to invest in.

text: An IT services company offers remote management of IT infrastructure and applications to its customers. One of the programs being managed for a particular client was in deep trouble, getting consistently poor customer satisfaction scores. Julie, an expert program manager was appointed by the PMO to investigate and suggest remedial action. She found that the program did not have clearly defined service level agreements with the customer, no clear charter for the components, project plans were either too perfunctory or absent and nobody in the program team could articulate how the program aligns with the business strategy. Which of these should be fixed first?

choices.text: Charters should be issued and approved first as it would immediately become clear which projects should not have been started in the first place
Service level agreements should be defined first as this would clarify expectations from the customer and act as the basis for planning
The project plans should be reviewed and completed because everything needs to follow the plan
Strategic alignment should be explained first to the team as everything follows from the strategic benefits overall

explanation: The issue under investigation is low customer satisfaction, which means that there is a clear mismatch of expectations between the customer and the organization. This needs to be fixed first.

text: A newly appointed program manager is struggling to come to terms with the level and rigor of risk management processes to be applied. The project managers seem to be doing a reasonable job preparing the risk register and planning responses for the identified risks on their individual projects, but the program manager is unable to figure out how to translate all this information to determine the extent of contingency and management reserves needed. What is the best way to come up with this plan?

choices.text: Program manager should consult the program steering committee and ask for level of reserves that are normally considered acceptable
Program manager should consult the Corporate PMO for advice
Program manager should appoint a risk management consultant who can cover for this gap in understanding
Program manager should meet with the project managers and take their opinion

explanation: The Program management office is supposed to be an organizational entity that is meant to mentor and guide program managers and guide with regard to process questions like this. It may be an option to go to risk management consultants, but it is better to tap into internal expertise first. The program steering committee is not meant to be an advisory forum and the project managers may have an opinion but may not be able to have the program manager’s vantage position to be able to determine program level reserves.

text: A customer escalated an issue to a program manager. They were promised delivery from one of the projects by a certain date and the project manager has reported the status as delayed. Upon inquiring with the project manager, the program manager learns that the deadline is impossible to meet and the Sales team made a big mistake in promising it to the customer. What should be the immediate concern for the program manager?

choices.text: Let the program steering committee know about this situation as they will also ultimately hear from the customer
Figure out why the Sales team made such a wild promise in the first place and put in place measures to prevent recurrence of this in the future
Figure out why the issue was not highlighted by the project manager earlier, i.e. before the customer escalated to her
Get an estimate of the amount of delay and present a revised forecast and a mitigation plan to the customer

explanation: The program manager has received an escalation and she needs to respond to the escalation. D is the only answer that talks about the response. The other actions may all be valid actions, but do not address how the program manager should respond, which is of immediate concern.

text: A large number of services and projects for a customer having diversified business interests are being managed by a vendor as part of a program. The program manager was recently alerted to the possibility of providing some additional services to the same customer, which would nearly double the business. The new services are in an adjacent domain in which the vendor has no prior experience or in-house expertise. However, it is possible to sub-contract this work to other vendors. What would be the best way for the program manager to proceed?

choices.text: Wait for the formal RFP to be floated by the customer and then consult the program steering committee
Submit a proposal to the customer and start looking for vendors who can perform the work under a sub-contracting arrangement
Prepare the charter for evaluating the possibility of doing the the additional work and submit to the program steering committee for approval
Discuss with the project and service managers in the program about their opinion regarding offering these additional services

explanation: The additional work brings in additional business (hence has a valid business driver) but the organizations capability and willingness to work on it has to be evaluated. Since it is in an adjacent domain, the approval of the program steering committee is necessary.

text: One of the projects that are part of a program has been delayed by about 4 weeks. What should the program manager be MOST concerned about?

choices.text: Identify the impact of the project’s delays on other parameters like cost, risk, quality and the ability to deliver to the baseline plan and try to mitigate it to the extent possible
Identify the impact of the project’s delays on the other projects and work with the other project managers to mitigate it to the extent possible
Identify the root causes of the delay and come up with an action plan to institutionalize the learning from the causes
Identify the impact of the project’s delays on the ability of the program to deliver the benefits back to the organization and try to mitigate it to the extent possible

explanation: All the statements are correct and should be important to the program manager. However, the most important goal of the program manager is to deliver the intended benefits to the organization. Therefore statement D is most inclusive and would probably involve the actions implied in the other statements to the extent that they contribute towards benefits deliver.

text: At a scheduled program level business review, a number of risks were highlighted by the project and operations managers. Which one should the program manager devote her personal attention to?

choices.text: A project is running late by about 2 weeks due to power shortages in the region which requires re-scheduling of the project working hours
Operations manager says staff turnover is a risk due to market conditions and the requirement to work in shifts
A project is facing shortage of skilled man-power in a niche skill set that is required to deliver a particular component
Operations manager complains that the warranty costs are rising due to failure of multiple products in the field when they are deployed in untested scenarios

explanation: This seems to point to failure of project teams to test the products in deployment scenarios. Since it seems to be impacting multiple products, it is pointing at a systemic flaw and program level action. The other risks are also valid, but they should be dealt with primarily at the component levels.

text: An automobile company is running a program for development and manufacture of its best-selling hatchback model. There are 4 integrated manufacturing plants across the country and a central research and development center where new developments take place. One day the paint shop at the largest factory burnt down. An emergency sub-program was put in place to reconstruct the paint shop, while minimizing the disruption to operations. In order to maintain production levels, the program manager has identified a paint factory about 100 miles away from the affected factory where the finished chassis can be sent for painting. The manager of the paint-shop operations brings up the issue that the workers are hesitant to move to the new location. All of the following measures will help address the issue, EXCEPT:

choices.text: Ask the workers who are resisting the move to work reduced hours with a slightly reduced compensation
Provide a free, express bus service to reduce the commute time for workers who do not want to shift their residence
Provide an additional allowance to the workers who agree to move and work at the new location
Order a safety audit of the affected factory and implement corrective actions

explanation: Option A talks about rewards and B talks about reducing the inconvenience. D is about penalty, which may sound harsh, but still can be effective. C is not addressing the core issue which is the reluctance of the workers to move.

text: A program has been initiated to implement an enterprise wide resource planning (ERP) system. Due to the heavy customization needed, multiple projects were initiated. There is a lot of user dissatisfaction as the projects are getting rolled out. It is found that the operational group which is responsible for supporting the end users has received product training but is not aware of the customizations and is heavily reliant on the project teams for help. The project teams are under severe deadline pressure. They see the support work as a disruption and tend to give it the lowest priority. This slows down the response and holds up vital business functions for the users. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Talk to the program steering committee & suggest the inclusion of the support and maintenance as part of the program until the customizations are completed so that they can be better managed together
Ask the provider of the ERP tool to organize a one week training to better enable the support staff
Implement an operational best practice model like CoBIT or ITIL to ensure a more efficient support team
Ask for details of all the user reported errors and undertake a thorough root cause analysis before deciding on what to do

explanation: The core of the issue is the lack of proper enablement of the operational staff, specifically with respect to the customizations that are being carried out by the project teams. This is only addressed through option A.

text: Two projects in a program are using the services of a vendor to deliver electronic chips for a large assembly. During a quarterly vendor review for the program, Project Manager A gave huge thumbs up for the vendor on quality and punctuality. Project Manager B rated the same supplier very poorly on the same aspects and wants permission to change vendors. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Give the vendor a 3 month extension due to good performance on Project A, but issue a warning that unless Project B was also satisfied, the contract may not be renewed
Ask Project Manager B to get in touch with Project Manager A to discuss the strengths and weaknesses of the vendor and come up with a recommendation
Ask project manager B to relay the feedback to the vendor and come up with a vendor development plan
Look up the past performance data for the vendor from the PMO archives to get more data about the vendor’s performance on other projects and programs

explanation: The program should focus on building relationships with vendors. Since the vendor has done well on at least one project, there is certainly potential for improvement. Perhaps there are practices that project A are following which are helping the vendor perform better.

text: A service improvement program is being implemented in the repairs and maintenance division of a company manufacturing high-end printers. The program manager noticed that in the past year, the cost of the repair and maintenance operation was well below budgeted levels, but there were instances where the clients would report a delay in completing the repairs beyond the service level agreements that were signed. Once the repairs were done, there was rarely any recurrence of the complaint. In response to this, the program manager decided to set performance objectives for the repair team based on “turnaround time for repairs”. What should the program manager expect to see after this change?

choices.text: The repairs will initially happen faster, but the quality will be poor and the cost will be somewhat uncertain
The repairs will actually slow down in the long term, while the cost will remain the same and quality will be poorer
The repairs will happen faster, but the cost will go up and the quality of the job may suffer
The repairs will happen faster, but at the cost of quality and the cost will be the same

explanation: Due to strong incentives to finish the job quickly, the repair staff will likely take the costlier route to restore service. There might be an impact on quality, however this is not very certain. As a program manager, one must be clear about what kind of behavior is being encouraged and discouraged by the metrics that are put in place.

text: A product line is deemed as non-strategic for an organization and is not getting much new investment. However it is earning sizeable revenues and has some very influential customers. The program manager is asked by the program steering committee to submit a proposal about the long term plan for this product line. There were a number of options considered. Which one is most suitable to be presented to the committee?

choices.text: Identify a partner who will take up and maintain the product line under licensing and revenue sharing model
Provide the customers a free upgrade to the latest products if they will stop requesting support for this product line
Announce a deadline of 6 months during which the customers will have to switch to other products or accept the withdrawal of services
Outsource the entire work to a low cost supplier so that cost of operations can be minimized while retaining the revenue

explanation: The product line may not be strategic to the company, but the customers still want it. Therefore, options B and C (which essentially ask the customers to abandon the usage) are likely to backfire. Option D is a risky option because the low cost may also come with low quality. Option A is interesting because it brings in an interested partner who will have incentives to provide good services to the existing customers and also benefit as a result.

text: A manufacturing organization is adopting Lean methodologies. A program has been constituted for achieving this transition. The Sponsor for the program is a senior executive who is convinced about the business benefits and is ready to commit the funds and resources necessary for the program. What are the 3 things the program manager should ask the Sponsor to do?

choices.text: Provide funds and resources, Manage the stakeholders of the program, Be available to deal with escalations
Manage the stakeholders of the program, Recruit the best project managers, Generate cross-functional support
Generate cross-functional support, provide funds and resources, Recruit the best project managers for the program
Generate cross-functional support, be available to deal with escalations, Ask good questions to track progress

explanation: This the only option where all the phrases make sense. In B and D, Recruit the best project managers is not correct – this is the Program manager’s responsibility. In C, managing stakeholders is not correct – it is the program manager’s responsibility to engage (not manage) stakeholders.

text: A large organization recently opened a new center for clinical research in a different geography. This activity was so far performed only in the parent geography and the existing staff has expressed serious reservations and anxiety about the move. What is the best statement that the program manager can make to justify the decision and address the team’s anxiety?

choices.text: The opening up of the new center will help reduce cost of research and improve operational margins
Diversity fosters innovation and inclusion of fresh talent will improve the quality of research
The program will announce a relocation policy so that staff can relocate to other regions if they so desire
There is no need to worry about the new center as there are no plans to retrench staff in the parent geography at least for 6 months

explanation: Statement A is probably correct and a valid reason from the organization’s perspective but it does nothing to assuage employee concerns. Statement B – even if it has a positive intent, may not immediately offer any succor to employees – some may even take it as a message that the organization is trying to move the entire operation. Statement –D is trying to reassure but only offering a guarantee of 6 months and offers no justification. Statement-C is focusing on the positive side and making the assertion that diversity would be good for everybody. Hence C is the best statement under the circumstances.

text: At the program initiation phase, the program manager realized that many of the components seemed to involve a very high amount of uncertainty. The project managers asked for high levels of management reserves as it was not possible to fully predict the risks on their components. Which of the following would help the program manager limit the amount of management reserves and create greater visibility into the uncertainties surrounding the program?

choices.text: Discuss with the project managers and make appropriate recommendation about the size of the contingency and management reserves needed
Appoint risk management consultants with domain expertise to better identify and analyze the risks
Outsource the work to a third party
Take the issue to the program steering committee to ascertain if the risk level is commensurate with the organization’s risk thresholds

explanation: The core issue here is that the components are unable to identify and analyze the risks, causing the management reserves to be bloated. The best way to increase visibility into the unknown unknowns and limit the management reserve requirement would be to provide greater due diligence in the identification and analysis, which is what the risk management consultant can potentially bring in. Actions B, C and D are reactive in nature and do not help in improving visibility into the risks, which is the question here.

text: A program team is spread over multiple countries. Due to a movement in currency exchange rates, the cost of operation in one of the countries has come down drastically. What would be a prudent thing for the program manager do to benefit from this occurrence?

choices.text: Return the excess budget to the organization
Discuss with the finance department about possibility of locking in the exchange rate by forward contracts
Do nothing, as exchange rate fluctuations are very volatile and my cause unnecessary risk to the program
Expand operations in that country

explanation: The first step should be to check if the current low rate can be leveraged to lock in the savings. Once they have been, then options C and D can be considered. The revenues and expenses of an international organization will always be subject to exchange rate fluctuations. Decisions about where to send work cannot be taken on the basis of movement in exchange rate alone.

text: A manufacturing organization is adopting Lean methodologies. A program has been constituted for achieving this transition. The Sponsor for the program is a senior executive who is convinced about the business benefits and is ready to commit funds and resources necessary for the program. The program manager is trying to identify senior stakeholders from every function that will be impacted so that they can be engaged and on-boarded to become champions for the initiative for that function. What is it that the program manager should NOT ask from these stakeholders?

choices.text: Budgetary support for changes needed within their functions
Help with recruiting change agents within their functions
To help evangelize the program within their functions
Participate in the program steering committee meetings to review progress periodically

explanation: The program sponsor is already committed to providing funds and resources; hence budgetary support is not needed separately from the functions.

text: A large program comprises of 7 projects and a service operation that supports the output of the projects and a program costing division that supports the program manager.
