Which of the following should be explicitly included in the program management plan rather than the component level plans?

choices.text: Stakeholder registers
Risk registers
Cost management plan
Interface management plan

explanation: The stakeholder and risk registers as well as the cost management plans would need to be maintained at both the component as well as the program levels. The interface management plan may be centrally maintained as part of the program management plan because it is in the program domain that the interfaces and integrations between the components will be managed.

text: A leading company is organized as follows. The R&D function is responsible for coming up with new product ideas and developing prototypes, Engineering function is responsible to design the product and set up the manufacturing process. Quality function is responsible to ensure that the processes and product is correct and meets expectations of current and future users. Manufacturing function takes over the operations once the Engineering is complete and Quality sign-off has been received. A highly strategic program is started in this company to come up with new products that rely on renewable energy sources. A number of projects are in flight to look at different products and components. What is the best way for the program manager to recruit the resources required for this program?

choices.text: Ask the functional managers to provide the resources
Ask the project managers to drive the recruitment processes as they know best the number and type of resources needed
Outsource the work so that the resources can be obtained quickly
Set up a recruitment function that will understand the requirements and determine the appropriate sourcing strategy

explanation: From the description provided, this seems to be a functional or matrix organization. In such an organization the resources are owned in the respective functions and hence they should be approached first (even if it is ultimately decided to outsource some or all of the work).

text: An automobile company is running a program for development and manufacture of its best-selling hatchback model. There are 4 integrated manufacturing plants across the country and a central research and development center where new developments take place. One day the paint shop at the largest factory burnt down. An emergency sub-program was put in place to reconstruct the paint shop, while minimizing the disruption to operations. Which of the data will be LEAST relevant to planning the scale of the alternative site for temporarily shifting the painting operations?

choices.text: Quantities and value of the raw material and machinery damaged in the fire
Demand forecast for the vehicles for the next 3 months
Lease rates of the alternative paint shop
Capacity utilization of all the factories for the past 6 months

explanation: Demand forecast will give an indication of the production level that needs to be maintained in the factories. The capacity utilization of the factories will help in assessing how much production can be shifted to other factories. The lease rates for the alternative paint factory indicate the cost of shifting temporarily to another facility. These are all relevant factors. The losses in the fire are not directly helpful in determining the plan for alternatives

text: A leading company is organized as follows. The R&D function is responsible for coming up with new product ideas and developing prototypes, Engineering function is responsible to design the product and set up the manufacturing process. Quality function is responsible to ensure that the processes and product is correct and meets expectations of current and future users. Manufacturing function takes over the operations once the Engineering is complete and Quality sign-off has been received. A highly strategic program is started in this company to come up with new products that rely on renewable energy sources. One of the issues for the program manager is that the team is not displaying a program identity and larger sense of purpose. They are still confining their loyalty to either their function or their product or the project. Which of the following is likely to be the most effective in addressing this?

choices.text: Frequently invite the CEO and board members to address the team
Create a brand for the program by distributing T-shirts and putting up posters about the program and its successes
Ask the project managers and functional managers to emphasize the strategic importance of the program
Circulate a survey about why they are not displaying program loyalty and take actions based on the findings

explanation: All of the measures are interesting. The impact would be higher if there is something that the team members and touch and feel, rather than hear as speeches. Communication is a complex process and has to be bolstered through multiple channels.

text: An organization intends to add a new product line that is in an adjacent space to an existing product line. Many of the components required to build the product are already present and there are strong partners available to fill in the gaps. The key success criterion would be to be able to integrate the components and develop a compelling value proposition that can be used to build a market. What is the best organization structure for this new product line?

choices.text: As a new portfolio item so that the strategic investments and benefits can be tracked effectively
As a new department or function which can best manage the in-house and vendor expertise required to develop and launch this product line
As a new project with multiple sub-projects to create the components
As a new program that will have projects to build or buy the components and use the program structure to integrate them into a strategic whole

explanation: The components seem to be related and there is a strong emphasis on coordination and integration. There is also an element of other work (e.g. contributing to marketing campaign) which makes this more of a program than portfolio or project.

text: A long running program is in the process of wrapping up. The program has delivered the intended benefits and most components have been closed and transitioned successfully and the rest will finish up in the coming 6 months. About 20% of the program’s budget is still unutilized. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Crash the schedule for the remaining 6 months to deliver the remaining benefits earlier and close the program before schedule
Report the unutilized budget to the steering committee and ask for their advise
Ask the program steering committee permission to utilize the left over budget to reward and recognize the team members who helped the program come in significantly under budget
Review the requirements that were left out of scope due to prioritization if any of them can be implemented with the remaining budget

explanation: The answer D amounts to gold plating. The program should have had a rewards and recognition budget in any case – and doing rewards and recognition at the fag end (as stated in C) is not a good idea. A may or may not be desirable – it depends upon the organization’s needs. B is the most reasonable choice – to let the organization figure out what to do with it.

text: A car manufacturer known for luxury and SUV models has decided to diversity into the economic, fuel efficient and small car segment. A program has been launched to manage the various components related to design, supply chain and assembly line management, etc. in an integrated fashion. The program manager was reviewing the quality reports from different components and noticed that the rate of “rejects” from many factories was increasing. The causal analysis suggested that in majority of the cases, the reason given was poor quality of spares, which were sourced from other suppliers. What action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Call for a meeting with the suppliers and ask them to explain the reasons for poor quality
Check if the quality threshold for the spare parts was excessively high and make corrections if necessary
Point out the deviations to the project managers and ask them to take the necessary action
Set up a committee to study the issue and recommend corrective actions

explanation: The issue seems to be widespread and the data seems to indicate a deeper root cause. This calls for institutionalized action on part of the program. Before such action can be taken, the issue needs to be studied in-depth. So C is the best answer. Other actions seem to be jumping the gun in terms of forming an opinion and proceeding to action on the basis of information that is not obvious.

text: Customer satisfaction ratings for a product line had gone down. In order to review the reasons behind this, an operations review was called by the program manager. One of the metrics that caught the program manager’s attention was that the average time to respond to a complaint had shot up nearly 30%. The operations manager offered a number of explanations for this. Which of the following is NOT a valid explanation?

choices.text: It is found that customers directly call up the engineers and do not inform support staff. Engineering staff do not have the training or resources to respond quickly enough
The support department is under-staffed and is overwhelmed by the number and nature of complaints
The number of complaints coming in via email have gone up and email is not being monitored very actively
The support department has not received proper training and lack technical knowhow on the product

explanation: The issue is about response time. Hence lack of technical know-how cannot be an excuse.

text: Stella, a program manager working on a large program came in to work after a week’s vacation. John, Alexis, Julia and Sunil manage several projects for her and Richard is the Program Sponsor and manager of the portfolio. She had several voice mails on her work phone. Which one seems most urgent?

choices.text: Hi Stella, this is John. Just a heads up that some unexpected errors came up during testing, which will cause a delay of about 2 weeks. I have sent a report – please have a look and send any comments
Hi Stella it is Richard. I was looking for the program costing report you normally send every month. There is a portfolio review next week and I want to make sure we are covered
Hi Stella, this is Alexis. I wanted to talk to you about a resignation on my team. I need to open up a replacement position and would like you approve it as soon as you return
Hi Stella, this is Sunil. Julia and I wanted to meet you to discuss a rate increase by a supplier Realtime Consultants. This will blow up our budgets and we don’t have any alternatives at the moment

explanation: There seems to be an impact on multiple projects and on the program’s finances, with potentially no alternative. This is probably the most urgent issue that the program manager needs to tackle.

text: The roll out of a new version of a mobile operating system is held up due to issues with the accuracy of the mapping application that is bundled with it. The program manager discovers that the issue is likely to take at least 2 more months to get fully rectified. What should the program manager present to the program steering committee?

choices.text: We are looking at the possibility of a delay, but we should put our best engineers on the job and hope that we can solve this issue sooner than 2 months
As this greatly impacts the quality of our product, we should delay the launch by 2 months to fully address this defect
We should not hold up the release of this entire system for one minor issue in the application. We should go ahead and release what we have and follow up with a fix in 2 months
We have three options. We can deliver with this known issue. We could delay the release for 2 months. We could find a workaround for this defect with a slight delay

explanation: As a program manager, one must always try to present multiple options to the program steering committee and take their opinion. Presenting them with a fait accompli might back fire, especially in the scenario that the program

text: A construction program currently leases earth moving equipment at a monthly rental under a T&M contract. A project manager on the site is suggesting that it would be better to simply buy the equipment. In support of his case, he presented the following data. Cost of buying: $80,000 per machine. Monthly rental for the operating lease: $6,000 per month. The equipment pays for itself in less than 14 months. Which of the following data is most important for the program manager to review the decision from the financial perspective?

choices.text: The financial solvency of the supplier
The depreciation policy of the organization
The total cost of ownership of the machine
The rate of discounting

explanation: TCO refers to the total cost of buying AND operating the equipment. This is the most important consideration to make a comparison of buying and leasing options from a purely financial perspective.

text: A component of a program was budgeted at $500,000 during the program planning stage. During the component initiation phase, the component manager revised the cost estimates and put the budget requirement as $750,000. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Defer the initiation of that component
Stick to the original budget unless the scope or schedule baseline for the component has changed
Ask the program steering committee for a proportionate increase in the program budget
Discuss with the component manager the ways to reduce the component budgetary requirements

explanation: It is entirely possible that the component cost estimates may change. This could be due to inflation in cost or simply that more information has come to light about the real or perceived complexity. Instead of relying entirely on the component manager or pushing back on the component manager, the program manager should get into a discussion about what can be done to pull the costs back to the budgeted level. If it is concluded that there are no options, ONLY then should the option to go to the program steering committee be exercised.

text: A program manager does not have staff to take care of program management activities. The program consists of 10 projects and is in the planning phase. The project managers have prepared the work breakdown structure for their projects and the program manager is preparing the program level Work Breakdown Structure (P-WBS). What should be contained in the P-WBS?

choices.text: Consolidation of the individual project’s WBS
High level milestones and activities across the program’s components
Skeletal information about each of the underlying projects
High level deliverables that the program manager would like to track

explanation: The WBS should not contain activities and milestones. The P-WBS should not be just a blind consolidation of all the project’s WBS. It should contain high level deliverables at the level of granularity that can be handled at the program level. This is important because it is stated that the program manager does not have staff and may run out of bandwidth.

text: A program comprises of multiple projects, all of which deliver specific enhancements to a telecom network management system that need to be released simultaneously. One of the enhancements is about providing an automated disaster recovery feature that will immediately switch the customer’s voice and data traffic through an alternate site in the event of a disaster. All the other projects are completed, but the overall deployment is pending because the disaster recovery feature is not working properly. Among the completed projects is an important regulatory report that is time critical. What can be done?

choices.text: Release the projects and find a manual work around for the disaster recovery feature until the defects with the automated solution can be worked out
Set up daily status meetings and teams working round the clock until the defects with the disaster recovery feature are fixed
Release the project which has the regulatory report and continue to work on resolving the issues with the disaster recovery feature
Delay the overall release until the deeper root causes of the defects can be identified and rectified

explanation: It may not be prudent to delay the entire program due to one feature, especially if one of them is time critical. The automated disaster recovery feature may be important, but if the absence of the feature was acceptable till date, the unavailability of the feature for some more time will not be catastrophic. The most pragmatic option is to provide a manual work around for that feature until it can be fixed and released. Meanwhile, the other features can be made available to the customers.

text: A program manager is evaluating which of two projects she would like to fund. Project A was started last year to improve operational cost for a business line by 30%. $300,000 has been already spent on the project and the project manager is asking for another $500,000. Project B has not been started yet. It also aims to achieve 30% savings in operational cost for the same business line and requires a budgetary allocation of $500,000. Which project should the program manager fund?

choices.text: Project A: Because it has already been started and a certain amount of money has been spent on it
Project B: It will achieve the same savings at a lower overall cost, thereby delivering higher RoI
Fund Project A and B both to the extent of half their expectation and encourage both project managers to achieve efficiencies within their own projects
Cannot decide based on this information

explanation: This is based on the principle of sunk cost. The cost already incurred should not be considered while making future investments. So both A and B are incorrect. It does not make any sense to have two parallel projects having the same objective. We need more information about the projects and their future cost-benefit pattern to be able to make a choice.

text: A program has been initiated in a retail food chain to rationalize the portion sizes for different products to increase sales by better matching customer’s buying preferences. One of the issues is that as a result of the recommendations, the company ends up producing a lot of plastic waste. The program is about to be closed and transitioned, when one of the team members points out that the plastic can be recycled giving a marketing advantage for the company as a responsible corporate citizen. What should the program manager do about this suggestion?

choices.text: Stop the closure of the program and initiate a project to see if waste can be recycled and added value delivered to the organization
Raise a request to initiate a new pilot project to re-use plastic waste creatively as suggested by the team member
Ask the team member that though the idea is interesting, it is not directly related to the program’s intent and therefore it cannot be immediately taken up
Send the suggestion to the company’s Sales and Marketing department for them to take it forward

explanation: From the description, it appears that the program has met its intended purpose and is about to close. Nevertheless, the idea that has been floated is interesting and potentially useful to the organization even if it is not aligned to the program’s purpose. The best way to deal with this would be to proceed with the closure formalities but try to capture the idea by initiating a new project to test the idea.

text: A program has been initiated to implement an enterprise wide resource planning system. Due to the heavy customization needed, multiple projects were initiated. The projects are generally well managed and most of the time, they fulfill the scope, cost and time constraints. However, the different modules produced do not integrate very well with each other. For example an order processed through the fulfillment module does not show up in the accounts payable module. This leads to manual data transition efforts and user dissatisfaction. Which of the following measures will best address this situation?

choices.text: Set up performance objectives for the project managers such that every integration error will reduce their bonus payments
Appoint a Technical architect to review the overall design and data model of the system and recommend a mechanism to ensure more seamless integration
Set up an integration testing team that will ensure that proper testing is done before the modules are released to the users
Set up an escalation mechanism for any integration error to be flagged up to the program manager directly, so that speedy resolution can be undertaken

explanation: The occurrence of integration errors seems to be systemic and needs to be addressed pro-actively. Testing is a good idea but it is still too late in the life-cycle if errors are detected during testing. Undertaking a review to improve the design is a much more pro-active step. Remember a program manager must think strategically and have a long term perspective.

text: One of the programs for an integrated energy company involves offshore drilling for gas in a desert. Each location for drilling represents a project until the reserves are ascertained. If the reserves are not commercially viable, the project is closed. If the reserves are commercially viable, new projects are initiated to undertake development activities and then transitioned over to operations. The key resource for each project is the oil rig used for drilling. The daily rentals are very high and availability of rigs is limited. One of the projects closed abruptly due to geological complexity and the rig became available about a month in advance. Another project which was supposed to start using the rig is not scheduled to start for another month. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Raise a change request to return the rig early and seek compensation from the vendor
See if the project can be started early so that the availability of the rig can be harnessed to speed up drilling activity
Explore options to restart the closed project after consulting expert geologists
Ask the program steering committee to take a decision based on the daily rentals and the contractual terms with the rig vendor

explanation: Since the oil rig is a precious and scarce resource, the program manager must try to harness it to the best extent in trying to deliver benefits to the organization.

text: A program is ramping up with the purpose of delivering and maintaining a brand new product line for the company. The program requires resources having a unique combination of skills. The pace of recruitment has been a concern. Which of the following measures is likely to make the most impact?

choices.text: An advertising campaign, including the use of social media
Triple the bonus and offer additional prizes on the internal referral program each referred candidate being recruited
Replace the recruitment team with a more energetic bunch of team members
To bring urgency, let the project managers know that positions that are not filled in the next 2 weeks will be eliminated

explanation: Normally, rewards work better than penalty (option C). Setting up meetings and campaigns may help, but ultimately reward will be a much more powerful influencer and work across the program.

text: A car manufacturer known for luxury and SUV models has decided to diversity into the fast growing economic, fuel efficient and small car segment. A program has been launched to manage the various components related to design, supply chain and assembly line management, etc. in an integrated fashion. The business case for the program is being presented to senior executives. Which of the following is the BEST way to state the intended benefits from the program?

choices.text: This program will help us exploit synergies with other assembly lines and lead to efficient operation
The program will help increase the inventory turnover
This program will help us make an entry into the mid-market segment which is growing at a quicker rate
This program will help increase the ratio of parts made in-house to the parts sourced from outside

explanation: The business case must be presented in a language that the business understands. The statements in B, C and D have merit, but they are not supported by the information provided in the question

text: An e-governance program was launched by a local municipal body. Many of the transactions and applications needed by the citizens will be made available online and not require a visit to the office. Most of the components of the program are dependent upon the digitization of land records and maps that are required to process all the applications. The mayor had made a public commitment that the system will be inaugurated on Independence day. A week from the inauguration, the digitization process is only 40% complete and there is no hope of achieving 100% coverage. There are far too many inaccuracies in the data available and ground surveys are necessary, which are time consuming. What can the program manager do?

choices.text: Raise a change request to deploy 500 emergency staff to complete the digitization work on a war footing so that the inauguration can proceed
Find a way to launch the program with a limited scope in the beginning and expand it as the more reliable data becomes available
Call for a program steering committee meeting and let the project manager in-charge of digitization explain the issues
Inform the mayor that the inauguration will have to be delayed as much of the backed work is delayed due to factors beyond the program’s control

explanation: It is unlikely that the executive sponsor of the program (the mayor) will take kindly to the delay, which makes Option A unattractive. Option B shifts all the responsibility to the project manager and offers no solution. Option C offers a solution, but it is questionable if it will be enough (are 500 people required – or is it 50 or 5000; how quickly can these people be trained; how confident is the program about the quality, etc.). Option D is the most practical approach. It offers a way to go ahead with the launch, but recognizes the issues and the need to adopt a phased approach to resolving the issues.

text: An equipment vendor for the thermal power sector is worried about the stagnation of its existing markets and resultant slowing down of growth. At a recent portfolio meeting, the program and portfolio managers reviewed various business ideas. Which one of the following business cases should they be most interested in?

choices.text: A proposal for getting into adjacent market spaces – such as nuclear power
A proposal to acquire another company in the same market space
A proposal to save operational costs to preserve margins
A proposal to invest in brand building to improve market share

explanation: The core issue as stated in the question is the stagnation of the existing markets (i.e. equipment supplies for thermal power). Only option B provides a long term solution for the issue.

text: A program is funded using a combination of debt and own funds in equal proportion and the overall cost of capital is 15%. The return on equity for the organization is 18%. Which of the following statements suggests that the program should not go ahead?

choices.text: The RoI for the program is 21%
The IRR for the program is 15%
The Net Present Value for the program is $300,000
The benefits/cost ratio is 1.5:1

explanation: The program should deliver returns at a rate higher than the cost of capital. The program is funded by a combination of debt and own equity, which implies the average cost of capital to be 15.5%. The IRR of 15% does not cover for this.

text: A program manager is putting together the overall program schedule and is awaiting information from one of the projects. The project manager claims it is hard to put a time line against any of her project’s deliverables because it requires a lot of research before confirming the approach. What is the best way to move forward?

choices.text: The program manager should put the onus on the project manager to provide a schedule for her project and set a deadline for finalizing it
The program manager should move forward with the overall program schedule making suitable assumptions about the project’s deliverables
The program manager should advise the project manager to make use of past data and expert judgment to arrive at a “best guess” schedule and revise as more information becomes available
The program manager should hold off on communicating the program schedule until more information about the project becomes available

explanation: It is not unusual that there is large uncertainty about the time estimates. The program manager should make use of the best information that is available and refine the program as things progress. Another reason why B is the best answer is that it emphasizes making use of past data and expert judgment – both are very important in the estimation process as it shows a mature organization learning from past experiences.

text: An influential stakeholder in a program is particularly interested in a specific project. In spite of sending him the reports about the program and the project as laid down in the communication plans, he keeps on calling the program manager asking for in-depth technical details. What should be done?

choices.text: Ask the project manager to set up a weekly technical de-brief with the stakeholder
Amend the project communication plan to address the communication needs of the stakeholder
Amend the program communication plan to add the details being requested by the stakeholder
Ignore the calls and stick to the communication protocol agreed with the stakeholders

explanation: The stakeholder seems to be inquisitive about technical details on a particular project, hence the communication plan of that project may need to be amended. Statement C (weekly call for technical de-brief) may be just one way of doing it, but the project and program managers must find ways to satisfy the communication needs of the stakeholder and keep him engaged.

text: A software development program has reached the final phase gate review just before sign-off and transition. The projects have delivered the components of the main system. The integration tests have been carried out and have been signed off by the quality manager. The results of the limited customer release have been reviewed and the lessons incorporated in the final deliverable. Unexpectedly, the program steering committee refused permission to transition the system. What could be the MOST likely reason for this?

choices.text: The project managers may not have submitted their final closure reports
The operations teams may not have been enabled to accept the system being transitioned
The program manager may have been unable to clearly articulate the value proposition of the system
The risk level on the program may have become unacceptable to the organization

explanation: It seems that most of the work has been completed and the system is ready. What is most likely to have been missing is the level of enablement given to the operations team, which will need to support the system.

text: A large, multi-year program that has been sanctioned a budget of $5,000,000 to build up its infrastructure, including tools, machinery and IT systems for better management. The program manager polled the projects to collect all their tools, machinery and IT systems requirements and it summed up to only to $3,500,000. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Ask all the project managers to buy twice the quantities they need so that they could be better prepared for the future
Discuss with the relevant stakeholders options to utilize the funds available for the long term benefit of the program
Ask the program steering committee for permission to utilize the excess sum for other purposes, such as travel and other operating expenditure
Return the excess sum back to the organization

explanation: Before returning the money or diverting it for operating expenses, the program manager must try his best to use the funds for the allocated purpose – i.e. for building long term infrastructure. Apart from project specific needs, the long term needs of the overall program should be considered. Blindly increasing each project’s allocation may not result in the best utilization.

text: While working on a program to deliver a large number of chipsets for a cell phone manufacturer, a designer in one of the projects came up with an innovative technique to protect the chips from adverse impact of static electricity during the manufacturing process. The program manager was very impressed by this innovation as it would potentially benefit other programs and organizations too. What is the most important thing for the program manager to do?

choices.text: Ask the designer to dpcument the invention and consult with experts about how it can be harnessed
Ask the project manager to reward the designer for her innovation
Send the designer to an international conference on electronics where this can be presented
Ask the designer to write a business case for a new program to monetize this opportunity

explanation: There seems to be potential for generating and monetizing intellectual property for the organization. So the program manager should try and evaluate if they can unlock this value for the organization.

text: An automobile company is running a program for development and manufacture of its best-selling hatchback model. There are 4 integrated manufacturing plants across the country and a central research and development center where new developments take place. One day the paint shop at the largest factory burnt down. An emergency sub-program was put in place to reconstruct the paint shop, while minimizing the disruption to operations. Which of the following options will be LEAST helpful the program manager to minimize disruption to operations?

choices.text: Shift most of the production from the impacted factory to other factories
Use the amount recovered from the insurance claims to fast track the construction of a new paint shop
Look for other paint shops in the city who might have spare capacity
Expand the capacity of the paint shops in other factories to pick up the slack

explanation: Options A, B and C provide some alternatives to restore operations quickly. D is a relatively longer term solution.

text: A program manager and the managers of the projects that are part of the program are working on defining the scope for the program and the constituent projects. They came up with the following sections. (I) Expectations from the program (II) Business impact (III) Description of projects and resources in each component (IV) Limitations and exclusions. Which of the above would be appropriate to include in the Program management plan?

choices.text: I and II
I, II, II, IV
I, III and IV
III and IV

explanation: All of these are part of the program management plan statement.

text: A service improvement program is being implemented in the repairs and maintenance division of a company manufacturing high-end printers. The program manager noticed that in the past year, the cost of the repair and maintenance operation was well below budgeted levels, but there were instances where the clients would report a delay in completing the repairs beyond the service level agreements that were signed. Once the repairs were done, there was rarely any recurrence of the complaint. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this?

choices.text: The repair staff lacked the skills necessary
The spares used were of poor quality
The repair staff tried too hard to fix the problem with the printer rather than take short cuts like replacing the faulty parts
The transition of knowledge from the projects to operations was not thorough

explanation: Statements A, B and D can explain why the repairs were delayed, but do not explain the fact that once done, the repairs were effective and did not lead to further issues. So they do not adequately explain the scenario. Statement C indicates that the repair staff tried to fix the devices rather than rip and replace parts, which not only explains why it took longer in some cases, but also that the cost of maintenance is lower and that once the repairs were implemented, the problems rarely recurred.

text: A program manager is setting the annual performance objectives for the project managers working on a large, multi-location program. Which of the following set of objectives make most sense? (A) – Deliver the projects on scope, cost and time and with good quality; (B) – Align with the strategy of the organization; (C) – Effectively monitor and track the delivery of benefits on the program; (D) – Establish a clear escalation path from the project to program level

choices.text: B
A
C
D

explanation: B, C and D are good objectives for the program manager, but for the project manager, the primary success criteria should be to deliver their projects with good performance on the Scope, Time, Cost and Quality parameters.

text: Customer satisfaction ratings for a product line had gone down. In order to review the reasons behind this, an operations review was called by the program manager. The program manager was particularly concerned about the blame game being played between the product and support teams. When a customer complaint could not be resolved by support/operations, it got escalated to the product teams, who did the higher level diagnosis and issued solutions as needed. It was found that the product teams typically took a long time to respond. Upon closer investigation, they revealed that the information they needed to diagnose a problem was not provided to them by the support teams. Which of the following measures might address this issue most effectively?

choices.text: Establish a staff rotation program between product and support teams to help them appreciate each other’s needs and result in service improvements
Set up performance objectives for the product teams based on the turnaround time for the escalated complaints
Let the product team manager and the operations manager work out a solution
Set up performance objectives for the support teams based on the amount of information they provide to the product teams

explanation: The issue in question is inadequate communication between the teams in response to customer complaints and thinking in silos. The measure that will best address this is staff rotation, which will not only result in cross training, but also a better appreciation of what information is needed against what is available and how to best provide it.

text: A program had 5 projects, which use 3 point estimates to better understand the variability in the likely time lines. The standard deviations of the duration are 4, 6, 7, 2 and 8 months respectively. Assuming that all the projects operate serially and that any delay would cascade and be passed down the chain, what would be the standard deviation of the program duration?
explanation: The variances (square of the standard deviations) are added up and the square root of the sum is the standard deviation for the program

text: Three projects from a program are heavily dependent upon a supplier for providing staff augmentation services. You have learnt that the supplier has agreed to be bought over by a competitor of your company. How should the program manager respond?

choices.text: Ask the project managers to come up with a succession plan to replace the contracted staff
Get into discussions with the supplier along with the Contracts department to explore options
Make job offers to the contracted staff, offering handsome salary increases
Inform the executive sponsor about the potential implication of this change

explanation: This is an issue which affects multiple projects, so it makes sense to come up with a program level, institutionalized response. The best way is to discuss with the supplier to explore options before going back to the sponsor or deciding to make job offers. Perhaps there may be a way forward within the existing contracts.

text: A program operates in an extremely dynamic business environment and requirements change frequently. It is also difficult to obtain a lot of detail about the requirements as many of them cannot be verbalized easily by the end users. What is the best option to plan the program benefits delivery phase?

choices.text: Organize requirements workshops and use multiple techniques to get as much detail as possible up-front and minimize change
Try to establish notional charging for changes to create disincentives for introducing too much change during the benefits delivery phase
Identify which projects are most likely to be impacted by the changes and staff it with the best engineers so that they can better respond to them
Adopt an incremental and iterative life-cycle so that projects can gather frequent feedback and adjust quickly to the changes

explanation: Option-A won’t be very helpful because no matter how creative you get with requirements gathering, changes will continue to happen (as the root cause of change is dynamic business environment and difficulty to verbalize requirements). B is not a good idea as it would create resentment among users – the idea should not be to resist change but to adjust to change. The amount of change may not necessarily be the best way to assign team members (option-C). D is the best option - to reduce the cost to make changes.

text: A government agency in an Asian country is working on a watershed development program in a remote hilly region which is often plagued by water shortages despite getting substantial rainfall during the tropical monsoon season. The program is likely to get funded by an internationally funded development institution which finances development projets in Asia. Which of the following measures might best help convince the bank to fund this program?

choices.text: Number of people benefited and nature and type of farming opportunities generated
Detailed cost-benefit analysis over a period of 10 years
Million cubic feet of water saved through the program
Number of malnourished children in the region

explanation: For programs in the social sector funded by development banks, the core consideration is the social benefit. They may not be interested necessarily in the detailed cost-benefit analysis as profit is not the core motive. C and D are somewhat relevant statistics, but do not really explain the impact that the program is likely to have on the situation.

text: A large program being managed as part of an outsourced contract is being transitioned from Company A to Company B. The plan is to have 6 months of overlap to let Company B acquire the knowledge and expertise and achieve 2 milestones while Company A is still around. Company A is bitter about the transition and is making the hand-over and knowledge transfer process tough for Company B. While working on one of the projects during the transition phase, there was a serious conflict between the team members from Company A and Company B leading to a complete impasse. Which of the following measures should be considered by the Program manager to unblock work?

choices.text: Remove the work from the scope for the immediate milestone and address it after the conflict has cooled down
Consider sub-contracting the work so that the team dynamics do not impact the work
Issue a deadline for the delivery and let the respective project managers resolve the issue
Provide additional funds for co-locating team members from the two companies for a short period until the work gets completed

explanation: This is essentially a conflict resolution question. The best way to move forward is to have a collaborating/problem solving approach, for which co-location may create the most conducive environment.

text: A machine and fabrication company specializes in making specialized mixing equipment. The company won an order from a pharmaceutical company. A program was initiated, overseeing different projects that manage the work in different areas, like the fabrication unit, electric components like motors, instrumentation and process control, piping and valves, etc. Each of these units have well defined process for guaranteeing quality. During the program delivery phase, the customer sent a request to perform a mandatory audit of the processes. The project managers are resisting this as they see it as an additional overhead. How should the program manager respond?

choices.text: Inform the customer that there are already well defined quality processes in place and that the customer need not micro-manage quality
Counsel the project managers about the necessity of audits and get them some coaching about techniques of facing a pharmaceutical audit
Review the adequacy of the project’s quality processes and techniques before making a decision to allow or disallow the customer audit
Instead of allowing the customer audit, set up an internal component to monitor the processes and agree to send the reports to the customer

explanation: Customers, especially in safety conscious domains will often want to audit the quality processes. Further, this order is significant in terms of value and complexity which is acknowledged by the performing organization. Hence rather than resisting the audit or trying to provide workarounds, the audit should be allowed and in fact the team should be coached on facing the audit and learning from it.

text: A program consists of about 15 projects. The projects deliver specific deliverables which need to be integrated to deliver the business benefits. The projects are well managed and seem to deliver on time and as per the specifications. However, the integration phase is usually challenging. Each project seems to complain about other projects making changes to the plans and the technical specifications without consulting others. Which of the following measures can best address this issue?

choices.text: Take the project managers to an offsite team building event to enhance their ability to effectively communicate with each other
Establish yourself as the authority to manage changes on the projects and sit on the change approval board of the projects until the situation stabilizes
Create an interface management plan and call for a weekly integration meeting to discuss the interfaces and all the changes that might impact the interfaces
Ask the Program Management Office for tools, templates and guidance on integration testing that can be shared with the project managers and their teams

explanation: The main challenge is that projects are making changes without considering the impact on the others. This can best be addressed by clearly defining the interface and then monitoring any alterations to the agreed upon interfaces. The other options tackle the peripheral issues but don’t solve the core issue. Option-B may improve team spirit, but may not directly impact the change management process. Option-C will make the change management process slower and more bureaucratic. Option-D is talking about a reactive approach (integration testing) where a more proactive approach is required.

text: During a recent operational review, the program manager observed that 40% of the service requests received by the service department could be prevented if the end users were educated about self-service procedures. This would have resulted in significant savings in the service costs. What is the best course of action for the Program manager to take advantage of this insight?

choices.text: Ask the Service department not to entertain customer requests which can be resolved through self service
Initiate a new project to build an awareness and education campaign around the self service procedures
Make use of social media to propagate the self service option among the customers
Initiate a change request to add a self service section to the company website

explanation: Options A, B and D are all about education of the end users, which is the right way to go. A is a more complete answer because it calls for initiating a component with a specific mandate and does not get into too much detail. C is not a good answer because refusing a requested service will make the customers unhappy.

text: A program manager was away in an offsite meeting when a major product launch was supposed to happen. The concerned project managers had been working very hard to make the launch successful. On the day of the launch, the program manager received a voice mail from a senior representative of the customer who said she had serious concerns about the way the launch was being handled and that they were deferring the launch indefinitely. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Call the project managers and ask them to get in touch with the customer instantly to find out and alleviate her concerns
Inform the Program Sponsor and request him to get in touch with the customer
Call the customer immediately and have a discussion about her concerns
Send a text message informing about your whereabouts and acknowledging the concerns and promise to look into the matter as soon as you get back

explanation: The mode and nature of the response has to be customized per the urgency of the situation. Here, the customer is distraught enough that they are delaying a major product launch. This is not the time to delegate the response upward (Sponsor) or downward (project manager). The program manager should personally intervene in a manner that at least conveys to the customer that he is aware of the seriousness of the matter.

text: A disaster relief program has been commissioned to deal with the after effects of a massive flood in a remote, mountainous region. Budget was allocated from the Prime Minister’s Relief fund. The program manager who is onsite notices that the weather is turning cold and there is urgent need for winter gear for relief workers and the survivors. This was not part of the original plan and due to the remoteness of the region, supplies have to be airlifted from other regions, which will further add to the cost. How should the program manager deal with the situation?

choices.text: Immediately place order for supplies from the nearest depot
Look for alternative clothing options that are based on locally available material
Put in a change request and add it to the agenda of the next emergency board meeting scheduled in 48 hours
Take a telephonic approval from the executive sponsor and look for sources that can fulfill the order the fastest

explanation: It is an emergency situation and every hour is crucial. Therefore, waiting for the next meeting is not the right option. The locally available resources would already be depleted given the calamity and it is not right to waste time looking for them. Even in this situation, the program manager should follow basic protocol of taking an approval and try to fulfill the requirement in the shortest time possible –hence C is the best choice.

text: A software company releases product suite for the large enterprises that consists of 10 products. The release of all the products in the suite needs to be coordinated and there are a number of interfaces and integrations between the products. The suite is managed as a program, and project managers manage individual product releases. The issue for the past several releases has been that there is strong product loyalty and comparatively little attention paid to the interfaces and integrations\ Which of the following measures can best increase awareness about the importance of integrations?

choices.text: Raise the visibility of the issue to the team in a town-hall type meeting and explain to them how important it is to work on integrations
Re-organize the program’s staff along functional rather than product lines to reduce the product loyalty
Introduce an additional testing phase that is totally dedicated to testing and validating the interfaces and integrations
Organize program wide learning initiatives to sensitize the team members about customer usage scenarios and how the poor integrations impact customers

explanation: The first thing to try would be to make the teams aware that the integrations are important to customers. Re-organizing along functional lines seems a drastic step, which may even impact product quality. Similarly, testing the integrations cannot improve the quality – it is too late in the life cycle and costly to recover from errors. Awareness can be better enhanced by exposing the team to actual customer usage scenarios than an exhortation from senior management which may not have a similar impact.

text: Projects A and B are part of a larger program. Project A was delayed due to an identified project level risk, and there is a cascading effect of the delay on Project B and the overall program. The delay will cause a monetary loss of $50,000 to Project A. How should this loss be budgeted?

choices.text: It should be funded by management reserves of project A and if this is not enough, the organization should bear the losses through an emergency grant
It should be funded through the contingency reserves of project A and if this is not enough, the program reserves should be used
It should be funded through the program level management reserves
It should be funded through the program contingency reserves as the risk was already identified by project A and known

explanation: The delay in project A was due to a known risk, so it should have been at least partly provided for in the project’s contingency reserves. If those reserves are not enough, the program should fund the rest. Since it is a project level risk, the program’s contingency reserves should not be the first resort (option B). Management reserves are meant to be used in the event of unknown unknowns (unidentified risk events) happening and hence C and D are not correct.

text: After the launch of the first version of a product, it was found the product is not really being taken up by the medical fraternity which was the target audience. On closer investigation, it was discovered that the Sales staff were not able to clearly articulate the value to doctors. What could be the best way to address this and promote Sales?

choices.text: Increase the commission rates and introduce penalties for not meeting quotas for the Sales staff
Offer a free trial period so that they can test the product without worrying about the costs
Offer promotions and incentives to doctors who will in turn help promote the product to others
Recruit Sales people from pharmaceutical companies, who are well trained at selling to doctors

explanation: The issue is that the sales people were not equipped to explain value to the doctors. B is not correct; because there is no evidence in the question that price is a concern. C might work, but then again the evidence provided suggests doctors haven’t even fully understood the value themselves. D is also not right because there is no information that this is a Sales commission issue.

text: At a recent program level review, it was felt that many quality issues were due to inadequate or inaccurate understanding of the requirements. This was especially true of those projects where the project teams were located geographically in a different time zone from the business users. Which of the following measures might be most helpful in this situation?

choices.text: Raise a change request to bring the project teams closer to the business users by adopting a near-shoring strategy
Appoint site coordinators at the project and user sites to act as single points of contact for communication between the project and user groups
Provide for an increased travel budget to have more face-to-face time between the business users and the project teams
Ask the project managers to pay special attention to quality and revise their performance objectives accordingly

explanation: The root cause of the issues is lack of or low band-width of the communication. Travel and face time can help this. Co-locating the business and project teams will also address this but seems to be an extreme measure – the feasibility of which may be questionable. C is not applicable, as limiting the communication channels is likely to further worsen the problem. Option D is putting the onus on the project managers without providing any help to resolve the issues.

text: A company engaged in business process outsourcing for banks and financial institutions recently had a data integrity issue reported in an audit. This is a very serious issue as the company handles all the customer data for its clients. The company took the breach seriously and has launched a program to look at all aspects of security and implement water-tight measures. The program manager is trying to put in place benefit measures for the program. Which of the following may be relevant measures that indicate the business benefits for the organization? (I) Number of security incidents thwarted (II) Number of review meetings of the security committee (III) Demonstrated compliance with industry standards (IV) Customer retention rate

choices.text: I, II, III and IV
I, II and IV
I, III and IV
I and III

explanation: The ideal measures would be those that directly correlate to the business benefit (as it is specifically asked in the question). Number of possible security threats prevented by the system is definitely a success measure as it protects the core business. Compliance with industry standards helps the company reassure its customers about the measures that are in place, so it is also relevant. Review meetings of the security committee may be a measure of the efforts being put in, but does not directly indicate any business benefit. Customer retention is influenced not just by security (which is just a hygiene factor) but primarily by the quality of services delivered.

text: An organization is working on a program to upgrade its brand image as a quality conscious and reliable supplier of services to its customers. Processes to focus on prevention rather than damage control are critical. The program manager has a goal to achieve a 30% savings in maintenance cost through quality improvements. Which of the following is the BEST goal to cascade to the project managers to align them towards this goal?

choices.text: Increase in number of defects detected within the projects before they reach the customer
30% increase in the customer satisfaction ratings
Reduction in deviations from the regulatory standards
Reduction in number of customer reported defects and recalls

explanation: The quality objective reflected in the program manager’s goals targets reduction in maintenance costs. This can only be achieved if the customers have fewer quality related issues and therefore less recalls. The other goals might be indicative, but they do not directly align as well as option A does.

text: An organization is experience high rates of personnel attrition and lack of career growth opportunities is cited as a common reason for leaving. A program in the organization comprises of 10 projects. 2 of the project managers, who were looking at a critical component, have resigned. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Try her best to retain the project managers by making compelling counter-offers
Advertise the 2 vacant project manager positions internally and externally and give preference to internal candidates if other factors are equivalent
Provide an opportunity to the remaining 8 project managers to manage additional components, thereby helping them grow in their careers
Highlight the increased risk level of the program to the program steering committee

explanation: In the crisis there may always be opportunity. While the project managers leaving may not be a positive occurrence, it provides the program manager a chance to address the career growth opportunity issue squarely. In so doing, the program manager demonstrates awareness of the environmental factors and tries to deal with the situation in a positive frame of mind.

text: Customer satisfaction ratings for a product line had gone down. In order to review the reasons behind this, an operations review was called by the program manager. Along with the dip in operational and support statistics, the program manager is concerned that the product releases have also been routinely delayed. The project managers complained that the delays were caused due to diversion of product teams for support activity, which was completely ad-hoc. What is the best way to ensure a predictable schedule was maintained for new product releases in this environment?

choices.text: Use data about the past few months to predict the amount of diversion for work on customer complaints and ask the project managers to incorporate this in the product release project plans
Set an upper limit to the number of complaints that can be escalated to product teams
Provide incentives for the product teams for timely completion and penalties for late completion of product releases
Defer all new product releases until the current customer complaints are resolved satisfactorily

explanation: This is where the program manager must encourage use of historical data to be able to come up with predictable plans. Setting an arbitrary limit may be counter-productive as some of the escalations may be necessary. Incentives and penalties do not really address the issue of diversion of effort. Also, deferring new product development may not be a good idea as it will stop new innovative features from coming to market – resulting in a loss of competitive advantage

text: A company offers project management services for the construction industry. A recently appointed senior project manager is recommending that the company should adopt a program management approach while working on customer projects. Which of the following statements would best convince the business leaders about the justification for this change?

choices.text: It would lead to operational efficiencies through better utilization of shared resources
It would lead to sharing of best practices among projects
It would lead to better alignment of the projects with the strategic objectives of the company
It would lead to a more streamlined management of dependencies

explanation: All of the reasons (A-D) are valid, but A, B and D are not expressed in the language that the business leaders will understand. C expresses the benefit in terms of the business, i.e. operational efficiency and hence is more likely to be accepted by the business leaders.

text: A program manager is trying to come up with a balanced scorecard to track and report on the benefits accruing from the program. She has identified 3 metrics so far: Operating margins (target at least 30%); Reduction in time taken from concept to deployment (target is less than 3 months); Customer satisfaction index (target at least 90%). Which of the following best supplements this set of metrics on the balanced scorecard?

choices.text: Operational efficiency improvements
Number of patents generated
Net operating cash flow generated
Reduction in warranty costs

explanation: The balanced scorecard comprises of metrics in 4 different areas: Customer; Financial; Internal/Process and Learning & Innovation. The first 3 areas are covered in the metrics that the program manager has already identified. That leaves learning and innovation. Only option D represents a metric that addresses this area.

text: A car manufacturer known for luxury and SUV models has decided to diversity into the economic, fuel efficient and small car segment. A program has been launched to manage the various components related to design, supply chain and assembly line management, etc. in an integrated fashion. One of the issues that the program is facing early on is diversity of stakeholder expectations. The existing customer base would like the brand value to be protected by not compromising on features. The marketing team would like the new models to lead the market in terms of fuel efficiency. The project teams are concerned about the re-use of the existing parts to keep the inventory of spares manageable. What is the BEST way to balance the needs of all the stakeholders?

choices.text: Conduct a product, portfolio and market needs analysis to come up with various decision points and initiate discussions to arrive at decisions
A program manager is responsible to deliver program benefits, so decisions should that are best suited to make the new product line successful should be favored
As there is a serious risk of the existing brand value being devalued due to excessive focus on economy, decisions should not be taken without taking the entire Sales organization into confidence
Take the diverse opinions to the program steering committee and ask them to make a decision in a timely manner

explanation: The decision should be taken in the larger interest of the overall organization. All of the stakeholders may have valid inputs and those should be considered. There needs to be a balanced view taking into consideration the product requirements, the overall portfolio and the needs of the market. Option A best balances these view points.

text: A program manager works for a web based retailer. The objective of the program is to improve the user experience of the visitors to the web site by improving the look and feel of the site, simplifying navigation and providing high speed responses to customer searches and transactions. The site was launched a few months ago and is yet to break even and the teams are all working on a shoestring budget. During Father’s day weekend, traffic to the site surged, causing congestion. After studying the problem, the network administrator suggested the situation can be rectified if urgent network upgrades can be applied, costing $50,000. This amount is above the program’s contingency reserves. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Offer a special discount for users who were affected by congestion to compensate for the inconvenience
Raise a change request and schedule an in-person meeting of the program steering committee as quickly as possible
Put up a message on the web site suggesting that the users should call a help line to get their orders through if they were not able to go through the website
Get special approval and make the change as quickly as possible

explanation: This is an emergency situation and must be dealt with immediately. For a fledgling retail organization, user experience is paramount. The workaround provided in option C seems impractical (how can a help line handle the congestion better than a web site or offer equivalent experience) and option D is post-facto with doubtful effectiveness. In an operational scenario, the emphasis should be on restoring normal operations as soon as possible.

text: A mid-sized company is struggling to meet operating margin targets because revenue growth is not as strong as expected. It has been working on a program to reduce operational expenditure to shore up margins to the extent possible. All of a sudden, an announcement was made that the company is getting acquired by a larger company which is the market leader in the segment. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Continue as planned before until the future strategic direction is communicated
Initiate a project staffed with representatives from the acquiring organization so that the program’s offerings can be expanded to the larger, merged entity
Recommend to the program steering committee that the current program be closed
Trim the size of the program, closing the projects which no longer make sense and await future direction from the program steering committee

explanation: There is a sudden change in the business environment and the current goals of the program may no longer be valid. The program manager must try and bring the program to an orderly closure and then explore future strategic direction.

text: A program comprises of many components which are led by highly motivated and energetic managers. The program manager delegates most of the activities to these managers. Which of the following activities should the program manager probably pay most attention to?

choices.text: Project B is located in a highly secure zone with strict access controls as they are working on highly confidential data
Project C has a very successful method to document and pro-actively manage the interfaces and dependencies with other projects and external vendors
Project D is finding it difficult to hire a resource for a niche skill set
Project A has a unique ritual of a team lunch every Friday to improve team bonding

explanation: A program manager should best spend time on activities that impact multiple components and deliver larger benefits through coordinated management of components.

text: An experienced program manager is in-charge of setting up a program management office. Which of the following would be the LEAST appropriate statements to include in the charter of the PMO?

choices.text: To provide guidance and coaching for program managers
To provide industry leading program management expertise to the internal and external customers
To regularly review and revise the program management processes in the organization
To conduct timely interventions to prevent catastrophic program failure within the organization

explanation: The PMO is meant to be a center of excellence for program management within an organization. All the statements have good intentions, but D seems to convey the impression that the PMO will intervene actively in the programs. This should not be the intent as it would directly impede the authority and reduce the effectiveness of the program managers.

text: A program comprises of various projects working on development of telecommunications equipment which is later transitioned into operations which maintain them and support customers. There is constant tension between operations and projects. Operational teams complain that the project teams do not take ease of maintenance into consideration while developing the equipment whereas the project teams complain that the operations teams do not follow instructions written in the manuals. Which is the best way to resolve this impasse?

choices.text: Appoint a member of the operational teams on the committee that gives requirements for new equipment
Increase allocation for training the operations staff before the release of any new equipment
Call for a meeting of the project managers and ask them to provide highest priority to maintainability and supportability requirements
Institute a policy of rotating few team members between projects and operations

explanation: There are two core issues – supportability requirements not reflecting in product development and support teams not following user manuals. Both of them arise from inadequate appreciation of each other’s world. This is best addressed with option D. Options A and B address only one part – whereas C is leaving matters in the hands of project managers, where an institutionalized response may be more appropriate.

text: A program management office an executive dashboard every month for an organization containing a snapshot of the ongoing programs and operations. The PMO is faced with a challenge because they have to chase the program managers to provide the required information. Despite their best efforts, the information is not available and the accuracy of the available information is suspect. Which of the following measures is most likely to give the desired results?

choices.text: Send an empty dashboard for a month to expose the problem and pressurize the stakeholders to reach a resolution
Request the executives to appoint an executive sponsor and initiate a program specifically to prepare the executive dashboard
Align the content of the dashboard with the informational needs and expectations of the stakeholders
Reduce the frequency from monthly to quarterly so that there is less overhead and chances of cooperation will improve

explanation: The most likely cause of the lack of cooperation is that the informational needs of the different stakeholders (data providers and consumers) is not matching and this is what needs to be addressed before thinking about carrot and stick approaches.

text: An IT services company offers remote management of IT infrastructure and applications to its customers. One of the programs being managed for a particular client was in deep trouble, getting consistently poor customer satisfaction scores .Julie, an expert program manager was appointed by the PMO to investigate and suggest remedial action. On one of the services, Julie found that there were a large number of trouble tickets being generated, many of whom were repetitive in nature. The number of tickets way beyond the band-width of the team was equipped to handle. What can be done to find a long term solution to this?

choices.text: Initiate a component to automate the resolution of tickets so that the team could get some breathing space
Carve out a portion of the team to perform deeper causal analysis to find and try to eliminate root causes over and above dealing with the immediate symptoms
Educate the customers to bunch related tickets together rather than log separate tickets
Add resources to increase the band-width of the team

explanation: The team needs to invest time and effort in long term/preventive measures in addition to applying band-aid which clearly is not proving to be enough. Simply adding resources will not solve the problem – it will likely make it worse. It is not fair to expect the customers to correlate their problems before logging tickets and asking them to do so would further aggravate customer satisfaction. Automation may help resolve tickets faster, it is still only addressing the symptom, not the root cause.

text: A steel manufacturer has come under severe cost pressure due to rising cost of inputs and slack demand due to which the increases could not be passed on to customers. The Board of Directors have decided to initiate a major program to find opportunities to reduce costs by 20% at which level the company will be able to stay afloat until the situation improves (which is expected to take about 2 years). Which of the following measures is likely to be most beneficial?

choices.text: Order an energy audit of the entire factory and identify opportunities to reduce the net energy requirements
Start a project to manufacture cement from fly ash generated from the blast furnace
Conduct a survey among employees to see if they would be receptive to taking a pay cut in exchange for an assurance that no retrenchment would be done
Start an advertising campaign to clearly outline the unique differentiators of the company’s products so that they could justify charging a price premium

explanation: Option B does not address cost – it talks about advertising to increase possibility of charging premium price. Option C is also not reducing cost, it is more likely to increase the cost in the medium term until the plant can become operational. Option D is amounting to coercing the employees to take a pay cut and probably should be the last resort. Option A seems reasonable as it is looking at the energy consumption and how it can be reduced. This is most likely to drive costs down.

text: A successful company operating in the retail segment, which has been around for many years is losing market share as it is seen by the customers as a boring company, lacking in new ideas. It has launched a program to trigger innovation that will help it shed its staid brand image. Which of the following components would be LEAST effective in generating such ideas?

choices.text: A series of offsite, brainstorming meetings
Display videos recalling the glorious history of the company to inspire the employees
Engaging external consultants and advisors from the industry
An idea competition among employees with attractive prizes

explanation: A (Rewards), B (Lateral thinking) and C (External perspective) are all likely to bring in new ideas. D is appealing to nostalgia, which might be inspiring, but probably least likely to trigger new ideas.

text: A program manager is working on a global expansion initiative for a leading product line for a farm implements company. One of the most lucrative markets for this product line is a region, whose government is well known for high incidence of corruption. While planning the expansion program, what would be the best way for the program manager to take these factors into consideration?

choices.text: Establish extra safeguards and policies to ensure that all the program staff are aware and able to follow the compliance and ethics measures while working with the local government
Let the concerned project managers deal with the issues on the ground
Initiate a project within the program for government liaison and outsource it to a third party who are able to absorb these activities and costs
Advise the parent organization against planning an operation in this region

explanation: This is an ethical responsibility question. Even if the corruption may be happening in another country and even if the illegal payments are being routed through a third party, the parent organization and the program manager is still accountable. There is no way around establishing high standards of ethics and compliance and sticking to them, no matter how high the stakes.

text: A product line is deemed as non-strategic for an organization and is not getting much new investment. However it is earning sizeable revenues and has some very influential customers. One of the customers is demanding a new feature which is critical for their business. This feature requires changes to multiple components and requires a sizeable amount of funding. What is the best approach for the program manager to secure funding for this feature?

choices.text: Ask the customer if they will agree to pay for the feature since it is being developed only for them
Approach the program steering committee and inform that in order to retain this customer, this funding is essential
Ask the project managers if the work can be done by working overtime without additional funding needs
Ask other customers if they also want the feature and accordingly put up a business case in front of the program steering committee

explanation: This is a product being used by multiple customers. If a feature is being requested by only one, it may not be an unreasonable assumption that the customer may agree to pay for it – since it is effectively a customization. Going back to the program steering committee (options A and D) will indicate that the program manager is misaligned with strategy and will most likely back fire. Option B (working free of cost) is also not a good option as the quality of the results may not be good.

text: The CIO of a large banking and finance organization recommended to the Board that the IT organization of the bank should follow ISO 20000 (ITIL) practices. This will need a major re-structuring of the internal IT organization, introduction of new processes and tools and investment in hiring consulting expertise.
