The board has approved this recommendation but remains skeptical about the business value of this exercise. Which of the following would BEST help the program manager and the CIO (who is also the Program sponsor) keep the Board members engaged in the program?

choices.text: Send them regular updates about the processes put in place, tools implemented and how it has helped to streamline the operations of the Internal IT
Track and report on the percent of outsourcing used by the IT organization before and after the program was put in place
Track and report on benefits accrued to the business as a result of increased reliability, performance and security of IT operations
Invite the Board to a gala event every quarter where the achievements of the program are showcased

explanation: The reporting should focus should on the benefits to the business, because that is the issue that the business has some reservations. A gala event may be a good idea but it could be viewed as “gold plating” and unnecessary by some stakeholders.

text: A program has been initiated to build a large township consisting of residential and commercial complexes, schools, hospitals and other utilities in a remote town. As part of the development activity, the program has dug several wells to tap ground water from the aquifers that are present in the region. What is the best way to sustain the benefits from these assets after the program closes?

choices.text: The ownership should be transferred to the local council
The wells should be sealed and closed to prevent safety incidents
Roof water harvesting techniques can be used to recharge the aquifers and the wells transitioned to the agency maintaining the township
The developers can retain ownership of the wells to use for other construction activities in the future

explanation: There is an opportunity to transition the existing resources to pass on the benefits as the program transfers to ongoing operations. Therefore Option-4 makes most sense from benefits sustainment perspective.

text: A consumer goods company is contemplating adding tablet computers to its portfolio of products. Which of the following represents the best set of questions it must ask to establish feasibility before approving the charter for the program to launch this product line?

choices.text: The feasibility of the underlying technology, the acceptability in the target market, the risk level in the new product line
The availability of technical expertise, the financial viability of the proposal and the stakeholders involved in the decision
The availability of technical expertise, the acceptability in the target market, the financial viability of the proposal
The feasibility of the underlying technology, the acceptability in the target market, the financial viability of the proposal

explanation: The question is about establishing feasibility. Tablet computers are not new products, so there is no question about the technical feasibility. What needs to be established is whether the company has the available technical know-how within its resources or partner resources. The stakeholder involvement is a core question to ask during initiation, but it does not address the issue of feasibility. This leaves only Option-B with valid set of questions that point towards feasibility.

text: For an organization wide process improvement program, a program manager is identifying forum and mechanisms through which she can identify, establish contact and effectively communicate with the stakeholders. Which of the following is the BEST channel to do so?

choices.text: Attending the weekly business review meetings for all the functional heads where senior members of each function are present
An email from the chief executive announcing the program to everybody in the organization – directing stakeholders to contact the program manager for next steps
A town hall style meeting of the top managers in the organization where the leadership of the organization announces the program
Attending Quality circle meetings where almost all the functions are represented

explanation: The program is going to primarily affect the processes and it will likely touch all the functions. Announcements are good to kick start the communication but will not provide for high bandwidth or effective communication. Quality circle meetings are best suited because the people who attend those would be interested in the program and a healthy discussion can be started. Business review meetings have a different focus so stakeholders may not be really receptive to other programs in that forum.

text: A program has been initiated under a fixed price contract with a customer. There are multiple components that deliver different products and services to the customer according to the agreement. At a program review, multiple component managers have complained about the customer trying to micro-manage their components. Some examples provided are – customers insisting on selecting the people chosen to work on the components or making design decisions, etc. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Speak to the Program sponsor and board members about the need to limit the customer’s intervention in the program
Issue an invoice for the additional work generated as a result of the unwarranted interventions by the customer
Have a conversation with the customer to back off from off-contract intervention and only go through the program manager for any internal queries
Ask the component managers to ignore the requests from the customer which are not aligned with the contract

explanation: This is a diplomatic tight rope – talking to a customer who seems to be stepping over the line. The customer definitely needs to be confronted, but it is good to have the program steering committee and sponsor on your side prior to that.

text: A UN mandated re-construction program is being conducted in a remote country in Africa. Health centers are being run in each major location to help the personnel who are working on the program. It works out very well because medical facilities are otherwise far away and people working on the program often need assistance. One of the workers who fell sick was administered medication at the center. Unfortunately, the worker developed serious side effects and is now in critical condition. This has caused a rebellion in the work force, who have gone on strike. The program manager is meeting the leader of the worker’s union. What is the best thing for the program manager say?

choices.text: The program is committed to the health of its work force; it regrets the incident; we shall offer appropriate compensation and conduct a thorough investigation followed by appropriate action
The program regrets the incident, but the service was being offered as a goodwill gesture. The program will transfer the patient to a professional hospital of the patient’s choice
The medical facilities are being offered as a courtesy service and the program cannot assume responsibility about the quality of treatment; the protest is unfounded and should be withdrawn
The program regrets the incident and will shut down the errant facility immediately; in case of any health needs, the patient will be transported to the nearest professionally run medical center

explanation: It may be true that the medical facility is being run as a courtesy or goodwill gesture. However, the program manager needs to understand the social obligations towards the work force. Therefore, steps must be taken to restore confidence of the work force in the program’s commitment to their health and well being. Withdrawing the facility (option C) will not help matters, whereas option D is a bit presumptuous about what is the appropriate response to the tragedy. B is a more measured response that promises some immediate steps (compensation) and a long term plan of action and hence is the best choice under the circumstances

text: A program that was intended to save operational costs for a large manufacturing company seems to be doing well. Against a targeted 10% Y0Y improvement, the program is showing a 13.9% improvement for the past 2 years. However, a source of concern is that the expenses have also been running high at nearly 110% of the budget in the past 2 years. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Find out which components have been running high expenses and order a detailed cost audit by the Corporate PMO for those projects
Wait for guidance from the program steering committee
Ask the components to cut expenses by 10% to be in line with the budgets
Approach the program steering committee with a request to increase the budget

explanation: The program seems to be delivering the benefits in excess of the projection so the increase in expenses should not be a major concern. While expense control may be required, the program manager should not try to apply the squeeze on a program that seems to be working well.

text: A project, which is part of a large program. Two other projects are dependent upon the deliverables this project. The program level CPI is 1.2. Who should be responsible for taking the decision about which strategy to employ?

choices.text: A committee of project managers of the delayed and impacted projects
Project manager of the delayed project
The program manager
The executive sponsor

explanation: In this case the program seems to be running under cost and there seems to be available reserves to deploy. Hence the program manager is in a position to take the decision in the interest of the program.

text: As a program manager, you are trying to define the vision statement for your program. Which of the following is probably NOT a good vision statement?

choices.text: We want to improve our capabilities in mobile application development
We shall become the engine of growth for the organization
Our aim is to deliver a 20% savings in operational costs
We want to provide fulfilling careers to our team members

explanation: A, B and D all describe a certain goal and a desired end state, which is the purpose of a vision statement. C seems to be a value statement rather than a goal. It may be appropriate for a mission statement, not really for a vision.

text: While preparing a program management plan, the program manager is working on a governance structure that includes the creation of a program steering committee. On the program steering committee, the program sponsor is appointed the chair person. The program manager, the key customer and the chief of the technical staff are appointed. Who among the following should also be on the committee?

choices.text: The portfolio manager
The project managers
Representatives of the end users
Some team members on rotation basis

explanation: The portfolio manager is an important member of the program steering committee because the portfolio is clearly representative of an organization’s true intent.

text: A program has been put in place to perform mechanical and fabrication works to supply process engineering parts to a large factory using bio-technology to extract alcohol from agricultural waste. The program is running slightly over budget, and regularly uses the services of a specialized fabrication vendor to get some of the parts manufactured. Since the parts are standard in terms of dimensions and specifications, fixed rate cards are used to issue the purchase orders. Over the past one month, the cost of iron and steel has risen significantly and the program manager is worried that the supplier may also be under cost pressure, resulting in default or delay in fulfilling the purchase orders. What would help the program manager the most in dealing with this situation?

choices.text: Issue a letter to the supplier that the delivery is expected on time and any delay will not be tolerated
Introduction of strict penalty clauses in the contracts in case of lack of timely delivery
Ask the project managers to factor in the possibility of default or delay in their project plans and increase the contingency buffer
Maintaining a good working relation with the supplier and keeping regular communication about the progress and issues

explanation: If the supplier is a regular provider to the program, temporary cost pressure should not really impact the deliveries, provided there is a long standing and healthy relationship. It is important that a program manager maintains the relationship. If you look at all the other options, they either rely on policing or penalizing (C and A), or defensive measures (B), which may not even be feasible given the fact that the program itself is running over budget.

text: There are a number of initiatives in progress in the transport department of a council. From the mission statements of the initiatives provided, which of the following sounds like a program?

choices.text: We are creating parking spaces at multiple spaces in the city including railway stations and bus stands so that more commuters can avail of park and ride services and get end-to-end connectivity
We are working on a mass transportation improvement system for the city which will reduce traffic congestion, save fuel, improve productivity and provide a better life-style for the citizens
We are developing a monorail system covering tourist destinations of the city so that tourists can travel without getting stuck in traffic or spending time and money on the fickle taxi services
We are creating a new bus rapid transport system for the city through which we shall improve the carrying capacity speed of movement through traffic to provide the commuters a better experience

explanation: Option D focuses on the benefits and has a more strategic direction as compared to the others, which are more focused on specific deliverables. It is not that deliverables are not important or that they do not have any associated benefits, but as a program manager, understanding and ensuring alignment with the strategy is most important.

text: A diversified company recently announced a strategy of divesting non-core businesses and focusing on core competencies, which is in telecommunications. A program manager is working on a portfolio that develops and offers competencies in outsourced billing and payment management services for multiple industry verticals. At the latest planning session, a number of projects came up for review. Which of the projects should the program manager look to close in order to align with the strategy?

choices.text: A project to extend support for new electronic metering systems that are primarily used by the energy and utilities sector
A project to standardize and automate the data collection for billing to improve operational efficiencies
A project to improve the scalability of the existing process by adopting distributed computing methods
A project to introduce support for payment via a new mobile payment gateway

explanation: Since the organization has decided to focus on telecommunications industry, this project may not be aligned with the strategy as it is geared towards the energy and utilities sector.

text: A project, which is part of a large program is running late. Two other projects are dependent upon the deliverables this project. The program level CPI is 1.2. What is the most appropriate action given this information?

choices.text: Perform rolling wave planning, with near term milestones planned in greater detail
Explore if additional resources can be deployed to speed up the delayed project
Examine the critical chain in addition to the critical path for the delayed project and program
Perform more activities in parallel

explanation: On the basis of available information, the delays in the project (SPI < 1) may cause a cascading delay in others. Hence action is needed to bring the project back on schedule. Since the program seems to be running under budget (CPI > 1), there is scope for crashing the schedule.

text: A program has multiple projects which rely on a test lab that has very expensive, specialized equipment for stress testing. The program is running at a CPI of 0.8. Since the lab is shared across multiple projects, its availability has always been an issue. Due to this, there is a tendency among project managers to hoard the lab when they have possession of it rather than release it when their work is done. This is further aggravating the situation and the lab availability is becoming a pet excuse for explaining project delays. Which of the following is the best way to handle this situation?

choices.text: Initiate a short project to create a reservation system that will make the usage details transparent to the entire team
Establish rules and policies around the lab usage setting clear guidelines and enforce them by centralizing allocation through the PMO
Ask the program steering committee for additional funding to buy another set of equipment to relieve this bottleneck
Provide special incentives for project teams that release the equipment in a timely manner

explanation: The program is running high on costs, so asking for additional equipment may not be received very well. It is the program’s responsibility to manage and optimize the utilization of shared resources and the best way might be to create a transparent reservation system that will also track usage. This will make it clear that there is no incentive for hoarding as well as allow teams to view the availability and plan in advance.

text: An automobile company is running a program for development and manufacture of its best-selling hatchback model. There are 4 integrated manufacturing plants across the country and a central research and development center where new developments take place. One day the paint shop at the largest factory burnt down. An emergency sub-program was put in place to reconstruct the paint shop, while minimizing the disruption to operations. What are the MOST likely components the sub-program should have to start with?

choices.text: Evaluate loss of production and inform dealerships, Fast track reconstruction efforts, Investigate root cause of the incident
Evaluate loss and inform dealerships, Fast track reconstruction efforts, assess damage and pursue insurance claims
Identify alternatives for ongoing operations, Assess damage and pursue insurance claims, Fast track reconstruction of the paint factory
Investigate root cause of the incident, Assess damage and pursue insurance claim, Evaluate loss and inform dealerships

explanation: A is the only option which contains a component that looks at alternatives to minimize disruption to ongoing operations. When an ongoing operation is disrupted, highest priority has to be given to restore the operation as soon as possible.

text: A project which is part of a program is delayed by several months. The primary reason is the lack of team members with certain niche skills, which are not present in the organization. Which of the following is the BEST way for the program manager to help the project manager in this case?

choices.text: Assign team members from other projects
Offer to send team members to a training to quickly ramp up on this niche skill
Make allowances for the delays which are occurring due to reasons beyond the project manager’s control
Discuss with the recruitment and procurement teams to study options to ramp up staffing in this area

explanation: The core issue is availability of skills and hence the program manager should try and address this. If the skill is not available within the organization, it does not make sense to send team members from other teams (option A). Sending team members to training may help to some extent, but ramping up on a niche skill simply on the back of training will be difficult and slow. Making allowances for delays is a reactive step. Recruitment and procurement teams may need to be brought in - to discuss hiring and contracting options.

text: Which of the following is the LEAST important reason that a Program manager should be involved in Procurement decisions on the projects within the programs?

choices.text: To ensure that the procurement lead times are incorporated into the project schedules
To look out for opportunities to negotiate bulk discounts from suppliers who are serving multiple projects
To protect the interests of the program and build relationships with the suppliers
To make sure that the program level policies related to procurement are being followed

explanation: Statement C says including the procurement lead times on PROJECT schedules. The project schedule is the domain of the project managers. All other statements express valid reasons for the program manager to be involved.

text: A leading company is organized as follows. The R&D function is responsible for coming up with new product ideas and developing prototypes, Engineering function is responsible to design the product and set up the manufacturing process. Quality function is responsible to ensure that the processes and product is correct and meets expectations of current and future users. Manufacturing function takes over the operations once the Engineering is complete and Quality sign-off has been received. A highly strategic program is started in this company to come up with new products that rely on renewable energy sources. The board of directors has recommended setting up of a steering committee to govern the program and review the progress periodically. What would be good metrics to show to the board highlight the success of the program? (i) Number of new product ideas generated (ii) Reduction in the number of design flaws detected during manufacturing (iii) Reduction in warranty costs (iv) Revenue from the new product line

choices.text: iv only
ii, iii and iv
iii and iv
I, ii, iii and iv

explanation: For the steering committee, the success measure has to be correlated with business success. While i, ii and iii are also good metrics, they are perhaps more relevant to the internal program management function.

text: A program manager recently had to let go of 2 members of the Program office and is severely constrained for band-width. She is looking to limit the amount of oversight she provides and delegate as much as possible, while providing for effective governance at the same time. Which of the following activities is BEST suited to get delegated to the component level?

choices.text: A program level contingency reserve is maintained. There is a quarterly review to make sure that the reserve is adequate for covering all program and inter-component events
A component team located in France is conducting yearly wage negotiations with the local labor union as part of a routine process
The program has an inventory of machinery shared by multiple components. This needs to be maintained in good condition and the utilization and allocation should be prioritized and monitored
There is a monthly review at the Portfolio level of the delivery of intended benefits and escalated issues. The program manager currently represents the program at this meeting

explanation: From the information provided, it seems that the union meetings are routine and localized (restricted to one component). Hence this is the best task to delegate. Other tasks require program level oversight.

text: A medium sized construction contractor bid and won a major portion of the State highway improvement program that is expected to last 3 years. A program manager recently took charge of the program after it had been running for about 2 years. After reviewing the risk register for the program and the individual components, the program manager was shocked at the high level of risk involved. There were stiff penalties in the contracts, serious concerns about getting possession of the sites, potential labor issues in the state, etc. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: The program manager should write an email clearly outlining the performance baseline when he took over, so that he can avoid being blamed later
Inform the state highway authority about likely delays due to the delays on their part in handing over the construction sites
The program has already been in existence for 2 years and the contracts are already signed – so the program manager should do the best he can under the circumstances
The program manager should call for an emergency meeting of the program steering committee to apprise them of the risks and ask for their advice

explanation: If the risk threshold of the program exceeds the risk threshold of the organization, the program manager should alert the program steering committee. There is no point trying to put up with a difficult situation in hope (A) or trying to avoid blame (B). Picking a bone with the customer when the program is in already in trouble is also ill-advised.

text: At a program level status review, one of the project managers said that they have implemented fast-tracking on their projects, thus compressing the schedule. Although there are 2 months left on the schedule, they have almost completed the deliverables. As a program manager, how should you react to this information?

choices.text: Congratulate the project manager and ask her to share the best practices with the rest of the program and the organization
Ask the project manager for details about the management of risk-time trade-off, which is critical whenever fast tracking techniques are employed
You need to make sure that the component responsible for receiving the deliverables is enabled and ready
Inform the program steering committee about the possibility of early completion of the program

explanation: Early completion of components is not necessarily good news. Unless the receiving components or operations are ready, this may result in a pile-up of inventory and add to costs. Therefore as a program manager your first reaction should be to check for the impact on the other components.

text: An automobile company is working on a program to improve the design of the engine for its electric cars. Even a 5% gain in efficiency translates into a big competitive advantage in a promising market. A design competition was held internally and 22 ideas were received, which were vetted by engineers as valid ideas. The next test would be to produce a test version and validate the output before finalizing on the design. To fabricate and test an engine and test it costs approximately $500,000 and takes nearly 3 months. What should the program manager do with the ideas?

choices.text: Set up a sub-program or a set of projects to evaluate all the ideas and report back on the findings as quickly as possible
Discuss with the program team to prune the list of ideas further to about 5 in order to limit the cost and duration of testing.
Use the Delphi technique to arrive at the best among the chosen blueprints and test only the best one
Pick any one idea and apply Kaizen techniques to refine it further

explanation: The business benefit of the program is the competitive differentiation from the efficiency gains. If there are so many ideas that the design competition has produced, it makes sense to evaluate all of them (especially since initial vetting has already been done). A program manager should not get hung up about the cost and time factors and focus on the benefits.

text: An organization is embarking on a large and ambitious program. The program manager has just been appointed and the business case is being worked out. The program manager has assembled a core team of project managers who will later on manage specific components. During the initiation activities, one of the project managers’ points out certain technical risks associated with a component might have a significant impact on the achievement of the objectives of the program. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Go to the program steering committee asking for advice on how to deal with the risk and whether the marketing requirement is a “must have” deliverable for the program
Advice the project manager to create a risk register and note the risk, which can later be utilized during component level project planning
Tell the project manager that the identification and analysis of risks will be done during planning stage, after the program and specific project is approved by the program steering committee
Include the risk in the program evaluation and creation of the business case

explanation: The identification of initial set of risks is very much a part of the program initiation process and should be considered during the creation of the business case (Sec w8.3.1.4).

text: A bank has undertaken a business service restructuring program to streamline and automate operations. Many staff members in the bank oppose this program out of fear that the program will end up eliminating their jobs. Despite the best efforts of the program team, some members of the staff remain steadfastly opposed to the program and their non-cooperation is impacting the progress. Who is responsible for solving this problem?

choices.text: The concerned component managers
The functional manager
The program steering committee
The program manager

explanation: If the program manager and the program team have tried their best, the only alternative for them is to escalate and the first point of escalation should be to the program steering committee including the program sponsor.

text: A business process outsourcing company is working for a Federal Government process and it applies program management techniques to maintain and enhance its service for the process. Although the profits from the program are minuscule, the company feels it is important to continue because having the Federal Government as a customer gives them a lot of credibility. What should the program manager do about this from the benefits management perspective?

choices.text: At the next rate negotiation, try to charge a higher billing rate to improve the revenues
Initiate a marketing campaign to take advantage of the “supplier to the government” status
Initiate a cost reduction project to improve margins and enhance the benefits
Make strategic investments to improve the service so that the company can get more business from the government

explanation: The core benefit highlighted in the scenario is the credibility of being a government supplier. Option B enhances this benefit to the hilt. The other options are also interesting, but not correlated to this benefit. For instance, there is nothing in the scenario to suggest that the company wants to increase the business it wants to do with the government (option D) or that it is trying to improve margins (A and C).

text: An automobile interior design company won a contract to design the interiors for luxury buses for a private operator. 4 different designs are to be created and about 100 numbers of each would be eventually completed with fittings and fixtures and delivered over a period of 2 years. There might be changes due to feedback received from operations. Given the complexity and diversity of this assignment, a program was initiated comprising of different projects that create sub-assemblies. The integration is done by a different component. The program manager finds that there are issues during the assembly. Which of the following measures will address this issue?

choices.text: Send the team members of all the teams for a training on testing best practices
Ask the components to independently test the sub-assemblies before they are shipped to the assembly unit
Create steep penalties for components that fail during assembly so that teams would be more careful before sending to the assembly unit
Create cut-outs of the design blue-prints, complete will all the diagrams and measurements and put them on the shop floors

explanation: The testing has to be done before the process because prevention is better than cure. Levying penalties (D) does not help much. A and B help in creating awareness but at a very generic level. C seems to address the core of the issue, which is the testing at the assembly level – not really at the individual component level

text: A company engaged in business process outsourcing for banks and financial institutions recently had a data integrity issue reported in an audit. This is a very serious issue as the company handles all the customer data for its clients. The company took the breach seriously and has launched a program to look at all aspects of security and implement water-tight measures. Which components should the program manager look at, while defining the scope for the program? (I) Physical security of the premises (II) Access controls for the data (III) Reference checks for the candidates being recruited

choices.text: I, II and III
I and II
I and III
II only

explanation: All these aspects are relevant to security. Physical security of the premises is important. Access controls for the data need to be present to prevent unauthorized access. Similarly reference checks may be required to ensure that undesirable elements do not get into the system

text: During the definition phase, the program manager is trying to assess the infrastructure needs for the program. While determining infrastructure needs, the program manager needs to consider all of the following, EXCEPT?

choices.text: The program steering committee
Core team members including the project managers
Involvement of the Program Management Office
An ERP tool that will be used to log time and prepare cost reports

explanation: The program steering committee is part of the governance structure. All others are part of the infrastructure supporting the program.

text: A bank has undertaken a business service restructuring program to streamline and automate operations. Many staff members in the bank oppose this program out of fear that the program will end up eliminating their jobs. Which of the following is MOST likely to reassure them about the program’s intentions?

choices.text: If the bank implements this program, it will gain a competitive advantage, which might spin off new business offerings and brighter career prospects for employees
Improvement in the quality of operations will help the bank attract top talent
If the bank saves money, its profitability will increase and it will reflect in the value of the shares held by everybody including the employees
If the bank does not implement this program, it will lose competitive edge to other banks and this will hit the career prospects of all the employees

explanation: The scenarios given in all the options are valid. A talks about benefits to shareholders, which might benefit some employees to some extent, but does not address their bigger concern (longevity of their careers). D does not address the question “what’s in it for me”. B and C do talk about the impact on the employees, but C appeals to hope whereas B appeals to fear. Therefore C is the best option.

text: A program manager is trying to set up success measures to keep track of benefits being delivered. Which of the following is the most balanced set of measures?

choices.text: Customer satisfaction, Productivity, Operational cost, Number of product innovations
RoI, Time-to-market, Customer satisfaction, Operating margin
Time-to-market, RoI, Operational efficiency, Number of product innovations
Time-to-market, Productivity, Operational cost, Number of product innovations

explanation: To find out the most balanced set of measures, one must look for metrics related to customer, finance, process and innovation. B provides the most balanced set as Customer satisfaction represents a customer metric, productivity is a process metric, operational cost is a financial metric and number of innovations is an innovation related metric.

text: A program is about to transition to operations. During the closure stage, the program manager needs to determine the location for the operations support center. There are a number of options available and the program manager is wondering which would make most sense from a benefits sustenance perspective. Which of the following is the most appropriate set of factors to consider in making this decision?

choices.text: Proximity to customers, preference of the program manager, availability of skills
Availability of skills, cost of operation, proximity to customers only for Development and Test
Availability of skills, preference of the program manager, quality of output
Availability of skills only for development and test, cost of operation, proximity to customers

explanation: Availability of skills is critical for any activity. Cost of operation is also a valid factor. The proximity to customers is valuable for development and test, but not much of a consideration for customer support which is usually provided over the phone or the web. Preference of the program manager may also be important, but relatively less important. Given these factors, A seems the best answer.

text: Different projects on a program are in the planning stage. The program manager noticed that all of them used different techniques for effort and cost estimation. Some of them preferred to use bottom-up estimation techniques, others preferred to use top-down approaches. What should the program manager be most concerned about?

choices.text: The project level estimates should match with the expectations of the customer and senior management, otherwise the program manager would need to try and reconcile the differences
The estimates should be developed using bottom-up or detailed methods so that there can be a high level of confidence in them
The project level estimates should be cross verified through a process of peer review by other project managers so that the estimates can become more reliable
Try to standardize the techniques used so that the estimates can be more easily shared across the components and combined to come up with the program management plan

explanation: The diversity in the methods of estimation need not necessarily be a concern for the program manager. The projects are using the techniques that are most relevant to their situation. The thing that the program manager most needs to worry about is to try and match up the estimate with high level expectations. Peer reviews by other projects may not be very useful especially if the projects are of a diverse nature. It may not always be possible to come up with bottom-up estimates if all the details are not available.

text: Availability of sand for mixing into mortar is a critical success factor for a construction program. This problem is aggravated during monsoon season, when dredging activities are not possible. The program is at a CPI of 0.8 and is hard pressed for funds to service the debt it has incurred from the banks. Which project should a program manager favor in deciding about who should get the limited quantity available?

choices.text: Project A: Is a 3 year project whose start has already been delayed by six months
Project C: Is on the verge of completion and has customers waiting
Project D: Is a research project that is looking into use of fly ash instead of cement in construction
Project B: Is on the critical path, meaning that any delay will cause a delay in the final delivery date

explanation: The program is already over budget and has banks breathing down its neck. It needs to quickly finish some projects and start unlocking value. At this point, there is no point in worrying about projects that are delivering value far into the future. Investing in research is good, but the project described in D is not relevant to the issue being discussed.

text: A life sciences company is working on developing a new product that will help doctors integrate data from different sources to make a faster diagnosis. One of the major concerns for the program manager is that the development team does not understand the medical domain well enough and the doctors do not have a clear view about the capabilities of the product. What is the best way to ensure that the product is being built will be accepted by the customers?

choices.text: Undertake a detailed study of the operations of a hospital before starting out on the development
Develop small prototypes for the features, and obtain feedback from the users before building up on that feature fully
Recruit resources who are skilled in medicine as well as product development and assign them to each project on the program
Organize an intensive workshop for specialists in medicine and product development to discuss the requirements in detail, adopting group creativity techniques like brainstorming and six thinking hats

explanation: The issue is that the scope is not clear either to developers or the end users (doctors). The best approach is to adopt an iterative life-cycle that allows the team to build the product incrementally, incorporating feedback along the way.

text: A business process outsourcing company is working for a Federal Government process and it applies program management techniques to maintain and enhance its service for the process. Although the profits from the program are minuscule, the company feels it is important to continue because having the Federal Government as a customer gives them a lot of credibility. The program manager is not convinced about this argument because she believes that this benefit is not sufficient to justify the investment being made. What are the measures that will help the program manager make this case to the program steering committee?

choices.text: Number and value of the contracts that the company got directly as a result of the government reference
Money saved on advertising and selling expenses as a result of the Federal government reference
Number of reference letters issued by the Federal government
Opportunity cost (margin lost) due to the investment locked up in the program and the margins from the programs which were acquired by referring to the government contract

explanation: The cost incurred in continuing the program is that the company may have foregone the opportunity to work on higher margin programs. The benefit from the government reference can be measured by the margins delivered by the programs acquired directly as a result of the reference. These two measures establish more convincingly the utility of the program to the organization or otherwise. Although the other measures (B,C and D) are relevant, they only look at one side (i.e. the benefit) without regard to the cost incurred

text: A diversified company recently announced a strategy of divesting non-core businesses and focusing on core competencies, which is in telecommunications. A program in this organization is serving the banking sector, working on credit card billing services. There are several important customers that are being supported and the revenue from them is sizeable. Therefore, the organization decides to continue this product and service line but wants to reduce the investment. Which of the following success measures would be least relevant in the balanced scorecard for the program?

choices.text: Customer satisfaction ratings
Revenue from new product offerings
Average revenue per employee
Expense to Revenue ratio

explanation: Since the organization is reducing investment in this portfolio, introduction of new product lines and tracking revenue gained from them may not be very relevant to this program.

text: A software company releases product suite for the large enterprises that consists of 10 products. The release of all the products in the suite needs to be coordinated and there are a number of interfaces and integrations between the products. The suite is managed as a program, with a project manager managing individual product releases. The issue for the past several releases has been that there is strong product loyalty and comparatively little attention paid to the interfaces and integrations. Which of the following measures will help the program manager bring teams in sync at an early stage?

choices.text: Add an agenda item to the weekly staff meeting attended by all the project managers specifically to talk about how integrations are going
Tell the project teams early on that if the integrations do not work in the customer environment, everybody stands to lose their variable bonus payments
Appoint a team to specifically work on the integrations between the products from the early stages of the life-cycle all the way till the end
Provide special incentives to any team member who points out a potential integration issue at an early stage

explanation: If the issue is really important, it must have dedicated resources working on it. Simply discussing at the project manager level (A) will not help. Special incentives (B) may encourage the right behavior, but it would again rely on individual initiative. Option-C is talking about penalties without putting any concrete measures in place and the effectiveness would only be known after the release. Having a dedicated team is the best option.

text: There are 6 projects which are part of a program. Projects A and B will start first and start producing some artifacts for projects C, D, E and F, which will begin about 3 months after the start of A and B. The program manager and project managers are working on the scheduling of the project and program level milestones. The time estimates for projects C, D, E and F are in line with expectations of the senior stakeholders, but time estimates given by A and B are considered to be too high by the customer and senior management. Which way should the program manager proceed in order to come up with a plan?

choices.text: Use the project team’s estimates to reset the expectations at the stakeholder level
Ask the project teams of A and B to compress their estimate to match the stakeholder’s expectations
Discuss with the project managers of A and B about the possibility of compressing the schedule to match stakeholder expectations
Use the project team’s estimates for half of the projects and the stakeholder’s estimates for the other half

explanation: The project team’s estimates need to be considered. Other stakeholders may have an opinion, but at the end of the day the estimates of the people who will be actually working on the project have to be given precedence. This still leaves open the possibility of using schedule compression techniques to reduce the time taken (option C).

text: A well-known international fast food chain – famous for high quality products and customer service is expanding into a new country, which is fairly large and remote. A number of activities need to happen, including creation and maintenance of supply chain for the raw materials, establish the franchise model, acquisition and re-branding of stores, setting up the IT infrastructure, etc. Given this information, what would be the best architecture for this expansion activity?

choices.text: Initiate a project, which will establish the infra-structure and then transition it into operations
Create a program to manage the operations and simultaneously expand in the region – bring in a mix of headquarters and local chefs
Appoint a country manager and treat this expansion as a separate portfolio with independent business goals
Treat this like an operational expansion project, and bring in the chefs from headquarters to ensure standardization

explanation: This expansion program will likely have many projects and will also need to manage some operations until the expansion roll out is completed. Since it is an international food chain, the standardization is important. Adding local staff is also important to bring in local expertise and to be able to scale further.

text: A program for setting up and commissioning a petroleum refinery consists of several components. The components make use of a welding and fabrication unit which is a shared resource. As the different components reach a critical stage, the availability of the fabrication unit is becoming a problem. Which of the following is the LEAST suitable criterion that the program manager can use to resolve the conflicting demands?

choices.text: Correlation with the benefits of the program
Relation the distillation unit, which is the heart of the refinery
Commissioning date
Positioning on the critical path of the projects

explanation: The prioritization of shared resources should be based on the correlation with the program’s intended benefits. A, B and C are all valid criteria to be used, but D encompasses all of them.

text: A transport company is changing its entire fleet from diesel to compressed natural gas (CNG) as a result of a regulatory directive. The change will be managed as a program and implemented over a period of five years. One of the critical issues for the program manager is to manage the re-skilling or re-hiring of the engineers in the workshops, who have never dealt with CNG engines and vehicles before. What is the best option for the program manager?

choices.text: Hire 30% new engineers and re-train 70% of the existing engineers, while letting 30% existing engineers go
Hire new engineers to deal with the CNG engines and gradually let go of the old engineers
Organize trainings for the engineers to up-train them on CNG engines
Offer voluntary retirement schemes for the engineers who have < 10 years left to retire and hire new engineers instead

explanation: In the absence of other information about the scenario, the best option is to re-train the existing engineers. Re-hiring is always expensive and it takes a while for new staff to get used to the company’s culture and work habits.

text: A retail company based in the United States which is well known for offering low priced but good quality merchandise has initiated a program to expand its store network in Europe. Given the geographical diversity of the region, the program manager has set up multiple projects for managing the roll-out. One of the project managers comes up with a change request that a mega event should be held while opening each new store, with surprise discounts and hand-outs for every 10th customer. How should the program manager deal with this request?

choices.text: The program manager should recommend against accepting this change as it amounts to gold plating
Push back against the change as the plan has already been finalized and it is too late to change
Let the project manager present his case in front of the change approval board and go by the advice of the board
The program manager should recommend that this change is accepted as it seems to have a valid business driver

explanation: Remember the company is known for selling low price merchandise already and is likely operating on low margins. Offering special discounts and freebies on a selective basis might not only cause margins to come under further squeeze, but it may actually cause a backlash as select customers are being given freebies – at the cost of others. This is potentially gold plating and the program manager must recommend against it. This is better than taking a passive approach (Option D).

text: An organization decided to embrace Lean principles to optimize its manufacturing operations. This is expected to be a large initiative incorporating many projects and it decided to create a program. A program manager was appointed and asked to come up with a business case before the program could be formally kicked off. Which of the following benefits should NOT be included in the business case?

choices.text: New products launched
Organizational learning as a result of new process
Likely saving in operational cost
Reduction in inventory

explanation: The program is about optimizing operations and hence it is least likely to result in the creation of new products.

text: An organization is adopting Lean manufacturing principles and has initiated a program to drive the change initiatives. A business case was recently approved at the board level and a program charter was issued. The program manager has just been appointed. What should be the first priority for the program manager?

choices.text: To define the cost and benefits from the initiative and put together a compelling value proposition for the program
Attend training on Lean manufacturing techniques to gain hands-on expertise to better lead the program
Identify the stakeholders from the program and start meetings with the stakeholders to understand their expectations and concerns
Identify the appropriate governance structure including the components and their managers along with the constitution of the program steering committee

explanation: For any program and specially for organization wide change initiatives, it is vitally important to identify and engage stakeholders early. While all of the ideas given are good ideas, getting a head start on stakeholder management should be the highest priority.

text: An organization started a new business division to manage the business in the Asia Pacific region, which is seen to be having a very high potential for future growth. There are a large number of customer engagements in this geographically widespread and diverse region. Some of them are long-running and semi-permanent, whereas others are more recent and much targeted. This division can best be expressed as:

choices.text: A portfolio
A program
A project
An operation

explanation: This is certainly not a single project or operation as there are a number of engagements going on. It seems more like a portfolio because it represents a strategic investment and there is no evidence about the components being related to each other in any way other than being grouped together due to geographic location. The components of a program have to be “related” in some way.

text: An agricultural produce supply chain company faces high risk from timeliness and reliability of information about the changing weather patterns, which impact crop patterns, quantum of produce, speed of transportation, etc. This has been a perennial problem for a program that manages various components related to seasonal produce. Which of the following risk management strategies will be MOST helpful to the program manager?

choices.text: Introduce a mechanism that will improve the accuracy and timeliness of information about the weather
De-centralize the management of logistics so that the producers can take spot decisions based on their knowledge of local conditions
Start a new project to gradually shift the production to green houses so that weather does not impact production
Start a research project to study the impact of weather on the parameters mentioned above

explanation: The question states that the risk is that of the reliability and the timeliness of information about the weather. This is best addressed by Option-C. Other options are interesting, but are either over-kill (A, D) or do not address this core issue (B).

text: A program’s budget is being reviewed as part of the annual budgeting cycle. There are severe constraints on funding due to a business slow down. Cuts to the extent of nearly 50% are envisaged. Which of the following is the best thing for the program manager to do?

choices.text: Try to accelerate the transition of the completed components so that the program can start realizing revenue, thus easing the funding requirements
Raise the matter with the program steering committee and explain the impact of not getting the required level of funding
Ask the project managers to look for ways in which they can reduce costs
Make a compelling business case with the help of the project managers

explanation: During funds crunch times, a program manager should be on the lookout to monetize the components that are completed rather than keep on fighting for resources which are already scarce. This is an area where the program manager can bring in their experience and add value to the program.

text: At a recent anonymous employee survey, an organization received poor scores for its reward and recognition policies. A program manager wants to take action based on these findings and institutionalize an effective rewards and recognition policy across the program. What is the best way to achieve this?

choices.text: Initiate an additional survey specific to the program soliciting specific inputs about which policy would be the most effective
Ask for more details about the survey data so that more targeted actions can be taken
Set up a committee with representation from across the components of a program to come up with a R&R policy and guidelines for implementation
Double the R&R budget for all projects and set a goal for all project managers to make sure the entire budget is spent

explanation: An empowered committee of employees is the best way to address this because they would be in a better position to have the pulse of the people and make valuable recommendations.

text: A program has been initiated to build a large township consisting of residential and commercial complexes, schools, hospitals and other utilities in a remote town. During the planning stage, funding was restricted and only a few of the proposed projects might take off in the initial phases. Several projects came up for approval. Which one should receive the highest priority? (A) A movie theater and mall that will provide entertainment and shopping facilities to the residents (B) A golf club that will serve the residents and also earn revenue by offering membership and rental facilities to outsiders (C) A temple complex in deference to the religious sentiments of the potential residents (D) A water purification plant that is required for treating waste from the complex as per the pollution control norms

choices.text: C
A
B
D

explanation: This is a compliance project, therefore will receive the highest priority. Priorities of others might vary depending upon the business and other justifications.

text: An automobile company is known for being socially responsible and has a great brand equity as a result of this. As part of an expansion program, a new factory block was established in a suburban area. A complaint was received from a resident of the suburb that the noise from the factory was causing a disturbance. Preliminary investigations suggested that the complaint did not have a lot of merit as the resident lived about a mile from the factory and there was a highway between his residence and the factory. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Meet with the complainant and try to address the issue
Ask the project manager in charge of the site to take up the complaint directly with the complainant and establish a clear time line to close it
Send the data to the complainant and ask for permission to close the complaint
Forward the complaint to the community and social responsibility department in your organization along with the readings and let them deal with it

explanation: A company whose USP is community and social responsibility cannot afford to be seen as ignoring this aspect. Even if the complaint is frivolous and without merit, it is incumbent on the program manager to take this matter seriously and address it directly (rather than forward it around or delegate it).

text: A program is in the delivery of benefits stage and large teams with several components are working in parallel. Some of the projects are finding their teams to be overloaded and burning midnight oil, while others have a comparatively relaxed schedule. Team members from projects A and B have been working over the weekends for the past month or so. The program manager is concerned that this may cause burn-out. What can the program manager do in this situation?

choices.text: Ask the managers of projects A and B if they need help in managing the situation
Ask the managers of projects A and B to plan for succession in case team members leave
Introduce a policy of over-time pay so that project managers do not over-work teams unless absolutely necessary
Announce a team outing on the following weekend so that the team members can chill out and relax after their hard work

explanation: There may be a lot of things the program manager can do (e.g. options B or C), they need to bear in mind that the project managers need to be given autonomy in taking care of the teams. Project managers should in any case be planning for successions (option-D) but it would be a defensive measure at best.

text: A large program is building infrastructure and services for a new airport terminal that is coming up. The program depends heavily on vendors and many components have outsourced the delivery and installation of several components, including baggage handling systems, ground transportation, parking management, etc. Many of these systems are so heavily integrated that even the slightest delay or compromise in specifications may cause the entire program to stall. The program manager is in the process of finalizing the program level procurement policy. Which of the following would be the LEAST suitable form of contract for this program?

choices.text: Revenue share
Firm Fixed price
Time and Material
Cost reimbursable, with incentives

explanation: The fixed price contract places all the cost risk on the supplier. It would make them less flexible in adjusting to even slightest changes that may be needed for effective integration of systems. As a program, it is heavily dependent upon timely delivery and flawless integration. Therefore the contracts need to reassure the suppliers that they will continue to make money and guarantee their continued commitment towards the program.

text: A long running project within a program has just received acceptance for its final customer deliverable. The project was already delayed by a few months – and the team members from this project were scheduled to immediately move into a different project which required the same skills. The project manager for the new project wants them to start immediately, without waiting for the final closure meeting and completion of the project archives and escrow formalities. What should be the recommendation of the program manager?

choices.text: Start the new project as it is important the ability of the program to continue delivering the benefits
Ask the project manager of the new project to defer the start of the project until all the necessary closure activities have been completed and signed off by the customer
Ask the program steering committee for a process deviation as an exception to skip closure formalities just for this one project
Ask the project manager of the completed project to accelerate closure formalities but do not release resources until the closure is complete

explanation: Following proper closure formalities is one of the strongest indicators of process maturity and PMI places a great emphasis on this. It is understandable that the new project is waiting impatiently, but the completion of closure formalities cannot be skipped (A, C and D are different shades of avoiding closure).

text: A program has been initiated under a SoW issued by a customer to build an IT infrastructure management system. This involves several projects, which gradually transition into operations. The customer has recently heard about new developments around Big Data concepts and wants the program team to evaluate how these concepts can be applied to their management system. The team suggests that a good way to evaluate the options would be to go to a Big Data conference. There is a need to fund travel and logistics for the conference trip. Who should approve this funding request?

choices.text: The project managers whose team members are traveling
The program steering committee
The customer
The program manager

explanation: This request has come about as a result of a customer directive/suggestion. It is still in the evaluation stage (no changes have been accepted yet) and therefore it is most appropriate that the customer provides funding for this stage.

text: An IT services company offers remote management of IT infrastructure and applications to its customers. One of the programs being managed for a particular client was in deep trouble, getting consistently poor customer satisfaction scores .Julie, an expert program manager was appointed by the PMO to investigate and suggest remedial action. Julie found that the customer’s confidence level was really low and there were frequent escalations to the senior management. This led to a further increase in the communication overhead and more time was spent in dealing with the escalation than in solving the problem. Which is the best way to address this issue?

choices.text: Set up an escalation matrix that clearly defines what problems get escalated and how the escalations are handled
Create a plan to improve the services so that there is no need for the customer to escalate any issues
Meet with the customers to explain that it is in their own interest to limit escalations to the bare minimum so that the team can focus on solving problems
Educate the teams to deal with escalations by focusing on the problem at hand rather than looking at the communication overhead

explanation: The team is clearly suffering from the absence of a clearly defined escalation policy and escalation matrix. Option-A is attractive, but not likely to lead to immediate benefits, given the state that the program is in. Options B and D are counter-productive because ignoring the escalation or asking the customers not to escalate will not help matters.

text: A program is part of the luxury cars portfolio of a large and well diversified automobile company. There is perceived to be a large market potential in an Asian country and it is believed that having a manufacturing entity in that country would really help in tapping into this market. The Sales team has prepared a proposal and sent a business case for a very large investment. What should do the program manager do about this proposal?

choices.text: Call for a meeting of the program steering committee and the portfolio manager to discuss the proposal
Make a personal visit to China to meet with the regional Sales team to get a feel from the ground before taking any further action
Meet with the project and operations managers to get their views about the proposal
Issue the charter for a new project to get the ball rolling on this investment

explanation: This is a strategic decision involving a very large investment. This decision is best taken at the strategic level involving the program steering committee.

text: For compliance and accounting purposes, a program manager needs to produce a report classifying expenditure as expense or capital. This requires all components to adhere to certain guidelines. A couple of project managers complain that the guidelines are cumbersome and that they find it difficult to get their team members to comply. What should you do as a program manager?

choices.text: Talk to the Accounting department about the difficulties being faced, but tell the project managers it is their responsibility to ensure 100% compliance
Raise the matter to the program steering committee for their advice
Tell the project managers that it is OK to use approximations – and the data need not be very accurate
Talk to the Accounting department and inform them that you will not be able to provide the report until the guidelines are simplified

explanation: The program manager should try and resolve issues wherever they are impacting the projects, especially multiple projects. However, the program manager should not compromise on the integrity of the data – especially where it is used for compliance and reporting purposes.

text: A program has set up an office in a city that is notorious for thefts and mugging. The organization has a stated policy of buying travel insurance for all its employees who travel on duty and theft insurance for all its equipment. As a result of the reputation of this city and a spurt in incidents in the recent past, the insurance company has hiked premiums significantly. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Evaluate the cost of accepting the risk against transferring (insuring)
Appoint special security staff for all the program’s employees and offices
Change the insurance provider
Budget for the increased premiums

explanation: Sometimes it may be beneficial to accept the risk of loss rather than try to insure at a very high premium. This option must be evaluated before switching to other options.

text: A project manager has escalated an issue to the program manager. A senior technical expert in her team just resigned. There is no back-up for this resource, who is working on critical path activities. The immediate milestones on the project will be delayed by about 4 weeks as a result of this setback. What should be the program manager’s immediate concern?

choices.text: Look for resources who can immediately back-fill the technical expert from other projects within the program
Determine the impact of the delay on other projects and the benefits delivery to the organization
Inquire why there was no succession planning and institutionalize better succession planning policies across the program
Forward the escalation to the executive sponsor and HR, requesting urgent action on identifying a successor

explanation: As a program manager, you need to focus on management of the overall program with the goal of delivering the benefits. A 4 week delay in a project’s deliverables may or may not have a big impact on this. If other projects are likely to be affected, then the impact might cascade. The first priority of the program manager is to assess the impact and then move on to likely solutions.

text: A large cell phone company A recently acquired a small app development company B. A is trying to merge B’s products into its portfolio and deliver added value to customers through this integration. A program was initiated for this purpose and it is frequently running into issues because the quality processes of project teams from B are very lose and informal as compared to A. What should be done to address this?

choices.text: A new quality policy needs to be formulated for the merged entity that takes best practices from both the relevant policies
The program should determine the quality policy based on the specific needs and inputs from stakeholders
As A is the acquiring company, their quality policies should be used and supplemented with B’s test suites
As B’s products are being integrated, their quality policies should be used and supplemented with A’s integration tests

explanation: There is no right or wrong policy – it depends upon the needs of the program. Furthermore, quality plan is influenced by the plan for scope, cost, time, risk etc., so the program manager has to take all these into consideration before deciding.

text: A large program being managed as part of an outsourced contract is being transitioned from Company A to Company B. The plan is to have 6 months of overlap to let Company B acquire the knowledge and expertise and achieve 2 milestones while Company A is still around. Company A is bitter about the transition and is making the hand-over and knowledge transfer process tough for Company B. This has caused a serious delay in the deliverables for the first milestone. How should the Program Manager from Company B approach this situation?

choices.text: Explain the situation to the program steering committee, clearly articulating how Company A’s non-cooperation has caused the delay
Ensure steady communication to the customer representatives and senior managements of Company A and B about the progress, blocking issues and steps being taken to address them
Examine the feasibility of using schedule crashing to bring the schedule back under control
Amend the baseline schedule to take the ground realities into account

explanation: It is quite natural that Company A is bitter and somewhat non-cooperative. However, both companies are ultimately responsible to the customer. It is important to keep the communication steady and non-confrontational (ruling out Option A). Option C is a process formality that will not address the issue. Option D fails to recognize that the delay is not due to shortage of resources but the lack of expertise and knowledge transfer.

text: An organization is working on a business process optimization program for the local government. The project managers are getting hit with arbitrary change requests and conflicting directions from the elected representatives and the bureaucrats. This is causing a lot of confusion and the program manager’s attempts to constitute a change management board have failed due to lack of cooperation from the customer’s end. This is impacting progress and deliveries. What might be the best course of action for the program manager?

choices.text: Ask the project managers to reject change requests which are not authorized
Escalate the matter to the program steering committee and ask for a high level meeting between the customer and Board representatives
Recommend closure of the program to see if the ultimatum works to introduce some discipline
Document the loss of time and resources due to such changes and bring them up if the program’s lack of progress is called into question

explanation: The program manager has not been able to resolve the issue and hence needs to escalate. It is up to the program steering committee to deal with the escalation and help the program manager resolve the issue.

text: An automobile company is running a program for development and manufacture of its best-selling hatchback model. There are 4 integrated manufacturing plants across the country and a central research and development center where new developments take place. One day the paint shop at the largest factory burnt down. An emergency sub-program was put in place to reconstruct the paint shop, while minimizing the disruption to operations. If you were the program manager in charge of this sub-program, what would be the most appropriate success measure that indicates the benefits delivered by the program?

choices.text: Number of customer complaints about the paint quality until the re-construction is completed
Reduction in disruption to planned production schedule till the new facility is commissioned
Planned vs. Actual cost of re-construction and operations till the re-construction is completed
Reduction in the fire safety hazards before re-construction through effective root cause analysis and commissioning of remedial measures

explanation: All of the measures given in the answers are relevant to some degree but the main reason or initiation of the sub-program was to quickly reconstruct the facility, while minimizing disruption to operations. This is best addressed by Option-A

text: A program has been initiated to build a large township consisting of residential and commercial complexes, schools, hospitals and other utilities in a remote town. One of the issues is that the location currently does not have cell phone connectivity which causes issues with communication with the staff which is onsite and those present at the headquarters. Which of the following change requests best addresses this issue from a program perspective?

choices.text: Amend the communication plan to make use of alternative techniques such as wired connections coupled with walkie-talkies and satellite phones depending upon urgency and need
Provide most of the facilities and delegate decision making authority to the site manager to minimize the need for frequent communication with headquarters
Relocate the program manager and all essential staff to the site
Get permission to construct a transmission tower that can be rented to a cell phone company which can then be persuaded to offer coverage

explanation: Option A is most innovative and likely to address the issue directly. The fact that a township is coming up means that cell phone coverage is bound to be required sooner or later. The possibility of introducing a tower that can potentially earn revenue in the future is aligned with program benefits. Option B is a work around and a cumbersome one at that. Options C and D ignore the fact that communication may be needed not just between site and headquarters but also within the site between different components as well.

text: A manufacturing organization is adopting Lean methodologies. A program has been constituted for achieving this transition. The Sponsor for the program is a senior executive who is convinced about the business benefits and is ready to commit funds and resources necessary for the program. The program was kicked off by the CEO, who rightly emphasized the need and urgency of the program to retain the competitive advantage. A cross-functional steering committee was formed and a clear vision and set of guidelines were communicated to the functions. Change agents were appointed in each function to take the changes forward. What could be the best NEXT step for the program?

choices.text: Create a communications campaign to explain the benefits of the program to the entire organization
Appoint project managers and issue project charters
Create some short term wins and communicate them across the organization
Identify influential stakeholders across the board and create a stakeholder engagement plan

explanation: C and D have already been done, based on the description given in the question. The program now needs to move forward. The best way to gain momentum to move forward in a change initiative is to create some highly visible short term gains.

text: At a program review, many project managers pointed out that it is very difficult to coordinate work because of strong functional loyalties which cause friction between the teams. For instance, the engineering and the testing teams are constantly at loggerheads because of conflicting goals. What is the best thing that the program manager can do?

choices.text: Ask for an increase in the contingency buffers on cost and time to account for delays and escalations due to the conflicts
Make a proposal that the organization be changed to a projectized structure to better align the resources along project and program work
Ask the project managers to use techniques like influencing without authority – as the organizational structure cannot be altered very easily
Request the program steering committee to involve the program team (comprising of project and program manager) in setting and evaluating performance goals for the staff assigned to the program

explanation: It would be somewhat presumptuous to suppose that a program manager can suggest a total overhaul of the organization structure (Option-C) but it is also not effective for the Program manager to remain passive or merely react to the situation (options A and D). The core issue being brought up by the projects is lack of alignment around goals and it might be solved if they are involved in the goal setting for the team.

text: At a recent phase gate review meeting, the program sponsor expressed the desire to have the first of the projects to release its product into the market within 3 months. The project manager has reviewed the plan and estimated the release time line to be a minimum of 6 months. How can the program manager help reconcile the top-down and bottom-up expectations in this case?

choices.text: Announce a special bonus for timely completion for all the project’s resources
Help the project manager out by slowing down other projects and diverting all resources freed up into this project
