Ask the project manager and program sponsor if 4.5 months is achievable and acceptable
Push back on the imposed deadline and get into discussions with the sponsor

explanation: This is a very common scenario, when the program manager needs to deal with mis-matching expectations. The principle that is being emphasized here is that others things being equal, the program manager must favor and believe the estimates given by the team and them get into discussions with the program steering committee about possibilities.

text: A manufacturing organization is adopting Lean methodologies. A program has been constituted for achieving this transition. The Sponsor for the program is a senior executive who is convinced about the business benefits and is ready to commit funds and resources necessary for the program. The program has been in delivery of benefits mode for over a year. Many functions have shown impressive improvements in operational efficiency. However in some functions, the improvements were not sustained and they gradually returned to the old ways of working. What is the MOST likely reason for this?

choices.text: The functions were not convinced about the projected and realized benefits
Lack of budgetary support for sustaining the changes
The team responsible for consolidating and institutionalizing the gains were not trained and enabled
Some functions may not have understood the urgency behind the intended changes

explanation: After achieving the initial gains, it is critical for the program team to make sure that the benefits are properly transitioned to the operations and that the operations are enabled to accept and sustain the benefits. This is most likely to have been the step where the gaps surfaced. From the description of the scenario so far, it does not appear as though the budgetary support was not available or that the urgency and business benefits were not explained to the teams.

text: A program has been initiated under a fixed price contract with a customer. There are multiple components that deliver different products and services to the customer according to the agreement. At a program review, multiple component managers complained about lack of availability of the business analysts (BA) from the customer end to clarify the requirements. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Ask the program steering committee to intervene and ensure the availability of the BA’s in a timely manner
Ask the component managers to make suitable assumptions, document them and proceed without the BA’s consent if required to prevent delays
Talk to the customer seeking more responsiveness, explaining that the impact of the absence of response
Ask the component managers to try and resolve the issues directly with the BA’s in person rather than starting a program wide escalation

explanation: In this case the matter is localized and it is in the customer’s best interests to sort it out amicably. Hence the program manager should make a direct approach and try to resolve it.

text: A program for drug manufacturing and research involves performing clinical trials for a product that is at an advanced stage of completion. The trials are expected to be done in India. The project manager for this project flags to you that one of the risks identified for the trials is that the drug may result in certain side-effects if administered to people who have received chicken pox vaccination before, which is a common practice in India. You decide to move the trials to UK, where another product is about to start trials and is unlikely to clash with the trials that are being planned. As a program manager in Question.13, in addition to the risk impact of the decision you have taken, you also need to consider which of the following.

choices.text: Identification of subjects for the trials
Quality and reliability of the setup
Arrangements for transportation of the samples
Additional cost of the trials, which have to be borne by the program’s reserves

explanation: All the other options are things that are definitely important, but really for the project manager of the concerned project to worry about. A program manager must focus on the program-level decisions, which is C.

text: You outsource software development work on your program to a company located in a different country on a T&M basis. The terms and rates are negotiated across the board and many projects use these services. One of your project managers has complained to you that the work allocated to the outsourcer was not completed on time and that he would like to with-hold the payments to this company until it is done. What should you do?

choices.text: Tell the project manager stopping payments is not an option
Issue a show-cause notice to the contractor
Stop payments to the contractor and give them notice
Call up the contractor and get their side of the story

explanation: In a T&M contract, typically the payments are not based upon work or milestone so stopping payment is not an option. You could do A or D, but you have to let the project manager know about the bottom line. Ultimately it is the seller’s responsibility to make sure that the hired contractors deliver as per expectations.

text: You are trying to help managers in your organization understand the difference between program life-cycles, project life-cycles and product life-cycles. Which of the following identifies the DIFFERENCE between project and product life cycles?

choices.text: The project management life-cycle only applies to some projects whereas product life-cycle applies to all products
The project management life-cycle is longer than the product life-cycle
The project life-cycle describes what you need to do to do complete the work of the project
The project life-cycle is created based on the top level of the work breakdown structure, whereas product life-cycle is based on the scope definition

explanation: Statements A, B and C are not true. D is the only one that seems plausible.

text: A program manager is preparing a program schedule. He has taken the scope statement and prepared the program-WBS with input from the project managers and stakeholders. The project managers were asked to come up with project level WBS, activity definition, sequencing and estimates. Once he had the project schedules, he combined them after adjusting for dependencies and resource leveling into a master program schedule. He then published the program schedule to the team and asked the project managers to start tracking against it. What step did the program manager miss?

choices.text: He did not prepare the network diagrams for the program
He did not consider over or under-utilization of shared resources
He did not do top-down planning
He failed to involve the team in the process

explanation: He did ask the project managers to prepare the program-WBS as well as the project schedules, so he did involve the team. He did ask the project managers to sequence the activities and considered project dependencies, so the part about program network diagrams is also covered. He also did resource-leveling, so over and under-utilization of resources is also taken care of. What does not appear to have been done (at least from the information available in the question) is to take top-down input, i.e. does the schedule which was arrived at by the team tally with the customer or sponsor’s expectations?

text: You are in-charge of a program for a chemicals company, which has the following goals. De-bottlenecking of the refining process, reducing the emissions by 15% and improving energy efficiency of the overall factory by 25%. During the planning process, you discover that you will urgently need to put in place a welding unit in order to manage the large number of a fabrication jobs required. If this is not done in time, a number of activities on the program might get delayed. You look for a project manager and ask for the project to begin immediately. The project manager asks for a project charter before she starts. What should your response be?

choices.text: Ask the project manager to prepare the charter and approve it
Tell the project manager to begin work and the charter will be issued in due course
Ask for senior management for a charter
Tell the project manager that this is an internal project and does not need a charter

explanation: A charter is a MUST and project should not start without it, so the project manager is right in demanding it. The question then is can the program manager issue it himself or should he ask senior management to provide it. As the program manager has been tasked with a certain set of objectives, it is his responsibility to figure out what projects are needed. So ideally the program manager should have a program charter and he should issue the charter for component projects on his own.

text: One of the project managers on your program has submitted a change that does not affect overall program schedule and is easy to complete. What should be the primary concern for the program manager in evaluating the change request?

choices.text: Impact on the quality of the project implementing the change
Using the right process for handling the change request
Impact on the risk level of the project implementing the change
Impact on other projects of the program

explanation: A program manager should always be concerned about the inter-dependencies between projects while handling change. A and B are the responsibility of project managers. D is also something that the program manager will look out for, but his primary concern should be C.

text: A program manager was assigned to a newly initiated program. The program is in a new domain and technology for the organization and there is not a lot of information or guidance available within the organization about managing such programs. How should the program manager go about establishing the governance structure for the program?

choices.text: Research industry best practices and external guidance
Conduct a meeting with the project managers to brainstorm about the best structure
Ask the PMO for advice
The program steering committee will set up the governance structure

explanation: The program manager is responsible for developing a structure using industry best practices and organizational standards (Task 1 in Program governance from the examination content outline). Since not a lot of expertise is available within the organization, the program manager must rely on information from industry practices

text: A program was started out to work on a novel product for the organization. The organization did not have much experience or expertise to work in this area before. During program closure, the program manager is preparing the final performance reports for the program. Which of the following is the most important data point to include in the report?

choices.text: Benefits realized vs. committed
Actual spending vs. budget
Productivity delivered
Scope delivered vs. planned

explanation: The primary reason of working on a program is to obtain benefits and therefore the closure report ought to focus on the realization of benefits that were planned. The other measures are secondary – especially given the fact that program was in a novel area.

text: During a status review, manager of project A reported that the project is now complete and requests for approval to close it. What is the most important step for the program manager?

choices.text: Wait for other projects to complete before approving the closure of all the related projects
Ask the project manager to ensure that the lessons learned are captured before releasing the team
Check to see if the project has any open contractual obligations before approving the closure
Validate that the deliverables are completed and integrated into the program before directing the project manager to start with the closure formalities

explanation: One of the tasks for a program manager during execution is to approve the closure of constituent projects upon the completion of deliverables (Task 24 from program life cycle management in the examination content outline).

text: A program manager managing a time critical program has received estimated time-lines from each of the component projects and is about to start schedule development. Some of the time lines do not match with the Top-down expectations of the executives. How should the program manager reconcile this?

choices.text: Analyze the impact of the mismatch in time lines with benefits delivery and try to arrive at a solution
Try to compress the project schedules if necessary by incurring additional cost
Perform the projects in parallel so that the overall program schedule is not expected
Highlight the mismatch as a risk and include the necessary contingencies

explanation: The program manager needs to translate the disparity in time lines in terms of the delivery of business benefits. After doing this, the impact of the mismatch can be assessed and accordingly the appropriate solution can be found

text: A is a company with a risk-taking culture that encourages individual initiative. B is a process-driven organization where deviation from the agreed upon procedure is not encouraged. The two companies merge to form a new company called AB, where A and B are run as different lines of business. Given the differences in culture, what kind of rewards structure would you NOT use to motivate the teams in the program?

choices.text: Team awards that focus on team achievements rather than individual
Rewards decided by you as the Program Manager based on your discretion
Individual awards that encourage outstanding performance
Awards specifically customized for the expected deliverables of your program

explanation: All of options A, B and D are good ideas and one could incorporate them into a rewards plan. What will NOT work, is a system where the program manager exercises his/her sole discretion in adjudicating for the awards. This will certainly displease people in company B, where procedures and guidelines are emphasized, and it will also not likely please people from company A, because individual excellence demands recognition for achievement, and if the program manager misses out or makes a mistake, it would be an unpleasant situation.

text: The manager of the program manager was writing the key results areas (KRA’s) for the program manager. The most important KRA for a program manager should be to ensure:

choices.text: Standardization of processes across all the program’s components
High approval ratings from the team members and stakeholders at the end of the program
Components of the program meeting their cost, time and quality objectives
Realizing the intended benefits from the program

explanation: Realization of benefits that the organization is looking for from the program should be the most important goal for a program manager. All the other answers definitely contribute to this achievement, but none in isolation is enough. Hence c. is the best answer.

text: The program manager has just resigned and you are trying to hire a replacement. What qualities would you look for in this individual above everything else:

choices.text: Technical and management skills that are respected by everybody on the team
Ability to influence without authority
Tough negotiator – hard to say no to
A pleasant personality, gets along with everybody on the team

explanation: The ability to influence others without necessarily having formal authority is a key skill for a program manager. It may involve negotiation skills, necessity to win friends by pleasing others and also perhaps technical and management skills. But none of the others in isolation will help the program manager without having the ability to influence others.

text: A program manager is initiating a component to improve the efficiency of the test procedures within the components. This will save 15% on the cost of quality and will be executed by establishing a community of practice. Different project team members will contribute to the community, working on a part time basis. Who should be issuing the charter for this project?

choices.text: The leader of the community of practice
The program steering committee
The program manager
The leader of the quality function in the organization

explanation: The component seems to be an internal component of the program that will have voluntary participation from the components. From the description it appears that the program manager can initiate this component.

text: Six months after a new management information system program went live at a large bank, a survey of users showed that barely 25% of the features were actively used and 65% of the users were dissatisfied with the new system. The only people who seemed happy with the new system seem to be the top management and technically accomplished people who were able to figure out how to work with the new system. This is MOST likely to be a failure of:

choices.text: Risk Management
Transition Planning
Scope Definition
Resource Management

explanation: The fact that some people who were able to figure out the system were happy with it shows that the system is inherently not faulty. The most likely cause of this situation therefore is improper transition planning, where bulk of the end users do not seem to have been trained on how to use the features of the new system.

text: In a development program, many projects produce intermediate deliverables and the responsibility of integrating them into various assemblies and sub-assemblies lies with another project. It has been found that under cost and time pressure, the projects tend to deliver sub-standard items resulting in issues in integrating. Which of the following is the best measure that the program manager can take to make the projects accountable not just for their deliverables but also the integration?

choices.text: Add the success of integration to the performance objectives of the project managers
Assign a member of the project teams to ensure successful integration and handover before the deliverables are accepted
For every integration defect that is found, ensure that the root causes are identified and documented
Ensure that the key requirements for integration are well documented and checked strictly during quality control

explanation: While all the measures have some merit in them, the best way to ensure there is accountability in terms of integration is to assign specific team members. This will generate more awareness about the issues discovered and spread the knowledge across the projects.

text: You are a program manager for a large consulting firm. The aim of the program is to achieve operational efficiencies by looking for opportunities to exploit synergies. Several projects are recommended for inclusion in the program, but you are currently only in a position to include one based on the program budget. Which of the following would you recommend selecting?Project A has an internal rate of return of 12%. Project B has a predicted Benefit Cost Ratio (BCR) of 1:3. Project C has an opportunity cost of $75,000. Project D has a payback period of six months. Based on this, WHICH project would you recommend?

choices.text: Project D, where the payback period is 6 months
Project C, where the opportunity cost of % $75,000
Project B where the benefits cost ratio is 1:1.3
Project A which has an IRR of 12%

explanation: B is not correct because BCR < 1. C is not correct because it is merely stating what option you have given up. Among A and D, A is a better answer because the IRR considers time-value of money and cash flows beyond the breakeven point as well.

text: Project A is part of a program. The schedule variance for the project has been negative for several weeks. The program manager is concerned that this may impact other projects. The project manager has reported that the major cause of the delay was the lack of technical knowledge within the team. Whose responsibility is it to solve this problem?

choices.text: The learning and development function within HR
Manager of Project A along with other affected projects
Manager of Project A
The program manager

explanation: The project manager is ultimately responsible for the projects being on time. The program manager may provide assistance in mobilizing the necessary resources, but the project manager needs to be in the driver’s seat.

text: You have a “best team of the quarter” award, which rewards the best performing team on your software development program. The last award was given to a team which delivered localized version of a report to a French customer going beyond the stated specifications. The previous quarter, the award went to a team which set for itself and achieved a 25% improvement on the service levels, which were already meeting requirements. What is wrong with this situation?

choices.text: Teams are being awarded for gold-plating.
Such awards may lead to unhealthy competition among teams.
Nothing. This is a perfect example of how to motivate teams.
Team awards will not work in a individual-oriented culture.

explanation: Gold-plating is a term that indicates giving something to the customer over and beyond the specifications. It is a bad thing because the customer may not want gold-plated deliverables.

text: You are managing a program that installs, commissions and operates wind turbines. The parts are manufactured in factories and sent to different project sites. Some of the parts are huge and transportation by road is a non-trivial activity. It turned out that the transportation cost was not included in the schedule or budget for any project. The sites are waiting for the parts to arrive. What should be done?

choices.text: Raise a change request to add a component for transportation and convene a meeting of the program steering committee
Initiate an emergency change and utilize the program reserves to kick off the transportation activity
Outsource the transportation to a third party to save time
Work with the project manager of the assembly project to include these tasks in the plan for that project

explanation: This seems to be a clear oversight on part of the program office to have missed out on a critical component in the P-WBS. Since it has been discovered late, it needs to be tackled in an emergency and the program should fund the required activities from the program reserves.

text: Your company has re-defined its strategic plan. Your program is responsible for a key component of the strategy. One of your product managers approaches you with a proposal to start a new project that will meet the needs of a key customer. The new project is in line with the previous strategy, but it is not aligned with the new one. The project seems to be feasible, looks to be profitable and is relatively low risk to execute. It also can potentially share resources with other projects in the program. As the program manager, what is the BEST course of action?

choices.text: Inform the customer of the change in corporate direction and ask him/her to take another look at the project
Ask the program steering committee for guidance
Issue a project charter and ask the project manager to finish the project quickly
Ask the project manager to submit a detailed cost benefit analysis of the project

explanation: Since the new project is not in line with the strategy, management needs to provide guidance about this. Even cost-benefit analysis involves effort and one should not commit that effort unless management approves that effort.

text: XYZ engineering is an oil exploration company. An important program of this company involves drilling 40 offshore wells in a promising area. Each well site is unique hence each is a project in its own right. The program has been in execution for the past several years. 5 out of the 40 wells struck oil or gas that is commercially exploitable. After completing the survey and assessment, those have been handed over to the production team for further development. You have almost completed the closure formalities on all the projects and the overall program. Suddenly in one of the meetings, a newly appointed geologist suggests drilling 5 more wells, as he believes there is a good possibility of finding exploitable reserves. What should you do?

choices.text: Ask for detailed technical reports to back up the geologist’s idea so that you can assess feasibility
Defer closure of the program and raise a change request asking for approval to initiate 5 more projects
Give approval for just one more well for the time being– if that turns out to be dry, do not approve the remaining four
Close the original program and work with the geologist to start a new program for the additional work

explanation: The objective of the program is to find oil and gas and the request made by the geologist is consistent with that objective. This is a change request, which needs to be evaluated for techno-commercial feasibility; hence A is a good answer. B is not a good answer because by closing the current program, you will close all existing contracts, release the resources etc., and the new program will start everything from scratch, which is an overhead. C is not a good answer because you do not have the technical expertise to evaluate the viability of the idea. D is neither here nor there – you don’t know which of the five wells might strike pay dirt, so you cannot really go by sequential logic in this case.

text: Few of the project teams working as part of a program are working remotely. At a recent employee survey, it was observed that the remote teams had a lower team engagement and motivation levels with the result that they did not feel connected with the overall goals. What should the program manager do to address this?

choices.text: Appoint strong local leadership for the remote teams so that they motivation levels are good
Discuss the observations with the program steering committee and raise a program level issue to be addressed on priority
Engage the HR team from the organization to work on this problem
Discuss with the project managers to identify underlying causes and possible remedies

explanation: The program manager is supposed to lead the human resource functions in a program in order to improve team engagement and achieve commitment to program’s goals (Task 19 in program life cycle management from the examination content outline). Therefore the program manager should play a proactive role in addressing the problem mentioned in the scenario.

text: A program manager for a recently constituted program left abruptly and you are taking over in an emergency. You did not get a chance to talk to the previous manager. You have had little by way of a transition and need to start from scratch. What is the BEST way to begin?

choices.text: Read the organization’s mission statement and validate the alignment of the program with the overall organizational strategy
Meet with the program sponsor to understand his expectations from the program
Meet with the project managers and understand the project scopes to build a picture of overall program level scope
Read the Program Charter and understand the overall business case and high level objectives

explanation: The program charter will contain a high-level description of the program scope. The project scope statements will only tell you about the scope of the constituent projects (a program may contain other work apart from the projects) and they may not all have been done yet as the program has just been constituted. Meeting with the sponsor is a good idea but you need to do your homework first. It is indeed important to ensure strategic alignment, but that may not be your first step as you are taking over the program.

text: Your program has expanded to include projects in multiple geographies. Some project teams are used to an informal communications style, relying a lot on meetings, instant messaging and phone calls. Other teams are used to having written documentation for the important artifacts and decisions. The issue has caused a lot of aggravation and has been escalated to you. What would you suggest to the teams?

choices.text: Call a meeting between teams to discuss the issue and come to a conclusion
Put the issue to vote and decide based on a majority
You will counsel the teams to rely on more formal communication
Let the project managers work on the communication plan for their projects

explanation: In a geographically dispersed team, certain degree of formality in hand-offs is required. Especially where you are working with out-sourced teams and contracts may be involved. You may want to rationalize the amount of documentation produced, but there is no escaping it.

text: A program has several constituent projects. At a routine status review meeting, an influential stakeholder requested for a change related to the features of a product. The stakeholder was not aware that the product was already completed and transitioned to operations. What is the most important action for the program manager?

choices.text: Review the program’s communication strategy to ensure correct information is circulated to all stakeholders in a timely manner
Inform the stakeholder that the product was already transitioned and no changes are possible
Request the program steering committee to recall the product and re-open the project to implement the change
Forward the change request to the operational team

explanation: An influential stakeholder not being aware that a project is completed and the product transitioned indicates a failure of the communication strategy for the program. Reviewing this is the most important action for the program manager. How to deal with the change (recalling the product or using the operations team to work on the change or refusing the change) depends upon the nature and impact of the change

text: Your overall program was budgeted at $2 million, but now has a CPI of 0.8 and one of your challenges is to ensure budget availability to all projects. At this time, you learn that one of the projects in your program is likely to finish under-budget by about $20,000. It so happens that this project involved some customized work for a particular customer and the customer is being billed for it under a cost-reimbursable contract. What should you do?

choices.text: Do additional work on the project to enhance the deliverable of the project and bill the entire amount.
Pad the costs with additional tasks until the entire budget is used up
Inform the customer about the actual v/s planned expense and ask for a decision on how to use the surplus
Find ways in which to bill the entire budgeted amount to the customer and transfer the surplus to the other projects in the program

explanation: It is unethical in a cost-reimbursable contract to bill the customer for unreasonable charges, therefore A is not the right option even if it helps a little with the financial difficulties. C is not the right option, unless the customer really wants the extra work and has approved it. D is unethical for the same reasons as above. B seems the most appropriate thing to do.

text: The program manager is preparing to make a presentation to the Senior management for approval of the program charter. Which of the following is the least appropriate section to include the presentation?

choices.text: Benefits forecast from the program
Composition of the program steering committee and the governance structure for the projects
High level cost and investment needed for the program
Major milestones in the program roadmap

explanation: The composition of the program steering committee and the mechanism to govern the projects may be known only after the approval of the program charter. All others may be part of the presentation for securing initial approval (Task 9 of the examination content outline – Strategic program management

text: A program team is in the planning phase. The program manager is trying to get the project managers together to decide the sequence of major activities and determine the critical path. How should the information about critical paths of the projects be used in planning the overall program?

choices.text: The program should look for opportunities to crash the critical paths of projects in order to reduce the program duration
Links between the critical paths of dependent projects should be investigated and appropriate feeding buffers planned
Resource allocation should always favor the projects which are on the critical path
The critical path of the program is the sum total of the critical paths of the projects

explanation: Resource allocation should favor achievement of overall program objectives (not necessarily critical path of every project). Crashing is called for only when you are looking to reduce durations. Critical path for the program is not merely the sum total of the project critical paths – it is also necessary to examine the dependencies between projects. Hence B is the best answer.

text: In an organizations’ portfolio, “question marks” represent the products that play in a market that has a high growth rate, but those products have a low share of the market. Following a recent portfolio review, a program manager discovered that many of the products that were being managed under her program fell under the question mark category. What would be the least appropriate strategy for the program manager with regard to these products?

choices.text: Stay invested to the extent determined by the program budget and ask for explicit management direction
Divest these products to conserve resources that can be re-deployed in products that have better prospects
Continue to exploit the revenues on these products for as long as possible while cutting costs to the extent possible
Invest in these products to realize their full potential in the market

explanation: “Question marks” is a term used in the BCG (Boston Consulting Group) matrix used for portfolio analysis. On such products, you either want to invest in them to increase the market share or divest them. Option C is more appropriate for Cash Cow products, i.e. products with a high market share and low growth rate. It may not apply in this situation.

text: Your company is participating in a highway construction program in a foreign country as a turnkey contractor. The projects are structured on a fixed price plus incentives basis. The additional incentives for completing the project early are very large as are penalties for delaying the projects. You manage the overall program, most of the work in which is done through local contractor, with whom you have signed indemnity clauses. On one day, you learn that there has been an accident at one of the construction sites where some people have been crushed under heavy machinery. What should be your immediate response?

choices.text: Issue a press note stating that the work on the site was being done under a contract, and the local contractor is liable for any damages.
Quickly research the situation, understanding that your organization may have to share responsibility for the mishap.
Make an immediate public announcement that your company will take full responsibility for any damages caused.
Appoint a legal counsel to defend your company’s personnel present on site.

explanation: Knee-jerk reaction in any form is not advisable until you can find out the facts and implications of any action, especially since you are dealing with a foreign country whose laws and social environment you may not be familiar with. You can neither reject nor accept liability until you understand the circumstances.

text: An insurance company is has started a program to revamp its portfolio of products and increase market share. An accomplished program manager who recently joined the company, has been asked to lead the program. The program has widespread support from the CEO and the senior executives. The program manager spent the next six months discussing with industry experts to put together a proposal in line with the market trends. The team worked out an aggressive launch schedule with a new brand under which the products would be sold. At the end of this period, the program manager came back to present to the executive team about the roadmap. The presentation was a disaster and angry executives stopped it mid-way saying it was completely unacceptable. What could have LIKELY gone wrong?

choices.text: The plan may not have aligned to the organization’s culture
The program manager might not have understood the insurance domain properly
The plan may not have aligned to the organization’s strategy
The market conditions might have changed

explanation: The program manager has engaged a team of experts for looking into the problem and it has only been 6 months since the plan was announced, hence A is less likely. The plan was conceived as part of a grand corporate strategy, hence B is also not likely. The program manager may have been from a different domain, but he seems to have engaged experts and consultants, hence this is not likely to be the issue either. Most likely cause might be (since most of the people working on the feasibility were either new or external to the company) that the plan did not consider the “culture” of the organization.

text: One of the statutory requirements that has surfaced recently is to adhere to a new set of emission norms. After discussing with the engineers, you feel majority of the models your company are narrowly in compliance. After studying the emission reports, you have a list of models on which work is required to comply with the new directive. This is best handled as:

choices.text: Separate projects for all the models which are still in design, modification projects for all “in-production” models
A new department should be created to ensure compliance on a regular basis
A special program initiated specifically for compliance, which will look at all the models
A separate project initiated for each model that needs a change

explanation: Compliance with the latest norms is a mandate and efforts towards this purpose can be better coordinated through a program

text: A program for drug manufacturing and research involves performing clinical trials for a product that is at an advanced stage of completion. The trials are expected to be done in India. The project manager for this project flags to you that one of the risks identified for the trials is that the drug may result in certain side-effects if administered to people who have received chicken pox vaccination before, which is a common practice in India. You decide to move the trials to UK, where another product is about to start trials and is unlikely to clash with the trials that are being planned. The risk management strategy employed here is called __________

choices.text: Accept
Avoid
Mitigate
Transfer

explanation: This action is trying to avoid the risk of side-effects, hence Avoidance is the technique used. It may be tempting to think of this as “Transfer” because the trials have been transferred from one location to another or combined with another project. But the rationale behind the shift in location needs to be considered.

text: Your organization recently went through a major portfolio reorganization exercise. Funding was pulled from many of the programs. Your program was one of the few that survived the cuts, and indeed received additional funding to add some more projects. Your organization took a policy decision to try and absorb most of the people made redundant on other programs. Accordingly, you are asked to take 10 people who used to work on an earlier program. They are located in a different city and there skills match your required skill set only to the extent of 70%. You have the option of hiring from outside. What should you do?

choices.text: Refuse the internal resources as they will not meet your programs requirements
Ask your manager to escalate this issue – it is best decided at a higher level
Agree in principle but ask your project managers to decide based strictly based on merit
Take the internal resources

explanation: This is a pretty common situation in large organizations, when funding reprioritizations happens. Internal transfers where feasible is best encouraged because it boosts the morale of everybody in the organization and spreads the impression of it being a caring organization. What you may loose due to a mismatch of skill sets can easily be recovered by greater commitment and familiarity with the organization’s culture and internal processes.

text: A program manager was working with ABC IT systems - an organization contracted to develop a set of IT systems for the customer facing services of the local municipal body. During a phase gate review, one of the members of senior management asked how the organization (ABC IT Systems) can leverage this assignment to developing marketing collateral. The program manager had no idea that this was the expectation. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: The program manager should get into discussions with the stakeholders about the expectations regarding marketing collateral and add it to the benefits register and develop a benefits realization plan
The program manager should forward the program details to the Marketing department
Tell the stakeholder that this expectation was not captured during the benefits identification stage
Initiate a component for working on this new assignment of developing marketing collateral

explanation: The program manager needs to maintain a benefits register to record the expected benefits and report to the stakeholders on the attainment of benefits (Task 6 in Benefits management from the examination content outline). Clearly one of the expected benefits (marketing collateral development) was missed out in this case and it needs to be added. After the discussions are completed, a benefits realization plan needs to be developed, which may involve adding a component or involving the Marketing function.

text: A program comprises of 5 projects all of which are inter-dependent. Due to some technical issues in project-1, the start of project-2 is delayed by about 6 months. The program manager agreed to this delay since it was unavoidable. Now, the program itself will get delayed by about 9 months as some of the complexity has spilled over into other tasks. What should be done about the schedule baseline for the program?

choices.text: It depends upon the nature of the technical issue
It should be changed to the revised schedule
This decision should be referred to the program boar
It should not be changed

explanation: As far as the program is concerned, the fact that is that the delay has occurred and the original plan failed to factor in the technical complexity. There doesn’t appear to have been any other change, hence there is not enough justification to change the baseline for the program.

text: A large construction program comprises of a number of residential and commercial projects in an integrated township. An architect who was part of the team that designed the original blue-print is a key resource who is in great demand. Several projects are starting at the same time and require his services urgently. You can sense that this is causing conflict among projects and project managers are complaining that this is delaying their projects. What is your best approach to solving this conflict?

choices.text: Call a meeting of the projects which are involved and try to arrive at the best course of action
Let the project managers negotiate among themselves and come to an agreement
Escalate the issue to senior management and ask for budget to hire more architects
Take a decision based on relative priorities of each project and communicate this to all concerned parties

explanation: Confrontation is most likely to result in a permanent resolution. Option-A may result in more skillful negotiators bullying other projects. The issue is not about hiring other architects but about this particular one. Therefore, B is not the answer. D seems appealing, but it amounts to the program manager “forcing” a decision without any discussion. While it is important to take a decision, it is also important to involve the conflicting parties in the decision – else it might actually worsen the conflict!

text: One of the important projects on a program has been lagging behind and the program manager is not happy with the project manager’s performance. The project manager was counseled in the past as well but he has shown no inclination to put in efforts to meet the overall program goals. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Set clear goals for the project manager and warn of strict action if the goals are not met
Assign a mentor for the project manager
Assign the project manager to a less important project so that the impact on the program can be minimized
Ask the program steering committee to replace the project manager

explanation: The program manager is responsible for reviewing the project manager’s performance in order to maximize their contribution to the program goals (Task 20 in life cycle management from the examination content outline). Since the project manager has already been counseled earlier and has shown no inclination to pull his weight, the program manager must take steps to replace him.

text: You conduct a weekly program review meeting where all project managers and service heads are present and provide a status of how their projects are doing, review risks and issues on the projects and any other interesting news to share. This information is helpful keep a close tab on the status of your program. Of late, you found that the attendance at this meeting is dwindling. Most of the project managers either do not attend or send a low-level representative who does not have answers to follow up questions. What could be the reason for this?

choices.text: The information at the meeting may not be of interest to everybody
Project managers are too busy – you need to look at their workload
The timing may not be suitable for everybody
You need to drive the meeting as per the agenda

explanation: Reviewing status for all projects in everybody’s presence may not be the best use of everybody’s time. Issues and information taken up at this meeting should be program-level, else people will loose interest pretty quickly.

text: All the projects in a program to produce a suite of software are dependent upon a key component that maintains the centralized database. The other projects constantly complain that the database is not stable, has several defects and causes their projects to be delayed. The project manager of the database project has in turn complained that the other projects are raising too many issues prematurely and this is affecting the morale of his team. This is an example of poor:

choices.text: Interface planning
Risk planning
Transition planning
Resource planning

explanation: Interface plan should describe how inter-project issues should be handled in detail. It looks like this interface is not defined adequately.

text: Which of the following is the LEAST appropriate task for a program manager in managing benefits from a program?

choices.text: Monitor the actual realization, compare against the projected benefits and take actions to correct any deviations
Identify synergies and efficiencies in the program to derive additional benefits and update the benefits realization plan as more benefits become apparent
Develop a benefits realization plan for the program and set up measurement criteria in order to develop a baseline and communicate with the stakeholders about benefits
Determine and change if necessary the strategic plan for the portfolio based upon the benefits expected to be realized by the program

explanation: Strategic direction of the portfolio will not be determined by the program manager. All other tasks are appropriate for the program manager to perform.

text: Sunil is a program manager for a complex program that has fifteen projects running in different continents and in a matrix organization structure. He finds that on more than one occasion, projects failed to deliver inter-mediate deliverables which other projects were expecting and were dependent on. Who is responsible for solving this problem?

choices.text: Program steering committee
Program Manager
Senior Management
The concerned project managers

explanation: It is the program manager’s job to have an interface plan that accounts for internal and external dependencies and to track issues that impact them. The program manager must perform this in coordination with the concerned project managers, but the primary responsibility is with the program manager.

text: You are the program manager for a new program and your team includes people from four countries. Most of the team members have not worked on international projects before. What is the BEST thing to ensure that cultural differences do not interfere with the program?

choices.text: Spend a little more time creating and documenting the interfaces between the projects
Create forums for cultural exchanges between the teams – like visits to other locations, speak about unique customs, cuisines, rituals, etc.
Make sure you learn few words from each language and start conversations with team members with a greeting in their local language
Create a dossier about working on cross-cultural teams and circulate it among the team

explanation: Option A does not do anything about cultural differences. B only deals with the manager’s messages, not about the others. Option C is most likely to foster greater understanding and appreciation about each other’s culture. D is a more passive and less effective way of trying to achieve the same thing.

text: During planning of the program, the program manager was thinking about rewards and recognition. The program has a large team, spread across many geographies. How should the program manager view the rewards and recognition system?

choices.text: The program needs to create as specific rewards and recognition policy for the program, though it will take guidance from the organizational policies
The program will use the performance appraisal system to determine the rewards system
Leverage the reward system currently in place throughout the company
Functional managers are primarily responsible for rewards and recognition as the team members report into the respective functions

explanation: Rewards and recognition is one of the most powerful motivators there can be and it has to be used tactfully. It can leverage organizational policies, take opinions of functional managers and also use performance appraisals as the basis, but ultimately the rewards and recognition system has to be customized for the program.

text: A large program is being initiated and the program manager is trying to assemble key members of the program team. Some of the projects in the program have a high level of technical complexity. Which of the following is the least important consideration for the program manager?

choices.text: The projects having a high technical complexity must have project managers with a technical background
Technical experts must be available to the program to address the technical complexity on some of the projects
The program manager must be supported by a team of coordinators and administrative staff in line with the size and complexity of the program
The project managers must be chosen based on their capabilities of managing complex projects

explanation: Statement A, C and D are reasonable. Statement B is of dubious validity. Technical capability of the project manager is desirable but not mandatory. Remember the project manager need not be a technical expert to be able to manage projects effectively.

text: You look after the new model development program for an automobile company. One of the statutory requirements that has surfaced recently is to adhere to a new set of emission norms. After discussing with the engineers, you feel majority of the models your company are narrowly in compliance. You have asked for emissions data for the current models. The quality analysts tells you that it will take about 2 months just to gather the data, because the monthly production for your most popular model is 200,000 units. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Outsource the inspection work to somebody who can do this sooner
Ask for the chart to be prepared based on a sample
Leave the most popular model out of the exercise for the time being
Prepare a histogram instead of a bar chart

explanation: Since you only need to get a reasonable indication of the variability, it is not necessary to inspect emission parameters on each and every unit produced.

text: A project manager of a project which is in the planning phase has flagged an issue that she is finding it difficult to define the scope of a large part of the work as a customer representative is not providing this information. How should the program manager deal with this situation?

choices.text: Escalate this issue to the program sponsor and request for his help
Ask the project manager to take this up directly with the customer representative and his manager
Ask the customer representative why he is not providing the information
Adjust the program plan to account for delay in defining the scope

explanation: A is abdicating responsibility completely, whereas B is being reactive. D might work only if the program manager somehow has a better leverage over the customer than the project manager. Hence, the best alternative is to ask for help from the sponsor.

text: All the projects in a program to produce a suite of software are dependent upon a key component that maintains the centralized database. The other projects constantly complain that the database is not stable, has several defects and causes their projects to be delayed. The project manager of the database project has in turn complained that the other projects are raising too many issues prematurely. Which of the steps below would lead to better understanding between the projects.

choices.text: Call an offsite meeting with all project managers to a resort where they can establish a rapport and get to know each other outside of work
Define the interfaces and appoint a version manager to periodically review the inter-project defects
Training the project managers on conflict management
Draw a Pareto chart to analyze root causes of the defects

explanation: A and B are good options, but they only deal with the project managers, not the core issue. C is also a good action to take, but Pareto chart does not address root causes. D is the only option that is addressing the issue squarely. Notice that the question is not about what is the best thing to do, but what is most likely to led to better understanding. Practice reading the “question” properly before jumping to an answer.

text: One of the projects in your program is a “research” project and the project manager has not been forthcoming in giving you any time estimate for this project. According to this project manager, the work required is too creative to provide you with any kind of estimate. However, there are other projects dependent on the results from this project and you need to give management a briefing containing a target date for your program. How do you break the deadlock?

choices.text: Use mathematical simulation techniques to come up with a prediction about the end date for the project
Provide the project manager a couple of weeks to conduct some experimentation and arrive at an estimate with reasonable assumptions
Send the R&D project manager on a training about project estimation
Ask this project manager to present at your management briefing to defend the absence of an end date

explanation: If the uncertainty is due to research component, some of that uncertainty can be eliminated by conducting some exploratory experiments and develop some understanding. Some time spent up-front on gaining this understanding will help in developing confidence in the technology and the estimates.

text: During a weekly program review meeting for a large construction program, you notice that one of the projects seems to have been late on deliverables for the past several weeks. The project and the overall program have a CPI of 1.1 and 1.2 respectively. The project manager clarifies the reason for the delay and promises you that he will be able to maintain the end delivery date by crashing some of the subsequent activities. What should be of utmost concern to you at this stage?

choices.text: The impact on the program cost
The likely impact of inter-mediate delays on the program schedule
The impact on the program schedule
How to represent the delay in the program status report

explanation: The project and program seem to be running under-budget so the increase in cost due to crashing may not be an issue. You will need to think about what your reports should say or what the customer might feel about the project’s progress, but even those are minor issues. What should definitely concern you is the impact on the program schedule. The project might pull back the schedule at the end, the inter-mediate deliverables might upset some of the dependencies that other projects have, so you need a full assessment of what this means to the overall program schedule.

text: One of the projects on your program has a CPI of 0.8 and jeopardizing the program budget. You meet with the project manager and discuss how to deal with this situation. Which of the following choices would DECREASE project costs?

choices.text: Delete an acceptance test from the project plan.
Move tasks B and H to occur concurrently, and take the risk of a 30% increase in the need for five more resources later.
Change task A to be completed by resource B instead of resource C. Resource B is a more experienced worker.
Change to component A from component B. Component A costs more to purchase but has a lower life-cycle cost than B.

explanation: The question asks which choice will decrease project cost. D is the only option that is guaranteed to decrease cost.

text: The goal of your program is to come up with a suite of software products that work together to provide the customers comprehensive views on their IT infrastructure. The suite comprises 15 different products, which share a common web-based dashboard and the data model. About a month from the launch, the marketing team has already started making presentations and accepting bookings for the software. At a readiness check meeting, you discover that one of the products responsible for reporting fails to function in certain conditions. The project manager tells you it would take about 6 months to fully address this issue. If you were the program manager, what would be your recommendation?

choices.text: Stick with the original launch plan and provide a special incentive for whoever solves the problem in the faulty product
Wait for the problem to be fixed – there is no point delivering a faulty product
Investigate why this problem was not detected earlier
Launch the suite after removing the suspect product from the suite

explanation: Considering that customers have already started booking the product, waiting for 6 months for the problem to be fixed seems to be an unreasonable choice. C is calling for a heroic effort on somebody’s part to reduce a 6-month fix to a 1-month fix. Even if somebody does it, you would not want to risk the entire suite on something like this because it may have other side-effects that you have no time to test or prevent. You would certainly want to find out why this wasn’t detected earlier, but that really comes after you have determined what to do about the launch first. As a program manager, your best bet is B, where you are unlocking a significant portion of the benefits to the customers by launching the suite, but refraining from releasing faulty products which might aggravate the customers.

text: In an organization, programs are mostly governed through the portfolio and the manager of the portfolio is usually the program sponsor and chairs the program steering committee. On one of the programs, the Head of the R&D function felt that the activities of the program aligned more with the R&D function and feels the program should report into the R&D unit rather than the portfolio. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Choose a structure that aligns with the activities of the program as most of the resources will be provided by the functions with which they align
Choose a structure that is consistent with the organizational requirements based on which business or function is the recipient of the benefits
Meet with the head of the R&D function and understand his position
Meet with the Portfolio manager and discuss the issue

explanation: A program manager must choose a governance structure that conforms with the organization’s governance structure and is consistent with the organization’s governance requirements. Since the portfolio is the likely recipient of the benefits delivered by the program, it makes more sense for the program to report into the portfolio.

text: Project A is part of a program. The manager of Project A is known to be quick at escalating issues. This is helpful as it raises the visibility of issues at the program level but it can also be disturbing as the program manager has to field a large number of escalations. One of the issues raised by the manager of Project A is that she is having difficulty in dealing with a senior stakeholder who keeps demanding changes and is not patient enough to wait for the change management process to work. What should the program manager do about this issue?

choices.text: Ask the project manager to deal with it as it is a project level issue
Explain to the stakeholder the change management procedures being followed on the program and why they are important
Investigate the issue and take action consistent with the program objectives
Request the program steering committee for help in dealing with the stakeholder

explanation: The program manager needs to manage the unresolved project issues in a manner that is consistent with the program objectives and benefits (Task 12 in program life cycle management in the examination content outline). The first step should be to investigate the issue and determine the way forward rather than jump to conclusions about the appropriate resolution.

text: An important product of your program includes web sites that are supposed to be localized for different languages as it has an international audience. The program is organized such that each project submits its pages to a localization team in a different location, which customizes it for different geographies. One of the pages works in English does not work when launched in Chinese text. The project manager from the localization team feels this is a development problem, whereas the development manager feels this is a localization issue. The issue has been lingering for about 4 weeks. You are approaching a major milestone. How should you resolve this conflict?

choices.text: Start daily conference calls and attend the first couple of calls yourself to push a resolution
Appoint a neutral expert to examine the issue
Use WAR room tactics till the problem is resolved
Test the page yourself and go with your gut feeling

explanation: If the issue is urgent and still has been lingering for 4 weeks, clearly there is a big gap in understanding. You need the teams to work from the same location for some time to come to a common ground.

text: Which of the following is the most appropriate statement about the program and project life cycles?

choices.text: There is no real difference, both projects and programs go through the same life-cycle of initiation, planning, executing, controlling and closing
During a program, projects get initiated and closed, hence program life-cycle is usually longer than the life-cycle of its constituent projects
Program life-cycle is nothing but the sum-total of the life-cycle of it’s projects
A project belonging to a program cannot be closed until the program actually meets the objectives, hence the duration of both life-cycles is the same

explanation: Projects get initiated during different stages in a program, hence a program usually lasts longer than the constituent projects, as stated in answer A. B is an incorrect statement, because it actually describes process groups – not life-cycle phases. C is also incorrect because programs may also comprise elements of operations and might extend beyond the life of the projects. D is incorrect because projects do get closed at different points in the program as and when the meet the requirements.

text: The customer for your program is not happy and has complained to you. One of his main concerns is that his staff is spending too much time on clarifying requirements and that multiple people from different projects are asking questions. What should you do?

choices.text: Ask the project managers that their team members should be discreet about contacting the customer
Dictate that all communication with the customer should be vetted by you before it is sent out in order to control the flow of information
Tell the customer that requirements clarification is an important step and unavoidable
Re-visit the communication plan and make changes as necessary

explanation: The reason for communication (requirements clarification) is genuine and cannot be done away with. However, option A is basically not addressing the customer concern that his team is spending too much time. Option B is not giving specific guidance to the projects other than asking them to be “discreet”. Option-D may not be a good idea as introducing another layer in requirements clarification might actually distort the message. Option-C is addressing the issue by re-visiting the communication plan to identify possible improvements. E.g. could the mode of communication be changed, are there too many channels of communication, is the communication being documented, etc.

text: A wildlife conservation program aims at increasing the population of tigers and other predators in a nature reserve. Which of the following components are least appropriate for inclusion in the program?

choices.text: Rehabilitation of inhabitants living in the core areas of the park
Construction of resorts and facillities for tourists visiting the wildlife reserves
Operational component for radio tagging predators to be able to track their movement
Development of water sources for animals in the reserve

explanation: The key benefit mentioned in the objective is increasing the population of predators. Tourist facilities do not contribute to this objective directly.

text: A program is meant to launch new products targeted at generating new revenue streams from clients that the organization hasn't targeted before. Which is NOT a good metric to include in the balanced scorecard for the program?

choices.text: Number of customers
Customer satisfaction index
Percent of market share in the target markets
Average investment per customer

explanation: C is not directly mentioned in the intended benefits of the program, hence it seems to be the least appropriate metric, though intuitively it seems to be perhaps the most important. All other metrics seem to be relevant to the market share objective.

text: Projects A and B are part of a program and are about 6 months into execution. The program manager arrives at a review meeting trying to get a status. The project manager of Project A informed that the Cost Performance Index is 0.81 and Schedule Performance Index is 1.1. The program manager would like to help the project manager address this situation. Which of the following resolutions will help achieve this?

choices.text: Ask manager of Project A to crash some of the critical path activities
Move resources from Project A to Project B for some time
Move resources from Project B to Project A for some time
Ask manager of Project A to slow down some of the non-critical activities

explanation: From the values of CPI and SPI, project A seems to be ahead of schedule but over budget. Option B best addresses this as movement of resources from Project A to Project B will reduce the cost run rate of Project A which seems to have some leeway on the time lines

text: You are in-charge of a program for a chemicals company, which has the following goals. De-bottlenecking of the refining process, reducing the emissions by 15% and improving energy efficiency of the overall factory by 25%. During the planning process, you discover that you will urgently need to put in place a welding unit in order to manage the large number of a fabrication jobs required. If this is not done in time, a number of activities on the program might get delayed. You discover that in order to achieve the 15% reduction in emissions, you need to employ a new catalytic adsorption process which will increase the cost of operations by 5% which was not envisaged earlier. What should you do?

choices.text: It does not matter: you have to do what you must to achieve the program’s goals
Ask for the details and look for alternatives to reduce the increase
Call for a meeting with the operations management to discuss this issue
Mention it in the transition plan for the program so that operations are aware of it

explanation: A 5% increase in cost in a commodity business like chemicals can be financially fatal. You can neither ignore it, nor can you hide it in a component of the program management plan that might not get read until the program is ready to go on stream. This needs to be addressed somehow, and rather than trying to do it alone, you need to involve operations management, as they are the experts in day-to-day management.

text: In your program, information is distributed according to the communications plan. Some inter-mediate deliverables on one of the projects has changed. Those changes were made according to the change control plan. One stakeholder expressed surprise to you upon being informed of a previously published change to a project deliverable. You know that all stakeholders received the communication containing notification of the change. What should you do?

choices.text: Review the communications plan to determine why the stakeholder did not understand his responsibility
Politely tell stakeholder when the information was published
Write a memo to the project manager to work this issue with the stakeholder directly
Review the communications plan and make revisions, if necessary

explanation: A does not serve any purpose – it will only antagonize the stakeholder further. D is you abdicating responsibility and asking the project manager to face the music – the project manager may feel he is being made scapegoat. C is the most appropriate as one needs to investigate why the existing communication plan did not work in this case. It does not necessarily mean that the stakeholder was irresponsible. It could be that the communication was not appropriately packaged or encoded. B is incorrect because the communication plan will not tell you why the stakeholder did not understand his responsibility

text: A program is about to start. Very few people within the organization were aware of the program as it included the development of a product line meant to be hidden from public view for some time. As the program is ready to begin, a lot more stakeholders now need to get involved and the program manager is wondering how to bring everybody up to speed with the program quickly. Which is the best mechanism for the program manager to use?

choices.text: Talk to each of the stakeholders individually in view of the confidentiality of the products
Ask the program steering committee to disseminate the necessary information about the program
Run the program on a “need-to-know” basis sharing minimal information
Conduct a kick-off meeting to bring everybody on the same page and apprise everybody about the program’s objectives and benefits to the organization

explanation: The program stakeholders need to be on-board and bought into the program. One of the best ways of doing so is by conducting a program kick-off meeting (Task 6 in Initiating section of program life-cycle management in the exam content outline). Even though some portions of the program might include some trade secrets, the stakeholders at least need to know the broad objectives and benefits that the organization can expect from it.

text: The primary responsibility of a program manager while managing change in the Program Delivery phase is:

choices.text: Making sure that change management is being followed
Being flexible and accommodating as many customer requests as possible
Delegating authority to project managers so that they can decide about changes to their own projects
Preventing unnecessary changes to the program

explanation: The best service a program manager can provide is to prevent “unnecessary” and disruptive changes from making it even before the change control board. Even the act of impact assessment and decision making diverts attention from core program work.

text: A telecommunications company has invested heavily in a program to roll out infrastructure for a new range of services that it intends to offer. The services are expected to deliver up to a billion dollars in additional revenue streams over the first few years of its launch. The program manager finds that many of the projects are reporting high cost over-runs due to increased cost of acquiring sites for putting up equipment and cabling. A phase gate review is coming up. How should the program manager present this with regard to continuation of the program?

choices.text: Add the likelihood of cost increases to the risk register and recommend that the program should be paused before the cost overruns are controlled
Present details of the increased cost and ask the program steering committee for advice on next steps
Request approval as long as the forecast benefits are still strong enough to justify additional costs
Ask the board to find ways to reduce the cost overruns

explanation: Based on the description provided, the infrastructure being rolled out is required to enable a significant new business line for the organization. As long as the benefits are still strong, the increase in cost should not be too much of a deterrent. This does not preclude exploring options or adding to the risks. But the program manager should ensure the program moves ahead and stays on course to deliver the benefits (Task 27 in program life cycle management from the examination content outline).

text: Project A and Project B both had included a risk in their risk register about the likelihood of their key technical lead leaving the organization. The lead working on Project A would like to work on cutting edge technologies and is unhappy that the work in Project A requires steadiness rather than innovation is not in his area of interest. The lead on Project B would like more stability and not comfortable with the constant switching of technical environment as B is a research project. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Talk to the project managers and explore if switching projects would help meet the aspirations of the leads
Examine the impact of the risk event on the program level objectives
Ask the project managers to switch the leads between Projects A and B
Do nothing unless the risks are escalated at the program level as the project managers need to manage the risks on their respective projects

explanation: The program manager should monitor key human resources across the program and identify opportunities to improve team motivation (Task 15 in program life cycle management in the examination content outline). Before initiating any steps, it is important to ensure that the project managers are bought into the decision as well.

text: The recent financial results of your organization were less than spectacular. The company’s products seem to be doing alright and there is demand for new products as well. However, “working capital management” is considered as a major weakness and causing delays in realizing cash flows that are urgently needed to invest into new product development. Senior management has decided to make this a major priority in the forthcoming accounting period. Which of the following measures should the program manager consider to align with the overall direction?

choices.text: Appoint more people from the projects to train salesmen so that they can sell more
Do not order material, machinery, etc. too far in advance of their use
Send some of the projects resources to customer sites so they get a better understanding of the product requirements
Resolve customer service requests quickly to improve their satisfaction level

explanation: Working capital stands for management of current assets and liabilities. It can be improved either by turning current assets into cash quickly or by delaying the liabilities as far as possible. C is the only answer that will improve the working capital situation by deferring the expenses to as late as possible.

text: A program manager is finding it difficult to cope with the workload. There are 10 projects in the program and they are located in different geographies. It consumes a lot of time to interpret and translate the reports, attend meetings, follow up on actions and issues. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Ask for more helping hands in the Program Office
Prioritize the work and focus only on the most critical projects
Reduce the extent of monitoring required from the Program Office
Take help from the Program Management Office

explanation: A program office reports to the program manager and carries out the tasks to administer and manage a program. The program manager who is struggling with the myriad tasks of managing a program should consider expanding the bandwidth of the program office.

text: Among all the activities mentioned below, which one is NOT normally used by Program Managers?

choices.text: Stakeholder analysis
Cost benefit analysis
Strategic decision making
Earned Value Management

explanation: Program managers are expected to align the programs with the strategic goals of the performing organization, but do not necessarily get involved in strategic decision making. All the others are definitely used by program managers at different stages on programs.

text: In a program, the project manager of project-1 is a X-theory manager, whereas the manager over project-2 is a Y-theory manager. The program manager himself leans towards X-theory behavior. What should be the recommended management style for the program?

choices.text: It should be X-theory because the project has been delayed already and there is no room for laxity
It should be Y-theory because a program manager should not have a micro-managing attitude
It should be X-theory because the program manager should be comfortable with the style used in the program
There is no need for having a recommended management style

explanation: The right answer is that the right management “style” is a function of individual preference and the peculiar dynamics of the team and the task it is performing.
