There is no “right” or “wrong” style, hence potentially there could be projects that require a lot of close attention and hence X-theory behavior and there could also be projects that can be handled autonomously by experts so it can be governed by Y-theory behavior.

text: You are in a phase-gate review, along with the program steering committee, the customer and the project managers. You have received formal acceptance that all the deliverables for the previous phase have been completed. You discussed lessons learnt and translated them into actions for the subsequent phased. You have the budget and resources lined up for the next phase and have the first draft of a plan. You reviewed the status of high-level risks on the program. You ended with an approval for the next phase and an informal team event. What did you miss?

choices.text: You need to have the final draft of the plan – not just the first draft.
Informal team events might not be in line with the organization’s culture
You should have reviewed alignment of the program with the organization’s strategy.
Risk response plans should have been discussed as well.

explanation: Reviewing alignment with the organization’s strategy is a mandatory topic for discussion at phase-gate reviews. The other options are valid points, but not mandatory.

text: You are managing a program that installs, commissions and operates wind turbines. The parts are manufactured in factories and sent to different project sites. Some of the parts are huge and transportation by road is a non-trivial activity. As the program manager, you would like to ensure that transportation does not hamper the schedule for the projects. Which of the following will NOT directly address transportation delays?

choices.text: Ensure that budget for transportation is provided for in the program budget
Start a new project to investigate if the parts can be manufactured and transported in parts and reassembled at the site
Use manufacturing facilities that are closest to the assembly site
Look for alternative means of transportation, such as air-lifting and dropping the parts directly at the assembly factory

explanation: B, C and D all seem options that could potentially address the transportation schedule. A is also a necessary (providing for budget), but the availability of budget at the program level does not necessarily rule out possible delays in the activity.

text: In the program management plan, you would like to document the constraints and assumptions that you have to work with. Which of the following is least likely to be a constraint for the program?

choices.text: The chief architect wants to use the latest technology that was launched last year.
There is a government restriction that all organizations employing 50 employees or more should provide for an employee union.
The customer wants to start seeing deliverables from the next quarter
Top management wants the program to cost no more than $25 million

explanation: Choice of technology is most likely to be an optional parameter. The others are more likely to be introduced as constraints.

text: Projects A and B are managed together in a program as they use shared resources and have dependencies, although they serve different customers. One of the stakeholders for Project B is concerned that the dependency on Project A may impact their deliveries. This stakeholder asked to be included in the status reporting for Project A. What is the right thing for the Project Manager of Project A to do?

choices.text: Only share the status of relevant (dependent) activities and remove any customer specific information
Discuss the request with the program manager
Refuse the request as the stakeholder is not present in the stakeholder register for Project A
Comply with the request since all the stakeholders will be included in the program level stakeholder register anyway

explanation: The management of inter-dependencies is one of the responsibilities of the program manager. As such the stakeholder of project B is not relevant for project A, but knowing that the program level stakeholders may be common, it is better that the program manager takes a call about the sharing of information across stakeholders of different components (should be part of the program level communication plan).

text: Which of the following is the most correct statement about the management reserves on projects and programs?

choices.text: The management reserves from the program must be utilized when additional risks are discovered on projects that are not provided for in the project level contingency reserves
Since the management reserve will be maintained at the program level, there is no need to maintain a separate management reserve at the project level
All projects that are part of the program must set aside some management reserves in order to cope with the risks perceived on the projects
The program manager must maintain a management reserve for the projects under the program to cope with unforeseen risks

explanation: Management reserve is a reserve set aside for “unknown unknowns”. Statement A is incorrect because the perceived risks should be covered in contingency reserves. Statement C is incorrect because if additional risks are discovered, the contingency reserves must be shored up (not deplete the management reserves). Statement D is incorrect because management reserves may be necessary both at project and program levels.

text: Your organization is experimenting with a university hiring program in which each business unit will have to induct a certain number of fresh university students into their active programs to get “on-the-job” training on skills required in the corporate world. Your program will have to take one graduate as well. Which of the following projects will you assign the graduate student?

choices.text: Project D, which is on the critical path
Project F, where there is novel technology
Project B, where there are already 2 other students
Project E which has the longest duration

explanation: The other options dont give any clue about whether or not the project is suitable for taking students on-board. The safest assumption is that the longest duration project would give the student enough time to get the required training and this project will most likely be able to spare the time to provide such training with the least possible impact on the program.

text: A large construction program has been hit hard by the increase in prices of cement and steel. The program manager has been asked to explain the impact and come up with a revised plan. What is the best way of achieving this?

choices.text: Ask each project to factor the increases into their budgets and come back with a revised baseline
Hire experts to predict the future trends and ask for a contingency reserve
Show how the increased prices have impacted the program and flag this as a major risk going forward
Meet with the project managers and experts to discuss the situation

explanation: D is the best answer because it is showing pro-activity in dealing with the situation. The increase in cost of basic inputs is a problem that affects all the projects and there has to be an institutionalized response to this. A is delegating all the responsibility to the projects, which may not be correct. B and C are both important, but it is not enough to merely increase risk and add a reserve.

text: One of the statutory requirements that has surfaced recently is to adhere to a new set of emission norms. After discussing with the engineers, you feel majority of the models your company are narrowly in compliance. As the deadline for compliance approaches, you ask that the emission test specification limits be changed to reflect the requirements of the new norms so that you are prepared in advance. This is an example of?

choices.text: Quality control
Quality assurance
Quality planning
Quality management

explanation: This is quality planning, because you are re-setting specification limits that you will measure the performance against.

text: A program has many projects which procure construction material from a supplier. In order to achieve economies of scale, the program manager has standardized the contract and negotiated special terms. One of the project managers told the program manager that he needs to change the specification of the material and deviate from the standard terms for a critical activity on his project. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Ask the project manager to discuss with the supplier if the changes can be accommodated within the existing contractual terms
Ask the Procurement department to re-negotiate the terms with the supplier
Study the impact of the changes requested and get into discussion with the supplier jointly with the project manager
Ask the project manager to stick to the agreed terms as it has been standardized

explanation:
The program manager must study the situation and be convinced that the changes are necessary and if they are, the program and project managers must both be involved in the discussions. This is because the changes may impact the standard contract as well and the relationship with the supplier must be maintained.
ContinueRetake test

text: A program consists of 5 projects. Each project has submitted budget requests including the contingency reserves. How should the program manager determine the contingency reserves required for the overall program?

choices.text: Program level contingency reserves based on analysis of program risks will be added to the project's contingency requests
Add up the contingency requirements of each project in the program
Program level contingency requirement will be less as all projects may not use their reserves at the same time
Contingencies will be maintained by the projects - the program does not need separate reserves

explanation: At a program level, you need to look at the program risks and determine the program level contingency on that basis. You also need to provide for the budgets including contingency reserves for the projects on the basis of project level risks.

text: The biggest challenge for a program manager in an organization where the portfolio is in a state of flux is:

choices.text: Maintaining conformance with the budget
Making sure the program is constantly aligned with the organization’s strategic plan
Re-validating the basis of the cost estimates and budget proposals
Ensuring that the benefit-cost analysis for the program is favorable

explanation: Of course ensuring the validity of the cost-benefit analysis, maintaining conformity with the budget and ensuring the cost estimates and budgets are based on valid assumptions is important. But when the portfolio is in a state of flux, the primary challenge becomes ensuring alignment with the strategy.

text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about programs and portfolios?

choices.text: Programs deliver strategic objectives; portfolios reflect the strategy of the organization
Program must be time-bound; portfolio may not have an explicit time dimension
Both programs and portfolios may also include operational components
Portfolio components are related to each other; program components need not be

explanation: All statements other than b are correct. Program components (by definition) must be related to each other whereas portfolio components are grouped only by the nature of investment they represent.

text: A program is being initiated. The program manager translated the program objectives and developed a program scope statement. Several projects were initiated to deliver specific benefits outlined in the program objectives. One of the key benefits was developing new revenue streams. Project A is delivering a new product that contributes to the delivery of this benefit, and Project B is responsible for creating a distribution network for this product. Who is responsible for managing the delivery of the benefit?

choices.text: The program manager
The program steering committee
The manager of Project A
The managers of Project A and B jointly

explanation: The managers of projects A and B are responsible for delivering the specific components for their projects. It is the responsibility of the program manager to integrate the deliverables and translate it into the delivery of the benefit (new revenue stream) for the organization. The program steering committee is ultimately accountable for the benefits delivery but the responsibility of managing it is with the program manager (Task 4 in Program life cycle management in the examination content outline)

text: Your program is responsible for deploying a technical solution upgrade to field offices that are spread across the country. It is a multi-phase program and specific projects are in-charge of each territory and different components of the technical solution. During one of the upgrades, there was a hurricane which caused power failures. This resulted in some critical information getting lost making it impossible to restore the system to its old state. The regional manager escalated the issue. The program manager met with the project managers and came up with several action items. Which action is most important to be tracked at the program level?

choices.text: Purchase insurance to cover for the scenario that the systems fail
Ensure that the back-out and back-up procedures are well documented and tested beforehand
Provide for a system to monitor weather forecasts so that the upgrades can be scheduled outside of the hurricane season
Ask the team to visualize other natural events that may cause similar outages and schedule the upgrades to ensure minimal damage

explanation: While all the actions are probably worth pursuing, what should be most disconcerting to the program manager is that the system did not back up important information and there was no way of backing out of an upgrade when hurricanes struck and power was lost. This points to an incomplete process and needs to be fixed.

text: A program team has analyzed the inter-dependencies among the projects and arrived at an overall program schedule.. While this is in execution, a program office member informs you that the team forgot to document a dependency between two projects. Luckily this dependency does not alter the critical path for any project nor the program. What should be the program manager's concern if at all - because of this discovery?

choices.text: The ndw dependency is likely to increase the duration of the program.
The start and finish times of some key milestones might get altered
It would add to the communication overheads and risk on the program.
There is no concern as the schedules are not impacted at all

explanation: It is already stated that the duration of the program or the projects will not increase, nor will any milestones. However, with the introduction of an additional dependency, the communication requirements and risk will definitely increase.

text: Due to a change in the governing policies, the risk exposure of the program has increased by 25%. The program contingency reserves are still just about adequate to cover the exposure. What should the program manager do to respond to this situation?

choices.text: Do nothing as long as adequate contingency reserves exist
Work with the project managers to identify risk response actions at project and program levels
Check if the increased risk levels are aligned with the organization’s risk threshold and escalate to the program steering committee if necessary
Increase the management reserves to cover the additional risk level on the program

explanation: Aligning with the risk threshold of the organization is a key task (Task-1 in the exam content outline) of program strategic alignment. Since the risk level has risen due to an external event, the program manager must examine the alignment and then escalate if necessary.

text: The governance plan for your program requires that the program manager should sign-off on project delivery before the project can be formally closed. One of the projects submitted to you for sign-off was about setting up an assembly line for automobile components. The project has a clearly defined deliverable, and the quality manager of the project has certified it meets the stated requirements and all other things seem to be in order. However, it only offers a performance guarantee of 3 defective parts per 10,000, which is much higher than your organization’s performance baseline. What should you do?

choices.text: Turn it back to the project manager for corrective action
Change the organizations performance baseline
Ask the sponsor if he is prepared to accept this quality level
Accept the project

explanation: The key statement in the question is that the project meets stated requirements. This goes to the basic definition of quality. Though your organization’s baseline may be different, it is more important to see what the project requirements state.

text: The company has just announced that there will be a major layoff in the next month, and your program has been asked to shed 15 people (out of a current strength of 60). What should be the basis for deciding who should be let go?

choices.text: Performance rating in the last appraisal cycle
The future needs of your program
The opinion of the project managers
Number of years of service in the company

explanation: All of the options are valid criteria, but ultimately you have to predict what type of resources your program will need in the future and retain those resources, even if some of them figure in the bottom 25% in performance ratings.

text: A program is at the planning stage. Many of the team members involved in the projects are new to the technical environment and are struggling with the estimation process. The program manager is concerned about the reliability of the estimates as the program schedule heavily depends on it. What is the best thing for the program manager to do?

choices.text: Borrow resources from outside the program to provide the estimates
Establish common guidelines and practices to make sure the process of estimation is standardized across the projects
Utilize the historical data available within the organization to come up with benchmarks and guidelines
Establish clear accountability for the reliability of estimates with the project managers

explanation: The estimates should ideally come from the team members who are going to work on the task. Borrowing estimates from outside the program is not going to be helpful. The difficulty with estimation is lack of expertise within the team which won’t be addressed by defining the process of estimation or by putting accountability with the project managers. The best course of action is to rely on the organization’s historical data.

text: While preparing for a program steering committee meeting, the program manager had a habit of contacting each of the board members individually to inquire if they wanted to introduce anything specific to the agenda. The program manager learned that one of the senior stakeholders who represented the interests of the end users wanted to propose several changes to the program in order to enhance its appeal to the users. The program manager was alarmed by this as this would significantly add to the duration and cost of the program, both of which are extremely tight at present. How should the program manager approach this?

choices.text: Request the stakeholder to defer the changes but make a commitment to consider them at a later stage when it was more opportune to do so
Get other stakeholders to counter these changes at the meeting by convincing them about the likely impact
Talk to the project managers and see if the changes could be accommodated within the current cost and budget
Talk to the sponsor about this and try to assess the opinion of the other board members about this

explanation: A program manager need to be open minded about changes that may result in additional benefits (even when it means additional cost and time). The program manager must first assess if the board is broadly in agreement with the proposed changes or not before taking further steps.

text: On your program, project A consumes some components delivered by project B. Project manager for project A has been escalating to you certain quality issues regarding these components for some time. Project manager for project B says her project’s deliverables are meeting the specifications given to her. What would you recommend?

choices.text: Tell the project manager of project B that project A is the customer and she should meet the specifications given by project B
Tell the project manager of project A that since B was meeting specifications, he should accept the deliverable as it is and workout a solution
Review the interface plan for the program
Ask project manager for project C to verify which of them is correct

explanation: There seems to be a mismatch of expectations between projects. The place where this should be documented is the interface plan. The other answers may be appropriate only in specific situations, but A is generally the first step of due diligence you will need to do.

text: A cell phone manufacturer is running a program to improve customer satisfaction with its products. This involves introduction of new models and features, tie-ups with leading network service providers for bouquet of offers and also improvement in the customer service for existing models, which has been a sore point with customers who complain that the service takes too long. One of the service technicians is working on forecasting techniques that determine how much stock of spares is required to support ongoing maintenance and outstanding warranties. This activity should:

choices.text: Be a separate project in the portfolio not the program
Should be part of the service department’s operations
Be part of the program
Not be included in the program

explanation: Service improvement seems to be an important benefit that the program intends to deliver; hence it seems aligned with the program. A program may include elements of ongoing operations certainly for some time. The program manager’s ability to influence technical specifications should not be the reason for including or excluding projects from programs.

text: A large construction program has been hit hard by the increase in prices of cement and steel. . Which of the following measures should the program manager be MOST interested in - for containing the impact of the cost escalation?

choices.text: A commodities trading strategy that will help the program hedge its exposure to price variations
Monitoring the usage of steel and cement on all projects to ensure that excess material is not being used
Examining the project manager’s contingency reserves and ensuring that they are adequate
Starting a new research project into a construction method that will help complete construction quickly

explanation: A is an interesting concept and it might potentially reduce the uncertainties as well, but as such it is unlikely to fructify during the life of the program. C and D should be the responsibility of the project managers. Hence B is the best option currently available to the program manager to protect the program from the variability in prices.

text: Project-A identified a risk that a new mixer it is renting is only available during limited times and if the time-window is not met, it would cause a delay and/or cost escalation. Project-B identified a risk that a senior engineer in the team is likely to quit the company is she is finding the site too long to commute. Project-C identified a risk that the paint and varnish chemicals it is planning to use may cause mildly toxic emissions which may cause the site to be shut down for a week. Project-D identified a risk that if certain technical specifications are not specified in time, the commissioning of the machines may get delayed. Which risk should you (the program manager) be most concerned about?

choices.text: Project-C
Project-D
Project-B
Project-A

explanation: A program manager should focus on risks that impact or which require action at the program level. C is closest to this description; hence it should be the one that deserves the program manager’s attention the most.

text: Which of the following statements about closure of programs correctly reflects when a program should be closed?

choices.text: Program D is being closed because most of the team members associated with the program have been let go
Program A is being closed because all the projects associated with it are completed
Program B is being closed because the program manager feels it has fulfilled its objectives in delivering benefits to the organization
Program C is being closed because the program steering committee felt the benefits forecast did not justify continued investment in the program

explanation: Decision about closure of a program ought to involve the program steering committee and the reason for closure should either be that the program has achieved its objectives (delivering benefits to the organization) or that it is no longer in a position to deliver expected benefits. Statement C most correctly reflects these.

text: A program is in the preparation stage and planning is in progress. It is an internal program for the organization meant to improve operational efficiencies and the directive from senior management is to keep a close eye on the program costs. The projects within the program have given their schedules and resource requirements to the program manager. What is the most appropriate step for the program manager at this stage?

choices.text: Figure out if there is an opportunity to crash the schedule of the projects
Find out which components can be executed in parallel to reduce the program duration
Figure out opportunities to integrate the inputs and outputs of the projects to rationalize the use of resources
Determine the benefits likely to be realized from the program vis-à-vis the cost to be incurred

explanation: Task-10 of the Exam content outline for Strategic program management says the program manager should look for opportunities to integrate the components. In this case the program budget is an issue, so all the more reason that the program manager should look for opportunities to integrate and rationalize.

text: A program has many projects. The dependencies among the projects is complex. The program is time constrained. The program’s components is also heavily dependent on vendors and the program manager is trying to standardize the procurement policies across the program. Which type of contract is least appropriate for this program?

choices.text: Revenue share
Fixed Price
Cost reimbursable
Time and Material

explanation: Fixed price contracts limit the compensation to the vendors, and in the process caps the cost for the buyer. In this case, cost is not a major consideration for the program (time is) – and hence the contract type needs to leave some flexibility for incurring additional cost to increase the speed of execution.

text: One of the projects within a program has the goal of developing a tool to automate the generate PMIS reports in order to save time. The project manager would like to develop a charter. The project manager asked the manager of the program to specify the metrics to determine the success criteria for the project. How should the program manager proceed?

choices.text: Ask the project manager to develop a detailed business case and supply estimated RoI so that the baselines can be set up
Use historical data to establish the expectations in terms of cost and time
Discuss with the program steering committee in order to come up with the measures
Specify the expectations in terms of simplification, reduction of errors and savings in terms of time and cost, so that the measures can be derived

explanation: The program manager is responsible for specifying the success criteria for the projects to effectively monitor and control the projects (Task 5 of program life cycle management from the examination content outline). In this case, this is a tool development project that is expected to bring in operational efficiencies and the program manager should be able to articulate the specific expectations from the program perspective.

text: The goal of your program is to come up with a suite of software products that work together to provide the customers comprehensive views on their IT infrastructure. The suite comprises 15 different products, which share a common web-based dashboard and the data model. About a month from the launch, the marketing team has already started making presentations and accepting bookings for the software. At a readiness check meeting, you discover that one of the products responsible for reporting fails to function in certain conditions. The project manager tells you it would take about 6 months to fully address this issue. Who is responsible for deciding the most appropriate action in this case?

choices.text: The project manager of the faulty product
The marketing department after surveying the customers about what they would prefer
The program steering committee
The program manager and the marketing department

explanation: This needs to go to the program steering committee. The project manager cannot decide about the entire program. The program manager in consultation with the marketing department might be able to make a recommendation, but really the decision needs to come from a higher authority as the stakes might be really high in this case. Surveying the customers about a product problem might actually prove counter-productive as it might dent their confidence at an early stage.

text: A project manager tells you that the quality requirements on his project are too stiff and he can only meet them up to 80%. You know that this project has a challenging technical environment which your organization doesn’t have much expertise in. What should you do?

choices.text: Call for a meeting of quality experts to brainstorm on possible means of improving the adherence to quality standards
Raise a change request to change the quality specs and approach the program steering committee
Examine the impact of the reduction in level of quality on the other projects and overall program benefits
Consider if the project can be outsourced to an organization which has the technical expertise needed to meet the quality requirements

explanation: The program manager needs to first determine if the level of quality mentioned in the project’s requirements is really needed to achieve the program’s benefits. If not, it may not be much of an issue but if it is needed (and the requirements may be restated) but if it is needed, then other measures may be necessary.

text: A program manager is working on creating and securing authorization for a Program charter. Which of the following activities make sense for the program manager to perform at this stage?

choices.text: Figure out the possible sources of funding and expectations of the people who will likely fund the program
Initiate studies to come up with high level estimates for cost and time
Perform an initial risk assessment for the program
Establish a structure for governing the program when it gets authorized

explanation: The program charter is developed using program formulation. A, C and D are performed during program formulation, but the governance structure is only determined after the program charter is authorized.

text: Midway through a program, the VP of the Information Technology department threatens to pull resources from a component of the program saying she does not agree with the program’s objectives and that it is no longer a priority for her department. You have tried to reason with her before and getting cooperation from her department has always been problematic. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Call for a meeting of all project managers to discuss what can be done under the circumstances
Note this as a program level risk and take it up at the steering committee meeting next month
Send the VP a copy of the charter which was signed off by the program steering committee and remind her of her department’s responsibilities
Inform the program steering committee and ask them for advise

explanation: The situation seems to call for a management action. This is where a program steering committee and Sponsor need to step in and protect the program. Actions A and B are definitely required, but do not address the core of the problem. Answer C is unlikely to help much, given that past attempts at reasoning with the functional head have not been useful.

text: A software development program comprises of several projects which have varying levels of complexity and duration. The program manager is very conscious of the need to achieve a high level of quality. Which quality policy can he think about imposing at the program level?

choices.text: All the deliverables on all projects will be subject to standardized acceptance tests
All project plans should follow the same template so that they can be read easily
100% of the code written should undergo code review on all projects
All projects should follow ISO 9001:2000 standards

explanation: Focus of quality management at the program level should be at imposing high-level policies that enable quality. The project-level quality planning should address what practices should be used depending upon the specific needs of the project. In this question, answer B talks about a high-level standard, this can be interpreted according to the project needs. The other options are too specific and their applicability to all projects is doubtful.

text: The program manager is about to initiate a project within the program and is working with the project manager on developing a charter. The project delivers an important product in the product suite that will be launched by the organization. The project manager thinks she would need additional help with a new technology and would like to hire team members either on full time or contract basis. The program manager had not budgeted for this and the program is tight on cost and time. How should the program manager proceed?

choices.text: Instead of hiring headcount, explore the possibility of training the existing team members on the new technology
Allow the team additional time for absorb the technology and work on the product development activities
Ask the project manager to provide detailed justification for the request and let her present to the program steering committee
Find a way to provide the necessary resources for the project by adjusting the program plan

explanation: The program manager is responsible for allocate appropriate resources to the project in order to achieve program objectives (Task 16 in Program life cycle management from the examination content outline). The project manager’s assessment has to be respected and the program manager has to find ways to reconcile the expectations from the program with the bottom-up inputs in terms of resource requirements.

text: Company A and B are both US based pharmaceutical companies. A has outsourced some research work to a biotech firm in India, and B is using contract teams in Philippines. Company A acquired company B and would like to standardize on one outsourced vendor. As a program manager in company B, what should your stand be?

choices.text: Make a visit to India to evaluate the contractor that company A is using
Come up with alternatives for contracting for the merged company
Migrate some of your projects to the India-based outsourcer and document lessons learnt
Ask your management to protect your program by retaining the services of your regular contractor

explanation: Just because company-A is the buyer, it does not mean that its contractor would automatically be retained. The outsourcing decision needs to be evaluated based on the impact of each on current projects and future strategic direction. Hence D is the best answer.

text: A program manager was working with ABC IT systems - an organization contracted to develop a set of IT systems for the customer facing services of the local municipal body. During a phase gate review, one of the members of senior management asked how the organization (ABC IT Systems) can leverage this assignment to developing marketing collateral. Which of the following would be the most meaningful metric to track attainment of the benefit of developing marketing collateral development?

choices.text: Number of new prospects identified
Number of brochures and white papers published
Number of press releases issued
Number of presentations made

explanation: The number of prospects identified is a better metric than the others because it focuses on the outcome expected from getting marketing leverage from the program.

text: A program manager is part of a matrix organization. She leads a team of project managers, all of whom belong to one or the other functions or lines of business (LoB). Whilst they are all committed to the program, they are also accountable for the projects they are performing to the functions. The program manager herself happens to be a part of one of the LoB’s, which contributes the most to the program’s budget and reports to the Director of that LoB. What is the biggest challenge that the program manager will have in this situation?

choices.text: Getting the functions to define scope of their projects
Communication across the project teams
Getting a charter for the program
Finding resources to manage the program

explanation: Communications is the biggest challenge that the program manager faces in an organization that has strong functional loyalties

text: A government owned shipyard is building a large cruise ship. This is a highly complex initiative that is expected to take up to 7 years. The ship is intended to join a fleet of other ships that serve customers in a specific geographic region. Some of the components of this task are as follows. Design and construction of the hull, design and construction of the suites and entertainment areas, building the engine and turbines, electric generator, etc. From the description provided, this seems to be an example of:

choices.text: A project with several sub-projects
A program with several projects, because all projects have a common budget
A program with several projects, because it has clearly outlined benefits
A portfolio because it addresses a niche market

explanation: A complex project can be sub-divided into several sub-projects. B is not the answer because the existence of benefits does not automatically classify this as a program. C is not the answer because a budget is divided even among sub-projects. D is not the answer because although this project may be part of a portfolio, it is not the portfolio itself.

text: In a program, it is a policy to carry out any activity that uses proprietary technology in-house, though any other activity can be outsourced. The manager of Project A - one of the projects asked the program manager to ask for permission to outsource an activity in her project, even though it used proprietary technology. Which of the following is the LEAST effective justification for approving this request?

choices.text: The organization itself is reviewing its policy of retaining the proprietary technologies
The key team members in Project A who knew the proprietary technology have left the organization
Project A is behind schedule and delays in this project will have cascading impact on other projects in the program
The activity that is being outsourced is not really core for the project and outsourcing will help the team focus on the important activities for Project A

explanation: Of all the reasons to justify deviation from policy, C is the least convincing as it shows no impact on the deliverables or the benefits

text: Project A and Project B are part of the same program. Project A’s manager states that her project is on schedule and reports the status as green. Manager of Project B states this cannot be true as his team has been delayed due to dependency on a deliverable from Project A, which is already delayed by 2 weeks. What should the program manager do at this point?

choices.text: Ask manager of project B to help project A in completing the delayed deliverable as quickly as possible
Ensure all project managers are aware of the dependencies across the program and their role in the program
Ask managers of Projects A and B to resolve the difference of opinion
Ask the manager of Project A to amend her report

explanation: The manager of Project A is reporting on-time status so she obviously doesn’t consider the deliverable to project B as a critical task. However, the deliverable is critical for project B. This indicates there is inadequate understanding and appreciation of bi-directional dependencies within the program. The program manager must take steps to correct this.

text: A is a company with a risk-taking culture that encourages individual initiative. B is a process-driven organization where deviation from the agreed upon procedure is not encouraged. The two companies merge to form a new company called AB, where A and B are run as different lines of business. A new program is started to exploit the synergies between their products and processes. Assuming that you need about equal representation from A as well as B, you want your program management plan to be:

choices.text: Very high-level, leaving the details to be determined by the project managers
Determined based on a consensus among project managers from A and B
As detailed, taking best templates available in company B
Depends upon your view of the program requirements because it is your plan

explanation: The right answer is that it depends upon the program requirements. The program management plan is the basis on which a program will be managed so it has to be customized to the program’s needs – which YOU need to decide. Leaving it to consensus or to one or the other managing style is abdicating responsibility and will likely lead to conflict later.

text: Sunil is a program manager for a complex program that has fifteen projects running in different continents and in a matrix organization structure. Which of the following is NOT a good method for communications on the program:

choices.text: A monthly review meeting where all project managers and program manager reviews the status
A weekly report that describes status of each task on the projects sent out to all team members and stakeholders
Planning summit where all project managers and program steering committee fly to one location for agreeing on a plan
Phase-gate reviews involving the program steering committee at the end of each phase on the project

explanation: A status report containing all tasks in all projects might result in information overload. All others are good ideas, worth implementing.

text: During a recent review, many project managers expressed apprehension that the currency exchange rate fluctuations may impact their budgets as most of their funding is denominated in dollars, whereas their expenses are denominated in euros. After consulting with the financial analyst, you decide on a hedging strategy using currency futures. What risk response strategy have you used?

choices.text: Mitigate probability
Mitigate impact
Avoid
Transfer

explanation: The closest answer is “avoid”, because currency futures effectively eliminates the uncertainty involved in the currency fluctuations.

text: You look after the new model development program for an automobile company. One of the statutory requirements that has surfaced recently is to adhere to a new set of emission norms. After discussing with the engineers, you feel majority of the models your company are narrowly in compliance. You have 2 years to achieve 100% compliance with the norms. What should you do first?

choices.text: Initiate a new project to modify the assembly lines of all models to achieve the norms within 2 years
Ask for a control chart that shows you the extent of the variation from the norms on all your models
Hire emission experts to advise you on the steps you need to take
See if you can get an extension to your non-compliant models

explanation: First step for you should be to find out how deviant your current models are from the norms, because all future actions will be dependent on these findings. A good way to depict this is through a control chart.

text: Your program is nearly complete. All projects but one have been formally closed and the last one is about to have a closure meeting. All of a sudden, the customer approaches the project manager demanding a major change to the scope of work. The project manager in turn escalates the matter to you. As a program manager you should:

choices.text: Inform the program steering committee, including senior management in your company and ask for their advice before proceeding
Tell the project manager you need more details about the change and a detailed impact statement before you can make a judgment
Contact the customer and ask him to initiate a new project under a new contract if he really wants the change
Advice the project manager not to accept the change as the program is finished

explanation: The impact is already known to be major and especially since it comes near the end of the program, the alternatives are limited. A management call is required here before one responds to the customer. For instance, if the customer is a ‘strategic” customer, the management may want to indulge the customer and accept the change.

text: You are running a large 5 year program, which has just entered the third year. Your organization has not done well financially and you know budgets are going to be tight in the following financial year. You anticipate that your program will have to absorb at least a 15% cut over the originally assumed budget for that financial year. What should you do?

choices.text: Look for replacing costly contractors with less costly resources
Tell all the project managers that they will need to cut 15% from their estimate
Discuss with the project and product managers to prioritize work and look for opportunities to achieve savings
Start booking expenses meant for the next year immediately – so that you can protect the program’s activities

explanation: Going through periods of tight finances is quite normal. Option-A is not a good idea as you are trying to gain something for your program at the expense of the organization. Option-B is a wrong approach, because one cannot apply the same savings to all projects. Option-D may or may not be appropriate because it might have a quality impact. The appropriate answer is C, where you will look for options to reduce costs, but not apply a peanut butter approach.

text: A program manager is reviewing the quality assurance activities that project managers plan to perform on their projects. The program involves integration of a large number of software applications to support the business of an enterprise. Which of these activities should the program manager be most concerned about?

choices.text: Projects A and B document their interface with each other in advance and plan a review
Project A has a practice of reviewing a process or design to detect possible issues in advance
Project A implements a test coverage tool that will ensure that all the logical paths in the program will be tested
Project B believes in periodic demo’s to the end-users of the system to ensure that the specifications are correct

explanation: All of the stated options are excellent examples of quality assurance activities. However, the program manager must focus on those activities that span across projects and track their progress. In this case, option-C deals with the interface between two projects, which always tends to be a grey area, and hence the program manager should be most interested in following up on that one.

text: A program manager was asked to compress the duration by about 10%. There are many projects which are inter-dependent. The duration estimates for the projects have been reviewed multiple times already and the dependencies have been analyzed to figure out the overall critical path for the program. What is the best way forward for the program manager?

choices.text: Analyze the project activities that are on the program's critical path and figure out ways to reduce their duration
Ask management to reduce the scope of the longest running projects
Push back on the demand to compress the schedule as it does not seem to be feasible
Take a fresh look at the estimates and cut the estimates for the longest running projects

explanation: The longest path across the program is the critical path. If the idea is to save time, the program manager must focus on those activities. Other options may also come into play, but the program manager must first consider what alternatives are available

text: The program you manage consists of 12 projects spread across the globe. Some of the teams are co-located and some are dispersed. Accordingly, each project has its own reporting format, resulting in you having to deal with 12 different styles of progress reports. Although it does contain all the information you need, your program office then needs to consolidate all the information into a program level report for senior management reporting. What can you do in such a situation?

choices.text: Hire an administrative assistant to work for the program office on combining and consolidating the reports
Create a web page where all projects can upload their information
Reduce the frequency of reporting so that it is easier on the program office
Create a standard reporting template and have project managers use it for reporting

explanation: The communication need of each project is unique. For example a collocated team may not need a very detailed report, whereas a dispersed team may need a detailed one. You should not force project managers to spend a lot of time on formatting their reports to your requirements or prepare another report for you. The program office should be prepared to work with diverse format – as it is much better equipped to do this.

text: You are looking after a program comprising five projects and a customer service department. You find that one of the project managers who is responsible for developing the software application is adopting unconventional means to finish the project. She has out-sourced the entire software development effort to an offshore company, reduced her team size and is focusing only on managing the validation and acceptance portion. You would not have chosen to do things this way. What should you do?

choices.text: Ask the project manager why she chose that approach
Determine if the changes impact the cost, time and quality of the deliverable
Determine if this fits into the organization’s outsourcing policy
Replace the project manager and employ somebody whose style matches yours

explanation: So long as the project is delivering what it is supposed to, you need to give project managers space to do things their own way. B and C are both sensible answers, but D is what you need to be ultimately concerned about.

text: A start-up software company is working on a program to launch a slew of products targeted at the use of next generation technologies. One of the projects relates to experimenting with a new networking protocol that has never been used on such a large scale before. Since your company does not have expertise in the area, the project manager suggests that the work should be outsourced to another vendor. Which of the following vendors is best suited for taking up this task:

choices.text: Vendor A, who is the program’s preferred vendor for all technical outsourcing projects, since it is better to centralize and consolidate suppliers
Vendor B, who has bid the lowest cost for the project
Vendor C, who has the most experience in the technology being worked on
Vendor D, who has an office in the same state, which makes it much easier to manage

explanation: Vendor consolidation, cost and location are all valid considerations in this decision. However, the rationale for outsourcing this task was technical know-how, which is addressed in C, hence that seems to be the most appropriate choice in this case.

text: A program is in the transition phase. The products created by the program will be transitioned to operations. Spares and supplies required for ongoing maintenance will have to be provided for, which requires contracts to be signed with some suppliers. How should this process be handled?

choices.text: The projects will enter into the agreements as and when they complete and are ready for transition
The program will plan for the transition and in the process will tie up these agreements
The agreements need to be determined by the Procurement department on behalf of the organization
The operations team will take over and subsequently tie up these agreements

explanation: The program is responsible not only to transition the products but to ensure that arrangements are in place for long term sustainment of the benefits (Task 13 in life cycle management – examination content outline). As the program has delivered the program, it is in the best position to plan the contracts for ongoing maintenance as well.

text: A is a company with a risk-taking culture that encourages individual initiative. B is a process-driven organization where deviation from the agreed upon procedure is not encouraged. The two companies merge to form a new company called AB, where A and B are run as different lines of business. A project manager managing people mostly from company A is complaining that her team is resisting compliance to time-reporting guidelines that are required to track program costs and accounting regulations. What should be your advice to the project manager?

choices.text: You modify the cost tracking system to use approximations because there is no point in forcing people to comply with the guidelines they are not used to
You should ask a project manager from company B, who is known to be a hard task-master to take over that team
You tell the project manager that you can help her communicate the message, but in the end it is her problem to solve and that you will hold her accountable for providing accurate time-reporting
You should require the project manager to complete everybody’s timecards in case the team does not want to

explanation: The operative word in the question is “accounting regulations”. Certain things are non-negotiable; accounting regulations being one of them. The project manager involved must bite the bullet and get the team to comply. You can help communicate the policy and rationale if required, but ultimately it just has to be done!

text: After a program review meeting, one of your project managers (say B) asks to talk to you one-on-one. His issue is that another project manager in the program (say A) has been consistently reporting an “on-time” status when he knows that her project is lagging behind. He has it from authentic sources that several tasks on the project are not progressing as per plan. He says it is unethical for somebody to report an incorrect status and that you need to take some action. What would you do?

choices.text: Ask B to work with A to sort out the issue and then report back to you
Issue a memo to A and ask her why her status reports are not reflecting reality.
Ask B to back off since he should really be focusing on his own project
Tell B to calm down and watch the behavior for a few more weeks before forming an opinion.

explanation: First of all, it is important to understand that a project can be on schedule even if a few of the tasks are behind schedule. So answer B is ruled out until you can establish that the reports were indeed inaccurate. Answer A is a bad option because you will be deemed as unresponsive to escalations. C is just deferring the issue which may actually let this feeling fester and gain strength. D is a good option because it is addressing the issue squarely and putting the onus on B to work it out.

text: A program comprises of several projects. Project A has exceeded the permitted threshold for defects on several occasions. Project B is one of the consumers of A’s product and as a result of the defects they have missed some intermediate deadlines. What action should the program manager take?

choices.text: Direct the manager of Project A to come back with a plan to fix the defects and avoid exceeding the threshold in the future
Work with the manager of Project B to pull back the schedule to minimize the impact on the program schedule
Revise the schedule based on the forecast and modify the schedule baseline
Investigate why Project A has missed on the quality specifications and advise about corrective actions

explanation: Adhering to the project’s quality specifications and sticking to the allowable thresholds is the responsibility of the project manager and the program manager must hold the project manager accountable for this (Task 4 in program life cycle management in the examination content outline)

text: In a program, one of the project manager proposes a change in the technical specification for an inter-mediate deliverable that is required to be able to deliver the project on time. The deliverable is required by another project which has already started with the original specifications in mind. Who needs to be involved in the first meeting to decide if this change should go ahead?

choices.text: The program manager, the concerned project managers and technical experts about the deliverable in question
The Program steering committee, the Program Manager and the concerned project managers
The customer, Program Manager and the concerned project managers
The Program steering committee, Program Manager, all the Project Managers

explanation: The extent of the impact needs to be assessed before it can be determined the level to which the change needs to be escalated (customer, program steering committee, etc.), which is best accomplished by a meeting between the participants mentioned in answer D.

text: You identified several stakeholders for your program. Which of the following should you be LEAST concerned from a program communication perspective?

choices.text: An environmentalist pressure group which voiced concerns about some of the projects that are located in eco-sensitive zones
The manager of the portfolio, who is primarily interested in the outcomes, not much concerned about the details
An executive within another department in the customer organization who is not directly involved with the program but perceives that his team might be impacted by the program
A highly skilled project manager, who is well on top of the tasks on his project and is capable of working with minimal direction

explanation: Though the resistance of the first mentioned first stakeholder mentioned does need to be contained, they do not have much legitimacy to be involved in the program and primarily have nuisance value. It can be contained using many means and the program does not necessarily need to spend a lot of time communicating with them.

text: A project manager has just reported that there has been a 2-month delay in his project. This delay will not affect the program’s overall schedule or the delivery of the intended benefits. The program has high visibility in the organization and senior executives are closely monitoring it. The project manager further requests that if he is allowed to incur an additional expense of $200000, the delay can be overcome by involving additional resources and machinery. The project manager is concerned about the impact of the delay on his performance appraisal and future career opportunities. The CPI for the program is 1.2. What would be your response?

choices.text: You inform the project manager that you will not support the proposal.
You deny the request to spend more money, but help the project manager on his performance rating.
You agree to spend more money to get the project back on time.
You decide to consult with the program steering committee and take their opinion.

explanation: From the program point of view, there is no case for spending more money – having a cost buffer (CPI > 1) is no reason to be profligate in spending. Since the issue is about how to use program reserves, there seems to be no need to escalate to the program steering committee. You need to first understand the causes of the delay in the project first, before agreeing to help on the performance review.

text: All the following statements about the difference in change management at the program level and at the level of its constituent projects are correct EXCEPT?

choices.text: Changes in a program affect all projects, whereas changes in projects do not affect others
Participants in change control board at a program level are typically at a higher level in the organization structure than project change control board
Change requests can get escalated from project to program level
Project change management is about the impact on the triple constraint, whereas at a program level, the emphasis on the program’s benefits

explanation: D is a suspect statement, because a change to a program does not always affect all the constituent projects. Further, a change to a project may also affect other projects directly or indirectly.

text: During risk planning, the team working on project A could not come up with an effective way to mitigate or insure against a risk. It is not a task that could be outsourced, nor could it be deleted. The project is an important component of a program and the program manager is involved in the risk planning. What would be the BEST solution?

choices.text: Accept the risk and add appropriate contingency reserve at the project level
Accept the risk and the program should provide for contingency reserve in case the event occurs
The project team should be directed to continue to look for ways to avoid, transfer or mitigate the risk
Add to the management reserve at the program level which can provide for events of this type

explanation: From the description provided, it seems that the only option open is to accept the risk. When you decide to accept a risk, appropriate contingency needs to be provided. Since this is a project level risk, the contingency reserve needs to be at the project level. Remember contingency reserves are maintained both at project and program level depending upon the nature of the risk.

text: XYZ engineering is an oil exploration company. An important program of this company involves drilling 40 offshore wells in a promising area. Each well site is unique hence each is a project in its own right. The program has been in execution for the past several years. 5 out of the 40 wells struck oil or gas that is commercially exploitable. After completing the survey and assessment, those have been handed over to the production team for further development. In documenting lessons learnt for this program, which of the following would NOT be relevant data or information in determining success:

choices.text: Results from safety audit –safety metrics for the program
Description of capabilities added in terms of experience with offshore drilling
A cost-benefit analysis summarizing the total cost incurred on the program, compared against the expected benefits from commercial exploitation
A cost-benefit analysis that compares the total cost incurred on the program against the approved budget

explanation: A and B are relevant to the program’s objectives and benefits. C is relevant to safety considerations which is an implicit expectation from the program. D is not a good statement. Comparison of costs incurred with the original budget is not really cost-benefit analysis. Further, in a program with an uncertain outcome, it is better to compare costs with the intended benefits that the program has delivered. This is an example of how a program manager has to look beyond the immediate cost-time-scope constraints.

text: Your organization, which is into online gaming, surveyed customers of the products of your program and the results were not good. All your products fared poorly on certain parameters. Some of the products were not visually appealing to all customer segments, some of them had content which was inappropriate for children and the website which hosted the games frequently crashed. You gather the project managers together to discuss the findings and decide on corrective actions. Which is the best course of action among the following?

choices.text: You initiate a deeper analysis by asking the survey responders the reasoning behind their feedback.
You own responsibility for the poor survey scores and quit.
You ask the project managers to investigate the observations and come up with a plan.
You initiate a “quality improvement project” with a manager reporting to you. This manager will be responsible for managing changes to all projects as per the survey results.

explanation: In this case, there seem to be different things that are problematic with the products. While content is the problem in some cases, the problem is with the visual impact in others. The feedback in such cases is best handled by the project it pertains to, rather than as a common initiative. Quitting does not solve the problem, which you must honestly attempt to do. While some respondents to surveys may be willing to get into more details, most would get put off if you keep going back to them for feedback.

text: A large program planned to last for the next 5 years, comprising of 25 projects having a total staff of over 1000 in 5 countries is in the planning stage and you are preparing the program WBS. To what level should you decompose to arrive at a satisfactory PWBS?

choices.text: Up to one level below the project
Up to the level of control you need to have
Up to the project level – 25 program packages is complex enough to manage
It is up to the project managers to decide

explanation: PWBS is decomposed up to the level of control that you desire to have. It is a program decision, not a project decision. The project managers manage to their project’s WBS

text: A program manager who was newly promoted into the role relies a lot on the program management office for support. Which of the following is the LEAST appropriate request to make of the PMO?

choices.text: Mentoring and coaching for the project managers working on the various components
Reviewing the program level risk management and risk response plans
Provide guidelines and templates for preparing stakeholder register and stakeholder engagement plans
Advising whether a project with a significant investment requirement should be initiated or not

explanation: PMO is an organization-wide body that governs program management practices. Action C truly should be decided by the program steering committee. Other requests can be addressed by the PMO.

text: The program you are working on is being held up due to one project on which several other projects are dependent. This project has been poorly estimated and poorly executed so far. You have reviewed the situation with the project manager and discovered it will take at least 6 months to complete. You know that any delay beyond 3 months would certainly delay the program which would really upset the customer. How will you handle this situation?

choices.text: Get the affected projects to contribute one staff member each to help the troubled project catch up
Tell the project manager his job is on the line if it is not done in 3 months
Discuss possible remedial measures with the project managers but inform the program steering committee of a likely delay
Announce all-expenses paid holiday for all the team members if they finish it in 3 months

explanation: A, B and C are all possible measures, though A is trying to use penal power which almost never works. The amount of reduction required is over 50%, which is always going to be challenging. D is the most complete answer because it does not pre-suppose what might be the possible remedy and it also is trying to be realistic about the outcome

text: During a weekly program review meeting for a large construction program, you notice that one of the projects seems to have been late on deliverables for the past several weeks. The project and the overall program have a CPI of 1.1 and 1.2 respectively. What is the LEAST likely cause of this delay?

choices.text: A concrete mixer was not made available to the project on time
There was a change in the structural design to accommodate for an additional floor that was sanctioned at the last minute
The concrete took 1 month for curing, before which the subsequent activities could not be started
A supervisor went on unscheduled leave for 1 month

explanation: All are likely causes, but C is the least likely because the fact that concrete takes a certain amount of time for curing should have been known up-front and planned for.

text: The HR department in an organization was running an initiative to start 360 degree appraisals for all first level managers, which applies to all the project managers in your program. The team members are in favour of the idea but the project managers are not sure. What should be done aboout the adoption of this technique?

choices.text: Do an anonymous survey instead of a 360-degree appraisal.
Ask the HR department in your company for guidance.
Go ahead because most of the team members want it.
Do not introduce it until the project managers are convinced.

explanation: The process of getting feedback is valuable, but the onus of taking action is on the individuals. If the project managers (who will be the recipient of most of the feedback) are not receptive, it will be a pointless exercise. If action is not taken on the feedback, team members will also turn skeptical which will be a bigger loss for the program.

text: One of the engineers working on your program is the most technically skilled team member. At least three projects want him to be working their teams full-time and the allocation of this engineer has always been an issue. It has become so bad that this issue was escalated to the program steering committee, which has asked you to decide on this issue. What should you do?

choices.text: Ask him to divide his time among the three projects until a solution can be found
Ask the engineer where he wants to be and assign accordingly
Assign him to projects which are on the critical path
Create a separate engineering consultancy project on your program led by this engineer, who will report directly to you

explanation: In the long run, you have to take care of your precious resources and abide by their wishes. If you fail to do so, your organization may loose him altogether.

text: A program commissioned to deliver a product suite. The project managers feel that they are ready to launch the products within the next 2 months. But it is learned that the accessories and spares necessary for maintenance will not be ready for another 6 months. Marketing wants you to launch the model as soon as possible because it is important to position it in the market, whereas the service department is adamant it will not support the products unless availability of spares is guaranteed. What should you do in this situation?

choices.text: Launch the product with a disclaimer that service for the new model will not be available for 6 months
Go with Support. There is no point launching a product that cannot be serviced or supported
Try to accelerate development of the accessories and spares project, and approach the program steering committee for a decision
Go with Marketing. It is unlikely that new phones will require service in the immediate future anyway

explanation: Option A is risky given the service history of the organization and the fact that it has been a problem for customers in the past. Option C is unlikely to fly – customers may be put off by such a disclaimer. Options D is a better answer than B, because the program manager is trying to take some pro-active action to solve the problem and involving the program steering committee in the decision.

text: A new program within a startup organization is being funded by a venture capital organization. The program aims to come up with a new business model based upon new algorithms and mobile apps that support them. The funding agency has limited experience in the technology being used but is convinced about the overall idea. There are many possible scenarios and parameters that would impact the ultimate realization of benefits from the program. What is the best way for the program sponsor and funding agencies to forecast the benefits and determine the level of investment that is appropriate?

choices.text: Commission a survey of users to determine possible size of the market
Rely on the estimates that the startup company has come up with
Use what-if scenario analysis and simulations to develop an initial estimate and monitor as data becomes available
Consult experts in the area

explanation: The program manager needs to continuously monitor the benefit metrics using what-if scenarios and simulations if necessary (Task 4 of benefits management in the examination content outline). The funding agency needs to work with the program manager to determine the benefits forecast to accordingly decide the level of investment.

text: A program is very high priority and has very high visibility in the organization. The steering committee wants to meet every other week to get an update and a phase gate review every other month. Which of the following is the least relevant agenda for the phase gate reviews for this program?

choices.text: Review of status of projects in the program, benefits realized from transitioned projects, readiness for the next stage
Review alignment to strategy, feedback from key stakeholders, update on key activities in the past stage, readiness for the next stage
Review of actual vs. planned performance on key program parameters, readiness for the next phase, review of overall risk level
Review delivery of benefits vs. plan, key milestones in the program roadmap, any escalated issues

explanation: Review of projects within the program need not be a topic of interest for the program steering committee. Project level oversight needs to be provided by the program manager. Most of the other items are relevant and can be included in the agenda depending upon the situation and management focus in a particular period.

text: A program is meant to launch new products targeted at generating new revenue streams from clients that the organization hasn't targeted before. One of the challenges for the initial team was to decide upon which products might best meet expectations of potential customers. What decision making technique would be most appropriate for this?

choices.text: Majority
Consensus
Management decision
Refer to sub-committee

explanation: Since it is a team of experts we are talking about, reaching a consensus is a near impossibility. Also since the program manager himself is not an industry expert, management decision might not be appropriate. Further delegating to another sub-committee seems pointless as the expert committee is itself a sub-committee. Hence the best choice might be to go by the majority view.

text: You are a program manager for one of the programs that is part of a portfolio. You have just emailed your weekly report where you flagged a risk of missing an important milestone on the program due to a delay in an external dependency. The portfolio manager is upset with this. He calls you and asks you to delete that reference from your report. He argues that sending this report to all the stakeholders will raise unnecessary alarms and uncomfortable questions. Instead, it is better to sort out the dependency and try to reduce the delay. What should you do?

choices.text: Delete the reference but also send a mail to the customer so that he is aware of the likely delay.
Tell the portfolio manager you are working on the issue, but that it is advisable that the report should be factually correct
Escalate this to the program director.
Delete the reference and work to reduce the delays

explanation: It does not matter how it will look – the risk of a significant delay has to be flagged as soon as possible. Hiding it is only going to be counter-productive. If the pressure persists, you may consider escalating the matter beyond the program manager, but as a first step you must be prepared to defend an assessment you have made. This is also an ethical responsibility question under the covers.

text: A company is at a critical stage in a portfolio review and the business environment is highly dynamic. The allocation of funds to different portfolios is likely to undergo significant changes. How does the organization determine the funding for different programs for the forthcoming financial period?

choices.text: Each program may have to justify allocations based on proposed revisions to the portfolio
Provide for an interim budget on a month by month basis for the time being
Determine the allocation based on last year’s baselines and the changes forecast in the forthcoming period
Review the business cases for each program and determine the allocations based on the funding patterns mentioned in the program roadmap

explanation: Since the portfolio is being revised significantly, the organization needs to re-baseline their allocations in line with the revised strategy. Remember that program managers are expected to be familiar with many more “general management” terms than project managers and this is especially true of management of budgeting and finances.

text: You are trying to come up with a cost baseline for the program. You had the project cost estimates reviewed through experts. You verified the cost for all projects using both top-down and bottom-up techniques and reconciled the differences. You also considered the costs of transitioning projects to the operational units as well as the cost of sustaining the program’s operations. What was the most glaring omission in this process?

choices.text: You should have used product life-cycle costs, not project costs
Contingency was not included in the estimates
It is important to first calculate NPV to come up with a cost baseline
You did not use earned value techniques

explanation: Option-A is incorrect, because your program cost need not include the entire life-cycle cost of its products. Earned value comes into picture only after a cost baseline is arrived at, hence option-B is not correct. Option-D is also incorrect as NPV can only be estimated once the cost estimate is in place. Hence option-C is the best option as contingency reserves need to be considered in the cost estimates.

text: As part of your program, you have just received approval for constructing a new paint mixing factory at a cost of $1.5 million. The cost is inclusive of construction, machinery, contracts for building and commissioning. The work is expected to be completed in this financial year itself although some of the payments may actually be made next year as your company will avail of the credit period. You want to give your company’s financial analyst a “heads-up” about this. Which of the following statements would be the most accurate?
