choices.text: The new factory will create liabilities worth more than $1.5 million (due to interest payments on loans taken)
This factory will have no impact on the P&L account of the company
Your company’s profits for the current year will be less by a certain amount, which depends upon how many of the payments can be deferred into the next fiscal year
Your company’s profits for the current year will be less by $1.5 million due to the expense on the new factory

explanation: The most correct statement is B, as the factory will create a capital asset, which will reflect on the assets side of the balance sheet.

text: A program manager has been appointed to oversee an ambitious product development initiative in an organization. The products envisaged, technology and domain are new to the organization. In the initiation of the program, what should be the most important concern for the program manager?

choices.text: Developing an elevating and purposeful mission statement for the program
Finding the right team for the program office to help him manage the program
Developing a water tight business case considering the market space and the benefits forecast
Establishing the feasibility of the program, assessing the capability of the organization to execute it

explanation: From the given description, the program and the domain are new to the organization and hence the program manager must pay attention to feasibility especially in terms of the ability of the organization to execute the program (Task 5 in the exam content outline)

text: Project A was merged with a running program based on the recommendations of the program steering committee. Project A has a different time reporting system than the rest of the program. Time sheet reports form an important part of cost management for the overall program. What is the best course of action for the program manager?

choices.text: Leave the time reporting systems intact
Move project A to the program wide time reporting system
Modify the costing tool to merge the data from the different reporting systems
Ask the program office to manually combine the cost reports from the two systems

explanation: The program manager needs to make sure that the PMIS aligns with the information needs of the program and if time and cost data is critical – then the inputs must be standardized (task 11 of the exam content outline in program life cycle management)

text: A project manager has just reported that there has been a 2-month delay in his project. This delay will not affect the program’s overall schedule or the delivery of the intended benefits. The program has high visibility in the organization and senior executives are closely monitoring it. What is the right action at the program level?

choices.text: Increase the risk level on the program but maintain the “on-time” overall status
Participate in the “lessons learnt” meeting of the project and document the root causes of the delay
Escalate the delay to the executive level
Hide the delay in the program buffers

explanation: The delay can be absorbed in the program, so the action mentioned in A is not required. B is not appropriate as there is no need to “hide” the delay. C seems appropriate, because any time there is a delay in a component deliverable, the risk level goes up. D represents an action which is more appropriate for the project manager.

text: The budget for a program has shrunk nearly 50% in the current year due to an economic downturn and money is hard to come by. The program manager is forced to re-visit budgetary allocations for each of its components. The program manager has asked all of the project managers for ideas around cost reduction. Which of the following makes the LEAST sense?

choices.text: Manager for Project A, which has just started proposes to delay some of the non-critical activities so they can be taken up in the subsequent financial year
Manager for Component D, which focuses on operations and support for existing product lines proposes to outsource some of its work to a supplier in a low cost environment
Manager for Project B, which began a year ago proposes to wind up the project as its deliverables are no longer relevant to the strategic plan
Manager for Project C, which is nearly complete proposes to delay transition and closure activities as the budget for training operations staff has shrunk

explanation: As the program is constrained on cost, the measures must address the financial stress being faced. At a time like this, the program must focuses on revenue generating and cost reducing activities. As project C is complete, it is surprising that it wants to delay the transition. Transition a completed project gives rise to the possibility for the organization to start realizing the benefits from the project early. If anything, the program should try to accelerate the transition of projects that are near completion.

text: During a program review meeting, a program manager learns that the schedule for one of the project seems to have been changed, causing an impact on other projects. On further investigation, the project manager tells you that the change was requested by one of the end-users and approved by her manager. This is a matter of concern for the program manager because:

choices.text: The customer may not pay for the change
The impact of the change on other projects does not seem to have been considered
Program sponsor has not been informed about it
It is the program manager's duty to prevent changes on the program

explanation: A and C are not obvious from the statements made in the question. D is an incorrect statement, because a program manager should not simply refuse changes. B is an important concern because you know at least some of the impacted projects do not seem to have been made aware. So there is a process issue you need to tackle first, before looking into A or C.

text: A scientist in a research program came up with an idea for a new product line with significant market potential. A program manager associated with the R&D unit was asked to help refine the idea for further evaluation. What is the most appropriate thing for the program manager to do?

choices.text: Work with the scientist to identify potential benefits to the organization and work on a high level cost-benefit analysis
Ask the scientist to conduct further studies and get a more detailed scope statement
Get some estimates and prepare a tentative program schedule with milestones
Identify resource requirements and examine how the program can gain efficiencies to deliver additional benefits and control

explanation: The idea has just been floated and the program is still in the formulation phase. Tasks B, C and D are more appropriate during the preparation (planning) stage. The initial task should be to identify the potential benefits and conduct a preliminary cost-benefit analysis (Task 6 of the examination content outline).

text: A program has been initiated for expansion and de-bottlenecking of a chemical factory. The location of the factory is likely to be declared as an eco-sensitive zone by the government. This might impact some of the components of the program. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Add a risk to the program risk register
Recommend the shifting of the program to a less sensitive zone
Ask the project managers of the impacted components to submit change requests for responding to the changed business environment
Study the impact on the program and discuss the changes with the program steering committee

explanation: The program manager should focus on the program level impact and start discussing with the program steering committee. Although the event has not yet occurred, it is likely to have a significant impact on the program objectives, and hence the strategic alignment has to be re-verified (Task-8 in strategic program management).

text: You have just completed the initiation processes of a small program and are moving into the planning stage when a stakeholder asks you for the program's budget and cost baseline. What should you tell her?

choices.text: There is no need to baseline the cost and budget as this is a small program.
The program budget and baseline will not be finalized and accepted until planning is completed.
The program budget can be found in the charter, which has just been completed.
It is impossible to complete an estimate before the program management plan is created.

explanation: The baseline cannot be finalized until the planning is completed. All other statements are incorrect.

text: The program manager has received project schedules from the project managers. She now understands the delivery dates and key milestones of all the projects. What else must be done for her to come up with the program roadmap that can be taken to the program steering committee for approval?

choices.text: Provide feeding buffers for all the dependencies to establish the critical chain
Perform leveling of resources so that the optimal utilization of resources across the board can be achieved
Compress the schedules of the projects to the extent possible for early realization of benefits
Translate the delivery dates into milestone for realization of benefits

explanation: For validating the roadmap with the program steering committee, the deliverables have to be translated in terms of realization of benefits, so that the program steering committee stakeholders can relate to it. All other options talk about mechanical steps that must be done to make a realistic roadmap, but do not contribute to the step mentioned.

text: A program manager is trying to decide on an escalated issue. Project A is responsible for integrating the output of Project B with the output of Project A and perform integration tests. Manager of Project A feels that integration testing should happen before the system is handed over, whereas Manager of Project B feels that the responsibility of integration testing should be with Project A after B has delivered the output. What is the most logical statement for the program manager to make in trying to resolve the conflict?

choices.text: Project B’s approach makes sense. They are responsible for delivering the output and Project A needs to proceed with the integration
Let Projects A and B focus on their own deliverables and let us make another project responsible for integration
Project A’s approach makes more sense. Integration is not just the responsibility of Project A but both teams jointly
It is up to Projects A and B to figure out the sequence. From a program standpoint, the systems should work well together. Let me know if you need any help

explanation: While the program manager may have his own views about this, he should leave the details of the solution to the projects and focus on the outcome. This gives a clear message to the projects that they need to work together and not in silos.

text: A program manager was identifying the stakeholders for a program. One of the important stakeholders is a senior user representative in the customer organization. She is considered influential and well connected within her organization and her opinion is valued by many. How should the program manager go about stakeholder analysis?

choices.text: Conduct personal interviews, review the role descriptions and publicly available information about this stakeholder
Understand the likes and dislikes about the stakeholder and try to make a good first impression
Find out who can counter-balance her influence on the outcomes and can be a point of escalation in case she comes out against the program
Use personal networks to gather insights and inside information into the stakeholder’s influence

explanation: The program manager is responsible for conducting stakeholder analysis through historical analysis, personal experience, knowledge base, etc. (Task 2 in stakeholder management from the examination content outline). While doing this, professional behavior and decorum must be maintained. While it is necessary to make a good impression and understand likes and dislikes – stakeholder analysis primarily should revolve around expectations from the program.

text: Engineers working on a program team are getting frustrated that they are getting directions from too many people. This includes their project managers, marketing, customer support and sometimes directly from senior management in escalated cases. Which of the following BEST solves the issue of conflicting instructions?

choices.text: Dictate that only project managers can give directions to the team – everybody else can only request the project managers.
Centralize the work authorization and allocation system with the program office.
Review the program and project plans to ensure that it reflects everybody’s requirements and ask that everybody follow the plan.
Train the engineers on “conflict management” techniques, because there is no easy answer to this situation.

explanation: The program office should not set up the work allocation system because it would subvert the authority of the project managers. The project managers are obviously finding it difficult to control flow of instructions so re-directing the issue to them is not a good resolution. Engineer’s expectation to have clear directions is quite reasonable. Sending them to conflict management classes may be a good thing, but it does not address this need. C is the most reasonable answer. The reason why there are conflicting instructions is perhaps that the plans do not account for all the work that engineers are supposed to do. It needs to be reviewed to ensure that there is a fair allocation of their time.

text: A program comprises of 5 projects all of which are inter-dependent. Due to some technical issues in project-1, the start of project-2 is delayed by about 6 months. The program manager agreed to this delay since it was unavoidable. What should be done about the schedule baselines for the project-2?

choices.text: It should not be changed
It depends upon the nature of the technical issue
It should be changed to reflect the revised schedule
This decision should be referred to the program steering committee

explanation: As far as project-2 is concerned, the delayed start is an unavoidable circumstance, which had nothing to do with the project per se hence it cannot be held to the original baselines. It would be an overkill to have the program steering committee rule on this and really the details of the technical issues in project-1 are irrelevant in this case.

text: A program manager is managing a large program being conducted across multiple geographies. The program management plan is being prepared and some of the projects are also in detailed planning. The project managers of projects A sent a detailed schedule for his project, whereas manager of project B sent only a list of high level milestones. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Ask the manager of project B to send a detailed version of his plan including an elaborate schedule
Provide the project managers guidance in terms of content and level of detail expected based on the requirements of the program
Ask the manager of project A to send a summary version of his project after stripping out all the details
Ask the PMO to provide a template for the schedule that can be followed by all of the projects

explanation: The program manager needs to establish guidelines to standardize the content and level of detail on the plans. Task 9 in Planning (Program life cycle management) from the exam content outline. The guidelines need to be based on the size and complexity of the program and the amount of detail that the program manager needs to get into.

text: One of the projects in a productivity improvement program for a car manufacturing factory comprises of a project to improve the level of automation in the painting jobs. The project is nearing completion and the program manager is about to approve the plans to implement it along with the factory manager and supervisor. The transition activity requires training of about 200 factory workers. How should the cost of this activity be budgeted for?

choices.text: Program should budget for it under the transition activity
Raising a change request and taking approval from the program steering committee
From the operational budget of the factory
Charge to organizational training budget

explanation: Transition of the program’s deliverables and providing for their sustenance is part of program closure and should be budgeted within the program.

text: One of the stakeholders for a program expects that the program will deliver a new revenue stream for the organization. Another stakeholder expects improvement in margins by reduction in cost. Another stakeholder expects reduction in number of errors and another expects improvement in customer satisfaction. Which of the following represents the best set of measurement criteria given this information?

choices.text: Incremental Revenues, Gross profit margin, Defects found, Number of customers added
Total Revenues, Profit margin, Defects/Month, Customer Satisfaction
Incremental revenues, Earning/Expense ratio, Defects/month, Customer Satisfaction Score
Incremental Revenues, Profit, Defect density, Net promoter score

explanation: The best measure for the first benefit is incremental revenues because the program is expected to add NEW revenue stream, The best measure for the second is earnings/expense ratio because the improvement in margins is expected to come through reduction in cost. The best measure for the third is Defects/month because it will indicate if the errors were reduced or not. The best measure for the third is some kind of a customer satisfaction score as the program is supposed to improve it.

text: A program is tight on costs and the program manager would like to instill discipline in terms of cost management across projects. During the definition of cost tracking mechanism, a challenge has come up. There are many shared resources like a test lab that are used by multiple projects and this is a significant component of the overall project and program cost. The program manager is wondering how to allocate the costs of the shared resources to different projects. Which of the following is the most reasonable way forward?

choices.text: Use a mechanism like activity-based-costing to apportion the cost of the resources to projects based upon the level of usage
Use the notion of accelerated depreciation to estimate the cost of resources used
Leave the shared resources at the program level and have the program budget pick up the cost
Implement a pricing mechanism for the shared resources and track the costs on a T&M basis

explanation: Activity-based costing is a well established mechanism to allocate the shared costs and overheads. It is a more logical mechanism than a simple T&M basis (Option D) because it determines the allocation based on activities not merely time. It is not a good idea to leave all the shared costs at the program level as these costs represent a significant proportion of the overall cost and it may be important for the program manager to come up with a more granular distribution.

text: What kind of risks are least appropriate for inclusion in the program level risk register?

choices.text: Risks related to the interfaces between the projects
Risks identified on projects within the program that can have a common mitigating action
Risks identified on projects within the program that affect multiple projects
Risks identified on projects that have a high level of urgency

explanation: The program manager should be focused on risks that impact more than one project and on risks that require a program-level response (shared mitigation actions). Risks related to interfaces may also be candidate for inclusion in the program risk register. Project risks should not be escalated to the program level merely because of higher level of urgency

text: Your overall program was budgeted at $2 million, but now has a CPI of 0.8 and one of your challenges is to ensure budget availability to all projects. At this time, you learn that one of the projects in your program is likely to finish under-budget by about $20,000. It turns out that the project which was under-budget was also behind schedule. What might be the reason a project might be under-budget but behind schedule?

choices.text: An unplanned risk event happened, which caused it to implement a costly workaround
Some tasks have been removed from scope with prior approval from the change control board.
Some tasks have been delayed due to which they are not taken up yet.
The project out-sourced the entire work to a group of highly skilled consultants.

explanation: If some tasks get delayed, you might have a situation where the cost involved are not spent yet, causing costs to be under-budget. In scenario B, the reduction in scope has occurred through change control, and it is more likely that the baseline would have been changed. C might actually cause a project to be ahead of schedule and over-budget, and D involves a costly workaround which is likely to have actually increased costs.

text: A program often needs to prioritize the allocation of shared resources across the projects. Which of the following is the best basis for prioritization that can be applied by the program manager?

choices.text: The priorities should be decided by the program steering committee
The priorities are based upon the preferences of the stakeholders
Technical dependencies across the projects will determine priorities
The projects which contribute most to the realization of benefits will be prioritized

explanation: Benefits realization being the primary purpose for the existence of a program, this should be the basis for also prioritizing the allocation of resources across the program’s components (Task 7 in Strategic program management in the examination content outline).

text: For your program, one of the project teams is located close to the client personnel at a remote location. There is a high level of interaction between this project team and client personnel, and client satisfaction is an important program objective. The client is very pleased with the particular project, but is not happy with the responsiveness of the other projects on the program. The other project managers are complaining that the client-facing project manager has been accepting a lot of changes which are impacting other projects in the program. As a result, the overall program is behind schedule and over budget. Morale among the other project team members is low. What action should you take to MOST effectively address these problems?

choices.text: You should create a reward and punishment system to ensure that the other project team members complete tasks within the timeframes outlined in the project plan
You should identify ways to make the other team members' work more satisfying using the most applicable motivational theory.
You should enforce scope change control in the projects and the program
You should incur the extra expenses necessary to be on-site to more closely monitor the activities of that particular project team.

explanation: Scope control seems to be lacking and appears to be the primary cause for the issues. All the other steps are dealing with the symptom not the cause.

text: During the review of projects within a program, a program manager finds that Project A is consistent with regard to delivering on time and within the budget, but frequently has issues with regard to quality. The reasons provided by the project manager were lack of skilled personnel and unreliable cost, time estimates. Which of the following actions would be most helpful to address these issues?

choices.text: Project C is currently running under budget and can transfer some of its budget to Project A
Project D is delayed due to unfulfilled dependencies and has spare resources to work on Project A for the time being
The program steering committee is open to reducing the scope of work if it helps make the product better
Project B has a lot of expertise with regard to the product and offers to train Project A’s team

explanation: Task 25 of program life cycle management (examination content outline) calls for the program manager to analyze the variances and trends to identify appropriate corrective actions and opportunities. As per the assessment provided, the problems in quality in project A stem from lack of skilled personnel (unreliable estimates could be an outcome of the same). Therefore the action that is most helpful is to boost the skill level of the team

text: A program manager was visiting an annual user’s conference where the user community of a company’s products gather together. One of the newer products on display was developed by a project within the program. An early user of the product mentioned several issues about the product at an informal reception to the program manager. What should the program manager do?

choices.text: Check if the feedback was consistent across other users or if they were one off issues
Send a note to the user thanking him for the feedback and follow up on the issues raised
Ask the project manager to look into the issues raised
Look into the project and program quality plans to understand why these issues were being raised

explanation: Proactive management of the issues raised by stakeholders is an important responsibility of the program manager. Since the issues were raised to the program manager at the user’s conference, the program manager must first acknowledge the issues and feedback and then follow up on closing the issues in a timely manner.

text: During the program life cycle, the program manager is regarded by all stakeholders as an individual that drives the change through the organization. The program manager has multiple communication channels that he engages in throughout the program and in every meeting. Consider you are in a meeting with 8 stakeholders. How many communication channels are there?
explanation: Communication channels =[ (yourself + 8) * (yourself + 8 -1)] / 2 = 36

text: Programs are intended to deliver benefits to the sponsoring organization. The program manager and steering committee monitor benefits realization throughout the program delivery and capture opportunities to maximize the delivery of benefits. Throughout the program, you monitor benefits using

choices.text: Preparing performance reports
Phase gate reviews
Heath checks reviews
Other program reports

explanation:
Health checks include performance reviews on periodic basis. They assess program’s ongoing performance and benefits realization and sustenance. Participants can send representatives and are not required to attend. These reviews result in performance reports and dashboards
Reference: SPM V4 Page 76 - 6.1.10

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. The program is kept confidential due to rising competition. You are now in the process of preparing the program management plan, which of the below is true about this plan?

choices.text: Integrates and manages program components
Establishes management controls
Integrates the program's subsidiary plans
All of the options

explanation:
The program management plan is a document that integrates the subsidiary plans and management control points in order to integrate and manage the individual components. The control points measure performance against the program management plan using collected information from constituent projects. Once the program management plan is approved, program delivery phase starts. It is worth noting that the program management plan development is iterative, prepared early in the program lifecycle and update throughout the program due to changes, priorities, etc
Reference: SPM V4 Page 94 - 7.1.2.2

text: Your company focuses a lot on quality of the output and it has made a name for itself in the market for the delivery of quality work. Each program has a team member dedicated to quality planning. Throughout the delivery phase, you are continuously focused on quality control. As part of the quality control, you should

choices.text: Conduct phase gate reviews
Implement quality assurance recommendations
Ensure checklists are completed
Conduct health checks

explanation:
Quality control involves the monitoring of specific components or deliverables to determine compliance to quality requirements and lead to benefit realization. It uses quality reviews performed with constituent component reviews. It is performed throughout program lifecycle and has the following outputs: quality change requests, quality control completed checklists and inspection reports, quality test reports or measurement results
Reference: SPM V4 Page 132 - 8.2.6.1

text: Your company A recently acquired company B. Company B has a program similar to the one you are managing in company A; your program is still in its early stages however the program in company B is already in its final stages. You knew this from an acquaintance of yours in company B while discussing the suite of programs in the pipeline of company B. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Inform the sponsor of company B about the similarity with one of company A’s programs
Continue as planned without mentioning the other program
Inform the sponsor of company A about this information
Terminate company B’s program as you are already undergoing a similar program

explanation:
Company B has a similar program and it’s already in its final stages, which means that it has a higher privilege of being pursued than company A’s program, so option D is wrong. Option C should be your first step as in this case, there is a clear conflict of interest and the sponsor needs to intervene. Option B is not correct as it does not reflect your transparency and integrity.
Reference: experience. Similar questions will occur on the exam and the answer is totally based on your experience; you will not find any of these in books

text: Stakeholder engagement is crucial to program success. During your 5-years program to launch a new drug that will help put an end to Cancer disease for patients in the early stages, multiple stakeholders are reporting that they are receiving performance reports on regular basis. In addition, they reported that the information sent is not complete and always needs to be updated. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Stop sending too many communications to the stakeholders
Use the feedback from stakeholders to enhance stakeholder engagement
Establish a well-designed PMIS with access rights to it
Establish a different communication policy with each stakeholder

explanation:
Receiving performance reports on regular basis is a good thing, which removes option A from the list. Option C is not correct here as it might not solve the issue which is that the information is not complete; establishing a PMIS may not solve the issue. Option D is hectic for the program manager and program team to maintain and is not a valid approach for a program manager to take except with major and key stakeholders with special reporting needs.
This scenario leads us to option B as the answer, because the stakeholder feedback is an output of program reporting; this output helps in enhancing the stakeholder engagement by consolidating the right information for them.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 127 - 8.2.2.2

text: You are now in the closing stage of your program and you are organizing program records for use in future programs; you are also collecting and archiving component records and documents. Which of the below options describes what your are doing?

choices.text: Conducting a post review meeting
Releasing resources
Organizing and archiving documents
Preparing the final report

explanation:
This scenario links to program information archiving done in closure phase. Other options are part of the closure phase but not related to this question. During information archiving, the program manager also meets with team members to capture the information from their feedback in the information archival. PMO can be consulted and can offer support as well
Reference: SPM V4 Page 139 - 8.3.2

text: You are the manager for a program to implement a new software for the government linking all the government departments together in order to better manage and engage with the residents. You and your program team worked hard on quantifying the program planned benefits because you realize that it is important for benefits management and program benefit reporting. Complementing this, you should

choices.text: Maintain a beneﬁts register
Conduct phase gate reviews
Conduct health checks
Try to list only the tangible benefits in the benefits management

explanation:
The question clearly points to option A. The benefits register records the list of planned benefits with their corresponding KPIs and thresholds, in addition the benefits register contains mapping of benefits to strategic objectives, mapping of planned benefits to program components as reflected in charter, brief description of how benefits are measured, risk assessment and probability of occurrence, progress indicator, target dates and milestones for benefit achievement, responsible party for delivering benefit, process for measuring progress and process for communicating progress. The benefits report is derived from the benefits register to report the status and progress of the benefits to stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1, in addition page 51 - 4.3 contains interesting information for you to know

text: You are the sponsor of a program and you are in the process of choosing a program manager. All the candidates have already managed programs for the company and they have done it successfully; they are highly regarded individuals in the organization and they tend to deliver to expectations. You choose the candidate who previously excelled in

choices.text: Identifying high-level risks
Establishing a benefits management plan
Establishing a governance plan
Stakeholder engagement

explanation:
Defining the high level risks is the most important of the options as it helps determining the probability of successfully delivering the benefits and helps identifying response plans and the strategy to apply them. It is one of the first steps performed by the program manager in collaboration with the sponsor and sponsoring organization and helps the steering committee approve or reject the business case. The other options are important, however not as important as option A.
Candidates here have excelled in program management previously so they should be accustomed with the other options
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You have finally reached the closing phase and are working on transitioning the program to operational entities for sustainment. During which phase, the components transition requests are prepared?

choices.text: Delivery phase
Closure phase
Planning phase
Transition phase

explanation:
During program delivery phase, components are authorized, initiated, integrated and transitioned. This question is important because you need to always look for specific words in the exam questions e.g. components, step, phase, activity, etc. In this question, the entire text focuses on program and program closure, however, the question targets the components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 91 - Figure 7-1 clearly shows this, in addition to Page 97 - 7.1.3.3

text: Your component manager came to you with a change request affecting the scope of his component and might affect the scope of another component as well. After thorough analysis, it was determined that the change affects both components. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Update PWBS
Inform both component managers to handle the request as part of their components and do nothing from your end as this change affects their components
Approve the change request and the funding for it

explanation:
This question is in program scope monitoring and controlling; as an output of it, the PWBS is updated. As a rule of thumb, when you have a scope change, you update PWBS and architecture. When you have a significant schedule change, you update roadmap and business case
Reference: SPM V4 Page 123 - 8.1.2.12

text: As a program manager you communicate program performance reports regularly and engage stakeholders to solicit their feedback and manage the program to a successful delivery. Which of the below is important for a program manager in order to have a well-informative program reporting?

choices.text: Do trend analysis and forecasts
Focus on critical success factors
Provide as much details on the projects as possible
Aggregate information across projects, subsidiary programs, and program activities

explanation:
The program reports aggregate information across projects, subsidiary programs, and program activities. The reports are provided to stakeholders with the needed information related to resources to deliver program benefits. These could be status reports or performance reports or any type of reports
Reference: SPM V4 Page 127 - 8.2.2.2

text: You are newly appointed to a program which is already in delivery phase. You notice that there are a lot of complex templates, everybody can see all information and you are getting a lot of similar questions to data you have already presented. Your best course of action is

choices.text: Review PMIS
Review stakeholder register
Review stakeholder engagement plan
Review stakeholder communication plan

explanation:
Best approach in this scenario is to review PMIS in order to define or update processes to share information while defining access rights on specific information. This will help in maximizing synergies. With relation to the question, you review the PMIS because you have a redundancy of questions on the same topics. After you review the PMIS, you will update the processes, templates maybe, and you will have for example multiple interpretations of the same data in different ways to cater for the need; of course you should not forget the access rights because not everybody can see any data.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 100

text: A CEO is furious because each and every one of the programs undergone by the company is successful and meets the objectives; however, the company is not meeting its strategic goals and objectives. In your opinion, which of the below is a reason behind this?

choices.text: Projects are interlinked and should have been managed as a program
The programs are not providing the needed benefits
The programs are not coping with the organization’s strategic changes or they are not aware of them
This is normal as the programs are undergone to deliver certain benefits and do not need to remain align with the strategic objectives if they change

explanation:
This scenario is clearly linked to option C because due to countless challenges, organizations’ strategies can change. This change needs to be communicated to the program manager in order to be able to integrate it by terminating components, adding components and updating others. All other options are irrelevant
Strategic changes occur outside of the program i.e. Portfolio level (SPM V4 Page 11 - Table 1-1 - Monitoring) and need to be passed to the subsequent levels i.e. programs and projects in order to align with the new direction. This answer is also based on experience and of performance of multiple programs and portfolios

text: You are managing a program to improve employee morale. Your CEO is backing up the program because many employees have been recently leaving the company and immediate action is needed. The program has several components and dedicated resources aiming for the program completion within the same year. Being on a tight schedule, which of the below is valid?

choices.text: Send a survey to be filled by each and every employee on their understanding of the program
Prepare a good charter
Resource reallocation between components
Plan weekly meetings with the program steering committee

explanation:
Being on a tight schedule with dedicated resources, the program manager needs to reallocate resources between components when components are closed. Options A and B are irrelevant; option D will slow down execution and will not necessarily act as a solution in your case
Reference: SPM V4 Page 119 - 8.1.2.9

text: In order to effectively manage a program, the program manager needs to define, analyze, plan and efficiently manage benefits. You are the program manager for a 2-years transformation program in your organization and they are implementing a new software system to manage the interdependency between different teams. You are currently analyzing and planning benefits; which of the below is the main output of this activity?

choices.text: Communicate program performance metrics to stakeholders
Benefits management plan
Benefits register
Quantify incremental beneﬁts

explanation:
Benefits analysis and planning establishes program benefits management plan, communicates it’s metrics to key stakeholders, develops metrics and frameworks for monitoring and controlling components, and measurement of benefits within program. Benefits analysis and planning defines and prioritize components and interdependencies, defines KPIs and associated quantitative measures. In addition, benefits analysis and planning include the quantification of incremental benefits including timing of benefits delivery, qualification of intangible benefits and quantification of the resulting benefits. Here we talk about the main output which is the benefits management plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: In order to effectively manage a program, the program manager needs to define, analyze, plan and efficiently manage benefits. You are the program manager for a 2-years transformation program in your organization and they are implementing a new software system to manage the interdependency between different teams. You have finished the benefits analysis and planning and have established the benefits management plan. The purpose of the plan is to

choices.text: Guide the delivery of beneﬁts
Generate reports to send to steering committee and stakeholders
Prioritize components
Derive stakeholder communication strategy

explanation:
The benefits management plan is the performance baseline, which guides the benefits delivery as the program progresses. Option D is derived from stakeholder engagement, option B and C are not purposes of this plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: You are the manager for a joint program between your company which is a leader in the transportation industry and the government to launch new electric metros and subways in order to lower the congestion and the travel time from city A to city B. During the program, as program benefits are further defined

choices.text: Scope is being achieved
Program is coming to an end
Risks are further refined and new benefit risks quantified
Probability of achievement is higher

explanation:
Based on SPM, as program benefits are further defined, risks are further refined and new benefit risks quantified. Other options are irrelevant. It is crucial to note that benefits and risks work hand in hand; you never define a benefit without defining its associated risks, and you never give a measurement whether related to benefits or not without giving its confidence factor which is associated with the linked risks and their levels
Reference: SPM V4 Page 49 - 4.2

text: You have been managing a large and complex program for your company for the past few years and your are approaching the end of it. Your program has delivered five components and one is still to be delivered. What should be your next step as a program manager?

choices.text: Work with your sponsor to issue a request for the closure or transition of components
Issue a program closure request
Prepare a final program performance report
Financial closure

explanation:
In this scenario, program is still in delivery phase; however, some of the components have delivered their outcomes and the program manager needs to collaborate with sponsor to prepare a request for the closure or transition of the five components. Option "Issue a program closure request" occurs at the end of program delivery phase; once approved, the closure phase debuts. All other options are part of program closure phase and not components transition and closure
Reference: SPM V4 Page 95 - 7.1.3.3

text: You are appointed as a program manager on a new program and your sponsor asks you to prepare a high level assessment in order to get the approval from the steering committee on the justification for resources expending. One of your recently assigned program team members, a junior engineer, has come to you asking if there’s a document that spans across multiple phases and is considered the baseline for program definition, planning and execution. Your answer to the junior project manager was

choices.text: Program Business Case
Program Roadmap
Program Charter
​Program management plan

explanation:
Program Roadmap sets the baseline for program definition, planning and execution. The roadmap assesses the program's progress toward realizing its expected beneﬁts, it is the basis for transition and integration, used to communicate plan and benefits to stakeholders to build and maintain advocacy. In addition, the roadmap shows major milestones, important components, incremental benefits, relationship between components & benefits and major decision points
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3

text: You are the sponsor of a high-priority program and want to assign a program manager to manage your program. The program manager needs to have the PgMP credential and needs to be knowledgeable in the art of communication and stakeholder engagement as you know that the program will span on a long period and will have a large number of stakeholders involved. Which of the below represents an important competency you will look for it in a program manager?

choices.text: Strategic visioning
Collaboration
Integration
Communication

explanation:
A successful program is based on aligning benefits to the strategic goals and objectives. The program manager must have integration competencies in order to be able to identify program outputs and integrate them to attain benefits.
Communication is important, however a project manager can have good communication skills, which does not make them able to be program managers. Program is about integrating components, and integrating outputs in operational departments; this is why integration or integration management is the most adequate answer, in addition to being the core activity done in a program.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 99 - 7.2.2

text: During the delivery phase of your program, you and the steering committee have planned for continuous reviews in order for the steering committee to be able to maintain oversight and follow up on program performance. Phase gate reviews are part of these reviews. Which of the below is true about phase gate reviews?

choices.text: Review and approve changes to the program
Held at components start and end
Mandates attendance of selected key stakeholders
All of the options

explanation:
Phase gate reviews enable governance approval for the continuation of a program from one phase to another, continuation may include modifications. It includes reviewing and approving changes to the program; it is held at milestones, components start and end; it mandates attendance of selected key stakeholders and it results in go/no-go decisions. Phase gate reviews criteria are strategic alignment and value delivery
Reference: SPM V4 Page 75 - 6.1.9, in addition to insights from exam questions

text: During the delivery phase of your program, you and the steering committee have planned for continuous reviews in order for the steering committee to be able to maintain oversight and follow up on program performance. Health check reviews are part of these reviews. Which of the below is true about health checks?

choices.text: Performance reviews on periodic basis
Assesses program ongoing performance
Participants can send representatives and are not required to attend
All of the options

explanation:
Health checks include performance reviews on periodic basis. They assess program’s ongoing performance and benefits realization and sustainment. Participants can send representatives and are not required to attend. These reviews result in performance reports and dashboards
Reference: SPM V4 Page 76 - 6.1.10

text: Organizations' strategies change, and changes might affect the programs. Some programs might be closed, updated or added. You have been working with your program management team to deliver your program and you are already mid-way through delivery. Your sponsor calls you and informs you, that due to the strategic changes in the organization, your program has been terminated; what is your course of action in this case?

choices.text: Archive PMIS
Transition finished components
Try to talk the sponsor to change his decision
Final performance review

explanation:
Program has been terminated; no matter the reason, you must start the closure phase activities, starting with preparing the final performance review. This review will be part of the final program report
Reference: ECO Task 31 - Closing The Program / SPM V4 Page 138 - 8.3

text: You are managing a program for the government and due to the high stakes you maintain close communication with the government representatives. You are working continuously to maximize opportunities and lowering threats. In your opinion, risk profiles are

choices.text: Collected through brainstorming sessions
Expressed in policy statements
Given by portfolio members
Collected through one-on-one interviews

explanation:
Risk profiles are expressed in policy statements or revealed in actions that may highlight organization’s risk appetite. Program risk management plan defines risk profiles of the program and the strategy to handle risks
Reference: SPM V4 Page 120 - 8.1.2.10

text: Your program steering committee is the review and decision making group in your program, its role is to endorse recommendations of a program under its authority. For this, you, as a program manager need to prepare a compelling program governance plan to guide the governance processes throughout the program lifecycle. Which of the below is part of program governance plan?

choices.text: Program governance summary
Structure and composition of governance members
Planned governance meetings
All of the options

explanation:
Governance plan describes the systems and methods to be used to monitor, manage, and support a given program, responsibilities of specific roles for ensuring timely and effective use of the systems and methods. It includes program governance summary; structure and composition of governance members; planned governance meetings; roles and responsibilities; dependencies, assumptions and constraints; benefits, performance metrics and measurements; components initiation and transition criteria; issues escalation process
Reference: SPM V4 Page 70 - 6.1.1

text: Program manager works hard throughout the program and especially in the planning sub-phase in order to guide the subsequent phases of the program. Today, on your program to deliver the next generation keyboards with gestures instead of a panel, you got your program management plan approved. Which of the below represents your next course of action?

choices.text: Review component charter
Prepare component initiation requests
Review program business case
Prepare PWBS

explanation:
After getting your plan approved you will start your delivery phase which includes the initiation, execution, transition and closure of components.
Each component requires to be initiated through an initiation request approved by steering committee. Steering committee approves the request based on the initiation criteria in governance plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 76 - 6.1.11

text: You are the program manager on a program to deliver a new metro station linking the 2 ends of the city. You program is of high priority to your company and to your city. You got your program management plan approved and multiple components have been initiated. You have multiple resources working on your program. As a result of component initiation, transition or closure, you

choices.text: Prepare a staffing management plan
Prepare your resource management plan
Revise and update your program resource management plan
Revise and update your stafﬁng management plan

explanation:
As changes to components are made i.e. initiation, transition or closure, resources may be impacted and revising the resource management plan and updating it may be needed as an output of program resource management activity. Options A and B should have been prepared before the start of the delivery phase; the scenario does not warrant the revision and update of the staffing management plan; the staffing management plan defines skills and competencies of a program
Reference: SPM V4 Page 133 - 8.2.7

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. As a program manager, you know that the primary objective of stakeholder engagement is

choices.text: Stakeholders identification
Gain and maintain stakeholders buy in to program beneﬁts
Stakeholders analysis and extracting the needs and expectations of stakeholders
Working with only the positive stakeholders as they have an added value

explanation:
Option D is not correct in any case. Options A and C are part of the stakeholder engagement planning, however, the primary objective for stakeholder engagement is to gain and maintain stakeholders buy in to program beneﬁts as it is essential for realizing benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 57

text: You know that quality is often performed at the component level; the governance board is responsible for reviewing and approving the approach for quality management and the standards by which quality will be measured. Program quality

choices.text: Satisfies scope
Conforms to requirements
Ensures fitness for use
All of the options

explanation:
Program quality satisfies scope, conforms to requirements and ensures fitness for use. Program quality management implements a quality management system through policies and procedures with continuous improvement activities
Reference: SPM V4 Page 132 - 8.2.6

text: You have three programs in your company: Program A supports 3 strategic objectives; Program B supports 2 strategic objectives; Program C supports 1 strategic objective. Which one do you recommend to pursue?

choices.text: Program A
Program B
Program C
None, as it doesn’t matter how many strategic objectives are supported by the program

explanation:
Clearly, A supports 3 strategic objectives and is strategically aligned with organization objectives. Option D is not correct as a program not strategically aligned and supports strategic objectives will not be pursued by the organization except if it is for compliance or regulatory purposes
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: Throughout the delivery phase of your program to launch the new drug for curing cancer, multiple components are initiated, integrated, transition and closed in order to drive the program to a successful delivery of benefits. For approving the transition or closure of a new component, it is the steering committee responsibility to

choices.text: Request an audit of the component
Transition it once the project manager states that it delivered the intended outcome
Aggregate data from the program and the related component to present it in a performance report
Establish minimum acceptance criteria for transition or closure

explanation:
It is the responsibility of the steering committee to establish minimum acceptance criteria for component transition or closure; in addition, the steering committee defines the methods to measure, communicate and endorse these criteria
Reference: SPM V4 Page 97 - 7.1.3.3

text: The program manager engages stakeholders by assessing their attitudes towards the program and change readiness. The program manager includes stakeholders in program activities and utilizes communications targeted to their needs and expectations. This is done as part of

choices.text: Communications monitoring and controlling
Information distribution and program reporting
Stakeholder engagement
Communications management

explanation:
This scenario is an overview of the stakeholder engagement. To note that stakeholder engagement resembles to risk management; so in exam, whenever you have an issue finding the answer when it comes to stakeholder engagement, think from a risk management perspective. Furthermore, stakeholder identification is very similar to risk identification; stakeholders are negative or positive as the risk are considered as threats or opportunities; stakeholder strategy comes after analysis, very similar to risk strategy
Reference: SPM V4 Page 64 - 5.4

text: You have been working hard for the past 5 years to deliver the new drug that will cure cancer throughout the world and you are extremely happy to get to the final stages with only a small deviation of the cost. In a program, who is responsible for the sign-off of component closure documents?

choices.text: Component project manager
Component steering committee
Program manager
Program steering committee

explanation:
Sign-off of component closure documents is done by project sponsor, which normally is the program manager. The program manager is normally the sponsor of components
Reference: multiple insights from exam questions

text: You have good relations with project managers in your company as you have been one of them. Recently, you have been assigned to manage a program for your organization and you are currently discussing with the steering committee about the assignment of project managers for two of the program’s components. In which phase are you?

choices.text: Definition phase – formulation sub-phase
Definition phase – planning sub-phase
Delivery
Closure

explanation:
During program delivery phase, components are authorized, initiated, integrated and transitioned. Project managers are assigned during this phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 95 - 7.1.3

text: You are managing a high-priority program in your company and the CEO is having a close eye on your program due to its strategic importance to the future of the company. For this reason, who should be the chairman of your program’s steering committee?

choices.text: Portfolio manager
CEO
Program sponsor
The daughter of the CEO as she has strong interpersonal skills and power in the company

explanation:
Normally, the sponsor is the chairman of the steering committee. All other options are irrelevant to this scenario. Sponsor is the individual responsible for committing the organizational resources to the program and enabling program success; he is normally a senior executive with insights an investment decisions; he is a program benefits advocate, he need to have the ability to influence, take decisions and he needs to have effective communication skills
Reference: SPM V4 Page 80 - 6.2.1

text: You are managing a restructuring program for your company which will include laying off a large number of employees and merger of multiple departments. It is a big change for the company; however, it is needed for the future of the company. In order to see how the company will adapt to change, you are now conducting a change assessment. As part of the assessment you

choices.text: Establish a change control board
Estimate probability and impact of the change
Establish an escalation process
Estimate communication needs

explanation:
As part of program formulation, potential change management considerations are identified and assessed to help develop the business case. The assessment identifies source of change (environmental factors, sensitivity to changes in organizational strategy, possible change frequency from components, etc.), estimates probability and impact from these sources and proposes positive responsive measures towards them
Reference: SPM V4 Page 107 - 8.1.1.1

text: You are in the definition phase of a 2-years program to improve employee morale in your organization. The turnover rate is high and employees are leaving the company to find better opportunities. The CEO took extreme measures and put your program as the highest priority program in the organization. You are currently in risk management planning. You should

choices.text: Set thresholds for triggering the project risks
Identify integration opportunities
Establish an agreed-upon basis to evaluate risks
Establish contingency reserves

explanation:
Risk management planning identifies how to approach and conduct risk management activities for a program by considering its components. It identifies the resources and time for risk management activities and an agreed-upon basis to evaluate risks. It is conducted early in the definition phase. During this activity, it is essential to define risk profiles of organization to construct the most suitable approach to managing risks, adjusting risk sensitivity and monitoring risk criticality. Options A and B are irrelevant and option D is done after defining risk response plans
Reference: SPM V4 Page 120 - 8.1.2.10

text: Your company focuses a lot on quality of the output and it has made a name for itself in the market for the delivery of quality work. Each program has a team member dedicated to quality planning. During a quality audit, the program team reports a finding that quality requirements have not been met for a component. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Revise and update the program quality management plan
Inform program team that they should find ways to fix the issue and apply them directly to the component and any other component with the same issue
Prepare and issue a quality assurance change request
Change the project manager as quality is the most important aspect for the company

explanation:
Audits have audit findings as results. Program manager needs to prepare and issue a quality assurance change request in order to implement solutions for the findings. This type of change requests are outputs of quality assurance and control activity.
Program audits are part of the quality assurance and control, which has an output as quality assurance change requests
Reference: SPM V4 Page 132 - 8.2.6

text: You are a just assigned program manager on a program to deliver potable water to the nearby city. Your program has the highest priority in your country as the individual rights and well-being are the most important aspects for your government. You start by preparing high level scope statement in order to define the use case for your program. What is your next step?

choices.text: Create scope description
Create business case
Create program charter
Create roadmap

explanation:
As part of program initiation (formulation), program manager translates strategic objectives into high-level program scope statements by negotiating with stakeholders, including sponsors, in order to create a program scope description. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 2 Program Life Cycle

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. When you first identified the program stakeholders, which of the following methods and techniques you used?

choices.text: Brainstorming
Historical information
Questionnaires and surveys
Interviews

explanation:
The brainstorming sessions are done with program team in order to identify potential program stakeholders, their roles and importance for the program. Later, you hold focus groups, meetings and interviews to analyze stakeholders’ needs and expectations and prioritize stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.1

text: You and your team are working on preparing the document to authorize the program manager and program management team to use organizational resources. You already got your business case approved and you are developing program charter using input from all stakeholders in order to

choices.text: Initiate and design program and benefits
Establish program infrastructure
Align implementation strategy with strategic objectives
Monitor and control program resources

explanation:
As part of program initiation (formulation), program manager develops program charter using input from all stakeholders in order to initiate and design program and benefits. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 1 Program Life Cycle

text: You have been appointed as a program manager for a just starting program to design a new remote control car with more features than the ones currently on the market. You know it is a critical program to the organization and you also know that there are a lot of regulatory criteria to meet; in addition, this program is confidential since there are a lot of companies in the market that are undergoing similar programs. While preparing the business case, which of the below should be included

choices.text: Comparative advantage analysis
Beneﬁt strategy
High-level roadmap
Stakeholders strategy

explanation:
Option B and D are included in program charter. Option C is not included in business case; however, it is an input to it. Option A is the correct answer as the comparative advantage analysis considers competing efforts and what-if analysis to show different approaches of attaining benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 39 - 3.4.2.1

text: The program manager identifies components in order to be able to deliver benefits through the delivery phase. You have identified the starting components for your program and need to secure resources for them. An important input consideration is

choices.text: Previous experience with resources
Your ability to negotiate with functional managers
The availability of resources
Possibility of outsourcing components

explanation:
When planning the resources, the availability is an important consideration especially for key resources in order to optimize their use across components. You have identified the mix of components and you want to start your delivery phase by initiating components. part of this is ensuring the availability of resources to perform the components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 76 - 6.1.11, in addition to important information from Page 119 - 8.1.2.9

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. In order to align the program with the expectations of stakeholders, you

choices.text: Develop a high-level milestone plan
Develop business case
Develop program charter
Develop program management plan

explanation:
As part of program initiation (formulation), program manager develops a high-level milestone plan using the goals and objectives of the program, applicable historical information, and other available resources e.g. PWBS, scope statement, benefit management plan, etc. in order to align the program with the expectations of stakeholders N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 3 Program Life Cycle

text: Funding models vary for programs and subsequent projects; funding can be internal or external. Consider you are managing a program funded by the government. The used funding is a step funding and requires the program to include workers from different cultural diversity. This is regarded as?

choices.text: Assumption
Constraint
Benefit
Suggestion

explanation:
This scenario clearly links to a constraint put by the funding organization. The program needs to abide by it and can’t continue without it
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: Your corporate PMO has defined a program management methodology to be used across all programs in the company. You were appointed to manage a transformation program in your company and are currently in the planning phase. Which of the below is considered important in defining program management activities?

choices.text: Quality management
Communication management
Stakeholder engagement
Infrastructure development

explanation:
Program quality should be considered when defining program management activities. It is especially important during planning to verify that quality activities and controls are applied to the program and to its subsequent components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 118 - 8.1.2.8

text: During the delivery phase of your program, you have planned to start a component and had already done the necessary communications in order to secure the resources for this component. The component is due to start soon and you still haven’t received all the required resources. What is your best course of action in response to the delay in getting the resources?

choices.text: Escalate to portfolio manager
Escalate to sponsor
Escalate to change control board
Escalate to functional manager

explanation:
If the question was related to issues with or between resources, option D would be correct. However, here, the issue is in getting the resources, which is the responsibility of the program sponsor.
Pay attention, if you had the Program SC as an option, you should choose it, as your first line of escalation is the SC, and in case the SC cannot get the resources, the sponsor intervenes as the one responsible for this activity and the highest hierarchical affiliation for it
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.8, in addition to multiple insights from exam questions

text: You are the program manager to build a new gas extraction station in a new country where it is the first time they try to extract gas. Your company has developed gas extraction stations in other countries, but it is its first program in this country. During definition phase and while determining resource requirements, you should

choices.text: Determine the number of resources needed for the components and add them together to have the total number of needed resources
Consider the availability of key resources
Review historical information
Consider the roadmap

explanation:
This scenario clearly states that your company has experience in building this type of extraction stations in other countries, thus, you should be checking the historical information in order to determine the type of required resources needed for the program because the company has already done this
Reference: experience. Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: In programs, normally the contracts are signed at program level but managed at component level; admin and closeout decisions are managed at component level. However, some of the contracts are administered at program level to benefit many components. In this case

choices.text: Contract closure is at component level
Contracts are always administered at the component level
Component managers coordinate or report deliverable information
Component managers report procurement results and closeouts

explanation:
Normally, once the program standards are in place and the contracts are awarded, administration and closeout of most of these contracts are transitioned to the components; the components report procurement results and closeouts to program. In this case, program manager maintains visibility to ensure the program budget is properly expended to obtain benefits. However, in some situations, procurement contracts are administered at program level; in this case, component managers coordinate or report deliverable information and contract changes and issues to the program management team
Reference: SPM V4 Page 131 - 8.2.5.1

text: You have successfully performed the implementation of the program to release a new drug to cure cancer all around the world and you are getting into the final stages before closure. You are currently closing all projects and contract. Successful closure of a contract is done after ensuring that

choices.text: All deliverables have been satisfactorily completed
All payments have been made
There are no outstanding contractual issues
All of the options

explanation:
In program contract closure, a formal closure is done after ensuring that all deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made and that there are no outstanding contractual issues. The three are done in same order
Reference: SPM V4 Page 140 - 8.3.3

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. During the meetings with stakeholders, the program management team tries to solicit the stakeholders’ attitudes, perceptions and response towards risks. This is important in order to

choices.text: Define and analyze risks
Prepare the program risk management plan
Determine stakeholder concerns that may lead to risks
Prepare the stakeholder communication strategy

explanation:
Program management team members try to understand the impact, urgency and probability of stakeholders’ concerns and based on this, determine the problems that may lead to risks affecting the program. This approach helps in defining risks and then analyzing them but is not the main idea in this scenario. Option D is prepared from the stakeholder engagement plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 134 - 8.2.8.1

text: You are in the definition phase of your program to deliver five new ice cream flavors and you realize that the program is of critical importance to the organization. You are currently in program initiation (formulation) sub-phase and are developing an accountability matrix by identifying and assigning program roles and responsibilities in order to

choices.text: Build the core team and to differentiate between the program and project resources
Build the core team and to assign program governance roles
Build the core team and to assign program management team members roles
All of the options

explanation:
During program initiation (formulation), program manager develops an accountability matrix by identifying and assigning program roles and responsibilities in order to build the core team and to differentiate between the program and project resources N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 4 Program Life Cycle

text: Funding varies between programs and between components of the same program. Funding can be internal or external. You are managing a program which will be funded externally by the government. The steering committee is responsible for agreements to secure funds and they should take into consideration that

choices.text: Funding will not be done at once, instead it will be a step funding
Funding is subject to regulations
Program will fund its work until deliverable, then, the government will release the funds as contracts are being closed
None of the Options

explanation:
Working with government or any external authority funding your program is most probably subject to regulations; funding organization will include regulations, constraints, and limitations and may include adherence to certain laws as well
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: You have multiple components in your program and are currently initiating two of these components. You are working closely with the component managers in order for them to understand the need and requirements and plan their projects accordingly. As a program manager, you define standard measurement criteria for success for all constituent projects by

choices.text: Analyzing stakeholders’ expectations and requirements across constituent projects
Letting the project managers analyze their projects stakeholders and roll back requirements to you and to the program management team
Only analyzing the stakeholders that are impacted by the program
Focus on positive stakeholders and do not analyze the negative ones

explanation:
During program initiation (formulation), you define standard measurement criteria for success for all constituent projects by analyzing stakeholders’ expectations and requirements across constituent projects in order to monitor and control the program. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 5 Program Life Cycle

text: You have successfully performed the implementation of the program to release a new drug to cure cancer all around the world and you are getting into the final stages before closure. You are currently closing all projects and contract in order to start the closure phase activities. As a program manager, you realize that the final decision in program closure is given to

choices.text: Program manager
Program sponsor
Program steering committee
CEO

explanation:
When in closure phase, program manager recommends the closure to steering committee which will check the successful delivery of the program against program charter. If successful, steering committee will recommend closure to sponsor who will check the success of the program against the business case and take a decision on closure
Reference: SPM V4 Page 97 - 7.1.4. Final approval comes from the sponsor or sponsoring organization.
