Option "Explain the program's vision" is irrelevant as it shows the program direction and “from status” to “to status”. Option "Perform beneﬁts management plan" is irrelevant in this scenario and option "Continue as planned" is not correct. Option "Allocate more time" is the correct answer as the known stakeholders influence the entire program especially other stakeholders. The program manager should spend a great amount of time in any program in order to maintain stakeholder engagement and alignment with program’s objectives
Reference: Stakeholder Engagement Chapter, in addition to experience. Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: During the last meeting with the steering committee, they advised you to update your risk management plan and do the program risk identification and analysis again because multiple unidentified risks have been occurring and the program is at a critical phase. The advice of the steering committee is given as part of its role in

choices.text: The escalation process
Program monitor and control
Program phase gate reviews
Program health checks

explanation:
Whether during a health check or a phase gate review, the advice of the steering committee is given as part of its role in program monitor and control
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.5

text: You are a member of the portfolio board and choosing a program to undertake. Program A has a Cost of $250000 and a revenue of $50000 per year, Program B has a Cost of $200000 and a revenue of $50000 per year, Program C has a Cost of $150000 and a revenue of $50000 per year, Program D has a Cost of $100000 and a revenue of $50000 per year. Which program will you recommend?

choices.text: Program A
Program B
Program C
Program D

explanation: In this case, the program with the highest ROI will be chosen; ROI = (Revenue / Cost) * 100. ROI-A = 20%, ROI-B = 25%, ROI-C = 33.3%, ROIC-D = 50%. The highest ROI is for program D. N.B: the numbers here are given for example purposes

text: Program manager spends a good amount of time preparing the schedule. From the scope statement, the program manager derives the PWBS which will help in the make-or-buy decisions, and in estimating the cost, quality, resource and duration. Consider you are building your schedule using the PWBS. Which of the below is the best approach to start with?

choices.text: Meet with components manager and build the schedule together
Design a first draft of the schedule including the components start and end dates
Have the components managers design their schedules and then combine all schedules together to form the program schedule
Have the program team build the schedule and let the components managers use the same schedule with changes based on their work

explanation:
When building a schedule, at the start it is a top-down approach and then it transforms into a bottom-up approach. The program manager starts by designing a first draft of the schedule including the components start and end dates. The project managers will then design their schedules and then roll-up any changes to the start and end dates. The program manager updates the program schedule accordingly and the new start/end dates for each component will act as a constraint at the level of the component
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11. This section is not detailed in the SPM, this is why we have included our instructors insights and experience in exam questions in this answer to help you better understand the flow

text: Your customer has outsourced your company to manage a transformation program on their premises. You have three components on your program; components A, B and C. Component A has a delayed milestone due to multiple changes and component B, which is dependent on the output of component A, is scheduled to use an important resource from component A. Component A’s project manager refuses to let go of the resource until the project delivers its due milestone. What should you, as the program manager do?

choices.text: Let Component A’s project manager give the resource to component B
Let Component B wait for component A to finish and release resources
Work to balance program needs with resource availability
Let component A and component B sit together and come up with a collaborative decision

explanation:
Option D is not correct since it is the responsibility of the program manager to do resource optimization by balancing the need with the availability. Options A and B can be the results of the balancing that is done in option C. As a program manager you should always search for optimal ways to balance the requirements with the availability, this can result in resource interdependency, prioritization or even in the merger of components in extreme cases.
Reference: insights from students who have taken the exam

text: Part of the program manager’s work is to track the planned benefits and identify opportunities for improvement in order to maximize and/or enhance benefits. You are managing a program to design remote control cars with the technology to climb walls not existing anywhere in the world. After identifying benefits and listing them in the benefit register, you

choices.text: Define critical success factors
Define KPIs
Review benefits management plan
You start engaging stakeholders

explanation:
Benefits identification is to analyze the available information about organizational and business strategies, and program drivers to identify benefits and list them in benefits register and qualify the benefits; it defines program objectives and critical success factors and identifies and qualifies business benefits.
N.B: sometimes PMI uses the word "outcome" to talk about "benefits". So if you face the word outcome instead of benefits, consider them being the same word
Reference: SPM V4 Page 46 - 4.1

text: The sponsor acts as an advocate in a program and ensures that the program gets the management attention while informing the program manager of any strategic change. The sponsor is an executive member who acts as the chair of the steering committee. Who usually takes up the role of sponsor in components’ steering committees?

choices.text: Program sponsor
Program manager
Project manager
Functional manager

explanation:
Usually, the program manager takes the role of component sponsor. All other options are not correct. It is important to note that this role is given to the program manager based on his experience and the degree of autonomy a program steering committee grants to him/her
This question has occurred on multiple occasions in the exam and is based on your experience in program management. Some of the questions you get in the exam cannot necessarily be found in books

text: Consider you are the program manager and your program is 5% complete. The program has a budget at completion BAC=5 million dollars, the actual cost is $250 000 and earned value is $245 000. What can you tell about the program status?

choices.text: The program is slightly over budget, which is not a problem at this stage
The program is slightly over budget, which is a huge problem at this stage
Budget needs to be re-baselined
Steering committee should intervene because the situation is out of control being at just 5%

explanation: The program is at just 5%, and the cost variance is CV = EV – AC = $5 000 which is totally insignificant when it comes to the $5M budget at completion. If you had bigger completion percentage (above 30%) and a bigger CV (greater than 50k), then you will have an issue

text: You are in a matrix organization and managing program A. Program steering committee is shared between your program and program B. Program B has been experiencing severe delays and steering committee has decided that multiple resources should be transferred from your program to be full-timers on program B. Two of the resources had issues with the transfer and are not accepting to communicate with you. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Terminate program A because there is no chance of delivering the intended benefits with less resources
Involve the functional managers of the resources to be transferred
Raise this issue to executive management and do not accept the resources transfer
Inform stakeholders of this change

explanation:
In a matrix organization, functional managers are responsible for resources; this is why in this case functional managers need to be involved to solve the resources issues.
N.B: in the exam question, if they do not mention what type of organization, by default you consider it as matrix organization
Reference: SPM V4 Page 18 - 1.7.1 (leadership skills section in particular)

text: Your company is project-based and has been delivering successful projects for many years. An executive manager was recently recruited and he comes from a programs-based organization. As a first act, he asked you to perform an initial assessment to know if adopting program approaches would be an added value to the organization; based on your findings, he will be able to present the approach to the executive management. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: ​Create business case
​Create roadmap
Analyze the strategic plan
Deﬁne the objectives

explanation:
Organizations derive strategic goals and objectives by performing a strategic planning cycle having as input the organization vision and mission. The strategic goals and objectives are documented in a strategic plan which is then divided into a set of initiatives to be undertaken by the portfolios, programs and projects. In this scenario, the program manager needs to analyze the strategic plan in order to validate alignment before proceeding any further.
Here you consider it as a new program proposal and you need to check if it is aligned with your company's strategies and objectives, thus strategic plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 34 - Figure 3-1 shows that it is the starting point for your program

text: Funding frameworks differ between programs. You are managing a step-funding program where the program receives funds at the start of each year. The remaining funds at the end of each year are returned back to the organization. What should you ensure as a program manager?

choices.text: You add a 15% to the total budget amount in order to stay on the safe side
Compiling all available financial information and listing all income and payment schedules in sufficient detail so that program costs can be tracked as part of program budget
You spend all the remaining money on rewarding the team
You make sure to only accept important change requests so you do not affect the budget

explanation:
Program budget consists of compiling all available financial information and listing all income and payment schedules in sufficient detail so that program costs can be tracked as part of program budget. Option A is not correct in any case, as the program manager should reflect the exact resources need of the program, based on this need, the business case is approved or rejected. Option C is irrelevant and option D is not correct in any case
Reference: SPM V4 Page 115 - 8.1.2.5

text: The CEO of a risk adverse company decided to change the culture of his organization after several pitfalls; he decided that the company needs to take more risks if it wants to gain from its investments. A program was designed with you as the program manager. While in the definition phase, in which of the following documents is the organization’s risk tolerance recorded?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Mandate
Strategic plan

explanation:
Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits and most importantly a high-level risk assessment containing the risk tolerance acting as a reminder and constraint when making program decisions.
Risk tolerances are not detailed in the standard, however they are part of the business case and they are used for validating the continuation of the program in phase-gate reviews; if the program surpasses the risk threshold, it might be terminated
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: You were planning to launch a new component in order to maximize the delivery of benefits; your recommendation got accepted by the steering committee and you need two of your program management team members to dedicate a week’s time to this component due to its strategic importance for the success of the program. To determine the availability of certain program resources, you reference

choices.text: Resources calendar​
Resources management plan
Governance plan
Project management plan

explanation:
Resources calendar shows the availability of program resources. All other options do not reflect the resources availability
Reference: resource calendar is mostly seen in PMP study material and abundantly on the WEB. We have included all you need to know in this QB

text: You are mid-way through your program and you realize that stakeholders have conflicting concerns and issues, and that operational departments are a bit reluctant to change. You do not understand the reason behind this, however, in your analysis of the issues in order to come out with necessary changes, you need to evaluate

choices.text: Resources availability
Program scope
Include the operational departments in the steering committee
Benefit register

explanation:
Changes may be related to scope; this type of changes originates from stakeholders, missing requirements at the start of the program or external resources. Scope changes affect the architecture and PWBS. The program manager needs to monitor and control the scope in this case in order to ensure successful completion of the program. Operational departments are a bit reluctant is normal in most programs and it is the job of the program manager to drive the change through organizations
Reference: SPM V4 Page 137 - 8.2.10

text: Which one of the below programs would you suggest to remove? Program A NPV at: 5% = 5,243, 10% = 2,841, 15% = 1,563; Program B NPV at: 5% = 2,320, 10% = 1,254, 15% = 688; Program C NPV at: 5% = 6,400, 10% = 3,275, 15% = 1,679; Program D NPV at: 5% = 3,000, 10% = 2,755, 15% = 700

choices.text: Program A
Program B
Program C
Program D

explanation: The higher the Net Present Value (NPV), the better. Program B has the lowest NPV, thus it should be the one to be removed

text: When you started your career, you were keen to get onto the management path and you worked day and night to get your PMP certification followed by the PgMP certification. Today, you are a highly regarded program manager in your organization and you are the one that people come to for advice. This warrants that

choices.text: Portfolio management will give you the choice to choose specific types of programs to undertake
Steering committee will give you a higher degree of autonomy
Management will give you a raise and make you a portfolio manager
You will assume the role of the steering committee in your programs

explanation:
Option A is not correct because it is the job of the portfolio manager and portfolio board to choose which programs to undertake based on strategic alignment. Option C is not correct because being a good program manager does not necessarily mean that you will be a good portfolio manager. Option D is not correct as, normally, the need for steering committee and role are different than of a program manager, and a well-established program requires both. Option B is the correct answer, the steering committee will give you a higher degree of autonomy and higher threshold for escalations
Reference: SPM V4 Page 86 - 6.3. This section clearly states this, however you can also check the following sections: Page 76 - 6.1.9, Page 84 - 6.2.4 and page 69

text: Programs are undertaken to deliver benefits to the sponsoring organization. Some of these benefits are targeted to the internal entities of the organization. In this context, consider you are managing a program to improve employee morale. You find it hard to define benefit level (value) because

choices.text: You are not experienced enough
You should consult with subject matter experts
This type of benefits is less easily quantified
You should consult the historical information

explanation:
Intangible benefits are harder to quantify and measure than tangible ones. In this case, employee morale is an intangible benefit
Reference: SPM V4 Page 44

text: The program managers work with the program management team for the entire course of the program in order to successfully deliver the benefits. Some programs succeed and others fail. You are now in closing phase and your program has delivered its benefits; you receive a call from the operations manager stating that he is not ready for the change. In this scenario, you should have

choices.text: Prepared a good benefits management plan
Been informing the functional managers
Added the operations manager to the steering committee
Let the operations manager prepare the benefit sustainment plan with you

explanation:
The benefits management plan shows how and when benefits are going to be delivered. It formally documents the activities necessary for achieving benefits (create, maximize and sustain benefits). It represents the baseline that guides the delivery of benefits during program performance. It also defines activities, processes and systems needed for the change, driven by the realization of benefits; and when the transition to operational state will occur. This plan will includes guidelines and approaches to perform the other options given in the answers set
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: Component A’s project manager has requested a resource which is currently being used by component B. This is an important resource and is required to work on component A in order to mitigate a spotted risk; however, the resource is also important for component B for 30% of her time each day. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Escalate to sponsor
Do resource prioritization
Do resource interdependency

explanation:
Here, the resource is to be shared among the components, as the components do not need her full time. The best option is to do resource interdependency and schedule the resource use accordingly between the different components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 133 - 8.2.7.1

text: One of your components managers has approached you with an opportunity that will benefit the program and speed up the delivery time dramatically. You have been avoiding the project manager’s request as you already have more important changes to undergo. What is the best course of action for the project manager?

choices.text: Escalate to project steering committee
Escalate to project CCB
Escalate to program steering committee
Escalate to program sponsor

explanation:
The change affects the program and not the particular project, which means that the next level of escalation needs to be to the program steering committee. If the change was affecting the component, the escalation level will be project CCB and then project steering committee
We have seen this on multiple occasions and multiple pages in the standard of which paragraph 6.1.6 is one.

text: Risks are an integral part of every program. During initiation, the program manager along with the sponsor and the available members of the program team, prepare an initial risk assessment which will be included in the presented business case. Risks are added, analyzed, refined and tracked throughout the program. You are now planning for a risk and you have already prepared your risk response, what next?

choices.text: Define management reserve
Define contingency reserve
Update the risk management plan
Derive a mitigation strategy

explanation:
After you prepare the risk response strategy and plan, you define contingency reserves. It is important to mention that program contingency reserve is different from the sum of its components contingency reserves. The management reserves are derived by the sponsor
Reference: SPM V4 Page 135 - 8.2.8.2 and 8.2.8.3

text: Due to the complexity and uncertainty of a program and the large number of stakeholders involved, the program manager needs to maintain a good level of communication and always present the right information at the right time. Which plan documents the process to communicate the right program information to the right person at the right time?

choices.text: Program communication management plan
Program stakeholder engagement plan
Program information management plan
Program benefits management plan

explanation:
Program communication management plan is a component of the program management plan. It describes how, when and by whom the information will be administered and communicated. It includes a communication strategy, communication table that outlines who is responsible to distribute what information to whom and using which channel, roles and responsibilities of communication management, constraints and resources allocated to communication
Reference: SPM V4 Page 112 - 8.1.2.2

text: Your team and yourself have worked hard for the tight schedule delivery of the program and are now in the closure phase. An unidentified issue was spotted in the product to be delivered to the customer. The delivery is due tomorrow and you do not have time to fix the issue prior to the delivery. In this case you should

choices.text: Deliver without mentioning the issue
Inform the customer about the issue and its impact
Escalate to sponsor
Escalate to steering committee

explanation:
As a program manager, you should be truthful to the program and all its stakeholders. You should inform the customer about the issue and its impact
Reference: code of conduct

text: You are in the definition phase of a 5-years program and you know that you need to plan thoroughly in order not to deviate from the purpose of the program and be able to continuously maintain viability of the program by integrating changes as needed. You have just completed the PWBS which will allow you to

choices.text: Develop the risk management plan
Identify critical success factors
Get authorization to start program work
Develop the program schedule

explanation:
PWBS helps in taking make or buy decisions and in estimations of cost, duration, quality and resources; in addition to risk identification and communications requirements analysis. From the above options, only option D is correct as good schedules can be built only after PWBS is established because consider you having a large task and you manager wants a schedule and related estimations; you will have to decompose the task into sub-tasks in order to be able to be able to give your manager what he/she wants
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11

text: Your program is delivering incremental benefits; you have already identified benefits and listed them in your charter, which was approved. During the conduct of the program, you realized that a key benefit was not valid anymore due to market change and you need to take corrective actions. What is your next step?

choices.text: Continue with the implementation as planned
Escalate to steering committee
Revising the beneﬁts management plan
Analyze the impact and the needed change

explanation:
Option A is incorrect. Option C is irrelevant as you first need to analyze the impact and then recommend the change to steering committee; following the decision, you will update the status across the affected documents. Option D is the correct answer. Option B comes next; it couldn’t be the first step, because the steering committee would have redirected the program manager to do the analysis and come back with his/her recommendations. All changes recommended by the program manager to the SC need to be analyzed, assessed and prepared prior to the recommendation, because the SC will not be doing the work, they will only look at your recommendations and numbers and take the decision accordingly
Reference: no particular reference. This is based on experience and based on multiple occurrences in the exam

text: Through program performance monitoring and controlling, the program management team continuously monitor the health of the program and ensure that it remains aligned with the strategic objectives and in-line with the planned values. During which phase you do program performance monitoring and controlling?

choices.text: Program definition
Program delivery phase
Program closure
Throughout the program

explanation:
The performance monitoring and controlling is done throughout the program delivery. As program manager and program team collect, measure and disseminate performance information and assess program trends.
Pay attention the question here is targeting the program performance based on the execution of this program and its components which happens during the delivery phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 101 - 7.2.2.3

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. You are now in the process of categorizing the stakeholders in order to analyze them. Which of the following is the best approach to get feedback about stakeholders’ attitudes regarding the program impact?

choices.text: Questionnaires and surveys
Interviews
Brainstorming sessions with the program team
Focus groups using open-ended questions

explanation:
Focus groups help in getting feedback about stakeholders’ attitudes regarding the program impact; it helps to understand the culture and concerns of stakeholders as well. In addition, the open-ended questions help solicit feedback furthermore by letting the stakeholders interact
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Which document visually represents the interactions of all stakeholders’ current and desired support and influence?

choices.text: Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Stakeholder Register
Stakeholder Map
Stakeholder strategy

explanation:
Stakeholder register lists stakeholders’ classifications, influence, support level and many other attributes. However, Stakeholder map shows which stakeholders to be engaged at what stage, and visually represents the interactions of all stakeholders’ current and desired support and influence
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: You have been assigned to a low-priority program in the organization and you have been struggling in getting the needed resources on time. You are working in a complex environment due to the changing market of the transportation industry. When working in complex environments with limited resources, the program manager should

choices.text: Establish Human Resource Management Plan
Establish a PMIS
Set up program change control board
Establish a good benefits realization plan

explanation:
Programs are complex, however, in this case, you have limited resources; this warrants that you do resource prioritization and optimization by assigning program roles and responsibilities. This is done as part of establishing a Human Resource management Plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 119 - 8.1.2.9 and Page 133 - 8.2.7

text: Your client has requested you to send him project managers in order to interview them before assigning them to components. Your client rejected the first project manager you sent. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Escalate to sponsor as it is his responsibility to handle resources
Reviewing the skill inventory
Call the client or meet him to find out the cause and take corrective action if any is needed
Escalate to steering committee

explanation:
Your client has rejected the first project manager you recommended. In this case, you do not take any assumption or decision; you consult the client, find out the rejection reason and take corrective actions if needed. Option A is not correct as it is the program manager responsibility to handle resources. Escalation to steering committee is not needed as the case is not significant. Option B here is not correct because maybe your client rejected the project manager because of his personality or because the project manager said something that irritated your client.
Pay attention in the exam, sometimes you do not get an option to meet the client, you then need to choose the closest option which is reviewing the sills inventory

text: Your client has requested you to send him project managers in order to interview them before assigning them to components. Your client has rejected multiple project managers you sent. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Escalate to sponsor as it is his responsibility to handle resources
Reviewing the skill inventory
Call the client or meet him to find out the cause and take corrective action if any is needed
Escalate to steering committee

explanation:
Your client has rejected multiple project managers you recommended. In this case, you should review the skill inventory and make sure that it reflects the client’s needs and expectations of a project manager. In addition, you should have already done option C earlier so that you do not waste your client's time and get their feedback on the issue quickly. Option A is not correct as it is the program manager responsibility to handle resources. Escalation to steering committee is not needed as the case is not significant.
Pay attention in the exam, sometimes you do not get an option to review the skills inventory, you then need to choose the closest option which is meeting the client

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. To resolve stakeholder expectations, which of the below techniques you use ?

choices.text: Brainstorming and expert judgment
Negotiation and Conflict Resolution
SWOT Analysis and Comparative analysis
Stakeholder checklists and program stake impact analysis

explanation:
Options A and D, along with organization analysis, are used as stakeholder identification tools and techniques. Option C is used in program planning; SWOT for charter and program management plan, and comparative advantage in business case. Option B is the only answer with the tools and techniques to resolve stakeholder expectations.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 16 - 1.7 and Page 65 - 5.4

text: Program manager is responsible for managing the financial aspects of the program with the oversight from the steering committee. Program payment schedules, component payment schedules and updates to program budget baseline are outputs of?

choices.text: Finance management planning
Component cost estimation
Procurement management
Program cost budgeting

explanation:
Based on SPM, Program cost budgeting has the following outputs: program payment schedules, component payment schedules and updates to program budget baseline. It is to note here that program payment schedules and component payment schedules are also outputs of Option A, however, option A established the program budget and baselines it. Option B has an output of component cost estimates and option C outputs are RFQ, RFP, IFB, proposal evaluation criteria, agreements administration plan and signed agreements.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 129 - 8.2.3.1

text: You are already mid-way through your program and the steering committee has been following up with you on a regular basis in order to ensure the delivery of benefits because this is the first program you manage in the company. Two of your components need the use of a scarce resource as a full-timer, and they have escalated this issue to you, what is your next course of action?

choices.text: Escalate to sponsor
Do resource interdependency
Do resource prioritization
Escalate to functional manager

explanation:
It is the responsibility of the program manager in this scenario to do resource prioritization and assign the scarce resource. There is no significant case for escalation to sponsor and there is no issue with or between resources to be escalated to the functional manager. Resource interdependency is to ensure that resources are correctly scheduled between components and with other programs in other portfolios; however in this case, components require the full usage (full-timer) of the resource
Reference: SPM V4 Page 133 - 8.2.7

text: You are in the definition phase of a 7-years program. You are determining the financial framework of the program with an oversight from the steering committee. Multiple funding options exist due to the strategic importance of the program to the medical industry. Program financial framework is used to?

choices.text: Coordinating available funding
Determine constraint and how funding is allocated
Defines and describes the program funding flows
All of the options

explanation:
Program financial framework is a high level plan for coordinating available funding, determining constraint and how funding is allocated. It Defines and describes the program funding flows so that money is spent as efficiently as possible. As it is developed, it may impact business case, program communication management plan and program engagement management plan, which are revised accordingly.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 114 - 8.1.2.4 and Page 165

text: During your program to design a new metro station for your city aimed to reduce traffic and travel time for the residents, you have been monitoring the financial environment due to the step-funding given by your government and trying to cope with it by planning for the necessary phase during each period. The objective of financing in program development is to?

choices.text: Obtain funds to bridge the gap between paying and getting benefits
Fund programs
Fund program components
Fund program and program components

explanation:
Based on SPM, the objective of financing in program development is to obtain funds to bridge the gap between paying and getting benefits; the gap is called negative cash balance
Reference: SPM V4 Page 114 - 8.1.2.4 - This section is usually missed by the students and this is why we stress on it. Usually you will get an exam question from it

text: You successfully managed your program to deliver the drug to cure cancer throughout the world and your sponsor has agreed to the closure. You are now working to transition your program to operations. Continued realization of the program benefits is ensured by the?

choices.text: Benefits sustainment plan
Program governance plan
Program management plan
Operations

explanation:
Based on SPM, the ongoing maintenance activities performed beyond the end of the program by the receiving organization to ensure benefits realization are documented in the benefits sustainment plan. This plan should be developed prior to program closure to identify risks, processes, metrics and tools necessary for continuous benefits realization.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 55 - 4.5

text: You are the program manager of a complex program in a risk adverse company; during the kick-off meeting, two employees moved out of the room as they were not interested in the change being proposed. What is your next course of action?

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Do nothing, as the functional managers are responsible for employees
Consult with the functional managers, do root-cause analysis and take appropriate actions
Escalate to functional manager

explanation:
Only two employees left the room, which means that the problem is not big and the functional managers should handle it. Functional managers handle resources issues. However as a program manager, it is your role to coordinate and collaborate with the functional managers for resolving resources issues.
You can find this question in other QB where they tell you to do nothing, however it is not correct. PMI is clear about this, you should work with functional managers to resolve such issues, because if you leave the functional managers and do not inform them of this, they might not notice it and the issue might persist or even get worse
Reference: SPM V4 Page 18 - 1.7.1

text: You are the program manager of a complex program in a risk adverse company; during the kick-off meeting, a lot of employees moved out of the room as they were not interested in the change being proposed. What is your next course of action?

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Do nothing, as the functional managers are responsible for employees
Consult with the functional managers, do root-cause analysis and take appropriate actions
Escalate to functional manager

explanation:
A lot of employees left the room, which warrants that you should consult with the functional managers, do root-cause analysis and take appropriate actions.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 18 - 1.7.1

text: Your operations manager is always asking about what will happen after the warranty period ends. You are currently in the closing stage and you want to make sure that the program is sustained after transition to operations. Which of the below may be required to oversee ongoing benefits?

choices.text: Post-transition meeting to get feedback
Post-transition meeting to document lessons learned
Check if there are any required residual activities
Final Performance review

explanation:
Options A, B and D are part of the closure phase steps, however, option C is the correct answer because residual activities may be required to oversee ongoing benefits and are transferred to the receiving organization; they may be done as part of a program or project
Reference: SPM V4 Page 139 - 8.3.1

text: Throughout the course of the program, the program manager and governance board work to ensure benefits realization within the program scope and company standards. Benefits are delivered through the work of components and component integration. Program ______ maps how the components will deliver outcomes in order to achieve program benefits?

choices.text: Roadmap
Architecture
Benefits management plan
Benefits register

explanation:
Program architecture maps how the components will deliver outcomes in order to achieve program benefits.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: You have a complex program and components in different countries. Each component is using a different architectural pattern; some are using waterfall and other agile. Components also are spanned across different cultures. What should you consider in this case?

choices.text: Define standard measurement criteria for all constituent projects within each country
Define measurement criteria for each constituent project based on the country and culture
Instruct the project managers to define measurement criteria each for his/her own project
Define standard measurement criteria for all constituent projects across all countries

explanation:
During the program initiation and in order to be able to effectively monitor and control the program, program manager defines standard measurement criteria for success for all constituent projects by analyzing stakeholder expectations and requirements across the projects. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 5 Program Life Cycle

text: During the course of the program, the program manager continuously tries to optimize benefits in order to maximize the benefits delivery. Which of the below warrants realizing more benefits?

choices.text: Enhance
Exploit
Share
Transfer

explanation:
Enhance = realize more benefits
Reference: PMBOOK; no need to revise it, all you need is in this QB

text: During the course of the program, the program manager continuously tries to optimize benefits in order to maximize the benefits delivery. Which of the below warrants maximizing benefits?

choices.text: Enhance
Exploit
Share
Transfer

explanation:
Exploit = maximize benefits
Reference: PMBOOK; no need to revise it, all you need is in this QB

text: You are in the definition phase of your 5-years program to build a subway to link three major cities in your country. You are currently preparing the business case and doing comparative advantage, which of the below is useful in this case?

choices.text: SWOT analysis
What-if analysis
Sensitivity analysis
Feasibility study

explanation:
Option A is used when preparing charter and program management plan. Option D is used while preparing business case but not for the purpose of comparative advantage. Option C is a quantitative risk assessment method and is irrelevant in this case. What-if analysis helps doing comparative advantage by doing the comparison between multiple options.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 39 - 3.4.2.1

text: You have delivered your program successfully to the operations. However, the call-center manager is worried about what will happen to the new system when the warranty period ends and you tender the sustainment plan to her in order to answer to her concern. Who plans the ongoing sustainment of benefits during program performance?

choices.text: Program manager and component project manager
Program manager
Component project manager
Program manager and operation manager

explanation:
Based on SPM, program manager and component project manager plan the ongoing sustainment of benefits during program performance. It is to note that, while these activities fall within program scope, they are operational and typically not managed as a program or project
Reference: SPM V4 Page 55 - 4.5

text: You are defining program components and are looking for project managers to manage these components. Your program is outsourced by a customer in another country and requires the component managers to be at all times in that country. Which of the below options is the most important for you when choosing a project manager for your program?

choices.text: Technical skills
Conflict resolution skills
Communication skills
Team management skills and knowledge of the country’s language

explanation:
Your program being offshore requires project managers with the country’s language in order to be able to integrate and speed up things and in order to better understand the cultural aspects of the implementation. In this scenario, option D is the most important. Options B and C are important for every project manager, however, option A is not.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 112 - 8.1.2.2 The cultural aspect is very important for the exam. We have included multiple questions on it to cover all the needed scenarios

text: Consider you are on the portfolio steering committee and choosing a program to undertake. You want to choose the most viable program, which requires you to check?

choices.text: Program charter
Program Roadmap
Program business case
Strategic plan

explanation:
Options A and B are not yet prepared as the program hasn’t been yet started. The viability of a program is checked in the business case. The business case is normally prepared prior to the start of a program. After the estimates of scope, resources and cost are done, program manager updates the business case if it was already created, or creates it in case it wasn’t. The viability of a program is continuously checked against the business case.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 26 - 2.3, in addition to insights from the exam. BC is used to check the viability as it includes the risk thresholds and the cost/benefit ration, alongside the ROI. All of this helps with ensuring viability

text: You are in the definition phase of your 5-years program to build a subway to link three major cities in your country. Your program is critical to the government as the congestion rate along with the stress rates have been affecting the growth of the country. In order to obtain initial validation and approval from the executive sponsor, you

choices.text: Define program charter
Define a high level roadmap with milestones and preliminary estimates
Define business case
Define benefits list

explanation:
During strategic program management, program manager defines a high level roadmap with milestones and preliminary estimates in order to obtain initial validation and approval from the executive sponsor. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 2 Strategic Program Management

text: You are mid-way through your program and due to changes; you realize the need to integrate two new components in order to realize expected benefits. Which of the following documents establishes the linkage of the new components to the already defined program components?

choices.text: Program charter
Program roadmap
Program scope statement
Program architecture

explanation:
Program architecture maps how the components will deliver capabilities and outcomes intended to achieve benefits. It provides the interlinking and interfacing between components. Another reason why we do not choose roadmap here is that roadmap only contains components that directly add to the value (major/milestone components) and not all components in a program; so here both the added components might not be part of the roadmap, because they might not be milestone components; however they are definitely part of the program architecture
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.2 - the architecture is rarely encountered in the exam, however we cover all its needed aspects in the QB

text: Program manager monitors the program performance and the business environment for any risk, issue or change that might affect the program, and act accordingly in order to ensure benefits are delivered. You monitor the business environment, program functionality requirements, and benefits realization in order to ensure

choices.text: Continue to the next phase
The program remains aligned with strategic objectives
Influence existing and future programs
Mitigate possible risks

explanation:
Through program governance, program manager monitors the business environment, program functionality requirements, and benefits realization in order to ensure the program remains aligned with strategic objectives. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 10 Governance

text: Throughout the course of the program, the program manager works to realize benefits within the constraints he/she has. Benefits are being continuously defined, revised, monitored and controlled. You have done benefits identification, defined critical success factors and developed a benefits register; what is next?

choices.text: Establish the benefits management plan
Start recording the progress of benefits
Update Roadmap and business case
Communicate with key stakeholders to define KPIs

explanation:
During benefits identification, the benefits register is developed based on business case, strategic plan and other information; it collects and lists the planned benefits and is used to measure and communicate the delivery of benefits. Then, it is reviewed with key stakeholders to develop KPIs. The KPIs associated qualitative analysis is done in benefits identification and quantitative analysis is done in benefits analysis and planning. This question is important to know the flow of the steps: Benefits identification is to analyze the available information about organizational and business strategies, and program drivers to identify benefits and list them in benefits register and qualify the benefits; it defines program objectives and critical success factors and identifies and qualifies business benefits. Benefits analysis and planning establishes the program benefits management plan and develops benefits metrics (KPIs) for monitoring and controlling benefits; it defines and prioritizes program components and performs quantitative analysis of benefits and defines metrics and KPIs
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1 targets the answer, the explanation is a summary from the entire Benefits Management Chapter

text: During the transition of a component, one of your stakeholders approached you and told you that she was not receiving status report on the component and she did not knew about the component until now. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Review stakeholder engagement plan
Review Communication Management Plan
Review benefits register
Re-send her all the reports at once and inform her that you will be assigning her a member of your team to explain the progress

explanation:
Program communication management includes the activities necessary for the timely and appropriate generation, collection, distribution, storage, retrieval and ultimate disposition of program information. Option A is an input to option B along with the stakeholder register. Option C is irrelevant and option D is not correct.
Pay attention in the exam, report distribution is always considered as part of communication management and this is why in case of not receiving a report, we consult the communication management plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 126 - 8.2.2.1 and Page 127 - 8.2.2.2

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Which of the below is the best way to communicate with stakeholders?

choices.text: Face to face meeting
Focus groups
Brainstorming
Surveys

explanation:
Face to face communication is the best way of communicating with stakeholders and soliciting the needed information for successful delivery of benefits.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 126 - 8.2.2.1 and experience and insights from our instructors

text: You noticed that your program manager had issues with monitoring and controlling the schedule of her project which was clearly noticeable due to the multiple delays she faced recently; you approached your project manager and gave her a suggestion, however, she delayed the decision which further delayed the schedule. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Fire her and put another competent project manager instead
Escalate the issue with the project manager to the sponsor
Coach the project manager
Escalate to steering committee

explanation:
The situation is not significant enough to go with options D or option B. As a program manager you coach your team members and component project managers and you train them on new skills such as decision making in this scenario.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 16 - 1.7, in addition to experience working as program managers

text: Stakeholders are engaged throughout the course of the program in order to ensure that the program successfully delivers its benefits. A program manager maintains a stakeholder register and continuously revises it in order to ensure correct and timely stakeholder engagement. Which of the below is part of the content of a stakeholder register?

choices.text: Influence
Impact
Classification
All of the options

explanation:
The stakeholder register lists stakeholders and categorizes their relationship to program (influence, support, etc.). It includes stakeholder influence, impact, classification, engagement strategy, communication preference, is influenced by, is in conflict with, role in the program, title, name, etc. It records the degree of opposition or support to the program and may contain sensitive information e.g. political, legal, etc. and have restrictions to accessing it.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 60 - 5.1

text: Contracts are signed and related work is initiated throughout the program lifecycle. Contracts are normally administered at component level and the program manager maintains oversight on the financial expenditure of a contract and on its closure requests. Which of the below lists the correct steps of closing a contract?

choices.text: There are no outstanding contractual issues, deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made,
All payments have been made, deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, there are no outstanding contractual issues
Deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made, there are no outstanding contractual issues
Deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, budget is closed, all payments have been made, there are no outstanding contractual issues

explanation:
Program procurement closure formally closes out each agreement after ensuring that deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made and there are no outstanding contractual issues. In case of early termination, program procurement closure manages the termination of active contracts to avoid unnecessary costs.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 140 - 8.3.3

text: Program manager spends a good amount of time preparing the schedule. From the scope statement, the program manager derives the PWBS which will help in the make-or-buy decisions, and in estimating the cost, quality, resource and duration. To what level should the PWBS be decomposed?

choices.text: First or second level
Until it reaches the work packages
Level of control required
Only to show the program packages

explanation:
PWBS is decomposed to the level of control required. PWBS is the output of baselining scope statement. PWBS helps in make or buy decisions, estimations of cost, duration, quality and resources; it also helps in risk identification and communication requirements analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 123 - 8.1.2.12

text: Throughout the course of the program, the program manager works to realize benefits within the constraints he has. Benefits are being continuously defined, revised, monitored and controlled. You have done benefits identification, defined critical success factors and developed a benefits register. Which of the below is part of the content of a benefits register?

choices.text: Benefit ID, details, expected improvement start date, expected target achievement date, target value, benefit realization constraint
Benefit ID, details, stakeholders affected by the benefit, target value, benefit realization constraint, benefit progress
Benefit ID, details, expected funding date, expected return on investment, target value, benefit realization constraint
Benefit ID, details, alternative approaches, target value, benefit realization constraint

explanation:
The benefit register contains the benefit ID, details, expected improvement start date, expected target achievement date, target value, benefit realization constraint and benefit progress. Benefits register doesn’t contain stakeholders affected by the benefit, expected funding date, expected return on investment, nor alternative approaches. In addition, the benefits register includes the list of planned benefits, mapping of benefits to strategic objectives, mapping of benefits to components as in roadmap, KPIs and thresholds, risk assessment and probability of achievement, responsible party, process for measuring progress and tracking and communication processes
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1, in addition to multiple insights from exam questions

text: Your company has acquired company B and multiple projects were transferred from company B to your program. The project managers are not reporting in the format required by your program and even you have met with them regularly and informed them of the need for a unified reporting, they refuse to comply. What should be your next action?

choices.text: Request the PMO to include company B reporting standards to your program
You have no other option but to comply to them and modify their reports to your needs
Use forced communication and inform them that strict actions will be taken in case of non-compliance
Do nothing and continue as planned

explanation:
Similar Project Managers' non-compliance can be diffused with forced communication as you have already tried other options to solve this, and you are left with forced communication which is a correct method to be used in such situations and reflects your experience and maturity for taking the correct level of handling issues.
Reference: Code of Conduct

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. From the below options, which are considered as key stakeholders?

choices.text: Press, component managers, competitors
Legal department manager, component managers, competitors
Program management team, component managers, media consultants
Program management team, family members, sponsors

explanation:
Key stakeholders include but are not limited to legal, component managers, competitors, program management team, sponsors, etc.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 61 - 5.1

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Throughout the program, you realize that stakeholders have different and/or contradicting views of the program objectives. You have reached a point where everyone is happy; however, you needed to negotiate on multiple points and compromise on others. You performed these activities as part of

choices.text: The communication strategy
Program stakeholder engagement
The communications log
Stakeholder analysis and planning

explanation:
The mentioned scenario mentions activities done as part of the stakeholder engagement (SHE); during SHE, program manager require negotiation skills and undertake many facilitated negotiation sessions to resolve conflicts
Reference: SPM V4 Page 65 - 5.4

text: You have good relations with your customer and you are managing a program for him. The customer doesn’t require you to send him performance reviews as he believes that you can manage to deliver a successful program. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Don’t send performance reviews because the customer requested it
Send the performance reviews as planned
Consult your steering committee for advice
Consult your sponsor for advice

explanation:
A program manager should send the performance reviews as planned because it is important for following up on the progress in order to successfully deliver program benefits.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 125 - 8.2.2 and multiple insights from exam questions

text: You have been newly assigned to manage a program to implement a new software system across the entire enterprise in all of its branches. You identify organizational benefits for the potential program using research methods such as market analysis and high level cost-benefit analysis in order to develop?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Program roadmap
Preliminary program scope and define benefits realization plan

explanation:
During strategic program management, you identify organizational benefits for the potential program using research methods such as market analysis and high level cost-benefit analysis in order to develop preliminary program scope and define benefits realization plan. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 6 Strategic Program Management

text: At closure, a lot of stakeholders have changed since the beginning and board members changed as well; a new board member just joined the company and has vague understanding of her roles and responsibilities. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Show her the benefit management plan
Show her the governance plan
Update the governance plan to include the new stakeholder
Continue with the closure

explanation:
Since you are already in the closure phase, your best course of action is to show her the governance plan which includes the responsibilities of the different governance roles. There is no need for updating the governance plan, in addition the plan contains responsibilities for roles and not for individuals, so it is not updated when an individual changes, it is updated when a role changes. Options A and D are not correct in this scenario.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 70 - 6.1.1.1

text: You have successfully reached to the closure phase of your program to deliver a drug that will cure cancer instantly around the world. You have also transitioned the program to operational entities in the company and are currently conducting the review meeting. Which of the below is an output of post review meetings?

choices.text: Obtain feedback and capture lessons learned
Close the budget
Make sure procurements are closed
PMIS archival

explanation:
During closure phase, post review meetings occur before the financial closure. They are held to obtain feedback and capture lessons learned. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 34 Closing the Program

text: You have successfully reached to the closure phase of your program to deliver a drug that will cure cancer instantly around the world. You have closed all components and related contracts. You have just got stakeholders approval for closure, what do you do next?

choices.text: Knowledge transition
Program transition
PMIS archival and resource disposition
All of the options

explanation:
During closure phase, you obtain stakeholder approval for closure in order to initiate close-out activities: Knowledge transition, program transition and PMIS archival (program documents, lessons learned, etc.) and resource disposition. You execute the transition or close-out of all program and constituent plans in order to meet program objectives and ongoing operational sustainability. You report lessons learned and best practices observed and archive to the knowledge repository in order to support future programs and organizational development
N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Tasks 32 to 35 Closing the Program

text: Programs deliver the intended benefits fully at closure or incrementally throughout the delivery phase. Some programs realize full benefits and others have to transition the program to operational entities to ensure the realization of benefits on the long run. If your program is based on incremental deliveries, what do you do with components after they deliver the intended benefits?

choices.text: Leave them open until program closure phase where they will be closed
Close them after delivering their outputs
Transition them without closure until reaching the closure phase
Put them on hold until the resources are no longer needed

explanation:
During benefit delivery, components are initiated, planned, executed, transitioned and closed.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 91 - Figure 7-1 and Page 97 - 7.1.3.3

text: Your program to deliver a new metro easing the life of the residents and decreasing travel time due to the busy city streets has begun. You are preparing a business case and you have already ensured the strategic alignment with organization and have performed a feasibility study; what else do you need to do?

choices.text: Benefit – cost analysis
Develop a high level milestone plan
Market analysis
List components

explanation:
Of the given options, option A is the most suitable answer as the business case includes a cost-benefit analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: You have been assigned by the sponsor to manage a high priority program in your organization. The program is already in its planning phase and the previous manager has retired. The planning phase spans a full year and is considered critical to the successful delivery of a program. As a first step, which document you study?

choices.text: Scope statement
Charter
Business case
Program management plan

explanation:
In order to quickly understand the program, you review the scope statement which describes why the program was undertaken, the work involved, etc. scope is usually described in the form of expected benefits and sometimes user stories or scenarios; it encompasses all benefits to be delivered by the program, reflected in a WBS
Reference: SPM V4 Page 11 -Table 1-1, Page 110 - 8.1.1.10 and Page 113 - 8.1.2.12

text: You have been assigned by the sponsor to manage a high priority program in your organization. The program is already in its delivery phase and the previous manager has retired. The delivery is already mid-way and the program is being delivered as planned. As a first step, which document you study?

choices.text: Roadmap
Charter
Business case
Program management plan

explanation:
The roadmap is periodically assessed and updated to ensure alignment with master schedule. Joining a program in its delivery phase requires the program manager to first check the roadmap to know where the program is and discover its pace, in addition to benefits status.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2 and Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: You have been working hard in the delivery phase of your program to build a new metro station in order to reduce the travel time between two cities and so far, you have managed to stay on track. An electrical shutdown occurred in the city and the operation stopped for two days with a loss of $150k and a slight delay in schedule. What should you do?

choices.text: Escalate to sponsor
Escalate to Steering committee
Escalate to executive management
Analyze impact and approve change request

explanation:
The disaster had already occurred and the impact is well known, so the best course of action is to consult the steering committee. Option B would have been correct if you want to escalate the issue directly when the disaster occurred and not two days afterwards. Option C is not the first level of escalation here and option D is invalid because you already know the impact and the magnitude of the change is big, which requires the approval of steering committee. In this case, the escalation will be an expedited one where the steering committee will directly take action or escalate to sponsor for decision.
Sometime in the exam, if you get that a disaster had occurred and you directly needed a decision, you need to choose the escalation to sponsor, if the option is not given, escalate to executive management. One of both options would definitely be there.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 73 - 6.1.6

text: You are starting to prepare a business case for a program and the sponsor informed you that the company is undergoing budget cuts due to financial difficulties and your program might not be fully funded. What must you do in this case?

choices.text: Prepare an initial risk assessment
Conduct a market study
Estimate the high-level ﬁnancial and non-ﬁnancial beneﬁts
Perform a SWOT analysis

explanation:
Option D is used when establishing Charter and Program Management Plan, option C is done to prioritize projects, option B is not relevant in this scenario as there is a major risk that the program might not be fully funded, leaving us with the correct answer, which is option A. Risk assessment is part of the business case and constitute an important input to the steering committee when approving the business case or denying it. When risks reach a level above the company accepted threshold, program will be terminated
Reference: SPM V4 Page 109 - 8.1.1.8

text: Funding differs between programs and between different components of a program. The funding organization may impose limitations which will be considered as constraints in the planning. One of your program components is funded externally, which of the below is correct?

choices.text: Programs can be funded externally but components can’t
Components can be funded externally but programs can’t
Both components and programs can be funded externally
Both components and programs can’t be funded externally

explanation:
The funding source is established during program financial framework establishment and the funding can be external or internal for both programs and components.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 114 - 8.1.2.4

text: A program manager maintains a close look on the program benefits throughout the program lifecycle. Governance board is also focused on delivering benefits and conduct regular meetings to ensure it. Benefits are the most important assets of a program and you constantly work to realize them. Early in your program, you have prepared a benefits management plan in order to guide benefits delivery, and guide benefits monitoring and controlling throughout the course of the program. Which of the below represents the performance baseline of a program?

choices.text: Benefit management plan
Benefits register
Performance reports
Program charter

explanation:
The benefits management plan is the performance baseline, which guides the benefits delivery as the program progresses. The benefits management plan shows how and when benefits are going to be delivered. It formally documents the activities necessary for achieving benefits (create, maximize and sustain benefits). It represents the baseline that guides the delivery of benefits during program performance. It also defines activities, processes and systems needed for the change, driven by the realization of benefits; and when the transition to operational state will occur. It should define each benefit with its assumptions and achievement, link components output to planned program outcomes, defines metrics (KPIs) and procedure to measure benefits, defines roles and responsibilities to manage benefits, how will benefits be transitioned to operational state, how will the capabilities be transitioned for sustaining benefits and provides a process for managing overall benefits management effort
Reference: SPM V4 Page 48 - 4.2 and Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. During the course of the program, a risk occurred, which is above your authority level. Which of the below is the correct action to take?

choices.text: You record it and assign a member to follow up on it
You record it, analyze it and recommend change to steering committee
You directly escalate to steering committee
You communicate it with all stakeholders

explanation:
Because the risk is above the program manager authority level, he should record the risk, analyze and escalate to steering committee. If he directly escalates, the steering committee will advise him to go analyze the risk and then come back with analysis results.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 134 - 8.2.8

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Program manager needs to maintain communication targeted to each stakeholder or stakeholder groups. You are starting a program to build a new cars line for your client that will be more fuel efficient and has more safety features. From the below, which option lists key stakeholders?

choices.text: Car dealers, component managers and sponsors
Customers, legal and executive management
Component managers, media consultants and customer
All of the options

explanation:
This question is tricky, however, it has been seen on multiple occurrences in the exam and the rationale behind it is simple. Key stakeholders in this case are components managers, sponsors and car dealers who will sell the cars for you. The customer is an important stakeholder; however he/she is not a direct stakeholder in this case, because he/she is not your client, your clients are the car dealers who will sell the cars to the customer. Option C is not correct as media consultants are not key stakeholders.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 61 - 5.1

text: You have prepared a performance report and presented the above to steering committee. Having looked at these numbers, which of the below is true?

choices.text: Program is over budget and ahead of schedule
Program is over budget and behind schedule
Component A is under budget and behind schedule
Component C is over budget and ahead of schedule

explanation:
The only correct answer is C because: CPI > 0 means under budget, and CPI < 0 means over budget; SPI > 0 means ahead of schedule and SPI < 0 means behind schedule
Reference: EVM from PMBOOK or found abundantly on the WEB

text: One of your program’s components will be outsourced. You are currently preparing a Statement Of Work (SOW) in order to send RFPs to the qualified sellers list. One of your steering committee members approaches you and asks you to grant the contract to a seller that he knows will do a great job. You find out that the seller has been removed from the qualified sellers list and you inform the steering committee member, however, he insists on selecting him. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Escalate to executive management
Escalate to sponsor
Inform sponsor, add the seller to the qualified sellers list and continue your process

explanation:
This is an unethical practice from the member and should be escalated. Your normal escalation would be to steering committee, however it is not correct to face the steering committee member straight in front of other members. In this case, you escalate to the sponsor who might talk directly with the steering committee member and can include you in the conversation as well.
Reference: experience, escalation process from the SPM and multiple insights from exam questions

text: You have been managing a program with a low risk tolerance and you have been managing potential risks closely in order to ensure proper mitigation. A new CEO joined your company and he is well known to take more risks than his precedent CEO. What should be you first course of action?

choices.text: Revise and update the business case
Revise and update the charter
Revise and update the roadmap
Continue as planned

explanation:
The questions points out that the CEO is more risk tolerant than his precedent CEO, which means that the risk profile of the company will change. As a program manager, you first work on updating the business case taking into consideration the new risk profile. The risk assessment determines the probability of successful delivery of benefits and risk response strategies and plan based on the new risk profile.
Risk assessment is parallel to the business case development, hence the need to re-do it and update the business case accordingly
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1 and Page 42 - 3.5.3

text: Program manager is the champion for change. The program manager integrates the change in the most efficient way in order to ensure proper realization and sustainment of benefits. During the course of the program and due to uncertainty, a new change needs to be integrated in the program. You then

choices.text: Analyze and update the benefits realization and sustainment plans
Analyze roadmap
Escalate to steering committee
Continue as planned as changes are normal in a program

explanation:
During strategic program management, you analyze and update the benefits realization and sustainment plans for uncertainty, risk identification, risk mitigation, and risk opportunity in order to determine if corrective actions are necessary and communicate to stakeholders. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 7 Benefits Management

text: You are managing a sporting event in a rural village. After the event, you plan on leaving the sporting arena and gaming material for the village. Few important stakeholders in the village are still against it. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Accept the fact that some of the stakeholders will be negative and you need to ignore them
Add the negative stakeholders to program steering committee

Meet with them one on one if you can or as a group, listen to them and let them know that they will have a sporting arena after the event and that multiple jobs will be offered to the youth during the event.
Focus only on positive stakeholders

explanation:
As a program manager you try to collaborate with stakeholders and diffuse their negativity. You can’t ignore them as they could have a drastic impact on the course of the program and could terminate it as well. Option C best describes the action that a program manager takes. This is part of the correct stakeholder engagement
Reference: SPM V4 Page 57 - 5 (the entire chapter targets this points), in addition to multiple insights from exam questions

text: You are in the definition phase of your program to deliver 5 new ice cream flavors and you are aware that this phase is the most important phase in order to guide the remainder of the program. You have finished the stakeholders’ analysis and have prepared the stakeholder engagement strategy and plan. What is next?

choices.text: Stakeholder engagement
Update stakeholder register
Issue the stakeholder engagement plan
Update business case

explanation:
Stakeholder engagement is the next activity after defining the stakeholder engagement strategy and plan. The steps in stakeholder engagement are as follows:
Stakeholder identification using the register template and tools and techniques from the stakeholder engagement plan document which is drafted prior to starting identification
Stakeholder analysis using input from the drafted engagement plan i.e. what questions to ask to stakeholders and tools and techniques for analysis
Stakeholder engagement strategy which will result in the update of the stakeholder engagement plan with the new strategy, standards and guidelines for component stakeholders engagement
Stakeholder engagement which will continuously make changes to the plan through monitoring and controlling. It is to note that communication management plan is derived from stakeholder engagement plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 57 - 5 (the answer is a summary of the steps)

text: You have been managing your program successfully and you have been doing a good job integrating the individual components to maximize the delivery of benefits.
