You have been integrating costs, schedules and effort of components throughout the program. As a program manager you develop and support the program integration management plan in order to

choices.text: Ensure operational alignment with program strategic objectives
Ensure continuation to the next phase
Prepare your master schedule
Preparing your program roadmap

explanation:
Through program governance, program manager develops and supports the program integration management plan in order to ensure operational alignment with program strategic objectives N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 11 Governance

text: During the planning phase, the program manager uses the scope baseline and the scope management plan to prepare the schedule management plan and derives, using the PWBS, the master schedule and management control points. Which of the below is part of the content of master schedule?

choices.text: Stakeholder engagement activities
Program-level risk mitigation activities
Individual component schedules
All of the options

explanation:
The program master schedule is a top-level program planning document that defines the individual component schedules and interdependencies among components, components milestones i.e. start and end dates; it includes as well stakeholder engagement activities, program-level risk mitigation activities and program-level reviews.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11

text: You are mid-way through your program and you are now collecting performance information in preparation of the next checkpoint. A project manager approached you with an issue with one of his resources; the resource is always late and reluctant for any advice. What would you suggest to the project manager?

choices.text: Escalate to functional manager
Escalate to project CCB
Escalate to project steering committee
Escalate to program steering committee

explanation:
First of all, checkpoint means a phase-gate review. Although it is put here with no real relevance to the actual question, you should keep in mind that checkpoint means phase-gate because PMI tend to use it in the exam.
By default, the organization is a matrix organization unless mentioned otherwise. This is clearly a misconduct issue with the resource and has to be escalated to his/her functional manager who is responsible for resources. All other options are irrelevant
Reference: SPM V4 Page 18 - 1.7.1

text: You have been working hard to keep the program to launch the new remote car design to the market on track and you have been integrating multiple changes along the way in order to keep the program aligned with the organization's objectives and goals. Your program is to deliver soon. You sponsor approached you in order to implement a mandatory change. What should you do?

choices.text: Analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request
Refuse to add changes as the program is nearing closure
Escalate to steering committee about the situation
Ask the component managers to send their feedback about implementing the change

explanation:
You do not question mandatory changes; you analyze them and take actions accordingly. In this case no one came to you with an allegation of a mandatory change, it is the sponsor who knows best and who is responsible for the success of the program. What you need to do is accept the change and start working on assessing and analyzing it
Reference: SPM V4 Page 125 - 8.2.1, in addition to insights from exam questions and from our instructors

text: You have been working hard to keep the program to launch the new remote car design to the market on track and you have been integrating multiple changes along the way in order to keep the program aligned with the organization's objectives and goals. Your program is to deliver soon. You sponsor approached you and asked you to add a change which he thinks is beneficial. You do not agree with the sponsor and know that the change will only result in wasting time. What should you do?

choices.text: Analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request
Refuse to add changes as the program is nearing closure
Escalate to steering committee about the situation and seek advice
Ask the component managers to send their feedback about implementing the change

explanation:
Even if you do not agree to it, you will analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request. The CR will include the requestor who is the sponsor and based on your recommendation, you will list the numbers and facts that make this component a non-beneficial one. The SC committee in this case will most probably not recommend the pursuit of the component unless it is a mandatory one (legal, compliance, etc.)
Reference: experience, and insights from multiple exam questions

text: You have been working hard to keep the program to launch the new remote car design to the market on track and you have been integrating multiple changes along the way in order to keep the program aligned with the organization's objectives and goals. Your program is to deliver soon. Your sponsor approached you and asked you to add a change which will enhance program benefits. What should you do?

choices.text: Analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request
Refuse to add changes as the program is nearing closure
Escalate to steering committee about the situation and seek advice
Ask the component managers to send their feedback about implementing the change

explanation:
Even if the change is beneficial, you will analyze the impact of the change and recommend a change request. The CR will include the requestor who is the sponsor and based on your recommendation, you will list the numbers and facts that make this component a beneficial one. The SC committee in this case will most probably recommend the pursuit of the component unless they find it non-strategically aligned.
Reference: experience, and insights from multiple exam questions

text: You program to deliver the cancer drug to cure all the patients around the world has been performing as expected and you are nearing the closure phase. In your program, one component is already in the closure phase and has been completed under budget. What should you do?

choices.text: Propose more benefits to be added to the sponsor
Take the team out for lunch and build team morale
Use the money on a different component to speed it up
Return to sponsor

explanation:
This question is tricky; option A is not valid as the component is already completed and you can’t add benefits to it. Option B is not correct. Option C and option D are confusing, however, you can’t use the money to speed up other components by yourself, you’ll need to return the money to the sponsor, propose speeding up another component and if it was agreed, the sponsor will authorize releasing the money to speed up the other component.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 140 - 8.3.4 - this section states that at component level the resources might be transferred to another component, however, this happens in stages, you return to sponsor and recommend the usage on another component, then the sponsor authorizes this

text: You are during the sixth month of your 2-years program and multiple changes are being reviewed in order to take go/no-go decisions on multiple components. One of the components has delivered the intended benefits and is already in the closure phase. Another component will need to undergo a big change in order to realign it with the program objectives. What is the first step that you will do next?

choices.text: Analyze change
Escalate to steering committee
Record change
Assign a team member to handle it

explanation: No matter the scale of a change, you first step is always recording the change. All other options come later.

text: Programs normally use the procurement policies and procedures of the organization, unless the program has particular procurement specifications; in this case, the program manager will use the organization procurement processes and tailor them with the support from PMO to the program’s needs. Which of the below options represents the correct steps for program procurement?

choices.text: RFP, RFI, RFQ, Bidder conference (BC)
RFI, RFP, RFQ, BC
BC, RFI, RFP, RFQ
RFQ, RFI, RFP, BC

explanation:
When procuring, you first send a Request For Information RFI in order to have information about the solutions that the vendors have, then you issue a Request For Proposal RFP to get a proposal for the solution you want followed by a Request For Quote. If any of the vendors have a question, you call for a bidder conference.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 131 - 8.2.5, PMBOOK and experience

text: You are the program manager of a complex program in a risk adverse company; during the last phase gate review, you realized that the program will not be able to deliver in the given benefits window and will probably be over budget when delivering the benefits. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Recommend termination of the program
Do a fast tracking
Do critical chain method
Continue as planned and try to fix the performance until the next phase gate review

explanation:
The program will neither deliver on time nor on budget. The best course of action is to recommend termination. Option B will not help because it shortens the schedule but it increases the risks which is not acceptable in this case for a risk adverse company. Option C addresses the availability of resources which is not an issue in this scenario. Option D is not correct
Reference: SPM V4 Page 90 - 7.1

text: When the program manager is assigned, normally the work on the program begins. The program manager starts with the initial assessments with the support of the sponsor and sponsoring organization. In order to develop, validate, and assess the program objectives, priority, feasibility, readiness, and alignment to the organization’s strategic plan, you

choices.text: Evaluate the organization’s capability by consulting with organizational leaders
Design business case
Meet with stakeholders
Define scope statement

explanation:
During strategic program management, you evaluate the organization’s capability by consulting with organizational leaders in order to develop, validate, and assess the program objectives, priority, feasibility, readiness, and alignment to the organization’s strategic plan. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 5 Strategic Program Management

text: You are appointed as a program manager for the development of new remote cars. The cars need to be available for a two-hour play time on a full battery and has to be pushed to the market within one year in order to beat competition. You are mid-way through the program and a lot of requirements have changed since the start, in addition, 55% of the budget has been used so far and the remaining budget will barely suffice the program. In addition, a good number of the remote cars are failing inspection. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Continue as planned with components transitions and closures
Re-baseline budget
Conduct a phase gate review
Requesting a quality assurance audit

explanation:
55% of the budget is a fair number being mid-project, and the question clearly states that the budget will suffice, even if barely; so there is no need to re-baseline budget. Option A is incorrect as you have a clear issue which is that a big number of cars are failing inspection, option C will not help in this case as phase get review are conducted to make a go/no-go decision. Option D is the correct answer; a quality assurance audit will help assess the results of the inspection done as part of Quality Control
Reference: SPM V4 Page 132 - 8.2.6

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Program manager needs to maintain communication targeted to each stakeholder or stakeholder groups. One of the company’s executive managers is wondering about why the program was undertaken. Which document do you present to him?

choices.text: Program charter
Scope statement
Business case
Benefits management plan

explanation:
The sponsor, CEO, or any executive manager are more interested in the business case in order to check the investment vs. profit. For other stakeholders, scope statement would suffice as the BC might contain sensitive information (monetary values, ratios, investments, etc.) and should not be available to any stakeholder.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1 and multiple insights from exam questions

text: Your program is mid-way through the delivery phase and it is performing as planned. So far, you have been managing the program successfully. One of your component project managers approached you asking advice on which analysis tool to use when analyzing risks. Which of the below would you suggest to the project manager?

choices.text: Impact vs. probability
Monte Carlo analysis
Qualitative techniques
Consult with project steering committee

explanation:
When asked for an analysis technique, you always provide quantitative techniques i.e. Monte Carlo analysis, What-if analysis and sensitivity analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 135 - 8.2.8.2, in addition to experience and multiple exam insights

text: You program is a low-priority program and right from the start of the program you noticed delays in supplying the program resources from the functional departments. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Resource leveling
Escalate to sponsor
Escalate to steering committee
Escalate to functional managers

explanation:
When there is delay in getting resources, you escalate to the SC first as it is usually formed of individuals with functional responsibilities for managing the different aspects and resources of the program. Option B is the next level of escalation as the sponsor has the ultimate responsibility for securing resources, however you should pass by the SC first. Option A is irrelevant because it targets resources efficiency and consistency which is not the case here. Option D is correct as well however escalating to SC usually covers it. Option D is mostly used when there is a conflict or a need for a certain resource (for quicker resolution)
Reference: SPM V4 Page 81 - 6.2.2

text: You are the program manager of a complex program in a risk adverse company; during the last phase gate review, you realized that the program will not be able to deliver in the given benefits window and will probably be over budget when delivering the benefits. You recommended program termination and steering committee approved it. What is your next course of action?

choices.text: Update business case and close the program
Update program charter and close the program
Update program benefits management plan and close the program
Update the status of the program across all program documents and close the program

explanation:
Program status should be updated across all program documentation and program should start the closure phase activities. No matter the reason for termination, closure phase activities should be performed.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 78 - 6.1.12

text: Your stakeholders on your program to deliver the next-generation remote control car are interested in knowing the progress of a program in delivering its benefits. Using which of the below, the program manager tracks the benefits delivery progress and reports to stakeholders?

choices.text: Benefits management plan
Benefits register
Business case
Benefits list

explanation:
The benefits register records benefits progress and program manager extract the benefits report from it in order to send it to stakeholders.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1

text: Your company was outsourced by a client in order to manage a program to do a company restructuring. You were appointed as the program manager. You realize that many employees will lose their jobs following the restructuring. You should start by?

choices.text: Foster relationships with stakeholders
Defining the business case
Understanding the organization culture
Benefits list

explanation:
Your first step when undertaking a program is to understand the organization culture and the acceptance of the change to be driven by the program. You will then prepare program vision, stakeholder identification and start with you initial assessments to prepare the business case.
Reference: we have seen multiple questions related to culture as it is an important concept. In the exam you normally get one question on it, however in our QB we covered all the possibilities

text: You are in program definition phase and are currently evaluating program objectives relative to regulatory and legal constraints, social impacts, sustainability, cultural considerations, political, climate and ethical concerns. You do this in order to?

choices.text: Identify organizational benefits
Ensure stakeholder alignment and program deliverability
Obtain organizational leadership approval
Perform an initial risk assessment

explanation:
During the strategic program management, program manager evaluates program objectives relative to regulatory and legal constraints, social impacts, sustainability, cultural considerations, political climate and ethical concerns. You do this in order to ensure stakeholder alignment and program deliverability N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 8 Strategic Program Management

text: The program manager tries throughout the program to resolve conflicts arising between stakeholders in order to maintain efficient benefits delivery. You notice that two of your sponsors are in conflict about buying or leasing a facility to be used by multiple components. What should be your best course of action?

choices.text: Let them sit together and solve their issues
Invite them to a steering committee meeting in order to solve their issue in front of everybody
Invite them together and listen to both, clarify program needs and work from there onward
Escalate to CEO

explanation:
Program manager collaborate with stakeholders and defuse any conflict such as in this case. Option C is the best approach to be taken.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 65 - 5.4

text: The program manager spends most of his time communicating with stakeholders to engage them with the program, gain and maintain their support. In order to foster relationships with your customer, you invited him to dinner and offered a small gift to him. This is

choices.text: Considered a bribe and it should not be done
It is always a good thing to foster relationships with customers
You should inform the sponsor of what you did in order for them to know that you are doing a good job
You should inform the steering committee of what you did in order for them to know that you are doing a good job

explanation:
In any case, this act is considered as a bribe and should not be accepted.
Reference: Code of conduct. As a program manager, you should remain transparent and have a high level of integrity

text: The program manager spends most of his time communicating with stakeholders to engage them with the program, gain and maintain their support. You customer invited you to dinner, you know that you should be fostering relationships and you

choices.text: Consult the steering committee first and then go to dinner
Go to dinner as you will be fostering relationships with customer
Escalate to sponsor first
Take a gift with you

explanation:
When a customer invites you to dinner, you consult the steering committee first and then go to dinner. You do not take gifts as they will be considered as bribes. Dinners are not bribes, they are ways to enhance the collaboration and relationship.
Reference: Code of Conduct and Stakeholder Engagement. As a program manager, you should maintain a good relation with the stakeholders, however you should not pass to a stage where you take bribes from them.

text: Your company is facing financial issues and has to terminate multiple programs as a result of this. When making the decision on which programs to terminate, Corporate Governance Board examines

choices.text: The number of resources used in each program
The strategic alignment
The estimate to complete of each program
Each program’s schedule

explanation:
In this case, the organization should be focusing on the strategic alignment of each program with the organizational strategies; all other options are irrelevant in this scenario
The 2 most important aspects to look for are strategic alignment and value delivery. Strategic Alignment comes in first place because a non-aligned component is not worth the execution even if it delivers value.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 52 - 4.3.2

text: During the program planning phase, you prepare the infrastructure that will guide the program and its components through the delivery phase. Which of the below represent the primary purpose of program infrastructure?

choices.text: Establish the management and technical resources of the program and its components
Oversight, integration and optimization of program components
Collect, measure and disseminate performance information
Optimize or integrate costs of individual components

explanation:
The primary purpose of program infrastructure is to establish the management and technical resources of the program and its components. Program infrastructure development takes as input the program management plan, best practices library, roadmap and organization policies and guidelines. Option B is a purpose of program delivery management. Option C is a purpose of program performance monitoring and controlling. Option D is a purpose of program activities and integration management.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 99 - 7.2.2.1

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Program manager needs to maintain communication targeted to each stakeholder or stakeholder groups. The program team and you have identified stakeholders who have interest/influence in the program. What is your next step?

choices.text: Analyze stakeholders
Develop a stakeholder map
Develop a stakeholder register
Develop a stakeholder engagement strategy

explanation:
The question asks about the next step, which is to develop the stakeholder register; if the question was about the next activity, it would be to analyze stakeholders; Option B is done as part of analysis and option D is done after analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 60 - 5.1

text: You are working in a matrix organization and resources from a variety of functional departments are working on your program and related components. Which of the following is true about your role?

choices.text: Resolve issues between resources
Establish a reward system
Develop a good charter to set clear roles and responsibilities
Release resources when they are no longer needed

explanation:
In a matrix organization, the functional managers are responsible for the resources, thus option A is not correct. Option B is irrelevant in the scenario and option C is incorrect as the charter does not define roles and responsibilities (they are mainly defined in each plan e.g. governance roles and responsibilities are defined in the governance plan, etc.). Option D is the only correct option, the program managers releases resources when they are no longer needed
Reference: SPM V4 Page 133 - 8.2.7.1

text: You are appointed as a program manager for the development of new remote cars. The cars need to be available for a two-hour play time on a full battery and has to be pushed to the market within one year in order to beat competition. You are mid-way through the program and everything is going according to plan. However, you are finding it more and more tiring to ensure stakeholders receive the appropriate information, in the right format and on time; this situation is due to the stakeholders having different communications needs. What will your best course of action be?

choices.text: Document lessons learned
Maintain a Benefit Register
Maintain a Stakeholder Register
Establish a Project Management Information System (PMIS)

explanation:
The only correct option is C. Program team should maintain a Stakeholder Register in order to use it for communication. It contains all the needed information for communication the right information, at the right time and through the correct channel
Reference: SPM V4 Page 60 - 5.1

text: The CEO of a risk adverse company decided to change the culture of his organization after several pitfalls; he decided that the company needs to take more risks if it wants to gain from its investments. A program was designed with you as the program manager. While in the definition phase, in which of the following documents is the organization’s risk tolerance recorded?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Mandate
Strategic plan

explanation:
Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits and most importantly a high-level risk assessment containing the risk tolerance acting as a reminder and constraint when making program decisions.
Risk tolerances are not detailed in the standard, however they are part of the business case and they are used for validating the continuation of the program in phase-gate reviews; if the program surpasses the risk threshold, it might be terminated
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: You are currently during the sixth month of your 2-years program and multiple changes are being reviewed in order to take go/no-go decisions on multiple components. One of the components has delivered the intended benefits and needs to be closed. What is your next step as a program manager?

choices.text: Resources re-deployment to other components
Final performance review to be presented to steering committee
Conduct a phase gate review with the steering committee
Work with your sponsor to transition this component

explanation:
The component has come to its successful end, delivering the intended benefits, so there is no need for phase gate reviews anymore. On another hand, the final performance review is done when the program reaches its closing phase which is not the case here. This leaves us with the next logical step for the program manager, which is to work with the sponsor to prepare and present the component transition request to the steering committee. Following the approval and transition, resources will be re-deployed
Reference: SPM V4 Page 91 - Figure 7-1 shows the component lifecycle as part of the program delivery phase, and Page 96 - 7.1.3.3 explains the component transition and closure

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. In order to maintain effective communication, you have already drafted and got the approval for the communications management plan for your program. Which of the following documents accompanies this plan throughout PLC?

choices.text: Risk register
Information distribution
Stakeholder register
Knowledge management plan

explanation:
Throughout PLC, the stakeholder engagement plan and the communication management plan work toe-to-toe. Stakeholder register records stakeholders’ roles in the program, influence, impact, classification, engagement strategy and communication, etc.; which are used for successful engagement and communication with stakeholders. All other options are irrelevant
Reference: SPM V4 Page 66 - 5.5

text: Your company won the bid for a large project for a multi-cultural company with offices spanning across multiple countries. In the Statement Of Work (SOW) presented by the customer, there was a clause that all project managers who will work on this program must have their PMP certifications. One of your starting components is managed by a strong project manager who always gets the job done within scope, quality, schedule and cost. This project manager, however, due to his busy schedule, failed his PMP test and has a second attempt scheduled two weeks after his component initiation date. You, as the program manager, are finalizing the definition phase and starting the delivery phase. What should your next course of action be?

choices.text: Inform the customer about the delay in getting the project manager certified
Host a kick-off meeting with key stakeholders
Finalize the program management plan and start the delivery phase
Inform your sponsor about the delay in getting the project manager certified

explanation:
This situation conflicts with the contract signed with the customer, including a clause to have all project managers certified before they can work on their projects; following PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, you as the program manager, should be informing your customer of the delay. Option B is done before this stage, option C is just rephrasing the current status of the program mentioned in the question, and option D is not correct here because when there is a conflict of interest, the appropriate party should be directly informed, thus A is the right answer here
Reference: Code of Conduct; as a program manager you need to be transparent and have the highest levels of integrity

text: Prior to a governance board meeting, a steering committee member called you and expressed his concern about the schedule delays and that he will be issuing a schedule staggering complaint and change request during the planned meeting. What should you do next?

choices.text: Record the change in Change Log and analyze its impact
Acknowledge that it is the role of the steering committee to endorse, approve or reject changes
Ignore the member concerns and conduct the meeting as planned
Update the business case and benefits realization plan

explanation:
Option C is directly eliminated as you cannot ignore concerns from steering committee members, option D is irrelevant to this question, option B is the correct answer because the scale of this concern and any subsequent change request to it is large and impacting the program schedule, thus needs the approval of the steering committee. Option A comes after holding the meeting, issuing the change request and getting the steering committee approval to proceed
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3 and Page 81 - 6.2.2

text: Portfolio managers have the role of choosing which programs to undergo based on a well-defined feasibility study and value delivery, in addition to organizational needs and legal requirements. A program has been selected and is now in delivery phase. Program manager is reviewing specific components outcomes of which a new HR management system and a new administration process are to be in place. Which of the following documents has the purpose of listing this type of outcomes?

choices.text: Benefits Management Plan (BMP)
Business case
Program Management Plan
Program Charter

explanation:
This type of outcomes is considered as program benefit (in the exam PMI uses outcome instead of benefit a lot of times). Option B is not the correct option even though it lists the benefits; the purpose of a business case is to present a cost-benefit analysis and a basis to ensure program viability throughout PLC. The program charter – Option D, has the purpose of listing the benefits to be delivered by the program, in addition to the resources and authorizations needed to conduct the program. Option A is not correct, because the BMP has the purpose of documenting How and When benefits are going to be delivered and option C is irrelevant in this context
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You have just prepared your benefits management plan (BMP) for this program; this plan is extremely helpful to

choices.text: Extract performance reports throughout PLC
Involve stakeholders and get their buy-in
Monitor and Control the program
Present methods to be used in order to fully realize intended benefits

explanation:
Option A, performance reports are extracted from aggregating information on the status of program and its components. Option B is irrelevant, option C is ambiguous in this scenario as it does not directly link to the BMP. Option D is the correct answer because BMP shows How and When benefits are going to be delivered, it contains the guidelines and approach for benefits management
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: Your program contains tangible benefits and intangible ones. Multiple key stakeholders are expressing their concerns regarding the measurement of the intangible benefits, asking for a way to measure and requesting you to update your benefits management plan (BMP) accordingly. As a program manager, you know that the BMP is useful as it

choices.text: Helps in quantifying intangible benefits
Is prepared with the help of key stakeholders who were not aware at that time of the intangible benefits in place
Serves as a baseline to guide the delivery of benefits
Helps realizing only the incremental benefits

explanation:
Option D is not correct, as it mentions only the incremental benefits; option B is incorrect as it is the job of the program manager to define program benefits in line with stakeholder and organization needs and expectations and communicating the related information to affected stakeholders; option A is incorrect. Thus leaving us with option C, that is the main idea behind defining a BMP
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: As program manager for the new ice cream flavors program, you want to select appropriate subcontractors to support your program and transfer a part from the work to be done to others. While preparing for the program, you prepare selection criteria in order to group which components to outsource and which components to undertake internally. You do this because you want to

choices.text: Do a cost-benefit analysis on whether to buy or to make
Do a cost-benefit analysis on whether to make or to buy
Outsource as much as possible in order to transfer any risk from the program to third parties
Optimize procurement selections based on specific factors and organization requirements

explanation:
Options A and B are the same and do not reflect the best choices for this question, option C is irrelevant as the question does not mention any risk issues or constraints. Option D is the correct answer as normally, the procurement process is part of the organization assets and spans across multiple programs, however, for programs presenting further procurement needs, the program manager should adopt a program-specific procurement approach. In either of the cases, the program manager has to review components procurement needs and plan to optimize the procurement based on a variety of factors and commonalities between components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 116 - 8.1.2.7

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You know the importance of the program and the fact that it has the highest priority in the organization, and you know that each stakeholders group and key stakeholders will be requesting reports in their own format to follow up on the program status. What is the best course of action you take, as a program manager, to optimize stakeholder engagement?

choices.text: Develop a communications strategy
Develop an Information distribution plan
Maintain a good Communications log
Develop a stakeholder register

explanation:
Option B is irrelevant, options C and D are not correct, because they do not guarantee a successful stakeholder engagement and program communication. Option A is the correct answer because it allows the program manager to engage stakeholders based on their power and interest and defines the generic communication requirements and strategies to cater for all stakeholders. It is important to note that specific communications strategies for specific stakeholders will be part of the stakeholder register, however the register is not the best answer here because it is a passive artifact; if you develop the register and put all information in it without having a correct engagement and communication strategy, it would not matter
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: As part of a major phase gate review, steering committee was looking at an escalated issue affecting 3 projects: X, Y and Z. The issue was escalated by Project X. As a result, steering committee decided to end projects Y and Z, continue with A as planned and add a new project W to cater for the misalignment caused by the issue. What is your next course of action as a program manager?

choices.text: Revise the program documentation to incorporate the change
Communicate change to stakeholders
Meet with program team and component managers to discuss the change
Give a reward to project A’s project manager for capturing the issue

explanation:
The correct answer here is A; upon initiation of a new component, all program-level documentation and records dealing with the component should be updated to reflect any changes to the affected components. Option D is not correct as this is the job of the project manager and does not warrant a reward. Option B and C come after option A
Reference: SPM V4 Page 77 - 6.1.11

text: Your company is switching to a projects-based company and is undergoing a migration process from the old functional approach. As part of this migration, new programs are put in place to define standards to follow when developing future programs; you are the program manager for one of the programs to define the process to be put in place when designing the charters and roadmaps of future programs. What is the first step, you as the program manager need to take?

choices.text: Prepare high level risk assessment
Prepare a feasibility study
Deﬁne program charter
Design the program roadmap

explanation:
Every program, once its vision is defined, needs to align programs with organization strategy. The first step towards alignment is the design of a business case, which is a documented feasibility study. The business case is used to align program with strategic objectives and to serve as a justification for the resources to be expended throughout the program. All other options come later
Reference: SPM V4 Page 34

text: You are in the second year of a five years program and the program has been successfully delivering the planned benefits. Your program management team and you are constantly on the lookout for environmental changes that might affect the program delivery. The activity performed here is part of which of the following?

choices.text: Program Communication management
Program pre-setup phase
Program setup phase
Program Financial Management

explanation:
Being in delivery phase, options B and C are directly eliminated, option A is irrelevant. Option D is the correct option because environmental changes, when they occur, can have an impact on the program budget, thus affecting the finance management activities
Reference: SPM V4 Page 128 - 8.2.3

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. Now that you got your charter approved by the steering committee, you should

choices.text: Engage stakeholders continuously
Initiate components by designing related business cases for each component
Define a change management plan
Define the governance structure to manage this program

explanation:
This question is situational and asks about the next activity to do after the approval of the charter; option D is done as part of defining the charter, options A and B are done as part of the delivery phase which comes after defining the program management plan including subsidiary plans such as the change management plan which guides the process of incorporating the change within the program e.g. define, analyze, get funding and implementing the change. Hence, option C is the correct answer
Reference: SPM V4 Page 34 - Figure 3-1 shows the correct flow of the documents preparation

text: The formulation phase marks the beginning of a program. Early on in formulation, the program manager is assigned by the sponsor. The program manager starts by defining the program’s vision and conducting the initial assessments. As a program manager and while conducting the initial assessment, if you do not have sufficient information to estimate all inputs to schedule or cost, you proceed by?

choices.text: Asking component managers for analysis of their components and roll back results
Terminating program
Making assumptions
Putting the non-assessed parts as constraints

explanation:
Option A is not correct as you are still in formulation. Option B and D are not correct. Option C is the correct answer; the program manager proceeds by making reasonable assumptions which will be further refined and validated during planning and during delivery after that
Reference: SPM V4 Page 40 - 3.4.2.4

text: You are in the second year of a four years program and the program has been successfully delivering the planned benefits. Management is now concerned about a new market competition and asks you to shorten the schedule to meet the newly shortened benefits window without increasing program risk. The program still have 3 components to initiate, the best course of action would be to

choices.text: Get the remaining components approved all at once
Fast track the program
Continue as planned
Update the program status across program and all its components

explanation:
Option B would be the correct option if the company was willing to raise the risk level because fast tracking shortens the schedule at the expense of increasing risk, option C is not correct because you cannot continue as planned after the management advise to shorten the schedule to meet the new benefits window, option D is irrelevant in this context. Hence, option A is the correct answer, getting all components approved at once and starting their implementation would be the best option to undertake, this way, you will not waste time conducting approval and initiation meetings for each component. Of course, other actions are needed in this case, but none are mentioned in the available answers
Reference: exam questions and insights from our instructors

text: You are in the second year of a four years program and the program has been successfully delivering the planned benefits. Due to market changes, an already planned benefit is no longer viable and needs to be removed from the list of program benefits. Now that you have updated the Benefit Management Plan (BMP), what should you do first?

choices.text: Reflect the update in the Benefit Register (BR)
Update the roadmap
Communicate the BMP to affected stakeholders
Present the updated BMP to the governance board for approval during the next governance meeting planned in one month

explanation:
Any update to the benefit management should be reflected in roadmap; the roadmap shows major milestones and incremental benefits, and should be updated to reflect the removal of this incremental benefit. Option D is incorrect because you should not wait for a month to get things moving on; other options come later
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3 and Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: Your company is switching to a projects-based company and is undergoing a migration process from the old functional approach. As part of this migration, new programs are put in place to define standards to follow when developing future programs; you are the program manager for one of the programs to define the process to be put in place when designing the charters and roadmaps of future programs. During the course of the program, you set up a phase gate review process. Such an approach

choices.text: Enables a focus on program continuation
Gives the final decision to program steering committee on all program changes
Enables a focus on program risk and changes
Ensures that program is continuously assessed

explanation:
Option B is incorrect, as changes within the program manager’s authority do not warrant the approval of steering committee, option C is irrelevant, option D is the purpose of health check reviews. Option A is the right option as during th phase gate reviews, program is assessed and a go/no-go decision is taking on whether to continue to the next phase, continue with changes or stop the program
Reference: SPM V4 Page 76 - 6.1.9

text: You are an experienced program manager with the required certifications to back it up. You have been managing large complex programs in multiple countries and you have been doing a good job. Recently, you have been assigned as the program manager for a 10-year program which you know will take longer. The best approach to take is to

choices.text: Focus on business value and strategic alignment
Establish a funding framework
Assess the cost and benefits of this program
Prepare a roadmap

explanation:
Among all the option, option D is the only one that points to the right answer, as the roadmap is a graphical chronological representation of the milestones of the program; in addition, the roadmap reflects the link between the business case and the implementation strategy. Option A is done in phase gate reviews, option B is irrelevant and option C would have been the correct answer in case you do not have the statement "you know will take longer"; this statement points you to the fact that you have already done the assessment, thus finalized the business case, and you found out that it will take longer, your next activity would be preparing the charter and roadmap. Roadmap is the correct answer here
Reference: SPM V4 Page 34 - Figure 3-1 shows the correct flow

text: All programs in your company seem to miss the allotted budget. The CEO advised to hire a subject matter expert (SME) in order to help while planning the programs’ budgets. But the situation does not seem to get any better. What is the most possible reason for this?

choices.text: You did not review/update the program formulation sub-phase documents regularly
You did not develop a good financial management plan which should be put in place for each program
You did not include SMEs in the program steering committee
You did not use, during the course of your program, the EVM to forecast the budget at completion

explanation:
Options A is the correct answer because, the program manager needs to continuously re-define the program and whenever needed revisit the formulation sub-phase in order to attain the optimum business value from the program. All other options do not warrant a successful program delivery. Changes affect aspects of the program which might affect the benefit window, cost/benefit ration, ROI, risk thresholds, benefits, governance structure, etc. thus warranting the update of the formulation sub-phase documents
Multiple activities warrants the need for BC, Charter and Roadmap updates. You can find a few references below:
Reference: SPM V4 Page 114 - 8.1.2.4
Reference: SPM V4 Page 52 - 4.3.1 and 4.3.2
Reference: SPM V4 Page 101 - 7.2.2.2
Pay attention, although the charter is updated in real-life, the SPM does not point out to any flagrant charter update as it does for Business Case and Roadmap. We have multiple insights from our students stating that they got a question in the exam where multiple formulation documents are updated, and the question asks about the document that is normally not updated, in this case, you need to choose charter as the correct option

text: You are working as a program manager and one of your components junior project managers comes to you seeking advice about the difference between program life cycle and project life cycle. Your answer to the junior project manager would be

choices.text: There is no difference between both
Program lifecycles assist in controlling the projects’ lifecycles
Programs have extended lifecycles, however projects don’t
Programs realize benefits during their lifecycles by integrating multiple projects; the benefits realized could not be realized if the projects were managed separately

explanation:
Option D is the only correct option between all the above options, all other options are incorrect
Reference: SPM V4 Page 3 - 1.2

text: You are appointed as a program manager for the development of new remote cars. The cars need to be available for a two-hour play time on a full battery and has to be pushed to the market within one year in order to beat competition. You are mid-way through the program and multiple delays have occurred. As a result, the governance board has decided to reduce the scope of the program and has communicated the decision to you. What should the governance board also check?

choices.text: How will you apply the corrective actions
Your performance as a program manager, because of the delays and the decision to reduce scope
Calculate the number of needed resources and if the organization can secure them
If the window of opportunity has been compromised

explanation:
Option A is irrelevant in this case and is incorrect, option B is not a correct option because the delays and scope reduction do not warrant a bad program manager, option C is incorrect as the number of resources should have been secured when the program charter was approved, and in this case the scope is being reduced. Option D is the correct answer as the governance board focus is on benefits delivery. A scope reduction warrants a re-check of the window of opportunity
Reference: SPM V4 Page 51 - 4.3.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. Being in a fast moving market, you are aware that a big number of changes will be requested during the course of this program. You have a steering committee designed of multiple members from the functional departments and many of the very important decision makers are in different countries. You realize that this will cause huge delays each time the steering committee needs to meet to agree on a decision, what is the best approach you can take in this case?

choices.text: Work with PMO to set up a change process to follow
Work with the program team and steering committee to set escalation levels
Directly decline the small change requests as you focus on more important ones
Plan ahead for monthly governance board meetings

explanation:
Option C is incorrect as no change requests should be declined based on its importance, every change request should follow the same approval/denial process. Option D will not guarantee speeding up the process as some changes will need direct intervention. Option A is irrelevant in this context. Option B is the correct answer because when you set escalation levels, when a change threshold is reached and a change is triggered due to the occurrence of a risk or issue, you can directly, as a program manager, know if you are eligible to take the decision or you need to escalate to SC. Option B is the only option leading to faster change processing if designed correctly
Reference: SPM V4 Page 112 - 8.1.2.1 and Page 73 - 6.1.6

text: You are in the second year of a four years program and the program has been successfully delivering the planned benefits. Two of your projects have planned for the use of the same resource at the same time. This scenario points to

choices.text: A trigger for you to intervene and resolve the allocation of this key resource
A risk to be escalated to steering committee
A project constraint to be managed by the project managers themselves
A program constraint to be managed by program manager

explanation:
The scenario here points to a resource allocation issue which should be solved by the program managers using resource management (prioritization, interdependency), thus the only correct option is A. This is not a risk to escalate to steering committee, nor is it a constraint, not it is something that you could not solve yet
Reference: SPM V4 Page 98 - 7.2 and Page 100 - 7.2.2.2

text: Your program for launching new flavors of ice cream is in its delivery phase and you have thoroughly planned it being of critical importance for your company, and you knew that a good planning will normally result in successful delivery and closure phases. You are mid-way through the program and your program is still on budget and on schedule, however it has been lagging in both and you anticipate that you’ll go over budget soon enough. What should you do in this situation?

choices.text: Re-baseline schedule
Suggest program termination to steering committee
Re-baseline budget
Program reporting

explanation:
The job of the program manager is to be transparent regarding the status of the program; stakeholders need to be informed of the lagging. Options A and C are irrelevant to this scenario and do not reflect a correct approach to be taken by the program manager in this situation, on another hand, re-baselining will need the approval of the steering committee. Option B is incorrect, because the situation does not warrant the termination of the program. Option D is the correct option because program reports are distributed through information distribution, thus, communicating the current status to stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 126 - 8.2.2.2

text: Your program for launching new flavors of ice cream is in its definition phase and you are thoroughly planning it being of critical importance for your company, and you know that a good planning will normally result in successful delivery and closure phases. In program lifecycle (PLC), program manager manages activities and facilitates program definition, delivery and closure. Which of the below statements is true?

choices.text: Program lifecycle is a combination of each of its projects’ lifecycles
It is helpful to design process to be applied across PLC phases
Purpose of PLC is to produce deliverables
Each project has unique lifecycle phases

explanation:
This question targets only one correct option, which is B; all other options are incorrect in any situation. Option B is correct because it is always helpful to establish common processes across all phases in order to ease PLC management
Reference: SPM V4 Page 9 - 1.3, Page 15 - 1.7, Page 20 - 1.9, Page 99 - 7.2.2.1 and many more sections stating that information should be used by the program and its components, thus the processes should work for both. In addition, the management plan and its subsidiary plans will be used as templates for the components in order to maintain the alignment and the consolidation of management.

text: A program manager maintains a close look on the program benefits throughout the program lifecycle. Governance board is also focused on delivering benefits and conduct regular meetings to ensure it. Benefits are the most important assets of a program and you constantly work to realize them. In the context of benefits, what is benefits breakdown structure?

choices.text: Helps define stakeholders’ objectives
Get the buy-in of stakeholders for their benefits
Model the stakeholders' expected beneﬁts
Extract critical success factors

explanation:
This question is to introduce you to the term “benefits breakdown structure” in case you haven’t encountered it before. The BBS helps model stakeholder expected benefits
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam. You can search the WEB, it has a lot of information on it, however the needed ones are included in this QB

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. What is the first thing you do as a program manager?

choices.text: Define strategic plan
Define business case
Establish program vision
Analyze program risk

explanation:
The first thing to be done by the program manager is to establish program vision, followed by program mission, objectives, goals and strategy. You will then need to start defining the BC, Charter and Roadmap. Option A is incorrect because it should be prepared by the portfolio.
Reference: this question has occurred multiple times in the exam and it is mostly one of the 20 test questions that are non-marked. The correct answer is similar to when you initiate any type of endeavor, you start with the vision, mission, objectives/goals and strategy. Once strategy is defined, you start the execution beginning with preparing the documents i.e. BC and charter

text: A program manager maintains a close look on the program benefits throughout the program lifecycle. Governance board is also focused on delivering benefits and conduct regular meetings to ensure it. Benefits are the most important assets of a program and you constantly work to realize them. Early in your program, you have prepared a benefits management plan in order to guide benefits delivery, their monitoring and controlling throughout the course of the program. Which option represents a use for Benefits Management Plan (BMP)?

choices.text: Identifying changes to components
Defining the projects’ charters
Identifying roles and responsibilities for program and subsequent projects
Identifying projects to be tackled by the program

explanation:
The BMP is the performance baseline of a program. Option A is the correct option because you validate program performance against the set baseline in order to determine whether to continue or whether changes need to be incorporated
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1, in addition to multiple insights from exam questions

text: Not all work on a program is done during the program; some of the work is performed prior to the program when grouping the initiatives into portfolios and sometimes preparing the business cases for the programs. However, the assignment of a program manager usually marks the official debut of a program. When in program pre-setup phase, how is the program manager chosen?

choices.text: Assigned by program sponsor
Appointed by the steering committee members
A person with a PgMP certification and experience in managing complex programs
A person with the needed technical knowledge

explanation:
Following the standard for program manager, the program manager is assigned by the sponsor. This assignment should be done at the earliest in the program, during program pre-setup phase, otherwise known as formulation sub-phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 92 - 7.1.2.1

text: Each change request is recorded in the change log to be analyzed and to determine its impact and urgency. Following this, a decision is made to approve or reject the change. In addition to this, the program manager is responsible to:

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Escalate to Change Control Board (CCB)
Document the rationale for the decision
Program reporting

explanation:
In the program change monitoring and controlling, program CCB should ensure that change is recorded in change log, communicated to appropriate stakeholders and reflected in updates to affected components plans. However, it is the responsibility of the program manager to do all of this. Option C is the correct option, option D is irrelevant in this case, options A and B are incorrect because many change types are within the authority of the program manager and do not warrant escalation
Reference: SPM V4 Page 74 - 6.1.8

text: You have been working for your company for ten years. You started as a junior project manager and today you are a highly regarded program manager. Throughout your years in the company, you have been using the lessons learned prepared by programs and projects throughout the years and you have been finding that the more lessons learned you record the helpful it will be when undertaking a similar program in the future. During which phase of the program are the lessons learned documented?

choices.text: Program definition phase
Program closure phase
Benefit delivery phase
Throughout the entire program

explanation:
Lessons learned should be documented throughout the entire program and not at a single specific phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 130 - 8.2.4.1, in addition to Page 92 - 7.1.2.1, Page 97 - 7.1.4 and Page 102 - 7.2.2.5

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. Time to market is key in order to beat the competition and the program is undergoing a lot of changes which might affect the go-live date. What should you, as the program manager, do?

choices.text: Continue with the work as planned
Escalate to executive management that the program will be delayed
Continuously review the program master schedule
Request additional human resources and budget

explanation:
The changes are affecting the schedule, and the question clearly states that the changes might affect the go-live date, so the program manager should maintain a close look on the master schedule in order to assess the impact of the changes and accelerate or decelerate components. Option D comes as a result of the assessment if needed e.g. if the program is delayed, you might want additional resources to speed it up.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11 and Page 136 - 8.2.9

text: Your company has been losing assets and failing to cope with the fast market. The CEO has taken a firm decision to group the projects in a program to attain more benefits. Part of the program is to restructure the company, which will lead to lowering the number of employees, thus, many will lose their jobs. You have been appointed to manage the program and you are new to the company. What is the first thing you should do?

choices.text: Prepare a business case
Analyze the cultural aspect of the company and its employees in order to assess the way the change is accepted
Prepare a high level roadmap
Analyze the high level risks

explanation:
The first thing you do in this situation is to study the cultural aspect which will help you determine the strategy to undergo for the program and will help you manage the communication with stakeholders in order to remain aligned with the strategic objectives, in addition to helping with risk management.
The cultural aspect is the most important one and is mentioned several time in the SPM of which the following are the most important:
Reference: SPM V4 Page 9 - 1.3, Page 62 - 5.2, Page 64 - 5.3 and Page 120 - 8.1.2.10

text: A big program is underway in company A and your company B is outsourced to deliver one of the components, which is managed as a program in your company, with you as the program manager. You have a very good relationship with company A. However, company A has been delaying a large payment which is needed to maintain your program performance. What is the best course of action for you?

choices.text: Re-baseline budget
Re-baseline schedule
Take corrective action
Issue a change request

explanation:
This situation clearly targets the program financial management aspect, which has corrective actions as an output. Option C is the correct answer. The situation does not warrant a re-baseline, so options A and B are incorrect. Option D is done later.
Although the questions targeting inputs and outputs are scarce in the exam, however this question and specifically the financial part has been spotted multiple times in the exam (in addition to scope and schedule).
Reference: SPM V4 Page 127 - 8.2.3

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are in delivery phase and are identifying risks in order to get the approval for proceeding and validate continuation. Which of the below is considered an important aspect when getting the approval?

choices.text: What are the constraints?
Assumptions are still valid
What is the probability of success?
Who are the key stakeholders?

explanation:
Based on the question, you are in the delivery phase and you are identifying risks. This is done to determine whether: Program assumptions are still valid; Assessed risk has changed from its prior state, with analysis of trends; Proper risk management policies and procedures are being followed; Cost or schedule contingency reserves are modified in line with the risks of the program
Reference: SPM V4 Page 134 - 8.2.8

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are preparing your program charter, which of the following is included in the charter?

choices.text: Market analysis
List of all the components to be initiated during the program
An assumption that the cost of material to be used will have only little price fluctuation throughout programs
List of planned program governance meetings

explanation:
Option B is not correct because at this stage, you do not know the list of all the components for sure, instead you have an initial mix of components that will be updated throughout the delivery phase. Option D is in the governance plan and not charter. Option A is part of the business case. Option C is correct as the assumptions are part of the program charter. Program charter includes justification, vision, strategic fit, outcomes, scope, components (planned, not all), risks, issues, assumptions, benefits and benefits strategy, stakeholders considerations, timeline, governance structure and resources needs
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You know that you will need to work in order to ensure that the program objectives remain aligned with the organization’s strategic goals and objectives. You ensure program alignment with the organization’s strategic plan, objectives, priorities, vision, and mission statement by

choices.text: Performing an initial program assessment
Defining a roadmap
Engaging stakeholders
Identifying benefits

explanation:
Through strategic program management, program manager performs an initial program assessment by defining the program objectives, requirements, and risks in order to ensure program alignment with the organization’s strategic plan, objectives, priorities, vision, and mission statement. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 1 Strategic Program Management

text: You have multiple projects in your program. Each project manager is identifying the work to be done on her/his project; which one of the below options guarantees that your program scope covers all the benefits?

choices.text: Use the standards set by the PMO
Prepare a scope statement
Prepare a program work breakdown structure
Prepare a beneﬁts realization plan

explanation:
The PWBS encompasses the entire scope of the program; it reflects all the benefits to be delivered by the program. All other options are irrelevant
Reference: SPM V4 Page 123 - 8.1.2.12

text: Knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. You are currently in the process of getting information from stakeholders in order to understand their organizations’ cultural aspect. Which of the below options best suits this process?

choices.text: Focus groups
Questionnaires and surveys
Interviews
Open-ended questions

explanation:
The best way to get stakeholder feedback and obtain as much information as possible (key information as well), is to do it while using open-ended questions. Open ended questions can be used during options A, B and C
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: Each program uses a variety of resources from different technical and management backgrounds. Resources are added and removed based on the program and its constituent components needs. Who is considered responsible for providing the needed resources to a program?

choices.text: Program governance board
Program sponsor
Program manager
Each project’s project manager

explanation:
Based on the SPM, the program sponsor is the one responsible for providing resources to the program. Sponsor is an advocate for the program and is accountable for enabling success
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.8, Page 61 - 5.1 and Page 79 - 6.2
Pay attention here that the program manager, functional managers and SC have a hand in providing resources, however this is the responsibility of the sponsor

text: You are establishing a new company and recruiting employees from all over the country. Some people will need to drive for 2 hours to get to the job site, others for a couple of minutes. Multiple investors have put their trust in your company and you are now designing the structure of your company initiation program’s steering committee with their roles and responsibilities. Members of the steering committee are the investors and a few senior managers in the company. What will you have to do next?

choices.text: Plan for governance meetings
Study the cultural aspect of the company
Start with stakeholders’ identification
Get your business case approved

explanation:
Based on the question, you are now designing the structure of the steering committee, which contains investors that are external to the company and definitely have busy schedules. What you need to do in this case in order to make sure than the steering committee does its role in the program, is to plan for regular meetings ahead in order to reserve a spot for the program in the investors’ busy schedules
Reference: SPM V4 Page 71 - 6.1.1.2

text: In definition phase, Business case, roadmap and charter are approved as part of the formulation sub-phase; and the program management plan (PMP) is approved as part of planning phase. Considering that your PMP has just been approved, what is your next step as a program manager?

choices.text: Establish the core team and appoint components project managers
Initiate component requests
Set up PMO and PMIS
Charter component projects

explanation:
Based on the question, the Program Management Plan has been approved, which indicates that you are now in the delivery phase. During this phase, components’ initiation requests are suggested to steering committee for approval. Option D comes later after approving the component BC and preparing the charter, Project managers are appointed in the projects’ charters. Option C is done prior to preparing the program management plan and establishing the core team is done as part of the infrastructure development after program charter approval and before preparing the program management plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 95 - 7.1.2.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are working on the preparation of the business case including a cost-benefit analysis in order to get your program approved by sponsor. Which of the below is correct?

choices.text: You should identify only the financial benefits
You should identify the key stakeholders
You should identify intrinsic and extrinsic beneﬁts
You should identify only high level benefits

explanation:
Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits, high-level risk assessment and intrinsic and extrinsic beneﬁts.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: Programs deliver benefits to the sponsoring organizations. It is the responsibility of the program manager and steering committee to ensure the successful delivery of a program by delivering the planned benefits. After performing benefits identification and setting up a benefit register, what should you do in order to develop the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the benefits?

choices.text: Check the success factors in business case
Meet with stakeholders
Check the clear measurement for success in program charter
Revise the roadmap to link components to benefits

explanation:
The benefits register needs to be reviewed with key stakeholders in order to define KPIs. The other options are irrelevant in this case
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1

text: You are managing a program to build a new generation of mobile phones with higher capabilities than the current products in the market. When preparing the business case, you should focus on

choices.text: Using a comparative advantage analysis
Having focus groups in order to study stakeholders’ influence, power and interest
Clearly defining the program vision
Conducting SWOT analysis

explanation:
The product needs to be of higher capabilities than what exists in the market; program manager should focus on comparative advantage analysis in order to depict the advantages of designing a new product, if other companies are doing a similar effort and to find alternative approaches in case the original approach fails
Reference: SPM V4 Page 39 - 3.4.2.1

text: In definition phase, Business case, roadmap and charter are approved as part of the formulation sub-phase; and the program management plan (PMP) is approved as part of planning phase. Considering that your PMP has just been approved, what will you, as a program manager, need to do?

choices.text: Leave the component managers do their work without interfering until they deliver the intended results
Ensure that component managers are collaborative
Work closely with each component manager to ensure project scope, time and budget remain within limitations
Help component managers with their daily work activities in order to maintain good relationships with them

explanation:
Option A is not correct, option C and D are not correct because the program manager can not intervene with the components managers’ work. The components’ managers will manage their components and the program manager will manage the interdependency between components and ensure the collaboration of component managers in order to deliver benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 13 - 1.4.3

text: Knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. During the last meeting, you realized that multiple important stakeholders were missing for the first time. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Do root-cause analysis
Call them and make it clear that they should attend the planned meetings no matter what
Analyze CPI and SPI in order to make sure that program is performing as expected and that the missing stakeholders have no reason to skip the meeting
Inform sponsor of this urgent matter

explanation:
Stakeholders’ participation is measured by stakeholder metrics defined in the stakeholder engagement plan. In case of non-participation, program manager conducts a root-cause analysis and does not make assumptions on his own. All other options are irrelevant. Participation trends are analyzed using root-cause analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 65 - 5.4

text: Consider you are the sponsor for a new program; this program has been sitting on the shelf for too long and the portfolio management decided during their last meeting that this program needs to be initiated. Today, you received the initiation decision. What should be your first act?

choices.text: Identify steering committee members
Define program vision
Identify key stakeholders
Appoint a program manager

explanation: Sponsor should appoint a program manager as early as possible during the program formulation sub-phase because the program manager will be conducting all the formulation activities and the sponsor will act as an advocate. Option D is the correct option, all other options are done by the program manager and not by the sponsor

text: You were outsourced by your company to manage a government program to bring electricity to all cities, towns and villages on a 24/7 basis. Working with the governance, you have designed a steering committee with high-level country officials and other countries’ partnerships. During the course of the program, which of the following is addressed by the steering committee?

choices.text: Define program thresholds
Aggregate performance of program and constituent components
Approve / reject all change requests
Endorsing / approving recommendations for programs

explanation:
Among these options, option D is the only one performed by the steering committee. Option A is not correct thresholds are defined by program manager and approved by steering committee. Option B is done by program manager in order to check the status of the program and get approval from steering committee for continuation or changes. Option C is not correct, as the program managers will directly approve changes within his authority level
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3
