text: You were outsourced by your company to manage a government program to bring electricity to all cities, towns and villages on a 24/7 basis. Working with the governance, you have designed a steering committee with high-level country officials and other countries’ partnerships. During the course of the program, you have been approving change requests within your authority level and recommending others to steering committee. You have encountered several planned risks and you have been continuously keeping a close eye on the KPIs and the thresholds in order to implement any preventive action needed. Which of the following documents records thresholds for evaluating KPIs and achievement?

choices.text: Business case
Roadmap
Benefits realization plan
Benefits register

explanation:
The benefits register records the list of planned benefits with their corresponding KPIs and thresholds, in addition the benefits register contains mapping of benefits to strategic objectives, mapping of planned benefits to program components as reflected in charter, brief description of how benefits are measured, risk assessment and probability of occurrence, progress indicator, target dates and milestones for benefit achievement, responsible party for delivering benefit, process for measuring progress and process for communicating progress
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1

text: Your CEO is a learning enthusiast and has recently completed his PgMP certification. He decided to switch the company from a silo-based company to a program-based company. You are in a committee meeting and are currently selecting which endeavors to be undertaken as programs. Which of the following validates to be undertaken as a program?

choices.text: Expanding a football field
Setting yearly objectives for employees
Upgrading the government information system
Use of a new project management tool

explanation:
Option A is a project, Option D is the implementation of a new tool and does not validate to be a program, option B is irrelevant. Option C is correct as the transformation will consist of multiple programs and projects to manage the legal, expansion, and other different aspects of the government’s information system across all the ministries
Reference: Page 3 - 1.2

text: You are managing a program which is very tight on schedule and any delay will cause the company to lose its investment, budget fluctuation within limits is accepted by the company and the program targets several internal aspects of the company. For best course of action, what should you do?

choices.text: Include the CFO in your steering committee
Send the component managers on time management trainings
Set a clear escalation process and have a quick response plan for schedule changes
Transfer the risk to another external party

explanation:
The program being tight on schedule and the budget not being a problem, makes option C the only correct option; setting up clear escalation process will give the manager the ability to approve changes within his authority quickly and having a quick response plan for schedule changes will make the schedule changes implementations faster. Option A is irrelevant. Option B may not help during this tight schedule given. Option D is not correct since the program targets several internal aspects of the company; any new company will need to study the organization culture and many other aspects which will lead to more delays
Reference: SPM V4 Page 66 - 5.5, Page 73 - 6.1.6

text: You have been struggling to keep up with the plan for your ice cream new flavor launching program due to high level of complexity and market competition. During the course of the program, multiple steering committee members are not participating in the planned meetings, in addition to not showing interest and sending substitutes for important meetings. What should you do?

choices.text: Meet them face to face
Analyze the situation and take appropriate actions
Raise this issue in the next steering committee meeting
Assign each stakeholder a team member to ensure they know about the program’s progress

explanation:
Before doing anything and making assumptions, program managers should analyze the situation and based on the output, take appropriate actions
Reference: SPM V4 Page 64 - 5.3 and Page 65 - 5.4

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Throughout the program, you realize that stakeholders have different and/or contradicting views of the program objectives and you need to resolve this before it affects the program. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Let the sponsor deal with this issue as he has more reach than you do
Meet with only the positive stakeholders and ignore the others
Conduct group meetings where you act as the facilitator
Maintain a stakeholder register

explanation:
In case of conflicts between stakeholders, program manager acts as a facilitator and conducts meetings in focus groups in order to solve the conflict. Option A is not correct as the scenario in this case does not warrant yet the sponsor’s intervention. Option B is irrelevant in all cases and option D does not warrant solving the conflict
Reference: SPM V4 Page 19 - 1.7.1 and Page 65 - 5.4

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Stakeholders are engaged throughout the course of a program when found needed. Which plan defines expectations for issue escalation including when to engage stakeholder?

choices.text: Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Program Governance Plan
Program Transition Plan
Communication Management Plan

explanation:
The Program Governance Plan defines expectations for issue escalation including when to engage stakeholders for effective issue resolution, with a focus on benefits delivery
Reference: SPM V4 Page 69, Page 70 - 6.1.1, Page 73 - 6.1.6 and Page 85 - 6.3

text: Your sponsor is a highly regarded individual in the company and has been working with you for a long time. You realize that a good sponsor will maintain a high level of exposure to the program and will facilitate its delivery and integration. You are currently working with your sponsor to conduct studies and estimates, and to prepare a high-level risk assessment. What are you doing here?

choices.text: Preparing the Business Case
Preparing the Program Charter
Preparing the Program Management Plan
Preparing the High-Level Roadmap

explanation:
During the preparation of Business Case, the program manager works with the sponsor and the sponsoring organization to initiate studies and estimates of scope, resources and costs, in addition to performing a high level risk analysis. Based on this, the Business Case can be created, or updated in case it was already created by portfolio. Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits, and most importantly a high-level risk assessment
Reference: SPM V4 Page 92 - 7.1.2.1, Page 109 - 8.1.1.8

text: You are mid-way through your program and performing as expected. During a portfolio review meeting, it was decided that your program needs to be terminated because a similar product was launched to the market last week. This issue is due to

choices.text: A technological change was pushed to the market
Alignment of program objectives with strategic goals
Poor program performance
Invalid risk assessment

explanation:
From the given options, option D is the only correct option because program is performing well, so option C is not correct, Option B is irrelevant and option A is not correct since the competition pushed a similar product to the market. Here, the program missed a good risk assessment where they should have found that a competitor is building the same product and focused their investments on a different product or on changing the targeted delivery date
Reference: experience and multiple insights from exam questions. You can read SPM V4 sections related to risk management

text: Companies undertake programs internal to the organization and programs external to the organization where the company is outsourced by a customer to deliver benefits based on a well-defined agreement. Consider you are studying a proposal to manage a program for a customer. In order to establish strategic alignment. You refer to

choices.text: Business case prepared by your portfolio board
Your organization's strategic plan, vision and mission
Your customer organization's strategic plan, vision and mission
Business case prepared by your customer

explanation:
Any program undertaken by your company to any client must first be strategically aligned to your company’s strategic objectives and goals. After all you will not start a program is it is not aligned to your company's goal even if it brings revenue e.g. if you are into designing roads, you will not accept a program for designing buildings
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam. It is thought to be one of the 20 test questions (non-marked), however it does not hurt to have the correct answer

text: Your company focuses a lot on quality of the output and it has made a name for itself in the market for the delivery of quality work. Each program has a team member dedicated to quality planning. What is the role of the steering committee when it comes to quality?

choices.text: None of the options
Monitor, control and report quality issues
Approves the proposed quality approach
Proposing standards to be approved by program team

explanation:
Options B is done by program team, option D is not correct in any case and option C is the correct answer as it is the role of the steering committee to endorse and approve the proposed quality approach
Reference: SPM V4 Page 81 - 6.2.2, Page 118 - 8.1.2.8

text: You have a large program with multiple components in it. Most of the work is outsourced to contractors. Which of the below represents the role of program manager in contract administration?

choices.text: Follow the contract management plan
Prepare a contract administration plan
Ensures program budget is spent properly to obtain benefits
Prepare Earned Value management reports

explanation:
In programs, normally the contracts are signed at program level but managed at component level; admin and closeout decisions are managed at component level and EV management reports are prepared at component level. Following this, options A, B and D are performed at component level. The correct answer is C because the program manager needs to ensure that program budget is being spent properly in order to obtain benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 131 - 8.2.5.1

text: Due to high complexity and uncertainty levels in a program, multiple risks occur and changes are constantly being implemented and integrated. The program aims to achieve its strategic goals and objectives and should remain aligned with the organization/corporate strategic goals and objectives. Who is the individual or entity responsible for achieving the organization/corporate strategic objectives?

choices.text: Program manager
Portfolio manager
Program sponsor
Program steering committee

explanation:
Option A is not correct because the program manager is responsible for achieving program objectives and realizing benefits, options D is incorrect because the steering committee is responsible for alignment of program objectives with strategic goals and objectives, option C is not correct because the sponsor is responsible for enabling success. Option B is the correct option because it is the job of the portfolio management (ultimately Portfolio Manager) to achieve the organization strategic objectives. The key word here is "Organization/corporate"
Reference: SPM V4 Page 10 - 1.4

text: Throughout your program to launch a new drug to cure cancer patients all around the world, you have been collecting data and measuring variations in order to communicate program performance data to steering committee and to continue the delivery of subsequent phase. Which of the below is included in program performance reports?

choices.text: Change requests
Resource usage
Audit conduct
Corrective actions

explanation:
Program performance reviews include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. It includes status about what work has been accomplished, what works remains to be completed, earned value, risk, issues and changes under consideration. Option D is not correct as corrective and preventive actions are controlling activities which result in program performance reports and forecasts. The program performance report includes resource usage to deliver program benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 127 - 8.2.2.2; Program reporting include program performance report (Page 101 - 7.2.2.3). The answer here is a combination of both paragraphs, in addition to insights from exam questions.

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Why is it important for program manager to perform stakeholder engagement?

choices.text: Receive feedback
Maintain program strategic alignment
Communicate risks
Communicate program beneﬁts

explanation:
Stakeholder engagement enables the program manager to communicate benefits to stakeholders and dissolve conflicts between stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 65 - 5.4

text: You are newly recruited and assigned as program manager on a transformation program. You have large experience in the industry and specifically in this particular type of transformations and the company recruited you because they have recently started with the program’s approach and they do not have experience in doing so. During the assessment, you noticed that the established governance is of low maturity. What should be your next action?

choices.text: Establish a well-structured governance for the program
Determine governance roles and responsibilities
Work extra time to prepare a good governance plan
Use your previous company governance practices

explanation:
In this scenario, the first step to perform is to assess the existing governance structure, determine the governance needs and define the new structure based on it. Option C is not correct since it does not fix the low maturity issue, option B is irrelevant and option D is not correct
Reference: SPM V4 Page 67 - Program Governance; the entire chapter focuses on the importance of a mature governance and the importance of governance roles and practices

text: You are in the definition phase and preparing the documents to guide program delivery and closure phases. You have your planned benefits and you are listing them along with the benefits strategy in the charter. Which artifact documents the relationship between program activities and the expected benefits?

choices.text: Beneﬁts realization plan
Charter
Roadmap
Benefit Register

explanation:
The roadmap documents the relationship between program activities and the expected benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3 And Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: During formulation sub-phase, the program manager and the program management team prepare a variety of documents in order to authorize the program and authorize the usage of resources. Which of the below is true regarding the program roadmap?

choices.text: It defines thresholds and metrics to measure benefits realization
It shows when the PMO deliverables are
It assesses the program's progress toward realizing its expected beneﬁts
It shows dependencies between all components

explanation:
Option A is part of the benefits realization plan; option B is part of PWBS; option D is part of Program architecture. Option C is the correct answer. The roadmap assesses the program's progress toward realizing its expected beneﬁts, it is the basis for transition and integration, used to communicate plan and benefits to stakeholders to build and maintain advocacy. In addition, the roadmap shows major milestones, important components, incremental benefits, relationship between components & benefits and major decision points
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3

text: During your program to design a new metro station for your city aimed to reduce traffic and travel time for the residents, you have been monitoring the financial environment due to the step-funding given by your government and trying to cope with it by planning for the necessary phase during each period. As part of the Financial Management, you manage?

choices.text: Operational costs
Program loss
Program profit
Performance reports and calculating CPI and SPI

explanation:
Profit and loss are not part of the financial management; option D is not correct as the performance report give status about program performance and are not managed as part of the financial management. Option A is the correct answer because the operational cost of the program, that is the expenditure on the program infrastructure, is to be managed as part of the Financial Management
Reference: SPM V4 Page 115 - 8.1.2.5 Operational Costs are included in the plan to be managed later on

text: Your stakeholders on your program to deliver the next-generation remote control car are interested in knowing the progress of a program in delivering its benefits. You have successfully maintained a benefit register. Each of your benefits is assigned a program team member to follow up on its progress and each benefit has a recorded probability level. A program manager should focus on

choices.text: Copying the related data from the benefit register to Benefit Realization Plan
The number of stakeholders involved
Organization’s ability of absorbing the change
Maintaining a good performance throughout the program

explanation:
Option A is not correct in all cases, as the information is copied from the Benefit Realization Plan to the benefit register. Options B and D are irrelevant for this scenario. Option C is the correct answer because the probability of achieving a benefit is directly related to the organization ability to absorb the change. Other factors affect probability such as number of interdependent components to realize a benefit which also affect the sustainability
Reference: SPM V4 Page 45, Page 49 - 4.2

text: After switching from silo-based company to a program-based company. You have been assigned a program manager role on a program to establish the Program Management Office (PMO) which will be common for all the programs in the organization. In a program, which of the below is the responsibility of a PMO?

choices.text: Use of enterprise environmental factors
Deﬁning quality standards
Ensuring that program objectives align with organizational strategic objectives
Conduct of phase gate reviews

explanation:
Option A is done by program manager. Options C and D are done by program steering committee. Option B is the correct answer because PMO support the program manager in many ways e.g. provides templates, gives guidance on how to develop PWBS, etc. One of the roles of PMO is to define quality standards for the program and its components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.9

text: On your program to design the metro station to reduce travel time between two ends of a city, you are currently preparing the program management plan in order to get steering committee approval and initiate the delivery phase. You are now preparing the program architecture. As a program manager, you realize that the ___________ establishes the program architecture

choices.text: Benefit Management
Program Charter
Program Roadmap
Program Schedule

explanation:
The Benefit Management establishes the program architecture which links the benefit to the components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: You are in the second year of a four years program and the program has been successfully delivering the planned benefits. During the last phase gate review, you noticed that some of the stakeholders have different understanding about the purpose for which the program has been undertaken, so you give them the scope statement. You have already baselined your scope during planning and are reviewing it continuously. Which of the below is part of the scope baseline?

choices.text: Scope statement
Program Work Breakdown Structure (PWBS)
PWBS dictionary
All of the options

explanation:
The scope baseline = Scope statement + PWBS + PWBS dictionary
Reference: Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam. This question has occurred in the exam, however rarely. The concept here is taught by several instructors in PMP

text: You are in the process of selecting project managers to manage the components in your program. One of the steering committee members asks you to hire his nephew. This being a conflict of interest, what should be your best course of action?

choices.text: Hire the steering committee member’s nephew
Document the potential concern, inform sponsor and continue the hiring process as planned
Being a conflict of interest, reject the steering committee’s request
Escalate issue to management

explanation:
Option D is not correct as the steering committee did not perform any unethical practice; in case of unethical practice i.e. steering committee member insists on hiring his nephew no matter what, program manager can report unethical practice directly to management. Option A is not correct as you need to follow the hiring process and check possible candidates before choosing one. Option C is not correct, because in the case of conflict of interest, you inform your direct manager (in this case sponsor), and proceed with the hiring process
Reference: Code of Conduct and experience. Sponsor should know about this, however this does not warrant an alarm as the SC member requested to include his nephew who might be a good supplier; if the member insisted on hiring his nephew or his nephew has been previously marked as a bad seller by the company, then you escalate.

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Which of the following represents a communication channel in a program?

choices.text: Client, Steering committee
Sponsor, public
Component managers
All of the options

explanation:
In the program delivery phase activity, the program communications management defines the communication channels to which program information is distributed. Communication channels are clients, sponsor, steering committee, public, etc.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 125 - 8.2.2

text: Your program is highly critical to your company and you realize that engaging the right stakeholder at the right time is key to success. While initiating the program, you noticed that multiple stakeholders have conflicting opinions about why the program was undertaken. In this scenario, you

choices.text: Provide the high level scope statement
Provide the business case
Provide the high level roadmap
Provide the strategic plan

explanation:
The high level scope statement shows why the program was undertaken; it represents a quick view about all the work involved in the program. Later during the lifecycle, the program manager will use the baselined scope statement. Business case and Charter are not used with all stakeholders because they contain sensitive information that should only be communicated to specific key stakeholders i.e. CEO, sponsor, etc and have restricted access to their content.
Scope statement is not included in the SPM, however it is part of the following tasks in ECO:
Reference: ECO Tasks 2, 3 and 7 - Program Life Cycle

text: Your company A recently acquired a new company B. Multiple projects in company B were added to your program. Component managers of company B are using their templates, processes and procedures to report to you which contradicts with your program. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Terminate the components
Replace the project managers
Let them report to you in their formats and you do the necessary changes in order to integrate it in your program
Consult your PMO to standardize program templates, processes and procedures

explanation:
The program management office facilitates program practices, standardizes processes and facilitates sharing of resources, methodologies, tools and techniques. It may as well extend to monitor compliance to program management practices as part of its governance role. In this scenario, program manager needs to consult PMO to standardize program templates, processes and procedures
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.9

text: During your 5-years program to design new stadiums to host the world cup in your country, you have encountered a lot of issues and changes; your plan seems to work as you have cleared the issues and performed the changes successfully. Changes are normally approved at the appropriate level and can be escalated to steering committee if they fall outside of the responsibility of the program manager. Which of the below options is the responsibility of steering committee with regards to changes?

choices.text: Documenting changes and their resolutions
Deﬁning changes the program manager can resolve
Serving as the program's change control board
Analyzing large changes

explanation:
From the given options, the only one performed by the steering committee is defining changes the program manager can resolve; changes above the authority of the program manager, will be escalated to the steering committee
Reference: SPM V4 Page 81 - 6.2.2 And Page 83 - 6.2.4

text: As a veteran program manager you realize that resources planning and optimization are needed in order to effectively deliver benefits on time and within planned cost. Resources can be shared between components or even acquired from other portfolios and programs in the organization. Consider you are managing a program and are in need of a scarce resource from another program in your organization. What is your best course of action in this case?

choices.text: You meet with the other program manager and do resource optimization; inform the sponsor of the availability and plan for this resource accordingly
Let the functional manager handle this issue
Speak to the other program manager and ask her to send you the schedule for this scarce resource; modify your schedule to cater for the resource availability
Use resource prioritization process

explanation:
Option D is not correct as the resource prioritization is done for available resources within the same program. Option C is not correct as you cannot modify the schedule without the approval of steering committee and it is not professional to ask the other program manager to send her program’s schedule which might be confidential. Option B is not correct as you do not have an issue with or between resources. Option A is the correct answer, the program manager needs to optimize the use of resources throughout the program; in this case, the resource is external to your program and the best approach is to do resource interdependency management
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam. The following section can be revised to let the resource management concepts soak (SPM V4 - 133 - 8.2.7)

text: You were outsourced by your company to manage a government program to bring electricity to all cities, towns and villages on a 24/7 basis. Working with the governance, you have designed a steering committee with high-level country officials and other countries’ partnerships. During the course of the program, you have been approving change requests within your authority level and recommending others to steering committee. You have encountered several planned risks and you have been continuously keeping a close eye on the KPIs and the thresholds in order to implement any preventive action needed. What is the impact of narrowing the program control thresholds?

choices.text: Slows down program execution
Speeds up program execution
There is no correlation between the program execution and the program control thresholds
Speeds up the schedule

explanation: When narrowing the program control thresholds, the type of change requests authorized by the upper level increases, small components issues to be handled by project managers will be escalated to you, and you will be spending more time solving issues. In addition, the types of changes that you are authorized to approve will decrease in numbers and you will need to escalate more changes to steering committee. All of this wastes time and slows down the program execution

text: Consider your program has a Budget of $ 1.2 M and is at the 3rd month of execution out of 9 months. Performance report showed: Planned Value PV = $ 320K, Expenditure to date = $ 350k, Earned Value EV = $ 340k. From the given information, you realize that currently

choices.text: Program is 30k ahead of schedule
Program is 10k over budget
Program is 10k ahead of schedule
Program is 20k over budget

explanation:
This is a recurrent question in the exam!
Expenditure to date = AC.
Let us calculate SV and CV:
SV = EV - PV = 20 k
CV = EV - AC = -10 k
This question asks about the current state, for this, you calculate SV + CV = 10k on the side of the schedule, which targets the answer to this question. This is a rough calculation done by program and project managers to compare the variances of the schedule to the cost and have a preliminary state of their endeavor.
However, some occurrences have asked about "what will be the state of this program when it finishes?", for this you need to multiply 10k by 3 = 30k, because if the program is currently 10k ahead of schedule, and it will be progressing the same as the scenario does not mention otherwise, you need to multiply it by 3 (which is 9 months / 3)

text: You have been recently assigned to manage a critical program to improve employee morale due to increase in the turnover rate. You started by preparing the business case which was recently approved by the steering committee. Now, you are working to get authorization to use organizational resources. You are working on

choices.text: Program roadmap
Scope statement
PWBS
Program Charter

explanation: Program charter is a high level document that serves as the primary document reviewed by the steering committee to authorize the program and program resources. Program charter includes justification, vision, strategic fit, outcomes, scope, components (planned, not all), risks, issues, assumptions, benefits and benefits strategy, stakeholders considerations, timeline, governance structure and resources needs

text: You have been asked by the program sponsor to manage a program. After knowing the program objectives and needed work to be done, you realized that you do not have the appropriate experience to manage this program. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: You consider this as a challenge and start studying the PgMP in order to be able to have the needed skills
You take the program knowing that you will have a good steering committee to support you, a good PMO to guide you and a great sponsor to maintain advocacy
You inform your sponsor and let him decide on the matter
You reject the assignment as you do not have the needed experience

explanation: As a management professional, you need to abide by the PMI code of ethics and refuse to take the assignment as you lack the necessary experience to undertake the program

text: Your program is mid-way and you are currently meeting with stakeholders to transition a component. You noticed that they have conflicting opinions about the benefit value. In your opinion, what is the reason behind this conflict?

choices.text: Program communication management plan has not been revised
Program business case has not clearly documented the benefit value
Program charter has not clearly documented the benefit value
Stakeholders have not been properly engaged

explanation: This question is important because it aims to target specific words in a question, for example in this scenario “benefit value”. The benefit value or level should be documented in the business case. The business case is a cost-benefit value analysis. Furthermore, charter lists benefits but do not define the benefit value. Option D is not correct because the stakeholders are not disagreeing on the component delivery, but on its benefit value. Option A is irrelevant

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Program manager needs to maintain communication targeted to each stakeholder or stakeholder groups. From which of the below options are the CEO and Sponsor mostly interested to know about?

choices.text: ETC
BAC
EAC
CPI and SPI

explanation: CEO, sponsor and executive management is normally more interested in knowing the total cost of the program. The Estimate At Completion EAC gives them this information

text: One of your components project managers discussed an issue with you that affects her component’s scope, after further discussion, you realized that the issue only affects this component. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Inform project manager to escalate first to project change control board CCB
Inform project manager to escalate first to steering committee
You create a change request and let the component manager handle it at component level
Replace the component manager as she should not have discussed this with you

explanation: Option D is neither correct nor professional. Option C is not correct as the change request does not affect other components, and a change request should not be created at the program level. For projects the escalation process is as follows: escalate to CCB, then steering committee, then project sponsor; further escalation is done to Program CCB, program steering committee and program sponsor.

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. For better understanding of stakeholders, in your benefits register, you map the benefits to program components as in?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Program roadmap
Benefits management plan

explanation: As per SPM, the benefits register maps the benefits to program components as in program roadmap. Option A and B do not reflect benefits mapping. Option D establishes program architecture which maps how the components will deliver outcomes.

text: During your program to design a new metro station for your city aimed to reduce traffic and travel time for the residents, you have been monitoring the financial environment due to the step-funding given by your government and trying to cope with it by planning for the necessary phase during each period. Program financial environment is defined and documented in?

choices.text: Program cost budgeting
Component cost estimation
Financial management planning
Financial framework establishment

explanation:
Program financial framework establishment defines the financial environment. Programs can be managed internally and funded separately, managed and funded externally, managed and funded internally. However, a program cannot fund itself.

text: Your program has 121 stakeholders that you'll need to communicate with. You'll also need which one of the following as an input to the information distribution process in your program?

choices.text: Change requests
Earned value management results
Stakeholder analysis plan
Performance reports

Fast track the program

Risk register

The program manager needs to meet again to ensure these stakeholders are receiving the information they need.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 127

text: For seven years, you have managed a program that involved breakthrough scientific research. You are now in the closing stage. You already met with each scientist involved in the program at the time his or her work was finished. You also met with a member of your enterprise program management office that specializes in knowledge management to ensure that the intellectual property developed in the program is captured and documented for future reuse. You are collecting your program’s records. You are ____________

choices.text: Organizing documents and archiving them for other purposes
Providing input to your final report
Recognizing individual efforts as well as the efforts of the entire project team
Officially releasing each scientist to his or her functional organization

explanation:
You are in the closing phase and working in Program Information Archiving and Transition. As you collect program records, you are organizing them for use throughout the organization. You also are collecting and archiving component records and documents.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 139

text: Assume your executive management team has requested that a standard process be put in place for a business case for new programs and projects to pursue in the organization. You are the leader of a cross-functional team that is designing this process. Your executives have stressed they wish to analyze each proposal from multiple business perspectives and want a balanced view of the business opportunity to be realized as well as the business risk to do so. The first step in this generic process should be to _____________

choices.text: Determine the key milestones in the program
Define the high-level requirements
Prepare a feasibility study
Analyze program complexity and strategic alignment

explanation:
Program strategy alignment begins with a business case. The business case is a documented economic feasibility study so it is the first step in the process. It is used to show the validity of the program’s benefits to be delivered and justifies how the expected outcomes would support the organization’s strategic goals.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 34

text: Recognizing the importance of benefits realization and management, as a program manager, it has been noted that a best practice to follow is to be able to quantify as many benefits in your benefits management plan as possible and also to be able to communicate their status as required quickly to stakeholders. You and your core team decided that a best practice to follow in your program to develop a new drug to cure bone cancer with limited if any side effects and to beat your competitors to market even with all the federal regulations was to ______________

choices.text: Use tangible benefits in your benefit management plan
Have each stakeholder sign off on your benefits management plan indicating his or her concurrence with it
Invite Governance to regularly schedule benefit reviews, which are included in your benefit management plan
Maintain a benefits register

explanation:
A benefits register is a best practice and can be easily translated into a benefits report. It is useful to report the benefits and their status to stakeholders.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 47, 50

text: As the program manager working on the development of an advanced polymer chemical for all types of furniture and clothing, you are in the process of beginning your program. You were selected as the program manager because in past program work, you excelled in several areas, one of which is _______________

choices.text: Identifying high-level risks
Ensuring alignment of program objectives with organizational strategic goals
Preparing a plan to initiate the program
Managing stakeholders in ensuring strategic benefits are understood

explanation:
Identifying high-level risks is done soon after the program manager is appointed. He or she works with the sponsoring organization to do so to analyze threats and opportunities. It helps in determining the program’s successful delivery of benefits and to identify risk response strategies and plans.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 92

text: Finally, your program to develop the advanced polymer chemical for all types of coats is near to completion. You have had seven components in your program, and the last one should finish in two months. You have been involving the people in your operations support group to be part of your program team meetings now for the last year and earlier included them on the distribution list for your status reports, so they felt they were part of the team for success as you recognize transition planning is the key to benefits sustainment in program management. As a program manager, you also recognize the importance of ensuring that component transition requests are prepared. It is especially important during _____________

choices.text: Transition Planning
Direct and Manage Program Execution
Develop Program Management Plan
Program Delivery

explanation:
This phase is where program components are authorized, planned, integrated, and recommended for component transition and closure.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 95

text: As you work on your program to design, develop, and manufacture a class of farm equipment that can be used above the Arctic Circle, you are also maintaining a spare parts inventory and fulfilling spares requests for clients in addition to the new work in this program. You met today with the spare parts project manager, and he had a change to his project that affected his scope dramatically. When you reviewed this change with him, you realized it also would affect the scope of the manufacturing project manager’s project in your program. As a result of your work in Program Scope Monitoring and Controlling, this means you should __________________

choices.text: Authorize funding for these changes
Issue an approved change request
Convene your CCB
Update the PWBS

explanation:
Working in Program Scope Monitoring and Controlling, there are a number of key activities including establishing an activity to administer scope changes. An output of this process is to update the PWBS.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 137

text: On your program to design, develop, and manufacture a class of farm equipment for use above the Arctic Circle, you want to make sure that the benefits from the program will be sustainable ones. Your sponsor is interested in having regular status reports about the progress of your program especially since she is located below the Arctic Circle and rarely makes on site visits given the weather conditions to assess progress herself. To provide a clear picture of your program’s performance as a whole, you must _____________

choices.text: Forecast information on the significant project components
Aggregate information across projects, subsidiary programs, and program activities
Provide detailed reports on component projects at regular intervals
Monitor the status of the key deliverables

explanation:
Program Performance Reports aggregate all performance information for all program work. The reports consolidate performance data to provide stakeholders with information regarding the use of resources to deliver program benefits.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 127

text: Assume you are working for a dry foods company. For the past five years, every one of your projects in this company has met its goals in terms of being on schedule, within budget, and meeting its specifications. However, your company finds that even though its projects are meeting its goals, overall the company is not meeting its strategic goals and objectives. You were asked to meet with the executive team to discuss your opinions as to what is occurring in the company as you are an experienced and successful project manager. You pointed out that you felt the basic problem was:

choices.text: The projects should be managed as a program
The programs were not providing needed benefits
The organization’s strategic goals would change, but the program managers were not aware of the changes
The organization requires a Program Management Office

explanation:
Organizations face numerous complexities and challenges, which lead to changes in its strategic goals and objectives, but often program managers are unaware of these changes unless there is close collaboration with the portfolio managers. To ensure programs remain in alignment with the organization’s strategic goals, they need know about these changes to see whether new projects should be added to the program, and other projects terminated if they do not support the new strategy.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 12, 33

text: It seems as if talent retention is a major concern in your area of your country as many outsourcing firms are located close to one another in two different cities. It is easy then for people to get jobs elsewhere as there are many companies that want the same types of skills and competencies. You are leading a program in your company focused on talent retention to avoid losing trained and component people. It has three components, and you have been given funding and dedicated people to work on the program team. You have three months to complete this program. You realize you can _________________

choices.text: Reallocate resources among components
Use the benefits in your charter and build on them during the three months
Send a questionnaire to each employee about the goals of your program
Meet with your program steering committee bi-weekly given the short time to complete the program

explanation:
Resources working on the components are less than the total resources needed to complete the program. This situation is one in which each time a component completes its work, the program manager can reallocate resources to other components in the program.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 119

text: There are numerous activities associated with benefits analysis and planning. Of these activities, it is especially important to _______________

choices.text: Communicate program performance metrics to stakeholders
Prepare the benefits management plan
Prioritize components and their interdependencies
Quantify incremental delivery of benefits

explanation:
Quantification of incremental delivery of benefits is necessary to enable the full realization of planned benefits to be measured during the program. The program manager and other stakeholders use these meaningful metrics to determine if benefits exceed their control thresholds and are delivered in a timely way.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 48

text: You have set up measurement criteria for each of the benefits you identified in your benefit management plan. You now want to establish a baseline for the benefits in the plan. As you establish your baseline, you have collected some key organizational, financial, and operational metrics against which you can measure improvements. The purpose of the baseline is to _________________

choices.text: Devise a strategy to collect meaningful metrics for stakeholders
Communicate progress with your sponsor and key stakeholders
Assess process interdependencies
Guide the delivery of benefits as the program progresses

explanation:
While the benefits management plan has many purposes, it serves as the baseline document, so it can guide the progress in delivering benefits as the program progresses.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 50

text: Finally, after two years of planning, your program management plan to convert customer relationship management software, supplier management software, human resource software, and telecom systems from legacy systems to an integrated platform was approved. At last, you are working to execute your plan, and you have four components in your program thus far. Since your program will last three years and is complex, you realize you _________________

choices.text: Need a Configuration Control Board
Must update all documents if a change is made
Need to mitigate any negative consequences that may affect benefit delivery
Need to quickly form a high-performing team, which includes people working on components

explanation:
During program delivery, risk identification, risk analysis, and risk response management are paramount to overall success. In developing risk responses, the program manager identifies and directs actions to mitigate any negative consequences that may affect potential benefit realization. He or she also may hold contingency reserves to support risk responses if required.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 135

text: You are managing a program with a long duration for the water management district in your county. At this time, it is scheduled to last nine years, but you believe the timeline could even be longer. You have seven projects in your program at this time, and you are only in year two. You and your program management team need to analyze any environmental or legislative changes during program delivery that may affect your program. This is a key activity to perform during the ______________

choices.text: Benefits Identification phase
Program Financial Management
Program Setup phase
Program Risk Monitoring and Control

explanation:
Environmental changes are critical, because they can affect the program financial management activities. It is necessary for the program’s finances and expenditures to be within budget and controlled; these environmental changes could create changes to the budget baseline.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 127–128

text: Finally, after four years of executing, your program to convert customer relationship management software, supplier management software, and human resource software from legacy systems to an integrated platform is almost completed. Only the telecom component remains to be completed. Your next step is to _______________

choices.text: Work with your sponsor to prepare a request to transition the three components
Deploy resources from the completed components to the telecom one to be able to close the program
Evaluate team member performance on the competed components
Review financial status before releasing resources

explanation:
When components are at the end of their life cycles, the program manager then collaborates with the sponsor to prepare a request to close or transition the components. Since this situation is an internal program, a transition request is appropriate, which is a formal request, and it is sent to the program steering committee for approval.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 101

text: In a disruptive economic world where change is the norm and not the exception, a new product released today may be obsolete tomorrow. Work often is done in silos in organization that do not manage by projects let alone by programs. But programs are a necessity if benefits can be provided if structured appropriately and also in terms of maximizing resources given the talent gap that exists in many organizations. Assume you are managing a program in an uncertain and complex environment. Your business case was approved by your Portfolio Review Board, and you now are initiating the program. You wish to encourage creativity and innovation in your team such that your new product when the program is complete has lasting value with sustainable benefits. You have established metrics to track effectiveness in achieving the benefits proposed in your business case. Recognizing that past programs have failed because of the inability to deliver value and the differences between stakeholder expectations, you decide to ______________

choices.text: Focus on stakeholder engagement as your key responsibility as a program manager
Continually reassess the alignment of your program’s goals with those of the organization
Establish governance as a networked approach to best create and realize value
Regularly hold sessions with the Portfolio Review Board to ensure their expectations for your business case are met or need refinement

explanation:
The majority of program steering committees focus on active controlling and monitoring. A value creation governance approach can focus on building innovative capabilities and sustained relationships. To do so, a culture change by the governance board focusing on collaboration is required with a view of involving stakeholders to craft the program’s vision, mission, and support to execute it. Strategy then defines the execution of the program with empowerment and delegation to the program team.
Thiry, Michel. Program Management, 2015. Surrey, England: Gower Publishing
Limited, 92–93

text: You are assuming a position in a company that has not had much experience with program management. You will be leading the program team and performing a business function for your program. The business case has already been made, and the program is scheduled to move into the Program Initiation phase. As the program manager, one competency that is embedded in your job is ___________________

choices.text: Communication
Political skills
Strategic visioning
Integration

explanation:
A successful program manager must identify program outputs and outcomes so benefits are aligned with the organization’s strategic goals and objectives.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 17

text: Assume you are managing a program at your University to establish a Master of Science degree in Program Management. Already, the University’s Master of Science degree in project management is well recognized, and it has been accredited by leading organizations. Your business case for this program was approved by the University’s trustees, and they asked for a benefits management plan, which you prepared, and they signed off on and approved. However, they want the program steering committee to conduct periodic reviews of progress to ensure _______________

choices.text: The identified benefits support best practices
The benefits are aligned with the University’s strategic objectives
A benefit owner is assigned
Realistic measures of these benefits can be prepared

explanation:
Strategic alignment is critical to be able to provide an integrated view of how outputs and outcomes of component support delivery of organizational benefits.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 33

text: Working on this program to establish a Master of Science degree in Program Management, assume you have a meeting coming up with your Governance Board in two weeks. You need to demonstrate at this stage gate review how you will report and track the benefits from your program. However, in your work in planning, you have identified a number of key factors external to your program that affect the proposed benefits, one of which is that your leading competitor in this field and located in your state also is looking into such a program and plans to offer it in an on-line fashion; your University only operates in a face-to-face mode. You know how important it is to track benefits and learning about this other University’s plans to offer the degree on line is a key benefit that you had not planned for but now feel it is essential. The new benefit actually represents a _______________

choices.text: New project
Opportunity
Major issue
New program

explanation:
Benefits realization requires analysis throughout the program. This scenario is an example of an opportunity. Opportunities optimize benefit delivery and need to be identified, refined, and quantified.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 49

text: As a program manager, you recognize the importance of effective risk management. You want to maximize any risks that may be opportunities that can benefit your program and the organization. As you work in program risk management planning, you define risk profiles, which ______________

choices.text: Are collected through surveys
You brainstorm with your team and other stakeholders
Are expressed in policy statements
You determine through interviews

explanation:
Risk profiles are used to construct the most suitable approach to managing program risks, adjusting risk severity, and monitoring risk criticality. Risk profiles may be expressed in policy statements or revealed in actions.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 120

text: You have long been a proponent of program management, and when PMI first announced the PgMP, you were one of the first people in the world to attain it. You tend to be selected to manage complex programs with your extensive experience. You have learned that having a program steering committee is essential to success, and you prepare a comprehensive governance plan. Therefore, you include in your governance plans ________________

choices.text: Stakeholder engagement
Benefits analysis and planning
Alignment with organizational goals
Stakeholder prioritization

explanation:
Stakeholder engagement provides a list of those stakeholders who should be engaged and receive communications during the program about governance activities. Many stakeholders will have an interest in the steering committee, and only a few are on the committee so engagement with those other stakeholders with interest in or influence over program activities is needed.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 71

text: As the program manager for a new pipeline system that has as its goal no potential incidents of any type, you have a major challenge as your company in the past has had a poor safety record. This program is complex, and this goal will be difficult to achieve. However, after working to plan the program for three years, your program steering committee met and approved your program management plan. As you move to approve components to be part of your program, you need to _______________

choices.text: Review the component charter
Set up a change request process
Review the program’s business case
Prepare component initiation requests

explanation:
A number of activities are required to verify the component supports the program’s outcomes before it is authorized; each component requires an initiation request, which is evaluated by the program steering committee.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 100

text: Your program management plan has been approved. So far, three projects have been initiated and authorized to be part of your program, and other components may be added later. You have staffed your program team with a variety of in-house staff members, selected consultants, and several new full-time employees. It is now time to ___________

choices.text: Prepare your team development plan
Update your program resource plan
Prepare your resource management plan
Update your staffing management plan

explanation:
Resource prioritization decisions are based on guidelines in the program resource management plan. As changes to components, such as initiating or terminating, may have impacts on program resources, updates to the resource plan may be needed; an output of Program Resource Management.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 133

text: Stakeholders are essential on programs, and you realize they are necessary to overall program success. However, your program is large and has at least 300 of them, and 50 have expressed an interest to be actively involved. You recognize the primary objective of stakeholder engagement is to ____________

choices.text: Identify, analyze, categorize, and monitor them
Work to turn as many stakeholders who are negative to the program into positive proponents of it
Identify and analyze stakeholder needs and expectations and further their support
Gain and maintain their buy in to program benefits

explanation:
Gaining and maintaining their buy in is essential to the program’s objectives, benefits, and outcomes.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 57

text: Assume you are new to your government agency, which is responsible for food safety. You are working on a program to determine whether camel milk is safe and should be approved for production and exported to other countries. You also need to determine the type of testing methods to be used to assess the safety of this milk. There are three components in your program. This agency recently changed its organizational structure to move from a silo approach in most cases so cross-functional teams could easily be formed. When you were appointed program manager for this camel milk program, you knew there will be many changes since you have a number of key stakeholders involved – the staff at the agency, the staff at its parent organization, the camel milk industry, testing manufacturers, consumer groups, and regulatory officials. Therefore, once your charter was approved and your core team was in place with four people, you decided to _______________

choices.text: Set up a process to include interested stakeholders in your program at regular milestones for buy in
Establish a change management process
Determine the role of governance for your program to present to the Agency Administrator
Establish a group for scientific experts to assist you and serve as subject matter experts

explanation:
A change management process is necessary and includes items such as the approach to request change, assess its impact, determine an appropriate decision, communicate it, and obtain funding to do the work.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 112

text: Sensemaking is critical in programs and enables different stakeholders who are involved in or interested in the program to make sense of it and have a collective understanding as to why the program is being undertaken. There are a number of individual and collective activities in sensemaking to ensure stakeholders are engaged and can accept the outcomes of the program. As a program manager to engage your stakeholders in sensemaking, you can ______________

choices.text: Develop social groups
Hold focus groups
Use cause-and effect analysis
Recognize different motivational styles

explanation:
Social groups are an example of a sensemaking activity. They are not digital networks but instead are used to enable people to connect with one another. The objective is for stakeholders to assimilate the impact of changes from the program as they are actively engaged in it.
PMI®, Managing Change in Organizations: A Practice Guide, 2013, 87–88

text: You are a member of your organization’s Program Selection Committee, which is conducting an off-site meeting to review the company’s five major strategic goals, all of which are weighted equally. Goal 1 is to produce the highest possible quality products; goal 2 is to provide outstanding customer relationship management; goal 3 is to reduce reliance on external supply sources and maximize internal resources; goal 4 is to reduce manufacturing costs; and goal 5 is to maximize productivity. You are considering four programs and will recommend one to the CEO. Program A partially supports goal 1, fully supports goals 2, 3, and 4, and does not support goal 5. Program B fully supports goals 1, 3, 4, and 5, but does not support goal 2. Program C fully supports goals 1 and 2, partially supports goals 3 and 4, but does not support goal 5. Program D partially supports goals 1, 2, and 5, and fully supports goals 3 and 4. Considering this information, your recommendation should be to select ________________

choices.text: Program A
Program B
Program C
Program D

explanation:
Programs should have a strategic fit with the organization’s long-term goals. In selecting a program to pursue, this is one area to consider. In this example, Program B fully supports four of the five goals.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 35

text: You are preparing for a major steering committee review of your program. The program sponsor is especially interested in progress on Project A, as it provides the foundation for two other projects, and at the last meeting it was behind schedule. You want to ask the committee to approve the initiation of a new project. However, it is the committee’s responsibility to _______________

choices.text: Request an audit of Project A
Focus on overall performance at this meeting and convene another meeting to determine if the new project should be initiated
Ask for data on Project A’s performance to date and especially its use of resources
Determine minimal acceptance criteria

explanation:
The program steering committee establishes the minimal acceptance criteria for a successful program and the methods to use to measure, communicate, and endorse these criteria.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 72

text: As a program manager, you consider the interests and concerns of all your stakeholders for program success. You manage communications to ensure that your stakeholders are informed about what is happening on your program and so that you can resolve any issues of importance to them and understand their feedback. This is done as part of your responsibilities in ____________

choices.text: Communications Control
Information Distribution
Stakeholder Engagement
Communications Planning

explanation:
Stakeholder engagement requires the program manager to be an excellent communicator. The program manager collects stakeholder issues and concerns and manages them to closure. He or she uses an issue log to document, prioritize, and track issues, which helps the program team understand stakeholder feedback.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 65

text: Assume you are managing a program so your organization, a Fortune 50 company, has a standard program management system (PMIS) that all programs in all of its 90 business units will use. Such a common PMIS is a major internal program, and as a result, you have a limited budget to work with to make sure it is a success and is adopted by the heads of the business units and its program managers. You are following guidelines in the Project Management Institute’s Standard for Program Management as you prepare his PMIS. You find as you monitor and control the program’s finances you need to be both proactive and reactive. An example of being proactive is ____________

choices.text: Identifying impacts to the components from overruns or underruns
Responding to necessary but unplanned activities that negatively affect the budget
Responding to necessary but unplanned activities that positively affect the budget
Using cost forecasting techniques on a regular basis

explanation:
In Program Financial Management, the program manager must be proactive in identifying factors that create changes to the budget baseline. Another example of being proactive is to identify impacts from components from overruns or underruns. Throughout the program If changes are made with a significant cost Impact, the program’s budget baseline is updated and is re-baselined. All approved changes to the program or a component are incorporated into the budget.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 128–129

text: You are Company A’s program manager for the development of an online banking system for your community bank, for which your company will receive $20 million. Your management at the highest level is totally committed to this program and it is the number one program in Company A’s portfolio. Your program steering committee is dedicated to its success. As a result, the chairperson of the committee is _______________

choices.text: The program sponsor
The CEO
The portfolio manager
The Director of the Enterprise PMO

explanation:
Governance structures differ based on numerous factors with the purpose to monitor and review the progress of the program and delivery of the benefits from the project and non-project work. The program sponsor typically is an executive with a senior role in the organization. In many organizations, the program sponsor is the chairperson of the program steering committee.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 80

text: People seem concerned of the disruptive nature in how work is done in the society throughout the word. Consider, for example, the advent of Uber and Lyft in the transportation services. Therefore, in your business case to meet future market demands, you are leading a program in your dairy cooperative to ensure its products are safe, meet regulatory and legislative requirements, and are ahead of the competition so it causes disruptions rather than reacts to them. You are now preparing your charter and decided to conduct a change assessment to see how the company will adapt to the various changes generated when your program is complete. To do so you _______________

choices.text: Involved a greater number of stakeholders and got their suggestions
Estimated the likelihood and possible impact of the changes
Included a change control board as part of your charter
Ensured you had the authority to approve or reject most of the proposed changes that could affect your program

explanation:
The purpose of a program change assessment is to provide inputs to the program charter among other items. In a change assessment an estimate of the likelihood of possible impacts of changes that could arise is conducted. By doing so, measures can be taken so the program manager can respond to them positively rather in a disruptive way.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 107

text: You want to identify threats to your program as well as any opportunities that could benefit from them. Therefore, as the program manager assume you are working on risk management planning for your program by considering its components. You realize in doing so that ___________________

choices.text: You should establish triggers for the project risks
You should establish an agreed-upon basis to evaluate risks
You should identify intra-project risks
You should establish a contingency reserve

explanation:
Program risk management planning identifies ways to approach and conduct risk management activities. Based on the importance of the program to the organization, it evaluates the needed level, type, and visibility of risk management. While it identifies risk management activities, it also establishes an agreed-upon basis to evaluate risks.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 120

text: Your organization is ISO 9001 certified. As program manager, you have arranged for a member of your company’s Quality Assurance Program (a Black Belt in Six Sigma) to support your program. This team member reports directly to you and by dotted line to the manager of the Quality Assurance Department. In his first audit, he finds that one of the projects includes several key service management activities that have not met quality requirements. Your next step is to ________________

choices.text: Facilitate an off-site meeting of your core program team to determine how best to handle this deficiency
Convene a meeting of your program steering committee to request that an additional resource be added to serve as a project manager for these activities
Prepare a quality assurance change request
Revisit the program’s quality management plan and update it

explanation:
Audits take time, and results must be documented. The program management team is responsible for implementing required quality changes. As a result of the audit, a quality assurance change request should be issued to implement the auditor’s findings, an output of Program Quality Assurance and Control.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 132

text: You are Company A’s program manager for the development of an online banking system for your community bank, for which your company will receive $20 million. One of your first tasks was to work with your sponsor and specify the purpose of the phase-gate reviews and when they will be held on this program. One goal of these reviews is to _________________

choices.text: Monitor the business environment for changes
Assess strategic alignment of the program
Approve the program to continue with modifications
Identify the key decision makers and stakeholders associated with this program

explanation:
Phase-gate reviews serve a number of different purposes. During these reviews, the program steering committee decides whether to continue to the next phase, continue but with modifications, or end the program or a component. The steering committee then approves or disapproves the program’s passage from one significant phase to another.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 75

text: You are a program manager for a software services company. This new software will bring your company into Cloud computing. It also will replace your company’s legacy finance and accounting systems. You are now preparing your program’s scope. You should use the ________________

choices.text: PWBS
Program charter
Business case
Financial framework

explanation:
The program work breakdown structure (PWBS) encompasses the total scope of the program and includes the deliverables to be produced by the components. It then is used to build realistic schedules, develop cost estimates, and organize the work.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 123

text: You manage a program for the Occupational Safety and Health Administration to make all the agency’s regulations performance based and applicable to any industry group. You identified 50 external stakeholders who are active participants in this process, and 30 who are interested but not active, along with 75 interested internal stakeholders. Initially, when you and our team identified these stakeholders, you used _______________

choices.text: Brainstorming
Documentation reviews
Questionnaires
Interviews

explanation:
A brainstorming session with the core team is useful in identifying potential stakeholders, their roles, and significance to the program. It aims to name stakeholders across the entire program life cycle.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 62

text: As a new program manager, your performance is evaluated according to the five domains in the Program Management Standard. One of the criterions in the governance domain is reviewing requests to initiate, transition, and close components. An example as to how you have met this criterion is by ___________________

choices.text: Following the defined escalation path
Ensuring resources are expended effectively
Providing input from customers and component leaders
Having a comprehensive business case

explanation:
This comprehensive business case includes metrics if benefits realization and contribution and comprehensive status reports are available that show deliverable status and assessment of readiness for transition and component closure reports.
PMI® Project Manager Competency Development Framework, 2017, 117–118

text: Assume you are working in a company, CDE, which specializes in new product development. The CDE executives are concerned because its last two products in the on-line music industry were late to market, and by the time they were on the market, competitors had products out with more attractive features to customers. As a result, CDE is in jeopardy of losing its market share in on-line music for mobile phones and tablets and in games for these phones and tablets. You are now in process of working with your research and development team to determine a new product to propose to CDE’s executives. Given the last two experiences, you believe you should include in your business case _______________

choices.text: Existing work under way
Benefit sustainment
High-level roadmap
Comparative advantage analysis

explanation:
Comparative advantage analysis is useful to consider any competing efforts within or external to the organization and is in the business case. it also may include ‘what-if’ analysis to show whether the program’s objectives and intended benefits could be achieved in other ways.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 39

text: You are managing a program to develop a new source of energy in the extreme northern latitudes when solar power is not available. Working with your core program team and your program steering committee, you have identified a number of component projects. Your company has several key projects under way, and resources will be difficult to acquire for this new program. A key consideration is _______________

choices.text: The availability of key staff members
Your ability to negotiate with functional managers for the needed staff
Previous work by the staff as a successful team
The availability of off-shore employees to drive down costs

explanation:
Resource requirements and the program’s resource plan are used in Program Resource Management. As the program manager conducts resource planning, availability is a key consideration in order that critical resources can be optimized for use across components.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 133

text: In your role of establishing this Masters of Science degree in Program Management, your benefit management plan includes both tangible and intangible benefits. You recognize the demand for the degree, and it in turn will lead to new income to the University. It also will enhance customer satisfaction with the University and will demonstrate to the overall project management community that it is following the trends in the profession. You expect a large number of people to enroll in the program based on the interest now in obtaining the PgMP® credential. You have seven projects in your program and are fortunate to have a PMO. You are preparing a defined set of reports in order that __________________

choices.text: There is an opportunity to publicize the program
People can see the overall program’s health
Funding limits are not exceeded
The metrics you identified can be quantified easily

explanation:
With a defied set of reports the PMO, stakeholders, governance, and sponsors can assess the overall program’s health and take action if needed for benefit delivery.
PMI®, The Standard for Program Management, 2017, 51

text: As you work on your program to improve the economic growth of your country, you are following a program management methodology that your agency’s Center of Excellence in Program Management prepared.
