text: The program you are managing spans three years. Phase-gate reviews are recommended to assist program control and management, as well as to facilitate governance. Phase-gate review dates have been defined and you are aware that you need to show evidence that the program can proceed to the next phase. Your program just finished the program definition phase. The program governance structure is established
Expected benefits are in line with the program business case
The risk level remains acceptable to the organization

a- Correct answer! At the end of the program definition phase, component projects are not yet initiated (started). All other answers provide valid phase-exit criteria. b- No! This is a requirement to exit this gate. c- No! This is a valid exit criterion at any gate. d- No! This is a valid exit criterion at any gate.

Because of major technical problems, it is very unlikely that project B will produce its remaining deliverables. During today's steering committee, you explained that only four benefits will be provided out of a total of six expected, and the steering committee has thus recommended that the program be closed. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Discuss the situation with the steering committee and convince them not to close the program until the two remaining benefits are realized
Ask project manager B to accelerate and produce the remaining deliverables which were committed
Ask the steering committee the reason for their request to close the program while two benefits are missing
Proceed to program closure as required by the steering committee

explanation:
a- No! The steering committee must have good reasons to ask for program closure. b- No! The probability of producing the remaining deliverables is very low. You should therefore follow the steering committee's recommendation. c- No! You should adhere to the steering committee's decision. d- Correct! Based on your presentation and on the program's status, the steering committee recommends program closure. Now is the time to close!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Closing the program - Task 33 and standard, section 6.1.12

text: You are managing program X which is composed of four projects: A, B, C and D. From the beginning of your program. you have been extremely sensitive to the fact that program outcomes must generate benefits in line with the strategic objectives of your company. The program is well underway, but you realize that several opportunities emerge that your program could take advantage of. You believe that more benefits could be generated if these opportunities are well managed. According to your estimate, one of your projects, project C, could handle one opportunity, and a new project could handle three other emerging opportunities. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Immediately find a project manager for the new project and propose the name to the steering committee for approval
Update your benefits management plan and show it to the steering committee for approval
Find a way to update the program business case in order to validate these opportunities before updating the plans
Tell project manager C that she will increase her scope of responsibilities by including a new opportunity in her project

explanation:
a- No! This is not the best option. Much too early! o- No! Too early because 'new benefits' are not yet approved by the board. Only an updated business case can show if it is true that those emerging opportunities really bring new benefits or not. c- Correct! This Is the best option. It Is too early to update the benefits management plan, and this should wait until the business case update shows evidence that these opportunities will really bring 'new benefits' to the program. d- No! This is not the best option. Too early!

text: Any program needs to have an appropriate governance structure in order to perform correctly. The program governance structure includes people such as the program manager, the sponsor, the PMO, etc. who will be involved in the various phases of the program using policies, procedures, standards that are derived from company assets. Which is the BEST list of governance plan ingredients?

choices.text: Definitions of roles and responsibilities, structure and composition of the program governance board, stakeholder engagement plan, component initiation criteria and planned phase-gate reviews
Definitions of roles and responsibilities, high level governance plan and meeting schedules, financial model, and periodic "health checks"
Definitions of roles and responsibilities, schedule of planned governance meetings such as phase gate reviews, program health checks and required audits
Definitions of roles and responsibilities, PWBS, structure and composition of the program governance board, governance goals summary, planned phase-gate reviews

explanation:
a- No! The stakeholder engagement plan is not an ingredient of the governance plan. b- No! The financial model is not an ingredient of the governance plan. c- Correct answer! This is a partial list of Ingredients of the program governance plan. d- No! The PWBS is not an ingredient of the governance plan
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 2 and standard, sections 6.1.1.1 and 6.1.1.2

text: In order to assess program performance against expected outcomes and planned benefits, the program manager will prepare phase-gate reviews to be approved by the steering committee. These phase-gate reviews are complemented by periodic health checks. Gate reviews and health checks are different in nature. What is the MAIN difference between gate reviews and heath checks?

choices.text: Gate reviews are planned ahead of time while health checks are performed when needed
Both gate reviews and health checks are formally planned ahead of time
Both gate reviews and health checks do not need to be scheduled ahead of time, only when necessary
Health checks are planned ahead of time while gate reviews are performed when needed

explanation:
a- Correct! Health checks are scheduled when it is necessary to assess program performance. Gate reviews ore formally defined in the program roadmap. Gate review requirements are developed in the governance plan. b- Wrong answer! Health checks are scheduled when it is necessary to assess program performance. c- Wrong answer! Gate reviews must be scheduled ahead of time. They are mentioned in the program roadmap. d- Wrong answer! Health checks are scheduled when it is necessary to assess program performance and gate reviews must be scheduled ahead of time.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 2 and standard, sections 6.1.9 and 6.1.10

text: The program manager should be aware of the Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEF) which may influence the overall management of the program. What is a CORRECT list of Enterprise Environmental Factors?

choices.text: Business environment, funding, program organization, regulatory, and economy
Business environment, geographic diversity, PMO, and technology,
Legislative, regulatory, industry, and market
Legislative, program manager, component project managers, and regulatory

a- No! Program organization in not an enterprise environmental factor (factor OUTSIDE the program). b- No! PMO is not an enterprise environmental factor. The PMO is a management structure. c- Correct! This is a partial list of the enterprise environmental factors. d- No! Program and component managers are not enterprise environmental factors.

choices.text: Comparative advantage analysis. feasibility studies, and PMIS
Comparative advantage analysis. feasibility studies, mandate and SWOT analysis
Feasibility studies, SWOT analysis. assumptions analysis. and historical information analysis

choices.text: Coordinate the management of several projects in order to be more efficient
Manage and optimize project interdependencies
Generate benefits which are in line with the strategic objectives
Generate benefits which are in line with customer expectations

text: You are the program manager of program X. Your program has been running for two years. All benefits have been realized except one, but you believe that the conditions are met to close the program. You prepare a presentation to the next board meeting in order to obtain their agreement. What is the BEST convincing argument you should use?

choices.text: All benefits have been realized, so the program may be closed
All benefits have not been realized, but you can prove that all necessary outcomes have been created to ensure that the missing benefit will be realized later on
You have developed a sustainment plan with the receiving organization
You can prove that all the closure conditions are met because the charter is fulfilled

a- No! The text says that all benefits have NOT been realized. b- No! This is very valid information to prove that the missing benefit will be realized later on. BUT, there may be other reasons not to close the program, such as procurement closure, financial closure, etc. c- This is very useful, but are all closure conditions met? d- Correct answer! text: During the program definition phase. you develop the program roadmap. which is a chronological representation of the program's intended direction. The sponsor recommendation
The program mandate
The program scope statement

Although optional, the mandate is one of the key Inputs for producing the program roadmap. It is an input to 'Program initiation' activities. In addition, an initial business case is usually used as an input. d- No! Too early at this stage. It will be developed later.

This contractor is also involved in other components of the program without any problem. choices.text: Ask for project A closure and try to resolve remaining procurement issues at program level
Do not ask for project A closure until all procurement issues are resolved
Ask for project A closure and call your legal department to open a dispute with the contractor

You will now try to resolve the remaining issues (claims if any, etc.) at program level before escalating if necessary. b- No! Because all contract clauses have been fulfilled, you should now ask for project closure. c- No! Try first to solve the problem at program level before escalating. d- No! Try first to solve the problem at program level before escalating.

text: You are preparing for an important governance board meeting. This meeting will review the performance of the program so far. A board member has informed you that an important stakeholder XYZ is very satisfied whereas another board member reports that another important stakeholder ABC is not satisfied at all. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Ask XYZ to meet ABC and share why she is so happy. You expect that ABC will change his mind when listening to XYZ
Meet ABC and explain why XYZ is happy
Meet ABC. listen carefully to his concerns. and put an agenda item at the next board meeting to introduce consistent mitigation of these concerns

explanation:

Doing this does not really take into consideration ABC's concerns. c- Correct! You have to address the concerns at governance board level because at least 3 persons are aware of the issue (ABC, a board member and you). It is likely that they will ask you to provide the status of it. d- No! You cannot just informally expect to solve such serious problems.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 4

text: Program governance ensures that benefits are realized in conjunction with the strategic objectives of the organization. Governance is composed of a full range of stakeholders: executive sponsor, program director. project managers, program manager. PMO, and project teams. Among the following options. which is the MOST recommended technique to be used in order to assess ongoing performance and progress against the expected outcomes of the program?

choices.text: Establishing formal gate reviews
Defining the timing and objectives of external audits
Planning of periodic health checks that have to be formally scheduled in the program roadmap
Planning of periodic health checks that have to be organized when needed

explanation:
a- No! Gate reviews do much more: they also review strategic alignment, risk level, benefits, etc. only at program gates. b- No! An external audit is not the core method for assessing health; it is more a complementary one. c- Wrong! Health checks are not scheduled in the program roadmap. d- Correct! Periodic health checks represent the best way to assess program health in a sustained way. Health checks are generally held between phase-gate reviews and the governance plan should specify the metrics used during health checks.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 1 1 and standard, section 6.1.10

text: Among the following options, which one is the MOST typical planning technique used to guarantee that all costs of conformance and of nonconformance will be incurred at program level?

choices.text: Cost of Quality (COQJ
Earned Value Method
Return on Investment
Net Present Value

explanation:
a- Correct answer! This Is one of the recommended Tools and Techniques mentioned in the "Plan quality management" process at project level. Quality related tools defined at the project level can be also used at the program level. b- Wrong! Earned Value Method has nothing to do with Quality costs. c- Retun on Investment has nothing to do with Quality costs. d- Wrong! Net Present Value has nothing to do with Quality costs.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 1 and PMBOK®Guide, section 8.1.2.3

text: Your program deals with many vendors and most of them will be common to several of your program's constituent projects. You have consequently decided to manage procurement at the program level rather than at project level. You have assigned one procurement expert in your PMO to manage all procurements on your behalf. This PMO expert has developed the procurement management plan. and is now conducting procurements. As of today. not all vendors have been selected. and no contract has been signed with any of them. When conducting procurements, the PMO expert will generate several outputs. Which is the CORRECT list of these outputs?

choices.text: Performance/earned value reports. request for quote (RFQ), awarded contracts. Program procurement plan. and quality checklists
Performance/earned value reports. invitation for bid (IFB). program budget updates. request for roadmap and program procurement standards
Proposal evaluation criteria. signed agreements. agreements administration plan, and request for proposal (RFPs)
Request for quote (RFQ). request for proposal (RFP). awarded contracts. and program roadmap updates

explanation:
a- No! Quality checklists are an output from the "Program Quality Planning" process. b- No! Request for roadmap is not an output from any process or activity. c- Yes! This Is a correct list of outputs expected from the "Program procurement management" activity. d- No! Program roadmap updates is not an output from the "Program procurement management" activity.
The standard, section 8.2.5

text: Your company is in the process of reorganizing its marketing channels and has decided to put in place a program to manage this major change in the organization. You are the program manager of this highly strategic program. You have identified the key stakeholders in the stakeholder register and you have performed a stakeholder analysis that provides information about stakeholders' attitudes with regard to the program. From your analysis. some stakeholders will have a positive attitude; some will certainly have a negative attitude. Once your program is underway. you find that you were right in your analysis. as one key stakeholder. a functional manager who provides several key resources to your program. shows negative attitudes during checkpoint meetings. During the last meeting. this manager said they will soon withdraw their resources from the program. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Do nothing because you definitely need those key resources. and you do not want them to be taken off the program
Tell this functional manager that because they agreed to provide your program with those key resources. they can't say anything
Talk to this functional manager and explain the importance of having their support
Talk to the program sponsor and explain the situation

explanation:
a- No! Always do something when the number of resources decreases! b- No! This is an autocratic attitude, not really desirable for the long term health of your relationship! c- Correct answer! Talk to the functional manager, explain, communicate, and then, if need be, talk to your sponsor. d- No! You should first talk to the functional manager, and then, if need be, to the sponsor.
PgMP®Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management -Task 3

text: You are managing a software development program which has four projects: A, B, C and D. Projects A, B and C are in charge of developing various software modules and project D mainly performs test activities for the other three projects. You have regular checkpoint meetings with the four project managers, both on an individual basis, and during group sessions. During one checkpoint meeting, project manager D reports a major risk that appeared recently on her project. One of her suppliers may not be able to deliver the test equipment on time; it may be two months later than originally planned. If this happens, it will jeopardize test sessions that are planned to start in one week from now and may delay the creation of the planned benefit by two months. What is the BEST way to handle the situation?

choices.text: Take corrective action and modify the benefits management plan to take into account the two months delay. Plans must reflect reality

Ask project manager D to immediately contact the supplier and work on an alternate solution if possible. You should also inform the steering committee about the two months delay in the benefit realization
Immediately inform the steering committee about the two months delay. They are most interested in benefit realization

Ask project manager D to immediately contact the supplier and work on an alternative solution if possible. You should also look at the plan to see what will be the consequence of the delay on the benefit realization

explanation:
a- No! It is much too early to modify the plan. It is only a risk and not an issue yet. b- No! It is too early to alert the steering committee. It is only a risk, not an issue. c- No! It is too early to alert the steering committee. It is only a risk, not an issue. d- Correct! It is a severe risk, but still not an issue. Project manager D should work with the vendor to find an alternative solution, If possible. Also you should look at what impact the delay has upon benefit realization. It may not be critical.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Benefits Management - Task 7

text: You are managing a software development program which has four projects: A, B, C and D. Projects A B a n d Care in charge of developing various software modules and project D mainly performs test activities for the other three projects. You have regular checkpoint meetings with the four project managers, both on an individual basis, and during group sessions. The meetings with your project managers are going well, but it appears that project teams spend a Jot of time discovering already known problems and correcting them. The same problems seem to pop up again and again in each project and across projects, week after week. Each project manager seems to forget what happened the previous week in their project and in the other projects. You want to understand the reason for this problem and you want to fix it. What is the MOST PROBABLE source of this problem?

choices.text: There is no proper PMIS database in place in the program, which makes life difficult for the projects
The PMO is not playing his support role which involves collecting information from the project managers
There is not a correct feedback process in place to capture lessons learned from the projects
Your project managers have neither read nor signed the communication plan

explanation:
a- No! There may be a PMIS in place, PMIS is only a tool, it does not solve the lack of lessons learned being capture. b- No! The PMO is not the source of the problem. You are responsible for making sure that lessons learned are correctly captured. c- Correct! This must be the number one problem. Make sure that a process Is in place (and used) to capture lessons learned from the projects and from the program. d- No! The problem comes from lessons learned not being properly captured.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Executing the Program - Task 1 8

text: You are managing a software development program which has four projects: A, B, C and D. Projects A, B and C are in charge of developing various software modules and project D mainly performs test activities for the other three projects. You have regular checkpoint meetings with the four project managers and with the PMO. The projects are progressing with difficulty. Project execution is complex, more complex than anticipated. Project members have little experience in their jobs and project managers spend a lot of time helping and counselling them. Two project managers report the fact that some of their members are showing a lack of motivation. Project managers ask you for recommendations about what to do to help project team members perform better. The program PMO is experienced in software development. What is the BEST option for you to take?

choices.text: Ask the PMO to develop a training course on software programming development for the project team members
Move PMO members to project teams in order to speed up software development
Hire an outside consultant to coach, train or mentor according to needs
Ask the PMO to perform an assessment of the situation and to recommend an action plan

explanation:
a- No! The PMO may not have the necessary skills to develop adequate training courses. b- No! The PMO should first conduct an assessment of the situation. c- No! This cannot be the option until the need is clearly stated. d- Yes! This Is the best option. And then, according to the findings, you take action.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Executing the Program - Task 1 9

text: You are a program manager within a humanitarian organization. The program's target is to expand its activities to new geographical regions. One of your project managers made the suggestion of including a local small airline company in the program to optimize freight in his sub region. This initiative could result in adding one more project into the existing program. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: You accept and mandate the project manager to initiate this project
You request the project manager to create a change request
You propose this to the next governance board meeting
You do nothing because this is a small project

explanation:
a- Wrong! The project manager has to justify the initiation of a new project at program level. For this, they first need to write a change request. Then this initiation has to be validated by the governance board. b- Correct! Because It helps the project manager to express this idea in coherence with the program infrastructure, it is up to you to then decide with the CCB (Change Control Board). c­ Wrong! First you have to assess the impact of this new project on the program according to the program management plan. d- No! At least ask "Why is this needed?"
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 28 and standard, section 8.2.1

text: You are managing a program which has four projects: A, B, C and D. You have regular checkpoint meetings with the four project managers, both on an individual basis, and during group sessions. Meetings are going well with all of them, except with project manager D who has a tendency to argue and disagree with most of your remarks. Project managers A, B and C have started to be a little bit nervous with their colleague who is creating a climate of discomfort in the program team. You realize that the situation has become difficult and you want to understand what is happening. You invite project manager D for a discussion in your office. You want to get the best out of the discussion. What skill should you exercise MOST during the discussion?

choices.text: Leadership
Conflict resolution
Influencing
Active listening

explanation:
a- No! Communication skills are most important in this situation. It is not a matter of leadership. b¬ No! Communication skills are most important in this situation. There may not be a conflict (yet!). c­ No! Communication skills are most important in this situation. d- Correct! Pay a lot of attention to what project manager D says, and be really Involved in the discussion. Active listening Is the most critical skill in a face to face discussion.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Executing the Program - Task 1 9 and Core Skills CS1

text: The program you are managing is in charge of designing, building and delivering a new space rocket to an important government agency. Even if it seems that this is a project, a program is needed in this case because it belongs to the space industry. According to the following options what is the BEST reason for having a program instead of a project?

choices.text: In this industry, it often happens that funds are not all available from day 1. Therefore, you need to deliver interim benefits to the contractor so that you obtain funds according to major outcomes
A program is needed because normally a rocket costs several tens of millions of Euros
This is a standard request from the contracting companies to have highly experienced people to direct the program.

A rocket is the sum of several technologies (boosters, air conditioning, solar panels, telecom payload, etc.) that require very careful management of interfaces between sub systems because of the technology complexity

explanation:
a- Yes! This is correct; financing a program is not straightforward, because of its size and duration. b- No! Budget at completion is not a criterion for deciding to have a project or a program. c- No! The choice of the person directing the project or program is not a criterion. d- No! This is not true in all cases because this answer is very 'project/sub-projects oriented'.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Strategic program Management - Task 7 and standard, section 8.1 .2.4

text: The program you are managing is in charge of designing, building and delivering a new space rocket to an important government agency. You have a change control board (CCB) at the program level to assess change requests on a number of criteria: scope. quality. schedule, cost. contracts, risks, etc. Because the program is quite large. changes that impact earned value less than 5% are processed at project level. this is an example of:

choices.text: Resource leveling
Smoothing
Tolerance
Delegation of governance

explanation:
a- No! Leveling means the even spreading of resources between components. b- No! Smoothing is a conflict resolution technique. c- Correct answer! d- No! Not really used by PMI, this concept being a hierarchy of issues and solutions.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 28

text: The program you are managing is in charge of designing, building and delivering a new space rocket to an important government agency. You just finished defining the program. It seems that the people working on the program do not really interrelate; meetings are slow, misunderstandings are numerous. and people quite often remain distant from each other. You would like to increase cohesion in the team. Among the following options. what is the BEST statement concerning this team?

choices.text: The team is in a forming phase
The team is in a storming phase
The team is in a transforming phase
The team is in a non-producing phase

explanation:
a- Yes! This is correct. The team is in the first phase of Tuckman's model b- No! This phase needs people to work interactively together; typically, people read each other’s documents and criticize them, but they interact. c- No! Not in PMI vocabulary. d- No! Not in PMI vocabulary.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Executing the Program - Task 1 9 and PMBOK® Guide, section 9.4 (Develop team)

text: The program architecture is the set of components that define the program and contribute to its planned benefits. During the development of the program architecture. rules for the inclusion (and exclusion) of program components should be defined. and the interrelationships between the components should also be identified. During the program life cycle, the architecture of the program is subject to change. but one key responsibility of the program manager is to properly manage the program architecture. Among all the options, which is the BEST reason to change the program architecture?

choices.text: The sponsor has decided to move the program manager to another position
The steering board is discussing the possibility of including one more project in the program
The steering board has agreed to close one program component
The steering committee has agreed to add one more component to the program

explanation:
a- No! This is not a valid reason to modify the program architecture. b- No! The steering committee is only investigating the possibility of including a new project. It is much too early to update the program architecture! c- No! This is not a good reason to modify the program architecture. This is part of the life of the program. Component projects will close one after the other, until the program also closes. d- Correct! The addition of the new component may have an impact on the program architecture.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Executing the Program - Task 1 7 and standard, section 4.2.2

text: The program architecture defines the relationships among its components, related to both operational and project activities. The program manager is responsible for managing all the interfaces between these components. During the life of the program, new components may be brought into the program and some may be removed from the program. In order to communicate interface changes to stakeholders, guidelines should be developed. In which of the following situations is it BEST to communicate a program interface change to stakeholders?

choices.text: A change request is rejected and the program architecture does not change
A change request is accepted at the component level but has no impact on other components
A new PMO member has been brought into the group
A scope change in one component has an impact on the program architecture

explanation:
a- No! The change request is rejected therefore no program architecture change and no interface change. b- No! The change request has no effect on other components. No interface change. c- No! This should not impact component interfaces. At least. this is not the BEST option. d- Yes! For sure, this needs to be communicated to stakeholders as it impacts component Interfaces.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 5 and standard, section 4.2.2 and section 6.1.8

text: You are managing a program which has three component projects and some other work. Recently, due to a big shift in the market, the strategic objectives of the company have changed. As a result of this change, your program has been impacted and management has decided to stop one of your components, and to initiate two new projects as part of your program. You know that, in your program, you are responsible for managing component interfaces. As a result of the management decision to stop one project and to add two more, HOW MANY program component interfaces are you managing now?

choices.text: Four interfaces
There is not enough information in the text
Six interfaces
Ten interfaces

explanation:
a- No! There is not enough information to be able to count the number of interfaces. b- Correct! It is not possible to determine precisely how many Interfaces the program manager has to manage. We have no idea about component Interrelationships. c- No! There is not enough information to be able to count the number of interfaces. d- No! There is not enough information to be able to count the number of interfaces.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Executing the Program - Task 23

text: You are a program manager attending a governance board meeting and presenting slides in order to pass a gate review. What is the MOST likely document to be reviewed in such a meeting?

choices.text: Program Management Plan
Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Benefits Register
Program Procurement Plan

explanation:
a- Yes! This ls correct because it simply includes all the other plans. b- No! This engagement plan could be reviewed but it is not the most likely to be reviewed. c- No! This register could be reviewed but it is not the most likely to be reviewed. d- No! This plan could be reviewed but it is not the most likely to be reviewed.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Governance - Task 3

text: Your program X is experiencing severe delays with component project A. Project manager A informs you that a possible reason is a resource conflict that still remains between 2 work packages in her project. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Organize a meeting with project manager A and the persons in charge of the delayed work packages to find an appropriate solution

Organize a meeting with project manager A and the persons in charge of the delayed work packages to impose your authority and prove that, as a program manager, you can perform better than project manager A
Ask project manager A to really assess to what extent this resource conflict is affecting the schedule of her own project
Meet the 2 persons in charge of the respective work packages to find a suitable solution

explanation:
a- No! The program manager coordinates efforts between projects but does not directly manage individual projects. b- No! The program manager coordinates efforts between projects but does not directly manage individual projects. c- Yes! This is the correct answer as you ask the project manager to perform an in-depth analysis of the relationship between resources and delay. By asking her to look at the project again, you are helping her to find and fix a possible misunderstanding of what ls really happening on the project. d- No! The program manager does not manage individual projects, not even parts of them.
The standard, section 6.1.6 (Issue governance)

text: You are the newly appointed program manager of company XYZ which specializes in global humanitarian aid. The board members have expressed dissatisfaction with the program performance during several board meetings. They state that it is difficult to see from the information provided whether the program needs correction or not. As newly appointed program manager, what is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Meet individually with each project manager to analyze their performance reports in order to formalize requests for corrective actions
Update the business case
Travel to meet the three most important regional CEOs
Assess the completeness of the information provided in the reports with respect to the concerns expressed by the board, and share a targeted update of the program report with all project managers

explanation:
a- No! This option does not take any action at program level even though it seems the board is upset by the PROGRAM 's performance reports not by the project performance reports. b- No! This does not address collecting, measuring and disseminating the performance report. c- No! This does not address collecting, measuring and disseminating the performance report. d- Yes! This is the first action to be taken to guarantee the completeness of the reports: gap analysis, risk analysis, issues analysis and trend, probability analysis.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 27 and standard, section 7.2.2.3

text: You are a program manager within a humanitarian organization. This program targets to expand its activities to new geographical regions. One of your project managers made the suggestion of including a local small airline company in the program to optimize freight in his sub region. This initiative could result in adding one more project to the existing program. The governance board rejected initiating the new project. What is the MOST probable cause of the board's refusal?

choices.text: One of the key sponsors was not consulted previously
There are already too many projects in your program
The outcomes of this project were not sufficiently validated with respect to the organizational strategy
You did not sufficiently argue that this new project coherently impacts the architecture of the program

explanation:
a- No! It is of course not essential to meet them all before, just good practice, even if it is not always possible. b- No! This is not a valid reason for rejection. c- Correct! Always explain the change in a strategic way to the board. d- Wrong! It is very likely that you showed the coherence of the program architecture to the board.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 29 and standard, section 8.2.1

text: You are contributing to the initiation of a program you expect to manage. This program consists of renewing the nationwide telecommunication backhaul network of your organization. The organization has several affiliates around the country and their expenditure costs have to be cut as a result of this program. As you introduce the stakeholder register to the governance board, several board members express concerns and at this stage, you fail to pass the review to authorize the program. What is the NEXT action you should take?

choices.text: Clearly identify the stakeholders list, including the sponsor, and create a matrix to state their position concerning the program
Invite new members to the governance board to be sure that all affiliates are represented on the board
Recommend a decentralized governance board structure to handle the complexity of the program which is due to the number of affiliates
Simply add the board members to the stakeholder list

explanation:
a- Correct! b- No! The governance board is representative of your environment, but it should have a limited number of members to be efficient. c- No! This is contrary to the definition of a governance board that centralizes all program information to take decisions. d- No! Don't be naïve!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task l

text: You are contributing to the initiation of a program you expect to manage. This program consists of renewing the continent wide telecommunication backhaul network of your organization. The organization has several affiliates all over the country and their expenditure costs have to be cut as a result of this program. As you introduce the stakeholder register to the governance board, several board members express concerns and at this stage, you fail to pass the review to authorize the program. Some board members even think that the program will face strong opposition from five stakeholders and that this is not good for the future of the program. What is the IMMEDIATE action you should take?

choices.text: Ask your assistant to organize a 10-day trip to meet and convince the affiliates throughout the continent
Check historical data on the five stakeholders to better understand them. Ask for the support of one of the veteran board members
Organize yourself to quickly obtain historical data on the five stakeholders, and ask your program team to provide you with their current positions
Emphasize the other good parts of the mandate you are elaborating to smooth one accommodate these concerns

explanation:
a- No! Ideal but this is time consuming and expensive, time is running on, and this list of 5 may be incomplete; you have to make sure that this list is complete first. b- Correct! c- No! You should not pass this problem to your program team; you need to solve the problem on your own. d- No! Never ignore a concern coming from a board member!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Stakeholder Management - Task 2

text: You are planning the activities for your program. The scope of the program is well defined; you understand the program requirements and the program architecture are established. You now want to decompose the work to be performed in the program and create the program work breakdown structure (PWBS). You ask your project managers to do the same for their projects and create their WBS. You plan to use the project's WBS as an input to creating the program WBS. You have drafted a program WBS on your own and you also have received the projects' WBS from your project managers. What is the BEST option now to create the PWBS?

choices.text: Incorporate the first or first two levels of the projects' WBS into the program WBS
Include each entire project's WBS into the program WBS
Select the projects' work packages and include them into the program WBS
Ignore the projects' WBS because they only relate to the projects and not to the program

explanation:
a- Correct! This is typically done when creating, a PWBS. b- No! Only include the top one or two levels from the projects' WBS into the PWBS, c- No! Do not include the projects' work packages in the PWBS! d- No! Do not ignore the projects' WBS because they are a key input to the PWBS creation!
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Planning the program - Task 8 and standard, section 8.1.2.12

text: You are planning the activities for a complex program composed of three projects. The scopes of the projects are well defined, but the scope at the program level is still not finalized. You are not sure if some non-project work will be incorporated in the program or not. You want to move ahead in the program planning activities and you start creating an initial version of the program work breakdown structure (PWBS). As of today, what is the BEST option to create a meaningful PWBS?

choices.text: Ask your project managers to develop their project's WBS, and consolidate the PWBS with the project's ones. If the non-project work is confirmed, you will then update the PWBS with that additional piece of work
Wait for confirmation on the non-project work as it will impact the PWBS
Ask your project managers to develop their project's WBS, and consolidate the PWBS with the project's ones. In any case, the non-project work will not impact the PWBS
The PWBS creation is not under your responsibility. It is the sponsor's responsibility because he is accountable for the program success

explanation:
a- Correct! You will update the PWBS with the non-project work when it is confirmed (or not). b- No! You should not wait. Consolidate now the PWBS with the data available from the projects at present. You will update the PWBS later if needed. c- Wrong! If confirmed, non-project work will impact the PWBS. d- Wrong! The PWBS creation is under the program manager's responsibility, not the sponsor's.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Planning the program - Task 8 and standard, section 8.1.2.12

text: You are planning the activities for a complex program composed of three projects and some recurring activities. You are developing the program management plan which integrates the program's subsidiary plans. The program management plan will be the primary input to program execution. The program management plan mainly describes how the program will be managed. What is NOT an appropriate list of plans included in the program management plan?

choices.text: The risk management plan, the schedule management plan, the governance pion, and the benefits management plan
The procurement management plan, the scope management plan, the stakeholder engagement plan, and the steering committee management plan
The resource management plan, the governance plan, the quality management plan and the benefits management pion
The quality management plan, the risk management plan, the financial management pion and the schedule management plan

explanation:
a- Wrong answer! This is a valid list or plans included in a program management plan. b- Correct answer! There is no 'steering committee management plan! c- Wrong answer! This is a valid list of plans included in a program management plan. d- Wrong answer! This is a valid list of plans included in a program management plan.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Planning the program - Task 9 and standard, section 7.1.2.2

text: You are planning the activities for a complex program composed of three projects and some recurring activities. You are developing the program management plan which integrates the program's subsidiary plans such as scope management, schedule management, etc. The program management plan will be the primary input to program execution. You are now developing the program quality management pion which will also be included in the program management plan. You are aware that most quality planning activities occur at each component level. What is the MOST appropriate list of elements you should include in the program quality management plan?

choices.text: Program quality standards, program quality policy, quality metrics, quality assurance and control specifications, and quality control activities required at component level
Program quality standards, program quality policy, quality checklists, and roles and responsibilities for quality related activities at component level
Program quality standards, program quality policy, and program quality estimates of costs
Component quality plans, program quality standards, and program quality policy

explanation:
a- Wrong! The program quality management plan should not include the quality control activities required at component level. b- Wrong! The program quality management plan should not include the roles and responsibilities at the component level. c- Correct! This is the most appropriate list (although incomplete!). d- Wrong! The program quality management plan should not include the quality plan of the components. It may be just a pointer to the plans.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Planning the program - Task 9 and standard, section 8.1.2.8

text: A portfolio is usually composed of components such as programs and projects. What is a TRUE statement with regard to portfolio components?

choices.text: Portfolios cannot include portfolios
Portfolios always include projects
Portfolios can include non-project work
Portfolios always include programs

explanation:
a- Wrong answer! Portfolios may include portfolios (or subsidiary portfolios). E.g. a company portfolio may include business unit portfolios. b- Wrong answer! Some portfolios might not include projects. c- Correct answer! Portfolios sometimes Include non-project work, such as recurring activities which are not managed as a project. For instance, regression tests, upgrading or debugging activities, maintenance, ongoing operations, etc. d- Wrong answer! Some portfolios might not include programs.
The Standard for Portfolio Management - Fourth Edition, section 1.3

text: You are managing a program composed of three projects: A, B and C. You want to evaluate the performance of your program using earned value parameters collected from each individual project. As of today, project A has a CPI of .8, and AC = 100. Project B has a SPI = 1.5 and EV = 200. For project C. cost variance (CV) = 50 and AC = 150. What is the earned value (EV) at program level?
explanation:
a- Wrong answer! Program EV = 480. b- Wrong answer! Program EV = 480. c- Correct! For project A, CPI (EV/AC) = 0.8 and AC = 100. So for project A, EV = 80. For project B, EV = 200. For project C, cost variance (CV = EV-AC) is 50, and AC = 150. So for project C, EV = 200. For the program, EV = sum of the components' EVs = 80 + 200 + 200 = 480. d- Wrong answer! Program EV = 480.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 25 and PMBOK® Guide, section 7.4.2.2

text: You are managing a program composed of three projects: A, B and C. You want to evaluate the performance of your program using earned value parameters collected from each individual project. As of today, project A has a CPI of .8, and AC = 100. Project B has a SPI = 1.5 and EV = 200. For project C, cost variance (CV) = 50 and AC = 150. What is the program actual cost (AC)?

choices.text: Not enough information to answer

explanation:
a- Wrong answer! There is not enough information to answer the question. b- Correct! For project B, we know the SPI (EV /PV = 1.5) and EV = 200. There is no Information about the actual cost (AC) for project B. So, we do not have enough Information to calculate the program AC (which Is the sum of its components' ACs). c- Wrong answer! There is not enough information to answer the question. d- Wrong answer! There is not enough information to answer the question.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 25 and PMBOK® Guide, section 7.4.2.2

text: You are managing a program composed of three projects: A, B and C. You want to evaluate the performance of your program using earned value parameters collected from each individual project. As of today, project A has a CPI of 8, and AC = 100. Project B has a SPI = 1.5 and EV = 200. For project C, cost variance (CV) = 50 and AC = 150. Which option is TRUE about projects A, B and C?

choices.text: Project A is under budget
Project A is over budget and project B is late
Project B is ahead of schedule and project C is under budget
Project A is over budget and project C is ahead of schedule

explanation:
a- Wrong answer! CPI is less than 1. So project A is over budget. b- Wrong answer! For project B, SPI is greater than 1, so project B is ahead of schedule. c- Correct! For project B, SPI is greater than 1, so project B is ahead of schedule. For project C, cost variance is positive, so project C is under budget. d- Wrong answer! We have no information about project C being late or ahead of schedule.
PgMP® Examination Content Outline 2011 / Controlling the Program - Task 25 and PMBOK® Guide, section 7 .4.2.2

text: During the program life cycle, the program manager is regarded by all stakeholders as an individual that drives the change through the organization. The program manager has multiple communication channels that he or she engages in throughout the program and in every meeting. Consider you are in a meeting with 8 stakeholders. How many communication channels are there?
explanation:
The
answer is incorrect.
Communication channels =[ (yourself + 8) * (yourself + 8 -1)] / 2 = 36

text: Programs are intended to deliver benefits to the sponsoring organization. The program manager and steering committee monitor benefits realization throughout the program delivery and capture opportunities to maximize the delivery of benefits. Throughout the program, you monitor benefits using

choices.text: Preparing performance reports
Phase gate reviews
Heath checks reviews
Other program reports

explanation:
Health checks include performance reviews on periodic basis. They assess program’s ongoing performance and benefits realization and sustenance. Participants can send representatives and are not required to attend. These reviews result in performance reports and dashboards
Reference: SPM V4 Page 76 - 6.1.10

text: In programs, normally the contracts are signed at program level but managed at component level; admin and closeout decisions are managed at component level. However, some of the contracts are administered at program level to benefit many components. In this case

choices.text: Contract closure is at component level
Contracts are always administered at the component level
Component managers coordinate or report deliverable information
Component managers report procurement results and closeouts

explanation:
Normally, once the program standards are in place and the contracts are awarded, administration and closeout of most of these contracts are transitioned to the components; the components report procurement results and closeouts to program. In this case, program manager maintains visibility to ensure the program budget is properly expended to obtain benefits. However, in some situations, procurement contracts are administered at program level; in this case, component managers coordinate or report deliverable information and contract changes and issues to the program management team
Reference: SPM V4 Page 131 - 8.2.5.1

text: You have successfully performed the implementation of the program to release a new drug to cure cancer all around the world and you are getting into the final stages before closure. You are currently closing all projects and contract. Successful closure of a contract is done after ensuring that

choices.text: All deliverables have been satisfactorily completed
All payments have been made
There are no outstanding contractual issues
All of the options

explanation:
In program contract closure, a formal closure is done after ensuring that all deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made and that there are no outstanding contractual issues. The three are done in same order
Reference: SPM V4 Page 140 - 8.3.3

text: Once funds are received and program begins paying expenses, the financial effort moves into tracking, monitoring and controlling the program’s funds and expenditures. As part of program financial management, the program team prepares component cost estimation and program cost budgeting. Which of the below is an input to the program cost budgeting?

choices.text: Component cost estimates
Cost of program management and supporting program activities
Contracts
All of the options

explanation:
Inputs to the program cost budgeting are component cost estimates, cost of program management and supporting program activities, program schedule and contracts
Reference: SPM V4 Page 129 - 8.2.3.1

text: Programs are complex; they undergo a lot of changes and face problems during their lifecycles. As a program manager, it is your responsibility to capture, analyze, record and take action against the problems that occur and implement changes as a result of that. Your program is having a lot of changes and it is over budget and behind schedule; however, the steering committee gave you a go decision during the last phase gate review meeting. What is a possible reason for this?

choices.text: You are a highly regarded program manager and steering committee is sure you can meet objectives
Program hasn’t crossed the organization’s risk threshold yet
You have met with key stakeholders and asked them to give you one last chance to course correct the program
You brother is the CEO

explanation:
The only correct reason is that your program hasn’t crossed the organization’s risk threshold yet
Reference: SPM V4 Page 41 - 3.5.2

text: Programs are complex in nature and undergo a lot of changes through their lifecycles. The changes may require modifications at the level of the program and program documents; bigger changes may affect the organization’s strategic objectives of the organization. Your program to launch the new ice cream flavors is having a lot of unexpected changes and stakeholders are not happy about this. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Do nothing as changes are normal in a program
Perform a change assessment and update the affected documents
Recommend program termination
Resign from your position

explanation:
The program is undergoing a big number of unexpected changes, which means that something was missed during the initial assessment. Re-doing the assessment would be the correct choice in this case to check what has changed or what have been missed and re-align the program accordingly.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 107 - 8.1.1.1

text: Success criteria are used in a program to maintain the minimum level of acceptable delivery of benefits, outputs or results. The program undergoes a lot of changes and it is the responsibility of the program manager to always keep an eye on meeting the program success criteria. Which of the below documents contains the component success criteria?

choices.text: Program business case
Program charter
Component business case
Program scope statement

explanation:
The question asks about the component success criteria, which is part of the component business case.
Pay attention to this in the exam. Questions may talk about the program however, when it comes to the end, they ask you about the component.
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam

text: You are managing a big festival near a village and during the festival; a big circus parade will be present with a lot of animals doing shows. A week before the festival start, animal rights agents have filed a complaint against you to the village council and their request was accepted. What is your mistake in this case?

choices.text: You did not analyze your stakeholder correctly
You did not have a strong business case
You did not identify animal rights agents as stakeholders in your program
You did not offer benefits to the village council

explanation:
The issue here is that you did not identify animal rights agents as stakeholders in your program; otherwise, you would have found out their opinion during analysis and tried to collaborate with them
Stakeholder identification is very important and should span the entire stakeholders range
Reference: SPM V4 Page 60 - 5.1

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups and you know that you will need a good communication strategy to maintain alignment with stakeholders’ expectations. Communication strategy is derived from?

choices.text: Business case
Stakeholder engagement strategy and plan
PWBS
Program architecture

explanation:
Communication strategy is derived from stakeholder engagement plan and particularly the strategy section
Reference: SPM V4 Page 64 - 5.3

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups and you know that you will need a good communication strategy to maintain alignment with stakeholders’ expectations. Stakeholders’ engagement strategy is derived from?

choices.text: Power vs. interest grid
Business case
Stakeholders’ engagement
Program architecture

explanation:
Stakeholder engagement strategy is derived from power vs. interest grid established in stakeholder analysis and planning activity. Each stakeholder is engaged according to his quadrant
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: Your CEO is a PMI member with the right experience to back it up. He injected the spirit of the project, program and portfolio management in the organization and has been leading the way all along. After the strategic planning cycle, objectives and goals were divided into initiatives to be targeted in portfolios. You were appointed as a program manager on an important program having the highest priority in the portfolio. Which of the below documents describes the purpose of the program?

choices.text: Program mission statement
Business case
Program charter
Program architecture

explanation:
Program mission statement is a general statement of how you will achieve your program's vision. It establishes the program direction.
Reference: multiple occurrence in the exam. ECO targets the mission statement as well in its strategic program management section, particularly tasks 1 and 4.
The BC is a cost vs benefit document and the BC is the first document prepared in a program and is used as the program justification for expending resources; it corresponds to "why the program was undertaken" which is the purpose of the program. The correct answer is BC
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: You are newly appointed to a program which is already in delivery phase. You notice that there are a lot of complex templates, everybody can see all information and you are getting a lot of similar questions to data you have already presented. Your best course of action is

choices.text: Review PMIS
Review stakeholder register
Review stakeholder engagement plan
Review stakeholder communication plan

explanation:
Best approach in this scenario is to review PMIS in order to define or update processes to share information while defining access rights on specific information. This will help in maximizing synergies. With relation to the question, you review the PMIS because you have a redundancy of questions on the same topics. After you review the PMIS, you will update the processes, templates maybe, and you will have for example multiple interpretations of the same data in different ways to cater for the need; of course you should not forget the access rights because not everybody can see any data.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 100

text: Your program to launch new flavors of ice cream is mid-way through the delivery phase and the steering committee is constantly having a close eye on the program closure because it is critical to the sustainability of the organization. Which of the below ensures achieving strategic alignment in a program?

choices.text: Health checks
Good planning
Phase gate reviews
Sustainment plan

explanation:
Phase gate reviews enable governance approval for the continuation of a program from one phase to another, continuation may include modifications. It includes reviewing and approving changes to the program; it is held at milestones, components start and end; it mandates attendance of selected key stakeholders and it results in go/no-go decisions. Phase gate reviews criteria are strategic alignment and value delivery. They are used to ensure achieving strategic alignment
Reference: SPM V4 Page 75 - 6.1.9

text: Your program is mid-way through the delivery phase and it is performing as planned. So far, you have been managing the resources allocation and optimization successfully. Today, one of your component managers raises an issue to you that one scarce resource is needed as a full-timer by two of the components concurrently. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Assign the needed resource to a component as prioritized by steering committee
Assign the needed resource to a component as prioritized by sponsor
Assign the needed resource to a component as prioritized by criteria defined in resource management plan
Assign the needed resource to a component as prioritized by the component managers

explanation:
Resource prioritization decisions should be based on the guidelines in the program resource management plan.
In the exam if you interdependency as an option in similar scenarios, do not choose it as the resource is needed as a full-timer on both components. If you had the choice to for example assign the resource to work 50% of his/her time on each component, you would have done interdependency management
Reference: SPM V4 Page 119 - 8.1.2.9

text: Benefits are the most important in a program; the successful delivery of the intended benefits is required for the program successful delivery. Due to the complexity and uncertainty in a program, a lot of changes occur and some of them are reflected to the benefit level. Changes to the benefit level are to be documented in

choices.text: Benefit register
Benefit list
Benefit transition plan
Benefit management plan

explanation:
Benefits register records the changes in benefits levels. It is used by the program manager to track the achievement of benefits. Benefits level, benefits progress, benefits realization levels or benefits delivery are all used in the exam to point to the benefits progress which is recorded in the benefits register and extracted in the benefits report to be communicated to related stakeholders.
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam

text: During the strategic planning cycle of an organization, the vision and mission are used to produce strategic goals and objectives documented in the strategic plan, which is then divided into sets of initiatives. Each set of initiatives may be grouped under a portfolio grouping multiple programs within it. When starting a program, what should be your first step/activity as a program manager?

choices.text: Preparing business case
Preparing high level roadmap
Engage stakeholders
Defining program vision

explanation:
The first step/activity of a program is to draft the program vision; the documents prepared during formulation and planning serve as the direction towards the vision.
Pay attention, the questions states "first step" and not "first document" which is key to point to the correct option. If it were "document", than BC would be the correct answer. However the first step is drafting the program vision
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam and insights from our instructors. Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: Resources are planned right from the beginning of a program, with an estimate of the required staff and facilities prepared during business case and reflected in program charter. You are managing a program which will include a large number of program resources due to its criticality and complexity. You realize, that in your program, you get permanent resources to manage the program during

choices.text: Program infrastructure development
Program delivery phase
Right before the closure phase
When preparing the charter

explanation:
You get permanent resources during program infrastructure development which occurs after the charter approval (which authorizes you to use resources).
You should distinct between these resources and the resources needed to manage the components as they become permanent after component charter approval.
Reference: it is a consolidation of multiple concepts from the charter section (Page 36 - 3.2) and the infrastructure development one (Page 99 - 7.2.2.1), and from a lot of insights from students who have taken the exam

text: During the course of the program, the program manager and program team use quantitative and qualitative analysis techniques to collect and analyze data related to risks, stakeholders, etc. Which of the below are quantitative analysis techniques and tools

choices.text: High/Medium/Low measurements
Impact Scale
Monte Carlo analysis
All of the options

explanation:
Monte Carlo is the only quantitative method. All others are qualitative
Reference: exam questions, PMBOOK methods for calculations

text: You are in the delivery phase of the program to deliver the next generation remote cars with an extremely reliable battery that will last for 12 hours of play time. You are mid-way through your program and due to changes you realize the need to integrate two new components in order to answer to new regulations. When integrating this change, which of the below is unlikely to be modified?

choices.text: Roadmap
Charter
Program management plan
Business case

explanation:
As a rule of thumb, a change affects all the mentioned artifacts; however, the charter defines the benefits, and when a change affects program benefits, charter would be updated as well. Here, the change does not affect program benefits, as the benefit is still the same, but two components are integrated to realize new regulatory aspects.
Business case is updated as both components will require resources such as cost which will alter the cost-benefit balance. Program Management Plan and Roadmap are updated to reflect the way to handle the components and the way the components fit in the timeline of the program

text: During the formulation phase of a program, the program manager does initial assessments in order to come out with estimates to be presented to the steering committee as part of the feasibility analysis in the business case. The steering committee is especially concerned when studying the business case in the cost of investment and the return on investment; they look at the total cost of ownership (TCO) in order to know the direct and indirect costs in a program. TCO includes

choices.text: Full cycle cost
Transition cost
Sustainment cost
All of the options

explanation:
The total cost of ownership helps in making a decision whether to pursue a program or pursue another one. It includes costs of full cycle, transition and sustainment
Reference: SPM V4 Page 113 - 8.1.2.3

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Who is responsible for stakeholder communication in a program?

choices.text: Program sponsor
Program manager
Program steering committee
All of the options

explanation:
Program manager is responsible for stakeholder communication in a program. Of course the remaining entities will have a role in this however it will not be one of their responsibilities e.g. in the case you have a minister as a key stakeholder, one of the SC members or even the sponsor will keep an eye on the communication with the minister, however you will be the one preparing the reports and sending them
Reference: SPM V4 Page 66 - 5.5 (this section only mentions the program manager as a responsible entity)

text: You and your program team are estimating the duration of the program. You came out with the following: - Optimistic: 5 months; - Pessimistic: 12 months; - Most probable: 8 months. What is the proposed duration of the program?

choices.text: 5 months
24.5 months
8.16 months
8 months

explanation:
PERT formula = (pessimistic + optimistic + 4*most probable) / 6 = 8.16 months
Reference: PMBOOK. No need to go study it, we have included the needed formula for PgMP (it has occurred in the exam however on rare occasions)

text: Organizations' strategies change, and changes might affect the programs. Some programs might be closed, updated or added. You have been working with your program management team to deliver your program and you are already mid-way through delivery. Your sponsor calls you and informs you, that due to the strategic changes in the organization, your program has been terminated; what is your course of action in this case?

choices.text: Archive PMIS
Transition finished components
Try to talk the sponsor to change his decision
Final performance review

explanation:
Program has been terminated; no matter the reason, you must start the closure phase activities, starting with preparing the final performance review. This review will be part of the final program report
Reference: ECO Task 31 - Closing The Program / SPM V4 Page 138 - 8.3

text: You are in the definition phase and preparing the program charter. You have your planned benefits and you are listing them along with the benefits strategy in the charter. Which document establishes the relationship between the expected benefits and the planned program activities?

choices.text: Program roadmap
Program architecture
Program schedule
Program charter

explanation:
A roadmap is a chronological representation of a program intended direction, graphically depicting dependencies between major milestones and decision points, reflecting linkage between the business strategy and the program work. Roadmap links benefits to the execution strategy, helps in assessing program benefits delivery progress, is used as input to master schedule and it reflects the pace at which benefits are realized. The roadmap establishes the relationship between the expected benefits and the planned activities
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3

text: You are conducting program assessments in order to prepare the business case for you program. You are excited about being the program manager on the program with the highest priority in your organization. You have submitted your business case. After business case approval, program manager?

choices.text: Prepares high level assessments
Prepares roadmap
Prepares charter
Prepares program management plan

explanation:
The correct steps in program definition are: Strategic plan -> high level assessment and high level roadmap -> business case -> program charter -> baseline roadmap -> program management plan and infrastructure development -> baselined benefits register and revised business case and roadmap
Reference: SPM V4 Page 34 - Figure 3-1, in addition to ECO Strategic Program Management tasks 2 and 3, and finally insights from the exam questions

text: You have been working on the launching of the new ice cream flavors and you have excelled in doing so. The program has arrived to the final stage and all the projects and contracts are now closed. After program close-out decision, you?

choices.text: Transition program
Do financial closure
Prepare final performance report
Close program

explanation:
The correct steps in program closure are: Contracts closed and projects closed -> customer/sponsor sign-off -> Closure phase which contains the following activities. Final performance report -> steering committee reviews and validates the program against a fulfilled charter -> steering committee recommends closure to sponsor -> sponsor validates delivery against business case -> close out decision -> program transition, knowledge transition, PMIS archival and resource disposition -> post review meeting -> financial closure -> program closed
Reference: SPM V4 Page 78 - 6.1.12, Page 97 - 7.1.4, Page 102 - 7.2.2.5, in addition to ECO Closing the Program - All tasks, and finally insights from exam questions.

text: During planning, the program manager and the program management team prepare the program management plan with its subsidiary plans in order to guide the program delivery and closure activities to a successful benefits realization. From the subsidiary plans, the change management plan is particularly important to monitor and control changes through the course of the program. What is considered a part of the Program change management plan?

choices.text: Establishes change management principles and procedures
Evaluates and determines disposition of requested changes
Includes how to authorize the change requests
All of the options

explanation:
The change management plan establishes change management principles and procedures, the approach for capturing changes, evaluates and determines disposition of requested changes, documents and communicates the change requests with supporting details, includes how to authorize the change requests and how to evaluate the impact of change requests
Reference: SPM V4 Page 112 - 8.1.2.1

text: Program manager manages performance throughout the program lifecycle and continuously report to steering committee and stakeholders about the progress. Earned value management EVM is used by the program manager to compare planned vs. actual work and is especially important for

choices.text: Performance Measurement
Financial Management
Contract Administration
All of the options

explanation:
All of the options is the correct answer.
Earned Value Management (EVM) helps project managers to measure project performance. It is a systematic project management process used to find variances in projects based on the comparison of work performed and work planned. EVM is used on the cost and schedule control and can be very useful in project forecasting, in addition it helps measuring the program benefits which resolve to quantitative terms i.e. financial terms (cost, etc.)
Reference: SPM V4 Page 101 - 7.2.2.3, Page 128 - 8.2.3, Page 131 - 8.2.5.1

text: You are mid-way through your program to launch a new line of remote control cars and due to the high level of complexity you realize that stakeholders have conflicting understandings of program purpose. What should be your best course of action in this case?

choices.text: Explain the program's vision
Allocate more time and effort with known stakeholders to align their understandings
Perform beneﬁts management plan
Continue as planned because this situation is normal in large and complex programs

explanation:
Option "Explain the program's vision" is irrelevant as it shows the program direction and “from status” to “to status”. Option "Perform beneﬁts management plan" is irrelevant in this scenario and option "Continue as planned" is not correct. Option "Allocate more time" is the correct answer as the known stakeholders influence the entire program especially other stakeholders. The program manager should spend a great amount of time in any program in order to maintain stakeholder engagement and alignment with program’s objectives
Reference: Stakeholder Engagement Chapter, in addition to experience. Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: During the last meeting with the steering committee, they advised you to update your risk management plan and do the program risk identification and analysis again because multiple unidentified risks have been occurring and the program is at a critical phase. The advice of the steering committee is given as part of its role in

choices.text: The escalation process
Program monitor and control
Program phase gate reviews
Program health checks

explanation:
Whether during a health check or a phase gate review, the advice of the steering committee is given as part of its role in program monitor and control
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.5

text: You are a member of the portfolio board and choosing a program to undertake. - Program A has a Cost of $250000 and a revenue of $50000 per year, - Program B has a Cost of $200000 and a revenue of $50000 per year, - Program C has a Cost of $150000 and a revenue of $50000 per year, - Program D has a Cost of $100000 and a revenue of $50000 per year. Which program will you recommend?

choices.text: Program A
Program B
Program C
Program D

explanation: In this case, the program with the highest ROI will be chosen; ROI = (Revenue / Cost) * 100. ROI-A = 20%, ROI-B = 25%, ROI-C = 33.3%, ROIC-D = 50%. The highest ROI is for program D. N.B: the numbers here are given for example purposes

text: Program manager spends a good amount of time preparing the schedule. From the scope statement, the program manager derives the PWBS which will help in the make-or-buy decisions, and in estimating the cost, quality, resource and duration. Consider you are building your schedule using the PWBS. Which of the below is the best approach to start with?

choices.text: Meet with components manager and build the schedule together
Design a first draft of the schedule including the components start and end dates
