Have the components managers design their schedules and then combine all schedules together to form the program schedule
Have the program team build the schedule and let the components managers use the same schedule with changes based on their work

explanation:
When building a schedule, at the start it is a top-down approach and then it transforms into a bottom-up approach. The program manager starts by designing a first draft of the schedule including the components start and end dates. The project managers will then design their schedules and then roll-up any changes to the start and end dates. The program manager updates the program schedule accordingly and the new start/end dates for each component will act as a constraint at the level of the component
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11. This section is not detailed in the SPM, this is why we have included our instructors insights and experience in exam questions in this answer to help you better understand the flow

text: Your customer has outsourced your company to manage a transformation program on their premises. You have three components on your program; components A, B and C. Component A has a delayed milestone due to multiple changes and component B, which is dependent on the output of component A, is scheduled to use an important resource from component A. Component A’s project manager refuses to let go of the resource until the project delivers its due milestone. What should you, as the program manager do?

choices.text: Let Component A’s project manager give the resource to component B
Let Component B wait for component A to finish and release resources
Work to balance program needs with resource availability
Let component A and component B sit together and come up with a collaborative decision

explanation:
Option D is not correct since it is the responsibility of the program manager to do resource optimization by balancing the need with the availability. Options A and B can be the results of the balancing that is done in option C. As a program manager you should always search for optimal ways to balance the requirements with the availability, this can result in resource interdependency, prioritization or even in the merger of components in extreme cases.
Reference: insights from students who have taken the exam

text: You have good relations with project managers in your company as you have been one of them. Recently, you have been assigned to manage a program for your organization and you are currently discussing with the steering committee about the assignment of project managers for two of the program’s components. In which phase are you?

choices.text: Definition phase – formulation sub-phase
Definition phase – planning sub-phase
Delivery
Closure

explanation:
During program delivery phase, components are authorized, initiated, integrated and transitioned. Project managers are assigned during this phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 95 - 7.1.3

text: The sponsor acts as an advocate in a program and ensures that the program gets the management attention while informing the program manager of any strategic change. The sponsor is an executive member who acts as the chair of the steering committee. Who usually takes up the role of sponsor in components’ steering committees?

choices.text: Program sponsor
Program manager
Project manager
Functional manager

explanation:
Usually, the program manager takes the role of component sponsor. All other options are not correct. It is important to note that this role is given to the program manager based on his experience and the degree of autonomy a program steering committee grants to him/her
This question has occurred on multiple occasions in the exam and is based on your experience in program management. Some of the questions you get in the exam cannot necessarily be found in books

text: Consider you are the program manager and your program is 5% complete. The program has a budget at completion BAC= 5 million dollars, the actual cost is $250 000 and earned value is $245 000. What can you tell about the program status?

choices.text: The program is slightly over budget, which is not a problem at this stage
The program is slightly over budget, which is a huge problem at this stage
Budget needs to be re-baselined
Steering committee should intervene because the situation is out of control being at just 5%

explanation: The program is at just 5%, and the cost variance is CV = EV – AC = $5 000 which is totally insignificant when it comes to the $5M budget at completion. If you had bigger completion percentage (above 30%) and a bigger CV (greater than 50k), then you will have an issue

text: You are in a matrix organization and managing program A. Program steering committee is shared between your program and program B. Program B has been experiencing severe delays and steering committee has decided that multiple resources should be transferred from your program to be full-timers on program B. Two of the resources had issues with the transfer and are not accepting to communicate with you. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Terminate program A because there is no chance of delivering the intended benefits with less resources
Involve the functional managers of the resources to be transferred
Raise this issue to executive management and do not accept the resources transfer
Inform stakeholders of this change

explanation:
In a matrix organization, functional managers are responsible for resources; this is why in this case functional managers need to be involved to solve the resources issues.
N.B: in the exam question, if they do not mention what type of organization, by default you consider it as matrix organization
Reference: SPM V4 Page 18 - 1.7.1 (leadership skills section in particular)

text: Your company is project-based and has been delivering successful projects for many years. An executive manager was recently recruited and he comes from a programs-based organization. As a first act, he asked you to perform an initial assessment to know if adopting program approaches would be an added value to the organization; based on your findings, he will be able to present the approach to the executive management. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Create business case
Create roadmap
Analyze the strategic plan
Deﬁne the objectives

explanation:
Organizations derive strategic goals and objectives by performing a strategic planning cycle having as input the organization vision and mission. The strategic goals and objectives are documented in a strategic plan which is then divided into a set of initiatives to be undertaken by the portfolios, programs and projects. In this scenario, the program manager needs to analyze the strategic plan in order to validate alignment before proceeding any further.
Here you consider it as a new program proposal and you need to check if it is aligned with your company's strategies and objectives, thus strategic plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 34 - Figure 3-1 shows that it is the starting point for your program

text: Funding frameworks differ between programs. You are managing a step-funding program where the program receives funds at the start of each year. The remaining funds at the end of each year are returned back to the organization. What should you ensure as a program manager?

choices.text: You add a 15% to the total budget amount in order to stay on the safe side
Compiling all available financial information and listing all income and payment schedules in sufficient detail so that program costs can be tracked as part of program budget
You spend all the remaining money on rewarding the team
You make sure to only accept important change requests so you do not affect the budget

explanation:
Program budget consists of compiling all available financial information and listing all income and payment schedules in sufficient detail so that program costs can be tracked as part of program budget. Option A is not correct in any case, as the program manager should reflect the exact resources need of the program, based on this need, the business case is approved or rejected. Option C is irrelevant and option D is not correct in any case
Reference: SPM V4 Page 115 - 8.1.2.5

text: The CEO of a risk adverse company decided to change the culture of his organization after several pitfalls; he decided that the company needs to take more risks if it wants to gain from its investments. A program was designed with you as the program manager. While in the definition phase, in which of the following documents is the organization’s risk tolerance recorded?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Mandate
Strategic plan

explanation:
Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits and most importantly a high-level risk assessment containing the risk tolerance acting as a reminder and constraint when making program decisions.
Risk tolerances are not detailed in the standard, however they are part of the business case and they are used for validating the continuation of the program in phase-gate reviews; if the program surpasses the risk threshold, it might be terminated
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: You were planning to launch a new component in order to maximize the delivery of benefits; your recommendation got accepted by the steering committee and you need two of your program management team members to dedicate a week’s time to this component due to its strategic importance for the success of the program. To determine the availability of certain program resources, you reference

choices.text: Resources calendar
Resources management plan
Governance plan
Project management plan

explanation:
Resources calendar shows the availability of program resources. All other options do not reflect the resources availability
Reference: resource calendar is mostly seen in PMP study material and abundantly on the WEB. We have included all you need to know in this QB

text: You are mid-way through your program and you realize that stakeholders have conflicting concerns and issues, and that operational departments are a bit reluctant to change. You do not understand the reason behind this, however, in your analysis of the issues in order to come out with necessary changes, you need to evaluate

choices.text: Resources availability
Program scope
Include the operational departments in the steering committee
Benefit register

explanation:
Changes may be related to scope; this type of changes originates from stakeholders, missing requirements at the start of the program or external resources. Scope changes affect the architecture and PWBS. The program manager needs to monitor and control the scope in this case in order to ensure successful completion of the program. Operational departments are a bit reluctant is normal in most programs and it is the job of the program manager to drive the change through organizations
Reference: SPM V4 Page 137 - 8.2.10

text: Which one of the below programs would you suggest to remove? - Program A NPV at: 5% = 5,243, 10% = 2,841, 15% = 1,563; - Program B NPV at: 5% = 2,320, 10% = 1,254, 15% = 688; - Program C NPV at: 5% = 6,400, 10% = 3,275, 15% = 1,679; - Program D NPV at: 5% = 3,000, 10% = 2,755, 15% = 700.

choices.text: Program A
Program B
Program C
Program D

explanation: The higher the Net Present Value (NPV), the better. Program B has the lowest NPV, thus it should be the one to be removed

text: When you started your career, you were keen to get onto the management path and you worked day and night to get your PMP certification followed by the PgMP certification. Today, you are a highly regarded program manager in your organization and you are the one that people come to for advice. This warrants that

choices.text: Portfolio management will give you the choice to choose specific types of programs to undertake
Steering committee will give you a higher degree of autonomy
Management will give you a raise and make you a portfolio manager
You will assume the role of the steering committee in your programs

explanation:
Option A is not correct because it is the job of the portfolio manager and portfolio board to choose which programs to undertake based on strategic alignment. Option C is not correct because being a good program manager does not necessarily mean that you will be a good portfolio manager. Option D is not correct as, normally, the need for steering committee and role are different than of a program manager, and a well-established program requires both. Option B is the correct answer, the steering committee will give you a higher degree of autonomy and higher threshold for escalations
Reference: SPM V4 Page 86 - 6.3. This section clearly states this, however you can also check the following sections: Page 76 - 6.1.9, Page 84 - 6.2.4 and page 69

text: Funding models vary for programs and subsequent projects; funding can be internal or external. Consider you are managing a program funded by the government. The used funding is a step funding and requires the program to include workers from different cultural diversity. This is regarded as?

choices.text: Assumption
Constraint
Benefit
Suggestion

explanation:
This scenario clearly links to a constraint put by the funding organization. The program needs to abide by it and can’t continue without it
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: You are in the definition phase of a 5-years program and you know that you need to plan thoroughly in order not to deviate from the purpose of the program and be able to continuously maintain viability of the program by integrating changes as needed. You have just completed the PWBS which will allow you to

choices.text: Develop the risk management plan
Identify critical success factors
Get authorization to start program work
Develop the program schedule

explanation:
PWBS helps in taking make or buy decisions and in estimations of cost, duration, quality and resources; in addition to risk identification and communications requirements analysis. From the above options, only option D is correct as good schedules can be built only after PWBS is established because consider you having a large task and you manager wants a schedule and related estimations; you will have to decompose the task into sub-tasks in order to be able to be able to give your manager what he/she wants
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11

text: Your program is delivering incremental benefits; you have already identified benefits and listed them in your charter, which was approved. During the conduct of the program, you realized that a key benefit was not valid anymore due to market change and you need to take corrective actions. What is your next step?

choices.text: Continue with the implementation as planned
Escalate to steering committee
Revising the beneﬁts management plan
Analyze the impact and the needed change

explanation:
Option A is incorrect. Option C is irrelevant as you first need to analyze the impact and then recommend the change to steering committee; following the decision, you will update the status across the affected documents. Option D is the correct answer. Option B comes next; it couldn’t be the first step, because the steering committee would have redirected the program manager to do the analysis and come back with his/her recommendations. All changes recommended by the program manager to the SC need to be analyzed, assessed and prepared prior to the recommendation, because the SC will not be doing the work, they will only look at your recommendations and numbers and take the decision accordingly
Reference: no particular reference. This is based on experience and based on multiple occurrences in the exam

text: Through program performance monitoring and controlling, the program management team continuously monitor the health of the program and ensure that it remains aligned with the strategic objectives and in-line with the planned values. During which phase you do program performance monitoring and controlling?

choices.text: Program definition
Program delivery phase
Program closure
Throughout the program

explanation:
The performance monitoring and controlling is done throughout the program delivery. As program manager and program team collect, measure and disseminate performance information and assess program trends.
Pay attention the question here is targeting the program performance based on the execution of this program and its components which happens during the delivery phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 101 - 7.2.2.3

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. You are now in the process of categorizing the stakeholders in order to analyze them. Which of the following is the best approach to get feedback about stakeholders’ attitudes regarding the program impact?

choices.text: Questionnaires and surveys
Interviews
Brainstorming sessions with the program team
Focus groups using open-ended questions

explanation:
Focus groups help in getting feedback about stakeholders’ attitudes regarding the program impact; it helps to understand the culture and concerns of stakeholders as well. In addition, the open-ended questions help solicit feedback furthermore by letting the stakeholders interact
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. The program is kept confidential due to rising competition. You are now in the process of preparing the program management plan, which of the below is true about this plan?

choices.text: Integrates and manages program components
Establishes management controls
Integrates the program's subsidiary plans
All of the options

explanation:
The program management plan is a document that integrates the subsidiary plans and management control points in order to integrate and manage the individual components. The control points measure performance against the program management plan using collected information from constituent projects. Once the program management plan is approved, program delivery phase starts. It is worth noting that the program management plan development is iterative, prepared early in the program lifecycle and update throughout the program due to changes, priorities, etc
Reference: SPM V4 Page 94 - 7.1.2.2

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. During the meetings with stakeholders, the program management team tries to solicit the stakeholders’ attitudes, perceptions and response towards risks. This is important in order to

choices.text: Define and analyze risks
Prepare the program risk management plan
Determine stakeholder concerns that may lead to risks
Prepare the stakeholder communication strategy

explanation:
Program management team members try to understand the impact, urgency and probability of stakeholders’ concerns and based on this, determine the problems that may lead to risks affecting the program. This approach helps in defining risks and then analyzing them but is not the main idea in this scenario. Option D is prepared from the stakeholder engagement plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 134 - 8.2.8.1

text: You are in the definition phase of your program to deliver five new ice cream flavors and you realize that the program is of critical importance to the organization. You are currently in program initiation (formulation) sub-phase and are developing an accountability matrix by identifying and assigning program roles and responsibilities in order to

choices.text: Build the core team and to differentiate between the program and project resources
Build the core team and to assign program governance roles
Build the core team and to assign program management team members roles
All of the options

explanation:
During program initiation (formulation), program manager develops an accountability matrix by identifying and assigning program roles and responsibilities in order to build the core team and to differentiate between the program and project resources N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 4 Program Life Cycle

text: Funding varies between programs and between components of the same program. Funding can be internal or external. You are managing a program which will be funded externally by the government. The steering committee is responsible for agreements to secure funds and they should take into consideration that

choices.text: Funding will not be done at once, instead it will be a step funding
Funding is subject to regulations
Program will fund its work until deliverable, then, the government will release the funds as contracts are being closed
None of the Options

explanation:
Working with government or any external authority funding your program is most probably subject to regulations; funding organization will include regulations, constraints, and limitations and may include adherence to certain laws as well
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: You have multiple components in your program and are currently initiating two of these components. You are working closely with the component managers in order for them to understand the need and requirements and plan their projects accordingly. As a program manager, you define standard measurement criteria for success for all constituent projects by

choices.text: Analyzing stakeholders’ expectations and requirements across constituent projects
Letting the project managers analyze their projects stakeholders and roll back requirements to you and to the program management team
Only analyzing the stakeholders that are impacted by the program
Focus on positive stakeholders and do not analyze the negative ones

explanation:
During program initiation (formulation), you define standard measurement criteria for success for all constituent projects by analyzing stakeholders’ expectations and requirements across constituent projects in order to monitor and control the program. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 5 Program Life Cycle

text: You have successfully performed the implementation of the program to release a new drug to cure cancer all around the world and you are getting into the final stages before closure. You are currently closing all projects and contract in order to start the closure phase activities. As a program manager, you realize that the final decision in program closure is given to

choices.text: Program manager
Program sponsor
Program steering committee
CEO

explanation:
When in closure phase, program manager recommends the closure to steering committee which will check the successful delivery of the program against program charter. If successful, steering committee will recommend closure to sponsor who will check the success of the program against the business case and take a decision on closure
Reference: SPM V4 Page 97 - 7.1.4. Final approval comes from the sponsor or sponsoring organization. SC has a role in approving closure however the sponsor takes the recommendation from the SC and goes to corporate or portfolio governance in order to get the final approval; for the program the sponsor gives the final approval. If the question does not contain sponsor as answer, SC would have been the correct choice

text: Program manager is responsible for controlling the budget in a program. Some programs are funded internally by the company, others externally. When a program is funded externally, the ____ is responsible for controlling the funding

choices.text: Steering committee
Program manager as well
Sponsor
PMO

explanation:
This scenario is related to a program funded externally. The steering committee is responsible for controlling the funding. The program manager has the authority to make changes to the budget up to a certain level only. However it is the responsibility of the steering committee to control the funding
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: You are the sponsor of a program and currently working on assigning a program manager to manage the definition phase. The output of this phase will be used as input in the planning phase and will be used to maintain program alignment and viability throughout the lifecycle. The change driven by this program needs to be integrated as well with the operations and throughout the company. In a program, who is considered the champion for change?

choices.text: Program manager
Program sponsor
Program steering committee
CEO

explanation:
The program manager is the champion for change and communicates all changes to appropriate stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 59

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. In order to build and maintain advocacy, program manager should

choices.text: Prepare a roadmap
Prepare a business case
Prepare a program charter
Prepare a strategic plan

explanation:
The roadmap assesses the program's progress toward realizing its expected beneﬁts, it is the basis for transition and integration, used to communicate plan and benefits to stakeholders to build and maintain advocacy. In addition, the roadmap shows major milestones, important components, incremental benefits, relationship between components & benefits and major decision points. Option D is not correct as the strategic plan is not prepared by program manage, it is the output of strategic planning cycle done by portfolio. Options B and C are irrelevant for advocacy\
Reference: SPM V4 Page 37 - 3.3

text: During the course of your 5-years program, you were closing contracts at the component level after the components successfully delivers the expected result. You have finished all your components and now are in the closure phase. During this phase, all program-level contracts are closed. For closing each contract, you should

choices.text: Meet with the component manager who administered the contract
Prepare a contract closeout report
Recommend contract closure to sponsor
Meet with all affected stakeholders and get their consent before closing

explanation:
In program contract closure, a formal closure is done after ensuring that all deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made and that there are no outstanding contractual issues. The program manager then prepares a contract closeout report
Reference: SPM V4 Page 140 - 8.3.3

text: You have been appointed by the sponsor to replace the program manager on a program half way through delivery. You have been informed that the stakeholders do not understand why this program was undertaken and what the boundaries of the program are. You notice that the scope statement was missing and you decided to prepare it. The program scope statement

choices.text: Facilitates overall planning
Builds a PWBS
Maintains advocacy
None of the options

explanation:
During program planning, the program manager develops a detailed program scope statement by incorporating program vision and all internal and external objectives, goals, influences, and variables in order to facilitate overall planning. Option C is done by preparing the roadmap. Option B is not a direct purpose for it. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 7 Program Life Cycle

text: Programs are complex; they undergo a lot of changes and face problems during their lifecycles. As a program manager, it is your responsibility to capture, analyze, record and take action against the problems that occur and implement changes as a result of that. Many of the changes are authorized directly by you but others require the approval of the steering committee. For all changes

choices.text: Program manager alone maintains a record of the proposed change for all changes
Program manager should maintain a record of the proposed change that he/she authorized it and steering committee should maintain a record of the proposed change that they authorized it
Program management team should maintain a record of the proposed change
Only important changes are maintained

explanation:
For each change in the program, the program management team should maintain a record of the proposed change. All other options are not correct; the Program Manager alone cannot do all the work
Reference: SPM V4 Page 74 - 6.1.8

text: During the program definition phase, you prepare the infrastructure that will guide the program and its components through the delivery phase. In your program to deliver a drug to cure cancer patients throughout the world, you are currently establishing a program management plan and schedule in order to

choices.text: Start the benefits delivery phase
Effectively forecast, monitor and identify variances during program execution
Get authorization for resources
Achieve program benefits

explanation:
During program planning, the program manager establishes program management plan and schedule by integrating plans for constituent projects and creating plans for supporting program functions (quality, risk, etc.) in order to effectively forecast, monitor and identify variances during program execution. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 9 Program Life Cycle

text: Throughout the delivery of your program, you have faced multiple issues and problems. Corrective actions were taken accordingly and program documentation was being continuously updated to maintain alignment. In a program, you identify and manage unresolved project-level issues in order to

choices.text: Maximize synergies in accordance with the governance model
Achieve program benefits
Define PMIS
facilitate overall planning

explanation:
During program planning, program manager identifies and manages unresolved project-level issues by establishing a monitoring and escalation mechanism and selecting a course of action consistent with program constraints and objectives in order to achieve program benefits. Option D is related to roadmap. Option C is irrelevant and option A is related to defining the PMIS N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 12 Program Life Cycle

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are in formulation and are preparing your charter and estimating costs, you should

choices.text: Consider the program roadmap
Consider the rough order of magnitude estimates while developing the business case
Let the component managers estimate their projects and roll back estimations to you
Re-do the assessment done in business case in order to make sure it is correct

explanation:
From the above options, the rough order of magnitude helps the program manager while preparing the charter as it includes information about the sources of cost that could not be estimated. Options C and D are not correct. Option A is prepared along with charter
Reference: SPM V4 Page 107 - 8.1.1.3

text: Program manager needs to closely monitor program components in order to efficiently manage the delivery of the program. Program manager constantly tries to maximize the benefits delivery and continuously tries to maximize the contribution of project managers to the program. During delivery phase, how does the program manager maximizes the contribution of a project manager in achieving program goals?

choices.text: Approve closure of the project
Deploy uniform standards
Review the project manager’s performance in executing the project management plan
Aggregate information from program and constituent projects

explanation:
During execution of the program, program manager reviews project managers’ performance in executing the project in accordance with the project management plan in order to maximize their contribution to achieving program goals. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 20 Program Life Cycle

text: Your program to bring potable water to the nearby city is nearing the end and you have successfully delivered the program benefits. During the course of the program, you executed the different plans to guide the delivery process. In a program, you execute the program management plan In order to

choices.text: Ensure program outcomes meet stakeholder expectations and standards
Deliver benefits
Establish consistency
Remain strategically aligned

explanation:
During execution of the program, program manager executes the program management plan with its subsidiary plans using the tools identified in the planning sub-phase and by auditing results in order to ensure program outcomes meet stakeholder expectations and standards. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 21 Program Life Cycle

text: You are bidding to gain a program for a reputable customer. After thorough analysis, you came out with a result of 3 years to finish and you cannot do it in less time; another company gave an estimation of 2.5 years and a third one of 2.8 years. You learned about a niche market technological breakthrough which will definitely make you finish the program in 2 years. Your given estimation would be

choices.text: 2 years
3 years as you haven’t yet used the new technological breakthrough
You ask for more time to analyze your bid
3 years as your company needs that much time to deliver

explanation:
The technological breakthrough will definitely lower the estimation to 2 years; and this should be your estimation because you have a definitive estimate in this case
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: Program manager needs to do resource optimization in order to effectively employ the program resources throughout the course of the program. This optimization will allow the successful delivery of benefits. How do you ensure that program resources are employed effectively?

choices.text: Regularly prepare performance reports
Conduct change impact assessment
Record each change request in a change log
Update program plans by incorporating corrective actions

explanation:
During the controlling of a program, program manager updates program plans by incorporating corrective actions to ensure program resources are employed effectively in order to meet program objectives. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 26 Program Life Cycle

text: Issues occur throughout the lifecycle of the program; issues should be handled at their appropriate level based on the escalation process prepared during the planning phase. Some of the issues are handled at project-level by project managers, others by program manager, and others by steering committees. How do you, as a program manager, manage program level issues?

choices.text: By managing changes in accordance with the engagement management plan
By managing changes in accordance with the risk management plan
By identifying and selecting a course of action consistent with program scope
By working with known stakeholders to consider all points of view

explanation:
During the controlling of a program, program manager manages program level issues (schedule, resources, etc.) by identifying and selecting a course of action consistent with program scope, constraints, and objectives in order to achieve program benefits. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 27 Program Life Cycle

text: Your program to design a new airport for your city is in its early phases and is expected to span along 7 years. The new airport will be built as an extension to the existing one with 5 times the runways it currently has. Which of the below documents expresses the program vision and the benefits the program is to produce?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Strategic plan
Program management plan

explanation:
"Business Case" is not correct as it doesn’t express program vision. "Strategic plan" is not correct as it doesn’t express program vision; strategic plan is divided into a set of initiatives to be undertaken by portfolios. "Program management plan" is irrelevant to the question. Program charter includes justification, vision, strategic fit, outcomes, scope, components (planned, not all), risks, issues, assumptions, benefits and benefits strategy, stakeholders considerations, timeline, governance structure and resources needs
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2

text: You program has a steering committee to provide support and oversight. This committee is responsible to provide governance support and resources to oversee and monitor program uncertainty and complexity. Which of the below ensures the effectiveness of the governance process?

choices.text: Regularly scheduled reviews
Preparing performance reports
Following the program management plan
Engaging stakeholders

explanation:
The governance plan includes planned governance meetings including phase gate reviews, health checks and other reviews in order to ensure the effectiveness of the governance process. In addition, governance plan describes the systems and methods to be used to monitor, manage, and support a given program, responsibilities of specific roles for ensuring timely and effective use of the systems and methods. It includes program governance summary; structure and composition of governance members; roles and responsibilities; dependencies, assumptions and constraints; benefits, performance metrics and measurements; components initiation and transition criteria; issues escalation process and guidelines to schedule additional meetings
Reference: SPM V4 Page 70 - 6.1.1.2, Page 75 - 6.1.9

text: You are newly appointed as a program manager to a program in its delivery phase. You have noticed that the program components are not effectively integrating with each other and the program seems to lack consistency. In order to drive efficiency and consistency among projects and deliver program objectives, you decided to

choices.text: Develop a good communication management plan
Obtain approvals to continue to the next phase
Develop program and project management standards and structure
Develop a roadmap

explanation:
Through program governance, program manager develops program and project management standards and structure (governance, tools, finance and reporting) using industry best practices and organizational standards in order to drive efficiency and consistency among projects and deliver program objectives. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 1 Governance

text: Throughout the program, program manager and steering committee work to deliver benefits within program scope. Continuous performance data maintains the alignment of the program with strategic objectives. As a program manager, you obtain authorization and approval through stage gate reviews by presenting the program status and performance data to governance authorities in order to

choices.text: Continue to the next phase
Get stakeholder feedback on the program status
Make sure that the business case is still viable
Evaluate key performance indicators

explanation:
Through program governance, program manager obtains authorization and approval through stage gate reviews by presenting the program status to governance authorities in order to proceed to the next phase of the program. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 3 Governance

text: As part of a major phase gate review, steering committee was looking at an escalated issue affecting 3 projects: X, Y and Z. The issue was escalated by Project X. As a result, steering committee decided to end projects Y and Z, continue with A as planned and add a new project W to cater for the misalignment caused by the issue. What is your next course of action as a program manager when it comes to initiating project W?

choices.text: Revise the program documentation to incorporate the change
Communicate change to stakeholders
Meet with program team and component managers to discuss the change
Give a reward to project A’s project manager for capturing the issue

explanation:
The correct answer here is A; upon initiation of a new component, all program-level documentation and records dealing with the component should be updated to reflect any changes to the affected components. Option D is not correct as this is the job of the project manager and does not warrant a reward. Option B and C come after option A
Reference: SPM V4 Page 77 - 6.1.11

text: You are appointed as a program manager for the development of new remote cars. The cars need to be available for a two-hour play time on a full battery and has to be pushed to the market within one year in order to beat competition. You are mid-way through the program and a lot of requirements have changed since the start, in addition, 55% of the budget has been used so far and the remaining budget will barely suffice the program. In addition, a good number of the remote cars are failing inspection. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Continue as planned with components transitions and closures
Re-baseline budget
Conduct a phase gate review
Requesting a quality assurance audit

explanation:
55% of the budget is a fair number being mid-project, and the question clearly states that the budget will suffice, even if barely; so there is no need to re-baseline budget. Option A is incorrect as you have a clear issue which is that a big number of cars are failing inspection, option C will not help in this case as phase get review are conducted to make a go/no-go decision. Option D is the correct answer; a quality assurance audit will help assess the results of the inspection done as part of Quality Control
Reference: SPM V4 Page 132 - 8.2.6

text: You are appointed as a program manager for the development of new remote cars. The cars need to be available for a two-hour play time on a full battery and has to be pushed to the market within one year in order to beat competition. You are mid-way through the program and everything is going according to plan. However, you are finding it more and more tiring to ensure stakeholders receive the appropriate information, in the right format and on time; this situation is due to the stakeholders having different communications needs. What will your best course of action be?

choices.text: Document lessons learned
Maintain a Benefit Register
Maintain a Stakeholder Register
Establish a Project Management Information System (PMIS)

explanation:
The only correct option is C. Program team should maintain a Stakeholder Register in order to use it for communication. It contains all the needed information for communication the right information, at the right time and through the correct channel.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 60 - 5.1

text: What is the difference between a Portfolio and a Program

choices.text: A portfolio includes initiatives that are independent
A program includes initiatives that are independent
A portfolio includes initiatives that are interdependent
Both have strict start and end dates

explanation:
Pay attention to the wording here, this question has occurred a lot of times in the exam. A portfolio includes initiatives that are independent is the correct answer
Reference: SPM V4 Page 26 - 2.4

text: Experience levels differ between project managers and the degree of autonomy and follow up from the program manager is highly dependent on the project manager’s experience. You have multiple components in your program. Component A’s project manager is the most experienced and has prepared a communication management plan. Others are approaching you for help in preparing their plans. You

choices.text: Ask the PMO for standardization
Ask all the projects to use the plan of component A and update it to their needs
Ask them to consult their functional managers
Ask all the projects to use the program communication management plan

explanation:
The best approach is to use the program communication plan for all components as it provides standards and guidelines to be used while preparing their communication management plans; so they will not be using the exact same plan, however they will be using it to help them framework their project plans
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam
Reference: SPM V4 Page 64 - 5.3 (this is not a direct reference however the concept is mentioned in this paragraph)

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are working on the preparation of the business case including a cost-benefit analysis in order to get your program approved by sponsor. Which of the below is correct?

choices.text: You should identify only the financial benefits
You should identify the key stakeholders
You should identify intrinsic and extrinsic beneﬁts
You should identify only high level benefits

explanation:
Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits, high-level risk assessment and intrinsic and extrinsic beneﬁts
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: During the definition phase, the program manager along with the program management team, prepare the program management plan with all its subsidiary plans which will guide the execution of the delivery phase. From the below options, who is responsible for reviewing all program management plans?

choices.text: Program manager
PMO
Steering committee
Sponsor

explanation:
Steering committee SC is responsible for reviewing all program management plans. All the plans need to meet the passing criteria of the SC. Program manager is responsible for preparing the plans and recommending them to SC. If in the exam you do not have SC as an option, you need to choose the Program Sponsor as the sponsor has the final say on all plans.
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3 (not a direct reference)

text: During the course of the program, the program manager will spend most of his time engaging stakeholders and managing their expectations. A stakeholder on your program is furious and is not accepting to meet you; even you tried to call him and went to his office but he refused to see you. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Try another time as it is your responsibility to maintain stakeholders buy-in
Escalate to PMO
Escalate to Steering committee
Escalate to Sponsor

explanation:
Option A has been already tried by the program manager and did not yield a result. The next escalation level for the program manager is the steering committee
Reference: SPM V4 Page 73 - 6.1.6

text: Your company was recently audited by the government and they had several findings. In order to implement the changes, you are now managing a program to acquire a new information system which will handle all the requested validations and authorizations. After sending the RFP, the vendor informs you that the IT department in your company had already issued an RFP for the same. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Proceed as planned
Ask for a meeting with the IT director
Escalate to steering committee
Retract your request and terminate your program

explanation:
This is a strategic issue and program manager needs to escalate to steering committee for advice. Options A and D are not correct and option B should not be undertaken without the recommendation of the steering committee
Reference: SPM V4 Page 73 - 6.1.6

text: The program manager needs to identify project managers with appropriate experience to manage the related component in order to ensure successful completion of the program. When identifying suitable profiles for project managers, the program manager needs to?

choices.text: Refer to the Human resources department
Refer to your acquaintances
Refer to functional managers
Escalate to Sponsor

explanation:
Resources are normally taken from their functional departments to work on the program and its components. Program managers needs to collaborate and coordinate with the functional managers to check if they have the skills required among their teams and to negotiate their use on the program.
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam
Reference: SPM V4 Page 105 (not a direct reference)

text: During the strategic planning cycle of an organization, the vision and mission are used to produce strategic goals and objectives documented in the strategic plan, which is then divided into sets of initiatives. Each set of initiatives may be grouped under a portfolio grouping multiple programs within it. In which phase of the program are the program managers assigned?

choices.text: Definition phase – formulation sub-phase
Definition phase – planning sub-phase
Before the start of the program
After approval of program charter

explanation:
Program manager is assigned by sponsor as early as possible during formulation phase. Program manager is officially authorized after charter approval
Pay attention, initiative means portfolio, program, project, etc. The word can be used in the exam to refer to any of those.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 26 - 2.3

text: Program governance enables and performs program decision making, establishes practices to support the program and maintains program oversight with a focus on delivering benefits. In addition, program governance

choices.text: Facilitates program funding to support business case
Outlines responsibility for approving each program’s approach
Is responsible for agreements needed for external funding
All of the options

explanation:
Usually, program governance outlines responsibility for approving each program’s approach and plan for how it will pursue program and organization goals, and for authorizing the use of resources to support components and program work. These approvals occur in program definition phase and are facilitated by business case and program charter. Program governance facilitates funding to support business case taking into consideration the organization’s priorities. When funding is from external resources, program governance is responsible for the agreements needed
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. You noticed that multiple stakeholders have conflicting priorities. In order to set clear expectations among stakeholders, you must possess

choices.text: Negotiation skills
Leadership skills
Customer management skills
Political skills

explanation:
Program manager uses negotiation skills to diffuse conflicting priorities and facilitate understanding and agreement.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 19 -1.7.1

text: Stakeholder engagement is one of the most important aspects in a program. The program manager is responsible for stakeholders’ identification, analysis and engagement throughout the program lifecycle. You perform stakeholder analysis through historical analysis, personal experience, interviews, knowledge base, review of formal agreements and inputs from other sources in order to

choices.text: Create the communication management plan
Create the stakeholder management plan
Create the stakeholder register
Engage stakeholders

explanation:
During stakeholder management, the program manager performs stakeholder analysis through historical analysis, personal experience, interviews, knowledge base, review of formal agreements and inputs from other sources in order to create the stakeholder management plan. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 2 - Stakeholder Management

text: Stakeholder engagement is one of the most important aspects in a program. The program manager is responsible for stakeholders’ identification, analysis and engagement throughout the program lifecycle. After stakeholders’ identification, your next activity is

choices.text: Update stakeholder register
Analyze stakeholders
Define critical success factor
Defines KPIs

explanation:
The question asks about the next "activity" which is analyzing stakeholders; however, similar questions have been spotted in exam where they ask about the next step, which will be updating the stakeholder register. Pay attention to the wording, activity is not the same as step!
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: Stakeholder engagement is one of the most important aspects in a program. The program manager is responsible for stakeholders’ identification, analysis and engagement throughout the program lifecycle. Stakeholders have different interests, expectations, level of support and impact on a program. Which document represents the interaction of all stakeholders’ current and desired support and influence?

choices.text: Stakeholder register
Stakeholder map
Stakeholder engagement plan
Communication management plan

explanation:
Stakeholder map represents the interaction of all stakeholders’ current and desired support and influence. It helps assess the impact of the program change on stakeholders; it also helps in making informed decisions and knowing when and how to engage stakeholders. Stakeholder register records stakeholders’ roles in the program, influence, impact, classification, engagement strategy and communication, etc.; which are used for successful engagement and communication with stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: Companies undertake programs internal to the organization and programs external to the organization where the company is outsourced by a customer to deliver benefits based on a well-defined agreement. Consider you are studying a proposal to manage a program for a customer. In order to establish strategic alignment. You refer to

choices.text: Business case prepared by your portfolio board
Your organization's strategic plan, vision and mission
Your customer organization's strategic plan, vision and mission
Business case prepared by your customer

explanation:
Any program undertaken by your company to any client must first be strategically aligned to your company’s strategic objectives and goals. After all if you are a company that manufactures airplanes, you will not accept a program to construct buildings even if it aligns with your customer's objectives.
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: Program managers may join at the early start of a program or during any other phase of it. When a program manager joins an already debuted program, he has a major responsibility of understanding the program and the program’s status in order to continue with a successful execution and delivery. You have been newly appointed as a program manager replacing another program manager who has left the company. You want to know about the vision, stakeholders’ considerations and program justification. You refer to

choices.text: Program roadmap
Business case
Program charter
Program scope statement

explanation:
Program charter includes justification, vision, strategic fit, outcomes, scope, components (planned, not all), risks, issues, assumptions, benefits and benefits strategy, stakeholders’ considerations, timeline, governance structure and resources needs
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2 and Page 93 - 7.1.2.1

text: Program managers may join at the early start of a program or during any other phase of it. When a program manager joins an already debuted program, he has a major responsibility of understanding the program and the program’s status in order to continue with a successful execution and delivery. You have been newly appointed as a program manager replacing another program manager who has left the company. You want to understand the program quickly. You refer to

choices.text: Program roadmap
Business case
Program charter
Program scope statement

explanation:
For quickly understanding the status of the program, you refer to the scope statement which will give you a bird’s eye view of the program. Scope is usually described in the form of expected benefits and sometimes user stories or scenarios; it encompasses all benefits to be delivered by the program, reflected in a WBS. The second best answer is the roadmap because roadmap contains major components which add up to the benefits realization and will show you the status quickly and how much you still have to go. But the question here is that you want to understand the program quickly! Always pay attention to the question because in the exam you will have such a question, however, they may alter the question and ask you about status (Roadmap), or similar to this one where you want to understand the program (scope statement), or sometimes you want to know the vision, timeline and stakeholders (charter)
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam

text: Planning is a very important sub-phase in the definition of a program because it will guide the entire program delivery. Program management plan and all subsequent documents are prepared, recommended by program manager and approved by steering committee. Which of the below methods help while doing the planning?

choices.text: SWOT analysis
Monte Carlo
Sensitivity analysis
80/20 rule

explanation:
SWOT analysis which reflects the Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats is used while developing the program charter and program management plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 40 - 3.4.2.3

text: The program managers work with the program management team for the entire course of the program in order to successfully deliver the benefits. Some programs succeed and others fail. You are now in closing phase and your program has delivered its benefits; you receive a call from the operations manager stating that he is not ready for the change. In this scenario, you should have

choices.text: Prepared a good benefits management plan
Been informing the functional managers
Added the operations manager to the steering committee
Let the operations manager prepare the benefit sustainment plan with you

explanation:
The benefits management plan shows how and when benefits are going to be delivered. It formally documents the activities necessary for achieving benefits (create, maximize and sustain benefits). It represents the baseline that guides the delivery of benefits during program performance. It also defines activities, processes and systems needed for the change, driven by the realization of benefits; and when the transition to operational state will occur. This plan will includes guidelines and approaches to perform the other options given in the answers set
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1

text: Component A’s project manager has requested a resource which is currently being used by component B. This is an important resource and is required to work on component A in order to mitigate a spotted risk; however, the resource is also important for component B for 30% of her time each day. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Escalate to sponsor
Do resource prioritization
Do resource interdependency

explanation:
Here, the resource is to be shared among the components, as the components do not need her full time. The best option is to do resource interdependency and schedule the resource use accordingly between the different components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 133 - 8.2.7.1

text: One of your components managers has approached you with an opportunity that will benefit the program and speed up the delivery time dramatically. You have been avoiding the project manager’s request as you already have more important changes to undergo. What is the best course of action for the project manager?

choices.text: Escalate to project steering committee
Escalate to project CCB
Escalate to program steering committee
Escalate to program sponsor

explanation:
The change affects the program and not the particular project, which means that the next level of escalation needs to be to the program steering committee. If the change was affecting the component, the escalation level will be project CCB and then project steering committee
We have seen this on multiple occasions and multiple pages in the standard of which paragraph 6.1.6 is one.

text: Risks are an integral part of every program. During initiation, the program manager along with the sponsor and the available members of the program team, prepare an initial risk assessment which will be included in the presented business case. Risks are added, analyzed, refined and tracked throughout the program. You are now planning for a risk and you have already prepared your risk response, what next?

choices.text: Define management reserve
Define contingency reserve
Update the risk management plan
Derive a mitigation strategy

explanation:
After you prepare the risk response strategy and plan, you define contingency reserves. It is important to mention that program contingency reserve is different from the sum of its components contingency reserves. The management reserves are derived by the sponsor
Reference: SPM V4 Page 135 - 8.2.8.2 and 8.2.8.3

text: Due to the complexity and uncertainty of a program and the large number of stakeholders involved, the program manager needs to maintain a good level of communication and always present the right information at the right time. Which plan documents the process to communicate the right program information to the right person at the right time?

choices.text: Program communication management plan
Program stakeholder engagement plan
Program information management plan
Program benefits management plan

explanation:
Program communication management plan is a component of the program management plan. It describes how, when and by whom the information will be administered and communicated. It includes a communication strategy, communication table that outlines who is responsible to distribute what information to whom and using which channel, roles and responsibilities of communication management, constraints and resources allocated to communication
Reference: SPM V4 Page 112 - 8.1.2.2

text: Your team and yourself have worked hard for the tight schedule delivery of the program and are now in the closure phase. An unidentified issue was spotted in the product to be delivered to the customer. The delivery is due tomorrow and you do not have time to fix the issue prior to the delivery. In this case you should

choices.text: Deliver without mentioning the issue
Inform the customer about the issue and its impact
Escalate to sponsor
Escalate to steering committee

explanation:
As a program manager, you should be truthful to the program and all its stakeholders. You should inform the customer about the issue and its impact
Reference: code of conduct

text: The program manager continuously looks into opportunities to maximize the realization of benefits and prepare plans for continuous benefits realization after the program ends. Your program to deliver the city metro which will link both ends of the city together is performing well and components are producing the intended outcomes. In order to align and integrate benefits within or across the organization, you

choices.text: Identify and evaluate integration opportunities and needs
Obtain organizational leadership approval
Develop a benefits register
Define program mission and vision

explanation:
During strategic program management, program manager identifies and evaluates integration opportunities and needs within program activities and operational activities in order to align and integrate benefits within or across the organization. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 10 Strategic Program Management

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, the program manager monitors and controls the status of the program, presenting it to the steering committee through reviews and recommending actions to course correct or enhance the delivery. You have been aggregating delivery information from the program and constituent components in order to prepare the performance reports. In order to determine program performance, you

choices.text: Compare final values to planned values for scope, quality, cost schedule and resources
Obtain organizational leadership approval
Develop a benefits register
Conduct phase gate reviews

explanation:
During program closure, program manager completes a program performance analysis report by comparing final values to planned values for scope, quality, cost schedule and resource data in order to determine program performance N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 31 Closing the Program

text: Benefits are the endpoint of a program manager, however, the delivery needs to be efficient and within set limitations in order to be considered a successful one. The program managers try to identify and capture synergies and efficiencies identified throughout the program lifecycle in order to

choices.text: Compare final values to planned values for scope, quality, cost schedule and resources
Obtain organizational leadership approval
Update and communicate the benefits realization plan to stakeholders
Ensure continued realization of benefits

explanation:
During program benefits management, program manager identifies and captures synergies and efficiencies identified throughout the program lifecycle in order to update and communicate the benefits realization plan to stakeholders N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 2 Benefits Management

text: Metrics are important in a program to be able to measure progress against planned values and maintain program alignment with set objectives. In your program to deliver the drug that will cure cancer patients instantly all around the world and throughout the program, you monitor metrics in order to

choices.text: Take corrective actions in the program and maintain and/or potentially improve benefits realization
Obtain organizational leadership approval
Update and communicate the benefits realization plan to stakeholders
Ensure continued realization of benefits

explanation:
During program benefits management, program manager monitors metrics (by forecasting, analyzing variances, what-if, causal analysis, etc.) in order to take corrective actions in the program and maintain and/or potentially improve benefits realization N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 4 Benefits Management

text: Programs normally use the procurement policies and procedures of the organization, unless the program has particular procurement specifications; in this case, the program manager will use the organization procurement processes and tailor them with the support from PMO to the program’s needs. Which of the below is an input to make or buy decisions?

choices.text: Scope statement
Benefits management plan
Procurement management plan
PWBS

explanation:
Scope statement takes as input the requirement of stakeholders (sponsors, clients, experts, legal, others), in addition to program management plan, scope management plan and requirements management plan. Its output is the PWBS which helps in make or buy decisions, estimations of cost, duration, quality and resources, risk identification and communication requirements analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 117 - 8.1.2.7

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Throughout the program lifecycle, you achieve and maintain stakeholders’ alignment to the program objectives by

choices.text: Negotiating the support of stakeholders by setting clear expectations and acceptance criteria
Performing stakeholders’ analysis
Updating business case
Updating program roadmap

explanation:
During program stakeholder management, program manager negotiates the support of stakeholders by setting clear expectations and acceptance criteria for the program benefits in order to achieve and maintain stakeholders’ alignment to the program objectives. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 3 Stakeholder Management

text: Communications are an integral part to every program. The program manager thrives to maintain a good communication level with all stakeholders. The communication strategy is derived from the stakeholder engagement strategy and plan to maximize engagement. In a program, you define and maintain communications adapted to different stakeholders in order to

choices.text: Maintain program alignment to strategic plan
Ensure their support for the program
Update business case
Update program roadmap

explanation:
During program stakeholder management, program manager defines and maintains communication adapted to different stakeholders in order to ensure their support for the program. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 5 Stakeholder Management

text: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) enable the team to make smart business decisions about the direction of a program and its subsidiary projects. They are used to follow up on program status and measure performance. Which of the below documents helps you identify the KPIs related to benefits?

choices.text: Benefit register
Benefit management plan
Governance plan
Business case

explanation:
You identify the KPIs using the identification methods listed in the benefits management plan. The identified KPIs are then recorded in the benefit register (BR); BR is for logging benefits, it does not contain the activity of identifying them. BR is a passive document into which your record the benefits
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam.
Reference: the entire benefits management chapter is a reference here

text: During definition phase, the program manager is responsible to prepare multiple documents and get them approved by the steering committee. These documents are continuously reviewed during the course of the program to maintain program viability and deliver the program successfully. Which of these documents contains the justification for the resources to be expended during the course of the program?

choices.text: Benefit register
Benefit management plan
Program charter
Business case

explanation:
The business case contains the justification for the resources to be expended during the course of the program
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1 and Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: Program success criteria are used in a program to maintain the minimum level of acceptable delivery of benefits. The program undergoes a lot of changes and it is the responsibility of the program manager to always keep an eye on meeting the program success criteria. Which of the below documents contains the program success criteria?

choices.text: Benefit register
Benefit management plan
Program charter
Business case

explanation:
The business case contains the program success criteria
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: Program success is measured against a successful delivery based on charter and business case. The success of a program can be viewed differently by stakeholders based on their position with relation to the program. For this reason, the program manager needs to define a clear definition for success and get it approved by steering committee. Which document contains the clear definition of success?

choices.text: Benefit register
Benefit management plan
Program charter
Business case

explanation:
The charter contains the clear definition of success; Business Case contains the success criteria
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2

text: Programs normally use the procurement policies and procedures of the organization, unless the program has particular procurement specifications; in this case, the program manager will use the organization procurement processes and tailor them with the support from PMO to the program’s needs. Procurement is done from a qualified sellers’ list. After completing the qualified sellers list, you normally?

choices.text: Issue an IFB
Sign Agreements
Issue an RFP
Update the program procurement management plan

explanation:
After completing the qualified sellers list, the program manager issues Request For Proposal RFP
This question occurred on multiple occasions in the exam and the correct answer is RFP because after you complete the qualified sellers list, you will be able to start the normal procurement process. The first option in a procurement process which is available here is the RFP
Reference: you can check the procurement process in the PMBOOK guide, however do not go into details because you do not need them for PgMP

text: A balanced scorecard is a performance metric used in strategic management to identify and improve various internal functions of a business and their resulting external outcomes. It is used to measure and provide feedback to organizations. In addition, Balanced score card is used to?

choices.text: Define critical success factor CSF
Define KPIs
Measure the value of benefit derived from the program
All of the options

explanation:
Balanced score card helps in classifying benefits; It enables organizations to clarify their vision and strategy and translate them into action. It is used to define critical success factors CSF, define KPIs and measure the value of benefit derived from the program
Reference: SPM V4 Page 71 - 6.1.1.3. In addition you can find a lot of information for BSC on the WEB, however all needed information is given in our QB

text: During the delivery phase, components are initiated, integrated, transitioned and closed. Each one of these steps represents different criteria for continuing to the next step. In your program to deliver the new metro which will link both ends of the city together, multiple components are being initiated. Which of the below is a part of components initiation criteria?

choices.text: Component business case
Lessons learned
Component roadmap
Component management plan

explanation:
The project initiation criteria follow these steps: Business case -> ensure resource availability -> define accountabilities -> communication of related information to stakeholders -> ensure component, program-level quality control plans -> authorize component governance structure
Reference: SPM V4 Page 77 - 6.1.11. The above sequence is based on multiple occurrences of questions in the exam and on insights from our instructors

text: During the delivery phase, components are initiated, integrated, transitioned and closed. Each one of these steps represents different criteria for continuing to the next step. In your program to deliver the new metro which will link both ends of the city together, multiple components are coming to their end. Which of the below is a part of components transition and closure criteria?

choices.text: Assess Component charter
Assess lessons learned
Assess Component roadmap
Assess Component management plan

explanation:
The project transition and closure criteria follow these steps: Confirm business case -> communication of related information to stakeholders -> component compliance with program-level quality plans -> assess lessons learned -> Confirm component to other practices
Reference: SPM V4 Page 77 - 6.1.11. The above sequence is based on multiple occurrences of questions in the exam and on insights from our instructors
