text: Your program for launching new flavors of ice cream is in its definition phase and you are thoroughly planning it being of critical importance for your company, and you know that a good planning will normally result in successful delivery and closure phases. In program lifecycle (PLC), program manager manages activities and facilitates program definition, delivery and closure. Which of the below statements is true?

choices.text: Program lifecycle is a combination of each of its projects’ lifecycles
It is helpful to design process to be applied across PLC phases
Purpose of PLC is to produce deliverables
Each project has unique lifecycle phases

explanation:
This question targets only one correct option, which is B; all other options are incorrect in any situation. Option B is correct because it is always helpful to establish common processes across all phases in order to ease PLC management
Reference: SPM V4 Page 9 - 1.3, Page 15 - 1.7, Page 20 - 1.9, Page 99 - 7.2.2.1 and many more sections stating that information should be used by the program and its components, thus the processes should work for both. In addition, the management plan and its subsidiary plans will be used as templates for the components in order to maintain the alignment and the consolidation of management.

text: A program manager maintains a close look on the program benefits throughout the program lifecycle. Governance board is also focused on delivering benefits and conduct regular meetings to ensure it. Benefits are the most important assets of a program and you constantly work to realize them. In the context of benefits, what is benefits breakdown structure?

choices.text: Helps define stakeholders’ objectives
Get the buy-in of stakeholders for their benefits
Model the stakeholders' expected beneﬁts
Extract critical success factors

explanation:
This question is to introduce you to the term “benefits breakdown structure” in case you haven’t encountered it before. The BBS helps model stakeholder expected benefits
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam. You can search the WEB, it has a lot of information on it, however the needed ones are included in this QB

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. What is the first thing you do as a program manager?

choices.text: Define strategic plan
Define business case
Establish program vision
Analyze program risk

explanation:
The first thing to be done by the program manager is to establish program vision, followed by program mission, objectives, goals and strategy. You will then need to start defining the BC, Charter and Roadmap. Option A is incorrect because it should be prepared by the portfolio.
Reference: this question has occurred multiple times in the exam and it is mostly one of the 20 test questions that are non-marked. The correct answer is similar to when you initiate any type of endeavor, you start with the vision, mission, objectives/goals and strategy. Once strategy is defined, you start the execution beginning with preparing the documents i.e. BC and charter

text: A program manager maintains a close look on the program benefits throughout the program lifecycle. Governance board is also focused on delivering benefits and conduct regular meetings to ensure it. Benefits are the most important assets of a program and you constantly work to realize them. Early in your program, you have prepared a benefits management plan in order to guide benefits delivery, their monitoring and controlling throughout the course of the program. Which option represents a use for Benefits Management Plan (BMP)?

choices.text: Identifying changes to components
Defining the projects’ charters
Identifying roles and responsibilities for program and subsequent projects
Identifying projects to be tackled by the program

explanation:
The BMP is the performance baseline of a program. Option A is the correct option because you validate program performance against the set baseline in order to determine whether to continue or whether changes need to be incorporated
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.1, in addition to multiple insights from exam questions

text: Not all work on a program is done during the program; some of the work is performed prior to the program when grouping the initiatives into portfolios and sometimes preparing the business cases for the programs. However, the assignment of a program manager usually marks the official debut of a program. When in program pre-setup phase, how is the program manager chosen?

choices.text: Assigned by program sponsor
Appointed by the steering committee members
A person with a PgMP certification and experience in managing complex programs
A person with the needed technical knowledge

explanation:
Following the standard for program manager, the program manager is assigned by the sponsor. This assignment should be done at the earliest in the program, during program pre-setup phase, otherwise known as formulation sub-phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 92 - 7.1.2.1

text: Each change request is recorded in the change log to be analyzed and to determine its impact and urgency. Following this, a decision is made to approve or reject the change. In addition to this, the program manager is responsible to:

choices.text: Escalate to steering committee
Escalate to Change Control Board (CCB)
Document the rationale for the decision
Program reporting

explanation:
In the program change monitoring and controlling, program CCB should ensure that change is recorded in change log, communicated to appropriate stakeholders and reflected in updates to affected components plans. However, it is the responsibility of the program manager to do all of this. Option C is the correct option, option D is irrelevant in this case, options A and B are incorrect because many change types are within the authority of the program manager and do not warrant escalation
Reference: SPM V4 Page 74 - 6.1.8

text: You have been working for your company for ten years. You started as a junior project manager and today you are a highly regarded program manager. Throughout your years in the company, you have been using the lessons learned prepared by programs and projects throughout the years and you have been finding that the more lessons learned you record the helpful it will be when undertaking a similar program in the future. During which phase of the program are the lessons learned documented?

choices.text: Program definition phase
Program closure phase
Benefit delivery phase
Throughout the entire program

explanation:
Lessons learned should be documented throughout the entire program and not at a single specific phase
Reference: SPM V4 Page 130 - 8.2.4.1, in addition to Page 92 - 7.1.2.1, Page 97 - 7.1.4 and Page 102 - 7.2.2.5

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. Time to market is key in order to beat the competition and the program is undergoing a lot of changes which might affect the go-live date. What should you, as the program manager, do?

choices.text: Continue with the work as planned
Escalate to executive management that the program will be delayed
Continuously review the program master schedule
Request additional human resources and budget

explanation:
The changes are affecting the schedule, and the question clearly states that the changes might affect the go-live date, so the program manager should maintain a close look on the master schedule in order to assess the impact of the changes and accelerate or decelerate components. Option D comes as a result of the assessment if needed e.g. if the program is delayed, you might want additional resources to speed it up.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 121 - 8.1.2.11 and Page 136 - 8.2.9

text: Your company has been losing assets and failing to cope with the fast market. The CEO has taken a firm decision to group the projects in a program to attain more benefits. Part of the program is to restructure the company, which will lead to lowering the number of employees, thus, many will lose their jobs. You have been appointed to manage the program and you are new to the company. What is the first thing you should do?

choices.text: Prepare a business case
Analyze the cultural aspect of the company and its employees in order to assess the way the change is accepted
Prepare a high level roadmap
Analyze the high level risks

explanation:
The first thing you do in this situation is to study the cultural aspect which will help you determine the strategy to undergo for the program and will help you manage the communication with stakeholders in order to remain aligned with the strategic objectives, in addition to helping with risk management.
The cultural aspect is the most important one and is mentioned several time in the SPM of which the following are the most important:
Reference: SPM V4 Page 9 - 1.3, Page 62 - 5.2, Page 64 - 5.3 and Page 120 - 8.1.2.10

text: A big program is underway in company A and your company B is outsourced to deliver one of the components, which is managed as a program in your company, with you as the program manager. You have a very good relationship with company A. However, company A has been delaying a large payment which is needed to maintain your program performance. What is the best course of action for you?

choices.text: Re-baseline budget
Re-baseline schedule
Take corrective action
Issue a change request

explanation:
This situation clearly targets the program financial management aspect, which has corrective actions as an output. Option C is the correct answer. The situation does not warrant a re-baseline, so options A and B are incorrect. Option D is done later.
Although the questions targeting inputs and outputs are scarce in the exam, however this question and specifically the financial part has been spotted multiple times in the exam (in addition to scope and schedule).
Reference: SPM V4 Page 127 - 8.2.3

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are in delivery phase and are identifying risks in order to get the approval for proceeding and validate continuation. Which of the below is considered an important aspect when getting the approval?

choices.text: What are the constraints?
Assumptions are still valid
What is the probability of success?
Who are the key stakeholders?

explanation:
Based on the question, you are in the delivery phase and you are identifying risks. This is done to determine whether: Program assumptions are still valid; Assessed risk has changed from its prior state, with analysis of trends; Proper risk management policies and procedures are being followed; Cost or schedule contingency reserves are modified in line with the risks of the program
Reference: SPM V4 Page 134 - 8.2.8

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are preparing your program charter, which of the following is included in the charter?

choices.text: Market analysis
List of all the components to be initiated during the program
An assumption that the cost of material to be used will have only little price fluctuation throughout programs
List of planned program governance meetings

explanation:
Option B is not correct because at this stage, you do not know the list of all the components for sure, instead you have an initial mix of components that will be updated throughout the delivery phase. Option D is in the governance plan and not charter. Option A is part of the business case. Option C is correct as the assumptions are part of the program charter. Program charter includes justification, vision, strategic fit, outcomes, scope, components (planned, not all), risks, issues, assumptions, benefits and benefits strategy, stakeholders considerations, timeline, governance structure and resources needs
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You know that you will need to work in order to ensure that the program objectives remain aligned with the organization’s strategic goals and objectives. You ensure program alignment with the organization’s strategic plan, objectives, priorities, vision, and mission statement by

choices.text: Performing an initial program assessment
Defining a roadmap
Engaging stakeholders
Identifying benefits

explanation:
Through strategic program management, program manager performs an initial program assessment by defining the program objectives, requirements, and risks in order to ensure program alignment with the organization’s strategic plan, objectives, priorities, vision, and mission statement. N.B: this is a question from ECO; you should have a good understanding of the ECO before attending the exam as a fair number of the scenarios are based on it
Reference: ECO Task 1 Strategic Program Management

text: You have multiple projects in your program. Each project manager is identifying the work to be done on her/his project; which one of the below options guarantees that your program scope covers all the benefits?

choices.text: Use the standards set by the PMO
Prepare a scope statement
Prepare a program work breakdown structure
Prepare a beneﬁts realization plan

explanation:
The PWBS encompasses the entire scope of the program; it reflects all the benefits to be delivered by the program. All other options are irrelevant
Reference: SPM V4 Page 123 - 8.1.2.12

text: Knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. You are currently in the process of getting information from stakeholders in order to understand their organizations’ cultural aspect. Which of the below options best suits this process?

choices.text: Focus groups
Questionnaires and surveys
Interviews
Open-ended questions

explanation:
The best way to get stakeholder feedback and obtain as much information as possible (key information as well), is to do it while using open-ended questions. Open ended questions can be used during options A, B and C
Reference: SPM V4 Page 62 - 5.2

text: Each program uses a variety of resources from different technical and management backgrounds. Resources are added and removed based on the program and its constituent components needs. Who is considered responsible for providing the needed resources to a program?

choices.text: Program governance board
Program sponsor
Program manager
Each project’s project manager

explanation:
Based on the SPM, the program sponsor is the one responsible for providing resources to the program. Sponsor is an advocate for the program and is accountable for enabling success
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.8, Page 61 - 5.1 and Page 79 - 6.2
Pay attention here that the program manager, functional managers and SC have a hand in providing resources, however this is the responsibility of the sponsor

text: You are establishing a new company and recruiting employees from all over the country. Some people will need to drive for 2 hours to get to the job site, others for a couple of minutes. Multiple investors have put their trust in your company and you are now designing the structure of your company initiation program’s steering committee with their roles and responsibilities. Members of the steering committee are the investors and a few senior managers in the company. What will you have to do next?

choices.text: Plan for governance meetings
Study the cultural aspect of the company
Start with stakeholders’ identification
Get your business case approved

explanation:
Based on the question, you are now designing the structure of the steering committee, which contains investors that are external to the company and definitely have busy schedules. What you need to do in this case in order to make sure than the steering committee does its role in the program, is to plan for regular meetings ahead in order to reserve a spot for the program in the investors’ busy schedules
Reference: SPM V4 Page 71 - 6.1.1.2

text: In definition phase, Business case, roadmap and charter are approved as part of the formulation sub-phase; and the program management plan (PMP) is approved as part of planning phase. Considering that your PMP has just been approved, what is your next step as a program manager?

choices.text: Establish the core team and appoint components project managers
Initiate component requests
Set up PMO and PMIS
Charter component projects

explanation:
Based on the question, the Program Management Plan has been approved, which indicates that you are now in the delivery phase. During this phase, components’ initiation requests are suggested to steering committee for approval. Option D comes later after approving the component BC and preparing the charter, Project managers are appointed in the projects’ charters. Option C is done prior to preparing the program management plan and establishing the core team is done as part of the infrastructure development after program charter approval and before preparing the program management plan
Reference: SPM V4 Page 95 - 7.1.2.2

text: You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. You are working on the preparation of the business case including a cost-benefit analysis in order to get your program approved by sponsor. Which of the below is correct?

choices.text: You should identify only the financial benefits
You should identify the key stakeholders
You should identify intrinsic and extrinsic beneﬁts
You should identify only high level benefits

explanation:
Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits, high-level risk assessment and intrinsic and extrinsic beneﬁts.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 35 - 3.1

text: Programs deliver benefits to the sponsoring organizations. It is the responsibility of the program manager and steering committee to ensure the successful delivery of a program by delivering the planned benefits. After performing benefits identification and setting up a benefit register, what should you do in order to develop the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the benefits?

choices.text: Check the success factors in business case
Meet with stakeholders
Check the clear measurement for success in program charter
Revise the roadmap to link components to benefits

explanation:
The benefits register needs to be reviewed with key stakeholders in order to define KPIs. The other options are irrelevant in this case
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1

text: You are managing a program to build a new generation of mobile phones with higher capabilities than the current products in the market. When preparing the business case, you should focus on

choices.text: Using a comparative advantage analysis
Having focus groups in order to study stakeholders’ influence, power and interest
Clearly defining the program vision
Conducting SWOT analysis

explanation:
The product needs to be of higher capabilities than what exists in the market; program manager should focus on comparative advantage analysis in order to depict the advantages of designing a new product, if other companies are doing a similar effort and to find alternative approaches in case the original approach fails
Reference: SPM V4 Page 39 - 3.4.2.1

text: In definition phase, Business case, roadmap and charter are approved as part of the formulation sub-phase; and the program management plan (PMP) is approved as part of planning phase. Considering that your PMP has just been approved, what will you, as a program manager, need to do?

choices.text: Leave the component managers do their work without interfering until they deliver the intended results
Ensure that component managers are collaborative
Work closely with each component manager to ensure project scope, time and budget remain within limitations
Help component managers with their daily work activities in order to maintain good relationships with them

explanation:
Option A is not correct, option C and D are not correct because the program manager can not intervene with the components managers’ work. The components’ managers will manage their components and the program manager will manage the interdependency between components and ensure the collaboration of component managers in order to deliver benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 13 - 1.4.3

text: Knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. During the last meeting, you realized that multiple important stakeholders were missing for the first time. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: Do root-cause analysis
Call them and make it clear that they should attend the planned meetings no matter what
Analyze CPI and SPI in order to make sure that program is performing as expected and that the missing stakeholders have no reason to skip the meeting
Inform sponsor of this urgent matter

explanation:
Stakeholders’ participation is measured by stakeholder metrics defined in the stakeholder engagement plan. In case of non-participation, program manager conducts a root-cause analysis and does not make assumptions on his own. All other options are irrelevant. Participation trends are analyzed using root-cause analysis
Reference: SPM V4 Page 65 - 5.4

text: Consider you are the sponsor for a new program; this program has been sitting on the shelf for too long and the portfolio management decided during their last meeting that this program needs to be initiated. Today, you received the initiation decision. What should be your first act?

choices.text: Identify steering committee members
Define program vision
Identify key stakeholders
Appoint a program manager

explanation: Sponsor should appoint a program manager as early as possible during the program formulation sub-phase because the program manager will be conducting all the formulation activities and the sponsor will act as an advocate. Option D is the correct option, all other options are done by the program manager and not by the sponsor

text: You were outsourced by your company to manage a government program to bring electricity to all cities, towns and villages on a 24/7 basis. Working with the governance, you have designed a steering committee with high-level country officials and other countries’ partnerships. During the course of the program, which of the following is addressed by the steering committee?

choices.text: Define program thresholds
Aggregate performance of program and constituent components
Approve / reject all change requests
Endorsing / approving recommendations for programs

explanation:
Among these options, option D is the only one performed by the steering committee. Option A is not correct thresholds are defined by program manager and approved by steering committee. Option B is done by program manager in order to check the status of the program and get approval from steering committee for continuation or changes. Option C is not correct, as the program managers will directly approve changes within his authority level
Reference: SPM V4 Page 72 - 6.1.3

text: You were outsourced by your company to manage a government program to bring electricity to all cities, towns and villages on a 24/7 basis. Working with the governance, you have designed a steering committee with high-level country officials and other countries’ partnerships. During the course of the program, you have been approving change requests within your authority level and recommending others to steering committee. You have encountered several planned risks and you have been continuously keeping a close eye on the KPIs and the thresholds in order to implement any preventive action needed. Which of the following documents records thresholds for evaluating KPIs and achievement?

choices.text: Business case
Roadmap
Benefits realization plan
Benefits register

explanation:
The benefits register records the list of planned benefits with their corresponding KPIs and thresholds, in addition the benefits register contains mapping of benefits to strategic objectives, mapping of planned benefits to program components as reflected in charter, brief description of how benefits are measured, risk assessment and probability of occurrence, progress indicator, target dates and milestones for benefit achievement, responsible party for delivering benefit, process for measuring progress and process for communicating progress
Reference: SPM V4 Page 47 - 4.1.1

text: Your CEO is a learning enthusiast and has recently completed his PgMP certification. He decided to switch the company from a silo-based company to a program-based company. You are in a committee meeting and are currently selecting which endeavors to be undertaken as programs. Which of the following validates to be undertaken as a program?

choices.text: Expanding a football field
Setting yearly objectives for employees
Upgrading the government information system
Use of a new project management tool

explanation:
Option A is a project, Option D is the implementation of a new tool and does not validate to be a program, option B is irrelevant. Option C is correct as the transformation will consist of multiple programs and projects to manage the legal, expansion, and other different aspects of the government’s information system across all the ministries
Reference: Page 3 - 1.2

text: You are managing a program which is very tight on schedule and any delay will cause the company to lose its investment, budget fluctuation within limits is accepted by the company and the program targets several internal aspects of the company. For best course of action, what should you do?

choices.text: Include the CFO in your steering committee
Send the component managers on time management trainings
Set a clear escalation process and have a quick response plan for schedule changes
Transfer the risk to another external party

explanation:
The program being tight on schedule and the budget not being a problem, makes option C the only correct option; setting up clear escalation process will give the manager the ability to approve changes within his authority quickly and having a quick response plan for schedule changes will make the schedule changes implementations faster. Option A is irrelevant. Option B may not help during this tight schedule given. Option D is not correct since the program targets several internal aspects of the company; any new company will need to study the organization culture and many other aspects which will lead to more delays
Reference: SPM V4 Page 66 - 5.5, Page 73 - 6.1.6

text: You have been struggling to keep up with the plan for your ice cream new flavor launching program due to high level of complexity and market competition. During the course of the program, multiple steering committee members are not participating in the planned meetings, in addition to not showing interest and sending substitutes for important meetings. What should you do?

choices.text: Meet them face to face
Analyze the situation and take appropriate actions
Raise this issue in the next steering committee meeting
Assign each stakeholder a team member to ensure they know about the program’s progress

explanation:
Before doing anything and making assumptions, program managers should analyze the situation and based on the output, take appropriate actions
Reference: SPM V4 Page 64 - 5.3 and Page 65 - 5.4

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Throughout the program, you realize that stakeholders have different and/or contradicting views of the program objectives and you need to resolve this before it affects the program. What is your best course of action?

choices.text: Let the sponsor deal with this issue as he has more reach than you do
Meet with only the positive stakeholders and ignore the others
Conduct group meetings where you act as the facilitator
Maintain a stakeholder register

explanation:
In case of conflicts between stakeholders, program manager acts as a facilitator and conducts meetings in focus groups in order to solve the conflict. Option A is not correct as the scenario in this case does not warrant yet the sponsor’s intervention. Option B is irrelevant in all cases and option D does not warrant solving the conflict
Reference: SPM V4 Page 19 - 1.7.1 and Page 65 - 5.4

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Stakeholders are engaged throughout the course of a program when found needed. Which plan defines expectations for issue escalation including when to engage stakeholder?

choices.text: Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Program Governance Plan
Program Transition Plan
Communication Management Plan

explanation:
The Program Governance Plan defines expectations for issue escalation including when to engage stakeholders for effective issue resolution, with a focus on benefits delivery
Reference: SPM V4 Page 69, Page 70 - 6.1.1, Page 73 - 6.1.6 and Page 85 - 6.3

text: Your sponsor is a highly regarded individual in the company and has been working with you for a long time. You realize that a good sponsor will maintain a high level of exposure to the program and will facilitate its delivery and integration. You are currently working with your sponsor to conduct studies and estimates, and to prepare a high-level risk assessment. What are you doing here?

choices.text: Preparing the Business Case
Preparing the Program Charter
Preparing the Program Management Plan
Preparing the High-Level Roadmap

explanation:
During the preparation of Business Case, the program manager works with the sponsor and the sponsoring organization to initiate studies and estimates of scope, resources and costs, in addition to performing a high level risk analysis. Based on this, the Business Case can be created, or updated in case it was already created by portfolio. Business case contains cost/benefit analysis, market demand and barriers, approved concepts, legal implications, capability analysis, business impact, operational impact, alignment level, problems and opportunities, time to market, alternative solutions, benefits, and most importantly a high-level risk assessment
Reference: SPM V4 Page 92 - 7.1.2.1, Page 109 - 8.1.1.8

text: You are mid-way through your program and performing as expected. During a portfolio review meeting, it was decided that your program needs to be terminated because a similar product was launched to the market last week. This issue is due to

choices.text: A technological change was pushed to the market
Alignment of program objectives with strategic goals
Poor program performance
Invalid risk assessment

explanation:
From the given options, option D is the only correct option because program is performing well, so option C is not correct, Option B is irrelevant and option A is not correct since the competition pushed a similar product to the market. Here, the program missed a good risk assessment where they should have found that a competitor is building the same product and focused their investments on a different product or on changing the targeted delivery date
Reference: experience and multiple insights from exam questions. You can read SPM V4 sections related to risk management

text: Companies undertake programs internal to the organization and programs external to the organization where the company is outsourced by a customer to deliver benefits based on a well-defined agreement. Consider you are studying a proposal to manage a program for a customer. In order to establish strategic alignment. You refer to

choices.text: Business case prepared by your portfolio board
Your organization's strategic plan, vision and mission
Your customer organization's strategic plan, vision and mission
Business case prepared by your customer

explanation:
Any program undertaken by your company to any client must first be strategically aligned to your company’s strategic objectives and goals. After all you will not start a program is it is not aligned to your company's goal even if it brings revenue e.g. if you are into designing roads, you will not accept a program for designing buildings
Reference: multiple occurrences in the exam. It is thought to be one of the 20 test questions (non-marked), however it does not hurt to have the correct answer

text: Your company focuses a lot on quality of the output and it has made a name for itself in the market for the delivery of quality work. Each program has a team member dedicated to quality planning. What is the role of the steering committee when it comes to quality?

choices.text: None of the options
Monitor, control and report quality issues
Approves the proposed quality approach
Proposing standards to be approved by program team

explanation:
Options B is done by program team, option D is not correct in any case and option C is the correct answer as it is the role of the steering committee to endorse and approve the proposed quality approach
Reference: SPM V4 Page 81 - 6.2.2, Page 118 - 8.1.2.8

text: You have a large program with multiple components in it. Most of the work is outsourced to contractors. Which of the below represents the role of program manager in contract administration?

choices.text: Follow the contract management plan
Prepare a contract administration plan
Ensures program budget is spent properly to obtain benefits
Prepare Earned Value management reports

explanation:
In programs, normally the contracts are signed at program level but managed at component level; admin and closeout decisions are managed at component level and EV management reports are prepared at component level. Following this, options A, B and D are performed at component level. The correct answer is C because the program manager needs to ensure that program budget is being spent properly in order to obtain benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 131 - 8.2.5.1

text: Due to high complexity and uncertainty levels in a program, multiple risks occur and changes are constantly being implemented and integrated. The program aims to achieve its strategic goals and objectives and should remain aligned with the organization/corporate strategic goals and objectives. Who is the individual or entity responsible for achieving the organization/corporate strategic objectives?

choices.text: Program manager
Portfolio manager
Program sponsor
Program steering committee

explanation:
Option A is not correct because the program manager is responsible for achieving program objectives and realizing benefits, options D is incorrect because the steering committee is responsible for alignment of program objectives with strategic goals and objectives, option C is not correct because the sponsor is responsible for enabling success. Option B is the correct option because it is the job of the portfolio management (ultimately Portfolio Manager) to achieve the organization strategic objectives. The key word here is "Organization/corporate"
Reference: SPM V4 Page 10 - 1.4

text: Throughout your program to launch a new drug to cure cancer patients all around the world, you have been collecting data and measuring variations in order to communicate program performance data to steering committee and to continue the delivery of subsequent phase. Which of the below is included in program performance reports?

choices.text: Change requests
Resource usage
Audit conduct
Corrective actions

explanation:
Program performance reviews include a summary of the progress of all program components. They describe whether the program’s goals will be met and benefits will be successfully delivered according to plan. It includes status about what work has been accomplished, what works remains to be completed, earned value, risk, issues and changes under consideration. Option D is not correct as corrective and preventive actions are controlling activities which result in program performance reports and forecasts. The program performance report includes resource usage to deliver program benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 127 - 8.2.2.2; Program reporting include program performance report (Page 101 - 7.2.2.3). The answer here is a combination of both paragraphs, in addition to insights from exam questions.

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Why is it important for program manager to perform stakeholder engagement?

choices.text: Receive feedback
Maintain program strategic alignment
Communicate risks
Communicate program beneﬁts

explanation:
Stakeholder engagement enables the program manager to communicate benefits to stakeholders and dissolve conflicts between stakeholders
Reference: SPM V4 Page 65 - 5.4

text: You are newly recruited and assigned as program manager on a transformation program. You have large experience in the industry and specifically in this particular type of transformations and the company recruited you because they have recently started with the program’s approach and they do not have experience in doing so. During the assessment, you noticed that the established governance is of low maturity. What should be your next action?

choices.text: Establish a well-structured governance for the program
Determine governance roles and responsibilities
Work extra time to prepare a good governance plan
Use your previous company governance practices

explanation:
In this scenario, the first step to perform is to assess the existing governance structure, determine the governance needs and define the new structure based on it. Option C is not correct since it does not fix the low maturity issue, option B is irrelevant and option D is not correct
Reference: SPM V4 Page 67 - Program Governance; the entire chapter focuses on the importance of a mature governance and the importance of governance roles and practices

text: You are in the definition phase and preparing the documents to guide program delivery and closure phases. You have your planned benefits and you are listing them along with the benefits strategy in the charter. Which artifact documents the relationship between program activities and the expected benefits?

choices.text: Beneﬁts realization plan
Charter
Roadmap
Benefit Register

explanation:
The roadmap documents the relationship between program activities and the expected benefits
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3 And Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: During formulation sub-phase, the program manager and the program management team prepare a variety of documents in order to authorize the program and authorize the usage of resources. Which of the below is true regarding the program roadmap?

choices.text: It defines thresholds and metrics to measure benefits realization
It shows when the PMO deliverables are
It assesses the program's progress toward realizing its expected beneﬁts
It shows dependencies between all components

explanation:
Option A is part of the benefits realization plan; option B is part of PWBS; option D is part of Program architecture. Option C is the correct answer. The roadmap assesses the program's progress toward realizing its expected beneﬁts, it is the basis for transition and integration, used to communicate plan and benefits to stakeholders to build and maintain advocacy. In addition, the roadmap shows major milestones, important components, incremental benefits, relationship between components & benefits and major decision points
Reference: SPM V4 Page 36 - 3.3

text: During your program to design a new metro station for your city aimed to reduce traffic and travel time for the residents, you have been monitoring the financial environment due to the step-funding given by your government and trying to cope with it by planning for the necessary phase during each period. As part of the Financial Management, you manage?

choices.text: Operational costs
Program loss
Program profit
Performance reports and calculating CPI and SPI

explanation:
Profit and loss are not part of the financial management; option D is not correct as the performance report give status about program performance and are not managed as part of the financial management. Option A is the correct answer because the operational cost of the program, that is the expenditure on the program infrastructure, is to be managed as part of the Financial Management
Reference: SPM V4 Page 115 - 8.1.2.5 Operational Costs are included in the plan to be managed later on

text: Your stakeholders on your program to deliver the next-generation remote control car are interested in knowing the progress of a program in delivering its benefits. You have successfully maintained a benefit register. Each of your benefits is assigned a program team member to follow up on its progress and each benefit has a recorded probability level. A program manager should focus on

choices.text: Copying the related data from the benefit register to Benefit Realization Plan
The number of stakeholders involved
Organization’s ability of absorbing the change
Maintaining a good performance throughout the program

explanation:
Option A is not correct in all cases, as the information is copied from the Benefit Realization Plan to the benefit register. Options B and D are irrelevant for this scenario. Option C is the correct answer because the probability of achieving a benefit is directly related to the organization ability to absorb the change. Other factors affect probability such as number of interdependent components to realize a benefit which also affect the sustainability
Reference: SPM V4 Page 45, Page 49 - 4.2

text: After switching from silo-based company to a program-based company. You have been assigned a program manager role on a program to establish the Program Management Office (PMO) which will be common for all the programs in the organization. In a program, which of the below is the responsibility of a PMO?

choices.text: Use of enterprise environmental factors
Deﬁning quality standards
Ensuring that program objectives align with organizational strategic objectives
Conduct of phase gate reviews

explanation:
Option A is done by program manager. Options C and D are done by program steering committee. Option B is the correct answer because PMO support the program manager in many ways e.g. provides templates, gives guidance on how to develop PWBS, etc. One of the roles of PMO is to define quality standards for the program and its components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.9

text: On your program to design the metro station to reduce travel time between two ends of a city, you are currently preparing the program management plan in order to get steering committee approval and initiate the delivery phase. You are now preparing the program architecture. As a program manager, you realize that the ___________ establishes the program architecture

choices.text: Benefit Management
Program Charter
Program Roadmap
Program Schedule

explanation:
The Benefit Management establishes the program architecture which links the benefit to the components
Reference: SPM V4 Page 50 - 4.2.2

text: You are in the second year of a four years program and the program has been successfully delivering the planned benefits. During the last phase gate review, you noticed that some of the stakeholders have different understanding about the purpose for which the program has been undertaken, so you give them the scope statement. You have already baselined your scope during planning and are reviewing it continuously. Which of the below is part of the scope baseline?

choices.text: Scope statement
Program Work Breakdown Structure (PWBS)
PWBS dictionary
All of the options

explanation:
The scope baseline = Scope statement + PWBS + PWBS dictionary
Reference: Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam. This question has occurred in the exam, however rarely. The concept here is taught by several instructors in PMP

text: You are in the process of selecting project managers to manage the components in your program. One of the steering committee members asks you to hire his nephew. This being a conflict of interest, what should be your best course of action?

choices.text: Hire the steering committee member’s nephew
Document the potential concern, inform sponsor and continue the hiring process as planned
Being a conflict of interest, reject the steering committee’s request
Escalate issue to management

explanation:
Option D is not correct as the steering committee did not perform any unethical practice; in case of unethical practice i.e. steering committee member insists on hiring his nephew no matter what, program manager can report unethical practice directly to management. Option A is not correct as you need to follow the hiring process and check possible candidates before choosing one. Option C is not correct, because in the case of conflict of interest, you inform your direct manager (in this case sponsor), and proceed with the hiring process
Reference: Code of Conduct and experience. Sponsor should know about this, however this does not warrant an alarm as the SC member requested to include his nephew who might be a good supplier; if the member insisted on hiring his nephew or his nephew has been previously marked as a bad seller by the company, then you escalate.

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Which of the following represents a communication channel in a program?

choices.text: Client, Steering committee
Sponsor, public
Component managers
All of the options

explanation:
In the program delivery phase activity, the program communications management defines the communication channels to which program information is distributed. Communication channels are clients, sponsor, steering committee, public, etc.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 125 - 8.2.2

text: Your program is highly critical to your company and you realize that engaging the right stakeholder at the right time is key to success. While initiating the program, you noticed that multiple stakeholders have conflicting opinions about why the program was undertaken. In this scenario, you

choices.text: Provide the high level scope statement
Provide the business case
Provide the high level roadmap
Provide the strategic plan

explanation:
The high level scope statement shows why the program was undertaken; it represents a quick view about all the work involved in the program. Later during the lifecycle, the program manager will use the baselined scope statement. Business case and Charter are not used with all stakeholders because they contain sensitive information that should only be communicated to specific key stakeholders i.e. CEO, sponsor, etc and have restricted access to their content.
Scope statement is not included in the SPM, however it is part of the following tasks in ECO:
Reference: ECO Tasks 2, 3 and 7 - Program Life Cycle

text: Your company A recently acquired a new company B. Multiple projects in company B were added to your program. Component managers of company B are using their templates, processes and procedures to report to you which contradicts with your program. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Terminate the components
Replace the project managers
Let them report to you in their formats and you do the necessary changes in order to integrate it in your program
Consult your PMO to standardize program templates, processes and procedures

explanation:
The program management office facilitates program practices, standardizes processes and facilitates sharing of resources, methodologies, tools and techniques. It may as well extend to monitor compliance to program management practices as part of its governance role. In this scenario, program manager needs to consult PMO to standardize program templates, processes and procedures
Reference: SPM V4 Page 20 - 1.9

text: During your 5-years program to design new stadiums to host the world cup in your country, you have encountered a lot of issues and changes; your plan seems to work as you have cleared the issues and performed the changes successfully. Changes are normally approved at the appropriate level and can be escalated to steering committee if they fall outside of the responsibility of the program manager. Which of the below options is the responsibility of steering committee with regards to changes?

choices.text: Documenting changes and their resolutions
Deﬁning changes the program manager can resolve
Serving as the program's change control board
Analyzing large changes

explanation:
From the given options, the only one performed by the steering committee is defining changes the program manager can resolve; changes above the authority of the program manager, will be escalated to the steering committee
Reference: SPM V4 Page 81 - 6.2.2 And Page 83 - 6.2.4

text: As a veteran program manager you realize that resources planning and optimization are needed in order to effectively deliver benefits on time and within planned cost. Resources can be shared between components or even acquired from other portfolios and programs in the organization. Consider you are managing a program and are in need of a scarce resource from another program in your organization. What is your best course of action in this case?

choices.text: You meet with the other program manager and do resource optimization; inform the sponsor of the availability and plan for this resource accordingly
Let the functional manager handle this issue
Speak to the other program manager and ask her to send you the schedule for this scarce resource; modify your schedule to cater for the resource availability
Use resource prioritization process

explanation:
Option D is not correct as the resource prioritization is done for available resources within the same program. Option C is not correct as you cannot modify the schedule without the approval of steering committee and it is not professional to ask the other program manager to send her program’s schedule which might be confidential. Option B is not correct as you do not have an issue with or between resources. Option A is the correct answer, the program manager needs to optimize the use of resources throughout the program; in this case, the resource is external to your program and the best approach is to do resource interdependency management
Pay attention, SPM is just a reference guide for the exam, so you will definitely have similar questions from outside the SPM in the exam. The following section can be revised to let the resource management concepts soak (SPM V4 - 133 - 8.2.7)

text: You were outsourced by your company to manage a government program to bring electricity to all cities, towns and villages on a 24/7 basis. Working with the governance, you have designed a steering committee with high-level country officials and other countries’ partnerships. During the course of the program, you have been approving change requests within your authority level and recommending others to steering committee. You have encountered several planned risks and you have been continuously keeping a close eye on the KPIs and the thresholds in order to implement any preventive action needed. What is the impact of narrowing the program control thresholds?

choices.text: Slows down program execution
Speeds up program execution
There is no correlation between the program execution and the program control thresholds
Speeds up the schedule

explanation: When narrowing the program control thresholds, the type of change requests authorized by the upper level increases, small components issues to be handled by project managers will be escalated to you, and you will be spending more time solving issues. In addition, the types of changes that you are authorized to approve will decrease in numbers and you will need to escalate more changes to steering committee. All of this wastes time and slows down the program execution

text: Consider your program has a Budget of $ 1.2 M and is at the 3rd month of execution out of 9 months. Performance report showed: - Planned Value PV = $ 320K; - Expenditure to date = $ 350k; - Earned Value EV = $ 340k. From the given information, you realize that currently

choices.text: Program is 30k ahead of schedule
Program is 10k over budget
Program is 10k ahead of schedule
Program is 20k over budget

explanation:
Expenditure to date = AC.
Let us calculate SV and CV:
SV = EV - PV = 20 k
CV = EV - AC = -10 k. Hence, the program is 10 k over budget

text: You have been recently assigned to manage a critical program to improve employee morale due to increase in the turnover rate. You started by preparing the business case which was recently approved by the steering committee. Now, you are working to get authorization to use organizational resources. You are working on

choices.text: Program roadmap
Scope statement
PWBS
Program Charter

explanation: Program charter is a high level document that serves as the primary document reviewed by the steering committee to authorize the program and program resources. Program charter includes justification, vision, strategic fit, outcomes, scope, components (planned, not all), risks, issues, assumptions, benefits and benefits strategy, stakeholders considerations, timeline, governance structure and resources needs

text: You have been asked by the program sponsor to manage a program. After knowing the program objectives and needed work to be done, you realized that you do not have the appropriate experience to manage this program. What should you do in this case?

choices.text: You consider this as a challenge and start studying the PgMP in order to be able to have the needed skills
You take the program knowing that you will have a good steering committee to support you, a good PMO to guide you and a great sponsor to maintain advocacy
You inform your sponsor and let him decide on the matter
You reject the assignment as you do not have the needed experience

explanation: As a management professional, you need to abide by the PMI code of ethics and refuse to take the assignment as you lack the necessary experience to undertake the program

text: Your program is mid-way and you are currently meeting with stakeholders to transition a component. You noticed that they have conflicting opinions about the benefit value. In your opinion, what is the reason behind this conflict?

choices.text: Program communication management plan has not been revised
Program business case has not clearly documented the benefit value
Program charter has not clearly documented the benefit value
Stakeholders have not been properly engaged

explanation: This question is important because it aims to target specific words in a question, for example in this scenario “benefit value”. The benefit value or level should be documented in the business case. The business case is a cost-benefit value analysis. Furthermore, charter lists benefits but do not define the benefit value. Option D is not correct because the stakeholders are not disagreeing on the component delivery, but on its benefit value. Option A is irrelevant

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Program manager needs to maintain communication targeted to each stakeholder or stakeholder groups. From which of the below options are the CEO and Sponsor mostly interested to know about?

choices.text: ETC
BAC
EAC
CPI and SPI

explanation: CEO, sponsor and executive management is normally more interested in knowing the total cost of the program. The Estimate At Completion EAC gives them this information

text: One of your components project managers discussed an issue with you that affects her component’s scope, after further discussion, you realized that the issue only affects this component. What should be your next course of action?

choices.text: Inform project manager to escalate first to project change control board CCB
Inform project manager to escalate first to steering committee
You create a change request and let the component manager handle it at component level
Replace the component manager as she should not have discussed this with you

explanation: Option D is neither correct nor professional. Option C is not correct as the change request does not affect other components, and a change request should not be created at the program level. For projects the escalation process is as follows: escalate to CCB, then steering committee, then project sponsor; further escalation is done to Program CCB, program steering committee and program sponsor.

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. For better understanding of stakeholders, in your benefits register, you map the benefits to program components as in?

choices.text: Business case
Program charter
Program roadmap
Benefits management plan

explanation: As per SPM, the benefits register maps the benefits to program components as in program roadmap. Option A and B do not reflect benefits mapping. Option D establishes program architecture which maps how the components will deliver outcomes.

text: During your program to design a new metro station for your city aimed to reduce traffic and travel time for the residents, you have been monitoring the financial environment due to the step-funding given by your government and trying to cope with it by planning for the necessary phase during each period. Program financial environment is defined and documented in?

choices.text: Program cost budgeting
Component cost estimation
Financial management planning
Financial framework establishment

explanation:
Program financial framework establishment defines the financial environment. Programs can be managed internally and funded separately, managed and funded externally, managed and funded internally. However, a program cannot fund itself.
Reference: SPM V4 Page 114 - 8.1.2.4
